items.title: 2022年12月六级第1套 · 选词填空
items.passage:
During the summer, when I was a visiting poet at a residency out of state, an angry, confused woman wandered into my class and said: "I have three guns and I want to use them." We all [26] _____ . It wasn't clear if she had the guns, but we each know that, when we teach in America, we are already in danger.

I was dizzy with fear. The woman, who later turned out to be a schizophrenic(精神分裂症患者 ) without [27] _____ to her medications, was, by some force, wrestled out and [28] _____ away, then put in a hospital for observation, in a step that was actually safer for everyone than any one of us pressing charges. My class went on; we talked about poems. But despite the fact that the rest of our days on campus passed [29] _____ , I was rattled. I couldn't shake the sense that in this country we always live at [30] _____ risk.

A few months later, crisis [31] _____ again. While my husband was locking his bike to drop off our 3-year-old daughter for her preschool-aged day camp, a different woman approached. Swiftly and for no [32] _____ reason, she bent down, picked up our daughter, and began to carry her down the street. It was

so fast and confusing that my daughter [33] _____ cried. My husband, in a burst of speed, chased the woman and reclaimed our daughter. The woman, clearly confused, retreated into the public library. A [34] _____ of homeless people who generally know the other homeless in the area said they did not recognize the woman. The woman was so clearly unwell that when she was taken into custody she was incoherent. Heartbreakingly, she called our daughter by the name of someone else's child. Each part of the episode was as haunting as it was [35] _____ .

questions.shortExplanation: 听到『我有三把枪』后所有人本能呆住
questions.detailedExplanation:
【答案】 F) froze 动词

【词性槽】 主语 We all 后缺谓语动词，需一般过去时

【依据】 听到『我有三把枪』后所有人本能呆住

上文 I have three guns and I want to use them. 是极端威胁，紧接 We all 的反应只能是吓得僵住——freeze 正是英语里表达『因恐惧而瞬间不动』的高频动词，与下文 I was dizzy with fear. 形成连贯的恐惧反应链。

【竞争词】 E) escorted 及物动词，缺宾语

escort 意为『护送某人』，必须带宾语，而句子是 We all __(26)__. 后面直接句号，无宾语；且 『我们护送了』也对不上听到威胁后的第一反应。

M) stifled 及物且语义不符

stifle 通常作及物动词（压抑哭声/笑声），后面缺宾语；语义上『我们都压抑了』也无对象，语境不通。

N) struck 强搭配指向第 31 题

strike 在此语境里更常以 crisis struck（危机突然发生）这一固定搭配出现，后文 crisis __(31)__ again 才是它的归宿；用在 26 空只能解作『打击/击中』，缺宾语也不成句。
questions.hint: 根据空格前后的词性、搭配与上下文选择词语；每个词最多使用一次。

questions.prompt: a schizophrenic\(精神分裂症患者 \) without __(27)__ to her medications
questions.shortExplanation: access to 是固定搭配，意为『使用权』
questions.detailedExplanation:
【答案】 A) access 名词

【词性槽】 介词 without 后接名词

【依据】 access to 是固定搭配，意为『使用权』

have/without access to + 物是英语里表达『（无法）获得/使用某物』的标准搭配。原句 without access to her medications 即『无法获得自己的药物』，与精神分裂症患者发病的语境完全契合：因为没药才会发作、闯进课堂。

【竞争词】 D) dedication 语义荒诞

dedication 指『奉献、专注』，dedication to her medications 字面是『对药物的奉献』，对精神患者而言荒诞；语义与上下文医疗背景脱节。

I) network 搭配指向第 34 题

network of people / network of homeless 是更经典的搭配，将在第 34 空发挥作用；用在 27 空 network to her medications 不成习语，搭配生硬。
questions.hint: 根据空格前后的词性、搭配与上下文选择词语；每个词最多使用一次。

questions.prompt: was, by some force, wrestled out and __(28)__ away
questions.shortExplanation: escorted away 表『被护送/押送离开』
questions.detailedExplanation:
【答案】 E) escorted 动词

【词性槽】 并列连词 and 后接同形态过去分词

【依据】 escorted away 表『被护送/押送离开』

escort 常与 in/out/away 搭配，表示有专人带某人离开。原文 wrestled out and escorted away, then put in a hospital for observation，先是被拽出去、再被护送走、然后送医观察——动作链条流畅自然。

【竞争词】 M) stifled搭配与语义都不对

stifled away 不是英语固定搭配；stifle 表『压抑哭声/欲望』，与『从课堂带走精神患者』这一物理动作毫不相干。
questions.hint: 根据空格前后的词性、搭配与上下文选择词语；每个词最多使用一次。

questions.prompt: the rest of our days on campus passed __(29)__
questions.shortExplanation: 与『despite + I was rattled』形成让步对比
questions.detailedExplanation:
【答案】 K) peacefully 副词

【词性槽】 修饰动词 passed，需副词

【依据】 与『despite + I was rattled』形成让步对比

原句 despite the fact that the rest of our days on campus passed __(29)__, I was rattled. 用 despite 引出让步：表面上的日子平静，与内心仍受惊形成反差。peacefully （平静地）正好与 rattled（心神不宁）构成『外平静、内不安』的对照。

【竞争词】 C) barely 语义反向，破坏让步逻辑

barely 意为『几乎不』，『日子几乎没过去』不成话；且与 despite 之后『虽然…平稳，但我仍受惊』的逻辑反向。

L) presumably 推测语气与亲历叙述冲突

presumably 表『大概、想必』，用于推测；作者亲身在校园，对自己后续的日子是亲历不是推测，语气不匹配。
questions.hint: 根据空格前后的词性、搭配与上下文选择词语；每个词最多使用一次。

questions.prompt: in this country we always live at __(30)__ risk.
questions.shortExplanation: at incredible risk 强调难以置信的高风险
questions.detailedExplanation:
【答案】 G) incredible 形容词

【词性槽】 介词 at 与名词 risk 之间需形容词

【依据】 at incredible risk 强调难以置信的高风险

incredible 在这里取『大到难以置信』的语义。前文叙述了课堂枪击威胁，作者由此得出 we always live at __(30)__ risk 的结论——『生活在难以置信的高风险里』，与全文的极端恐惧场景吻合，且与下段又一桩街头事件互证。

【竞争词】 H) indignant 对象错配

indignant 修饰人或情绪，an indignant risk 不成习惯搭配，语法上虽通但语义荒诞。

J) overriding 色彩偏向中性『首要』

overriding risk 偏向 commercial/legal 等正式语体里『首要风险』，多用于风险评估；与本句日常生活的弥散性恐惧的语感不符，更不如 incredible 突出『程度令人震惊』。

【易错】 最具迷惑性的错误词是 J) —— overriding risk 像高级搭配但语体错位。考生背过 overriding priority/concern 这类搭配，会自然延伸出 overriding risk，且词性也对、句法也通。防坑：本文是抒情散文，谈的是『日常生活里弥散的恐惧』，需要程度词 （incredible），不是商务正式语体里的『首要风险』。判断不准时回到全文情绪基调—— 能与 I was dizzy with fear. 共振的，才是答案。
questions.hint: 根据空格前后的词性、搭配与上下文选择词语；每个词最多使用一次。

questions.prompt: crisis __(31)__ again.
questions.shortExplanation: crisis struck again 是地道高频搭配
questions.detailedExplanation:
【答案】 N) struck 动词

【词性槽】 主语 crisis 后缺谓语动词

【依据】 crisis struck again 是地道高频搭配

strike 作不及物动词时常表示『（灾难/危机/事故）突然降临』，crisis/disaster/tragedy struck 是固定句式。本段开头 A few months later, crisis __(31)__ again. 正是用这一句承接上一段课堂事件，引出新的危机——结构上与 Each part of the episode was as haunting as it was __(35)__. 所暗示的反复灾祸呼应。

【竞争词】 E) escorted 及物且语义反向

escort 必须带人作宾语；且 crisis escorted 字面是『危机护送』，毫无意义。

M) stifled主语错位

stifle 是『压抑、扼制』，主语通常是人或机构（压抑某种东西），crisis stifled 反过来了，且 stifle 也需要宾语，本句缺。
questions.hint: 根据空格前后的词性、搭配与上下文选择词语；每个词最多使用一次。

questions.prompt: Swiftly and for no __(32)__ reason, she bent down, picked up our daughter
questions.shortExplanation: for no apparent reason 是固定搭配
questions.detailedExplanation:
【答案】 B) apparent 形容词

【词性槽】 no 与名词 reason 之间需形容词修饰

【依据】 for no apparent reason 是固定搭配

for no apparent reason 意为『没有明显的理由』，是英语里描述行为突兀、动机不明的常用表达。陌生女子毫无来由抱走孩子，正符合此意——上文 Swiftly and for no __(32)__ reason 用 Swiftly 强调动作之突兀，apparent 与之呼应。

【竞争词】 H) indignant 感情色彩错位

indignant 形容『义愤填膺的』，用于描述人或情绪，而非 reason；an indignant reason 不成搭配，逻辑上女子也并非出于义愤。

J) overriding 搭配相反

overriding reason 意为『压倒一切的理由』，是『有强烈理由』；与本句 no（没有）连用语义自相矛盾——无『压倒一切』的理由是把强调有理由的词放到了否定语境，明显别扭。
questions.hint: 根据空格前后的词性、搭配与上下文选择词语；每个词最多使用一次。

questions.prompt: my daughter __(33)__ cried
questions.shortExplanation: 事情发生太快太懵，孩子几乎没来得及哭
questions.detailedExplanation:
【答案】 C) barely 副词

【词性槽】 主谓之间修饰动词 cried

【依据】 事情发生太快太懵，孩子几乎没来得及哭

上文 It was so fast and confusing 已经为此空铺垫——动作迅猛、孩子来不及反应。 barely cried 即『几乎没哭出声』，与『fast and confusing』因果连贯：还没反应过来， 父亲就追上抢回了孩子。

【竞争词】 L) presumably 推测语气与亲历叙述冲突

presumably 表『大概』，是写作者对未亲见之事的推测；但作者一家亲历整段，包括孩子的反应，无须推测，语气错位。

【易错】 最具迷惑性的错误词是 L) —— presumably 看似谨慎但叙述视角不对。副词组只剩 C/L 两个，presumably cried 也能勉强解为『大概哭了』，似乎留有余地；但本段是作者一家亲历，连孩子叫了别人孩子的名字这种细节都记得，没必要用『大概』。防坑：副词二选一时回看叙述视角——亲历用具体程度词（barely），未亲见才用推测词（presumably）。
questions.hint: 根据空格前后的词性、搭配与上下文选择词语；每个词最多使用一次。

questions.prompt: A __(34)__ of homeless people who generally know the other homeless in the area said they did not recognize the woman.
questions.shortExplanation: a network of homeless people 表『流浪者之间的人际网』 network of + 人群指『某群体的人际网络』，与定语从句 who generally know the other homeless in the area 完美呼应——彼此互相认识的群体正是『一张网』。
questions.detailedExplanation:
【答案】 I) network 名词

【词性槽】 冠词 A 与 of 短语之间的主语位置

【依据】 a network of homeless people 表『流浪者之间的人际网』 network of + 人群指『某群体的人际网络』，与定语从句 who generally know the other homeless in the area 完美呼应——彼此互相认识的群体正是『一张网』。

【竞争词】 D) dedication搭配与单复数都不对

dedication of homeless people 不构成英语习惯搭配；且 dedication 表抽象品质，与定语从句『相互认识』的群体属性无关。
questions.hint: 根据空格前后的词性、搭配与上下文选择词语；每个词最多使用一次。

questions.prompt: Each part of the episode was as haunting as it was __(35)__.
questions.shortExplanation: 与 haunting 同色调、共同收束恐怖基调
questions.detailedExplanation:
【答案】 O) terrifying 形容词

【词性槽】 as…as 比较结构后接形容词

【依据】 与 haunting 同色调、共同收束恐怖基调

haunting 意为『萦绕心头、挥之不去的（恐惧）』，与 terrifying（令人恐惧的）感情色彩一致——孩子被陌生人抱走这一段经历，既挥之不去又骇人。这个收尾与第二段 I couldn't shake the sense that in this country we always live at __(30)__ risk. 的恐惧基调一脉相承，是全文情感的回扣。

【竞争词】 G) incredible 词义模糊，色彩不齐

incredible 表『难以置信』，可褒可贬；与 haunting 的负面色调虽不冲突但不够对位，而 incredible 已在 30 题作为更精准的『难以估量的风险』所需。

H) indignant 对象错配

indignant 是『义愤的』，形容人或情绪，不修饰 episode（事件）。

J) overriding 语义不搭

overriding 是『压倒一切的、最重要的』，an overriding episode 不成英语；与 haunting 也不构成同色调对应。
questions.hint: 根据空格前后的词性、搭配与上下文选择词语；每个词最多使用一次。

items.title: 2022年12月六级第1套 · 信息匹配
items.passage:
A) Michael Wardian pushed forward into the penetrating arctic(北极的) wind, fighting the urge to speed up. Too much effort and he'd begin to sweat, which, he was told, would only increase the risk of hypothermia(体温过低 ).

B) At the 2014 North Pole Marathon, the temperature dipped to minus-22 degrees F, with a wind chill that made it feel even colder. Along the route, armed guards wandered the large sheets of floating ice to minimize the risk of polar bear attacks.

C) "I like to do stuff that scares me," Wardian said. With ice frozen to his beard, Wardian crossed the finish line that April afternoon in a winning time of 4 hours 7 minutes and 40 seconds, almost two hours slower than his personal best over 26.2 miles. The race for Wardian, however, was less about the result than overcoming his aversion to the cold.

D) In a few days, Wardian will once again compete in an unfamiliar territory and below-freezing temperatures. He will line up Monday in Antarctica( 南极 ) for the first leg of the World Marathon Challenge—joining 32 other adventure seekers on an unusual journey where participants travel through different time zones and climates to run seven marathons on seven continents in seven days.

E) An elite ultra-runner, Wardian has his sights on breaking the event's record average marathon time of 3:32:25 set last January by U.S. Marine Corps captain Daniel Cartica. Wardian, a 42-year-old Arlington resident, is a record-breaking racer, known in the ultra-running community for seeking tough courses and setting world records. Last year, he ran 1,254.65 miles in 47 races. The World Marathon Challenge, like most of Wardian's running goals, will be about pushing his limits. "I love diverse and unique challenges," he said. "I'm definitely interested in seeing what I can handle and what my body can accept. That drives me."

F) Something about the way Richard Donovan carried himself appealed to Wardian. Perhaps it was the sense of adventure Donovan displayed when they first met at the 2010 50K Championships in Galway, Ireland, where Donovan was the race director. The two hit it off, and soon Wardian was participating in Donovan's events. It was at the North Pole Marathon, a race that Donovan organizes, that Wardian first heard about the Irishman's plan for the World Marathon Challenge—a challenge that Donovan himself completed in 2009 and 2012. "I knew that many people had a goal of running seven marathons on seven continents during any time period," Donovan, 50, said. "I felt the natural extension to this idea would be to try to achieve it within a seven-day period."

G) Wardian started saving for the trip in 2014, connecting with sponsors and getting approval from his wife, Jennifer, before committing. Registration for the event costs 36,000 euros, which covers international charter flights to each of the seven marathon locations: Union Glacier (Antarctica), Punta Arenas, Chile (South America), Miami (North America), Madrid (Europe), Marrakesh, Morocco (Africa), Dubai (Asia) and Sydney (Australia). The challenge is a test of both physical strength and mental fitness. Sleeping on a crammed plane, adjusting to different time zones and finding food to eat (Wardian is a vegetarian) would make it an exhausting trip over a month, let alone a week. "The key to a race like this is getting comfortable being uncomfortable," said Becca Pizzi, last year's women's champion. "The highs of the race are incredibly high, and the lows incredibly low."

H) Since turning it into an organized event in 2015, Donovan has attracted a variety of runners. This year's challenge will feature a far more elite field, which includes Ryan Hall, America's fastest marathon runner. Despite his proven track record, Hall said he has no time goals and that he still suffers from the same fatigue issues that forced him to leave the professional ranks in 2015. Hall plans to run with his friend, Pastor Matthew Barnett of The Dream Center in Los Angeles—one of the six American men who will be competing. "I don't expect to run a step with Mike, but I will be excited to see how he does," said the 34-year-old Hall, who began weight-lifting after retiring. "If I finish within an hour of him in each marathon, I'd be surprised."

I) Instead, 43-year-old Petr Vabrousek, an elite Czech Ironman champion, is expected to be Wardian's closest challenger. To others on the trip, simply finishing will be its own reward. Sinead Kane of Ireland is aiming to become the first blind person to complete the challenge. And Beth Ann Telford, a 47-year-old federal government worker from Fairfax and the only American female in this year's mix, is using the event as a platform to raise money for cancer research. It's a cause with a personal connection to Telford, who was diagnosed with brain cancer in 2004. "Doing something like this is definitely the hardest challenge that I've ever done except for the chemotherapy and brain surgery," she said. "It's going to raise awareness. …I just wanted to do something that is epic and this certainly is right up there." Wardian, too, hopes his involvement will give him a platform to promote a cause. He recently became an ambassador for the United Nations Women's HeForShe initiative to fight inequalities faced by women and girls worldwide.

J) On a chilly December afternoon, Wardian wove through Washington's crowded sidewalks on the way home from his full-time job as an international ship broker. His elastic, 6-foot frame bounced gently and efficiently off the ground with each step of the hilly six-mile trip back to Arlington. This is a daily routine during the week for Wardian, who started racing professionally in 2003 and runs seven days a week, often multiple times a day. When he travels, he prefers to explore new places on his feet.

K) But in some ways, Wardian still has trouble thinking of himself as a runner. For the majority of his childhood, Wardian devoted his energy to becoming a Division I lacrosse( ⻓曲棍球 ) player-a dream he realized when he was recruited to play at Michigan State University. "Once he decides to do something, he just works at it until he does it," Michael's younger sister, Mariele, said. "Once he decides to do it, it's usually something that's going to happen. He's always been like that. He's a very motivated individual."

L) It was only a year or so ago that Wardian realized that he had been a runner longer than a lacrosse player. It was not until he ran in the 2004 U.S. Olympic Marathon Trials-the first of three for Wardian-that he felt that he was a legitimate runner. Now more than 10 years and numerous ultra-marathon national titles and world records later, he embraces that identity. Wardian wants to see how far his legs can take him, one epic challenge at a time. "I want to always keep doing things that are exciting, adventurous, different and most importantly, probably things I'm not the best at," Wardian said, "because if you're not seeking things out that are challenging and difficult for you, then you're not growing … So I hope maybe people see what I do, and say, 'Okay, I want to do something different or try something new. … I'm going to do something that scares me.' That's what I'm hoping people will take from it."

questions.prompt: Wardian regards the various extraordinary challenges as a test of his physical endurance
questions.shortExplanation: 把各种非凡挑战当作身体耐力的测试
questions.detailedExplanation:
【答案】 E 段（弱锚点）

【锚点】 把各种非凡挑战当作身体耐力的测试

【定位】 I love diverse and unique challenges, he said. I'm definitely interested in seeing what I can handle and what my body can accept. That drives me.

「我热爱多样而独特的挑战，」他说，「我非常想看看自己能扛多少、身体能接受到什么程度。这正是驱动我前进的东西。」

【改写】 the various extraordinary challenges ↔ diverse and unique challenges 形容词同义词替换

a test of his physical endurance ↔ seeing what I can handle and what my body can accept 动词短语被概括为抽象名词（名词化）

【辨邻】 L L段的核心是if you're not seeking things out that are challenging and difficult for you, then you're not growing——是「成长论」而非「身体耐力测试论」，话题相邻但命题方向不同。 I want to always keep doing things that are exciting, adventurous, different and most importantly, probably things I'm not the best at

K K段焦点在Once he decides to do something, he just works at it until he does it ——这是「决心-执行力」的评价，与「身体耐力测试」无关。 Once he decides to do something, he just works at it until he does it
questions.hint: 先定位陈述句中的人物、数字或关键词，再比较原文同义表达。

questions.prompt: Wardian hopes his participation in the seven-day marathon series will contribute to a worthy cause.
questions.shortExplanation: 希望以七日赛参与为公益事业出力
questions.detailedExplanation:
【答案】 I 段（弱锚点）

【锚点】 希望以七日赛参与为公益事业出力

【定位】 Wardian, too, hopes his involvement will give him a platform to promote a cause. He recently became an ambassador for the United Nations Women's HeForShe initiative to fight inequalities faced by women and girls worldwide. items.title: 2022年12月六级第1套 · 仔细阅读 · 第一篇
items.passage:
Many people associate their self-worth with their work. The more successful their career, the better they feel about themselves. Work-related self-esteem is therefore a worthy ideal to pursue with vigor, right? Well, not always. According to recent research, in which psychologists interviewed 370 full-time workers over a period of three weeks, the reality is a little more complicated. And it involves negative as well as positive consequences.

It's natural to be drawn towards pleasure and to step away from pain. In the workplace, if that pleasure comes from a triumph which swells our self-respect, people will try to repeat the accomplishment. But repeating that accomplishment is often not realistic, which can lead to severe negative emotional consequences when it doesn't reoccur. This form of motivation is widely regarded as a negative type of motivation. It can hinder other more positive motivation types, such as completing a task purely because it's fulfilling or enjoyable.

What consumes the employee instead is a pressing need to feel mighty and sure of themselves. They then take on only tasks and objectives which serve that ego-driven need. As a result, to avoid feelings of shame and worthlessness associated with failure, they extend themselves to such a degree that there's a subsequent adverse effect on their well-being. This internal pressure to succeed at all costs demands a lot of effort. It depletes their energy, culminating in disproportionate levels of damaging sentiment.

Those negative emotions mount into heightened anxiety, impacting their ability to make the most of their personal life. Their desire to avoid feeling inferior ends up making them feel inferior when it comes to their diminished capacity for friendship and leisure. They end up dissatisfied both at work and outside of it.

But thankfully, for those people compelled almost entirely by this specific form of motivation, the news isn't all bad, or bad at all. The study also discovered several positive outcomes that can actually outweigh the harmful ones. Though these types of employees are motivated by the desire to avoid negative consequences, they are also motivated by the excitement of pursuing emotional rewards. This excitement makes pursuing goals enjoyable and stimulates pleasure and pride that would result from success. An effect of the positive motivation is that it neutralizes the existence of negative motivation.

Sure, it affects people's personal lives to what could be deemed an unhealthy extent, because leisure activities are often seen as a part of life that must be sacrificed to manage work and family demands. However, the way people feel about their work has less to do with whether they're motivated by the preservation of self-esteem but more with the fact that they're simply motivated.

questions.prompt: What does the author say about the pursuit of work-related self-esteem?

options.text: It may result in negative motivation.

questions.shortExplanation: Work-related self-esteem is therefore a worthy ideal to pursue with vigor, right? Well, not always. According to recent research, in which psychologists interviewed 370 full-time workers over a period of three weeks, the reality is a little more complicated. And it involves negative as well as positive consequences.
questions.detailedExplanation:
【答案】 A （细节题）

【判型】 What does the author say about the pursuit of work-related self-esteem 直接问作者对某话题的陈述，没有 infer/imply，需要回到原文找到该话题的明确表态句。

【拆句】 题干主干 What does the author say about... 是 wh- 疑问句，about 后接介宾 the pursuit of work-related self-esteem，结构平铺直叙，无陷阱。

【定位】 Work-related self-esteem is therefore a worthy ideal to pursue with vigor, right? Well, not always. According to recent research, in which psychologists interviewed 370 full-time workers over a period of three weeks, the reality is a little more complicated. And it involves negative as well as positive consequences.

于是工作型自尊就是一个值得全力追求的理想，对吗？嗯，并非总是如此。根据一项让心理学家在三周内访谈 370 名全职员工的近期研究，现实要更复杂一些。它既牵涉正面后果，也牵涉负面后果。

【选项】 A) ✓ 正确 involves negative as well as positive consequences ↔ It may result in negative motivation 预判的负面后果在 negative motivation 中被精确收口为研究真正定义的负面后果类型 ——动机层面的负面，故锁定 A。

B) 与原文相反 It contributes to one's accomplishments 把 a worthy ideal to pursue with vigor 当成作者真实观点，但作者立刻用 not always 否定了这种乐观说法。

C) 偷换概念 It can increase one's vigor as one keeps trying 把原文中描述追求方式的 with vigor 改造成追求会增加 vigor，混淆 vigor 作方式状语与作宾语的角色。

D) 过度推断 It costs too much emotionally and psychologically 给出 too much 的程度判断， 但首段仅说 involves negative as well as positive consequences，并未将代价定性为过高。

Pursuit of goals affects people's personal lives to an unhealthy extent.

questions.shortExplanation: However, the way people feel about their work has less to do with whether they're motivated by the preservation of self-esteem but more with the fact that they're simply motivated.
questions.detailedExplanation:
【答案】 D （推断题）

【判型】 What can we infer from the last paragraph 明示 infer，定位段已锁尾段，要求基于尾段明示信息做一步推断。

【拆句】 题干主干 What can we infer，from the last paragraph 是介词短语作状语指出推断的依据来源，结构简单。

【定位】 However, the way people feel about their work has less to do with whether they're motivated by the preservation of self-esteem but more with the fact that they're simply motivated.

然而，人们对工作的感受真正取决于的，与其说是他们是否被维护自尊的渴望所驱动，不如说是他们到底有没有被驱动这件事本身。

【选项】 A) 偷换概念 Workers have to make sacrifices to preserve self-esteem 把 leisure activities are often seen as a part of life that must be sacrificed to manage work and family demands 中牺牲闲暇的目的改成 preserve self-esteem，目的错位。

B) 与原文相反 Self-esteem swells when workers are strongly motivated 把因果说成动机强则自尊膨胀，但原文 has less to do with whether they're motivated by the preservation of self-esteem 反而弱化了自尊在因果链里的地位。 C) 以偏概全 Pursuit of goals affects people's personal lives to an unhealthy extent 把 Sure, it affects people's personal lives to what could be deemed an unhealthy extent 这一让步分句当作尾段主结论，但 However 之后才是作者真正立场。

D) ✓ 正确 the way people feel about their work has less to do with whether they're motivated by the preservation of self-esteem but more with the fact that they're simply motivated

↔ People feel positive about their work as long as they are motivated 预判中的有动机即正向感受被 as long as they are motivated 完整收拢，且 positive 与文章正向 good news 区段的态度一致，故锁定 D。
questions.hint: 回到原文定位题干关键词，比较选项与原文的含义。

items.title: 2022年12月六级第1套 · 仔细阅读 · 第二篇
items.passage:
Degradation of the world's natural resources by humans is rapidly outpacing the planet's ability to absorb the damage, a recent UN environmental study has found. The study concludes that without radical action the level of prosperity that millions of people in the developed world count on will be impossible to maintain or extend to poorer countries.

Water scarcity is the curse of some of the poorest regions on Earth, leaving developing countries increasingly unable to feed themselves, and causing hardship for millions of people. There appears little prospect of this desperate situation being remedied without radical action being taken. Water resources are under increasing threat from population growth, climate change, rapid urbanization, rising levels of consumption, and the degradation of lands that previously provided a natural replenishment( 补充 ) of water resources.

The rate of damage to the natural environment was found to increase globally, despite concerted efforts to persuade government to take measures to improve the condition. "If current trends continue, and the world fails to improve patterns of production and consumption, then the state of the world's environment will continue to decline," warned UN executive director Achim Steiner.

He said the tools for improving the environment for millions of people existed in developed countries, but were in danger of not being used.

The study found that basic measures to tackle some of the key causes of environmental damage were still not being taken. These included measures to reduce air pollution; to control the damage to marine ecosystems, which can have a huge effect on fish stocks on which hundreds of millions of people depend; and to curb the degradation of land where modern agricultural methods were pursued without regard to the longer-term consequences.

Despite the recent global agreement on cutting greenhouse gas emissions, global carbon output continues to rise. This will put a long-term strain on the ability of developing economies to feed their own people. Climate change is aggravated by the emissions of greenhouse gases from chemical and natural fertilisers used in agriculture which increased by more than a quarter between 2000 and 2010. Other problem areas identified in the report included glaciers, which provide vital water resources for millions of people, but which are shrinking as the climate warms.

In rich countries, these problems have built up over decades and centuries while economic growth was pursued at the expense of the environment. Subsequent efforts to remedy the environment have met with partial success. But in developing countries, the path of future development has more potential to change, which has encouraged international institutions to devise more sustainable growth pathways that are supposed both to alleviate poverty and preserve the environment.

questions.prompt: What is the major finding of the UN environmental study?

options.text: Human activity has rendered Mother Earth almost uninhabitable.
Humans are doing more damage to the earth than it can cope with.
Environmental problems have considerably weakened human prosperity.
Environmental damage is more serious in developed countries these days.

questions.shortExplanation:
【答案】 B （主旨题）

【判型】 题干 What is the major finding of the UN environmental study? 问的是研究的"主要发现"，对应全文的中心结论，而非局部细节。

【拆句】 What is the major finding of the UN environmental study? 是典型 wh-疑问句，主干 What is the major finding，of 短语修饰 finding，无从句、无否定，结构平铺直叙，无陷阱。
questions.detailedExplanation:
【答案】 B （主旨题）

【判型】 题干 What is the major finding of the UN environmental study? 问的是研究的"主要发现"，对应全文的中心结论，而非局部细节。

【拆句】 What is the major finding of the UN environmental study? 是典型 wh-疑问句，主干 What is the major finding，of 短语修饰 finding，无从句、无否定，结构平铺直叙，无陷阱。

【选项】 A) 无中生有 Mother Earth almost uninhabitable 说地球"几乎不宜居住"，原文只说破坏速度超过吸收能力，并未提到地球已濒临不宜居住的程度。

B) ✓ 正确 Degradation of the world's natural resources by humans is rapidly outpacing the planet's ability to absorb the damage

↔ Humans are doing more damage to the earth than it can cope with 预判"破坏速度超过地球承受力"在 Humans are doing more damage to the earth than it can cope with 中以 more...than it can cope with 完整复现，是定位句的标准同义替换。 C) 偷换概念原文意思是"破坏超过吸收能力会使富国当前繁荣不可维持"——是"环境破坏会损害繁荣"的预言；Environmental problems have considerably weakened human prosperity 改成"环境问题已经显著削弱了人类繁荣"，把未来的预警偷换成已发生的事实。

D) 无中生有 Environmental damage is more serious in developed countries these days 断言发达国家环境破坏更严重，原文从未做"发达国家 vs 发展中国家谁更严重"的横向比较，是无中生有的比较。
questions.hint: 回到原文定位题干关键词，比较选项与原文的含义。

questions.prompt: What is said about water scarcity in some of the poorest regions?

options.text: It is getting so serious that there is little hope of solution.
It largely accounts for their slow economic development.
It can hardly be relieved if no drastic measures are taken.
It is primarily caused by the acceleration of climate change.

questions.shortExplanation: There appears little prospect of this desperate situation being remedied without radical action being taken. 如果不采取激进行动，这种绝望的状况几乎没有得到改善的前景。
questions.detailedExplanation:
【答案】 C （细节题）

【判型】 题干 What is said about water scarcity in some of the poorest regions? 形式 "What is said about X"，问的是文中对 X 的具体陈述，是典型细节题。

【拆句】 What is said about water scarcity in some of the poorest regions? 被动语态，主干 What is said，about 介词短语带出讨论对象，in 短语限定范围；结构清楚、无陷阱。

【定位】 There appears little prospect of this desperate situation being remedied without radical action being taken. 如果不采取激进行动，这种绝望的状况几乎没有得到改善的前景。

【选项】 A) 过度推断原文是"不激进行动则无望"——前提是"如果不采取"，there is little hope of solution 把条件去掉、直接断言"几乎无解"，把有条件的判断推为无条件结论，过度推断。

B) 张冠李戴原文只说水资源短缺让发展中国家 increasingly unable to feed themselves, and causing hardship for millions of people，关心的是粮食与民生；It largely accounts for their slow economic development 转到"经济发展缓慢"上，原文未做此因果归因。

C) ✓ 正确 There appears little prospect of this desperate situation being remedied without radical action being taken

↔ It can hardly be relieved if no drastic measures are taken 预判"无激进行动→几乎无望解决"在 It can hardly be relieved if no drastic measures are taken 中以 hardly + if no...are taken 完整复刻，是定位句的标准同义重写。

D) 以偏概全原文罗列了 population growth, climate change, rapid urbanization, rising levels of consumption, and the degradation of lands 五个并列威胁因素；It is primarily caused by the acceleration of climate change 单挑"气候加剧"为主因，原文从未做此排序。
questions.hint: 回到原文定位题干关键词，比较选项与原文的含义。

questions.prompt: What does Achim Steiner say about the environmental condition?

options.text: It is being slowly remedied globally.
It will shrink the world's population.

questions.shortExplanation: If current trends continue, and the world fails to improve patterns of production and consumption, then the state of the world's environment will continue to decline.
questions.detailedExplanation:
【答案】 A （细节题）

【判型】 题干 What does Achim Steiner say about the environmental condition? 问具体人物对具体话题的具体陈述，属于事实细节，不是推断或主旨。

【拆句】 What does Achim Steiner say about the environmental condition? 主动语态特殊疑问句，主干 What does Achim Steiner say，about 短语带出陈述对象，无从句无否定，结构透明。

【定位】 If current trends continue, and the world fails to improve patterns of production and consumption, then the state of the world's environment will continue to decline.

如果当前趋势继续下去，世界又无法改善生产与消费模式，那么全球环境状况将持续恶化。

【选项】 A) ✓ 正确 the state of the world's environment will continue to decline ↔ It will deteriorate worldwide 预判"环境将持续恶化"在 It will deteriorate worldwide 中以 will deteriorate 保留 will 未来时态，worldwide 保留全球范围，整句结构紧贴定位句。

B) 无中生有 It is attracting global attention 说环境正吸引全球关注，原文 Steiner 引语只谈"将继续恶化"，未提全球对它的关注度。 C) 与原文相反 It is being slowly remedied globally 说环境正在被缓慢修复，与原文 the rate of damage to the natural environment was found to increase globally 及 Steiner 引语"将继续恶化"完全相反。

D) 无中生有 It will shrink the world's population 说环境状况会缩减世界人口，原文 Steiner 引语只字未提人口收缩。
questions.hint: 回到原文定位题干关键词，比较选项与原文的含义。

questions.prompt: What is the dilemma developing countries face?

options.text: They cannot modernise farming without causing land degradation.
They cannot promote industrialisation without polluting waterways.
They cannot boost crop yields without causing greenhouse gas emissions.
They cannot catch up with rich countries without sacrificing the environment.

questions.shortExplanation: This will put a long-term strain on the ability of developing economies to feed their own people. Climate change is aggravated by the emissions of greenhouse gases from chemical and natural fertilisers used in agriculture which increased by more than a quarter between 2000 and 2010. 这（碳排放上升）将长期压制发展中经济体养活本国人口的能力。气候变化又被农业中化肥 （化学与天然）所排放的温室气体所加剧——这类排放在 2000 到 2010 年间增长了超过四分之一。
questions.detailedExplanation:
【答案】 C （细节题）

【判型】 题干 What is the dilemma developing countries face? 问的是文中明确描述的具体两难，是文中实有陈述的细节，不是推理。

【拆句】 What is the dilemma developing countries face? 主干 What is the dilemma，后接省略关系代词的定语从句 (which/that) developing countries face 修饰 dilemma；基础薄弱考生易把 face 误解为名词"面孔"，须留意它在此是及物动词"面对"。

【定位】 This will put a long-term strain on the ability of developing economies to feed their own people. Climate change is aggravated by the emissions of greenhouse gases from chemical and natural fertilisers used in agriculture which increased by more than a quarter between 2000 and 2010. 这（碳排放上升）将长期压制发展中经济体养活本国人口的能力。气候变化又被农业中化肥 （化学与天然）所排放的温室气体所加剧——这类排放在 2000 到 2010 年间增长了超过四分之一。

【选项】 A) 张冠李戴 cannot modernise farming without causing land degradation 是"现代化农业导致土地退化"，原文第 5 段才提 curb the degradation of land where modern agricultural methods were pursued，但与本题第 6 段的"养人 vs 温室气体"两难是两个不同话题。

B) 无中生有 cannot promote industrialisation without polluting waterways 说"工业化必然污染水道"，原文未谈发展中国家工业化的两难，也未谈水道污染。

C) ✓ 正确 This will put a long-term strain on the ability of developing economies to feed their own people

↔ boost crop yields Climate change is aggravated by the emissions of greenhouse gases from chemical and natural fertilisers used in agriculture

↔ causing greenhouse gas emissions 预判"养人靠提产、提产致排放"在 They cannot boost crop yields without causing greenhouse gas emissions 中以 cannot...without... 双重否定形式把目的与代价绑成两难，与原文两面对应。

D) 偷换概念 cannot catch up with rich countries without sacrificing the environment 说"追赶富国必牺牲环境"，这是 P7 谈"富国曾以环境换增长"的引申、且原文 P7 的态度是发展中国家"有潜力改变路径"——选项把 P7 的论点反向化，又错放进本题两难。
questions.hint: 回到原文定位题干关键词，比较选项与原文的含义。

questions.prompt: What should developing countries do in their future development according to the passage?

options.text: They turn to developed countries for the assistance they need.
They remedy environmental damage by slowing economic growth.
They avoid damaging interference from international institutions.
They improve people's livelihood without harming the environment.

questions.shortExplanation: But in developing countries, the path of future development has more potential to change, which has encouraged international institutions to devise more sustainable growth pathways that are supposed both to alleviate poverty and preserve the environment.
questions.detailedExplanation:
【答案】 D （细节题）

【判型】 题干 What should developing countries do in their future development according to the passage? 明确要 according to the passage，问文中给出的具体建议，是细节题不是推断。

【拆句】 What should developing countries do in their future development according to the passage? 情态动词疑问句，主干 What should developing countries do，in 短语限定时间范围，according to 短语指明答题依据；结构清晰无陷阱。

【定位】 But in developing countries, the path of future development has more potential to change, which has encouraged international institutions to devise more sustainable growth pathways that are supposed both to alleviate poverty and preserve the environment.

但在发展中国家，未来发展的路径有更大的可改变潜力，这促使国际机构设计了更可持续的发展路径——既要减贫，又要保护环境。

【选项】 A) 无中生有 turn to developed countries for the assistance they need 说"向发达国家求援"，原文 P7 只说国际机构"设计了可持续路径"，未提向发达国家求援。

B) 与原文相反 remedy environmental damage by slowing economic growth 说"靠放缓经济增长来修补环境"，但原文 P7 提的 sustainable growth pathways 是"既减贫又护环境"—— 发展与环保并行，不是减速换环保。 C) 与原文相反 avoid damaging interference from international institutions 说"避开国际机构的破坏性干预"，但原文 P7 has encouraged international institutions to devise more sustainable growth pathways 中国际机构是建设性角色——选项把它颠倒成"破坏性"。

D) ✓ 正确 alleviate poverty↔ improve people's livelihood preserve the environment↔ without harming the environment 预判"减贫与护环境兼顾"在 They improve people's livelihood without harming the environment 中以 improve...without harming 双动作并列承接 both...and 结构，是 P7 对策句的标准同义改写。
questions.hint: 回到原文定位题干关键词，比较选项与原文的含义。

items.title: 2022年12月六级第2套 · 选词填空
items.passage:
The task of the global strategist of a business is to build a platform of capabilities derived from the resources, experiences and innovations of units operating in multiple locations, to transplant those capabilities wherever [26] _____ , and then to systematically upgrade and renew them—ahead of the competition.

Apple is an outstanding case of a company whose unique capabilities give it a worldwide [27] _____ advantage, particularly with respect to its ability to build platforms from a product base that integrates functional and [28] _____ design. Apple has been able to leverage and exploit its California-based design and marketing advantages successfully throughout the world. IKEA is another such case. The do-it-yourself furniture and houseware company first developed a compelling set of capabilities to design, manufacture and [29] _____ furniture at low cost and sell it in a novel way in Sweden. Later, IKEA successfully [30] _____ this formula in many other countries.

By contrast, Telefonica, a Spanish telecommunications company that is now the world's fifth largest telecom by [31] _____ , first developed its special advantage abroad. In 1989 and 1990, Telefonica had

the opportunity to enter Chile and Argentina, countries that shared many institutional and cultural characteristics with its home country but that were [32] _____ more rapid market reform. Throughout the 1990s, Telefonica took what it learned in Chile and Argentina about reconstructing former state-owned telecoms to other Latin American countries that were privatizing their state telecoms and deregulating their telecom markets.

These examples might lead the reader to believe that creating a global advantage is an easy task. But many other [33] _____ of expensive failed experiments suggest that creating a lasting global advantage actually requires a great deal of [34] _____ and operational finesse(技巧). Our research suggests that global winners typically create and sustain their international presence through a systematic process of [35] _____ , renewing and enhancing their core capabilities.

questions.prompt: to transplant those capabilities wherever __(26)__, and then to systematically upgrade and renew them
questions.shortExplanation: wherever appropriate 是英文公文/学术死搭配 wherever appropriate（在合适的地方/凡合适之处）是英文公文与学术写作的经典短语， 与上文"把那些能力移植到合适的地方"的全球战略逻辑完美匹配。
questions.detailedExplanation:
【答案】 B) appropriate 形容词

【词性槽】 wherever + __ 让步从句省略

【依据】 wherever appropriate 是英文公文/学术死搭配 wherever appropriate（在合适的地方/凡合适之处）是英文公文与学术写作的经典短语， 与上文"把那些能力移植到合适的地方"的全球战略逻辑完美匹配。

【竞争词】 A) aesthetic 话题错

wherever aesthetic 在语义上无意义；本句讲战略选址，不是审美判断。

F) fiscal 话题错

wherever fiscal 不构成英文表达；fiscal 修饰 year/policy 等具体名词，不用作"地点合适与否"的判断。
questions.hint: 根据空格前后的词性、搭配与上下文选择词语；每个词最多使用一次。

questions.prompt: Apple is an outstanding case of a company whose unique capabilities give it a worldwide __(27)__ advantage
questions.shortExplanation: competitive advantage 是商科死搭配全文在讨论企业如何打造全球优势（to build a platform of capabilities ... ahead of the competition），competitive advantage（竞争优势）是商业战略文献中的高频固定搭配，与上文 ahead of the competition 形成完美呼应。
questions.detailedExplanation:
【答案】 D) competitive 形容词

【词性槽】 名词 advantage 前的定语位

【依据】 competitive advantage 是商科死搭配全文在讨论企业如何打造全球优势（to build a platform of capabilities ... ahead of the competition），competitive advantage（竞争优势）是商业战略文献中的高频固定搭配，与上文 ahead of the competition 形成完美呼应。

【竞争词】 A) aesthetic 义域偏窄、与 advantage 不搭

aesthetic advantage（美学优势）不是固定搭配，且本句讲的是 Apple 在全球的整体优势，不是单指美学；A 留给下文真正讨论 design 的空。

B) appropriate appropriate advantage 不成立

appropriate 修饰 advantage 在语义上别扭——"恰当的优势"无意义；它的典型搭配是 wherever appropriate / appropriate measures。

F) fiscal话题不对

fiscal 指财政/财务的，全文没有讨论税收或财政政策，与本句"独特能力带来的优势"语义无关。

M) strategic 义近但被下文锁定

strategic advantage 虽勉强通，但 M 在第 34 空有更刚性的固定搭配 strategic and operational finesse；按"先难后易"原则，本空让位、把 M 留给 34。
questions.hint: 根据空格前后的词性、搭配与上下文选择词语；每个词最多使用一次。

questions.prompt: its ability to build platforms from a product base that integrates functional and __(28)__ design
questions.shortExplanation: functional 与 aesthetic 是设计学经典对子
questions.detailedExplanation:
【答案】 A) aesthetic 形容词

【词性槽】 functional and __ design 并列形容词

【依据】 functional 与 aesthetic 是设计学经典对子

在工业设计领域，functional（功能性）和 aesthetic（美学性）是描述产品设计的两大维度——前者管用，后者好看；Apple 正以"功能+美学"的双轨设计闻名于世，与本句精准契合。

【竞争词】 F) fiscal话题完全错

fiscal design（财政设计）不构成英文搭配，也与 functional 不在同一维度——一个讲产品属性、一个讲税收政策，明显风马牛不相及。

【易错】 最具迷惑性的错误词是 F) —— fiscal 词性对、话题完全错。integrates functional and __(28)__ design 中，F fiscal 是形容词、词性匹配；陷阱在于"functional and fiscal"听起来好像在讲企业的两条线，容易让人误填。防坑：functional 是产品设计属性，应与 aesthetic 构成设计学经典对子；记住 functional/aesthetic 这对就不会误选 fiscal。
questions.hint: 根据空格前后的词性、搭配与上下文选择词语；每个词最多使用一次。

questions.prompt: a compelling set of capabilities to design, manufacture and __(29)__ furniture at low cost
questions.shortExplanation: ship furniture 是"运输/发货"动词
questions.detailedExplanation:
【答案】 L) ship 动词

【词性槽】 动词不定式三个并列动作

【依据】 ship furniture 是"运输/发货"动词

ship 作动词义为"发货、运输"，与 design（设计）、manufacture（生产）构成宜家从生产到出货的完整产业链；ship furniture（发货家具）是英语商业语境的自然搭配。

【竞争词】 N) transcend 义不对路

transcend furniture（超越家具）在语义上荒谬；transcend 通常接抽象名词（limits、 boundaries），与"低成本生产家具"的产业链逻辑完全脱节。
questions.hint: 根据空格前后的词性、搭配与上下文选择词语；每个词最多使用一次。

questions.prompt: Later, IKEA successfully __(30)__ this formula in many other countries.
questions.shortExplanation: reproduced this formula = 复制这一套打法
questions.detailedExplanation:
【答案】 I) reproduced 动词

【词性槽】 主语 + 副词 + __ + 宾语，过去式谓语位

【依据】 reproduced this formula = 复制这一套打法

reproduce a formula / model / pattern 在英语里指"在别处复制同一套做法"，与上文"先在瑞典打造能力、再到许多其它国家"的逻辑严丝合缝；与 overview 中"transplant capabilities wherever appropriate"主旨完全一致。

【竞争词】 H) rehabilitated 义不对路

rehabilitate 意为"使（人/建筑/制度）恢复、改造"，宾语通常是受损或失效之物；this formula （一套成功打法）并未受损，无需"康复"，逻辑不通。
questions.hint: 根据空格前后的词性、搭配与上下文选择词语；每个词最多使用一次。

questions.prompt: Telefonica, a Spanish telecommunications company that is now the world's fifth largest telecom by __(31)__
questions.shortExplanation: by revenues 商业排名固定表达
questions.detailedExplanation:
【答案】 J) revenues 名词

【词性槽】 by + __ 名词位

【依据】 by revenues 商业排名固定表达

world's Nth largest company by revenues（按营收排名世界第 N 大公司）是英美商业报道的高频固定句式，与"全球电信公司排名"语境精准契合。

【竞争词】 C) clusters 搭配错

by clusters（按群/簇）不是衡量公司大小的维度，逻辑不通。

E) exploiting 义不对路

the world's fifth largest telecom by exploiting（按开发利用排名）讲不通；E 后文有刚性搭配 a systematic process of exploiting, renewing and enhancing。

K) safeguarding 义不对路

by safeguarding（按保卫）同样不是排名维度，话题完全脱钩。
questions.hint: 根据空格前后的词性、搭配与上下文选择词语；每个词最多使用一次。

questions.prompt: countries that shared many institutional and cultural characteristics with its home country but that were __(32)__ more rapid market reform
questions.shortExplanation: undergoing reform 经历改革的标准表达 undergo reform / undergo change 是"经历某种变革"的固定搭配；本段讲智利和阿根廷"正在经历更快速的市场改革"，O 在词义和搭配上同时命中。
questions.detailedExplanation:
【答案】 O) undergoing 动词

【词性槽】 were + __ 后接宾语，构成现在进行体

【依据】 undergoing reform 经历改革的标准表达 undergo reform / undergo change 是"经历某种变革"的固定搭配；本段讲智利和阿根廷"正在经历更快速的市场改革"，O 在词义和搭配上同时命中。

【竞争词】 E) exploiting 主体不对

国家"利用"市场改革（exploiting market reform）在语义上不通；exploiting 的主语通常是企业/人，且 E 在第 35 空有刚性并列结构。

K) safeguarding 义反

safeguarding reform（保卫改革）与全文"加速改革、私有化国有电信"的语境逻辑相反——国家是在推进改革，不是在防卫改革。
questions.hint: 根据空格前后的词性、搭配与上下文选择词语；每个词最多使用一次。

questions.prompt: But many other __(33)__ of expensive failed experiments suggest that ...
questions.shortExplanation: instances of failed experiments 自然搭配
questions.detailedExplanation:
【答案】 G) instances 名词

【词性槽】 many other __ of … 复数名词位

【依据】 instances of failed experiments 自然搭配

instances of（…的实例/例子）是英语常用搭配；上一段以 Apple、IKEA、Telefonica 为正面例子，这里转折说"还有许多其他（失败的）实例"，逻辑无缝衔接。

【竞争词】 C) clusters搭配不成立 + 语义错位

clusters of experiments（实验簇）在英语中不是惯用搭配；clusters 通常修饰 stars、cells、 companies 等，不指"案例的合集"。

J) revenues 义不对路

revenues of expensive failed experiments（昂贵失败实验的收入）逻辑荒谬，且 J 在第 31 空有死搭配 by revenues。
questions.hint: 根据空格前后的词性、搭配与上下文选择词语；每个词最多使用一次。

questions.prompt: creating a lasting global advantage actually requires a great deal of __(34)__ and operational finesse(技巧 )
questions.shortExplanation: strategic 与 operational 是经典并列 strategic and operational（战略与运营层面）是管理学经典对子；全文反复用 the global strategist、systematic process（our research suggests that global winners typically create and sustain their international presence through a systematic process），话题精准锁定 strategic。
questions.detailedExplanation:
【答案】 M) strategic 形容词

【词性槽】 并列结构 a great deal of __ and operational

【依据】 strategic 与 operational 是经典并列 strategic and operational（战略与运营层面）是管理学经典对子；全文反复用 the global strategist、systematic process（our research suggests that global winners typically create and sustain their international presence through a systematic process），话题精准锁定 strategic。

【竞争词】 A) aesthetic 话题错位

aesthetic 属设计/审美范畴，与 operational 不构成对子；本段讲的是"持久全球优势的运营要求"，不是设计美学。

B) appropriate 义偏空泛

a great deal of appropriate（大量恰当的）与 and operational 并列在语义上失衡，且 appropriate 在第 26 空有刚性搭配。

F) fiscal 话题不对

fiscal 指财政，全文未讨论财政与运营的二分，是话题外干扰。
questions.hint: 根据空格前后的词性、搭配与上下文选择词语；每个词最多使用一次。

questions.prompt: global winners typically create and sustain their international presence through a systematic process of __(35)__, renewing and enhancing their core capabilities.
questions.shortExplanation: exploiting, renewing and enhancing 进取三连
questions.detailedExplanation:
【答案】 E) exploiting 动词

【词性槽】 of + __, renewing and enhancing 三个动名词并列

【依据】 exploiting, renewing and enhancing 进取三连

exploit one's capabilities（开发/善用既有能力）+ renew（更新）+ enhance（增强）构成对核心能力的三段式进取式动作链，正对应 overview 强调的"打造-移植-升级"主旨；且与第二段 Apple 段的 exploit 用词遥相呼应。

【竞争词】 K) safeguarding 语义指向不对

safeguarding（保卫）属于防御性动作，与 renewing、enhancing 这两个进取性动作不在同一向量上；全文论调是"主动打造并升级全球优势"，不是"防卫既有能力"，K 是话题外干扰。

【易错】 最具迷惑性的错误词是 K) —— safeguarding 词性形态全对、唯方向反。a systematic process of __(35)__, renewing and enhancing their core capabilities 中，K safeguarding 的 -ing 形与介词 of 完全匹配，"保卫核心能力"中文读起来也顺；陷阱在于它与 renewing/enhancing 这两个进取动作方向相反。防坑：并列动词读三遍"V1, V2, V3"，看情感/方向是否同向，发现 safeguarding 一守二攻立即剔除。
questions.hint: 根据空格前后的词性、搭配与上下文选择词语；每个词最多使用一次。

items.title: 2022年12月六级第2套 · 信息匹配
items.passage:
A) What do we lose when natural spaces and species disappear? Increasingly, research has shown that as species and ecosystems vanish, it also chips away at our ability to preserve what remains—because we no longer understand what we're losing.

B) You probably see it all the time. The neighbor who puts pesticides on his lawn rather than deal with annoying bees. The politician who votes against wildlife protection because she's never seen a wolf in the wild. The corporation that wants to bulldoze(⽤推⼟机推平 ) the habitat of a rare frog.

C) At best this can be termed "the extinction of experience," where our cultural and natural histories fade from our memories and therefore our reality. At its worst it becomes something even more concerning: "biophobia," the fear of living things and a complete aversion to nature.

D) This isn't the fiction of living in a cold, empty dystopia(绝望的世界). Sadly, it's becoming a way of life for too many people—especially children. A recent study in Japan paints a striking portrait of this problem. A survey of more than 5,300 school children in the Tochigi Prefecture examined their perception of 14 local insect species and one spider. The results? A collective "ew!" Most of the students saw the species as things to dislike or fear, or even as sources of danger. The less experience the students had with nature, the more negative their feelings.

E) The results were published earlier this year in the journal Biological Conservation. Lead researcher Masashi Soga with the University of Tokyo says the study stemmed from observations about today's nature-deficient children. "Humans inherently avoid dangerous organisms such as bees, but children these days avoid even harmless insects such as butterflies and dragonflies(蜻蜓)," he says. "I have long wondered why so many of today's children react like this."

F) Although the children's reactions were somewhat expected, the new study did contain an unexpected finding: Many of the surveyed children revealed that their parents also expressed fear or disgust of the same animals. In fact, these parental emotions were strong enough to overwhelm any positive experiences the children might have gained from direct experiences in nature. As Soga and his coauthors wrote in their paper, "Our results suggest that there is likely a feedback loop in which an increase in people who have negative attitudes towards nature in one generation will lead to a further increase in people with similar attitudes in the next generation."

G) And that's possibly the greater threat posed by extinction of experience. Soga suggests the generational loss—condition previously dubbed environmental generational amnesia(遗忘)—could chip away at our societal ability to preserve what we're losing. "I believe that increased biophobia is a major, but invisible, threat to global biodiversity," Soga says. "As the number of children who have biophobia increases, public interest and support for biodiversity conservation will gradually decline. Although many conservation biologists still consider that preventing the loss of wildlife habitat is the most important way to conserve biodiversity, I think preventing increased biophobia is also important for conservation."

H) What's to be done about this? The paper makes several recommendations, the most obvious of which is that children should experience nature more often. The authors also suggest establishing policies to guide these natural experiences and increasing educational programs about the natural world.

I) Helping parents to see species around them in a new light would make a difference, too. And, of course, maintaining support for preserving the wild spaces where these "scary" creatures live is the most important thing of all. That's a point reinforced by another recent study, which found that wild spaces located within urban areas—and the plants and animals that thrive in them—are particularly important for human health and well-being.

J) Published in the journal Frontiers in Sustainable Cities, the study examined attitudes toward Discovery Park, the heavily forested 534-acre public park in Seattle, Washington. It found that the public had the most appreciation for—and gained the most value from—the wildest parts of the park. "I have seen whales, seals, fish, eagles, shorebirds and many other sea creatures in their natural habitat," one survey participant wrote. "Coming here with people has allowed me to connect and talk with them about conversation that simply does not happen in everyday life," wrote another.

K) The participants reported that their most valuable experiences in the park included encountering wildlife, walking through open spaces, exploring the beach and finding beautiful views. "We saw that a large majority of participants' interactions, especially their most meaningful interactions, depended on Discovery Park's relative wildness," says lead author Elizabeth Lev, a master's student in the University of Washington's Human Interaction with Nature Lab. This is only possible because the park is relatively wild. After all, you can't enjoy watching birds if there are no birds to follow, gaze at the sunset if it's obscured by skyscrapers, or stop and smell the flowers if they don't have room to grow.

L) And yet even this long-protected space could someday become less hospitable to nature. Over the past few years a lot of people and organizations have suggested developing parts of Discovery Park or the neighboring area. Most recently a plan proposed building 34 acres of much-needed affordable housing and parking spaces adjacent to the park, bringing with them noise, traffic and pollution.

M) If anything like that happened, both the park and the people of Seattle could lose something vital. And that would continue the trend of chipping away at Seattle's—and the world's—natural spaces, leaving just tiny pocket parks and green-but-empty spaces that offer little real value to wildlife, plants or people.

N) "It is true that any interaction with nature is better than none, but I don't want people to be satisfied with any small bit of grass and trees," Lev says. "We have been in this cycle of environmental generational amnesia for a long time, where the baseline keeps shifting and we don't even realize what we're losing until it's gone. If we can get people to understand how much meaning and value can come from having more experiences with more wild forms of nature, then maybe we can stop this cycle and move toward conserving and restoring what we have left."

O) Building this understanding in an ever-more fearful and disconnected world may be the biggest challenge. Peter Kahn, the senior author of Lev's paper and the director of the Human Interaction with Nature lab, made several suggestions for bridging this gap in this 2011 book, Technological Nature. They echo the recommendation about getting children into nature, but also include telling stories of how things used to be, imagining what things might be like in the future, and developing a common language about nature, "a way of speaking about wild and domestic interaction patterns, and the meaningful, deep and often joyful feelings that they generate."

P) No matter what techniques we use, this growing field of research illustrates that saving nature requires encouraging people to experience it more often and more deeply. That calls for additional research—Lev and her coauthors have published a toolkit that other municipalities can follow to study the value of their own wild spaces—and clear communication of the results. "If we can continue to show people the benefits of these wild spaces," Lev says, "maybe people will begin to see more value in keeping these areas undeveloped—for the sake of our mutual benefit."

许多受访的孩子透露，他们的父母对同样这些动物也表达了恐惧或厌恶。事实上，这些父母的情绪强到足以盖过孩子从自然中亲身获得的任何正面体验。

their parents also expressed fear or disgust of the same animals aversion=fear or disgust 的概括

would pass on to their children ↔

there is likely a feedback loop in which an increase in people who have negative attitudes towards nature in one generation will lead to a further increase in people with similar attitudes in the next generation pass on=代际反馈循环的概括

【辨邻】 L L 段 Most recently a plan proposed building 34 acres of much-needed affordable housing and parking spaces adjacent to the park 是提案描述，后果判断的源头是 M 段 both the park and the people of Seattle could lose something vital，因此 L 不是 Q43 源头。 bringing with them noise, traffic and pollution

items.title: 2022年12月六级第2套 · 仔细阅读 · 第一篇
items.passage:
Some people in the US have asserted that forgiving student loan debt is one way to stimulate the economy and give assistance to those in need. One government proposition is to eliminate $10,000 of debt for 'economically distressed' students. Some in US Congress have gone so far as to suggest forgiving up to $50,000 in debt per student borrower, but does forgiving student debt necessarily correlate to helping the economically disadvantaged?

The answer is no. This policy is just giving money away to universities and the most affluent students in attendance. Federal Reserve data reveals that the highest-income 40 percent of households owe approximately 60 percent of outstanding student debt, while the lowest 40 percent owe just under 20 percent. This could be due to a combination of factors: students from high-income households are more likely to go to expensive colleges, less likely to receive financial aid, and more likely to have high incomes post-graduation. Plus, the majority of student debt is held by graduate degree earners, who earn approximately 25 percent more than their undergraduate counterparts. Clearly, giving free reign to banks to forgive student debt is a step in the wrong direction.

Other proposals for broader, long-term student loan plans have some fundamental problems. One idea is to cancel student debt only for undergraduate degrees and for students making less than $125,000.

This attempts to address the fact that Congress' previously mentioned student loan forgiveness plan largely helps out the wealthy, but is an adverse incentive for universities to keep raising tuition and for students to choose to major in low-earning degree programs. Colleges have no reason to make their programs more affordable if they believe students will just take out more debt. And, students will feel more comfortable making the irresponsible decision to go tens of thousands of dollars in debt to major in impractical or idealistic subjects if they know their loans will be forgiven.

This is especially concerning given the pandemic(⼤流⾏病 ) has rendered a college education practically worthless. Students are paying tens of thousands of dollars per year to live at home and be lectured on the Internet. Do we really want to tell colleges that they can get away with providing below-average service for an outrageous cost?

In the case of any of these student debt plans, working-class Americans who chose not to or could not afford to go to college will be subsidizing the education of the professional class. Plumbers and retail workers will be paying for the degrees of doctors and lawyers.

The US government's effort to help those in debt is commendable but is this really the solution that will help the poor financially recover?

questions.prompt: Why do some people advocate forgiving student loan debt?

options.text: They assert it will narrow the gap between the wealthy and the poor.
They believe it will benefit both the economy and the underprivileged.
They claim it will eliminate economic distress among college students.
They think the cost of education is the responsibility of the government.

questions.shortExplanation: Some people in the US have asserted that forgiving student loan debt is one way to stimulate the economy and give assistance to those in need.
questions.detailedExplanation:
【答案】 B （细节题）

【判型】 Why do some people advocate forgiving student loan debt? 直接问 "为何主张"，要求回原文找其陈述的理由，属事实陈述题。

【拆句】 题干为标准 Why 引导的特殊疑问句，主谓宾结构清晰：主语 some people，谓语 advocate，宾语动名词短语 forgiving student loan debt，无从句、无否定、无陷阱。

【定位】 Some people in the US have asserted that forgiving student loan debt is one way to stimulate the economy and give assistance to those in need.

美国一些人主张：免除学生贷款债务是刺激经济、为困难人群提供援助的一种方式。

【选项】 A) 过度推断原文只说 give assistance to those in need，并未说 narrow the gap between the wealthy and the poor——"帮助困难者" 不等于 "缩小贫富差距"。

B) ✓ 正确 stimulate the economy ↔ benefit ... the economy give assistance to those in need ↔ benefit ... the underprivileged 预判要求同时覆盖 "经济" 与 "弱势群体"，B 用 both the economy and the underprivileged 并列结构精准对应定位句的并列宾语，是唯一双满足项。 C) 偷换概念原文 economically distressed 只是 "被免债 1 万美元" 的资格描述，并未声称免债能 eliminate economic distress among college students。 D) 无中生有原文未出现 the cost of education is the responsibility of the government 这一表述，主张方只谈 "免债" 这一具体动作，未上升到 "教育成本应由政府承担" 的责任归属。
questions.hint: 回到原文定位题干关键词，比较选项与原文的含义。

questions.prompt: What do we learn from the Federal Reserve data?

options.text: Approximately 60% of student debt remains unpaid.
Cancelling student debt benefits wealthy families most.
Forgiving student debt provides little benefit to universities.
Low-income families owe the biggest amount of student debt.

questions.shortExplanation: This policy is just giving money away to universities and the most affluent students in attendance. Federal Reserve data reveals that the highest-income 40 percent of households owe approximately 60 percent of outstanding student debt, while the lowest 40 percent owe just under 20 percent.
questions.detailedExplanation:
【答案】 B （细节题）

【判型】 What do we learn from the Federal Reserve data? 问 "我们从某数据得知什么"，要求复述数据所支持的具体结论，属客观信息检索。

【拆句】 Wh- 疑问句，what 作宾语前置，"learn from" 为搭配，from 后接信息来源；句式简洁无修饰。

【定位】 This policy is just giving money away to universities and the most affluent students in attendance. Federal Reserve data reveals that the highest-income 40 percent of households owe approximately 60 percent of outstanding student debt, while the lowest 40 percent owe just under 20 percent.

该政策不过是把钱白送给大学和在读的最富有学生。美联储数据显示：收入最高的 40% 家庭欠下了大约 60% 的未偿学贷，而收入最低的 40% 仅欠不到 20%。

【选项】 A) 偷换概念原文 60% 指 outstanding student debt 中由高收入家庭持有的比例，并非 Approximately 60% of student debt remains unpaid——"未偿" 在原文里是 outstanding（仍欠着），但 60% 修饰的是高收入家庭占比而非未偿率。 B) ✓ 正确 giving money away to universities and the most affluent students in attendance ↔

Cancelling student debt benefits wealthy families most the highest-income 40 percent of households owe approximately 60 percent of outstanding student debt

↔ wealthy families 数据要证明 "消债是给富人送钱"，B 把这一结论用 benefits wealthy families most 复述，是唯一锁定 "受益者方向" 的选项。

C) 与原文相反原文 giving money away to universities 明示大学正是免债的受益方，C 项却说 Forgiving student debt provides little benefit to universities，与原文截然相反。

D) 与原文相反原文 the lowest 40 percent owe just under 20 percent 明确说低收入家庭只欠不到 20%，D 项称 Low-income families owe the biggest amount of student debt，方向完全反向。

questions.prompt: What does the author say students are likely to do if they know they needn't repay their loans?

options.text: They will choose to study subjects without considering their job prospects.
They will be free to pursue their goals without being burdened financially.
They will over-borrow and live beyond their means.
They will be able to enroll in expensive universities.

questions.shortExplanation: And, students will feel more comfortable making the irresponsible decision to go tens of thousands of dollars in debt to major in impractical or idealistic subjects if they know their loans will be forgiven.
questions.detailedExplanation:
【答案】 A （细节题）

【判型】 What does the author say students are likely to do 问的是作者所言，要求复述作者在原文对该情形下学生行为的明确说法，属直接陈述题。

【拆句】 复合疑问句：主句 What does the author say，宾语从句 students are likely to do， 后跟条件状语从句 if they know they needn't repay their loans；需把 if-从句视为情景前提。

【定位】 And, students will feel more comfortable making the irresponsible decision to go tens of thousands of dollars in debt to major in impractical or idealistic subjects if they know their loans will be forgiven.

并且，如果学生知道自己的贷款将被免除，他们会更安心地做出不负责任的决定——为了主修不实用或理想化的专业而背上数万美元的债务。

【选项】 A) ✓ 正确 major in impractical or idealistic subjects ↔

study subjects without considering their job prospects major in ↔ study subjects 把 impractical / idealistic 翻译为 "不考虑就业" 这一行为机制，是定位句到 A 项的唯一等值路径；其余三项均跳出此语义域。

B) 与原文相反原文将这一行为定性为 the irresponsible decision（不负责任的决定），B 项却美化为 be free to pursue their goals without being burdened financially（自由追求目标、 不受经济负担），态度方向完全相反。 C) 偷换概念原文谈的只是 major in impractical or idealistic subjects 选专业行为；C over-borrow and live beyond their means 把话题扩到 "超支度日" 的生活方式，越界。

D) 无中生有原文未提学生因免债 enroll in expensive universities 报昂贵学校的行为，借贷增多与 "昂贵大学" 没有原文支持。

questions.prompt: What does the author imply about colleges offering online education?

options.text: They cannot get away with the serious consequences.
They have suffered greatly from the current pandemic.
The tuition they charge is not justified by the quality of their service.
The tuition they charge has surged outrageously during the pandemic.

questions.detailedExplanation:
【答案】 C （推断题）

【判型】 What does the author imply about colleges offering online education? 中 imply 明示作者并未直说，需要从其用词与反问句推断态度。

【拆句】 Wh- 疑问句嵌 about 介词短语：主干 What does the author imply，宾语 about colleges offering online education，offering 为现在分词作定语；无陷阱。

【定位】 Students are paying tens of thousands of dollars per year to live at home and be lectured on the Internet. Do we really want to tell colleges that they can get away with providing below-average service for an outrageous cost?

学生每年花费数万美元只为待在家里、通过网络听课。我们真的愿意告诉大学：它们可以一边收取离谱的费用、一边提供低于平均水平的服务，还安然无恙吗？

【选项】 A) 过度推断原文反问句 Do we really want to tell colleges that they can get away with ... ? 表达 "作者认为大学不该逃过去"，但 A 项 They cannot get away with the serious consequences 直接把 "逃不掉" 当作论点，作者只是质问、并未陈述其事实结果，且 "serious consequences" 系原文未提的后果维度。

B) 张冠李戴原文 Students are paying tens of thousands of dollars per year，受害方是学生，B 却把 "受害" 戴给大学：They have suffered greatly from the current pandemic，主语与原文相反。 C) ✓ 正确 below-average service for an outrageous cost ↔

The tuition they charge is not justified by the quality of their service outrageous cost ↔ the tuition they charge 反问句的反义即 "学费不应换来低于平均的服务"，C 用 not justified by the quality of their service 把这一态度客观化，是唯一锁定 "价质不匹配" 的选项。

D) 无中生有原文只说学费 "离谱"（outrageous），未说它 has surged outrageously during the pandemic 在大流行期间 "飙涨"；时间维度的涨幅描述无原文支撑。

Working-class students will have increasing access to subsidized education.

Plumbers and retail workers will be paying for the degrees of doctors and lawyers. 无论这些学生贷款方案的哪一种实施，那些选择不上大学或负担不起大学的工薪阶层美国人都将在补贴专业阶层的教育。管道工和零售工将为医生和律师的学位埋单。

【答案】 C （细节题）

【判型】 What will happen if any of the proposed student debt plans is implemented? 问方案实施后的结果，原文有对应客观陈述句即可作答。

【拆句】 Wh- 疑问句加 if 条件状语：主句 What will happen，从句 if any of the proposed student debt plans is implemented，被动语态 is implemented 表 "被实施"；逻辑是 "实施→什么结果"。

【定位】 In the case of any of these student debt plans, working-class Americans who chose not to or could not afford to go to college will be subsidizing the education of the professional class. Plumbers and retail workers will be paying for the degrees of doctors and lawyers. 无论这些学生贷款方案的哪一种实施，那些选择不上大学或负担不起大学的工薪阶层美国人都将在补贴专业阶层的教育。管道工和零售工将为医生和律师的学位埋单。

【选项】 A) 与原文相反原文谈的是 working-class Americans 要补贴别人，而非 "获得成为专业阶层的机会"； A Plumbers and retail workers will have a chance of becoming professionals 把方向反过来，让他们成为受益人。

B) 与原文相反原文 working-class Americans who chose not to or could not afford to go to college 强调工薪阶层不上大学，B 说 Working-class students will have increasing access to subsidized education，把不上大学的工薪阶层反向描述为 "上大学且获补贴"。

C) ✓ 正确 Plumbers and retail workers↔ Blue-collar workers will be paying for the degrees of doctors and lawyers↔

will have to bear the cost of educating would-be high-earners 预判要求保留 "蓝领→白领" 的财政方向，C 用 Blue-collar workers 与 would-be high-earners 把双方上位化后保留方向，是唯一忠实复述者。 D) 答非所问原文谈的是 "谁为这些学位埋单" 的财政分配，而非 A growing number of students will be able to earn degrees in medicine and law 这种 "医法学位人数增加" 的供给变化，未对应题干 What will happen 所问的方案后果。
