items.title: 2022年12月六级第2套 · 仔细阅读 · 第二篇
items.passage:
If there's one rule that most parents cling to in the confusing, fast-changing world of kids and media, it's "No screens before age 2."

As of today, that rule has been thrown out the window.

The American Academy of Pediatrics (AAP), which first issued that recommendation back in 1999, has extensively updated and revised its guidelines for children and adolescents to reflect new research and new habits.

The new guidelines, especially for very young children, shift the focus from WHAT is on the screen to WHO else is in the room. And in doing so, they raise some intriguing points about the future of learning from media.

For babies younger than 18 months, AAP still says no screens at all are the best idea—with one notable exception: Live video chat. Surveys indicate that families already popularly believe that "Face time doesn't count", or at least that the benefit of virtual visits with grandparents or other relatives outweighs the potential cost of exposing babies to the laptop or smartphone.

The AAP doesn't cite positive evidence that infants actually get something out of this kind of "conversation", the way that they clearly do from live social interaction. But there's some observational research that infants as young as six months old are emotionally engaged by playing live peekaboo(躲猫猫) with Grandma online.

For infants and toddlers(学步⼉童), ages 15 months to 2 years old, there's limited evidence from a couple of very small studies that they can learn new words from educational media, if and only if parents are watching alongside them, repeating what the video says and/or drawing attention to what is on the screen. In other words, treating a video or an app like a picture book is the best bet.

The flip side of this is that many studies have actually shown poorer language skills correlated with earlier solo viewing of "educational" videos. There's also research that shows language delays in children who watch more TV and start watching earlier. In both cases, the problem seems to be media replacing interaction with people. For this reason, the new AAP guideline has changed from "avoid all screens under age 2" to "avoid solo media use in this age group."

For preschoolers ages 2 to 5, there's more evidence that they have the ability to transfer knowledge from screens to the real world, including early literacy and math. For this age group, AAP recommends no more than an hour a day of screen use. And, just as with younger children, they want care-givers to take part in screen time: "Co-view with your children, help children understand what they are seeing, and help them apply what they learn to the world around them."

questions.prompt: What do we learn about the "No screens under 2" rule?

options.text: It has met more and more resistance from parents.
It has proved helpful to children's healthy growth.
It confuses parents with regard to kids' education.
It has been discarded in line with recent research.

questions.shortExplanation: As of today, that rule has been thrown out the window.
questions.detailedExplanation:
【答案】 D （细节题）

【判型】 题干 What do we learn about the "No screens under 2" rule? 指向一个具体规则的现状/命运，不含 infer/imply/mainly about，属于围绕特定对象核对事实的典型细节题。

【拆句】 题干主干 What do we learn about the "No screens under 2" rule，是 learn about + 对象的常规疑问句；引号内的 No screens under 2 是省略 be 动词的口号式标题，全句结构平铺直叙，无陷阱。

【定位】 As of today, that rule has been thrown out the window.

从今天起，那条规则已被扔出窗外（即被彻底弃用）。

【选项】 A) 无中生有 met more and more resistance from parents 在原文中找不到对应；rule that most parents cling to 反而显示家长一直紧抱旧规则，与"抵制"相反。 B) 无中生有 proved helpful to children's healthy growth 在原文中无对应；原文只是说家长一直奉行该规则，并未给出"该规则被证明对孩子健康有益"的证据。

C) 张冠李戴 confuses parents with regard to kids' education 把"令家长困惑"扣在旧规则头上； 但原文 in the confusing, fast-changing world of kids and media 中 confusing 形容的是"kids and media 这个世界"，不是 No screens under 2 这条规则——这是典型的张冠李戴。

D) ✓ 正确 that rule has been thrown out the window ↔ It has been discarded extensively updated and revised its guidelines... to reflect new research ↔

in line with recent research 预判落点"被弃用/依据新研究"两个要素，正好分别对应 discarded 与 in line with recent research，D 是定位句与紧邻背景句的整合同义替换。
questions.hint: 回到原文定位题干关键词，比较选项与原文的含义。

questions.prompt: What do the new AAP guidelines advocate?

options.text: Young children should be accompanied by parents during screen time.
Parents should be emotionally involved in their children's upbringing.
Young children should watch videos carefully selected by parents.
Parents should protect their children from too much media exposure.

questions.shortExplanation:
【答案】 A （主旨题）

【判型】 题干 What do the new AAP guidelines advocate? 不指向某一条具体规则，而是问 new AAP guidelines 整体在主张什么，需要把全文若干段拼起来才能回答，属于局部主旨题。

【拆句】 题干 What do the new AAP guidelines advocate? 是 what 作宾语的常规疑问句，主语 new AAP guidelines、谓语 advocate；唯一需要留意 advocate 的语义
questions.detailedExplanation:
【答案】 A （主旨题）

【判型】 题干 What do the new AAP guidelines advocate? 不指向某一条具体规则，而是问 new AAP guidelines 整体在主张什么，需要把全文若干段拼起来才能回答，属于局部主旨题。

【拆句】 题干 What do the new AAP guidelines advocate? 是 what 作宾语的常规疑问句，主语 new AAP guidelines、谓语 advocate；唯一需要留意 advocate 的语义指向"主张/提倡"， 不是"批评/警示"。

【选项】 A) ✓ 正确 if and only if parents are watching alongside them ↔

accompanied by parents during screen time Co-view with your children ↔ accompanied by parents during screen time they want care-givers to take part in screen time ↔

accompanied by parents during screen time 预判要点"父母陪同孩子用屏"在 P7 P9 至少三处同义表述同时成立，A 项一句话覆盖这条主线，是新指南的整体主张。

B) 过度推断 emotionally involved in their children's upbringing 把范围从"屏幕时间陪伴"扩到"整体育儿过程"；本文限定话题在"屏幕/媒体使用"，不涉及通用育儿建议。 C) 与原文相反 videos carefully selected by parents 强调父母"挑选视频内容"，与 shift the focus from WHAT is on the screen to WHO else is in the room 明确告示的方向相反—— 新指南要的是 WHO（有谁陪），不是 WHAT（挑什么内容）。

D) 以偏概全 protect their children from too much media exposure 偏向"控制屏幕时间总量"，确实贴近 P8 与 P9 的"一小时上限/避免独看"，但只是 P9 的局部要点之一；它没覆盖贯穿全文的 co-view 主线，作为整体主张以偏概全。
questions.hint: 回到原文定位题干关键词，比较选项与原文的含义。

questions.prompt: What do families think of live video chat according to surveys?

options.text: It should not be regarded as screen time.
It helps babies to develop their verbal skills.
It is not as harmful as playing games on laptops.
It is a good substitute for video viewing.

questions.shortExplanation: Surveys indicate that families already popularly believe that "Face time doesn't count", or at least that the benefit of virtual visits with grandparents or other relatives outweighs the potential cost of exposing babies to the laptop or smartphone.
questions.detailedExplanation:
【答案】 A （细节题）

【判型】 题干 What do families think of live video chat according to surveys? 指向一句调查结论，答案落在原文一两句话里，是典型细节题。

【拆句】 题干 What do families think of live video chat according to surveys? 主干为 What do families think of...，think of = "对……怎么看"；尾部 according to surveys 是状语，限定信息来源，不是 think 的宾语。

【定位】 Surveys indicate that families already popularly believe that "Face time doesn't count", or at least that the benefit of virtual visits with grandparents or other relatives outweighs the potential cost of exposing babies to the laptop or smartphone.

调查显示，许多家庭已经普遍相信"视频聊天不算（屏幕时间）"，或者至少认为与祖父母等亲属虚拟相见的好处大于让婴儿接触电脑或智能手机的潜在代价。

【选项】 A) ✓ 正确 "Face time doesn't count" ↔ It should not be regarded as screen time 预判落点是"家庭把视频聊天排除在屏幕时间之外"，A 恰好是这句话的书面化、完整化版本，是定位句的标准同义替换。

B) 张冠李戴原文 P5 没有说视频聊天帮助婴儿"发展语言能力"；emotionally engaged 给出的也是"情感投入"而非语言；P7 谈到 learn new words 但前提是 educational media+父母伴看，与 live video chat 是不同话题。 C) 无中生有 not as harmful as playing games on laptops 把视频聊天与"在笔记本上玩游戏"作比较，但原文 P5 只比较"虚拟探访的好处"与"接触手机的潜在代价"，从未把 video chat 与 playing games 放一起比较。

D) 无中生有 a good substitute for video viewing 把视频聊天说成"看视频的好替代品"，但 P5 只说家庭认为视频聊天"不算屏幕时间"，并未在视频聊天与看视频之间建立替代关系。
questions.hint: 回到原文定位题干关键词，比较选项与原文的含义。

questions.prompt: What do researchers find about kids solo viewing educational videos?

options.text: It arouses their interest in language learning.
It works no better than reading picture books.
It hampers their development of language skills.
It helps them acquire independent learning skills.

questions.shortExplanation: The flip side of this is that many studies have actually shown poorer language skills correlated with earlier solo viewing of "educational" videos.
questions.detailedExplanation:
【答案】 C （细节题）

【判型】 题干 What do researchers find about kids solo viewing educational videos? 指向一句研究结论，是典型细节题。

【拆句】 题干 What do researchers find about kids solo viewing educational videos? 主干 What do researchers find about X；about 的宾语 kids solo viewing educational videos 是"动名词复合结构"——solo viewing 作动名词中心，前面 kids 是逻辑主语，相当于"孩子独自观看教育视频"这一行为。

【定位】 The flip side of this is that many studies have actually shown poorer language skills correlated with earlier solo viewing of "educational" videos.

另一方面，许多研究实际上已经表明，过早地独自观看"教育"视频与较差的语言能力相关。

【选项】 A) 与原文相反 arouses their interest in language learning 原文未提兴趣，且原文方向是"独看伴随更差语言能力"，与"激发兴趣"方向相反。

B) 偷换概念 works no better than reading picture books 把 treating a video or an app like a picture book is the best bet 错读为"二者效果一样"；原文是"把视频当绘本来读才是最佳做法"，并未说"独看视频和读绘本一样"。 C) ✓ 正确 poorer language skills correlated with earlier solo viewing of "educational" videos ↔

It hampers their development of language skills 原文 poorer skills correlated with solo viewing 等同于"独看与语言能力变差相关"，C 的 hampers 正是这一负向相关的动词化表达。

D) 无中生有 helps them acquire independent learning skills 把"独看"硬扯成"获得自主学习能力"；原文不仅未提及自主学习，反而把 solo 与负向后果绑定。
questions.hint: 回到原文定位题干关键词，比较选项与原文的含义。

questions.prompt: What does the author say about preschoolers ages 2 to 5?

options.text: They can understand pretty well what they see on the screen.
They can learn on their own without much parental guidance.
They can make use of educational videos to develop digital literacy.
They can relate what they learn on the screen to real life situations.

questions.shortExplanation: For preschoolers ages 2 to 5, there's more evidence that they have the ability to transfer knowledge from screens to the real world, including early literacy and math.
questions.detailedExplanation:
【答案】 D （细节题）

【判型】 题干 What does the author say about preschoolers ages 2 to 5? 指向作者对一个具体人群的具体陈述，可在某一段内得到完整答案，是细节题。

【拆句】 题干 What does the author say about preschoolers ages 2 to 5? 主干 What does the author say about X；ages 2 to 5 是 preschoolers 的同位修饰语，等价于 who are 2 to 5 years old，结构平铺直叙，无陷阱。

【定位】 For preschoolers ages 2 to 5, there's more evidence that they have the ability to transfer knowledge from screens to the real world, including early literacy and math.

对于 2 到 5 岁的学龄前儿童而言，有更多证据表明他们能够把从屏幕上学到的知识迁移到现实世界，包括早期识字与数学能力。

【选项】 A) 偷换概念 understand pretty well what they see on the screen 与原文 help children understand what they are seeing 中的"理解"措辞相近，但原文这句是 AAP 对父母的"建议"——要父母帮孩子理解，并非"孩子已经能理解"的事实结论。

B) 与原文相反 learn on their own without much parental guidance 与原文 they want care-givers to take part in screen time 直接相反——原文强调要父母参与，B 项说不需要父母指导。

C) 偷换概念 develop digital literacy 把原文 early literacy and math 中的"早期识字"偷换为"数字素养"——early literacy 指儿童的识字、阅读能力，与 digital literacy（数字素养/媒介使用能力）不是一回事。

D) ✓ 正确 transfer knowledge from screens to the real world ↔

relate what they learn on the screen to real life situations 预判要点"屏上所学应用到现实"，D 用 relate to real life situations 准确还原 transfer to the real world，是定位句的同义替换。
questions.hint: 回到原文定位题干关键词，比较选项与原文的含义。

items.title: 2022年12月六级第3套 · 选词填空
items.passage:
American colleges and universities are using 64 percent less coal than they did a decade ago, burning 700,000 tons last year, down from 2 million tons in 2008, the U.S. Energy Information Administration (EIA) said in a report [26] _____ yesterday.

All 57 schools that were burning coal in 2008 are using less now, and 20 have [27] _____ coal completely, EIA found.

Most universities have turned to natural gas as a [28] _____ , with state funding backing the fuel switch.

While academic institutions use less than 0.1 percent of U.S. coal burned for power, campus coal use has a history dating back to the 1800s when [29] _____ to power was scarce.

Many universities still operate their own power plants. The Public Utility Regulatory Policies Act of 1978 encouraged more electricity generation by allowing institutions to sell [30] _____ power to utilities.

But EIA noted many coal-fired universities have signed onto the American College and University Presidents Climate Commitment, which was launched in 2007.

About 665 schools are part of the program, which aims to [31] _____ greenhouse gas emissions. Thirty percent of the participants have pledged to be carbon [32] _____ within 20 years.

The Sierra Club's Beyond Coal campaign, which also leads campaigns for universities to withdraw their [33] _____ in coal and other fossil fuels, lists 22 schools that have pledged to move "beyond coal," including Clemson University, Indiana University, Ohio University, Penn State University, the University of Louisville and the University of Tennessee, Knoxville.

The largest coal use [34] _____ at colleges were in Michigan, Missouri, Tennessee and Indiana. Indiana's universities alone cut coal [35] _____ by 81 percent between 2008 and 2015.

During the same period, Michigan made an 80 percent cut and Tennessee cut back by 94 percent at state institutions.

questions.prompt: the U.S. Energy Information Administration (EIA) said in a report __(26)__ yesterday.
questions.shortExplanation: release a report = 发布报告，是固定搭配
questions.detailedExplanation:
【答案】 K) released 动词

【词性槽】 「a report ___ yesterday」report 后修饰、yesterday 锁过去时 → 过去分词作后置定语

【依据】 release a report = 发布报告，是固定搭配

said in a report __(26)__ yesterday 中 release a report（发布报告）是新闻语篇里的典型搭配，与「EIA 昨天发布的一份报告里说……」语义完全咬合。

【竞争词】 G) mobilized mobilize a report 不通

mobilize 与「人力、资源、军队」搭，从不修饰 report；语义上「动员一份报告」也讲不通。
questions.hint: 根据空格前后的词性、搭配与上下文选择词语；每个词最多使用一次。

questions.prompt: All 57 schools that were burning coal in 2008 are using less now, and 20 have __(27)__ coal completely
questions.shortExplanation: 「彻底放弃燃煤」与全文「减煤」主线完全吻合 20 have __(27)__ coal completely 与 American colleges and universities are using 64 percent less coal than they did a decade ago 形成程度递进——大多数学校少用，20 所 「彻底放弃」。abandon coal 是脱煤议题的高频表达。
questions.detailedExplanation:
【答案】 A) abandoned 动词

【词性槽】 「have ___ coal completely」现在完成时缺过去分词

【依据】 「彻底放弃燃煤」与全文「减煤」主线完全吻合 20 have __(27)__ coal completely 与 American colleges and universities are using 64 percent less coal than they did a decade ago 形成程度递进——大多数学校少用，20 所 「彻底放弃」。abandon coal 是脱煤议题的高频表达。

【竞争词】 G) mobilized 「动员了煤炭」与「停用煤炭」方向相反

mobilize 意为「动员、调动」，have mobilized coal completely 等于「已经把煤完全动员起来用」，与「彻底放弃」截然相反，逻辑错位。

K) released release coal 不通且与上下文矛盾

release coal 不是常用搭配（release 多与 report、information、emissions 搭），且与「使用」无关；后续 26 题更需要 released 来搭配 report，此处不应抢用。

【易错】 最具迷惑性的错误词是 K) —— released 词性形态都对，最易抢走 27 题。have ___ coal completely 处 K)released 形态完全合规，且 release 在新闻语体里高频；但 release coal 不是自然搭配，且 26 题 a report ___ yesterday 才是 released 的归属。考生若不按「先易后难、用过即划」的顺序，容易把 K 提前用到 27 题、导致 26 题再也找不到合适的过去分词。防坑：先做 26 题（因为 a report released yesterday 的搭配更硬），把 K 划走，27 题就自然落到 abandoned 上。
questions.hint: 根据空格前后的词性、搭配与上下文选择词语；每个词最多使用一次。

questions.prompt: Most universities have turned to natural gas as a __(28)__, with state funding backing the fuel switch.
questions.shortExplanation: 「转向天然气作为替代品」语义最贴
questions.detailedExplanation:
【答案】 L) replacement 名词

【词性槽】 不定冠词 a 后的空 → 单数名词

【依据】 「转向天然气作为替代品」语义最贴

Most universities have turned to natural gas as a __(28)__, with state funding backing the fuel switch. 句末 the fuel switch（这次燃料切换）直接点题——天然气是 「替代品」，replacement 与 fuel switch 形成同义复现。

【竞争词】 C) consumption 义指消耗量，与「替代」无关

consumption 表「消耗、消费」，turn to natural gas as a consumption 不通——天然气不是「一种消耗」，而是「煤的替代」。
questions.hint: 根据空格前后的词性、搭配与上下文选择词语；每个词最多使用一次。

questions.prompt: campus coal use has a history dating back to the 1800s when __(29)__ to power was scarce.
questions.shortExplanation: access to power = 用电的途径
questions.detailedExplanation:
【答案】 B) access 名词

【词性槽】 「__ to power was scarce」做主语，缺主语名词

【依据】 access to power = 用电的途径

campus coal use has a history dating back to the 1800s when __(29)__ to power was scarce 1800 年代「用电途径稀缺」，故学校自建煤电厂——语义和逻辑都通；access to 是六级听读写都常考的固定搭配。

【竞争词】 C) consumption consumption of/in，不与 to 搭配

consumption 后通常接 of，「consumption to power」不是英语习惯表达；语义上「电力消费稀缺」也讲不通，因为后文说要自建电厂正是为了「获取电」而非「消费电」。

F) investments 复数主语需 were，且 investments to power 不通

investments 是复数，与 was 不一致；且 investments in 才是常见搭配，「投资稀缺」也偏离 「为何要自建煤电厂」的因果。
questions.hint: 根据空格前后的词性、搭配与上下文选择词语；每个词最多使用一次。

questions.prompt: allowing institutions to sell __(30)__ power to utilities
questions.shortExplanation: surplus power = 剩余电力，正是发电后多余卖给电网的部分
questions.detailedExplanation:
【答案】 N) surplus 形容词

【词性槽】 「sell ___ power to utilities」名词 power 前需形容词修饰

【依据】 surplus power = 剩余电力，正是发电后多余卖给电网的部分

Many universities still operate their own power plants. The Public Utility Regulatory Policies Act of 1978 encouraged more electricity generation by allowing institutions to sell __(30)__ power to utilities. 大学自办电厂、鼓励多发电——多发出来的电只能是 「剩余的」，卖给公共电网（utilities），surplus 完美对应。

【竞争词】 O) void void power 语义错位

void 表「无效的、空的」，void power 字面意思偏向「无效电力 / 空的功率」，与「多发的电卖给电网」完全相反。
questions.hint: 根据空格前后的词性、搭配与上下文选择词语；每个词最多使用一次。

questions.prompt: About 665 schools are part of the program, which aims to __(31)__ greenhouse gas emissions.
questions.shortExplanation: slash emissions = 大幅削减排放，新闻语篇高频搭配
questions.detailedExplanation:
【答案】 M) slash 动词

【词性槽】 「aims to ___ greenhouse gas emissions」不定式 to 后接动词原形

【依据】 slash emissions = 大幅削减排放，新闻语篇高频搭配

aims to __(31)__ greenhouse gas emissions 与下一句 pledged to be carbon __(32)__ within 20 years 形成「大幅削减 → 实现碳中和」的目标链；slash 表「大幅削减」，正是减排议题中比 reduce 更有力的词。

【竞争词】 D) contrive contrive 多接 to do，不直接带 emissions

contrive 表「谋划、设法做成」，常用结构是 contrive to do something，不接 emissions 这类名词宾语；语义上也偏「图谋、设计」，与减排目标不搭。

【易错】 最具迷惑性的错误词是 D) —— contrive 是动词原形、看似能填 to ___ 位。aims to __(31)__ greenhouse gas emissions 处 contrive 形态正合「to + 动词原形」，且词面冷僻、容易让考生「越冷越对」地误选；但 contrive 不能直接带 emissions 作宾语，语义也偏「图谋」。防坑：减排议题里 to + 动词 + emissions 几乎只配 cut/slash/reduce/curb 这一类「强削减动词」，背主题搭配最稳。
questions.hint: 根据空格前后的词性、搭配与上下文选择词语；每个词最多使用一次。

questions.prompt: Thirty percent of the participants have pledged to be carbon __(32)__ within 20 years.
questions.shortExplanation: carbon neutral = 碳中和，正是减排承诺的目标
questions.detailedExplanation:
【答案】 I) neutral 形容词

【词性槽】 「to be carbon ___ within 20 years」处在不定式 be 的表语位置

【依据】 carbon neutral = 碳中和，正是减排承诺的目标

About 665 schools are part of the program, which aims to __(31)__ greenhouse gas emissions. Thirty percent of the participants have pledged to be carbon __(32)__ within 20 years. 上一句讲削减温室气体排放，下一句承诺「20 年内 carbon ___」——只有 neutral 能与 carbon 组成减排议题的核心术语，对应「净零排放」。

【竞争词】 H) negligent 义为「玩忽职守」，与碳排话题不搭

negligent 指人疏忽、失职，从不与 carbon 搭配，语义方向也与「减排承诺」相反。

N) surplus 「碳过剩」不是承诺目标

carbon surplus 一来不是固定术语，二来「碳过剩」是要避免的问题，而非「pledged to be」 的对象。

O) void 「carbon void」非术语、且 void 多与 of 连用

void 作形容词常说 void of/null and void，与 carbon 不构成减排领域的固定搭配，意思也与 「碳中和」对不上。
questions.hint: 根据空格前后的词性、搭配与上下文选择词语；每个词最多使用一次。

questions.prompt: campaigns for universities to withdraw their __(33)__ in coal and other fossil fuels
questions.shortExplanation: withdraw investments in fossil fuels = 撤资行动
questions.detailedExplanation:
【答案】 F) investments 名词

【词性槽】 「withdraw their ___ in coal」中物主代词 their 后 + 介词 in，必为名词

【依据】 withdraw investments in fossil fuels = 撤资行动

campaigns for universities to withdraw their __(33)__ in coal and other fossil fuels 与 Beyond Coal 运动一致，呼吁大学从化石燃料中「撤资」——withdraw investments in 是经济议题的固定搭配，复数 investments 也与 their 自然搭配。

【竞争词】 C) consumption 「撤回消费」语义怪

withdraw their consumption in coal 不是英语习惯说法；且后文 22 所高校宣布「move beyond coal」是从资本层面撤离，不只是减少使用。

J) reductions 「撤回削减」逻辑反了

reductions 指「削减」，withdraw their reductions 等于「撤回削减」，与全文主旨完全相反 ——campaigns 的目的不是阻止削减，而是推动撤资以加速脱煤。
questions.hint: 根据空格前后的词性、搭配与上下文选择词语；每个词最多使用一次。

questions.prompt: The largest coal use __(34)__ at colleges were in Michigan, Missouri, Tennessee and Indiana.
questions.shortExplanation: the largest coal use reductions = 最大的煤炭使用削减量 The largest coal use __(34)__ at colleges were in Michigan, Missouri, Tennessee and Indiana. 与下文 Indiana's universities alone cut coal __(35)__ by 81 percent 同义复现 ——「削减幅度最大的州」与「印第安纳州削减 81%」对应，reductions 与 cut 是同根名动呼应。
questions.detailedExplanation:
【答案】 J) reductions 名词

【词性槽】 「The largest coal use ___ at colleges were in Michigan...」主语缺名词中心，谓语 were 提示复数

【依据】 the largest coal use reductions = 最大的煤炭使用削减量 The largest coal use __(34)__ at colleges were in Michigan, Missouri, Tennessee and Indiana. 与下文 Indiana's universities alone cut coal __(35)__ by 81 percent 同义复现 ——「削减幅度最大的州」与「印第安纳州削减 81%」对应，reductions 与 cut 是同根名动呼应。

items.title: 2022年12月六级第3套 · 信息匹配
items.passage:
A) In 1913, classical music sparked a riot in Paris. Igor Stravinsky was introducing his revolutionary "Rite of Spring" ballet to the world, with its discordant melodies and unorthodox choreography(编舞 ), and the purists in the crowd expressed their disapproval loud and clear. It might have been classical music's version of the time Bob Dylan went electric at the Newport Folk Festival. "The noise, fighting, and shouting in the audience got so loud," NPR's music reporter Miles Hoffman said of the Stravinsky debut, "that the choreographer had to shout out the numbers to the dancers so that they knew what they were supposed to do."

B) It's difficult to imagine a similar disturbance occurring today within America's sacred symphony halls. In fact, it's hard to picture any kind of disruptive activity at all (unless someone's cell phone happens to go off, and then you'd better watch your back). A mannerly aura(氛围 ) hangs over most classical proceedings, and many of the genre's biggest supporters would have it no other way.

C) Today, Western audiences for classical music and opera and ballet are almost always well dressed, older, respectful, achingly silent and often very wealthy (one has to be able to afford most tickets). But as many of America's most storied "highbrow"(⾼ 雅的 ) institutions struggle financially—the Philadelphia Orchestra's much-publicized rebound from bankruptcy is just one recent example— classical music fans and theorists are wondering how the medium can weave itself into the 21st century's cultural fabric without sacrificing its integrity.

D) For example, should we feel OK "clapping" during classical music events, even if nobody else is? Why shouldn't we cheer for something great, like we do at a rock concert? The Huffington Post recently ran a Great Debate on this issue and many commenters came out on the side of silence. "There is no more rewarding experience in life than being part of an audience where everybody is leaning forward in silence, thoroughly carried away by a great performance of a masterpiece," one commenter wrote. "Why is it so difficult for folks to develop an appreciation and understanding for the mannerisms and traditions of classical music?" asked another.

E) The truth is that classical music audiences weren't always so polite. Robert Greenberg, an award-winning composer, said that when Beethoven first performed his 7th Symphony, audiences forced the orchestra to perform encores( 重演 ) of certain movements immediately, applauding wildly. And in the last few decades, he said, many audiences at opera performances have abandoned pretenses, yelling "Bravo" when they feel like it.

F) "I don't think there's anything wrong with an audience showing their enthusiasm for a proper moment by applauding, showing their joy," Greenberg said, noting that the stuffiness in concert halls is "one aspect of contemporary concert etiquette" he doesn't understand. "Instead of waiting half an hour to show enthusiasm, why not show it every eight or nine minutes?"

G) Until the rules about behavior and clothing change, it's hard to imagine multitudes of young people filling concert halls on their own accord. They're probably more likely to head to Central Park to watch a free performance with a bottle of wine and their friends. "I think anyone should be able to come into a performance dressed any way they like, and be comfortable any way they like, sitting in that seat ready to enjoy themselves," Greenberg said. "Because it's enjoyable."

H) Greenberg stressed that he doesn't want people to start respecting the music less, and he's not suggesting that we "dumb down" the experience. Rather, it's about opening up "access." When operas first instituted subtitles(字幕 ) during shows, he said, many purists didn't like the idea, believing that the audience should instead study the works before attending. But now it's commonplace to find titles on the seatback in front of you—choose a language, sit back, and understand what's going on.

I) Allison Vulgamore, president of the Philadelphia Orchestra, is certainly looking to the future. She says certain "classics concerts" dedicated to the old masters will always exist, but not every program has to feature Beethoven and Brahms—or even a stage and seats. "We're trying to introduce different kinds of concerts in different ways," she said. "We are an interactive society now, where people like to learn."

J) As the Philadelphia Orchestra rebounds from its financial straits, it is also aiming to experiment, without alienating the loyalists. Vulgamore pointed to Cirque de la Symphonie, a recent offering in which jugglers( 玩杂耍的 ⼈ ) and acrobats(杂技演员 ) interacted with musicians. An upcoming collaboration with New York City's Ridge Theatre, meanwhile, will feature a "suspended dance installation" and other theatrical elements occurring in conjunction with an orchestral piece.

K) The orchestra also continues to offer $25 annual memberships to Philadelphia students, who can buy rush tickets to every concert on the schedule. "Students line up for the concerts they want, and we get roughly 300 or 350 kids a night coming to these. They take any of the open seats available, 5 minutes before the concert starts," Vulgamore said. "It's like the running of the bulls, that energy when the doors open."

L) Greenberg thinks that youthful energy needs to be harvested. Conductors don't have to be arrogant and untouchable—they can be accessible. Perhaps there could even be a "bit of humor" about them, he suggested, and an abandoning of pretension within the high-art institutions themselves. "On one hand, these organizations are all saying the same thing: we want more general audiences, to break down cultural barriers," he said. "But then they come up with some very snooty( ⽬中⽆⼈的 ) thing that makes you crazy."

M) John Terauds, a critic who has covered Toronto's classical music scene extensively, also wants to do away with the stuffiness. He suggested that the warmer an audience is, the better the musicians themselves will respond. "But the producer or organizer has to let everyone know it's OK," he said. "It's OK to enjoy yourself." At the Toronto Symphony Orchestra, for example, conductor Peter Oundjian often stops between pieces, taking a moment to talk about the composer or the music in a very amiable way. And some nights, Terauds said, "at least a third" of the audience consists of students who have purchased cheaper tickets. On these nights, the energy of the room drastically shifts. It becomes a less intimidating place.

N) Back in February, Terauds wrote on his blog about how going to classical performances can be intimidating. Certain people "think they have to dress up," he wrote. "They think they have to know something about the music before they go. And, I'm sure, sitting in a seat, trembling in fear that this might be the wrong time to applaud, is also one of the factors."

O) Everyone in the classical world agrees on the need for increased "accessibility," but achieving it is often easier said than done. Nowadays, there are unknown, unorthodox opera singers wowing(博得 …… 的喝彩 ) viewers on TV programs like "America's Got Talent" and "The Voice". What can higher institutions do with any of that? And if they appeal to these outlets, do they risk compromising the integrity or the intelligence of the music?

P) Vulgamore seems to understand this. She thinks an organization can have it both ways, claiming the new while keeping the old. And as she reorganizes the Philadelphia Orchestra, she will attempt to do just that. "The world's most respected musicians brought together as an orchestra will always exist," she said. "But it's essential that we be willing to experiment and fail."

items.title: 2022年12月六级第3套 · 仔细阅读 · 第一篇
items.passage:
How can one person enjoy good health, while another person looks old before her time? Humans have been asking this question for thousands of years, and recently, it's becoming clearer and clearer to scientists that the differences between people's rates of aging lie in the complex interactions among genes, social relationships, environments and lifestyles. Even though you were born with a particular set of genes, the way you live can influence how they express themselves. Some lifestyle factors may even turn genes on or shut them off.

Deep within the genetic heart of all our cells are telomeres, or repeating segments of noncoding DNA that live at the ends of the chromosomes(染⾊体). They form caps at the ends of the chromosomes and keep the genetic material together. Shortening with each cell division, they help determine how fast a cell ages. When they become too short, the cell stops dividing altogether. This isn't the only reason a cell can age—there are other stresses on cells we don't yet understand very well—but short telomeres are one of the major reasons human cells grow old. We've devoted most of our careers to studying telomeres, and one extraordinary discovery from our labs is that telomeres can actually lengthen.

Scientists have learned that several thought patterns appear to be unhealthy for telomeres, and one of them is cynical hostility. Cynical hostility is defined by high anger and frequent thoughts that other people cannot be trusted. Someone with hostility doesn't just think, "I hate to stand in long lines"; they think, "Others deliberately sped up and beat me to my rightful position in the line!"—and then get violently agitated. People who score high on measures of cynical hostility tend to get more heart disease, metabolic disease and often die at younger ages. They also have shorter telomeres. In a study of British civil servants, men who scored high on measures of cynical hostility had shorter telomeres than men whose hostility scores were low. The most hostile men were 30% more likely to have short telomeres.

What this means: aging is a dynamic process that could possibly be accelerated or slowed—and, in some aspects, even reversed. To an extent, it has surprised us and the rest of the scientific community that telomeres do not simply carry out the commands issued by your genetic code. Your telomeres are listening to you. The foods you eat, your response to challenges, the amount of exercise you get, and many other factors appear to influence your telomeres and can prevent premature aging at the cellular level. One of the keys to enjoying good health is simply doing your part to foster healthy cell renewal.

How genes influence the aging process.
How various genes express themselves in aging.
Why people have long been concerned about aging.

questions.shortExplanation: Humans have been asking this question for thousands of years, and recently, it's becoming clearer and clearer to scientists that the differences between people's rates of aging lie in the complex interactions among genes, social relationships, environments and lifestyles.
questions.detailedExplanation:
【答案】 A （细节题）

【判型】 What have scientists come to know better today?问的是科学家"已经"了解到的客观事实，要求回原文找事实句，不需要推断。

【拆句】 结构平铺直叙：主语scientists + 谓语have come to know（"逐渐了解到"，动词短语作完成时）+ 比较级状语better today。无陷阱，唯一要注意的是come to know是"逐渐认识到"，非"来认识"。

【定位】 Humans have been asking this question for thousands of years, and recently, it's becoming clearer and clearer to scientists that the differences between people's rates of aging lie in the complex interactions among genes, social relationships, environments and lifestyles.

几千年来人类一直在问这个问题，而最近，科学家越来越清楚地认识到：人与人之间衰老速度的差异，源于基因、社会关系、环境和生活方式之间的复杂互动。

【选项】 A) ✓ 正确 the differences between people's rates of aging ↔ Why people age at different rates it's becoming clearer and clearer to scientists↔ come to know better 预判"为何人们衰老速度不同"与Why people age at different rates逐词同义对应，且A 完整覆盖了定位句的核心信息（差异+原因）。 B) 过度推断定位句只说"差异源于基因等多因素互动"，并未具体阐述"基因如何影响衰老过程"；选项 How genes influence the aging process问的是机制原理，是原文没展开的内容。

C) 无中生有定位句只点名"基因等因素互动"，原文Even though you were born with a particular set of genes, the way you live can influence how they express themselves.虽提到基因表达，但并未说"各种基因如何在衰老中表达自己"——选项C说的various genes在衰老中"各自如何表达"原文未有此层级讨论。

D) 答非所问 Why people have long been concerned about aging问的是"人们为何长期关注衰老"，对应原文Humans have been asking this question for thousands of years提到的"已问数千年"——但这是背景，不是"科学家最近搞清楚的事"，与题干come to know better today错位。
questions.hint: 回到原文定位题干关键词，比较选项与原文的含义。

questions.prompt: Why are some lifestyle factors considered extremely important?

options.text: They may shorten the process of cell division.
They may determine how genes function.
They may affect the lifespan of telomeres.
They may account for the stresses on cells.

questions.shortExplanation: Even though you were born with a particular set of genes, the way you live can influence how they express themselves. Some lifestyle factors may even turn genes on or shut them off.
questions.detailedExplanation:
【答案】 B （细节题）

【判型】 Why are some lifestyle factors considered extremely important?问的是被认定为重要的客观理由，在原文有对应解释句。

【拆句】 被动语态主干lifestyle factors are considered extremely important，相当于"people consider lifestyle factors extremely important"。注意被动里considered是"被认为"，不是"考虑"，读出主动意思即可。

【定位】 Even though you were born with a particular set of genes, the way you live can influence how they express themselves. Some lifestyle factors may even turn genes on or shut them off.

尽管你生来就带着一套特定的基因，但你的生活方式可以影响这些基因如何表达。某些生活方式因素甚至能把基因"打开"或"关闭"。

【选项】 A) 无中生有原文从未提及生活方式与"细胞分裂过程的缩短"有关；shorten the process of cell division中的"cell division"虽在P2出现，但与lifestyle factors并无原文连接。 B) ✓ 正确 turn genes on or shut them off ↔ determine how genes function the way you live can influence how they express themselves ↔

determine how genes function 预判"能决定基因的工作方式"与determine how genes function逐词对应；且原文"开关基因"这一极端动作正是"决定基因如何工作"的最强佐证。 C) 张冠李戴 affect the lifespan of telomeres说"影响端粒寿命"，但定位句在P1，此处尚未引入 telomeres概念；telomeres是P2才出现的话题，与第47题对接的lifestyle factors考点句不在同一区间。

D) 与原文相反 account for the stresses on cells说生活方式"解释了细胞所受的压力"，但原文there are other stresses on cells we don't yet understand very well明确说细胞的其他压力"我们还不太了解"——既然还没搞清楚，就谈不上由生活方式"解释"。
questions.hint: 回到原文定位题干关键词，比较选项与原文的含义。

questions.prompt: What have the author and his colleagues discovered about telomeres?

options.text: Their number affects the growth of cells.
Their length determines the quality of life.
Their shortening process can be reversed.
Their health impacts the division of cells.

questions.shortExplanation: We've devoted most of our careers to studying telomeres, and one extraordinary discovery from our labs is that telomeres can actually lengthen. 我们把职业生涯的大部分时间都投入到对端粒的研究中，而我们实验室一个非凡的发现是： 端粒其实可以延长。
questions.detailedExplanation:
【答案】 C （细节题）

【判型】 What have the author and his colleagues discovered about telomeres?问的是已经"发现"了的客观结论，原文必有对应陈述。

【拆句】 现在完成时疑问句，主干the author and his colleagues have discovered后接介词短语 about telomeres限定话题。结构无陷阱，重点是发现的内容（discovered的宾语，需到原文找）。

【定位】 We've devoted most of our careers to studying telomeres, and one extraordinary discovery from our labs is that telomeres can actually lengthen. 我们把职业生涯的大部分时间都投入到对端粒的研究中，而我们实验室一个非凡的发现是： 端粒其实可以延长。

【选项】 A) 偷换概念原文从未提及"端粒的"数量"（number）影响细胞生长"；端粒只谈"长短"，未谈"多少"。

B) 过度推断原文谈端粒影响"细胞衰老速度"和"人类细胞何时停止分裂"，但从未上升到the quality of life（生活质量）这一宏观概念——"生活质量"是远超细胞机制的延伸推断。

C) ✓ 正确 telomeres can actually lengthen ↔ Their shortening process can be reversed one extraordinary discovery from our labs ↔ the author and his colleagues discovered 预判"端粒缩短的趋势可被逆转"与Their shortening process can be reversed核心动词 reverse直接对应；且"端粒能变长"在本段"只会变短"的基线之上，唯一合理解读就是"缩短可被逆转"。

D) 无中生有原文是"端粒变短到一定程度，细胞就停止分裂"——细胞分裂决定于端粒长度，而非端粒"健康"影响细胞分裂。选项Their health impacts the division of cells把端粒"健康状态"当原因，且"健康"本身原文未提及。
questions.hint: 回到原文定位题干关键词，比较选项与原文的含义。

questions.prompt: What have scientists learned about cynical hostility?

options.text: It may lead to confrontational thought patterns.
It may produce an adverse effect on telomeres.
It may cause people to lose their temper frequently.
It may stir up agitation among those in long lines.

questions.shortExplanation: Scientists have learned that several thought patterns appear to be unhealthy for telomeres, and one of them is cynical hostility. 科学家发现，有几种思维模式似乎对端粒有害，其中之一就是"愤世嫉俗式敌意"。
questions.detailedExplanation:
【答案】 B （细节题）

【判型】 What have scientists learned about cynical hostility?问的是科学家研究后得出的客观结论，归细节题。

【拆句】 现在完成时疑问句，结构与第48题同型。注意cynical意为"愤世嫉俗的、玩世不恭的"， hostility是"敌意"，合起来指一种带不信任色彩的敌意性格。

【定位】 Scientists have learned that several thought patterns appear to be unhealthy for telomeres, and one of them is cynical hostility. 科学家发现，有几种思维模式似乎对端粒有害，其中之一就是"愤世嫉俗式敌意"。

【选项】 A) 偷换概念 lead to confrontational thought patterns说cynical hostility"导致对抗性思维模式"——但cynical hostility本身就是一种thought pattern（思维模式），不存在"导致另一思维模式"的链条；题干问的是其后果，A把因果维度错位。

B) ✓ 正确 unhealthy for telomeres ↔ produce an adverse effect on telomeres They also have shorter telomeres. ↔ produce an adverse effect on telomeres 预判"对端粒有害"与produce an adverse effect on telomeres词义直接对应；且后文 had shorter telomeres的实证数据更强化了这一判断。 C) 因果颠倒 cause people to lose their temper frequently说敌意"导致人们频繁发脾气"，但原文里"经常的愤怒"(frequent anger)是cynical hostility的定义性特征，是"因"不是"果"——发脾气是这种心态的表现，不是它造成的后果。

D) 以偏概全 stir up agitation among those in long lines说敌意"在排长队的人中引发激动"——原文里long lines只是个举例（举例说明带敌意者的思维特征），并非科学家研究的结论； 把例子当作结论是典型以偏概全。
questions.hint: 回到原文定位题干关键词，比较选项与原文的含义。

questions.prompt: What do we learn from the last paragraph about the process of aging?

options.text: It may vary from individual to individual.
It challenges scientists to explore further.
It depends on one's genetic code.
It may be controlled to a degree.

questions.shortExplanation: What this means: aging is a dynamic process that could possibly be accelerated or slowed— and, in some aspects, even reversed.
questions.detailedExplanation:
【答案】 D （细节题）

【判型】 题干是回末段问"我们了解到aging的什么"，本质上是末段的细节信息题，不是问全文主旨。

【拆句】 结构平铺，主干What do we learn，介词短语from the last paragraph限定信息来源， about the process of aging限定话题。无陷阱。

【定位】 What this means: aging is a dynamic process that could possibly be accelerated or slowed— and, in some aspects, even reversed.

这意味着：衰老是一个动态过程，可以被加速或减缓——而且，在某些方面，甚至可以被逆转。

【选项】 A) 张冠李戴 vary from individual to individual说衰老"因人而异"——这是首段the differences between people's rates of aging的话题，不是末段重点；末段讲的是衰老"可调控"， 不是"个体差异"。

B) 无中生有 challenges scientists to explore further说衰老"促使科学家进一步探索"——末段从未表达"号召科学家继续研究"的意思，整段是给出已得出的结论。 C) 与原文相反 depends on one's genetic code说衰老"取决于基因密码"——但末段telomeres do not simply carry out the commands issued by your genetic code恰好明确反对"完全由基因决定"的观点；末段的核心就是"超越基因决定论"。

D) ✓ 正确 could possibly be accelerated or slowed—and, in some aspects, even reversed↔

It may be controlled to a degree Your telomeres are listening to you.↔It may be controlled to a degree 预判"衰老在某种程度上可被控制"与It may be controlled to a degree逐词对应；尤其 may+to a degree精准对应原文possibly+in some aspects的限定，是六级阅读"程度词不能改"的典型考察点。
questions.hint: 回到原文定位题干关键词，比较选项与原文的含义。

items.title: 2022年12月六级第3套 · 仔细阅读 · 第二篇
items.passage:
Scientists have created by accident an enzyme(酶 ) that breaks down plastic drinks bottles. The breakthrough could help solve the global plastic pollution crisis by enabling for the first time the full recycling of bottles.

The new research was spurred by the discovery in 2016 of the first bacterium that had naturally evolved to eat plastic at a waste dump in Japan. Scientists have now revealed the detailed structure of the crucial enzyme produced by the bug.

An international team then adjusted the enzyme to see how it had evolved, but tests showed they had accidentally made the molecule even better at breaking down the plastic used for drinks bottles. "What actually turned out was we improved the enzyme, which was a bit of a shock," said head researcher Prof. McGeehan, at the University of Portsmouth, UK.

Currently, the enzyme takes a few days to start breaking down the plastic, far faster than the centuries it takes in the oceans, but the researchers are optimistic this can be speeded up even further and become a viable large-scale process.

"What we are hoping to do is use this enzyme to turn this plastic back into its original components, so we can literally recycle it back to plastic," said McGeehan. "It means we won't need to dig up any more oil and, fundamentally, it should reduce the amount of plastic in the environment."

About 1 million plastic bottles are sold each minute around the globe and, with just 14% recycled, many end up in the oceans where they have polluted even the remotest parts, harming marine life and potentially people who eat sea food. "Plastic is incredibly resistant to degradation," said McGeehan. "It is one of these wonder materials that has been made a little bit too well."

Currently those bottles that are recycled can only be turned into opaque fibres for clothing or carpets, while the new enzyme indicates a way to recycle old clear plastic bottles back into new clear plastic bottles.

"You are always up against the fact oil is cheap, so plastic is cheap," said McGeehan. "It is so easy for manufacturers to generate more of that stuff, rather than even try to recycle, but I believe there is a public interest here: perception is changing so much that companies are starting to look at how they can properly recycle these bottles."

Prof. Adisa Azapagic, at the University of Manchester in the UK, agreed the enzyme could be useful but added: "A full life-cycle assessment would be needed to ensure that the technology does not solve one environmental problem—waste—at the expense of others, including additional greenhouse gas emissions."

questions.prompt: What do we learn from the passage about an enzyme scientists have created?

options.text: It was identified during a lab experiment accident.
It may make full recycling of plastic bottles a reality.
It was a breakthrough made with persistent efforts.
It may initiate a radical reform in plastic industry.

questions.shortExplanation: The breakthrough could help solve the global plastic pollution crisis by enabling for the first time the full recycling of bottles.
questions.detailedExplanation:
【答案】 B （细节题）

【判型】 题干 What do we learn from the passage about an enzyme scientists have created? 是 What do we learn about X 的标准客观陈述问法，不含 infer / imply，不问 main idea / attitude，属细节题。

【拆句】 题干主干为 What do we learn from the passage about an enzyme，about 引导的介词短语限定 learn 的对象；其后 scientists have created 是省略 that 的定语从句修饰 enzyme，结构清晰，无陷阱。

【定位】 The breakthrough could help solve the global plastic pollution crisis by enabling for the first time the full recycling of bottles.

这一突破有望首次实现塑料瓶的完全回收，从而帮助解决全球塑料污染危机。

【选项】 A) 偷换概念 identified during a lab experiment accident 偷换了原文 created by accident——原文意思是"偶然创造出"，A 项却说成"在一次实验事故中被识别（identified）出来"， identified（识别）≠ created（创造），且 lab experiment accident（实验事故）也无原文支撑。

B) ✓ 正确 enabling for the first time the full recycling of bottles ↔

may make full recycling of plastic bottles a reality the full recycling of bottles ↔ full recycling of plastic bottles B 项既覆盖"完全回收"又保留"可能性"语气，与定位句 could help…by enabling for the first time the full recycling of bottles 严格对应，是定位句的同义改写。

C) 与原文相反 breakthrough made with persistent efforts 与原文 created by accident 直接相反； 同段还点明 a bit of a shock 进一步坐实"意外性"。 D) 无中生有 initiate a radical reform in plastic industry 中的 radical reform（根本性改革）在原文中无任何对应句；原文谈的是"帮助解决污染"和"完全回收"，并未谈及行业改革。
questions.hint: 回到原文定位题干关键词，比较选项与原文的含义。

questions.prompt: What does the passage say about the bug that produces the important enzyme?

options.text: It has a natural ability to consume plastics.
It is a bacterium that reproduces at a high rate.
It is essential to the recycling of plastic bottles.
It has a chemical structure unknown to scientists.

questions.shortExplanation: The new research was spurred by the discovery in 2016 of the first bacterium that had naturally evolved to eat plastic at a waste dump in Japan.
questions.detailedExplanation:
【答案】 A （细节题）

【判型】 题干 What does the passage say about the bug that produces the important enzyme? 用 say about 直接索取原文对 the bug 的客观陈述，不含推断词，属细节题。

【拆句】 the bug that produces the important enzyme 中 that 引导的定语从句修饰 bug；六级考生需看清 produces 的主语是 the bug 而非更靠近的 enzyme，即所问对象是 bug 本身的特征。

【定位】 The new research was spurred by the discovery in 2016 of the first bacterium that had naturally evolved to eat plastic at a waste dump in Japan.

这项新研究的契机是 2016 年在日本一处垃圾场发现的首个自然进化出能吃塑料能力的细菌。

【选项】 A) ✓ 正确 naturally evolved to eat plastic ↔ natural ability to consume plastics A 项把定位句的动词陈述（自然进化出去吃塑料）改写为名词陈述（具有自然消化塑料的能力），是该细菌核心特征的客观转述。

B) 无中生有 reproduces at a high rate（高速繁殖）在原文中没有任何对应句；原文只说该细菌"自然进化"且"吃塑料"，没有谈论其繁殖速度。

C) 偷换概念 essential to the recycling of plastic bottles 把所问对象（bug 本身的属性）偷换成"对回收的必要性"——这是对其衍生用途的评价，而非对 bug 本身的描述；且原文也未声称 bug 对回收"必不可少"。

D) 与原文相反 chemical structure unknown to scientists 与原文 Scientists have now revealed the detailed structure of the crucial enzyme produced by the bug. 相反；原文明确"已揭示详细结构"，选项却说"科学家不知道"。
questions.hint: 回到原文定位题干关键词，比较选项与原文的含义。

questions.prompt: By adjusting the enzyme produced by the bug, the scientists_______.

options.text: made it more effective by chance
found its evolutionary process sped up

questions.shortExplanation: An international team then adjusted the enzyme to see how it had evolved, but tests showed they had accidentally made the molecule even better at breaking down the plastic used for drinks bottles.
questions.detailedExplanation:
【答案】 A （细节题）

【判型】 题干是不完整陈述 By adjusting the enzyme produced by the bug, the scientists_______.，要选项补全，问的是科学家做了什么的客观结果，不含推断动词。

【拆句】 By adjusting the enzyme produced by the bug, the scientists_______. 主干是 the scientists ____；By 引导方式状语，produced by the bug 是过去分词短语后置定语修饰 enzyme，结构清晰。

【定位】 An international team then adjusted the enzyme to see how it had evolved, but tests showed they had accidentally made the molecule even better at breaking down the plastic used for drinks bottles.

国际团队随后调整了该酶以观察其进化过程，但实验表明他们意外地让这一分子分解饮料瓶塑料的能力变得更强了。

【选项】 A) ✓ 正确 accidentally made the molecule even better at breaking down the plastic ↔

made it more effective by chance A 项 made it more effective 复述 even better at breaking down，by chance 复述 accidentally，正好等值改写定位句两个核心要素。

B) 无中生有 discovered an extraordinary chemical 中 extraordinary chemical 在原文无出处；研究者操作的是已知酶分子，并非"发现一种新化学物质"。 C) 过度推断 altered its basic molecular composition 中 basic molecular composition（基本分子组成）属于结构层级更深的概念，原文只说 adjusted the enzyme（调整酶），未说改变其"基本组成"。

D) 偷换概念 found its evolutionary process sped up 中 sped up（加速）与原文 to see how it had evolved（观察其如何进化）不一致；原文目的是观察，并未发现进化过程被加速。
questions.hint: 回到原文定位题干关键词，比较选项与原文的含义。

questions.prompt: What does Prof. McGeehan say about the recycling of plastic bottles?

options.text: Manufacturers are implementing it on an increasingly larger scale.
It generates huge business opportunities for plastic manufacturers.
It has aroused persistent interest among the general public.
Manufacturers are beginning to explore ways of doing it.

questions.shortExplanation: perception is changing so much that companies are starting to look at how they can properly recycle these bottles.
questions.detailedExplanation:
【答案】 D （细节题）

【判型】 题干 What does Prof. McGeehan say about the recycling of plastic bottles? 索取 McGeehan 关于回收的客观说法，属细节题。

【拆句】 What does Prof. McGeehan say about the recycling of plastic bottles? 标准 Wh- 疑问句，about 短语限定 say 的话题对象，无陷阱。

【定位】 perception is changing so much that companies are starting to look at how they can properly recycle these bottles.

公众观念变化如此之大，以至于企业正开始研究如何妥善回收这些瓶子。

【选项】 A) 过度推断 implementing it on an increasingly larger scale 中 implementing on a larger scale （大规模实施）远超 starting to look at（开始研究）的程度——原文是观念转变后的初始阶段，并未谈到任何实施规模。 B) 无中生有 generates huge business opportunities for plastic manufacturers 中 huge business opportunities（巨大商业机会）原文未提；McGeehan 谈的是企业态度转变，不是回收带来的商机。

C) 偷换概念 aroused persistent interest among the general public 中 persistent interest（持续 / 长期兴趣）与原文 perception is changing so much（观念正在巨大变化）不一致 ——原文说"正在变化"，C 说"已激起且持续"；且讨论对象是公众而非回收行为本身， 与题干 about the recycling of plastic bottles 错位。 D) ✓ 正确 companies are starting to look at how they can properly recycle these bottles ↔

Manufacturers are beginning to explore ways of doing it companies ↔ Manufacturers D 项把"才刚开始"和"探索如何回收"两个核心信息都对齐原文，是定位句的精准同义改写。
questions.hint: 回到原文定位题干关键词，比较选项与原文的含义。

questions.prompt: What is Prof. Adisa Azapagic's advice concerning the application of the enzyme?

options.text: Developing technologies to address greenhouse gas emissions.
Considering the extra cost involved in producing the enzyme.
Assessing its possible negative impact on the environment.
Studying the full life cycle of the enzyme as the first step.

questions.shortExplanation: A full life-cycle assessment would be needed to ensure that the technology does not solve one environmental problem—waste—at the expense of others, including additional greenhouse gas emissions.
questions.detailedExplanation:
【答案】 C （细节题）

【判型】 题干 What is Prof. Adisa Azapagic's advice concerning the application of the enzyme? 索取该专家的具体建议，属细节题。

【拆句】 What is Prof. Adisa Azapagic's advice concerning the application of the enzyme? 中 concerning the application of the enzyme 是介词短语修饰 advice，limit 范围为"针对酶的应用"，结构清晰。

【定位】 A full life-cycle assessment would be needed to ensure that the technology does not solve one environmental problem—waste—at the expense of others, including additional greenhouse gas emissions.

需要进行一次完整的生命周期评估，以确保该技术不会以制造其他环境问题（包括额外的温室气体排放）为代价来解决一个环境问题（废弃物）。

【选项】 A) 偷换概念 Developing technologies to address greenhouse gas emissions 中 developing technologies 与原文 assessment（评估）不同——原文建议"评估"，并非"开发新技术"去解决排放问题。 B) 无中生有 Considering the extra cost involved in producing the enzyme 中 extra cost in producing the enzyme（生产酶的额外成本）原文无出处；Adisa Azapagic 的建议是评估环境影响而非经济成本。

C) ✓ 正确 does not solve one environmental problem—waste—at the expense of others, including additional greenhouse gas emissions

↔ Assessing its possible negative impact on the environment A full life-cycle assessment would be needed↔ Assessing C 项的 Assessing 对应 assessment，possible negative impact on the environment 对应 not solve…at the expense of others, including additional greenhouse gas emissions；正答完整覆盖建议的两个语义要点。 D) 偷换概念 Studying the full life cycle of the enzyme as the first step 中 the full life cycle of the enzyme（酶本身的生命周期）与原文 A full life-cycle assessment（针对技术应用的全生命周期评估）所指不同——原文评估的是技术对环境的全周期影响，并非"酶的寿命周期"；另外 as the first step（作为第一步）原文亦无对应。
questions.hint: 回到原文定位题干关键词，比较选项与原文的含义。

items.title: 2022年6月六级第1套 · 选词填空
items.passage:
The city of Bath was founded by the Romans almost two thousand years ago. It has been famous for its [26] _____ pleasing architecture and healing thermal springs ever since.

There are three hot springs in Bath; one is the King's Spring, upon which the Roman Baths and a temple were [27] _____ . The other two are the Cross Spring and the Hetling Spring, close to each other in Hot Bath Street. Although Bath is [28] _____ known as a Roman and Georgian city, many people came in the intervening centuries to make use of the [29] _____ waters.

While the Georgians made 'taking the waters' or bathing particularly fashionable, it was [30] _____ generations who paved the way, creating greater interest in Bath and its springs. Charles II, desperate for an heir and unable to produce a [31] _____ son, came to Bath to take the waters in the hope that their magical powers would do something to [32] _____ the situation. Craving for a male heir, James and Mary both came to Bath and soon after produced a son, which bred many conspiracy theories about who was the real father of their [33] _____ . Regardless, the 'miracle' created something of a boom in tourism for Bath and once Queen Anne had paid a visit in 1702, sealing it as the place to be, the whole nation [34] _____ to the city.

Afterwards, the spas(矿泉疗养浴场 ) in Bath continued to go in and out of fashion for more than 150 years until they closed completely. The new Bath Spa, which opened in 2006, [35] _____ modern architecture with the ancient spring, now the New Royal Bath.

questions.prompt: It has been famous for its __(26)__ pleasing architecture and healing thermal springs ever since.
questions.shortExplanation: 审美上令人愉悦 = 建筑美观
questions.detailedExplanation:
【答案】 A) aesthetically 副词

【词性槽】 修饰形容词 pleasing 的副词

【依据】 审美上令人愉悦 = 建筑美观

famous for its __ pleasing architecture 说的是巴斯以"美观的建筑"闻名，aesthetically pleasing 是英文里描述"赏心悦目、审美上令人愉快"的高频固定搭配，与后面"healing thermal springs"（治疗效果）并列，分别从美感和功效两方面定调全城特色。

【竞争词】 K) principally 义为"主要地"，与 pleasing 不搭

principally pleasing 意为"主要令人愉悦"，不符合英语习惯搭配；且 principally 通常修饰动词或限定范围（principally known as 等），更适合放在第 28 题修饰 known。

M) rhetorically 修辞地 ≠ 美感

rhetorically 指"在修辞表达上"，与建筑外观的视觉美感没有关系，rhetorically pleasing architecture 在英语里不成立。
questions.hint: 根据空格前后的词性、搭配与上下文选择词语；每个词最多使用一次。

questions.prompt: one is the King's Spring, upon which the Roman Baths and a temple were __(27)__.
questions.shortExplanation: 建在泉水之上 upon which 引导的定语从句修饰 the King's Spring，意为"罗马浴场和神庙建在国王泉之上"，constructed（建造）正是该语义的标准词。
questions.detailedExplanation:
【答案】 B) constructed 动词

【词性槽】 were ___ → 被动语态过去分词

【依据】 建在泉水之上 upon which 引导的定语从句修饰 the King's Spring，意为"罗马浴场和神庙建在国王泉之上"，constructed（建造）正是该语义的标准词。
questions.hint: 根据空格前后的词性、搭配与上下文选择词语；每个词最多使用一次。

questions.prompt: Although Bath is __(28)__ known as a Roman and Georgian city
questions.shortExplanation: "主要被认作罗马 & 乔治亚城"对应 although 让步
questions.detailedExplanation:
【答案】 K) principally 副词

【词性槽】 修饰过去分词 known 的副词

【依据】 "主要被认作罗马 & 乔治亚城"对应 although 让步

全句 Although Bath is __(28)__ known as a Roman and Georgian city, many people came in the intervening centuries 用 although 让步："尽管巴斯主要以罗马 / 乔治亚之城闻名，但中间几个世纪也有很多人来"。principally"主要地"恰好建立"主流认知 vs. 例外史实"的对照，是该让步逻辑的标准副词。

【竞争词】 M) rhetorically修辞地 known 不成立

rhetorically known 在英文中不成习惯搭配，且"修辞上被认作"与让步逻辑无关；本句讨论的是事实层面的主流印象，与修辞无关。

【易错】 最具迷惑性的错误词是 M) —— rhetorically 词性也对、形态也对，唯独搭配不通。副词槽 Although Bath is __(28)__ known as a Roman and Georgian city 留下 principally 与 rhetorically 两词同时过关词性，词义又都比较"专业"，容易让考生选错。防坑：看 although 让步逻辑——只有"主要地"才能与让步对照（虽然主要是 A，但也有 B）， rhetorically 没有让步含义。
questions.hint: 根据空格前后的词性、搭配与上下文选择词语；每个词最多使用一次。

questions.prompt: many people came in the intervening centuries to make use of the __(29)__ waters.
questions.shortExplanation: natural waters = 天然温泉
questions.detailedExplanation:
【答案】 H) natural 形容词

【词性槽】 the + 空 + 复数名词 waters → 修饰名词的形容词

【依据】 natural waters = 天然温泉

上文 healing thermal springs 已点明巴斯的水是"天然温泉"，本句指"中间几个世纪人们来利用这些（天然温泉）水"，natural 直接呼应温泉的天然属性，搭配 natural waters 是英语描述天然泉水的常见说法。

【竞争词】 G) legitimate "合法的水"语义荒谬

legitimate 指"合法的、婚生的"，与温泉水的属性毫不沾边；且 legitimate 在后文 unable to produce a __(31)__ son 里有更贴合的位置（legitimate son = 婚生子）。

O) versatile"多才多艺的水"不通

versatile 多形容人或物用途广，搭配 waters 不通顺；且全文没出现需要 versatile 的语境，它是典型的干扰词。
questions.hint: 根据空格前后的词性、搭配与上下文选择词语；每个词最多使用一次。

questions.prompt: it was __(30)__ generations who paved the way, creating greater interest in Bath and its springs.
questions.shortExplanation: previous generations 与下文乔治亚时代构成时间对照
questions.detailedExplanation:
【答案】 J) previous 形容词

【词性槽】 it was ___ generations who paved → 强调结构中修饰复数名词的形容词

【依据】 previous generations 与下文乔治亚时代构成时间对照

本句让步逻辑是 While the Georgians made 'taking the waters' or bathing particularly fashionable, it was __(30)__ generations who paved the way——虽然是乔治亚人让"浴疗"流行起来，但真正铺路的是"前几代人"。previous generations"前几代人"正好与 the Georgians（乔治亚一代）形成时间上的对照，且与后文查理二世、詹姆士与玛丽这些"前任王朝"事例呼应。

【竞争词】 O) versatile"多才多艺的几代人"与铺路逻辑无关

versatile generations 既不构成时间对照，也与"paved the way（铺路）"的因果关系无关； versatile 整篇都找不到落脚点，是命题人埋的干扰词。
questions.hint: 根据空格前后的词性、搭配与上下文选择词语；每个词最多使用一次。

questions.prompt: Charles II, desperate for an heir and unable to produce a __(31)__ son
questions.shortExplanation: legitimate son = 婚生子（合法继承人）
questions.detailedExplanation:
【答案】 G) legitimate 形容词

【词性槽】 a + 空 + 名词 son → 修饰 son 的形容词

【依据】 legitimate son = 婚生子（合法继承人）

查理二世"desperate for an heir"——急需王位继承人；legitimate son 在英语里专指"婚生子"，即可以合法继承王位的儿子。下文 Craving for a male heir 再次印证关注点在合法男嗣，与 legitimate 完美吻合。

【竞争词】 O) versatile多才多艺与王位继承无关

versatile son"多才多艺的儿子"与文意"急需合法继承人"完全错位；查理二世在意的不是儿子才艺，而是儿子是否婚生、是否能继位。
questions.hint: 根据空格前后的词性、搭配与上下文选择词语；每个词最多使用一次。

questions.prompt: in the hope that their magical powers would do something to __(32)__ the situation.
questions.shortExplanation: remedy the situation = 补救局面
questions.detailedExplanation:
【答案】 L) remedy 动词

【词性槽】 do something to + 动词原形 → 不定式动词

【依据】 remedy the situation = 补救局面

查理二世来巴斯泡温泉 in the hope that their magical powers would do something to __ the situation，希望温泉魔力"做点什么来挽救 / 补救（生不出合法继承人的）局面"。 remedy 作动词意为"纠正 / 补救"，remedy the situation 是英语固定搭配，与 desperate 的语气一致。

【竞争词】 D) extract "提取局面"语义不通

extract 意为"提取 / 抽出"，搭配名词通常是 extract information/data/oil，不能与 situation 搭配；且与"求子续嗣"语境无关，是干扰项。
questions.hint: 根据空格前后的词性、搭配与上下文选择词语；每个词最多使用一次。

questions.prompt: which bred many conspiracy theories about who was the real father of their __(33)__.
questions.shortExplanation: their offspring = 他们的子嗣
questions.detailedExplanation:
【答案】 I) offspring 名词

【词性槽】 形容词性物主代词 their 后 → 名词

【依据】 their offspring = 他们的子嗣

前文 James and Mary both came to Bath and soon after produced a son 明确他们生了一个儿子，本句又紧接"who was the real father of their __"，空处应是"他们的孩子"。 offspring 正是"子女、后代"的中性书面词，与上下文阴谋论的语气吻合。
questions.hint: 根据空格前后的词性、搭配与上下文选择词语；每个词最多使用一次。

questions.prompt: the whole nation __(34)__ to the city.
questions.shortExplanation: flock to = 蜂拥而至前文铺垫"安妮女王 1702 年访问巴斯，把它坐实为时尚胜地"once Queen Anne had paid a visit in 1702, sealing it as the place to be，后面紧接"全国都___去这座城市"，逻辑上必须是"大规模、公开地涌向"，flocked（成群蜂拥而至）正是描写旅游热的标准词，与前句"created something of a boom in tourism"完美呼应。
questions.detailedExplanation:
【答案】 E) flocked 动词

【词性槽】 主语 the whole nation + 空 + to the city → 过去式动词

【依据】 flock to = 蜂拥而至前文铺垫"安妮女王 1702 年访问巴斯，把它坐实为时尚胜地"once Queen Anne had paid a visit in 1702, sealing it as the place to be，后面紧接"全国都___去这座城市"，逻辑上必须是"大规模、公开地涌向"，flocked（成群蜂拥而至）正是描写旅游热的标准词，与前句"created something of a boom in tourism"完美呼应。

【竞争词】 N) sneaked 潜行 ≠ 公开蜂拥

sneaked 指"偷偷溜走 / 潜行"，是小规模、隐秘的动作，主语是"全国（the whole nation）"时显然不合理；而且与"boom in tourism""the place to be"传递的高调、公开氛围正好相反，属典型反义诱惑项。

【易错】 最具迷惑性的错误词是 N) —— sneaked 与 flocked 都能搭配 to，词义边界相反。the whole nation __(34)__ to the city 里 sneaked 看似也能填，是典型"正话反说"诱惑。防坑：看主语量级（the whole nation 是大规模、公开的）+ 上文气氛（boom in tourism、the place to be），明显与"偷偷溜走"矛盾。
questions.hint: 根据空格前后的词性、搭配与上下文选择词语；每个词最多使用一次。

questions.prompt: The new Bath Spa, which opened in 2006, __(35)__ modern architecture with the ancient spring
questions.shortExplanation: incorporate A with B = 把 A 与 B 融合 __(35)__ modern architecture with the ancient spring 的搭配框架"___ A with B"暗示"将现代建筑与古泉结合 / 融合"，incorporates"把……融合 / 并入"正是该框架的标准动词， 与"new"（新）和"ancient"（古）形成的对比相呼应。
questions.detailedExplanation:
【答案】 F) incorporates 动词

【词性槽】 主语 The new Bath Spa + 空 → 第三人称单数动词

【依据】 incorporate A with B = 把 A 与 B 融合 __(35)__ modern architecture with the ancient spring 的搭配框架"___ A with B"暗示"将现代建筑与古泉结合 / 融合"，incorporates"把……融合 / 并入"正是该框架的标准动词， 与"new"（新）和"ancient"（古）形成的对比相呼应。

【竞争词】 C) designates designate = "指定 / 命名"，搭配 with 不成立

designate 通常搭配 as（designate A as B）或直接接宾语，不与 with 搭配；且语义"指定 / 命名"与"把现代建筑与古泉融合"完全不同，代入读不通。
questions.hint: 根据空格前后的词性、搭配与上下文选择词语；每个词最多使用一次。

items.title: 2022年6月六级第1套 · 信息匹配
items.passage:
A) Fazila is a young woman that has been dealing with eczema(湿疹), a common skin condition, for the past five years, but never got it treated. The nearest hospital is an hour away, by boat and bus, and her skin condition didn't seem serious enough to make the trek, so she ignored it—until a new technology brought the doctor to her. Fazila lives on one of the remote river islands in northern Bangladesh. These islands are low-lying, temporary sand islands that are continuously formed and destroyed through sand buildup and erosion. They are home to over six million people, who face repeated displacement from flooding and erosion—which may be getting worse because of climate change—and a range of health risks, including poor nutrition, malaria(疟疾 ) and other water-borne diseases.

B) The most dangerous thing for these remote island dwellers is land erosion. The second is lack of access to medical supplies and doctors. There are no doctors within miles, and while child mortality and maternal death have gone down in the rest of the country, this is not the case for the islands. The medical situation is so bad that it really takes away from the quality of their life. Yet for many island inhabitants—some of Bangladesh's poorest—paying for health care is a costly ordeal. Victims of erosion lose their houses, agricultural land and jobs as farmers, fishermen and day laborers. Though government hospitals are free, many people hesitate to go, citing long commutes, endless lines and questionable diagnoses. For convenience's sake, one-third of rural households visit unqualified village doctors, who rely on unscientific methods of treatment, according to a 2016 study in the peer-reviewed journal Global Health Action.

C) On the islands, there's even a colloquial(⼝头的) expression for the idea of making medical care your lowest priority: It's known as "rog pushai rakha" in Bengali, which roughly translates to "stockpiling their diseases"—waiting to seek medical attention until a condition becomes extremely serious. Now, a new virtual medical service called Teledaktar (TD) is trying to make health care more easily accessible. Every week, TD's medical operators travel to the islands by boat, carrying a laptop, a portable printer for prescriptions and tools to run basic medical screenings such as blood pressure, blood sugar, body temperature and weight. They choose an area of the island with the best Internet reception and set up a makeshift(临时凑合的 ) medical center which consists of plastic stools and small tables borrowed from the locals' homes, a tent in case of rain and a sheet that is strung up to give the patients privacy during their session.

D) Launched in October 2018, TD has eight centers in towns and villages across rural Bangladesh and on three islands. It is funded by a nonprofit organization founded by Bangladeshi entrepreneurs, finance and technology professionals. Inside the center, the laptop screen lights up to reveal Dr. Tina Mustahid, TD's head physician, live-streamed( ⽹络直播 ) from the capital city of Dhaka for free remote medical consultations. Affectionately called Doctor Apa—"older sister" in Bengali—by her patients, she is one of three volunteer doctors at TD.

E) "I diagnose them through conversation," says Dr. Mustahid. "Sometimes it's really obvious things that local doctors don't have the patience to talk through with their patients. For example, a common complaint mothers come in with is that their children refuse to eat their meals. The mothers are concerned they are dealing with indigestion, but it's because they are feeding the children packaged chips which are cheap and convenient. I tell them it is ruining their appetite and ask them to cut back on unhealthy snacks." Dr. Mustahid says building awareness about health and nutrition is important for island patients who are cut off from mainland resources.

F) Even off the islands, Bangladesh faces a critical deficit of health services. The country has half the doctors-per-person ratio recommended by the World Health Organization: roughly one doctor per 2,000 people, instead of one doctor per 1,000 people. And of those physicians, many are concentrated in cities: 70% of the country's population live in rural areas, yet less than 20% of health workers practice there. Over 70% of TD's 3,000 patients are female, in part because many are not comfortable speaking with local doctors who tend to be male. The rural women are mostly not literate or confident enough to travel on their own to the nearest town to visit medical facilities. Many have spent their entire lives rebuilding their homes when the islands flood. Early marriage and young motherhood, which are prevalent in these parts of Bangladesh, also contribute to the early onset of health problems.

G) For most TD patients on the islands, Dr. Mustahid is the first big-city doctor that they've ever consulted. TD doctors are not meant to treat serious illnesses or conditions that require a doctor to be physically present, such as pregnancy. But they can write prescriptions, diagnose common ailments —including digestive issues, joint pain, skin diseases, fever and the common cold—and refer patients to doctors at local hospitals. The visit is also an opportunity for the patients, especially women, to air their concerns about aging, motherhood and reproductive health according to Dr. Mustahid. The doctors also offer health, dietary and lifestyle advice where necessary, including insight on everything from recognizing postnatal( 产后的 ) depression to daily exercise. Dr. Mustahid regularly recommends her patients to take a daily thirty-minute morning walk before the sun gets too intense.

H) After a few sessions about general health issues Fazila finally opened up about something else that was bothering her: her persistent skin condition. It can get expensive to travel to the doctor, so usually the women living on the islands describe their illness to their husbands. The husbands then go to the pharmacy, try to describe the issue and return home with some random medicines. Nothing worked for Fazila until she started seeing Dr. Apa.

I) Other nonprofits are also starting to provide health services on the islands. A local non-governmental organization called Friendship operates floating boat hospitals that provide health services to islands all over Bangladesh, docking at each for two months at a time. Friendship also runs satellite clinics in which one doctor and one clinic aide who are residents of the community disperse health and hygiene information.

J) TD still has a few major challenges. Many residents complain the medicines they are prescribed are sometimes unaffordable, but the government isn't doing enough for them. Patients often ask why the medicine isn't free along with the consultation from the doctors. The organizations are linked to local pharmacies and offer discounts to the patients and make sure to prescribe the most cost-effective brands, but still many residents can't afford even that.

K) Nevertheless, TD's remote consultations seem to be popular: Of 3,000 patients, at least 200 have returned for follow-ups, according to TD. The reason, explains one resident, might be the simple gesture of treating the island inhabitants with respect. "Dr. Apa is patient," he says, "At government hospitals, the doctors treat us very badly, but here they listen to us, I can repeat myself many times and no one gets annoyed."

questions.prompt: Some children on the remote islands won't eat their meals because they are fed cheap junk food.
questions.shortExplanation: 孩子不肯吃饭+垃圾零食
questions.detailedExplanation:
【答案】 E 段（强锚点）

【锚点】 孩子不肯吃饭+垃圾零食

【定位】 The mothers are concerned they are dealing with indigestion, but it's because they are feeding the children packaged chips which are cheap and convenient. 母亲们担心孩子是消化不良，但其实是因为她们给孩子吃了既便宜又方便的袋装薯片。

【改写】 children ↔ their children 同词复现

won't eat their meals ↔ refuse to eat their meals 助动词否定替换实义动词

cheap junk food ↔ packaged chips which are cheap and convenient 上位词概括下位实例
questions.hint: 先定位陈述句中的人物、数字或关键词，再比较原文同义表达。

questions.prompt: Unlike other parts of Bangladesh, the number of women who die from giving birth remains high on the river islands.
questions.shortExplanation: 孕产妇死亡率+岛屿例外
questions.detailedExplanation:
【答案】 B 段（强锚点）

【锚点】 孕产妇死亡率+岛屿例外

items.title: 2022年6月六级第1套 · 仔细阅读 · 第一篇
items.passage:
Selective colleges and universities in the U.S. are under fire for being too elite and too expensive, and for not training graduates for the world of work. Such charges ignore the fact that these institutions continue to prepare students for success in their work, for thoughtful engagement in civic life, for lifelong learning, and for understanding the world and those with whom they live.

These colleges and universities must be doing something right. Applications are at record highs, and their financial aid programs make them more accessible than ever. This model of education has long played a central role in creating opportunity, driving economic growth, and spurring innovation.

Yet, there is growing skepticism about the value of this model. The recent tax reform bill is a wake-up call that our strongest colleges and universities are under assault by some in government. The initial proposals would have made education unaffordable for many by taxing tuition waivers for graduate students and ending deductions for student loan interest. Thankfully, these provisions were ultimately stripped from the bill, but lawmakers let stand a new tax on the investment income of some colleges and universities.

While these attacks are motivated by misguided ideas, we need to do a better job of explaining why these claims are false and why what we do is valuable. We cannot take for granted that any of this is obvious.

It is often said that elite colleges and universities do not train students, particularly those who study the liberal arts, for the workforce. But this can be refuted by scholarly research. The data are clear: a liberal arts education is great career preparation, both for excellent lifetime earnings and for satisfaction with the work. This education develops the skills of critical thinking, rigorous analysis of data and facts, communication with the written and spoken word, understanding of cultural differences and issues, and the ability to keep learning. In fact, liberal arts graduates do extremely well in every imaginable field.

Access to an education at selective colleges and universities is now more available than ever to low-and middle-income families. We have built endowments from donations by alumni(校友) and parents who understand and appreciate our mission to provide access and opportunity, and a significant portion of the returns from these endowments is used to fund financial aid.

Ironically, the new tax on endowments drains financial aid funds from the very schools most able to offer opportunity to those who have earned a spot but cannot otherwise afford this education. Beyond the virtue of access to those who have earned a place at these schools, the diversity of economic backgrounds enhances the education and experience of all of our students.

questions.prompt: What fact does the author emphasize concerning selective colleges and universities?

options.text: They have been ignoring the training of graduates for the world of work.
They have been doing well in ensuring their students a successful future.
They have been constantly attacked for being too elite and too expensive.
They have been actively engaged in civic life beyond the school campus.

questions.shortExplanation: Such charges ignore the fact that these institutions continue to prepare students for success in their work, for thoughtful engagement in civic life, for lifelong learning, and for understanding the world and those with whom they live.
questions.detailedExplanation:
【答案】 B （细节题）

【判型】 What fact does the author emphasize 明确询问作者强调的事实，对应原文某一处具体表述，不要求跨段推断。

【拆句】 主干是 What fact does the author emphasize，concerning selective colleges and universities 是介词短语后置修饰 fact，相当于 about。无否定、无比较，平铺直叙。

【定位】 Such charges ignore the fact that these institutions continue to prepare students for success in their work, for thoughtful engagement in civic life, for lifelong learning, and for understanding the world and those with whom they live.

这些指控忽视了一个事实：这些院校仍在持续地为学生做准备——为他们的事业成功、公民生活的深入参与、终身学习，以及理解世界与共处之人做准备。

【选项】 A) 与原文相反 They have been ignoring the training of graduates for the world of work 把“忽视” 这一动作扣到了院校头上，正好与原文相反——原文是说指控者忽视了事实，并不是院校忽视培养。

B) ✓ 正确 these institutions continue to prepare students for success in their work ↔

doing well in ensuring their students a successful future Such charges ignore the fact that ↔ They have been doing well 预判说“院校仍在为学生未来成功做准备”，B 项 doing well in ensuring their students a successful future 正是这一表述的同义替换，故选 B。

C) 答非所问 They have been constantly attacked for being too elite and too expensive 复述的是 Selective colleges and universities in the U.S. are under fire for being too elite and too expensive 这一事实——但这是别人对院校的指控，不是作者要强调的 fact； 题干问 What fact does the author emphasize。 D) 偷换概念 They have been actively engaged in civic life beyond the school campus 把原文中 “院校培养学生参与公民生活”的对象（学生）偷换成了院校本身参与公民生活，主体被替换。
questions.hint: 回到原文定位题干关键词，比较选项与原文的含义。

questions.prompt: What does the author say in arguing for the model of education in the U.S.?

options.text: It has contributed substantially to the nation's overall development.
It has succeeded in maintaining sustainable financial aid programs.
It has given priority to innovative programs for graduate studies.
It has played a central role in attracting international applicants.

questions.shortExplanation: This model of education has long played a central role in creating opportunity, driving economic growth, and spurring innovation.
questions.detailedExplanation:
【答案】 A （细节题）

【判型】 What does the author say 询问作者具体表态了什么，对应一句具体陈述，仍属细节题。

【拆句】 主干 What does the author say，in arguing for the model of education in the U.S. 是介词短语作状语，交代 say 发生的语境。结构简单。

【定位】 This model of education has long played a central role in creating opportunity, driving economic growth, and spurring innovation.

这一教育模式长期以来在创造机会、推动经济增长与激发创新方面扮演着核心角色。

【选项】 A) ✓ 正确 creating opportunity, driving economic growth, and spurring innovation ↔

contributed substantially to the nation's overall development has long played a central role ↔ contributed substantially 三项并列贡献可统一抽象为 the nation's overall development，A 项正是这一上位概括，故选 A。 B) 偷换概念 succeeded in maintaining sustainable financial aid programs 把“该模式的整体贡献”偷换成了“维持可持续的资助项目”——原文 their financial aid programs make them more accessible than ever 只是说援助项目使学校更可及，没说“可持续维持”， 更不是作者为之辩护的核心论据。 C) 无中生有 given priority to innovative programs for graduate studies 把 spurring innovation 中的 innovation 拼接成“研究生项目优先”，但原文从未谈及研究生项目优先级，是凭空捏造。 D) 无中生有 played a central role in attracting international applicants 套用了原文 played a central role 的句式，却把宾语换成了 attracting international applicants（吸引国际申请人），但原文从未提国际申请人，是用熟悉句式包装的新内容。
questions.hint: 回到原文定位题干关键词，比较选项与原文的含义。

questions.prompt: What do we learn about the initial proposals concerning the recent tax reform bill?

options.text: They would have stripped many students of life's chances.
They would have deducted graduate student loan interest.
They would have added to many students' financial burden.
They would have increased the number of tuition waivers.

questions.shortExplanation: The initial proposals would have made education unaffordable for many by taxing tuition waivers for graduate students and ending deductions for student loan interest.
questions.detailedExplanation:
【答案】 C （细节题）

【判型】 What do we learn about the initial proposals 问关于某物的具体信息，定位句即答案出处，属细节题。

【拆句】 主干 What do we learn about the initial proposals，concerning the recent tax reform bill 是 the initial proposals 的后置修饰。注意虚拟语气 would have made 暗示这些提议未实施，比对选项时四个选项都是 would have，与原文虚拟一致。

【定位】 The initial proposals would have made education unaffordable for many by taxing tuition waivers for graduate students and ending deductions for student loan interest.

最初的提议本来会通过对研究生学费减免征税、取消学生贷款利息抵扣，使许多人负担不起教育。

【选项】 A) 偷换概念 would have stripped many students of life's chances 把“加重经济负担”夸大为“剥夺人生机会”——原文 unaffordable for many 只到“许多人负担不起”，未到“剥夺人生机会”的程度，且 life's chances 范围过宽。 B) 与原文相反 would have deducted graduate student loan interest 把原文 ending deductions for student loan interest 中的“取消抵扣”反过来说成“抵扣”，方向完全相反。 C) ✓ 正确 would have made education unaffordable for many ↔

would have added to many students' financial burden taxing tuition waivers for graduate students and ending deductions for student loan interest ↔

financial burden unaffordable for many 与 added to many students' financial burden 在虚拟语气下完全等值，故选 C。 D) 与原文相反 would have increased the number of tuition waivers 与原文 taxing tuition waivers 相反——原文是对学费减免征税（变相缩减或削弱），选项却说“增加学费减免数量”， 方向相反。
questions.hint: 回到原文定位题干关键词，比较选项与原文的含义。

questions.prompt: What do the data show about elite colleges and universities?

options.text: Their graduates lack the rigor required for doing statistical analysis.
Their students prove to be inadequately prepared for their future careers.
Their focus on research is conducive to developing students' critical thinking.
Their liberal arts education enables graduates to excel in whatever field they are in.

questions.shortExplanation: The data are clear: a liberal arts education is great career preparation, both for excellent lifetime earnings and for satisfaction with the work. ... In fact, liberal arts graduates do extremely well in every imaginable field.
questions.detailedExplanation:
【答案】 D （细节题）

【判型】 What do the data show 询问数据呈现的客观结论，对应原文具体陈述句，属细节题。

【拆句】 主干 What do the data show about elite colleges and universities，about 短语限定讨论对象。注意题干用的是 data show（data 复数对应原文 The data are clear），属于细节呼应。

【定位】 The data are clear: a liberal arts education is great career preparation, both for excellent lifetime earnings and for satisfaction with the work. ... In fact, liberal arts graduates do extremely well in every imaginable field.

数据很清楚：博雅教育是出色的职业准备，既能带来优厚的终身收入，也能带来工作满意度。……事实上，博雅毕业生在每一个可以想象的领域都表现极佳。

【选项】 A) 与原文相反 Their graduates lack the rigor required for doing statistical analysis 与原文 rigorous analysis of data and facts（严谨的数据与事实分析能力）正相反——原文说博雅教育培养这种严谨，选项却说他们缺乏。 B) 与原文相反 Their students prove to be inadequately prepared for their future careers 与原文 a liberal arts education is great career preparation 正相反——原文说“出色的职业准备”，选项说“准备不充分”。

C) 无中生有 Their focus on research is conducive to developing students' critical thinking 借用了 scholarly research 和 critical thinking 两个原文词，拼出“院校以研究为重心、研究有助于培养批判性思维”——但原文只说博雅教育培养批判性思维，并未说研究是其重心，更未谈“研究→批判性思维”的因果。 D) ✓ 正确 liberal arts graduates do extremely well in every imaginable field ↔

Their liberal arts education enables graduates to excel in whatever field they are in a liberal arts education is great career preparation ↔

Their liberal arts education enables graduates to excel 预判“在任何领域都表现出色”，D 项 excel in whatever field they are in 是其精准同义替换，故选 D。
questions.hint: 回到原文定位题干关键词，比较选项与原文的含义。

questions.prompt: What is an advantage of providing financial aid for students?

options.text: Every student can choose the institution they wish to attend.
All students can benefit from a diversified student population.
All students will be able to earn a place on university campus.
Less privileged students will be more competitive at elite schools.

questions.shortExplanation: Beyond the virtue of access to those who have earned a place at these schools, the diversity of economic backgrounds enhances the education and experience of all of our students.
questions.detailedExplanation:
【答案】 B （细节题）

【选项】 A) 无中生有 Every student can choose the institution they wish to attend 谈“学生可以自由选择学校”，原文从未涉及“选校自由”这一层，是凭空捏造。
