↔ All students can benefit from a diversified student population the diversity of economic backgrounds↔ a diversified student population 原文明确说 all of our students 都从多样性中获益，与 B 项 All students can benefit 完全对位，故选 B。 C) 偷换概念 All students will be able to earn a place on university campus 把原文 those who have earned a spot（那些已凭实力争得席位的人）扩大为“全体学生都能争得席位” ——原文说的是 access 给了已经“earned”的人，并不是让所有人都能 earn。 D) 无中生有 Less privileged students will be more competitive at elite schools 谈“弱势学生在精英校竞争力更强”，原文只说资助让他们有 access、让全体学生从多样性中获益，并未对比“是否更具竞争力”。

items.title: 2022年6月六级第1套 · 仔细阅读 · 第二篇
items.passage:
When a group of Australians was asked why they believed climate change was not happening, about 36% said it was "common sense", according to a report published last year by the Commonwealth Scientific and Industrial Research Organization. This was the most popular reason for their opinion, with only 11% saying their belief that climate change was not happening was based on scientific research.

But what do we mean by an appeal to common sense? Presumably it's an appeal to rationality of some sort that forms the basis of more complex reasoning. The appeal to common sense, however, is usually nothing more than an appeal to thinking that just feels right, but what feels right to one person may not feel right to another. Whether it feels right is usually a reflection of the world view and ideologies we have internalised, and that frames how we interact with new ideas. When new ideas are in accord with what we already believe, they are more readily accepted. When they are not, they, and the arguments that lead to them, are more readily rejected.

We often mistake this automatic compatibility testing of new ideas with existing beliefs as an application of common sense, but, in reality, it is more about judging than thinking. As Nobelist Daniel Kahneman notes in Thinking, Fast and Slow, when we arrive at conclusions in this way, the outcomes also feel true, regardless of whether they are. We are not psychologically well equipped to judge our own thinking.

We are also highly susceptible to a range of cognitive biases such as giving preference to the first things that come to mind when making decisions or giving weight to evidence.

One way we can check our internal biases and inconsistencies is through the social verification of knowledge, in which we test our ideas in a rigorous and systematic way to see if they make sense not just to us, but to other people. The outstanding example of this socially shared cognition is science.

That does not mean that individuals are not capable of excellent thinking, nor does it mean no individual is rational. But the extent to which individuals can do this on their own is a function of how well integrated they are with communities of systematic inquiry in the first place. You can't learn to think well by yourself.

In matters of science at least, those who value their common sense over methodological, collaborative investigation imagine themselves to be more free in their thinking, unbound by involvement with the group, but in reality they are tightly bound by their capabilities and perspectives. We are smarter together than we are individually, and perhaps that's just common sense.

questions.prompt: What does the author intend to show by citing the findings from the report published last year?

options.text: People seldom appeal to rationality in their thinking.
It is often the case that truth lies in the hands of a few.

Few people know if climate change is really happening.

questions.shortExplanation: But what do we mean by an appeal to common sense? Presumably it's an appeal to rationality of some sort that forms the basis of more complex reasoning. The appeal to common sense, however, is usually nothing more than an appeal to thinking that just feels right.
questions.detailedExplanation:
【答案】 A （例证目的题）

【判型】 What does the author intend to show by citing the findings from the report 同时出现 "intend to show" 与 "citing"，典型的"作者引用例证想说明什么"句式。

【拆句】 Q51 主干是 "What does the author intend to show"，by 引导方式状语 "by citing the findings from the report published last year"，published last year 是过去分词作 report 的后置定语；结构平铺，无陷阱。

【定位】 But what do we mean by an appeal to common sense? Presumably it's an appeal to rationality of some sort that forms the basis of more complex reasoning. The appeal to common sense, however, is usually nothing more than an appeal to thinking that just feels right.

但我们说"诉诸常识"究竟意味着什么？大概是诉诸某种作为更复杂推理基础的理性吧。然而，所谓"诉诸常识"，往往不过是诉诸"感觉对"的想法罢了。

【选项】 A) ✓ 正确 about 36% said it was "common sense" ... only 11% saying their belief that climate change was not happening was based on scientific research

↔ People seldom appeal to rationality in their thinking The appeal to common sense, however, is usually nothing more than an appeal to thinking that just feels right

↔ appeal to rationality in their thinking 作者列调查只是"由头"，紧跟的转折句把"common sense"等同于"feels right"而非 rationality；合起来等于说"人们很少真的诉诸理性"，与 People seldom appeal to rationality in their thinking 直接对接。

B) 无中生有原文谈"大多数人凭感觉判断"，并未提及 truth lies in the hands of a few 这种"真理掌握在少数人手中"的命题。 C) 与原文相反作者把"常识"与"科学"对立，并贬低前者；选项却说二者是 two sides of a coin"一体两面"，与原文的对立关系正相反。 D) 答非所问 Few people know if climate change is really happening 谈的是"人们是否知道气候变化"，而题干问的是作者引用调查的目的——目的在论证"常识非理性"，不在论证"人们对气候变化的认知"。

questions.prompt: What is the appeal to common sense according to the author?

options.text: It is the basis for the internalisation of individuals' ideologies.
It is a series of conceptions formulated from complex reasoning.
It is collective wisdom that helps people interact with new ideas.

questions.shortExplanation: The appeal to common sense, however, is usually nothing more than an appeal to thinking that just feels right, but what feels right to one person may not feel right to another. Whether it feels right is usually a reflection of the world view and ideologies we have internalised.
questions.detailedExplanation:
【答案】 D （细节题）

【判型】 What is the appeal to common sense according to the author 直接问一个概念"是什么"，定义在文中可被直接定位回答。

【拆句】 Q52 主干 "What is the appeal to common sense"，according to the author 是介词短语作整句的状语，限定信息来源；句式简单。

【定位】 The appeal to common sense, however, is usually nothing more than an appeal to thinking that just feels right, but what feels right to one person may not feel right to another. Whether it feels right is usually a reflection of the world view and ideologies we have internalised.

然而所谓"诉诸常识"，往往不过是诉诸"感觉对"的想法罢了，可一个人觉得对，另一个人未必觉得对。是否觉得对，通常只是我们已经内化的世界观和意识形态的投射。

【选项】 A) 与原文相反原文是"内化的意识形态"决定"是否感觉对"——意识形态是因、感觉是果；选项却把诉诸常识当成 basis for the internalisation of individuals' ideologies，把因果颠倒过来。 B) 与原文相反原文 Presumably it's an appeal to rationality of some sort that forms the basis of more complex reasoning 是作者先假设的"理想状态"，紧随 however, is usually nothing more than 被否定；formulated from complex reasoning 恰是被否定的那一面。 C) 张冠李戴原文从未说 common sense 是 collective wisdom"集体智慧"；作者后文反而把集体智慧的代表给了"science"而非 common sense，是典型张冠李戴。

D) ✓ 正确 an appeal to thinking that just feels right ↔

something subjective based on what one perceives to be right what feels right to one person may not feel right to another ↔ something subjective 预判"凭感觉对的主观判断"与 something subjective based on what one perceives to be right 在两个语义点上完全对齐：subjective ↔ feels right 因人而异；perceives to be right ↔ feels right。

questions.prompt: What does Daniel Kahneman think is the problem of testing new ideas with existing beliefs?

options.text: It may lead to incorrect judgment.
It makes no use of common sense.
It fails to correct mistakes through serious reasoning.
It can produce psychologically unacceptable outcomes.

questions.shortExplanation: As Nobelist Daniel Kahneman notes in Thinking, Fast and Slow, when we arrive at conclusions in this way, the outcomes also feel true, regardless of whether they are. We are not psychologically well equipped to judge our own thinking. 正如诺贝尔奖得主丹尼尔·卡尼曼在《思考，快与慢》中所言，当我们以这种方式得出结论时，结果"感觉上是真的"，至于它们到底是不是真的并不重要。我们在心理上并不擅长审视自己的思考过程。
questions.detailedExplanation:
【答案】 A （细节题）

【判型】 What does Daniel Kahneman think is the problem 直接问某人对某事的看法，文中可定位到原话或转述。

【拆句】 Q53 主干 "What does Daniel Kahneman think"；think 后接省略 that 的宾语从句 "is the problem of testing new ideas with existing beliefs"，其中 of 短语作 the problem 的后置定语；testing... 为动名词作 of 的宾语。

【定位】 As Nobelist Daniel Kahneman notes in Thinking, Fast and Slow, when we arrive at conclusions in this way, the outcomes also feel true, regardless of whether they are. We are not psychologically well equipped to judge our own thinking. 正如诺贝尔奖得主丹尼尔·卡尼曼在《思考，快与慢》中所言，当我们以这种方式得出结论时，结果"感觉上是真的"，至于它们到底是不是真的并不重要。我们在心理上并不擅长审视自己的思考过程。

【选项】 A) ✓ 正确 the outcomes also feel true, regardless of whether they are ↔

It may lead to incorrect judgment it is more about judging than thinking ↔ incorrect judgment 两条语义在 P3 里共同作用：判断而非思考、结果感觉真但不一定真——合起来就是"该过程会带来错误判断"，对应 It may lead to incorrect judgment。

B) 答非所问 Kahneman 谈的是该过程的"问题"，不是评论它"用没用 common sense"；makes no use of common sense 把话题从"问题是什么"偷换为"是否使用了常识"。

C) 过度推断原文只说该过程产生的"感觉真"未必真，并未谈到能不能"通过严肃推理修正错误"—— 这是基于原文延展出去的额外命题。

D) 偷换概念 psychologically unacceptable outcomes 把原文 not psychologically well equipped（人在心理上没有能力）偷换成"心理上无法接受的结果"——一个谈"能力"， 一个谈"接受度"，貌似都有 psychologically 实则不同。

questions.prompt: What can we do to be less susceptible to cognitive biases?

options.text: Give equal weight to evidence of both sides in a conflict.
Provide convincing examples in developing an argument.
Establish socially shared cognition via scientific methods.
Avoid inconsistencies when addressing controversial issues.

questions.shortExplanation: One way we can check our internal biases and inconsistencies is through the social verification of knowledge, in which we test our ideas in a rigorous and systematic way to see if they make sense not just to us, but to other people. The outstanding example of this socially shared cognition is science. 我们能够检验自身内在偏差与矛盾的一种方式，是通过对知识的社会化检验：以严格、系统的方式检验我们的想法，看它们不仅对自己说得通，对别人也是否说得通。这种社会共享认知最杰出的例子就是科学。
questions.detailedExplanation:
【答案】 C （细节题）

【判型】 What can we do to be less susceptible to cognitive biases 问做法，原文有明确对策句可对应。

【拆句】 Q54 主干 "What can we do"；to be less susceptible to cognitive biases 是不定式作目的状语；be susceptible to 为固定搭配，意为"易受……影响"，less 修饰 susceptible，整体表示"少受影响"。

【定位】 One way we can check our internal biases and inconsistencies is through the social verification of knowledge, in which we test our ideas in a rigorous and systematic way to see if they make sense not just to us, but to other people. The outstanding example of this socially shared cognition is science. 我们能够检验自身内在偏差与矛盾的一种方式，是通过对知识的社会化检验：以严格、系统的方式检验我们的想法，看它们不仅对自己说得通，对别人也是否说得通。这种社会共享认知最杰出的例子就是科学。

【选项】 A) 无中生有 P4 只提到我们对证据有偏向，Give equal weight to evidence of both sides in a conflict 把它包装成"双方等量赋权"作为对策；原文从未给出这一对策。

B) 无中生有原文谈"用科学的社会共享认知去检验自己的想法"，并未提及在论证中 Provide convincing examples in developing an argument"举有说服力的例子"这一具体写作技巧。 C) ✓ 正确 through the social verification of knowledge ↔ Establish socially shared cognition we test our ideas in a rigorous and systematic way ↔ via scientific methods 预判"通过社会化检验、典型即科学"与 Establish socially shared cognition via scientific methods 在两个核心点上同义对齐——前半部分是手段，后半部分是手段的载体。 D) 偷换概念 Avoid inconsistencies when addressing controversial issues 把 internal biases and inconsistencies里的 inconsistencies 搬走，却换上一个原文没谈的 controversial issues 场景；并且对策从"通过社会化检验来检查"偷换成"直接避免不一致"。

【答案】 D （主旨题）

【拆句】 Q55 主干 "What message does the author try to convey"；at the end of the passage 是介词短语作地点状语，限定信息发生位置；try to convey 是"想要传达"，注意 try to 自带"主观意图"色彩，对应主旨题问法。

【选项】 A) 无中生有末段从未谈及"多元视角能激发人们对未知的兴趣"——stimulate people's interest in exploring the unknown 是被自造出的概念，与原文金句无关。 B) 以偏概全 Individuals can enhance their overall capabilities by interacting with others 把范围窄化为"提升个人综合能力"，遗漏了原文的"科学探究"语境与"克服局限"这一关键含义；末段强调的是"集体优于个人"，不是"通过互动让个人变强"。

items.title: 2022年6月六级第2套 · 选词填空
items.passage:
Thinking kind thoughts about yourself and your loved ones can prove beneficial for your overall wellbeing, empirical evidence has shown. Researchers carried out an investigation to explore the [26] _____ between having kind thoughts and a person's psychological state.

For the study, five groups of participants were presented with a different set of audio instructions, some of which encouraged the participants to think [27] _____ about themselves and others which persuaded them to think in a self-critical manner. After listening to the audio instructions, the participants were asked to answer a series of questions. These included whether they felt agitated, how likely they were to show kindness to themselves and how [28] _____ they felt to other individuals.

The participants who were instructed to think kindly about themselves were more likely to exhibit a bodily response associated with being relaxed and feeling safe. Their heart rates also dropped, which is a healthy sign of a heart that can respond flexibly to situations. Yet, [29] _____ , those who listened to the critical audio clips were noted as having a higher heart rate and sweat response afterwards, both of which [30] _____ feelings of threat and distress.

Having the ability to switch off the body's natural threat response can [31] _____ a person's immune system. This, in turn, gives them a greater likelihood of recovering quickly from illness. These findings help us to further understand some of our clinical trials research findings, where we show that individuals with [32] _____ depression benefit particularly from self-awareness-based [33] _____ therapy. They essentially learn to become more sympathetic to themselves.

The sense is that for people [34] _____ to depression, meeting their negative thoughts and feelings with [35] _____ is a radically different way; that these thoughts are not facts. It introduces a different way of being and knowing that is quite transformative for many people.

questions.prompt: Researchers carried out an investigation to explore the __(26)__ between having kind thoughts and a person's psychological state.
questions.shortExplanation: explore the correlation between A and B 是固定搭配
questions.detailedExplanation:
【答案】 G) correlation 名词

【词性槽】 定冠词 the 后 + 介词 between 前，须填名词

【依据】 explore the correlation between A and B 是固定搭配

题干 explore the __(26)__ between having kind thoughts and a person's psychological state 正是研究『两个变量之间的相关性』的标准说法，correlation between A and B 在学术英语中是高频搭配。

【竞争词】 E) compassion 词义虽贴主题，但与 between A and B 搭不上

compassion 表『同情心』，不能说『探索善念与心理状态之间的同情』，逻辑不通；且 compassion 在第 35 空有更精准的归宿，留着备用。

J) insulation 词义『绝缘/隔离』与研究主题完全无关

insulation 多用于物理/工程语境，放在 explore the __(26)__ between 中说『探索…之间的绝缘』明显荒谬。
questions.hint: 根据空格前后的词性、搭配与上下文选择词语；每个词最多使用一次。

questions.prompt: some of which encouraged the participants to think __(27)__ about themselves
questions.shortExplanation: 与后文 self-critical 形成正反对照
questions.detailedExplanation:
【答案】 B) amiably 副词

【词性槽】 动词 think 之后修饰动词，须填副词

【依据】 与后文 self-critical 形成正反对照

本句结构 some of which encouraged the participants to think __(27)__ about themselves and others which persuaded them to think in a self-critical manner ——前半『鼓励善待自己地想』、后半『劝其自我批判地想』，是一对反义。amiably （友好地）正与 self-critical（自我批判）相反，呼应主旨 Thinking kind thoughts about yourself。

【竞争词】 A) adversely 义为『不利地』，方向与 self-critical 同

adversely 偏负面，无法与后半 self-critical 构成对照；且第 29 空 yet 转折更需要它。

I) indignantly 义为『愤慨地』，色彩负面且不合主旨

indignantly 表强烈不满，与『善待自己』完全相反，逻辑不通。
questions.hint: 根据空格前后的词性、搭配与上下文选择词语；每个词最多使用一次。

questions.prompt: how __(28)__ they felt to other individuals
questions.shortExplanation: feel connected to sb 是高频固定搭配 how __(28)__ they felt to other individuals——『他们感到与他人有多紧密的联系』， feel connected to 是描述人际联结感的标准表达，与上句『对自己友善』并列考察人际维度，自然落地。
questions.detailedExplanation:
【答案】 F) connected 形容词

【词性槽】 系动词 felt 后作表语，且与 how 引导的程度副词搭配

【依据】 feel connected to sb 是高频固定搭配 how __(28)__ they felt to other individuals——『他们感到与他人有多紧密的联系』， feel connected to 是描述人际联结感的标准表达，与上句『对自己友善』并列考察人际维度，自然落地。

【竞争词】 H) fascinated fascinated 搭 by/with，不搭 to

fascinated to 不构成固定搭配；语义『对他人着迷』也不符合研究问卷情境。

K) lavish lavish 不能与 felt to 搭配

lavish 表『奢华的』，无法与『对他人感到』语义对接。
questions.hint: 根据空格前后的词性、搭配与上下文选择词语；每个词最多使用一次。

questions.prompt: Yet, __(29)__, those who listened to the critical audio clips were noted as having a higher heart rate
questions.shortExplanation: Yet 后承接转折，需『相反地』对接前段善念组的正面反应前段 The participants who were instructed to think kindly about themselves were more likely to exhibit a bodily response associated with being relaxed——善念组放松；本句 Yet, __(29)__, those who listened to the critical audio clips were noted as having a higher heart rate——批判组反而心率升高。adversely 在此 = 『反之、不利地』，把转折讲透。
questions.detailedExplanation:
【答案】 A) adversely 副词

【词性槽】 句首逗号隔开的独立修饰位，副词作状语

items.title: 2022年6月六级第2套 · 信息匹配
items.passage:
A) In the long view, the human relationship with forests has been one of brutal destruction, but even it carries elements of slow hope. In the Middle Ages, there was no shortage of timber in most parts of the world, and few saw cutting down forests as a problem. Yet in 1548 the people of Venice estimated that an important timber supply would last only 30 years at their current rate of usage— but different forest management would make it possible to meet the demand for many centuries to come. The idea of preserving resources came out of a concern for the future: a fear of using up resources faster than they could be replenished(补充 ).

B) Economic interests were at the core of this understanding of trees and forests. It would take more than three centuries before scientists began to understand that timber production is not the only, and possibly not the most important, function of forests. The late 19th and early 20th century saw an increasing recognition that forests serve as habitats for countless animal and plant species that all rely on each other. They take over protective functions against soil erosion and landslides( 塌⽅ ); they make a significant contribution to the water balance as they prevent surface runoff; they filter dirt particles, greenhouse gases and radioactive substances from the air; they produce oxygen; they provide spaces for recreation and they preserve historic and prehistoric remains. As a result, forests around the world have been set aside as parks or wilderness areas.

C) Recent years have seen a big change in our view of forests. Peter Wohlleben's book The Hidden Life of Trees (2015), an international bestseller, suggests that trees can warn each other of danger through a "wood wide web" of roots and fungi(真菌 ). They support each other through sharing of nutrients and information, and they even keep ancient stumps alive by feeding them solutions of sugars. Such insights have made us aware of deep ecological relationships between humans and the more-than-human world.

D) Awareness of ecologies is a recent phenomenon. It was not until the 1940s that the concept of the "environment" embracing all living and nonliving things developed. In the 1970s, the term "environment" gained currency, becoming widely adopted in the English and Romance languages, and as "Umwelt" ("surrounding world") in German. The emergence of the idea led to the rise of environmental agencies, regulations and environmental studies, and to environmental science as new, integrated academic disciplines. It was in 1956 that the very first bachelor of science in environmental studies was awarded, at the State University of New York College of Forestry at Syracuse. Since the 1970s—with the rise of "environmentalism"—environmental studies programmes have sprung up at hundreds of universities. There is (slow) hope in the fact that scholars from many different disciplines have adopted the term "environment" over the past decades. They are exploring intricate connections within and between complex ecologies, as well as the impact that human environment-making (through techno-industrial, economic and other manipulative developments) has had on the biosphere.

E) The rise of the idea of the environment and a scholarly understanding of ecological processes has influenced new technologies and also politics. We have come to ask questions about vulnerability and risk, world ecologies, and the relationship between nature and power. The search for an adequate response to climate change occupies centre stage in international diplomacy.

F) Social and environmental activists, scientists and indigenous groups have called the Paris Agreement of the United Nations Climate Change Conference in December 2015 insufficient, weak, or compromised. To some extent, they are right: climate change has already destroyed tens of thousands of livelihoods, and the situation will worsen in the near future for millions of mostly poorer people, who will join the ranks of those who have already been displaced by climate change and extreme weather events. But the Paris Conference nevertheless marked a historic step toward the recognition of the need for action on climate change, the cutting of carbon emissions, and world cooperation. There were 195 nations that came to the table in Paris and agreed to limits on emissions. Historically, nothing comparable had happened prior to this. Before the 20th century, a handful of scientists had been interested in the theoretical relationship between greenhouse gases and climate change, but only the empirical evidence accumulated since the late 20th century established a clear connection between the burning of fossil fuels and a vastly accelerated rise in global temperatures.

G) The current crisis is not the first that humans have encountered, and a look at the struggles with pollution in recent history reveals transformations that once seemed unimaginable. The "London fog" that came to define the capital through British novels and thrillers is in reality smog or smoke, a legacy of industrialisation. After a century of ignorance, London was hit by the Great Smog of December 1952—the worst air-pollution event in the history of the United Kingdom which caused the deaths of approximately 12,000 people. Shortly thereafter, public initiatives and political campaigns led to strict regulations and new laws, including the Clean Air Act (1956). Today, London has effectively reduced traffic emissions through the introduction of a Congestion Charge Zone in 2003, and an Ultra Low Emission Zone in 2019.

H) Scientific evidence that we are living in an era of climate change, resource exhaustion and potential ecological disaster is overwhelming. How do we motivate a public exhausted by never-ending scenarios of doom and disaster, when the challenges seem so huge and so impossible to solve? Statistics about extinction and the gloom of decline will not in themselves get us out of our often self-created ecological traps: instead, they are more likely to result in paralysis and inaction.

I) We need stories and histories of change and transformation: ecological stories that make us confront the fact that human power is potentially destructive, and that the survival of our species on this planet depends on the preservation of soil and water, and the habitats and ecological systems.

J) It is time that we showed successes and accelerations in ecological awareness, action and restoration: stories that include past successes and future visions about the rise of urban gardening and of renaturalised riverscapes, of successful protests against polluted air and water, of the rise of regional markets and slow food, and the planting of trees around the globe, of initiatives and enterprises that work towards ecological restoration. The reality of ecological curses seems far greater than the power of the hopes left at the bottom of Pandora's box. But if we believe that nothing can be changed, then we are giving up our opportunity to act.

K) Today's saving powers will not come from a deus ex machina( 解围之神 ). In an ever-more complex and synthetic world, our saving powers won't come from a single source, and certainly not from a too-big-to-fail approach or from those who have been drawn into the whirlpool of our age of speed. Hope can work as a wakeup call. It acknowledges setbacks. The concept of slow hope suggests that we can't expect things to change overnight. If the ever-faster exhaustion of natural resources (in ecological terms) and the "shrinking of the present" (in social terms) are urgent problems of humans, then cutting down on exhaustive practices and working towards a "stretching of the present" will be ways to move forward.

items.passage:
Since American idol star Taryn Southern started composing music with AI in 2017, musicians all over the world have begun wondering about the implications of AI and modern technology where music production is concerned. Using AI in the creation of music is perceived by some as a helpful tool and by others as almost "the beginning of the end".

In Taryn's case, AI software enabled her to communicate melodies and chords that she didn't know how to put together herself. The end product was therefore a collaborative effort, rather than a piece entirely produced by technology. Taryn's story has a distinctly positive feel that highlights the advantages of using AI in music production. It can serve as a source of inspiration, and as an ideal jumping-off point should a musician be hit with writer's block(⽂思枯竭 ).

Contrary to seeing AI as a tool, some musicians consider it to be hugely detrimental to the music scene. At the moment, because such technology is still so young, the music it's producing is not necessarily what we want to hear. In short, it's not of great quality. Those who have produced their own music, or even fans of authentic, artistic music, will also argue that a computer could never emulate the work (and human touch) of a true musician.

Music has been an integral part of the story of humans for ages; in fact, the first known piece of music is believed to be around 3,400 years old. Songs have long been used as a means of communicating messages and folk stories, covering everything from societal ethics to world history. Since many people see music as such an inherently human expression, it is often considered as too precious to impart to technology. The thought of a computer generating a "random" piece of music that hasn't been painstakingly created by an artist is almost seen as sacrilegious(亵渎神圣的 ).

Regardless of which side of the argument you fall on, it seems likely that the use of AI in music production will only become more frequent. Our modern world is preoccupied with technological advancements. Instead of shying away from the idea of this bleak future, the best approach to take is one of optimism and curiosity. While there are always bound to be stubborn old-school musicians who refuse to use tech, music producers should consider AI as something to be embraced. AI music software is still very much in its infancy, but with more investors interested in the development and outcomes of such technology, and considering the rapid growth rate of other tech advances in recent years, it's only a matter of time before AI-produced music is seen as the new norm.

items.passage:
A few weeks ago, a well-meaning professor tried to explain the physiological process behind viruses and the human body in a tweet and was immediately criticized for a mistake in his information. He then issued an apology and deleted his erroneous tweet.

Communicating science beyond the academic bubble is necessary to augmenting public understanding of health and environmental issues and helping individuals make well-informed personal decisions.

However, scientists who engage in science communication must acknowledge that even in their area, their expertise is deep but narrow. They need to recognize the constraints in their own knowledge. That is not to suggest that they only write or present on their own research, but rather, that they consult with an expert if the topic is outside of their discipline. Fact-checking with a scientist who works in the specialty will prevent the unintentional spread of misinformation, and the process of doing so may yield tiny pieces of interesting new information that can be incorporated.

Some have argued that the public is not educated enough to understand scientific information, especially for any complex phenomena, but this is absurd. Science instruction can be found at all levels of public education with most secondary schools offering classes on biology, physics, and chemistry. If anything, social media has shown that the public craves knowledge based on a solid scientific foundation. Even the public discourse that follows most scientific articles shows that online readers can understand even the most baffling of scientific principles.

It is equally imperative to emphasize that being an expert on a topic does not automatically make a scholar qualified to communicate it to a nonscientific audience. A number of scientists recently have been offering public-aimed explanations of scientific phenomena. Even though they have appropriate credentials, they often do very little in the way of explaining. One biologist shared an intricate analogy involving a library, books, paper, a recipe, ingredients, and a cake to explain the process behind vaccines. Any explanation that requires a written key to keep track of what each item represents is not a clear example for public consumption.

Science communication is a science in and of itself. It requires rigorous training and instruction. A scientist should take communication courses that can teach a person how to identify and eliminate jargon and how to develop effective analogies to explain complex concepts. One cannot assume communication expertise—imagine if someone just decided that they were a physicist and started trying to contribute to the field without the necessary background. Doing a poor job communicating science to the public will only create confusion and widen the gap between science and society, a gap that scientists are trying to close.

questions.prompt: What does the author say about communicating science to the general public?

【判型】 What does the author say about communicating science to the general public? 问的是「作者对某话题说了什么」，要求回到原文找出作者关于这件事的明确表态，属于细节理解。

【拆句】 Q51 是简单的 What 引导特殊疑问句，主干是 the author say about 后接动名词短语 communicating science to the general public，无从句、无否定、无陷阱。

【定位】 Communicating science beyond the academic bubble is necessary to augmenting public understanding of health and environmental issues and helping individuals make well-informed personal decisions.

把科学传播到学术圈外，是增进公众对健康与环境议题理解、帮助个人做出明智决策的必要途径。

【选项】 A) 无中生有 keep abreast of the latest scientific developments 把「最新科学进展」塞进选项， 而 P2 只说提升理解、辅助决策，从未提及 latest developments。

B) ✓ 正确 necessary to augmenting public understanding of health and environmental issues ↔

a necessary means to improve their understanding of scientific issues a necessary means to improve their understanding of scientific issues 同时命中预判的「必要性」与「提升理解」两条语义槽，无多余成分，是定位句的标准同义改写。 C) 偷换概念 get them more involved in academic debates on environmental problems 把原文 「帮助个人做明智决策」偷换为「让公众参与学术辩论」，方向完全相反——原文恰恰是要把科学带到学术圈外，而非把公众拉进学术辩论。

D) 张冠李戴 augment scientists' influence beyond the academic circle 把「augment 的对象」 从原文的 public understanding 偷换为 scientists' influence——augment 这个词留下了，受益人却换了，是典型「同词不同对象」陷阱。

【拆句】 Q52 主干 What does the author advise scientists to do，后接不定式短语 to deal with topics outside of their specialty 表目的，整体直白。

【定位】 That is not to suggest that they only write or present on their own research, but rather, that they consult with an expert if the topic is outside of their discipline.

这并不是说他们只能写或讲自己的研究，而是说，如果话题超出本人学科范围，他们应当请教该领域专家。

【选项】 A) 无中生有 Write or present on them from new angles 凭空加入 new angles 这一限定，原文 they only write or present on their own research 是作者要排除的误读，且无任何 「新角度」之意。

B) 偷换概念 Utilize information from diverse sources 把作者明确指出的「咨询专家 + 事实核查」 泛化为「使用多元来源信息」，方向被悄悄稀释——作者强调的是「找对人」，不是 「找够多源头」。 C) ✓ 正确 consult with an expert if the topic is outside of their discipline ↔

Turn to a specialist for professional help Turn to a specialist for professional help 把预判的「请教 + 该领域专家」两要素逐一对上，且 specialist 与 specialty 同根，符合作者「领域内行家」的限定。

D) 张冠李戴 Fact-check with colleagues in their field 保留 Fact-check 这一动词（直接借自原文 Fact-checking with a scientist who works in the specialty），但把对象偷换为 colleagues in their field——原文恰恰强调因为话题在 their field 之外，才要找该话题所在领域（specialty）的专家。
questions.hint: 回到原文定位题干关键词，比较选项与原文的含义。

questions.prompt: What does the author say we can learn from social media?

options.text: A solid academic foundation is essential to understanding baffling scientific principles.
Modern technology has facilitated communication between scientists and the public.
Scientific articles have gained increasing popularity among the general public.
The public's understanding of science is much better than some have claimed.

questions.shortExplanation: If anything, social media has shown that the public craves knowledge based on a solid scientific foundation. Even the public discourse that follows most scientific articles shows that online readers can understand even the most baffling of scientific principles.
questions.detailedExplanation:
【答案】 D （细节题）

【判型】 What does the author say we can learn from social media? 问的是「从某事例中能得出什么结论」，本质仍是回到原文找作者就 social media 给出的论断句，属于细节而非推断。

【拆句】 Q53 主干 What… we can learn from social media，宾语从句简单，无陷阱。

【定位】 If anything, social media has shown that the public craves knowledge based on a solid scientific foundation. Even the public discourse that follows most scientific articles shows that online readers can understand even the most baffling of scientific principles.

如果说有什么的话，社交媒体反而表明，公众渴望以扎实科学基础为支撑的知识。甚至大多数科学文章后面的公众讨论都显示，在线读者能够理解最难懂的科学原理。

【选项】 A) 与原文相反 A solid academic foundation is essential to understanding baffling scientific principles 把原文「公众渴望基于科学的知识」误读为「必须具备学术根基才能理解科学」——原文是「公众主动 craves 知识」，不是「没有 foundation 就不行」。 B) 偷换概念 Modern technology has facilitated communication between scientists and the public 把 social media 上位概括为 modern technology，又把「公众理解力」偷换为 「双向沟通」，原文从未谈及 facilitated communication。

C) 以偏概全 Scientific articles have gained increasing popularity among the general public 把原文用作佐证的 the public discourse that follows most scientific articles 偷换为 「科学文章越来越受欢迎」——原文谈的是文章后面的「公众讨论显示理解力」，不是文章本身受欢迎程度。 D) ✓ 正确 online readers can understand even the most baffling of scientific principles ↔

The public's understanding of science is much better than some have claimed Some have argued that the public is not educated enough to understand scientific information… but this is absurd

↔ much better than some have claimed The public's understanding of science is much better than some have claimed 把作者用 social media 反驳「公众不够聪明」的结论一一对应——选项里 some have claimed 与原文 Some have argued 同源指代，结论同向。
questions.hint: 回到原文定位题干关键词，比较选项与原文的含义。

questions.prompt: What does the example of the biologist who shared an intricate analogy show?

options.text: It is helpful to use illustrations in explaining scientific phenomena.
It is imperative to have appropriate titles to explain scientific issues.
A learned scholar is not necessarily a qualified science communicator.
A nonscientific audience cannot duly understand principles of science.

questions.shortExplanation: It is equally imperative to emphasize that being an expert on a topic does not automatically make a scholar qualified to communicate it to a nonscientific audience.
questions.detailedExplanation:
【答案】 C （例证目的题）

【判型】 What does the example of the biologist who shared an intricate analogy show? 直接问「这个例子说明了什么」，是典型例证目的题。

【拆句】 Q54 主干 What does the example show，example 后接 of 短语 + who 引导的定语从句修饰 biologist，从句虽长但仅作识别身份用。

【定位】 It is equally imperative to emphasize that being an expert on a topic does not automatically make a scholar qualified to communicate it to a nonscientific audience.

同样必须强调的是，成为某话题的专家并不自动使学者具备向非科学受众传播该话题的资格。

【选项】 A) 与原文相反 It is helpful to use illustrations in explaining scientific phenomena 把「复杂类比」 当成正面建议，与作者用此例所要表达的「这种类比反而不清晰」相反——作者明确说 not a clear example for public consumption。 B) 偷换概念 It is imperative to have appropriate titles to explain scientific issues 把原文 appropriate credentials 偷换为 appropriate titles，且作者强调的恰恰是「光有 credentials 不够」，本选项反而说「必须有合适头衔」，方向与作者完全相反。

C) ✓ 正确 being an expert on a topic does not automatically make a scholar qualified to communicate it to a nonscientific audience

↔ A learned scholar is not necessarily a qualified science communicator Even though they have appropriate credentials, they often do very little in the way of explaining.

↔ A learned scholar is not necessarily a qualified science communicator A learned scholar is not necessarily a qualified science communicator 把作者「专家≠科普者」的论点压缩成一句格言式陈述，与论点句一对一。 D) 张冠李戴 A nonscientific audience cannot duly understand principles of science 把矛头指向受众理解力不足，与本段乃至 P4 的论调（公众有理解力，问题在科学家不会讲）相反；本题考点是「专家≠科普者」，与受众能力无关。
questions.hint: 回到原文定位题干关键词，比较选项与原文的含义。

questions.prompt: What does the author suggest scientists do to close the gap between science and society?

options.text: Make appropriate use of scientific terms.

questions.shortExplanation: A scientist should take communication courses that can teach a person how to identify and eliminate jargon and how to develop effective analogies to explain complex concepts.
questions.detailedExplanation:
【答案】 D （细节题）

【判型】 What does the author suggest scientists do to close the gap between science and society? 仍是问「作者建议做什么」，是对原文末段建议句的事实复述。

【拆句】 Q55 主干 What does the author suggest scientists do，后接不定式 to close the gap between science and society 表目的，suggest 后接省略 that 的从句结构 scientists (should) do，是六级常考的虚拟语气省略，需要识别。

【定位】 A scientist should take communication courses that can teach a person how to identify and eliminate jargon and how to develop effective analogies to explain complex concepts.

科学家应当修习传播课程，这些课程能教人如何识别并消除行话、如何构造有效的类比以解释复杂概念。

【选项】 A) 与原文相反 Explain complex concepts scientifically 把建议对象偷换为「科学地解释复杂概念」 ——原文要做的恰好相反，是用 effective analogies 把复杂概念变得通俗，而不是「更科学地」讲。 B) 与原文相反 Make appropriate use of scientific terms 与作者建议背道而驰——原文明确说 identify and eliminate jargon，选项却让科学家「合理使用术语」，方向反置。 C) 以偏概全 Take courses in public speaking 把原文 communication courses 偷换为 public speaking——「沟通课」覆盖书面/口头/类比/受众分析等多个维度，而 public speaking 只是其中一种，且方向更窄。 D) ✓ 正确 take communication courses that can teach a person how to identify and eliminate jargon and how to develop effective analogies

↔ Develop communication skills Science communication is a science in and of itself. It requires rigorous training and instruction.

↔ Develop communication skills Develop communication skills 用最高一级的概括把原文末段全部建议吃下，且与段首主张 Science communication is a science in and of itself 完全同向，是稳妥的正确答案。
questions.hint: 回到原文定位题干关键词，比较选项与原文的含义。

items.title: 2022年9月六级第1套 · 选词填空
items.passage:
The now extinct passenger pigeon has the dubious honor of being the last species anyone ever expected to disappear. At one point, there were more passenger pigeons than any other species of bird. Rough [26] _____ of their population went as high as five billion and they accounted for around 40 percent of the total indigenous bird population of North America in the early 19th century.

Despite their huge population, passenger pigeons were [27] _____ to human intrusion into their nesting territory. Their nests were shabby things and two weeks after the eggs [28] _____ , the parent pigeons would abandon their offspring, leaving them to take care of themselves. People discovered that these baby pigeons were really tasty, and the adult birds were also quite [29] _____ . First the Native Americans and then the transplanted Europeans came to consider the birds a great [30] _____ .

By the 1850s, commercial trapping of passenger pigeons was proceeding at an [31] _____ pace. Hundreds of thousands of the birds were being harvested every day to be made into popular pigeon pies. In addition, large [32] _____ of the pigeons' nesting territory were being cleared away for planting crops and creating pasture land. As numerous as the passenger pigeons were, they were not an [33] _____

resource. By the 1880s, it was noticed that the bird population had become seriously [34] _____ . The last passenger pigeons killed in the wild were shot in 1899.

Eventually those billions and billions of birds shrank to a single remaining [35] _____ , a passenger pigeon named Martha, who died on September 1,1914, in captivity at the Cincinnati Zoo. In addition to being the end of an era, it was also the first time humans were able to exactly time the extinction of a species.

questions.prompt: Rough __(26)__ of their population went as high as five billion
questions.shortExplanation: 估算数量的专用词
questions.detailedExplanation:
【答案】 L) estimates 名词

【词性槽】 主语位置的复数名词

【依据】 估算数量的专用词

estimates of their population 即 "对其种群数量的估算"，与下文 went as high as five billion 给出一个具体估算上限完全对应，rough estimates 也是常见搭配。

【竞争词】 K) excerpts 搭配对象错

excerpts 是文章节选，对象为文本，不能修饰 population；且 rough excerpts 在英语里也不成搭配。
questions.hint: 根据空格前后的词性、搭配与上下文选择词语；每个词最多使用一次。

questions.prompt: passenger pigeons were __(27)__ to human intrusion into their nesting territory
questions.shortExplanation: vulnerable to 固定搭配 + 让步逻辑
questions.detailedExplanation:
【答案】 A) vulnerable 形容词

【词性槽】 were + ___ + to 表语形容词

【依据】 vulnerable to 固定搭配 + 让步逻辑

be vulnerable to 是固定搭配 "易受……影响"；句首 Despite their huge population 已用 despite 标出让步，主句必须给出 "虽多却脆弱" 的反差，vulnerable 正合此意。

【竞争词】 E) robust 搭配 + 逻辑双错

robust 不与 to 搭配，且语义是 "强健的"，与 despite 让步要求的 "脆弱" 反转完全相反。

【易错】 最具迷惑性的错误词是 E) —— 把 vulnerable 与 robust 看反。vulnerable 与 robust 都是描述生物的形容词，词义相反；只盯 "形容动物状态" 而忘了 Despite their huge population 的让步要求，就会反向填 robust；防坑口诀：despite 之后必反差。
questions.hint: 根据空格前后的词性、搭配与上下文选择词语；每个词最多使用一次。

questions.prompt: two weeks after the eggs __(28)__, the parent pigeons would abandon their offspring
questions.shortExplanation: 鸟蛋孵化的固定搭配
questions.detailedExplanation:
【答案】 I) hatched 动词

【词性槽】 时间状语从句缺谓语动词

【依据】 鸟蛋孵化的固定搭配

主语是 the eggs，下一句又紧跟 the parent pigeons would abandon their offspring， 逻辑链是 "蛋孵出 → 幼鸟出生 → 父母两周后弃之而去"，只有 hatched（孵化）能让这条链成立。

【竞争词】 J) expired 语义反了

expired 表 "死亡/失效"，若蛋死了下文就不存在 their offspring 让父母遗弃，前后矛盾。

N) depleted 搭配错位

depleted 主语通常是资源/数量，不能说 "蛋被耗尽"；而且后文 the bird population had become seriously __(34)__ 才是它真正的归宿。
questions.hint: 根据空格前后的词性、搭配与上下文选择词语；每个词最多使用一次。

questions.prompt: the adult birds were also quite __(29)__
questions.shortExplanation: 与幼鸽好吃形成并列
questions.detailedExplanation:
【答案】 M) edible 形容词

【词性槽】 系动词 were 后接表语

【依据】 与幼鸽好吃形成并列

前一句 People discovered that these baby pigeons were really tasty 已说幼鸽好吃，连词 also 表 "成鸟也……"，下一句又紧跟 came to consider the birds a great __(30)__ 把它们视作佳肴，edible（可食用的）与 "好吃/佳肴" 一脉相承。

【竞争词】 A) vulnerable 留给 27 题

vulnerable 在 passenger pigeons were __(27)__ to human intrusion 中与 to 形成 vulnerable to 固定搭配，是 27 题的标配，这里硬塞会让 27 题无解。

E) robust 语义跑题

robust（强健的）与上下文 "可吃—佳肴" 这一主线无关，且后文紧接说人类把它们当美味，与 "强健" 没有逻辑承接。
questions.hint: 根据空格前后的词性、搭配与上下文选择词语；每个词最多使用一次。

questions.prompt: came to consider the birds a great __(30)__
questions.shortExplanation: 与 tasty/edible 同色升级
questions.detailedExplanation:
【答案】 O) delicacy 名词

【词性槽】 consider sb/sth + ___ 的宾补名词

【依据】 与 tasty/edible 同色升级

前两句已铺垫 these baby pigeons were really tasty 和 the adult birds were also quite __(29)__ 即可食用，结论自然是把它们视为 a great delicacy（一道美味佳肴）。

【竞争词】 F) refuge 语义脱轨

refuge 指 "避难所"，与 "被吃掉" 的语境完全相反；把动物当 refuge 在逻辑上不通。
questions.hint: 根据空格前后的词性、搭配与上下文选择词语；每个词最多使用一次。

questions.prompt: By the 1850s, commercial trapping of passenger pigeons was proceeding at an __(31)__ pace
questions.shortExplanation: 前所未有的速度
questions.detailedExplanation:
【答案】 B) unprecedented 形容词

【词性槽】 冠词 + ___ + 名词作定语

【依据】 前所未有的速度

下一句 Hundreds of thousands of the birds were being harvested every day 用 "每天数十万只" 直接量化了这种空前的捕猎规模，an unprecedented pace（以前所未有的速度）正与之匹配，且 at an unprecedented pace 是地道搭配。

【竞争词】 H) infinite 程度过头且搭配怪

infinite 指 "无限的"，pace 一旦无限就不再是速度而成悖论；且 infinite 更适合修饰 resource，将留给 33 题。
questions.hint: 根据空格前后的词性、搭配与上下文选择词语；每个词最多使用一次。

questions.prompt: large __(32)__ of the pigeons' nesting territory were being cleared away
questions.shortExplanation: 大片土地的专用搭配
questions.detailedExplanation:
【答案】 C) tracts 名词

【词性槽】 形容词 + 名词 + of 结构

【依据】 大片土地的专用搭配

tracts of land 是固定表达，指 "大片土地"，与 large __(32)__ of the pigeons' nesting territory were being cleared away for planting crops and creating pasture land 中 "被开垦为农田和牧场" 的语境严丝合缝。

【竞争词】 G) plazas 语义场不符

plazas 指 "城镇广场"，是城市建筑用语，无法描述森林/筑巢地被砍伐开垦的乡野场景。

K) excerpts 对象错配

excerpts 指 "文章节选"，对象是文本而非土地，与 nesting territory 不搭配。
questions.hint: 根据空格前后的词性、搭配与上下文选择词语；每个词最多使用一次。

questions.prompt: As numerous as the passenger pigeons were, they were not an __(33)__ resource
questions.shortExplanation: 无穷资源呼应数量再多也有尽前半句让步 As numerous as the passenger pigeons were 与主句 "they were not an __(33)__ resource" 形成转折，逻辑应为 "虽多但并非用之不竭"，infinite resource（无尽资源）正是这个反转点；且为下文 the bird population had become seriously __(34)__ 的锐减做铺垫。
questions.detailedExplanation:
【答案】 H) infinite 形容词

【词性槽】 an + ___ + 名词的形容词

【依据】 无穷资源呼应数量再多也有尽前半句让步 As numerous as the passenger pigeons were 与主句 "they were not an __(33)__ resource" 形成转折，逻辑应为 "虽多但并非用之不竭"，infinite resource（无尽资源）正是这个反转点；且为下文 the bird population had become seriously __(34)__ 的锐减做铺垫。

【竞争词】 M) edible 可食用不构成逻辑反转

edible resource（可食用资源）与前半句 "数量众多" 之间不形成 "虽多但不取之不尽" 的让步— 转折逻辑，且 edible 真正用武之地在 29 题描述成鸟。

【易错】 最具迷惑性的错误词是 M) —— 无视让步逻辑只挑元音。33 题 they were not an __(33)__ resource 中 an 让 M edible 和 H infinite 都满足元音条件，若忽略前半 As numerous as the passenger pigeons were 的让步逻辑，很容易误填 edible；防坑：看到 As…as 让步必找反义。
questions.hint: 根据空格前后的词性、搭配与上下文选择词语；每个词最多使用一次。

questions.prompt: it was noticed that the bird population had become seriously __(34)__
questions.shortExplanation: 数量被大量耗减上文 Hundreds of thousands of the birds were being harvested every day 加上大片栖息地被砍伐，必然导致种群锐减；depleted 表 "被耗尽/锐减的"，与下文 The last passenger pigeons killed in the wild were shot in 1899 的灭绝倒计时呼应。
questions.detailedExplanation:
【答案】 N) depleted 形容词

【词性槽】 had become + 副词 + ___

【依据】 数量被大量耗减上文 Hundreds of thousands of the birds were being harvested every day 加上大片栖息地被砍伐，必然导致种群锐减；depleted 表 "被耗尽/锐减的"，与下文 The last passenger pigeons killed in the wild were shot in 1899 的灭绝倒计时呼应。
questions.hint: 根据空格前后的词性、搭配与上下文选择词语；每个词最多使用一次。

questions.prompt: Eventually those billions and billions of birds shrank to a single remaining __(35)__, a passenger pigeon named Martha
questions.shortExplanation: 仅存的个体/标本同位语 a passenger pigeon named Martha 把空位释义为 "一只名叫 Martha 的旅鸽"， specimen 在生物学语境下正好表 "个体/标本"，与 "the last passenger pigeons killed in the wild" 后所剩唯一一只的画面相称。
questions.detailedExplanation:
【答案】 D) specimen 名词

【词性槽】 形容词 + 名词作宾语

【依据】 仅存的个体/标本同位语 a passenger pigeon named Martha 把空位释义为 "一只名叫 Martha 的旅鸽"， specimen 在生物学语境下正好表 "个体/标本"，与 "the last passenger pigeons killed in the wild" 后所剩唯一一只的画面相称。

【竞争词】 F) refuge 语义指向偏离

refuge 指 "避难所"，是地点概念，无法被同位语 "a passenger pigeon named Martha" 解释，且与 shrank to a single 的 "萎缩到一只" 这个个体数概念不匹配。
questions.hint: 根据空格前后的词性、搭配与上下文选择词语；每个词最多使用一次。

items.title: 2022年9月六级第1套 · 信息匹配
items.passage:
A) As computer coding has become an increasingly sought-after skill, more K-12 schools are working it into their curriculums. Some states have considered allowing students to forgo(放弃) foreign language for coding classes, despite opposition from educators.

B) There's a debate over whether it's appropriate to teach coding in elementary schools, with fierce opinions on each side. When it comes to allowing coding to fill foreign language requirements, though, most educators agree: Coding should be added to curriculums, but not at the expense of foreign language classes.

C) The idea is that computer programming is a language, allowing people to communicate with machines and programs. It's the language of the 21st century and more valuable than a natural language, some advocates argue. The computer science field is growing faster than schools can keep up because of budget constraints and a lack of skills training for teachers.

D) According to the 2016 U.S. News/Raytheon STEM Index, computer science jobs have helped boost wages in the U.S., and computer-related jobs hold the top seven positions in STEM fields for highest number of workers. Foreign language interest, on the other hand, is declining for the first time since 1995. The number of higher education language enrollments declined between 2009 and 2013 by more than 111,000 spots, according to the Modern Language Association of America.

E) "I think the opportunity to give people a choice is important," says Florida state Senator Jeremy Ring, who introduced a bill last year that would allow Florida students to choose between foreign language and coding classes for the purpose of university admissions requirements, "I think if you're going to give two years of language in high school, you might as well do computer coding."

F) The Florida bill died this year after passing 35:5 in the state Senate when the full Legislature failed to take action. It would have been the first state to try this initiative. Ring says that although he will be out of office, an identical bill will be reintroduced within the next year by others on his behalf. "In the speech I gave on the Senate floor, I said, 'We can be the first state to do this, or we can be the 50th state to do it. It's our choice. It's going to happen,'" Ring says.

G) A Kentucky bill similar to the one in Florida was met with complaints from educators, and was then amended to promote computer science education initiatives with no mention of foreign language requirements. Instead, the state will provide support for higher quality certified teachers for programming classes. Under the Washington bill, public universities would accept two years of computer science classes in place of two years of foreign language for admission purposes. A report detailing the opinions of state university officials is due to the Legislature by November 2017.

H) Texas passed a bill in 2013 that allows students to substitute computer coding only after they have attempted and performed poorly in a foreign language class. Srini Mandyam, CTO and co-founder of kid-friendly instructional coding company Tynker, believes allowing students to forgo foreign language because they struggle with it is unproductive because every subject, whether art, math or language, is a significant contribution to a well-rounded existence. "Many students don't fare well with algebra but we never discuss eliminating it or … say chemistry is now counted as an algebra class," he said via email. "We teach algebra because it's important and we should teach foreign language and coding for the same reason. Exposure to a wide breadth of subjects and material results in well-rounded students who are able to make informed decisions … about what they want to pursue."

I) Computer science courses already fulfill a math or science high school graduation requirement in 28 states and the District of Columbia, up from only 12 states in 2013. And while advocates of the bills say they should count as foreign language instead, opponents stress the importance of balancing computer and foreign language skills.

J) Studies show that bilingualism( 双语 ) correlates with cognitive development, intelligence, memory and problem solving abilities, according to the American Council on the Teaching of Foreign Languages. A 2007 study showed that foreign language students outperformed their non-foreign language peers on standardized tests after only two to three years of study. And while a 2014 report from German and American universities suggests that programmers are using language (but not mathematical) regions of the brain when understanding code, critics remain wary. They say that regardless of cognitive functions, being monolingual is a disadvantage in the increasingly international economy, even if English has become the de facto(事实上的 ) language of business.

K) "Our world is shrinking but its problems are really growing," says ACTFL National Language Teacher of the Year Ted Zarrow, who teaches high school Latin in Westwood, Massachusetts, and has also studied Spanish, French, German, Italian and Greek. "We need to find a way to put ourselves at the global table and to treat each other with mutual respect. And learning languages allows us to do that because language is not part of culture, language is culture."

L) Even with the benefits and skill sets languages provide, recruiters and employers value computer skills more. According to the National Association of Colleges and Employers' 2016 report, study abroad and foreign language fluency were not very influential in the employee hiring processes, but 55 percent of employers looked for computer skills on applicants' resumes. However, although 2016 computer science graduates can expect to make the second highest starting salary compared with other jobs this year, the Bureau of Labor predicts the demand for computer programmers will decrease 8 percent or by 26,500 jobs by 2024.

M) Ring says foreign language skills are important, but expresses doubt that school districts could work both coding and language into their curriculum in a significant way because they lack the time in the school day. "Nothing against language," he says. "I just think it's something you have to start early and not just have something that you do for a couple of years in high school," he says.

N) Zarrow agrees that foreign language education should begin earlier, but says it is possible to work both computer programming and foreign language learning into schools evenly. He suggests an immersive, dual language program where students spend half the day in English and half the day in another language, as several schools around the country have successfully implemented. "The study of language fosters a respect for diversity, a respect for ethnicity and really a respect for language," Zarrow says.

O) Though the benefits of computer programming skills are vast, foreign language and coding experts agree that computer science should be negotiated into curriculums rather than replacing foreign language outright. Mandyam says the two skill sets are essential but unrelated. "Coding is an incredibly important 21st century skill for our kids to learn, and that's why we spend so much time trying to teach it," Mandyam says via email. "But I believe it is the same as or even really comparable to learning a foreign language. It would be a shame to lose something so important for the sake of adding something else, even something as important as coding. Clearly, education leaders must figure out a way to teach both."

items.title: 2022年9月六级第1套 · 仔细阅读 · 第一篇
items.passage:
The U.S. and China don't agree on much these days. Germany and France share a border and a currency but are frequently at odds. The U.K. and India like to march to their own drum. But there's one issue on which all these countries see eye to eye: Technology companies are too big, too powerful, and too profitable. And that power is only likely to intensify, leaving governments with no choice but to confront it head-on by taking the companies to court, passing new competition laws, and perhaps even breaking up the tech giants.

China is the latest to implement an anti-trust crackdown, unveiling anti-monopoly rules last month. The draft rules followed the surprise suspension of a $37 billion stock offering by billionaire Jack Ma's Ant Group Co., making clear that no company can evade the government's regulation. The moves in China coincide with accelerating efforts in the U.S. and Europe to rein in Amazon.com, Apple, Facebook, and Google.

"The big get bigger and bigger but without being better," says Andreas Schwab, a German member of the European Parliament who championed a 2014 resolution to break up Google. "Growing economic power, growing influence on local markets all over the world, and a growing concern of competitors and consumers altogether have made it happen now."

In this new anti-trust era, the old focus on pricing power no longer applies, because several of the biggest tech companies have established trillion-dollar monopolies by charging consumers next to nothing. Tech giants are increasingly assuming powerful positions in banking, finance, advertising, retail, and other markets that force smaller businesses to rely on their platforms to reach customers.

For years, Europe alone confronted the power of digital giants. Governments were alarmed that European companies were failing to match Silicon Valley's innovations or to stop Google and Facebook from vacuuming up personal data and, with that, advertising revenue. Led by Margrethe Vestager, the European Union's competition chief, countries have sought to police the market and encourage fair play.

In China the crackdown has been driven at least partly by fear that the homegrown tech industry is becoming too powerful. The country has long championed Alibaba and Tencent, but their massive accumulation of data on the Chinese citizenry is a growing concern for Beijing.

In the U.S., a new breed of anti-trust experts argues that consideration should be given to privacy, control over data, workers' rights, and the overall impact on smaller companies. And the public in general has grown increasingly skeptical of social media companies. More than 60% say the sector has a negative effect on the country, and almost half want more regulation for social media, according to a 2020 Pew Research Center study.

questions.prompt: What does the author say is the issue all major economic powers have to address?

options.text: How to ensure the sustainable growth of their tech giants.
How to keep the competitiveness of their tech companies.
How to break up the powerful giant tech companies.
How to stop tech companies from gaining monopoly.

questions.shortExplanation: But there's one issue on which all these countries see eye to eye: Technology companies are too big, too powerful, and too profitable. And that power is only likely to intensify, leaving governments with no choice but to confront it head-on by taking the companies to court, passing new competition laws, and perhaps even breaking up the tech giants.
questions.detailedExplanation:
【答案】 D （细节题）

【判型】 What does the author say is the issue all major economic powers have to address? 直接问"是什么 issue"，是对作者陈述的具体内容的提取。

【拆句】 主干是 What does the author say is the issue，all major economic powers have to address 是省略 that 的定语从句修饰 the issue；have to address 是"必须解决"，不是"可以解决"，程度词不能弱化。

【定位】 But there's one issue on which all these countries see eye to eye: Technology companies are too big, too powerful, and too profitable. And that power is only likely to intensify, leaving governments with no choice but to confront it head-on by taking the companies to court, passing new competition laws, and perhaps even breaking up the tech giants.

但有一个议题，所有这些国家看法一致：科技公司过于庞大、过于强大、利润过高。而这种权力只会加剧，使各国政府别无选择，只能正面迎击——把公司告上法庭、出台新的竞争法，甚至拆分这些科技巨头。

【选项】 A) 与原文相反 ensure the sustainable growth 是"确保巨头持续增长"，与原文"政府必须正面对抗、 甚至拆分"完全相反。

B) 偷换概念 competitiveness of their tech companies 是"维护本国科技公司的竞争力"，原文谈的是"限制巨头权力"，竞争力≠垄断权力，主语对象与目标都被偷换。

C) 以偏概全 break up the powerful giant tech companies 仅是原文列举对抗手段中的一项 perhaps even breaking up the tech giants，且原文用 perhaps even (甚至) 表示这只是极端可选项，不是"必须解决的 issue"本身。

D) ✓ 正确 Technology companies are too big, too powerful, and too profitable ↔

tech companies from gaining monopoly confront it head-on by taking the companies to court, passing new competition laws, and perhaps even breaking up the tech giants

↔ How to stop tech companies 预判"必须阻止科技公司权力进一步膨胀/取得垄断地位"与 How to stop tech companies from gaining monopoly 在主谓宾三层 (政府-stop-巨头取得垄断) 上一一对应。

【答案】 C （推断题）

【判型】 What does the suspension of Ant Group Co.'s stock offering suggest? 含 suggest， 问"该事件暗示什么"，是要求基于事实做一步逻辑延伸。

【拆句】 主干 What does the suspension suggest；of Ant Group Co.'s stock offering 是介词短语修饰 suspension。注意 stock offering 是"股票发行"，整个主语是"蚂蚁集团股票发行被暂停"这一事件本身。

【定位】 The draft rules followed the surprise suspension of a $37 billion stock offering by billionaire Jack Ma's Ant Group Co., making clear that no company can evade the government's regulation.

新规草案紧随蚂蚁集团 370 亿美元股票发行被突然叫停之后出台，明确表示任何公司都不能逃避政府监管。

【选项】 A) 过度推断 All attempts to evade regulation are doomed to failure 把原文"不能逃避"延伸为"所有逃避企图必然失败"，多走了"企图必败"这一步，且原文没说"企图"这一主体。

B) 偷换概念 All attempts to monopolize sales must be cracked down 把对象从"逃避监管"偷换为"垄断销售"；原文从未谈"销售垄断"，且 Ant Group 的 IPO 暂停与 monopolize sales 也无直接因果。 C) ✓ 正确 no company can evade the government's regulation ↔

All companies must be regulated by the government the government's regulation ↔ regulated by the government 从预判"任何公司都逃不过监管"出发，只有 All companies must be regulated by the government 完整且对等地承接"no…evade → all…must be regulated"这一逻辑变换。

D) 无中生有 All companies, domestic or foreign, are created equal 谈"公司是否生而平等"，是宪法/法律观念，原文从未涉及；且 domestic or foreign (内外资) 这一区分原文也没有。

questions.prompt: How are smaller companies impacted by tech giants' business expansion?

options.text: They can no longer do business independent of tech giants.
They are frequently denied access to tech giants' platforms.
They have to change marketing strategies to keep customers.
They no longer have the power to price their own products.

questions.shortExplanation: Tech giants are increasingly assuming powerful positions in banking, finance, advertising, retail, and other markets that force smaller businesses to rely on their platforms to reach customers.
questions.detailedExplanation:
【答案】 A （细节题）

【判型】 How are smaller companies impacted by tech giants' business expansion? 直接问"小公司怎样被影响"，要的是原文给出的具体影响，不需要做推断。

【拆句】 主干 How are smaller companies impacted，by 引导施动者 tech giants' business expansion；被动语态的施动者就是影响来源，找原文时要找"巨头扩张→小公司怎么了"的因果链。

【定位】 Tech giants are increasingly assuming powerful positions in banking, finance, advertising, retail, and other markets that force smaller businesses to rely on their platforms to reach customers.

科技巨头正越来越多地在银行、金融、广告、零售等其他市场占据强势地位，迫使小企业必须依赖它们的平台才能触达客户。

【选项】 A) ✓ 正确 force smaller businesses to rely on their platforms to reach customers ↔

They can no longer do business independent of tech giants to reach customers ↔ do business 预判"小企业被迫依附巨头平台"与 They can no longer do business independent of tech giants 是同一命题的肯定式与否定式表达，二者一一对应。

B) 与原文相反 They are frequently denied access to tech giants' platforms 说小企业"经常被拒绝接入巨头平台"，与原文"被迫依赖平台"恰好相反——原文的痛点是"必须用"，不是"不让用"。 C) 无中生有 change marketing strategies to keep customers 谈"改变营销策略以留住客户"，原文未谈营销策略，也未谈"留住老客户"；原文谈的是"通过谁去触达客户"，主体动作完全不同。

D) 偷换概念 no longer have the power to price their own products 把"被迫依附"偷换成"无定价权"。原文第四段确实提了 the old focus on pricing power no longer applies，但那是说"反垄断不再以定价权为衡量"，并非"小企业失去定价权"，主体与对象都被偷换。

questions.prompt: What have EU countries done to confront the power of digital giants?

options.text: They have imposed strict regulation over digital giants' advertising.
They have considered regulatory action to promote fair competition.
They have limited sales of digital giants' products.
They have sought to protect consumers' privacy.

questions.shortExplanation: Led by Margrethe Vestager, the European Union's competition chief, countries have sought to police the market and encourage fair play.
questions.detailedExplanation:
【答案】 B （细节题）

【判型】 What have EU countries done 直接问"做了什么"，是对原文动作的提取，无推断信号。

【拆句】 主干 What have EU countries done，不定式 to confront the power of digital giants 表目的——回答须是"为了对抗巨头"所采取的动作，不是其他动机的动作。

【定位】 Led by Margrethe Vestager, the European Union's competition chief, countries have sought to police the market and encourage fair play.

在欧盟竞争事务专员 Margrethe Vestager 的带领下，各国致力于监管市场、推动公平竞争。

【选项】 A) 以偏概全 imposed strict regulation over digital giants' advertising 把监管对象限缩为"广告"。原文 advertising revenue 只是"巨头吸收个人数据并由此攫取广告收入"问题的一部分，并非欧盟监管的对象本身；选项把局部问题升格为全部监管对象。 B) ✓ 正确 police the market ↔ considered regulatory action encourage fair play ↔ promote fair competition 选项 considered regulatory action to promote fair competition 把"police the market + encourage fair play"打包成"regulatory action + promote fair competition"，与预判完全对应。 C) 无中生有 limited sales of digital giants' products 谈"限制巨头产品销售"，原文未提及任何关于销售/产品限制的措施。 D) 以偏概全 sought to protect consumers' privacy 是"保护消费者隐私"，原文 vacuuming up personal data 确实涉及隐私，但那是问题描述而非欧盟主要动作；本段对动作的总结是 police the market and encourage fair play 这一更上位的表达，选项以"隐私保护"代替"市场监管+公平竞争"是以偏概全。

【选项】 A) 以偏概全 invading people's privacy 谈"侵犯隐私
questions.detailedExplanation:
【答案】 C （态度题）

【判型】 What do Americans generally think of social media companies 问"普遍怎么看"，要的是评价/态度极性，是态度题。

【拆句】 generally 是程度副词"普遍/总体上"，提示答案要覆盖大多数人的态度，不能拿少数派或个别极端表态做答；according to the author 限制信息源只能是文章本身。

【选项】 A) 以偏概全 invading people's privacy 谈"侵犯隐私"，原文第七段未直接谈"美国公众认为社交媒体侵犯隐私"，前文 privacy, control over data 是"反垄断专家应考虑的因素"清单，不是美国公众对社媒公司的看法。 B) 答非所问 increasingly influential (越来越有影响力) 是中性偏正的极性，与原文负向极性矛盾； 同时原文第七段未直接评价"影响力大小"，而是评价"影响是好是坏"。 C) ✓ 正确 the public in general has grown increasingly skeptical of social media companies↔

They are becoming untrustworthy More than 60% say the sector has a negative effect on the country↔

becoming untrustworthy 选项 C 在极性 (负向)、强度 (becoming 渐进体) 上都与原文 increasingly skeptical 完全对偶，且不引入任何原文没有的额外维度。

D) 过度推断 growing out of control 是"日益失控"——"失控"的判断超出原文。原文只说公众觉得社媒"负面影响大、需要更多监管"，并未说"已经失控"；要求更多监管恰恰说明"还可被监管"，与"out of control"相反。
