items.title: 2022年9月六级第1套 · 仔细阅读 · 第二篇
items.passage:
Born from the accessibility of mass air travel, modern international tourism has been popularized as "holiday-making" in regions that offer comparative advantages of sand, sun and sea. Travel is often portrayed as a tool for personal growth and tourism as an economic motor for destination countries and cities. There is a tendency to assume that tourism is good for everyone involved.

Today the big bang of tourism drives over 1.2 billion tourists across international borders annually. Many popular places are literally being loved to death. Recent protests in ports of call like Venice and Barcelona against disturbances created by cruise ships show the unfortunate consequences of emphasizing quantity over quality in tourism.

Uncontrolled tourism development has become a primary driver of social and environmental disruption. Tourism studies provide much documentation of the many negative social impacts of tourism and resulting resentment that local populations direct toward visitors.

Antagonism toward tourists typically develops in mature, heavily visited destinations. Protests in heavily visited destinations suggest that traditional tourism has overstayed its welcome.

Residents often become frustrated when the benefits of tourism are not felt locally. Although it can generate foreign exchange, income and employment, there's no guarantee that multinational hotel chains will allocate these benefits equitably among local communities.

On the contrary, when people stay at large resorts or on cruise ships, they make most of their purchases there, leaving local communities little opportunity to benefit from tourist spending. These forms of tourism widen economic and political gaps between haves and have-nots at local destinations.

In recent decades, local residents in destination communities also have found themselves negotiating new cultural boundaries, class dynamics, service industry roles and lifestyle transformations. For example, data show that tourism activity corresponds to increased social problems as local residents adopt the behaviors of tourists.

What does all this mean for the everyday traveler?

First, all tourists should make every effort to honor their hosts and respect local conditions. This means being prepared to adapt to local customs and norms, rather than expecting local conditions to adapt to travelers.

Second, tourism is a market-based activity and works best when consumers reward better performers. In the information age, there's little excuse for travelers being uninformed about where their vacation money goes and who it enriches.

Informed travelers also are better able to distinguish between multinational companies and local entrepreneurs whose businesses provide direct social, environmental, and economic benefits for local residents. Such businesses are in love with the destination and are therefore deserving of market reward. In the long run, being a responsible traveler means ensuring net positive impacts for local people and environments. With the information available at our fingertips, there has never been more opportunity to do so.

questions.prompt: What is the popular assumption about international tourism?

options.text: Its benefits may compensate for the adverse environmental consequences.
Its rapid development is attributed to people's improved living standard.
It appeals to people in places with favorable geographical conditions.
It contributes to the economy of destination countries and regions.

questions.shortExplanation: Travel is often portrayed as a tool for personal growth and tourism as an economic motor for destination countries and cities. There is a tendency to assume that tourism is good for everyone involved.
questions.detailedExplanation:
【答案】 D （细节题）

【判型】 题干 What is the popular assumption about international tourism 直接问"那个普遍看法是什么"，要求复述原文里被点名的那一句假设，不要求推断。

【拆句】 题干主干 What is the popular assumption about international tourism，What is 引导特殊疑问，about international tourism 是后置介词短语修饰 assumption，结构平铺直叙，无陷阱。

【定位】 Travel is often portrayed as a tool for personal growth and tourism as an economic motor for destination countries and cities. There is a tendency to assume that tourism is good for everyone involved.

旅行常被描绘为个人成长的工具，旅游业则被描绘为目的地国家和城市的经济发动机；人们倾向于假设旅游业对所有相关方都是好事。

【选项】 A) 无中生有选项 A 谈"收益可以弥补不利环境后果"，但 P1 只笼统说"旅游对各方都好"，从未提出"补偿环境代价"的对比框架。

B) 偷换概念选项 B 说"旅游业的快速发展归因于生活水平提高"，原文虽提到 Born from the accessibility of mass air travel——"源于大众航空旅行的可及性"——但归因对象是"航空可及"而非"生活水平"。 C) 张冠李戴选项 C 说旅游业"吸引地理条件优越地区的人"，但原文 has been popularized as "holiday-making" in regions that offer comparative advantages of sand, sun and sea 讲的是旅游业"在"那些地区被普及，并不是这些地区的人"被"旅游业吸引。 D) ✓ 正确 tourism as an economic motor for destination countries and cities ↔

It contributes to the economy of destination countries and regions 预判中"推动目的地经济"在选项 contributes to the economy of destination countries and regions 中找到对应，且 destination 一词原词重合，锁定 D。
questions.hint: 回到原文定位题干关键词，比较选项与原文的含义。

questions.prompt: What do we learn from some studies about uncontrolled tourism development?

options.text: It gives rise to an increase in mass confrontations.
It incurs local residents' antagonism to tourists.
It inhibits the steady growth of local economy.
It brings in a large chunk of mobile population.

questions.shortExplanation: Uncontrolled tourism development has become a primary driver of social and environmental disruption. Tourism studies provide much documentation of the many negative social impacts of tourism and resulting resentment that local populations direct toward visitors.
questions.detailedExplanation:
【答案】 B （细节题）

【判型】 题干 What do we learn from some studies about uncontrolled tourism development 要求复述研究的结论，结论句必为原文明写，不需推断。

【拆句】 题干主干 What do we learn，from some studies 是状语，about uncontrolled tourism development 修饰 studies 限定研究主题，句子无从句、无否定，理解上无陷阱。

【定位】 Uncontrolled tourism development has become a primary driver of social and environmental disruption. Tourism studies provide much documentation of the many negative social impacts of tourism and resulting resentment that local populations direct toward visitors.

失控的旅游发展已成为社会和环境破坏的首要推手。旅游研究大量记录了旅游业的种种负面社会影响，以及本地居民由此对游客产生的怨恨。

【选项】 A) 以偏概全选项 A 说"导致大众对抗增加"，原文虽提到 Recent protests in ports of call like Venice and Barcelona，但只是举例两地抗议，且这是 uncontrolled tourism development 的背景，不是"研究告诉我们的内容"。 B) ✓ 正确 resulting resentment that local populations direct toward visitors ↔

It incurs local residents' antagonism to tourists 预判中"研究记录居民对游客的怨恨"在选项 It incurs local residents' antagonism to tourists 中找到几乎一一对应的同义替换，锁定 B。

C) 无中生有选项 C 说"它抑制本地经济稳定增长"，原文仅说收益分配不均（no guarantee that multinational hotel chains will allocate these benefits equitably），并未说旅游会让本地经济"不增长"。 D) 答非所问选项 D 说"它带来大量流动人口"，原文虽提到 over 1.2 billion tourists across international borders annually，但这是"旅游业体量"的描述，不是"失控发展"研究的结论。
questions.hint: 回到原文定位题干关键词，比较选项与原文的含义。

questions.prompt: Why does the author say local residents of popular destinations often feel frustrated?

options.text: They fall victim to social conflicts and environmental disturbances.
They have little opportunity to enjoy themselves on cruise ships.
They cannot find employment in multinational hotel chains.
They do not think they benefit as much as they deserve.

questions.shortExplanation: Residents often become frustrated when the benefits of tourism are not felt locally. Although it can generate foreign exchange, income and employment, there's no guarantee that multinational hotel chains will allocate these benefits equitably among local communities.
questions.detailedExplanation:
【答案】 D （细节题）

【判型】 题干 Why does the author say local residents of popular destinations often feel frustrated 用 Why does the author say，是请考生复述作者给出的原因，原文必有明示原因。

【拆句】 Why does the author say 引导原因疑问，宾语从句 local residents... feel frustrated 完整，主语后置定语 of popular destinations 限定 residents，副词 often 提示常态，无否定无让步，无陷阱。

【定位】 Residents often become frustrated when the benefits of tourism are not felt locally. Although it can generate foreign exchange, income and employment, there's no guarantee that multinational hotel chains will allocate these benefits equitably among local communities.

当旅游业的好处在本地感受不到时，居民们常常感到失望。尽管旅游业可以带来外汇、收入和就业，但跨国酒店集团并不一定会把这些好处公平地分配给本地社区。

【选项】 A) 张冠李戴选项 A 说"他们沦为社会冲突和环境干扰的受害者"，原文 P3 谈过失控的社会环境破坏，但 P5 解释 frustrated 的原因是经济收益分配不公，而不是"自己成了社会/环境的受害者"。 B) 张冠李戴选项 B 说"他们没机会在邮轮上玩乐"，但原文 when people stay at large resorts or on cruise ships 谈的是"游客"在邮轮消费，而不是"本地居民"没机会享乐。 C) 与原文相反选项 C 说"他们在跨国酒店连锁找不到工作"，原文 Although it can generate foreign exchange, income and employment 明确说旅游业"能"带来就业，问题在于"分配不公"而非"无工作"。 D) ✓ 正确 the benefits of tourism are not felt locally ↔

They do not think they benefit as much as they deserve 预判中"没拿到应得份额"在 They do not think they benefit as much as they deserve 落地，锁定 D。
questions.hint: 回到原文定位题干关键词，比较选项与原文的含义。

questions.prompt: How does the author say local residents in destination communities respond to tourism activity?

options.text: They endeavor to adapt to it.
They immerse tourists in their culture.
They try to upgrade their business models.

questions.shortExplanation: In recent decades, local residents in destination communities also have found themselves negotiating new cultural boundaries, class dynamics, service industry roles and lifestyle transformations.
questions.detailedExplanation:
【答案】 A （细节题）

【判型】 题干 How does the author say local residents in destination communities respond to tourism activity 是 How does the author say...的格式，等同于 Why does the author say，复述作者所写的反应方式。

【拆句】 How does the author say 主问句，宾语从句中 local residents in destination communities 是主语，respond to tourism activity 是谓宾结构；in destination communities 是后置介词修饰 residents，结构清晰，无陷阱。

【定位】 In recent decades, local residents in destination communities also have found themselves negotiating new cultural boundaries, class dynamics, service industry roles and lifestyle transformations.

近几十年来，目的地社区的本地居民发现自己正在为新的文化边界、阶层动态、服务业角色和生活方式转变进行磋商和调适。

【选项】 A) ✓ 正确 negotiating new cultural boundaries, class dynamics, service industry roles and lifestyle transformations

↔ They endeavor to adapt to it 预判"居民在主动调适"在 They endeavor to adapt to it 落地：endeavor 抓住主动努力的语气，adapt 抓住调适的方向，锁定 A。

B) 过度推断选项 B 说"他们乐于采纳新生活方式"，但原文 as local residents adopt the behaviors of tourists 与 tourism activity corresponds to increased social problems 并列，说明这种采纳被作者视为社会问题，绝非"乐于"。 C) 答非所问选项 C 说"他们让游客沉浸在本地文化里"，方向完全相反；原文是 being prepared to adapt to local customs and norms, rather than expecting local conditions to adapt to travelers，恰是"游客适应当地"，但本题问的是本地居民的反应，不是游客的反应。

D) 无中生有选项 D 说"他们尝试升级商业模式"，原文虽提到 local entrepreneurs whose businesses provide direct social, environmental, and economic benefits，但这是作者对游客的建议"应该奖励哪类商家"，与居民是否"升级商业模式"无关。
questions.hint: 回到原文定位题干关键词，比较选项与原文的含义。

questions.prompt: What can tourists do to exert more positive impacts on the tourist destinations?

options.text: Show interest in local customs and lifestyles.
Seek possibilities to invest in local companies.
Use the services provided by local businesses.
Give favorable comments about their services.

questions.shortExplanation: Informed travelers also are better able to distinguish between multinational companies and local entrepreneurs whose businesses provide direct social, environmental, and economic benefits for local residents. Such businesses are in love with the destination and are therefore deserving of market reward.
questions.detailedExplanation:
【答案】 C （细节题）

【判型】 题干 What can tourists do to exert more positive impacts on the tourist destinations 在问可采取的行动，原文最后两段是显式建议段，属于明示信息复述。

【拆句】 What can tourists do 主干，to exert more positive impacts 是不定式状语表目的，on the tourist destinations 介词短语修饰 impacts；more 是 positive 的比较程度修饰，提示"更多"而非"唯一"，无陷阱。

【定位】 Informed travelers also are better able to distinguish between multinational companies and local entrepreneurs whose businesses provide direct social, environmental, and economic benefits for local residents. Such businesses are in love with the destination and are therefore deserving of market reward.

见多识广的游客也更能区分跨国公司与本地企业家——后者的生意能为本地居民带来直接的社会、环境与经济效益。这类企业对目的地怀有情感，因而值得获得市场回报。

【选项】 A) 以偏概全选项 A 说"对当地风俗和生活方式表示兴趣"，原文 being prepared to adapt to local customs and norms 谈的是"准备好去适应"，且该建议是"第一条"，而题干问的是"对目的地施加更多正面影响"，需的是更具体的对策——本地消费。 B) 过度推断选项 B 说"寻找投资本地公司的可能性"，原文谈的是 deserving of market reward 即消费层面的市场奖励，从未要求游客投资本地企业。 C) ✓ 正确 local entrepreneurs whose businesses provide direct social, environmental, and economic benefits for local residents

↔ Use the services provided by local businesses tourism is a market-based activity and works best when consumers reward better performers↔

Use the services provided by local businesses 预判中两个要素"消费"与"本地企业"在 Use the services provided by local businesses 一一落地，锁定 C。

D) 无中生有选项 D 说"对其服务给好评"，原文 deserving of market reward 的市场奖励是消费行为，没有任何关于点评/留言的字样。
questions.hint: 回到原文定位题干关键词，比较选项与原文的含义。

items.title: 2023年12月六级第1套 · 选词填空
items.passage:
The desert is deceiving. At first glance it looks lifeless, barren, and bone-dry. For most passersby humming through the Mojave on their way to try their luck in Las Vegas or heading towards the Grand Canyon, it's just a [26] _____ stretch of land with some mountains in the distance and more [27] _____ to be a setting for a movie that takes place on Mars. The desert, however, is [28] _____ with life, mystery, and magic.

The Mojave desert sees less than two inches of rain a year, and like most deserts, is a land of [29] _____ . Temperature fluctuations vary from freezing to [30] _____ hot, not only between seasons, but even within the same day.

At the heart of this vast, 25,000-square-mile desert is Mojave National Preserve. The folks managing and working there wear the wide-brimmed( 宽边的 ) hats that have become [31] _____ with places like Yosemite. The preserve is rich with history, culture, biodiversity, and endless opportunities to [32] _____ your interest, especially for anyone who loves the outdoors. For a photographer, it requires patience and [33] _____ a few spare tires to maneuver the network of unpaved "roads", but the rewards are plenty.

Photographing here requires a good, [34] _____ pair of shoes and a lot of preparation. Plenty of water, spare tires, and a full tank of gas are needed to explore this unit of the national park system, which is the third largest in the country.

Like all deserts, though, if you are patient, you will be rewarded, as they often reveal their secrets slowly. During my last outing, I was surprised to see how much of the area was shaped by ancient volcanoes and geological forces, much of which remains today, giving the area a [35] _____ feel and painting a colorful background for great photographs.

questions.prompt: it's just a __(26)__ stretch of land with some mountains in the distance
questions.shortExplanation: flat 表"平坦的、单调的"，呼应"路过者只觉无趣"
questions.detailedExplanation:
【答案】 D) flat 形容词

【词性槽】 a ___ stretch of land，冠词后名词前作定语

【依据】 flat 表"平坦的、单调的"，呼应"路过者只觉无趣"

前文铺垫 it looks lifeless, barren, and bone-dry，路过者的视角下沙漠是"一片平坦无奇"的土地，flat 既符合视觉特征又含"乏味"色彩，与 "some mountains in the distance" 远景一片低平相对照。

【竞争词】 O) unique unique 是褒义"独特的"，与路过者负面初印象冲突

本句站在"匆匆路过、误解沙漠"的视角，褒义词不合逻辑；unique 真正贴合的是 35 题描写沙漠真实风貌处。

M) sturdy sturdy 常修饰人/物结实，不修饰 stretch of land

sturdy 用来形容鞋、家具、人结实耐用，与 "一片土地" 不搭。

A) apt apt 后常跟 to/at，单独作定语少见

apt 作定语虽语法可行（恰当的），但语义上"恰当的一片土地"没说清啥；且 A 在后文"more ___ to be a setting" 句里和 to 搭配更合身，应留给那处。

【易错】 最具迷惑性的错误词是 O) —— unique 是褒义，与路过者负面初印象相反。unique 词性也对、放进 "a ___ stretch of land" 句也通，但本句视角是"误解沙漠的路过者"，褒义形容词违和；忽略说话人态度色彩就会被钓走。
questions.hint: 根据空格前后的词性、搭配与上下文选择词语；每个词最多使用一次。

questions.prompt: and more __(27)__ to be a setting for a movie that takes place on Mars.
questions.shortExplanation: be apt to do = 易于/倾向于做某事
questions.detailedExplanation:
【答案】 A) apt 形容词

【词性槽】 more ___ to be，比较级框架后形容词

【依据】 be apt to do = 易于/倾向于做某事

be apt to do 是固定结构，意为"很可能/适合于……"，与 more 连用表"更像/更适合作火星电影背景"，配合 more __(27)__ to be a setting for a movie that takes place on Mars. 上下文极顺。

【竞争词】 O) unique unique 不接 to do

unique 后接 to 时表"为……所独有"（unique to X），不接 to do 不定式；且 unique 是绝对级形容词，语义上也不与 more 自然搭配。

M) sturdy sturdy 不接 to do，且不修饰场景

sturdy 没有 "be sturdy to do" 的固定结构，语义也偏"结实耐用"，与"像火星电影场景"扯不上。
questions.hint: 根据空格前后的词性、搭配与上下文选择词语；每个词最多使用一次。

questions.prompt: The desert, however, is __(28)__ with life, mystery, and magic.
questions.shortExplanation: be overflowing with 表"充满、洋溢着"，与转折语义吻合
questions.detailedExplanation:
【答案】 F) overflowing 形容词

【词性槽】 be ... with 结构，空处作表语形容词

【依据】 be overflowing with 表"充满、洋溢着"，与转折语义吻合

首句说沙漠看似 lifeless, barren, and bone-dry，然后 however 转折，需要一个表"满满都是"的强对比形容词，overflowing 与 with 构成固定搭配 "be overflowing with"，正好与 life、mystery、magic 这一串积极名词配伍。

【竞争词】 N) synonymous 搭配虽对，但语义指向"等同"而非"充满"

be synonymous with 意为"与……同义/紧密关联"，放进 is __(28)__ with life, mystery, and magic. 会变成"沙漠等同于生命、神秘与魔法"，语义太绝对，且后文段 31 才真正用到 synonymous，更切合那里。

【易错】 最具迷惑性的错误词是 N) —— synonymous with 也成立，但语义太强、抢了 31 题的位置。synonymous 与 with 搭配看似也对，会把考生骗进"沙漠等同于生命与神秘"的过度判断；记住做选词填空要全篇预判搭配归属，把唯一性最强的搭配留给真正的位置 （31 题）。
questions.hint: 根据空格前后的词性、搭配与上下文选择词语；每个词最多使用一次。

questions.prompt: is a land of __(29)__
questions.shortExplanation: a land of extremes = 极端反差之地
questions.detailedExplanation:
【答案】 C) extremes 名词

【词性槽】 a land of ___，of 后填名词

【依据】 a land of extremes = 极端反差之地

后文 Temperature fluctuations vary from freezing to __(30)__ hot, not only between seasons, but even within the same day. 正好解释了"极端"——温差从冰点跨到酷热， extremes 既匹配语义又是英语里常见的固定表达 "a land of extremes"。

【竞争词】 E) fractionsfractions 指"分数/小部分"，与沙漠特征无关

"a land of fractions" 没有这种说法，也无法解释后文的温度反差，语义完全跑偏。

G) parasitesparasites 寄生虫，与沙漠语境不符

把沙漠说成"寄生虫之地"语义离奇，且后文谈的是温度而非生物，逻辑指向不对。
questions.hint: 根据空格前后的词性、搭配与上下文选择词语；每个词最多使用一次。

questions.prompt: from freezing to __(30)__ hot
questions.shortExplanation: burning hot 表"灼热"，与 freezing 形成强对比
questions.detailedExplanation:
【答案】 B) burning 副词

【词性槽】 副词修饰形容词 hot

【依据】 burning hot 表"灼热"，与 freezing 形成强对比

前文是 freezing（冰冻）极端冷，空处需要与之对称的极端热表达，burning 常以 burning hot 形式强调"灼热"，呼应 29 题的 a land of extremes。

【竞争词】 H) probably probably 表可能性，与温度程度无关

"freezing to probably hot" 逻辑荒谬：极端温度对比里不会说"大概热"，且 probably 也无法与 freezing 形成对称的程度感。

I) sparingly sparingly 指"节俭地"，语义完全错位

sparingly 用来修饰使用、消费等动作，放在 hot 前"节俭地热"毫无意义。
questions.hint: 根据空格前后的词性、搭配与上下文选择词语；每个词最多使用一次。

questions.prompt: wear the wide-brimmed(宽边的) hats that have become __(31)__ with places like Yosemite.
questions.shortExplanation: be/become synonymous with = 成为……的代名词
questions.detailedExplanation:
【答案】 N) synonymous 形容词

【词性槽】 have become ___ with，空作表语形容词

【依据】 be/become synonymous with = 成为……的代名词

宽边帽 the wide-brimmed(宽边的) hats 与优胜美地等国家公园在大众认知里已经画等号，synonymous 完美贴合 "become synonymous with places like Yosemite" 这一固定表达。

【竞争词】 A) apt apt 不与 with 搭配

apt 常说 be apt to do/be apt at，搭配是 to 或 at，不与 with 连用，语法上首先就被排除。
questions.hint: 根据空格前后的词性、搭配与上下文选择词语；每个词最多使用一次。

questions.prompt: endless opportunities to __(32)__ your interest
questions.shortExplanation: stimulate one's interest = 激发某人的兴趣 stimulate 是 interest 的高频搭配动词，意为"激发兴趣"，与"无尽的机会去激发你的兴趣"完全吻合，且前文 rich with history, culture, biodiversity, and endless opportunities 也在铺垫"种种激发兴趣的资源"。
questions.detailedExplanation:
【答案】 L) stimulate 动词

【词性槽】 to ___ your interest，不定式后接动词原形

【依据】 stimulate one's interest = 激发某人的兴趣 stimulate 是 interest 的高频搭配动词，意为"激发兴趣"，与"无尽的机会去激发你的兴趣"完全吻合，且前文 rich with history, culture, biodiversity, and endless opportunities 也在铺垫"种种激发兴趣的资源"。

【竞争词】 J) sprinkle sprinkle 表"撒、洒"，与 interest 不搭

sprinkle one's interest 不是英语自然表达，sprinkle 宾语多为水、糖粉、点缀物等具体物质。

K) steer steer 是"驾驶/引导"，宾语常为人、船、方向

steer your interest 虽勉强可懂，但搭配生硬；英语里"激发兴趣"的固定动词是 stimulate/arouse/spark，不会用 steer。
questions.hint: 根据空格前后的词性、搭配与上下文选择词语；每个词最多使用一次。

questions.prompt: it requires patience and __(33)__ a few spare tires to maneuver the network of unpaved "roads"
questions.shortExplanation: probably 表"很可能"，符合作者经验之谈的口吻
questions.detailedExplanation:
【答案】 H) probably 副词

【词性槽】 副词修饰整句/动词性结构 a few spare tires to maneuver...

【依据】 probably 表"很可能"，符合作者经验之谈的口吻

作者在分享在保护区拍照的经验：耐心是必须，备胎"很可能"也需要，probably 正好传达这种"建议但留余地"的语气。

【竞争词】 I) sparingly sparingly 与名词 a few spare tires 语义冲突

sparingly 意为"节制地、少量地"，但句中已经用 a few 限定数量，再加 sparingly 既冗余又改变重心；语义上也与"建议多备"的语境相反。
questions.hint: 根据空格前后的词性、搭配与上下文选择词语；每个词最多使用一次。

questions.prompt: requires a good, __(34)__ pair of shoes and a lot of preparation.
questions.shortExplanation: sturdy 形容鞋"结实耐用"，与 good 同向
questions.detailedExplanation:
【答案】 M) sturdy 形容词

【词性槽】 a good, ___ pair of shoes 并列修饰

【依据】 sturdy 形容鞋"结实耐用"，与 good 同向

沙漠拍照路况差 the network of unpaved "roads"，鞋需要"结实"才扛得住，sturdy 与 good 形成自然的双形容词修饰："一双好的、结实的鞋"。

【竞争词】 O) unique unique 修饰鞋偏向"独特款式"，与实用语境不符

沙漠摄影准备讲的是耐用、防护，不是款式独特；unique 真正切题之处在 35 题描写沙漠地貌。
questions.hint: 根据空格前后的词性、搭配与上下文选择词语；每个词最多使用一次。

questions.prompt: giving the area a __(35)__ feel and painting a colorful background for great photographs.
questions.shortExplanation: unique feel = 独一无二的感觉
questions.detailedExplanation:
【答案】 O) unique 形容词

【词性槽】 giving the area a ___ feel，名词前定语

【依据】 unique feel = 独一无二的感觉

前文 much of the area was shaped by ancient volcanoes and geological forces 强调这片土地由古火山与地质力量塑造，留给观者"独特"的观感，unique 与彩色摄影背景描述完美衔接。

items.title: 2023年12月六级第1套 · 信息匹配
items.passage:
A) On the hills of central Kenya, almost lime-green with the sparkle of tea bushes in the sunlight, farmers know all about climate change. "The rainy season is no longer predictable," says one. "When it is supposed to rain it doesn't, then it all comes at once." Climate change is an issue that will affect everyone on the planet. For Africans its consequences will be particularly bitter: whereas other regions were able to grow rich by burning coal and oil, Africa will pay much of the human price without having enjoyed the benefits. "Africa only represents 2% of global greenhouse-gas emissions but it is the continent that is expected to suffer the most from climate impacts," says Mafalda Duarte, who runs the World Bank's $8bn Climate Investment Funds.

B) Although there are huge uncertainties as to the precise impacts of climate change, enough is known to say that global warming represents one of the main threats to Africa's prosperity. Parts of the continent are already warming much more quickly than the average: temperatures in southern Africa have increased by about twice the global rate over the past 50 years. Even if the world were to cut emissions enough to keep global warming below 1.5 ℃ , heat-waves would intensify in Africa and diseases would spread to areas not currently affected. Farming would also be hit hard. About 40% of the land now used to grow maize(⽟⽶ ) would no longer be suitable for it. Overall, it is estimated that maize yields would fall by 18-22%.

C) Africa is particularly vulnerable, in part because it is already struggling to feed itself and it will have to vastly increase yields and productivity if it is to put food on the plates of a fast-growing population, even without climate change. The UN's Food and Agriculture Organisation reckons that by 2050 global food production would have to rise by about 70% over its level of 2009 to meet demand from a population that is growing in numbers and appetite. Much of this new demand will be in Africa. Yet the continent already imports about $50bn-worth of food a year and that figure is expected to more than double over the next five years. Self-sufficiency is not Africa's goal, but the fact that it spends more money importing food than it does buying capital goods suggests it has room for improvement.

D) Finding out why is not hard. Most farms are tiny, ploughed by hand and reliant on rain. More than half of Africa's people make their living from farming. Although its total harvest has climbed over the past few decades, this is mainly because there are more people farming more land. But in many places there is no spare land to farm. Plots in Rwanda are so small that you could fit 250 of them onto the average American farm. And although output per worker has improved by more than half over the past 30 years in Africa, that is still far behind the 2.5 times improvement in Asia. Yields of maize are generally less than two tonnes per hectare, a fifth the level in America.

E) The low productivity of African farmers is reflected in national economic statistics—despite absorbing so much labour, farming generates just 15% of GDP. "They can't even feed their families," says Jennifer Blanke, a vice-president of the African Development Bank in charge of agriculture. "Farm productivity hasn't improved in many parts of Africa for 100 years."

F) One reason is that in the first few decades of independence, many African governments neglected farming as they focused on industrialising their economies. Others damaged it by pushing down the prices that state monopolies paid for their crops in order to subsidise workers in cities with cheap food. Ghana taxed cocoa( 可可粉 ) exports so heavily that production collapsed by half between the 1960s and 1980s, despite a jump in the global price of cocoa. Yet over the past two decades or so governments and donors have begun to look again at farming as a way of providing jobs for the 13 million young people entering the workforce each year. Much of the focus has been on getting small farmers to use fertiliser and, more important, better seeds. The results can be impressive. Improved varieties of sorghum(⾼梁), for instance, can produce a crop that is 40% larger than the usual variety. Infrastructure is important. A World Bank irrigation project in Ethiopia helped farmers increase their potato harvest from about 8 tonnes per hectare to 35 tonnes.

G) Better techniques help, too. Small coffee farmers in Kenya are able to increase their incomes by 40% by following a few simple guidelines on caring for their bushes, such as trimming all but three of their stems. Many of their neighbours do not follow the advice, because it seems counter-intuitive. More stems ought to lead to more coffee beans, they say. Yet after seeing those following the advice get bigger harvests for a season or two, many others start doing the same.

H) One way of spreading knowledge is to link farms to big buyers of their harvests. When Diageo, a British drinks giant, built a brewery in western Kenya, it wanted to use local crops to make a beer cheap enough to compete with illicit home brew. It organised farmers into groups, improved supply chains for them to get seeds and fertiliser and then agreed to buy their grain. It now provides a market to about 17,000 farmers. Across the region it has doubled its use of local raw material to about 80% over five years, says John O'Keeffe, who runs its Africa business.

I) An even more important change is the move from traditional farming to building businesses that can profitably bring technology and investment to small farmers. Taita Ngetich, a young Kenyan, was studying engineering when he wanted to earn a little money on the side. He scraped together 20,000 Kenyan shillings (about $200) to plant tomatoes. Everything went wrong. The crop was attacked by pests. "Then there was a massive flood that swallowed all our capital," he says. Mr Ngetich persevered by looking into buying a greenhouse to protect his plants from bugs and rain. The cheapest ones cost more than $2,500 each, so he designed his own for half the price. Soon neighbouring farmers started placing orders with him, and now his firm, Illuminum Greenhouses, has sold more than 1,400 greenhouses that provide livelihoods to about 6,000 people. The business does not stop there; he also supplies fertiliser, high-quality seedlings and smart sensors that increase yields.

J) Illuminum's success shows how technology can help even small farms become more productive. Because such a large share of Africa's population earns a living from agriculture, even small improvements in productivity can lift the incomes of millions of people. But over the longer run small-scale farming can go only so far, especially in the face of climate change and population pressure.

K) "If we really want to lift people out of poverty we have to finance projects that will get them an income of at least $100 a month so that they can pay for health care and education," says Mr Ngetich. "Projects that give them an extra $2 a month from growing beans or maize aren't going to get them there." Getting those big jumps will need better jobs in factories and cities.

questions.prompt: It is said that agricultural productivity in many African countries has remained low for a century.
questions.shortExplanation: 一百年未提升的农业生产率
questions.detailedExplanation:
【答案】 E 段（强锚点）

【锚点】 一百年未提升的农业生产率

【定位】 Farm productivity hasn't improved in many parts of Africa for 100 years.

非洲许多地方的农业生产率已经一百年没有改善了。

【改写】 agricultural productivity in many African countries has remained low for a century ↔

Farm productivity hasn't improved in many parts of Africa for 100 years 数字单位换写 + 否定改善 = 维持低位

【辨邻】 D D 段 output per worker has improved by more than half over the past 30 years in Africa 给的时间是 30 年、方向是「提升过半」，与题干 remained low for a century 的「停滞一百年」结论完全相反，属于只覆盖局部 + 方向相反，不是源头段。 output per worker has improved by more than half over the past 30 years in Africa, that is still far behind the 2.5 times improvement in Asia
questions.hint: 先定位陈述句中的人物、数字或关键词，再比较原文同义表达。

questions.prompt: Building connections between farms and major purchasers of their produce can promote African farmers' use of advanced farming techniques.
questions.shortExplanation: 把农场连到大买家以推广技术
questions.detailedExplanation:
【答案】 H 段（弱锚点）

【锚点】 把农场连到大买家以推广技术

【定位】 One way of spreading knowledge is to link farms to big buyers of their harvests.

传播知识的一种方式，是把农场与他们农产品的大买家连起来。

【改写】 Building connections between farms and major purchasers of their produce ↔

link farms to big buyers of their harvests 建立连接 = link；大买家 = big buyers；农产品 = harvests

can promote African farmers' use of advanced farming techniques ↔

One way of spreading knowledge 传播知识即让农民用上先进做法

【辨邻】 F F 段重心在 getting small farmers to use fertiliser and, more important, better seeds，讲的是「输入端」做法，没有「把农场连到大买家」这件事，与题干 Building connections between farms and major purchasers 的渠道连接路径不同。 Much of the focus has been on getting small farmers to use fertiliser and, more important, better seeds

G G 段 Many of their neighbours do not follow the advice 走的是「邻里看效果再跟」的路径，与 Building connections between farms and major purchasers 的 「连到买家」机制不同。

Small coffee farmers in Kenya are able to increase their incomes by 40% by following a few simple guidelines on caring for their bushes
questions.hint: 先定位陈述句中的人物、数字或关键词，再比较原文同义表达。

questions.prompt: Parts of Africa are getting warmer much faster than the average, with southern Africa witnessing roughly twice the global warming rate over the last half century.
questions.shortExplanation: 南部非洲约两倍全球升温速度
questions.detailedExplanation:
【答案】 B 段（强锚点）

【锚点】 南部非洲约两倍全球升温速度

【定位】 Parts of the continent are already warming much more quickly than the average: temperatures in southern Africa have increased by about twice the global rate over the past 50 years.

非洲部分地区已经在以远高于平均的速度变暖：过去 50 年里，南部非洲的气温升幅约为全球升温速率的两倍。

【改写】 southern Africa witnessing roughly twice the global warming rate ↔

temperatures in southern Africa have increased by about twice the global rate roughly = about，witness 等价于 have increased by 的概括说法

over the last half century ↔ over the past 50 years half century = 50 years

Parts of Africa are getting warmer much faster than the average ↔

Parts of the continent are already warming much more quickly than the average continent = Africa 上下位换名；getting warmer = warming

Kenyan farmers ↔ Small coffee farmers in Kenya Kenyan farmers 与 farmers in Kenya 等价

The results can be impressive impressively 与 impressive 同根同义

Climate change is an issue that will affect everyone on the planet

尽管过去 30 年里非洲的人均产出提升了一半以上，这仍远落后于亚洲的 2.5 倍提升。

【定位】 But over the longer run small-scale farming can go only so far, especially in the face of climate change and population pressure. 但从更长远看，小规模农业能走的也就这么远，尤其是面对气候变化和人口压力的时候。

【改写】 In the long term, the potential for small farms in Africa to increase productivity is quite limited ↔

over the longer run small-scale farming can go only so far long term = longer run；quite limited = can go only so far

especially owing to the warming climate and a growing population ↔

【辨邻】 I I 段 Illuminum Greenhouses, has sold more than 1,400 greenhouses that provide livelihoods to about 6,000 people 给的是「小农通过科技获得收益」的正面案例，与题干 the potential for small farms in Africa to increase productivity is quite limited 的「潜力有限」断言方向相反，是 42 题的归属段而非本题。 An even more important change is the move from traditional farming to building businesses that can profitably bring technology and investment to small farmers

K K 段 Projects that give them an extra $2 a month from growing beans or maize aren't going to get them there 给的是收入门槛论证，没有「长期看 + 气候变化 + 人口」这套与题干 especially owing to the warming climate and a growing population 完全对位的双因表述。 Getting those big jumps will need better jobs in factories and cities

items.title: 2023年12月六级第1套 · 仔细阅读 · 第一篇
items.passage:
One of the great successes of the Republican Party in recent decades is the relentless propagation of a simple formula for economic growth: tax cuts.

The formula doesn't work, but that has not affected its popularity. And while the cult of tax cuts has attracted many critics, it lacks for obvious rivals.

Democratic politicians have tended to campaign on helping people left behind by economic growth. When Democrats do talk about encouraging economic growth, they often sound like Republicans.

This is not just a political problem for Democrats; it is an economic problem for the United States. The nation needs a better story about the drivers of economic growth. The painful lessons of recent decades point to a promising candidate: higher wages.

Raising the wages of American workers ought to be the priority of economic policymakers. We'd all be better off paying less attention to quarterly updates on the growth of the nation's gross domestic product (GDP) and focusing instead on the growth of workers' paychecks.

Set aside, for the moment, the familiar argument for higher wages: fairness. The argument here is that higher wages can fuel the engine of economic growth.

Perhaps the most famous illustration of the benefits is the story of Henry Ford's decision in 1914 to pay $5 a day to workers on his Model T assembly lines. He did it to increase production—he was paying a premium to maintain a reliable workforce. The unexpected benefit was that Ford's factory workers became Ford customers, too.

The same logic still holds: Consumption drives the American economy, and workers who are paid more can spend more.

Mainstream economists insist that it is impossible to order up a sustainable increase in wages because compensation levels reflect the unerring judgment of market forces.

The conventional wisdom held that productivity growth was the only route to higher wages. Through that lens, efforts to negotiate higher wages were counterproductive. Minimum-wage laws would raise unemployment because there was only so much money in the wage pool, and if some people got more, others would get none.

It was in the context of this worldview that it became popular to argue that tax cuts would drive prosperity. Rich people would invest, productivity would increase, wages would rise.

In the real world, things are more complicated. Wages are influenced by a tug of war between employers and workers, and employers have been winning. One clear piece of evidence is the widening gap between productivity growth and wage growth since roughly 1970. Productivity has more than doubled; wages have lagged far behind.

A focus on wage growth would provide an antidote(矫正⽅法 ) to the attractive simplicity of the belief in the magical power of tax cuts.

questions.prompt: Why does the formula of tax cuts remain popular though ineffective?

options.text: Its critics' voice has not been heard throughout the country.
There seem to be no other options available to replace it.
The cult of tax cuts has been relentlessly propagated by all policymakers.
There appears to be a misunderstanding of the formula among the public.

questions.shortExplanation: And while the cult of tax cuts has attracted many critics, it lacks for obvious rivals.
questions.detailedExplanation:
【答案】 B （细节题）

【判型】 Why does the formula of tax cuts remain popular though ineffective? 用 Why 直接问原因，是要回到原文找一句明确解释。

【拆句】 主句 Why does the formula of tax cuts remain popular 加状语从句 though ineffective ——though 后省略了 it is，完整是 though it is ineffective；六级常用 though 引出让步状语，识别它是看懂题干逻辑的关键。

【定位】 And while the cult of tax cuts has attracted many critics, it lacks for obvious rivals.

尽管对减税的崇拜招致了许多批评，但它（在政策市场上）没有明显的替代品。

【选项】 A) 无中生有原文只说 the cult of tax cuts has attracted many critics——招致很多批评，没有说这些批评"未被全国听见"。

B) ✓ 正确 it lacks for obvious rivals ↔ There seem to be no other options available to replace it. B 项是 it lacks for obvious rivals 的同义重写，与预判完全吻合。 C) 以偏概全原文 One of the great successes of the Republican Party 明确只是共和党在传播， 选项扩大为 all policymakers（所有政策制定者）。 D) 无中生有原文只说该公式 doesn't work, but that has not affected its popularity，并未说大众"误解"了这个公式。
questions.hint: 回到原文定位题干关键词，比较选项与原文的含义。

questions.prompt: What does the author think is a more effective measure for driving economic growth in the U.S.?

options.text: Aiding people left behind by economic growth.
Prioritizing the growth of the nation's GDP.
Introducing even more extensive tax cuts.

questions.shortExplanation: Raising the wages of American workers ought to be the priority of economic policymakers.
questions.detailedExplanation:
【答案】 C （细节题）

【判型】 What does the author think is a more effective measure for driving economic growth in the U.S.? 直接问作者认为有效的措施，原文必有一句明确给出。

【拆句】 主句 What does the author think，think 后跟省略 that 的宾语从句 is a more effective measure for driving economic growth in the U.S.；六级常考插入语式的 author think， 识别它后面才是真正提问的内容。

【定位】 Raising the wages of American workers ought to be the priority of economic policymakers.

提高美国工人的工资，应当是经济政策制定者的首要任务。

【选项】 A) 张冠李戴 Democratic politicians have tended to campaign on helping people left behind by economic growth. 这是作者描述民主党的做法，紧接着 P4 就把它否定为"政治问题"。

B) 与原文相反 We'd all be better off paying less attention to quarterly updates on the growth of the nation's gross domestic product (GDP)——作者明确说应少关注 GDP 增长。

C) ✓ 正确 Raising the wages of American workers ↔ Increasing the compensation for labor. C 项是 Raising the wages of American workers 的逐字同义改写，与预判完全吻合。 D) 与原文相反全文要驳斥的就是减税公式（tax cuts），作者不可能反过来主张更大规模减税。
questions.hint: 回到原文定位题干关键词，比较选项与原文的含义。

questions.prompt: What is the logic underlying the author's viewpoint?

options.text: The growth of workers' paychecks ultimately boosts the nation's economy.
Paying a premium to maintain a reliable workforce attracts more customers.
Consumption stimulates the desire for higher wages.
Familiar arguments for higher wages are outdated.

questions.shortExplanation: Consumption drives the American economy, and workers who are paid more can spend more. 消费驱动着美国经济，而薪酬越高的工人能消费得越多。
questions.detailedExplanation:
【答案】 A （细节题）

【判型】 What is the logic underlying the author's viewpoint? 用 What 直接问支撑作者观点的逻辑机制，原文应有明确陈述。

【拆句】 What is the logic underlying the author's viewpoint?——underlying 是现在分词作后置定语，修饰 logic，等于 that underlies；六级阅读高频，看到 -ing 后置定语要意识到它修饰前面那个名词。

【定位】 Consumption drives the American economy, and workers who are paid more can spend more. 消费驱动着美国经济，而薪酬越高的工人能消费得越多。

【选项】 A) ✓ 正确 workers who are paid more can spend more ↔

The growth of workers' paychecks ultimately boosts the nation's economy. Consumption drives the American economy ↔ ultimately boosts the nation's economy A 项用 ultimately 把 P8 的两句话压成一句因果，与预判的"加薪→消费→经济增长"完全一致。 B) 偷换概念 He did it to increase production—he was paying a premium to maintain a reliable workforce. 是福特出于产能目的支付溢价；The unexpected benefit was that Ford's factory workers became Ford customers, too. 中"工人变顾客"是意外结果， 并非"支付溢价"直接导向"吸引更多顾客"。 C) 与原文相反原文 workers who are paid more can spend more 是高工资 → 高消费，选项反成"消费刺激加薪欲望"，因果链方向倒置。

D) 过度推断 Set aside, for the moment, the familiar argument for higher wages: fairness.—— 作者只是说"暂且搁置"公平这一旧论据，并未说它过时。
questions.hint: 回到原文定位题干关键词，比较选项与原文的含义。

questions.prompt: What is the basis for higher wages according to the conventional wisdom?

options.text: The unerring judgment of market forces.

questions.shortExplanation: The conventional wisdom held that productivity growth was the only route to higher wages. 传统观点认为，生产率的提高是通往更高工资的唯一途径。
questions.detailedExplanation:
【答案】 B （细节题）

【判型】 What is the basis for higher wages according to the conventional wisdom? 用 What 直问按传统观点加薪的依据，回原文找明确陈述句。

【拆句】 主句 What is the basis for higher wages + 介词短语 according to the conventional wisdom——according to 引出陈述主体，意味着答案要看 conventional wisdom 那方怎么说，而非作者本人怎么说；六级常借这个介词短语区分立场，须警觉。

【定位】 The conventional wisdom held that productivity growth was the only route to higher wages. 传统观点认为，生产率的提高是通往更高工资的唯一途径。

【选项】 A) 张冠李戴 Set aside, for the moment, the familiar argument for higher wages: fairness. 中"公平"是作者列出的另一种加薪理由（且被搁置），与 conventional wisdom 无关。

B) ✓ 正确 productivity growth ↔ Increase in productivity. B 项就是 productivity growth 的同义改写，与预判直接对应。 C) 张冠李戴 Raising the wages of American workers ought to be the priority of economic policymakers. 是作者本人的主张，不是传统观点对加薪基础的判断。

D) 张冠李戴 Mainstream economists insist that ... compensation levels reflect the unerring judgment of market forces. 是主流经济学家的判断，且原文中"市场力量的无误判断"是指工资水平的决定方式，不是加薪的依据。
questions.hint: 回到原文定位题干关键词，比较选项与原文的含义。

questions.prompt: What do we learn about things in the real world in America for the past 50 years or so?

options.text: People have failed to see a corresponding increase in wages and in productivity.
People have been disheartened by the widening gap between the haves and have-nots.
People have witnessed a tug of war between Republicans and Democrats over tax cuts.
People have seen the link disappearing between productivity and workers' well-being.

questions.shortExplanation: In the real world, things are more complicated. Wages are influenced by a tug of war between employers and workers, and employers have been winning. One clear piece of evidence is the widening gap between productivity growth and wage growth since roughly 1970. Productivity has more than doubled; wages have lagged far behind.
questions.detailedExplanation:
【答案】 A （细节题）

【判型】 What do we learn about things in the real world in America for the past 50 years or so? 问我们从原文得知的事实，原文必有对应陈述。

【拆句】 What do we learn about things in the real world in America for the past 50 years or so?——主干是 What do we learn about things，三层介词短语 in the real world/in America/for the past 50 years or so 层层限定 things；六级长题干常用这种层层限定， 要逐层抓住主体（things=各种情况）。

【定位】 In the real world, things are more complicated. Wages are influenced by a tug of war between employers and workers, and employers have been winning. One clear piece of evidence is the widening gap between productivity growth and wage growth since roughly 1970. Productivity has more than doubled; wages have lagged far behind.

在现实世界里，情况更复杂。工资受到雇主与工人之间拉锯战的影响，而雇主一直在胜出。 一个明显的证据是，自 1970 年前后以来，生产率增长与工资增长之间的差距越来越大：生产率已经翻了一倍多，而工资远远落在后面。

【选项】 A) ✓ 正确 Productivity has more than doubled; wages have lagged far behind.↔

People have failed to see a corresponding increase in wages and in productivity. the widening gap between productivity growth and wage growth↔

a corresponding increase in wages and in productivity A 项用 failed to see a corresponding increase 表达"生产率翻倍而工资落后"的整体含义，与预判完全吻合。

B) 无中生有原文 a tug of war between employers and workers 是劳资博弈，不是贫富分化 （haves and have-nots）；且原文未提任何人 disheartened（沮丧）。

C) 偷换概念原文 a tug of war between employers and workers 是劳资双方的拉锯战，而非两党的争斗；且原文未说民主党与共和党在减税上拉锯。 D) 过度推断 Productivity has more than doubled; wages have lagged far behind. 说的是"差距扩大"，并未说"联系消失（link disappearing）"——差距大 ≠ 联系断；且 well-being （福祉）也比 wages 范围更大。
questions.hint: 回到原文定位题干关键词，比较选项与原文的含义。

items.title: 2023年12月六级第1套 · 仔细阅读 · 第二篇
items.passage:
Journal editors decide what gets published and what doesn't, affecting the careers of other academics and influencing the direction that a field takes. You'd hope, then, that journals would do everything they can to establish a diverse editorial board, reflecting a variety of voices, experiences, and identities.

Unfortunately a new study in Nature Neuroscience makes for disheartening reading. The team finds that the majority of editors in top psychology and neuroscience journals are male and based in the United States: a situation that may be amplifying existing gender inequalities in the field and influencing the kind of research that gets published.

Men were found to account for 60% of the editors of psychology journals. There were significantly more male than female editors at each level of seniority, and men made up the majority of editors in over three quarters of the journals. Crucially, the proportion of female editors was significantly lower than the overall proportion of women psychology researchers.

The differences were even starker in the neuroscience journals: 70% of editors were male, and men held the majority of editorial positions in 88% of journals. In this case, the proportion of female editors was not significantly lower than the proportion of female researchers working in neuroscience—a finding that reveals enduring gender disparities in the field more broadly.

Based on their results, the team concludes that "the ideas, values and decision-making biases of men are overrepresented in the editorial positions of the most recognized academic journals in psychology and neuroscience."

Gender inequality in science is often attributed to the fact that senior academics are more likely to be male, because historically science was male-dominated: it's argued that as time goes on and more women rise to senior roles, the field will become more equal. Yet this study showed that even the junior roles in psychology journals tended to be held disproportionately by men, despite the fact that there are actually more female than male junior psychology faculty.

This implies that a lack of female academics is not the problem. Instead, there are structural reasons that women are disadvantaged in science. Women receive lower salaries and face greater childcare demands, for instance, which can result in fewer publications and grants—the kinds of things that journals look for when deciding who to appoint. Rather than simply blaming the inequality of editorial boards on tradition, we should be actively breaking down these existing barriers.

A lack of diversity among journal editors also likely contributes to psychology's WEIRD problem. If journal editors are largely men from the United States, then they will probably place higher value on papers that are relevant to Western, male populations, whether consciously or not.

questions.prompt: What would we expect an editorial board of an academic journal to exhibit in view of its important responsibilities?
questions.shortExplanation: You'd hope, then, that journals would do everything they can to establish a diverse editorial board, reflecting a variety of voices, experiences, and identities. 那么，你会希望期刊竭尽所能去建立一个多元化的编委会，从而反映各种各样的声音、经验与身份。
questions.detailedExplanation:
【答案】 D （细节题）

【判型】 What would we expect an editorial board of an academic journal to exhibit in view of its important responsibilities? 问的是「鉴于职责，应当呈现什么」，是原文一句话可以直接回答的事实，不含 infer/imply。

【拆句】 题干主干是 What would we expect an editorial board…to exhibit，what 作 exhibit 的宾语前置；in view of its important responsibilities 是介词短语作原因状语，可剥离。剥离后等价于 We expect an editorial board to exhibit what?，结构平铺，无陷阱。

【定位】 You'd hope, then, that journals would do everything they can to establish a diverse editorial board, reflecting a variety of voices, experiences, and identities. 那么，你会希望期刊竭尽所能去建立一个多元化的编委会，从而反映各种各样的声音、经验与身份。

【选项】 A) 无中生有全文没有任何句子提到「洞察力」相关概念，Insight 是从职责一词主观联想出来的属性。

B) 偷换概念原文谈的是编辑的「身份多样性」而非「专业能力」；编辑工作虽要求专业，但全文没有任何一句强调专业能力，Expertise 是属性偷换。 C) 无中生有全文未出现「诚信／正直」相关讨论，Integrity 同样是从「重要职责」一词联想出的主观属性。

D) ✓ 正确 diverse editorial board ↔ Diversity 预判语义「多元」与 Diversity 完全同义，其它三项均无对应原文支撑，锁定 D。

questions.prompt: What do we learn from the findings of a new study in Nature Neuroscience?

options.text: The majority of top psychology and neuroscience journals reflect a variety of voices, experiences and identities.
The editorial boards of most psychology and neuroscience journals do influence the direction their field takes.
The editorial boards of the most important journals in psychology and neuroscience are male-dominated.
The majority of editors in top psychology and neuroscience journals have relevant backgrounds.

questions.shortExplanation: The team finds that the majority of editors in top psychology and neuroscience journals are male and based in the United States: a situation that may be amplifying existing gender inequalities in the field and influencing the kind of research that gets published. 研究团队发现，顶级心理学与神经科学期刊的大多数编辑是男性，且在美国工作——这种状况可能正在放大该领域既有的性别不平等，并影响着哪些研究得以发表。
questions.detailedExplanation:
【答案】 C （细节题）

【判型】 What do we learn from the findings of a new study in Nature Neuroscience? 问的是研究本身陈述了什么，原文有直陈句，不需要跨段推断。

【拆句】 题干主干 What do we learn from the findings…?，what 作 learn 的宾语前置；from the findings of a new study in Nature Neuroscience 是 of 套 of 的多层介词结构，但只是限定 findings 来源，对理解无障碍。

【定位】 The team finds that the majority of editors in top psychology and neuroscience journals are male and based in the United States: a situation that may be amplifying existing gender inequalities in the field and influencing the kind of research that gets published. 研究团队发现，顶级心理学与神经科学期刊的大多数编辑是男性，且在美国工作——这种状况可能正在放大该领域既有的性别不平等，并影响着哪些研究得以发表。

【选项】 A) 与原文相反 reflect a variety of voices, experiences and identities 是 P1 中作者「期望」的状态，而 P2 恰恰指出现实并非如此——选项把「期待」当成「现实」，方向完全反了。

B) 答非所问 do influence the direction their field takes 借用 influencing the direction that a field takes，但那是 P1 描述「编辑职责」的总论，不是 P2 的「研究发现」；题干问 findings of a new study，本选项答的是 P1 的背景，与 52 题问的范围错位。 C) ✓ 正确 the majority of editors in top psychology and neuroscience journals are male ↔

The editorial boards of the most important journals in psychology and neuroscience are male-dominated. top psychology and neuroscience journals ↔

the most important journals in psychology and neuroscience 「顶级=最重要」「以男为主=男性主导」两组同义替换都成立，C 是定位句的精确同义复述。

D) 无中生有全文没有任何句子谈及编辑的「相关背景／资质」是否充足；P2 谈的是性别和国籍分布，不是专业相关性，have relevant backgrounds 凭空冒出。

questions.prompt: What fact does the author highlight concerning the gender differences in editors of psychology journals?

options.text: There were quite a few female editors who also distinguished themselves as influential psychology researchers.
The number of female editors was simply disproportionate to that of women engaged in psychology research.
The proportion of female editors was increasingly lower at senior levels.
There were few female editors who could move up to senior positions.

questions.shortExplanation: Crucially, the proportion of female editors was significantly lower than the overall proportion of women psychology researchers.
questions.detailedExplanation:
【答案】 B （细节题）

【判型】 What fact does the author highlight concerning the gender differences in editors of psychology journals? 问的是「作者强调了什么事实」，原文有一句直接陈述，属细节而非主旨。

【拆句】 题干主干 What fact does the author highlight…?；concerning the gender differences in editors of psychology journals 是 concerning 引导的介词短语作 highlight 的范围状语，限定话题。结构平铺，无陷阱。

【定位】 Crucially, the proportion of female editors was significantly lower than the overall proportion of women psychology researchers.

至关重要的是，女性编辑的占比显著低于心理学领域整体女性研究者的占比。

【选项】 A) 无中生有原文只对比「女编辑占比」与「女研究者占比」，并未说有「兼任出色研究者的女编辑」；distinguished themselves as influential psychology researchers 是凭空添加的属性。

B) ✓ 正确 the proportion of female editors was significantly lower than the overall proportion of women psychology researchers

↔

The number of female editors was simply disproportionate to that of women engaged in psychology research. the overall proportion of women psychology researchers ↔

that of women engaged in psychology research 唯一刻画「女编辑占比 vs 女研究者占比」这一比例对照的选项是 B；其它选项要么换了对比对象，要么换了讨论范围。

C) 过度推断 The proportion of female editors was increasingly lower at senior levels. 把原文 「各级别男编辑都更多」的事实曲解为「越往高级越少」的递进趋势；原文 There were significantly more male than female editors at each level of seniority 只说「每一级都更多」，并没有给出「越往上越严重」的递进关系。

D) 偷换概念原文没有讨论「女编辑能否升迁」这一职业流动问题；few female editors who could move up to senior positions 把性别比例话题换成升迁话题，方向错位。

questions.prompt: What can we infer from the conclusion drawn by the team of the new study on the basis of their findings?

options.text: Women's views are underrepresented in the editorial boards of top psychology and neuroscience journals.
Male editors of top psychology and neuroscience journals tend to be biased against their female colleagues.
Male researchers have enough representation in the editorial boards to ensure their publications.
Female editors have to struggle to get women's research articles published in academic journals.

questions.shortExplanation: Based on their results, the team concludes that "the ideas, values and decision-making biases of men are overrepresented in the editorial positions of the most recognized academic journals in psychology and neuroscience." 基于研究结果，研究团队总结道：「在最受认可的心理学与神经科学学术期刊的编辑岗位上，男性的想法、价值观与决策偏见被过度代表。」
questions.detailedExplanation:
【答案】 A （推断题）

【判型】 What can we infer from the conclusion drawn by the team of the new study on the basis of their findings? 含明确的 infer 标志词，正确答案是定位句的一步同义延伸，而非原文逐字表述。

【拆句】 题干主干 What can we infer from the conclusion…?；drawn by the team of the new study 是过去分词短语作后置定语，修饰 conclusion；on the basis of their findings 是介词短语状语，说明结论的依据。三层修饰仅在定位 conclusion 这个核心名词，不影响主干理解，但基础薄弱的同学要看清 from 后面真正的对象是 conclusion 而不是 team。

【定位】 Based on their results, the team concludes that "the ideas, values and decision-making biases of men are overrepresented in the editorial positions of the most recognized academic journals in psychology and neuroscience." 基于研究结果，研究团队总结道：「在最受认可的心理学与神经科学学术期刊的编辑岗位上，男性的想法、价值观与决策偏见被过度代表。」

【选项】 A) ✓ 正确 the ideas, values and decision-making biases of men are overrepresented↔

Women's views are underrepresented in the editorial boards of top psychology and neuroscience journals. the editorial positions of the most recognized academic journals in psychology and neuroscience

↔ the editorial boards of top psychology and neuroscience journals 在「男过度代表」基础上仅走一步就到「女代表不足」，A 是唯一这样做的；其它选项要么走第二步（偏见、歧视），要么换了话题。

B) 过度推断原文 decision-making biases of men 指的是「决策中的偏见模式被过度呈现」这一统计事实；be biased against their female colleagues 则把它推到「男编辑刻意歧视女同事」的人际行为层面，多走了一步。

C) 答非所问题干问「能推断出什么」，ensure their publications 谈的是「男编辑的发表得到保障」，原文没有任何句子谈论这种保障机制；且本研究的论调是批评不平等而非赞颂男性发表优势，与原文立场相反。

D) 无中生有原文从未谈论女编辑为发表女性研究而「斗争」，struggle to get women's research articles published 是凭空虚构出来的情节。

questions.prompt: What does the author suggest we do instead of simply blaming the inequality of editorial boards on tradition?

options.text: Strike a balance between male and female editors.
Increase women's employment in senior positions.
Enlarge the body of female academics.

questions.shortExplanation: Instead, there are structural reasons that women are disadvantaged in science. Women receive lower salaries and face greater childcare demands, for instance, which can result in fewer publications and grants—the kinds of things that journals look for when deciding who to appoint. Rather than simply blaming the inequality of editorial boards on tradition, we should be actively breaking down these existing barriers. 实际上，是结构性的原因让女性在科学界处于不利地位。例如，女性薪资更低、育儿负担更重，这会导致她们论文与基金更少——而这些恰恰是期刊在选拔编辑时所看重的。与其简单地把编委会的不平等推给传统，不如主动去拆除这些既有的壁垒。
questions.detailedExplanation:
【答案】 D （细节题）

【判型】 What does the author suggest we do instead of simply blaming the inequality of editorial boards on tradition? 问作者明确建议什么，原文有 Rather than… we should… 的直陈句，是细节题而非主旨题。

【拆句】 题干主干 What does the author suggest we do，what 作 do 的宾语前置；instead of simply blaming the inequality of editorial boards on tradition 是 instead of 引导的动名词介词短语，作状语，表达「与其…不如…」的对比关系。看清 instead of 后面是「要被否定的旧做法」，suggest we do 后面才是「要肯定的新做法」，二者不可弄反。

【定位】 Instead, there are structural reasons that women are disadvantaged in science. Women receive lower salaries and face greater childcare demands, for instance, which can result in fewer publications and grants—the kinds of things that journals look for when deciding who to appoint. Rather than simply blaming the inequality of editorial boards on tradition, we should be actively breaking down these existing barriers. 实际上，是结构性的原因让女性在科学界处于不利地位。例如，女性薪资更低、育儿负担更重，这会导致她们论文与基金更少——而这些恰恰是期刊在选拔编辑时所看重的。与其简单地把编委会的不平等推给传统，不如主动去拆除这些既有的壁垒。

【选项】 A) 以偏概全 Strike a balance between male and female editors 只触及「编辑性别比例」这一表层结果，与作者主张的「拆除导致不平等的结构性原因」相比，停留在症状而非根因； 原文反对的就是「只盯比例不动结构」的浅层对策。 B) 答非所问 Increase women's employment in senior positions 借的是 P6 「初级岗位也男性偏多」这一对照性数据；但 P6 是作者用来「驳斥传统论」的论据，并非建议；55 题问的是「P7 作者建议什么」。

C) 与原文相反原文 This implies that a lack of female academics is not the problem. 已明确否定 「女学者太少」是问题；Enlarge the body of female academics 恰恰反过来主张「扩充女学者队伍」，方向完全相反。

D) ✓ 正确 actively breaking down these existing barriers↔Implement overall structural reforms. structural reasons that women are disadvantaged in science↔structural reforms 把「主动拆除结构性壁垒」概括为「实施整体结构性改革」，是 D 与原文唯一吻合的同义改写；其它选项要么停留在「男女比例」「升迁」等局部对策，要么误把原因当对策。

items.title: 2023年12月六级第2套 · 选词填空
items.passage:
Our brains respond to language expressing facts differently than they do to words conveying possibility, scientists at New York University have recently found. Their work offers new insights into the impact word choice has on how we [26] _____ between statements expressing what is real versus what is merely possible. The researchers assert their findings are important because we are presented with false information all the time. Some of this is [27] _____ , as is the case with deceptive advertisements, but the problem is [28] _____ by individuals who believe they are sharing correct information. Thus, it is more important than ever to separate the factual from the possible or merely [29] _____ in how we communicate. This is especially true as the study makes clear that information presented as fact [30] _____ special responses in our brains, which are distinct from when we process the same content with clear indicators of [31] _____ .

In their new study, the scientists intended to [32] _____ how the brain computes possibilities as expressed by words such as "may," "might," and "if." The researchers compared brain responses to statements expressing factual [33] _____ and those expressing possibility. "There is a monster under my bed" exemplifies a factual statement. "I will stay home," is also factual. This is opposed to statements that express possibility, like "There might be a monster under my bed," or "If it rains, I will stay home."

The results of the study showed that factual language [34] _____ a rapid increase in brain activity, with the brain responding more powerfully and showing more engagement with factual phrases compared to those communicating possibility. Thus, facts rule when it comes to the brain. Brain regions involved in processing [35] _____ rapidly distinguish facts from possibilities. Further, these regions respond in a much more robust fashion to factual statements.

questions.prompt: the impact word choice has on how we __(26)__ between statements expressing what is real versus what is merely possible
questions.shortExplanation: differentiate between A and B 固定搭配
questions.detailedExplanation:
【答案】 E) differentiate 动词

【词性槽】 情态动词 can + 动词原形

【依据】 differentiate between A and B 固定搭配

how we __(26)__ between statements expressing what is real versus what is merely possible，differentiate between 表示「在 A 与 B 之间作区分」，与上文 respond to language expressing facts differently than they do to words conveying possibility 的 differently 同根呼应。

【竞争词】 C) ascertain 不与 between 搭配

ascertain 义为「查明」，常接 that 从句或名词，不接 between，搭配上直接出局。

H) inhibit 义为「抑制」与「区分」语义相反

inhibit 表示阻止，与上下文「区分事实和可能」无关，且不接 between。
questions.hint: 根据空格前后的词性、搭配与上下文选择词语；每个词最多使用一次。

questions.prompt: Some of this is __(27)__, as is the case with deceptive advertisements
questions.shortExplanation: 与 deceptive advertisements 同向：蓄意欺骗
questions.detailedExplanation:
【答案】 D) deliberate 形容词

【词性槽】 be 动词 is 后接表语形容词

【依据】 与 deceptive advertisements 同向：蓄意欺骗

Some of this is __(27)__, as is the case with deceptive advertisements, but the problem is __(28)__ by individuals who believe they are sharing correct information. but 之后是「自以为正确」的无意之失，那么 but 之前的虚假信息就是「故意为之」的； deliberate「蓄意的」正与 deceptive 同义递进。

【竞争词】 N) unanimous 义为「全体一致」与虚假信息无关

unanimous 修饰意见或决议的「一致同意」，无法描述 some of this（部分虚假信息），且与 deceptive 也无语义关联。
questions.hint: 根据空格前后的词性、搭配与上下文选择词语；每个词最多使用一次。

questions.prompt: but the problem is __(28)__ by individuals who believe they are sharing correct information
questions.shortExplanation: 「问题被…加剧」与上下文反差逻辑契合
questions.detailedExplanation:
【答案】 B) aggravated 动词

【词性槽】 be + 过去分词构成被动语态

【依据】 「问题被…加剧」与上下文反差逻辑契合

上文 Some of this is __(27)__, as is the case with deceptive advertisements, but the problem is __(28)__ by individuals who believe they are sharing correct information，but 之后引入「以为自己在分享正确信息的人」也让问题恶化—— aggravated「使加剧」精确表达「使问题更严重」。

【竞争词】 A) activated 义为「激活」与「问题恶化」语义不符

activate 多用于激活机制、开关、神经元；the problem is activated 不是地道表达，也不符合 but 转折所要强调的「问题更糟」语义。activated 留给 34 题更贴切（脑活动被激活）。

【易错】 最具迷惑性的错误词是 A) —— activated 误填被动语态。the problem is __(28)__ by individuals 被动语态卡位，A)activated 与 B)aggravated 都是过去分词；但「problem 被激活」搭配反常，且 but 转折要求「程度加深」语义，应选 aggravated。防坑：被动语态先看搭配地道度，再看上下文转折方向。
questions.hint: 根据空格前后的词性、搭配与上下文选择词语；每个词最多使用一次。

questions.prompt: to separate the factual from the possible or merely __(29)__ in how we communicate
questions.shortExplanation: 与 possible 同义递进、扣题「可能性」
questions.detailedExplanation:
【答案】 M) speculative 形容词

【词性槽】 or 并列两个形容词作宾语补足语

【依据】 与 possible 同义递进、扣题「可能性」

全文核心对立是 fact vs possibility，此处用 or merely 把 possible 进一步弱化为「仅仅是推测性的」，speculative 正好表达「猜测性的、未经证实的」，与 the factual from the possible 完美对应。

【竞争词】 D) deliberate 义为「蓄意的」与上下文无关

deliberate 强调「故意的」，to separate the factual from the possible or merely __(29)__ 谈的是事实/可能/推测的区分，没有「故意」的语义场。

N) unanimous 义为「全体一致」与单数抽象类别冲突

unanimous 一般用于人群意见一致，无法与 possible 并列描述命题性质；且与 fact/possibility 对立无关。
questions.hint: 根据空格前后的词性、搭配与上下文选择词语；每个词最多使用一次。

questions.prompt: information presented as fact __(30)__ special responses in our brains
questions.shortExplanation: evoke responses 是固定搭配且时态正确
questions.detailedExplanation:
【答案】 G) evokes 动词

【词性槽】 主语 + ___ + 宾语一般现在时谓语

【依据】 evoke responses 是固定搭配且时态正确

information presented as fact __(30)__ special responses in our brains，evoke responses 表示「引起反应」是常见高频搭配；主句为一般现在时陈述规律，三单形态 evokes 正好匹配主语 information。

questions.prompt: we process the same content with clear indicators of __(31)__
questions.shortExplanation: 与「事实 vs 可能」对照中表示「不确定性」
questions.detailedExplanation:
【答案】 O) uncertainty 名词

【词性槽】 介词 of 后接名词作宾语

【依据】 与「事实 vs 可能」对照中表示「不确定性」

items.title: 2023年12月六级第2套 · 信息匹配
items.passage:
A) Most visitors come to Cape Canaveral, on the northeast coast of Florida, for the tourist attractions. It's home to the second-busiest cruise ship port in the world and is a gateway to the cosmos. Nearly 1.5 million visitors flock here every year to watch rockets, spacecraft, and satellites blast off into the solar system from Kennedy Space Center Visitor Complex. Nearly 64 kilometers of undeveloped beach and 648 square kilometers of protected refuge fan out from the cape's sandy shores.

B) Yet some of Cape Canaveral's most legendary attractions lie unseen, wedged under the sea's surface in mud and sand, for this part of the world has a reputation as a deadly ship trap. Over the centuries, dozens of majestic Old World sailing ships smashed and sank on this irregular stretch of windy Florida coast. They were vessels built for war and commerce, crossing the globe carrying everything from coins to cannons, boxes of silver and gold, chests of jewels and porcelain, and pearls from the Caribbean.

C) Cape Canaveral contains one of the greatest concentrations of colonial shipwrecks in the world. In recent years, advances in radar, diving, detection equipment, computers, and GPS have transformed the hunt. The naked eye might see a pile of rocks, but technology can reveal the precious artifacts(⼈ ⼯制品 ) that lie hidden on the ocean floor.

D) As technology renders the seabed more accessible, the hunt for treasure-filled ships has drawn a fresh tide of salvors(打捞⼈员 ) and their investors—as well as marine archaeologists(考古学家 ) wanting to bring to light the lost relics. But of late, when salvors have found vessels, their rights have been challenged in court. The big question: who should have control of these treasures?

E) High-stakes fights over shipwrecks pit archaeologists against treasure hunters in a vicious cycle of accusations. Archaeologists regard themselves as protectors of history, and they see salvors as careless destroyers. Salvors feel they do the hard work of searching for ships, only to have them stolen from under them when discovered. This kind of clash inevitably takes place on a grand scale. Aside from the salvors, their investors, and the maritime archaeologists who serve as expert witnesses, the battles sweep in local and international governments and organizations like UNESCO that work to protect under-water heritage. The court cases that ensue stretch on for years. Are finders keepers, or do the ships belong to the countries that made them and sent them sailing centuries ago? Where once salvors and archaeologists worked side by side, now they belong to opposing, and equally contemptuous, tribes.

F) Nearly three million vessels lie wrecked on the Earth's ocean floor—from old canoes to the Titanic— and likely less than one percent have been explored. Some—like an ancient Roman ship found off Antikythera, Greece, dated between 70 and 60 BC and carrying astonishingly sophisticated gears and dials for navigating by the sun—are critical to a new understanding of our past. No wonder there is an eternal stirring among everybody from salvors to scholars to find them.

G) In May 2016, a salvor named Bobby Pritchett, president of Global Marine Exploration (GME) in Tampa, Florida, announced that he had discovered scattered remains of a ship buried a kilometer off Cape Canaveral. Over the prior three years, he and his crew had obtained 14 state permits to survey a nearly 260-square-kilometer area off the cape; they worked 250 days a year, backed by investor funds of, he claims, US $4 million. It was hard work. Crew members were up at dawn, dragging sensors from their expedition vessels back and forth, day in and day out, year after year, to detect metal of any kind. Using computer technology, Pritchett and his crew created intricate, color-coded maps marked with the GPS coordinates of thousands of finds, all invisible under a meter of sand.

H) One day in 2015, the magnetometer( 磁⼒计 ) picked up metal that turned out to be an iron cannon; when the divers blew the sand away, they also discovered a more precious bronze cannon with markings indicating French royalty and, not far off, a famous marble column carved with the coat of arms of France, known from historical paintings. The discovery was cause for celebration. The artifacts indicated the divers had likely found the wreck of La Trinité, a 16th-century French vessel that had been at the center of a bloody battle between France and Spain that changed the fate of the United States of America.

I) And then the legal storm began, with GME and Pritchett pitted against Florida and France. The Sunken Military Craft Act of 2004, a US federal act, protects any vessel that was on a military mission, allowing the originating country to claim their ship even centuries later. In 2018, two long years after Pritchett's discovery, the federal district court ruled in favor of France. For Pritchett, the decision was devastating. Millions of dollars of investor funding and years of labor were lost.

J) But this is far from the first time a salvor has lost all rights to a discovery. In 2012, for instance, Spain won a five-year legal battle against Odyssey Marine Exploration, which had hauled 594,000 gold and silver coins from a Spanish wreck off the coast of Portugal across the Atlantic to the United States. "Treasure hunters can be naive," says attorney David Concannon, who has had several maritime archaeologists as clients and represented two sides in the battles over the Titanic for 20 years. "Many treasure hunters don't understand they are going to have to fight for their rights against a government that has an endless supply of money for legal battles that treasure hunters are likely to lose."

K) Putting an inflated price on artifacts rather than viewing them as cultural and historical treasures that transcend any price is what irritates many archaeologists. For the archaeologist, everything in a wreck matters—hair, fabric, a fragment of a newspaper, rat bones-all things speak volumes. Archaeologists don't want artifacts ending up in a private collection instead of taking humanity on a journey of understanding.

L) George Bass is one of the pioneers of under-water archaeology, and a researcher at Texas A&M University. He has testified in court against treasure hunters, but says archaeology is not without its own serious problems. He believes archaeologists need to do a better job themselves instead of routinely criticizing treasure hunters. "Archaeology has a terrible reputation for not publishing enough on its excavations(发掘 ) and finds," he says. Gathering data, unearthing and meticulously preserving and examining finds, verifying identity and origin, piecing together the larger story, and writing and publishing a comprehensive paper or book can take decades. A bit cynically, Bass describes colleagues who never published because they waited so long they became ill or died. Who is more at fault, Bass asks, the professional archaeologist who carefully excavates a site and never publishes on it or the treasure hunter who locates a submerged wreck, salvages part, conserves part, and publishes a book on the operation?

M) Pritchett concedes that his find deserves careful excavation and preservation. "I think what I found should go in a museum," he says. "But I also think I should get paid for what I found." Indeed, it's a bit of a mystery why governments, archaeologists, and treasure hunters can't work together—and why salvors aren't at least given a substantial finder's fee before the original owner takes possession of the vessel and its artifacts.

items.title: 2023年12月六级第2套 · 仔细阅读 · 第一篇
items.passage:
Could you get by without using the internet for four and a half years? That's exactly what singer and actress Selena Gomez has done in a bid to improve her mental health.

She has spoken extensively about the relationship between her social media usage and her mental wellbeing, recalling feeling like "an addict" when she became Instagram's most followed user in 2016. "Taking a break from social media was the best decision that I've ever made for my mental health", says she. "The unnecessary hate and comparisons went away once I put my phone down."

Ditching the web at large, however, is a far more subtle and complicated prospect. The increasing digitisation of our society means that everything from paying a gas bill to plotting a route to a friend's house and even making a phone call is at the mercy of your internet connection. Actively opting out of using the internet becomes a matter of privilege.

Ms Gomez's multi-millionaire status has allowed her to take the "social" out of social media, so she can continue to leverage her enormous fame while keeping the trolls( 恶意挑衅的帖⼦ ) at bay. The fact that she's still the second most-followed woman on Instagram suggests it's entirely possible to maintain a significant web profile to promote various projects—by way of a dedicated team—without being exposed to the cruel comments, hate mail and rape or death threats.

It goes without saying that this is fundamentally different from how the rest of us without beauty deals and films to publicise use the likes of Instagram, TikTok and Twitter, but even the concept of a digital detox(戒瘾 ) requires having a device and connectivity to choose to disconnect from.

The UK's digital divide has worsened over the past two years, leaving poorer families without broadband connections in their homes. Digital exclusion is a major threat to wider societal equality in the UK, so witnessing companies like Facebook championing the metaverse( 元宇宙 ) as the next great frontier when school children are struggling to complete their homework feels particularly irritating.

Consequently, it's worth bearing in mind that while deleting all social media accounts will undoubtedly make some feel infinitely better, many other people benefit from the strong sense of community that sharing platforms can breed.

Internet access will continue to grow in importance as we edge further towards web 3.0, and greater resources and initiatives are needed to provide the underprivileged with the connectivity they desperately need to learn, work and live. It's crucial that people who feel that social media is having a detrimental effect on their mental health are allowed to switch off and for those living in digital exclusion to be able to switch on in the first place.

questions.prompt: What do we learn about singer and actress Selena Gomez in the past four and a half years?

options.text: She has had worsening mental problems.
She has won Instagram's most followers.
She has refrained from using social media.
She has succeeded in a bid on the internet.

questions.shortExplanation: Taking a break from social media was the best decision that I've ever made for my mental health
questions.detailedExplanation:
【答案】 C （细节题）

【判型】 What do we learn about singer and actress Selena Gomez in the past four and a half years? 指向「她过去四年半发生了什么」这一具体事实，没有 infer/imply/mainly。

【拆句】 What do we learn about singer and actress Selena Gomez in the past four and a half years? 是一般疑问句，主干 What do we learn；介词短语 in the past four and a half years 作时间状语，限定考察范围。结构平铺直叙，无陷阱。

【定位】 Taking a break from social media was the best decision that I've ever made for my mental health

远离社交媒体是我为心理健康做过的最好的决定。

【选项】 A) 与原文相反原文说她远离社媒是为改善心理健康（the best decision that I've ever made for my mental health），而 She has had worsening mental problems 把「为改善心理健康」反过来说成「心理问题加重」，与原文方向相反。

B) 偷换概念原文说她「在 2016 年成为 Instagram 关注最多的用户」（she became Instagram's most followed user in 2016），是过去某一时点的事实；She has won Instagram's most followers 用现在完成时把这件 2016 年的事说成「过去四年半内取得」，与题干 in the past four and a half years 不符。

C) ✓ 正确 Taking a break from social media was the best decision that I've ever made for my mental health

↔ She has refrained from using social media 预判「远离社媒」与 She has refrained from using social media 完全吻合，且原文- 选项之间的替换属于六级阅读高频同义替换模式。 D) 偷换概念原文 in a bid to improve her mental health 中 bid 意为「努力、尝试」（熟词僻义），整个短语意为「为改善心理健康所作的努力」；She has succeeded in a bid on the internet 把 bid 当作「竞拍」用，与原文意思完全两回事。

【答案】 C （细节题）

【判型】 Why does actively opting out of using the internet become a matter of privilege? 已把结论摆出，要在原文找直接给出的原因，属于原因型细节题。

【拆句】 Why does actively opting out of using the internet become a matter of privilege? 主干 does opting out become a matter of privilege；动名词短语 actively opting out of using the internet 作主语；a matter of privilege 是表语。Why 直接问原因。

【定位】 The increasing digitisation of our society means that everything from paying a gas bill to plotting a route to a friend's house and even making a phone call is at the mercy of your internet connection. Actively opting out of using the internet becomes a matter of privilege.

我们社会日益数字化意味着——从交一笔煤气费、规划一条去朋友家的路线，甚至打一通电话——一切都受制于你的网络连接。主动选择不使用互联网由此变成一种特权。

【选项】 A) 答非所问 Most people find it subtle and complicated to give up using the internet 改写自 Ditching the web at large, however, is a far more subtle and complicated prospect，描述的是「难度」，并未回答题干「为何成为特权」。 B) 张冠李戴 Most people can hardly ditch the web while avoiding hate and comparisons 把 「避开仇恨与攀比」塞给「为何不上网是特权」这一问题；但 The unnecessary hate and comparisons went away once I put my phone down 讲的是 Gomez 远离社媒后的结果，与 Q47 的因果无关。 C) ✓ 正确 The increasing digitisation of our society means that everything from paying a gas bill to plotting a route to a friend's house and even making a phone call is at the mercy of your internet connection

↔ Most people can hardly get by without the internet due to growing digitisation Could you get by without using the internet for four and a half years? ↔

Most people can hardly get by without the internet 预判的因果（数字化 → 离不开网 → 不上网成特权）与 Most people can hardly get by without the internet due to growing digitisation 一一对应。 D) 无中生有 Most people have been seriously addicted to the web without being aware of it 拿 like "an addict" 套到「普通人不自觉成瘾」上，但原文只说 Gomez 自己感觉像 addict，并没有「普通人不自觉成瘾」这一论断，且与 Q47 因果无关。

Digital exclusion is a major threat to wider societal equality in the UK, so witnessing companies like Facebook championing the metaverse(元宇宙) as the next great frontier when school children are struggling to complete their homework feels particularly irritating.

英国的数字鸿沟在过去两年里加剧，导致较贫困家庭家中没有宽带。数字排斥是英国社会整体公平的一大威胁，因此当学童正为完成作业犯难时，看到 Facebook 之类的公司还在把元宇宙鼓吹成下一个伟大前沿，就让人尤其感到刺目。

↔ due to the metaverse 预判「鼓吹元宇宙会加深数字鸿沟」与 The UK digital divide would further worsen due to the metaverse 完全对应，且推断只走一步，未越界。 B) 无中生有 The concept of the metaverse is believed to be still quite illusory 评价的是「元宇宙是否虚幻」，原文只用 the next great frontier 描述公司的宣传口径，并未对 metaverse 概念本身的「虚幻与否」作判断。

D) 以偏概全 Most families in the UK do not have stable broadband connections 把原文 leaving poorer families without broadband connections in their homes 的「较贫困家庭」扩大为「大多数家庭」；同时这只是引发 irritating 的背景之一，而不是作者觉得 irritating 的核心原因。
