items.title: 2023年12月六级第2套 · 仔细阅读 · 第二篇
items.passage:
Psychologists have long been in disagreement as to whether competition is a learned or a genetic component of human behavior. Whatever it is, you cannot but recognize the effect competition is exerting in academics and many other areas of contemporary life.

Psychologically speaking, competition has been seen as an inevitable consequence of human drives. According to Sigmund Freud, humans are born screaming for attention and full of organic drives for fulfillment in various areas. Initially, we compete for the attention of our parents. Thereafter, we are at the mercy of a battle between our base impulses for self-fulfillment and social and cultural norms which prohibit pure indulgence.

Current work in anthropology( ⼈类学 ) has suggested, however, that this view of the role of competition in human behavior may be incorrect. Thomas Hobbes, one of the great philosophers of the seventeenth century, is perhaps best remembered for his characterization of the "natural world," that is, the world before the imposition of the will of humanity, as being "nasty, brutish, and short." This image of the pre-rational world is still widely held, reinforced by Charles Darwin's highly influential work, The Origin of Species, which established the doctrine of natural selection. This doctrine, which takes for granted that those species best able to adapt to and master the natural environment in which they live will survive, has suggested that the struggle for survival is an inherent human trait which determines a person's success. Darwin's theory has even been summarized as "survival of the fittest"—a phrase Darwin himself never used—further highlighting competition's role in success. As it has often been pointed out, however, there is nothing in the concept of natural selection that suggests that competition is the most successful strategy for "survival of the fittest." Darwin asserted in The Origin of Species that the struggles he was describing should be viewed as metaphors and could easily include dependence and cooperation.

Many studies have been conducted to test the importance placed on competition as opposed to other values, such as cooperation—by various cultures, and generally conclude that Americans uniquely praise competition as natural, inevitable, and desirable. In 1937, the world-renowned anthropologist Margaret Mead published Cooperation and Competition among Primitive Peoples, based on her studies of several societies that did not prize competition, and, in fact, seemed at times to place a negative value on it. One such society was the Zuni Indians of Arizona, and they, Mead found, valued cooperation far more than competition. After studying dozens of such cultures, Mead's final conclusion was that competitiveness is a culturally created aspect of human behavior, and that its prevalence in a particular society is relative to how that society values it.

questions.prompt: What does the author think is easy to see in many areas of contemporary life?

options.text: The disagreement on the inevitability of competition.

questions.shortExplanation: Whatever it is, you cannot but recognize the effect competition is exerting in academics and many other areas of contemporary life. 不管竞争是什么（天生还是习得），你都不得不承认竞争正在学术界以及当代生活的许多其他领域中所产生的影响。
questions.detailedExplanation:
【答案】 D （细节题）

【判型】 题干What does the author think is easy to see in many areas of contemporary life?问的是作者在"当代生活的许多领域"中明确认为容易见到的东西，属于对原文某一具体表述的复述题，没有 infer/imply/mainly about 等推断或主旨信号。

【拆句】 Q51主干是 What ... is easy to see；the author think 是插入的宾语从句性插入语，问的实际是 What is easy to see；in many areas of contemporary life 是地点状语，限定范围。句式平铺，无陷阱。

【定位】 Whatever it is, you cannot but recognize the effect competition is exerting in academics and many other areas of contemporary life. 不管竞争是什么（天生还是习得），你都不得不承认竞争正在学术界以及当代生活的许多其他领域中所产生的影响。

【选项】 A) 偷换概念 The disagreement on the inevitability of competition.借的是Psychologists have long been in disagreement as to whether competition is a learned or a genetic component of human behavior这一句，但原文说"心理学家一直有分歧"，而题干问的是"你不得不看到"的东西，把分歧与显而易见混为一谈；而且原文的分歧点是 learned or genetic（天生还是习得），不是 inevitability（必然性），偷换了概念。

B) 无中生有 The consequence of psychological investigation.中 psychological investigation 在 P1里找不到对应——第 1 段只提到 psychologists in disagreement，没有提任何 investigation 的 consequence；且 consequence（后果）也不是原文 effect 的对应词。属凭空捏造。

C) 张冠李戴 The effect of human drives.借了human drives这个词，但 human drives 出现在第 2 段心理学内部解释里，是"竞争"的原因之一；题干问的是"在当代生活各领域中容易见到的东西"，对应第 1 段尾句，而非第 2 段。属张冠李戴。

D) ✓ 正确 the effect competition is exerting in academics and many other areas of contemporary life↔

The impact of competition. 预判落在"竞争在当代生活中产生的影响"上，The impact of competition.就是它的最简同义改写，词义、对象、范围都对得上。
questions.hint: 回到原文定位题干关键词，比较选项与原文的含义。

questions.prompt: According to psychology, what do people strive to do following the initial stage of their life?

options.text: Fulfill individual needs without incurring adverse effects of human drives.
Indulge in cultural pursuits while keeping their base impulses at bay.
Gain extensive recognition without exposing pure indulgence.
Satisfy their own desires while observing social conventions.

questions.shortExplanation: Thereafter, we are at the mercy of a battle between our base impulses for self-fulfillment and social and cultural norms which prohibit pure indulgence.
questions.detailedExplanation:
【答案】 D （细节题）

【判型】 题干According to psychology, what do people strive to do following the initial stage of their life?问"心理学认为人在初始阶段之后努力做什么"，要的是具体行为描述，属于细节题。

【拆句】 Q52主干是 what do people strive to do；According to psychology 是来源状语； following the initial stage of their life 是介词短语作时间状语。strive to do = 努力去做，注意题干问的是"努力的内容"而不是"努力的结果"。

【定位】 Thereafter, we are at the mercy of a battle between our base impulses for self-fulfillment and social and cultural norms which prohibit pure indulgence.

在那之后，我们便受制于一场拉锯战——一边是我们自我满足的本能冲动，另一边是禁止纯粹放纵的社会与文化规范。

【选项】 A) 与原文相反 Fulfill individual needs without incurring adverse effects of human drives.把原文中的两个对立面（本能冲动 vs 社会规范）改写成"满足需求且不引发本能冲动的负面效应"——但原文里 human drives 本身是积极的追求自我满足的力量，不是"会带来负面后果的东西"；且原文中真正的对立面是 social/cultural norms，与 human drives 无关。属与原文相反兼偷换概念。 B) 与原文相反 Indulge in cultural pursuits while keeping their base impulses at bay.中"沉湎于文化追求、压制本能冲动"完全把原文反过来——原文说的是文化规范禁止放纵、人的本能冲动想要放纵；选项却说人沉湎在文化里、压制本能。属与原文相反。

C) 张冠李戴 Gain extensive recognition without exposing pure indulgence.把"获得广泛认可"放在答案核心——但 recognition 对应的是we compete for the attention of our parents的初始阶段，是题干所问"之后"的前一阶段，时段错位；且 extensive（广泛） 也是对 attention of our parents 的过度扩大。属张冠李戴。 D) ✓ 正确 base impulses for self-fulfillment↔ Satisfy their own desires social and cultural norms which prohibit pure indulgence ↔

while observing social conventions 预判要求同时包含"追求自我欲望"和"受社会规范约束"两端，且两端关系是同时进行的"边追求边受约束"；Satisfy their own desires while observing social conventions. 的 while 把两端缝在一起，与原文 a battle between ... and ... 等值。
questions.hint: 回到原文定位题干关键词，比较选项与原文的含义。

questions.prompt: What do we learn about the "natural world" characterized by Thomas Hobbes?

options.text: It gets misrepresented by philosophers and anthropologists.
It gets distorted in Darwin's The Origin of Species.
It is free from the rational intervention of humans.
It is the pre-rational world rarely appreciated nowadays.

questions.shortExplanation: Thomas Hobbes, one of the great philosophers of the seventeenth century, is perhaps best remembered for his characterization of the "natural world," that is, the world before the imposition of the will of humanity, as being "nasty, brutish, and short."
questions.detailedExplanation:
【答案】 C （细节题）

【判型】 题干What do we learn about the "natural world" characterized by Thomas Hobbes? 问"我们从原文中了解到 Hobbes 所刻画的自然世界是什么"，要的是对术语含义的复述，属于细节题。

【拆句】 Q53主干是 What do we learn about the "natural world"；characterized by Thomas Hobbes 是过去分词短语作后置定语，修饰 natural world，含义="由 Hobbes 所刻画的"。这里要扣的是 Hobbes 给 natural world 下的定义，不是后人的评价。

【定位】 Thomas Hobbes, one of the great philosophers of the seventeenth century, is perhaps best remembered for his characterization of the "natural world," that is, the world before the imposition of the will of humanity, as being "nasty, brutish, and short."

Thomas Hobbes 这位 17 世纪的大哲学家，最为人记得的或许是他对"自然世界"——也就是人类意志介入之前的世界——的刻画："令人厌恶、野蛮且短暂"。

【选项】 A) 无中生有 It gets misrepresented by philosophers and anthropologists.说自然世界被哲学家和人类学家"歪曲表述"——但原文只说 Hobbes 这一形象"被达尔文的工作强化"（reinforced by Charles Darwin's highly influential work），后来又说当代人类学研究"质疑了这一观点"（questioned），并没有说 Hobbes 关于 natural world 的描述被哲学家和人类学家共同歪曲。属无中生有。

B) 与原文相反 It gets distorted in Darwin's The Origin of Species.说自然世界在达尔文的书里被歪曲——但原文是This image of the pre-rational world is still widely held, reinforced by Charles Darwin's highly influential work，达尔文是"加强"而非"歪曲"，方向相反。属与原文相反。 C) ✓ 正确 the world before the imposition of the will of humanity ↔

It is free from the rational intervention of humans. 预判要求答案体现"无人类理性介入"这一特征；It is free from the rational intervention of humans.正是同位语的直接同义改写——free from 完美匹配 before （按时间顺序的不及）。 D) 与原文相反 It is the pre-rational world rarely appreciated nowadays.说 pre-rational world"当今很少受到欣赏"——但原文紧接着说This image of the pre-rational world is still widely held，明确说这一形象"仍被广泛持有"，与选项的 rarely 完全对立。属与原文相反。
questions.hint: 回到原文定位题干关键词，比较选项与原文的含义。

questions.prompt: What can we conclude from Darwin's assertion in The Origin of Species?

options.text: All species inherently depend on others for survival.
Struggles for survival do not exclude mutual support.
Competition weighs as much as cooperation as a survival strategy.
The strongest species proves to be the fittest in natural selection.

questions.shortExplanation: Darwin asserted in The Origin of Species that the struggles he was describing should be viewed as metaphors and could easily include dependence and cooperation. 达尔文在《物种起源》中断言：他所描述的那些斗争应当被视为隐喻，完全可以涵盖依赖与合作。
questions.detailedExplanation:
【答案】 B （推断题）

【判型】 题干What can we conclude from Darwin's assertion in The Origin of Species?用 conclude from 引导，要求从达尔文的断言中得出结论，属于"一步推断题"。

【拆句】 Q54主干是 What can we conclude from Darwin's assertion；in The Origin of Species 是地点状语限定该断言出自哪本书。conclude from 重在"从断言本身推出"，所以答案必须紧贴 Darwin 那句原话，不能拿别的句子做依据。

【定位】 Darwin asserted in The Origin of Species that the struggles he was describing should be viewed as metaphors and could easily include dependence and cooperation. 达尔文在《物种起源》中断言：他所描述的那些斗争应当被视为隐喻，完全可以涵盖依赖与合作。

【选项】 A) 过度推断 All species inherently depend on others for survival.中 All species（所有物种）+ inherently（天生地）是绝对化用语；原文只是说"斗争可以包含依赖与合作"，并未推出"所有物种都天生依赖他者才能生存"。属过度推断。

B) ✓ 正确 the struggles he was describing should be viewed as metaphors and could easily include dependence and cooperation

↔ Struggles for survival do not exclude mutual support. 预判说斗争不排斥互助；Struggles for survival do not exclude mutual support.中 do not exclude 与原文 could include 等值，mutual support 概括 dependence and cooperation，逻辑等值、范围一致。 C) 过度推断 Competition weighs as much as cooperation as a survival strategy.中"竞争与合作作为生存策略权重相当"，把两者并列等值——但原文只说斗争"可以包含"合作，并未在"权重相当"的层面比较两者；权重比较是凭空引入。属过度推断。

D) 偷换概念 The strongest species proves to be the fittest in natural selection.说"最强的物种被证明是最适合的"——但原文的关键点是"survival of the fittest 这个短语达尔文自己从未使用"，且本句要的是"Darwin's assertion"（达尔文的断言），不是社会上对"适者生存"的概括；况且 fittest 也不等于 strongest，原文专门指出自然选择并不暗示竞争才是最优策略。属偷换概念。
questions.hint: 回到原文定位题干关键词，比较选项与原文的含义。

questions.prompt: What conclusion did Margaret Mead reach after studying dozens of different cultures?

options.text: It is characteristic of humans to be competitive.
Americans are uniquely opposed to cooperation.
Competition is relatively more prevalent in Western societies.
People's attitude towards competition is actually culture-bound.

questions.shortExplanation: After studying dozens of such cultures, Mead's final conclusion was that competitiveness is a culturally created aspect of human behavior, and that its prevalence in a particular society is relative to how that society values it. 在研究了数十个这样的文化之后，Mead 的最终结论是：竞争性是人类行为中由文化塑造出的一面；它在某个具体社会中的普遍程度，取决于该社会对它的评价。
questions.detailedExplanation:
【答案】 D （细节题）

【判型】 题干What conclusion did Margaret Mead reach after studying dozens of different cultures?问"Mead 得出了什么结论"，是对原文最后一句明文表达的结论的复述，属于细节题。

【拆句】 Q55主干是 What conclusion did Margaret Mead reach；after studying dozens of different cultures 是时间状语。注意问的是"Mead 的结论"，所以答案必须是 Mead's final conclusion 那一句的同义改写，而不是 Mead 研究过程的具体发现（那是中间结论， 不是 final conclusion）。

【定位】 After studying dozens of such cultures, Mead's final conclusion was that competitiveness is a culturally created aspect of human behavior, and that its prevalence in a particular society is relative to how that society values it. 在研究了数十个这样的文化之后，Mead 的最终结论是：竞争性是人类行为中由文化塑造出的一面；它在某个具体社会中的普遍程度，取决于该社会对它的评价。

【选项】 A) 与原文相反 It is characteristic of humans to be competitive.说"竞争是人类的天性"——但这正是 Mead 想要驳斥的观点，Mead 的结论恰恰相反：竞争性不是天生的，而是文化塑造的。属与原文相反。

B) 偷换概念 Americans are uniquely opposed to cooperation.说美国人"独一无二地反对合作"——但原文是Americans uniquely praise competition as natural, inevitable, and desirable，说美国人独一无二地"赞美竞争"，并未说他们反对合作；"赞美 X"与"反对 Y"不可直接对调。属偷换概念。

C) 过度推断 Competition is relatively more prevalent in Western societies.说"竞争在西方社会中相对更普遍"——但 Mead 的最终结论是"竞争普遍程度取决于社会评价"，并未把社会分成"西方/非西方"两类、也未声称"竞争在西方更普遍"是普遍规律。属过度推断兼以偏概全。 D) ✓ 正确 competitiveness is a culturally created aspect of human behavior↔

People's attitude towards competition is actually culture-bound. its prevalence in a particular society is relative to how that society values it↔

actually culture-bound 预判要求答案体现"竞争性受文化决定"；People's attitude towards competition is actually culture-bound.中 culture-bound 直接等值于 culturally created，是 Mead 结论的最简同义改写。
questions.hint: 回到原文定位题干关键词，比较选项与原文的含义。

items.title: 2023年12月六级第3套 · 选词填空
items.passage:
Modern U.S. cities were designed to make exercise unnecessary. Cars and elevators once symbolized urban areas as machines for more efficient living. Now it is clear that these improvements provide great benefits but also [26] _____ health costs. Recent studies show that urban [27] _____ encourages more driving and is associated with heavier weight. This [28] _____ suggests that the layout and design of cities can hinder or promote healthier lifestyle choices and it is [29] _____ that urban planners bear this in mind.

Unfortunately, urban planning still centers in large part on solving the problems of the past. Of course cities still need to [30] _____ standard public health practices, such as separating toxic facilities from homes and restricting heavy truck traffic through [31] _____ residential areas. But it's also important to create healthier cities—and the discussion is already underway. More and more city planners are paying increasing attention to encouraging physical activity by making it easier and safer for people to recreate, walk, bike and take public transportation. Many studies of [32] _____ show that people live the longest in environments where physical activity is part of everyday life.

Providing more walkable spaces, better protected bike lanes and more [33] _____ spaces are important steps. But even smaller changes can be effective.

Cities can close off streets on weekends to encourage communities to get out and walk. They also can provide more seating in public places, so that less-fit residents can rest during their journeys. Using public spaces in cities as places where people can exercise promotes [34] _____ , rather than allowing physical activity to become restricted to private gyms with often-expensive monthly fees that [35] _____ less wealthy people from joining.

questions.prompt: these improvements provide great benefits but also __(26)__ health costs
questions.shortExplanation: impose costs 是固定地道搭配 impose costs/burden/restrictions on… 是英语里高频搭配，表"强加、招致（成本/负担）"。本句用 but also 把"带来好处"与"招致健康代价"形成转折并列：provide great benefits but also __(26)__ health costs，impose 在 cost 前正是最自然的动词。
questions.detailedExplanation:
【答案】 G) impose 动词

【词性槽】 also 后并列谓语缺动词

【依据】 impose costs 是固定地道搭配 impose costs/burden/restrictions on… 是英语里高频搭配，表"强加、招致（成本/负担）"。本句用 but also 把"带来好处"与"招致健康代价"形成转折并列：provide great benefits but also __(26)__ health costs，impose 在 cost 前正是最自然的动词。

【竞争词】 J) navigate "导航健康代价"搭配不成立

navigate 不与 costs 搭配；意义上也无法表达"招致"。

N) vibrate 义为"振动"，与抽象 health costs 不搭

vibrate 是物理动词，与抽象代价宾语无法搭配。
questions.hint: 根据空格前后的词性、搭配与上下文选择词语；每个词最多使用一次。

questions.prompt: Recent studies show that urban __(27)__ encourages more driving and is associated with heavier weight.
questions.shortExplanation: urban sprawl 是地道术语，对应"城市蔓延招致开车多+肥胖" urban sprawl（城市无序扩张）是城市规划/健康研究里高度固定的术语，指城市低密度向外摊大饼。摊得越大，居民越依赖开车、越少步行，自然 encourages more driving and is associated with heavier weight——因果链严丝合缝。
questions.detailedExplanation:
【答案】 M) sprawl 名词

【词性槽】 形容词 urban 后需名词作主语

【依据】 urban sprawl 是地道术语，对应"城市蔓延招致开车多+肥胖" urban sprawl（城市无序扩张）是城市规划/健康研究里高度固定的术语，指城市低密度向外摊大饼。摊得越大，居民越依赖开车、越少步行，自然 encourages more driving and is associated with heavier weight——因果链严丝合缝。

【竞争词】 A) correlation下一题 28 才需要 correlation

correlation 多表"相关性"，更适合下句 This __(28)__ suggests that… 指代"上一句揭示的相关性"，留给 28 题更恰当；而且 urban correlation 也不是常见说法。

D) equity "城市公平鼓励开车"逻辑荒诞

equity 本意"公平"，与"鼓励更多开车、体重更重"的负面后果在逻辑上矛盾。34 题的 promote ___ 才是它的归宿。

I) longevity"城市寿命鼓励开车"语义不通

longevity "长寿" 与 "鼓励开车、体重增加" 的负面因果对不上；32 题的 studies of ___ 才与它匹配。

O) vicinity"城市附近鼓励开车"指代不清

vicinity 指"附近地区"，多用于 in the vicinity of 短语，单独作 "urban + vicinity" 搭配不成立，也无法解释"鼓励开车"。

【易错】 最具迷惑性的错误词是 O) —— vicinity 看着也能配 urban。urban + 名词的位置最容易被 vicinity 干扰——"城市的附近地区"似通非通。但比对学科术语 urban sprawl 才是城市规划的固定说法，且后文"鼓励开车/体重增加"只能由"无序扩张"解释。防坑句：拿不准就回看后续 encourages more driving 因果链是否成立。
questions.hint: 根据空格前后的词性、搭配与上下文选择词语；每个词最多使用一次。

questions.prompt: This __(28)__ suggests that the layout and design of cities can hinder or promote healthier lifestyle choices
questions.shortExplanation: 回指上句"扩张→开车多→更胖"的相关性上一句 Recent studies show that urban __(27)__ encourages more driving and is associated with heavier weight. 描述的就是"城市蔓延"与"体重"之间的关联——is associated with 的标准说法正是 correlation。本句用 This correlation 回指，紧扣"相关性"语义。
questions.detailedExplanation:
【答案】 A) correlation 名词

【词性槽】 指示词 This 后需单数名词

【依据】 回指上句"扩张→开车多→更胖"的相关性上一句 Recent studies show that urban __(27)__ encourages more driving and is associated with heavier weight. 描述的就是"城市蔓延"与"体重"之间的关联——is associated with 的标准说法正是 correlation。本句用 This correlation 回指，紧扣"相关性"语义。

【竞争词】 D) equity "这种公平"无回指对象

上句没有讨论"公平"，equity 在此找不到回指意义；语段焦点是"扩张和体重的关联"。

I) longevity 上句谈"体重增加"不谈"寿命"

longevity "长寿" 与上句"鼓励开车、体重增加"语义对不上号。

O) vicinity vicinity 表地点，不指代研究结论

This vicinity 只能指"这一带"，无法回指上句揭示的关系。
questions.hint: 根据空格前后的词性、搭配与上下文选择词语；每个词最多使用一次。

questions.prompt: it is __(29)__ that urban planners bear this in mind
questions.shortExplanation: "城市规划者必须铭记这一点至关重要"
questions.detailedExplanation:
【答案】 F) imperative 形容词

【词性槽】 it is ___ that 句型中需形容词作表语

【依据】 "城市规划者必须铭记这一点至关重要"

imperative "至关重要的、势在必行的" 恰好是 it is imperative that 的高频搭配，并且 that 从句里 bear this in mind 用了 bear（虚拟语气的原形动词），正与 imperative 引导的虚拟语气句型对得上。语义上承接上文 Recent studies show that urban __(27)__ encourages more driving and is associated with heavier weight.，把"城市规划要顾及健康"提到一个必须做的高度。

【竞争词】 H) irrespective 不用于 it is ___ that 句型

irrespective 只能搭配 of，不进入 "it is + adj. + that" 句型，结构上排除。

L) rotten 色彩与作者立场相反

作者整段在呼吁城市规划者重视健康，是正面倡导；代入 it is rotten that…（"这件事真糟糕"） 情感色彩完全相反。
questions.hint: 根据空格前后的词性、搭配与上下文选择词语；每个词最多使用一次。

questions.prompt: cities still need to __(30)__ standard public health practices
questions.shortExplanation: "推行/促进标准公共卫生做法"
questions.detailedExplanation:
【答案】 E) foster 动词

【词性槽】 情态动词 need to 后需动词原形

【依据】 "推行/促进标准公共卫生做法"

foster 表"促进、推行、培育"，与 standard public health practices 搭配恰好表达"城市仍需推行/促进标准公共卫生做法"。本句承接 urban planning still centers in large part on solving the problems of the past，foster 体现"继续保留并落实传统做法"的正面动作。

【竞争词】 C) deter "阻止公共卫生做法"与全文立场相反

deter 表"阻止"，城市不可能去"阻止"公共卫生措施；它的归宿在 35 题的"deter…from joining"句式里。

G) impose impose 强调"强加"，色彩偏重 + 留给 26 题用

impose 多与 burden/cost/tax/restriction 搭配，强调强行加诸；与 standard public health practices 的正面语义不搭。26 题的 impose health costs（招致健康代价）是它的真正归宿。

J) navigate "导航公共卫生做法"搭配不通

navigate 指"穿行、操纵"，常配 navigate the system/streets，不与 practices 直接搭配表示"推行"。

N) vibrate 义为"振动"，与公共卫生主题南辕北辙

vibrate 是物理动作，与抽象的 practices 完全无法搭配。

【易错】 最具迷惑性的错误词是 G) —— impose 也能后接抽象宾语。动词空填 impose 看似可行 （"施加公共卫生做法"似乎也通），但 impose 色彩偏"强加、施压"，与 standard public health practices 的正面/中性语义不合；况且 26 题的 impose health costs 才是 impose 真正的归宿。防坑句：动词色彩要与宾语色彩一致。

questions.prompt: restricting heavy truck traffic through __(31)__ residential areas
questions.shortExplanation: "限制重型卡车穿越人口稠密的居民区"语义最顺
questions.detailedExplanation:
【答案】 B) dense 形容词

【词性槽】 名词 areas 前需形容词作定语

【依据】 "限制重型卡车穿越人口稠密的居民区"语义最顺

句子讲的是公共健康措施——把有害设施与住宅隔开、限制重卡穿行居民区。能让"限制重卡"具有现实意义的形容词，最自然的就是"人口稠密的"：人越密，重卡穿行的健康风险越大。代入后 restricting heavy truck traffic through __(31)__ residential areas 读作 dense residential areas，搭配地道、语义贴。

【竞争词】 F) imperative 义为"至关重要的"，与 residential areas 语义不搭

imperative 通常修饰任务、需求（it is imperative that…），不用来形容"居民区"的物理属性； 而且后面 29 题正需要 it is imperative that… 的句式，留给那里更合适。

H) irrespective 几乎只用作 irrespective of 短语，做后置状语

irrespective 几乎不放在名词前作前置定语，本句也没有 of 引出的比较对象，结构上就用不了。

K) recreational "娱乐的居民区"语义不通

recreational 通常修饰 spaces、activities、facilities；与 residential 一起说"娱乐的居民区"逻辑奇怪。况且 33 题的 more __(33)__ spaces 正等着 recreational。

L) rotten 色彩太负面，超出此处中性描述

rotten 强调"腐败""糟糕透顶"，色彩极重；文章只是中性地讲"哪些居民区要保护"，没有要把这些社区贬为"破败"之意。

questions.prompt: Many studies of __(32)__ show that people live the longest in environments where physical activity is part of everyday life.
questions.shortExplanation: "长寿研究"与 live the longest 完美呼应
questions.detailedExplanation:
【答案】 I) longevity 名词

【竞争词】 D) equity "公平研究"与活得最久无关

equity 与 live the longest 没有语义指向；equity 留给 34 题正合适。

O) vicinity "附近地区研究"语义空泛

studies of vicinity 不是常见搭配，也不指向"寿命/活得久"这个研究结论。

questions.detailedExplanation:
【答案】 K) recreational 形容词

【依据】 "更多娱乐空间"呼应"鼓励市民活动" 第三段在讲"提供促进活动的城市要素"，与 walkable spaces（步行空间）、protected bike lanes（受保护的自行车道）并列的第三项理应是同一逻辑的活动空间。recreational spaces "娱乐/休闲空间" 正好契合：让人有地方运动、玩耍，呼应 encouraging physical activity by making it easier and safer for people to recreate, walk, bike and take public transportation 里的 recreate。

不能作前置定语，结构上排除。

questions.shortExplanation: deter sb. from doing 是固定搭配
questions.detailedExplanation:
【答案】 C) deter 动词

【词性槽】 that 引导的定语从句缺谓语

【依据】 deter sb. from doing 是固定搭配

deter "使打消念头/阻止"，固定搭配 deter sb. from doing sth.。代入恰好表达"昂贵会员费让低收入者打消加入健身房的念头"，与 34 题的 equity 形成正反对照，把"私人健身房不公平"这层意思讲透。

impose sth. on sb. 是其正确搭配，不能说 impose sb. from doing。26 题才是它的归宿。

navigate 是"穿行、操纵"，与"阻止某人做某事"语义和结构都不匹配。

N) vibrate 义为"振动"，与抽象的"阻止加入"无关

vibrate 是物理动词，无法承接 sb. from doing。

items.title: 2023年12月六级第3套 · 信息匹配
items.passage:
A) You may have heard that learning another language is one method for preventing or at least postponing the onset of dementia. Dementia refers to the loss of cognitive abilities, and one of its most common forms is Alzheimer's disease(阿尔茨海默⽒病). At this time, the causes of the disease are not well understood, and consequently, there are no proven steps that people can take to prevent it. Nonetheless, some researchers have suggested that learning a foreign language might help delay the onset of dementia.

B) To explore this possibility more deeply, let's look at some of the common misconceptions about dementia and the aging brain. First of all, dementia is not an inevitable part of the normal aging process. Most older adults do not develop Alzheimer's disease or other forms of dementia. It is also important to remember that dementia is not the same thing as normal forgetfulness. At any age, we might experience difficulty finding the exact word we want or have trouble remembering the name of the person we just met. People with dementia have more serious problems, like feeling confused or getting lost in a familiar place. Think of it this way: If you forget where you parked your car at the mall, that's normal; if you forget how to drive a car, that may be a signal that something more serious is going on.

C) The idea that dementia can be prevented is based on the comparison of the brain to a muscle. When people talk about the brain, they sometimes say things like "It is important to exercise your brain" or "To stay mentally fit, you have to give your brain a workout." Although these are colorful analogies, in reality the brain is not a muscle. Unlike muscles, the brain is always active and works even during periods of rest and sleep. In addition, although some muscle cells have a lifespan of only a few days, brain cells last a lifetime. Not only that, but it has been shown that new brain cells are being created throughout one's lifespan.

D) While it makes for a colorful analogy, comparing the brain to a muscle is inaccurate and misleading. So, if the brain is not a muscle, can it still be exercised? Once again, researchers don't know for sure. There are now many computer, online, and mobile device applications that claim to be able to "train your brain," and they typically tap into a variety of cognitive abilities. However, research suggests that although this type of training may improve one's abilities at the tasks themselves, they don't seem to improve other abilities. In other words, practicing a letter-detection task will, over time, improve your letter-detection skills, but it will not necessarily enhance your other perceptual abilities.

E) However, there is some reason to believe that learning languages might be different. The best evidence that foreign language learning confers cognitive benefits comes from research with those who are already bilingual(双语的). Bilingualism most commonly occurs when children are exposed to two languages, either in the home (mom speaks Dutch, dad speaks Spanish) or more formally in early schooling. But bilingualism certainly occurs in adulthood as well.

F) Bilingualism and multilingualism are actually more common than you might think. In fact, it has been estimated that there are fewer monolingual speakers in the world than bilinguals and multilinguals. Although in many countries most inhabitants share just one language, other countries have several official languages. Switzerland, for example, has four official languages: German, French, Italian, and Romansh. Throughout large parts of Africa, Arabic, Swahili, French, and English are often known and used by individuals who speak a different, native language in their home than they do in the marketplace. So bilingualism and multilingualism are to be found throughout the world. And with regard to cognitive abilities, the research on those who speak more than one language paints an encouraging picture.

G) For one thing, bilinguals are better at multitasking. One explanation of this superiority is that speakers of two languages are continually inhibiting one of their languages, and this process of inhibition confers general cognitive benefits to other activities. In fact, bilingual individuals outperform their monolingual counterparts on a variety of cognitive tasks, such as following complex instructions, and switching to new instructions. For the sake of completeness, it should be noted that the advantages of being bilingual are not universal across all cognitive domains. Bilingual individuals have been shown to have smaller vocabularies and to take longer in retrieving words from memory when compared to monolinguals. In the long run, however, the cognitive and linguistic advantages of being bilingual far outweigh these two drawbacks.

H) If the benefits of being bilingual spill over to other aspects of cognition, then we would expect to see a lower incidence of Alzheimer's disease in bilinguals than in monolinguals, or at least a later onset of Alzheimer's for bilinguals. In fact, there is evidence to support this claim. The psychologist Ellen Bialystok and her colleagues obtained the histories of 184 individuals who had made use of a memory clinic in Toronto. For those who showed signs of dementia, the monolinguals in the sample had an average age of 71.4 years at time of onset. The bilinguals, in contrast, received their diagnosis at 75.5 years, on average. In a study of this sort, a difference of four years is highly significant, and could not be explained by other systematic differences between the two groups. For example, the monolinguals reported, on average, a year and a half more schooling than their bilingual counterparts, so the effect was clearly not due to formal education.

I) A separate study, conducted in India, found strikingly similar results: bilingual patients developed symptoms of dementia 4.5 years later than monolinguals, even after other potential factors, such as gender and occupation, were controlled for. In addition, researchers have reported other positive effects of bilingualism for cognitive abilities in later life, even when the person acquired the language in adulthood. Crucially, Bialystok suggested that the positive benefits of being bilingual were only found in those who used both languages all the time.

J) But encouraging as these kinds of studies are, they still have not established exactly how or why differences between bilinguals and monolinguals exist. Because these studies looked back at the histories of people who were already bilingual, the results can only say that a difference between the two groups was found, but not why that difference occurred. Further research is needed to determine what caused the differences in age of onset between the two groups.

K) Other studies of successful aging suggest that being connected to one's community and having plenty of social interaction is also important in delaying or even preventing the onset of dementia. Once again, however, the results are far less clear than the popular media might lead you to believe. Older individuals who lead active social lives are, almost by definition, healthier than their counterparts who rarely leave their homes or interact with others. So we can't really say whether being socially active prevents the onset of dementia, or if people who don't have dementia are more likely to be socially active.

L) But even if studying a foreign language is not a magical cure-all, there is one thing it will do: It will make you a better speaker of a foreign language. Doing that confers a whole host of advantages we do know about.

questions.prompt: It is claimed that more monolinguals suffer from Alzheimer's disease than bilinguals.
questions.shortExplanation: 单语者中阿尔茨海默氏病人更多
questions.detailedExplanation:

【锚点】 单语者中阿尔茨海默氏病人更多

【定位】 If the benefits of being bilingual spill over to other aspects of cognition, then we would expect to see a lower incidence of Alzheimer's disease in bilinguals than in monolinguals, or at least a later onset of Alzheimer's for bilinguals. In fact, there is evidence to support this claim.

如果双语带来的好处可以外溢到其他认知层面，那么我们就可能预期双语者中阿尔茨海默氏病的发病率低于单语者，或者至少双语者发病时间更晚。事实上，确实有证据支持这一主张。

items.title: 2023年12月六级第3套 · 仔细阅读 · 第一篇
items.passage:
Research is meant to benefit society by raising public awareness and creating products and innovations that enhance development. For research to serve its full purpose, the results must leave the confines of research laboratories and academic journals.

Findings effectively communicated can go a long way to serve the interests of the public. They can help address social injustices or improve treatments offered to patients.

Many researchers seem to be content with sharing the results of their studies in academic journals or at conferences. But few journals allow everybody to read the findings. Even articles freely available are usually written in academic language incomprehensible to the average reader.

For researchers in the tenure-track system, their main goal is winning tenure, which in part can be achieved by getting a number of papers published in prominent journals. Pressures like this mean community-level outreach is not prioritised.

Many researchers lack the writing skills to describe their results to a general audience. They may also worry about whether the public will understand their findings, or about findings being used to influence controversial policies. These concerns cause some researchers to shy away from communicating their findings outside the academic community.

Propagating research findings beyond academic publications is particularly crucial for addressing certain social discrepancies. It can help families, communities, healthcare providers, policymakers, government agencies and other stakeholders to understand and respond to crises that plague society.

The benefits of sharing findings flow both ways. Engaging with other researchers and the public can lead to unexpected new connections and new ideas that could suggest fruitful new directions for research.

To benefit both researchers and the communities, the need to find innovative, accessible ways to share the work cannot be overstated.

Institutions and funding organisations should support more researchers to publish in open access journals so that the public doesn't have to pay to read them. Institutions and researchers should invest in partnerships that expand capacity for sharing results more broadly.

Furthermore, ethics committees should make it mandatory for researchers to share their results with the public. Every research participant should opt in or out of receiving results, as part of the process of giving informed consent.

There could be misunderstanding of the findings presented by the researcher because of technical terms. But this can be resolved by researchers engaging the services of professional writers or communication officers to help with translating their study into more accessible language and share it widely with media outlets and the public.

Sharing results with the people who are most affected by them makes us better researchers and ensures that our work can be used to improve people's lives. Institutions and collaborators must recognise the value of doing so.

questions.prompt: How can research serve its full purpose according to the author?

options.text: With researchers being aware of public interests.
With its findings published in prominent journals.
With researchers creating products that enhance social development.
With its findings properly communicated beyond the academic circle.

questions.shortExplanation: For research to serve its full purpose, the results must leave the confines of research laboratories and academic journals.
questions.detailedExplanation:
【答案】 D （细节题）

【判型】 How can research serve its full purpose according to the author? 问的是"通过什么方式"，要求从文中找到作者明示的条件句。

【拆句】 题干 How can research serve its full purpose according to the author? 是一个标准 How 类疑问句：情态动词 can 提到主语 research 前，谓语 serve 带宾语 its full purpose；according to the author 是状语，只是限定信息来源，不影响理解。结构平铺直叙，无陷阱。

【定位】 For research to serve its full purpose, the results must leave the confines of research laboratories and academic journals.

要让研究充分发挥其作用，研究结果必须走出实验室和学术期刊的范围。

【选项】 A) 无中生有 With researchers being aware of public interests 说"研究者要意识到公众利益"，原文从未谈论"研究者的觉察"这一前提，P1 强调的是"传播"而非"觉察"。

B) 与原文相反 With its findings published in prominent journals 把"发表在顶级期刊上"当作答案， 但 P1 恰恰指出"必须离开学术期刊"——发表在顶级期刊只是 P4 中讲到的研究者评职称的手段，与"研究发挥充分作用"相反。 C) 张冠李戴 With researchers creating products that enhance social development 把 creating products and innovations that enhance development 这句"研究的目标之一"挪用来作为"研究发挥作用的方式"——这是研究的目的描述，不是 serve its full purpose 的条件。

D) ✓ 正确 the results must leave the confines of research laboratories and academic journals ↔

With its findings properly communicated beyond the academic circle 选项 With its findings properly communicated beyond the academic circle 用同义替换还原了预判的"研究结果必须走出学术圈"，是定位句的标准转述。
questions.hint: 回到原文定位题干关键词，比较选项与原文的含义。

questions.prompt: Why do ordinary readers find it difficult to access the results of researchers' studies?

options.text: They cannot understand the academic language used for reporting these results.
They feel intimidated by the jargon researchers use to describe their findings.
They do not attend conferences where these results are freely available.
They have few chances to locate the journals that publish these findings.

questions.shortExplanation: Even articles freely available are usually written in academic language incomprehensible to the average reader.
questions.detailedExplanation:
【答案】 A （细节题）

【判型】 Why do ordinary readers find it difficult to access the results of researchers' studies? 问具体原因，且原因点是"读不懂研究结果"这一具体行为，需回原文找直接陈述。

【拆句】 题干 Why do ordinary readers find it difficult to access the results of researchers' studies? 主干是 readers find it difficult to access，find sth difficult to do 是常见结构，it 是形式宾语，真正宾语是后面的不定式 to access...；the results of researchers' studies 是多重 of 修饰的名词短语。无难点。

【定位】 Even articles freely available are usually written in academic language incomprehensible to the average reader.

即便那些免费可读的文章，通常也是用普通读者无法理解的学术语言写成。

【选项】 A) ✓ 正确 academic language incomprehensible to the average reader ↔

They cannot understand the academic language used for reporting these results 选项 They cannot understand the academic language used for reporting these results 是定位句"X 对 Y 不可理解"到"Y 不能理解 X"的标准视角转换，与预判完全吻合。 B) 无中生有 They feel intimidated by the jargon researchers use to describe their findings 中 feel intimidated（感到畏惧）原文从未提及；jargon（行话）原文也未出现这个词。

C) 偷换概念 They do not attend conferences where these results are freely available 把 freely available 从"免费可读"偷换为"会议上免费提供"；原文是说"少数期刊允许人人阅读，即便免费可读也用艰涩语言"，不是说在 conferences 上免费提供。 D) 答非所问 They have few chances to locate the journals that publish these findings 说"普通读者找不到这些期刊"，但原文 But few journals allow everybody to read the findings 说的是"少数期刊允许所有人阅读"——即"读到"的问题，而非"找到"的问题； 且题干问的是 difficult to access the results（读懂结果），不是 difficult to locate the journals（找到期刊）。
questions.hint: 回到原文定位题干关键词，比较选项与原文的含义。

questions.prompt: What is one of the reasons some researchers won't prioritise communicating their findings to the public?

options.text: They can thrive on the papers published.
Their top consideration is to win tenure
Their main goal is gaining recognition in their field.
They have to struggle to reach out to the community.

questions.shortExplanation: For researchers in the tenure-track system, their main goal is winning tenure, which in part can be achieved by getting a number of papers published in prominent journals. Pressures like this mean community-level outreach is not prioritised.
questions.detailedExplanation:
【答案】 B （细节题）

【判型】 What is one of the reasons some researchers won't prioritise communicating their findings to the public? 直接问"原因之一"，要求从原文找明示因果句。

【拆句】 题干 What is one of the reasons some researchers won't prioritise communicating their findings to the public? 主干是 What is one of the reasons...；reasons 后的 some researchers won't prioritise... 是省略 that 的定语从句修饰 reasons；communicating 后的 their findings to the public 是 V-ing 短语的双宾语结构。结构略长但语义清晰。

【定位】 For researchers in the tenure-track system, their main goal is winning tenure, which in part can be achieved by getting a number of papers published in prominent journals. Pressures like this mean community-level outreach is not prioritised.

对处在终身教职轨制度中的研究者来说，他们的主要目标是获得终身教职，而获得终身教职部分可以通过在顶级期刊上发表若干论文实现。诸如此类的压力意味着面向社区层面的对外传播不被优先考虑。

【选项】 A) 答非所问 They can thrive on the papers published 说"他们靠发表的论文茁壮成长"——题干问的是"为什么不优先对外传播的原因"，A 描述的是"发文的结果/好处"，而非"不愿对外传播的原因"，且 thrive on 的积极语义与原文"压力"对应不上。

B) ✓ 正确 their main goal is winning tenure ↔ Their top consideration is to win tenure 选项 Their top consideration is to win tenure 是定位句 their main goal is winning tenure 几乎逐词的同义替换，且与预判"首要目标是 tenure"完全一致。

C) 无中生有 Their main goal is gaining recognition in their field 把研究者目标改成"在领域内获得认可"——原文 their main goal is winning tenure 明确写的是 winning tenure（拿到终身教职），不是 recognition；这是把因果中段的"靠发文"过度泛化为"求认可"。 D) 与原文相反 They have to struggle to reach out to the community 说"他们必须努力对外传播"， 但原文 community-level outreach is not prioritised 是说"不优先做"——不是"努力做"，方向完全相反。
questions.hint: 回到原文定位题干关键词，比较选项与原文的含义。

questions.prompt: How can sharing findings benefit researchers themselves?

options.text: By helping them to identify new research directions.
By enabling them to understand crises plaguing society.
By enabling them to effectively address social discrepancies.
By helping them to forge ties with government agencies.

questions.shortExplanation: Engaging with other researchers and the public can lead to unexpected new connections and new ideas that could suggest fruitful new directions for research.
questions.detailedExplanation:
【答案】 A （细节题）

【判型】 How can sharing findings benefit researchers themselves? 问"如何受益"，需要在原文找具体受益机制的陈述。

【拆句】 题干 How can sharing findings benefit researchers themselves? 主干 sharing findings 作主语（动名词短语），benefit 是及物动词，researchers themselves 是宾语+反身代词强调。themselves 是理解关键，标明"受益方是研究者自己"。

【定位】 Engaging with other researchers and the public can lead to unexpected new connections and new ideas that could suggest fruitful new directions for research.

与其他研究者及公众的互动可能催生意想不到的新联系和新想法，进而可能指明富有成果的新研究方向。

【选项】 A) ✓ 正确 could suggest fruitful new directions for research ↔

By helping them to identify new research directions 选项 By helping them to identify new research directions 是定位句 could suggest fruitful new directions for research 的同义改写，且 By Ving 结构正好回应题干 How。

B) 张冠李戴 By enabling them to understand crises plaguing society 借用了 respond to crises that plague society 的措辞——但 P6 讲的是"分享有助于其他主体（家庭、社区、政策制定者等）理解危机"，受益者并非"研究者自身"；与题干 researchers themselves 错位。

C) 张冠李戴 By enabling them to effectively address social discrepancies 借用 addressing certain social discrepancies 的措辞——同样是 P6 讲对社会的好处，而非对研究者自身的好处；与题干 themselves 错位。

D) 无中生有 By helping them to forge ties with government agencies 说"帮助他们与政府机构建立关系"——原文虽提过 government agencies（P6 列举受益方时），但从未把"与政府机构结盟"作为研究者自身的受益方式。
questions.hint: 回到原文定位题干关键词，比较选项与原文的含义。

questions.prompt: Why are researchers advised to engage the services of professional writers or communication officers?

options.text: To satisfy ethics committees' mandatory requirements of researchers.
To translate their study into languages accessible to readers overseas.
To make their publications correctly understood by the public.
To render their findings acceptable by prominent journals.

questions.shortExplanation: But this can be resolved by researchers engaging the services of professional writers or communication officers to help with translating their study into more accessible language and share it widely with media outlets and the public. 但这可以通过研究者聘请专业写手或传播官来解决，让他们帮助把研究"翻译"成更通俗易懂的语言，并广泛地向媒体和公众分享。
questions.detailedExplanation:
【答案】 C （细节题）

【判型】 Why are researchers advised to engage the services of professional writers or communication officers? 问"为何建议聘请"，需要从原文找明示的目的或结果状语。

【拆句】 题干 Why are researchers advised to engage the services of professional writers or communication officers? 是被动语态：are advised to do（被建议做）；engage 在此为正式词义"聘请"；professional writers or communication officers 是并列名词词组。结构清晰，注意 engage 不是"参与"而是"聘用"。

【定位】 But this can be resolved by researchers engaging the services of professional writers or communication officers to help with translating their study into more accessible language and share it widely with media outlets and the public. 但这可以通过研究者聘请专业写手或传播官来解决，让他们帮助把研究"翻译"成更通俗易懂的语言，并广泛地向媒体和公众分享。

【选项】 A) 张冠李戴 To satisfy ethics committees' mandatory requirements of researchers 把 ethics committees should make it mandatory 这一伦理委员会的强制要求挪用来作为聘请写手的目的；但 P10 与 P11 是两个独立建议——伦理委员会强制研究者分享是一回事，聘请写手帮助翻译是另一回事，两者目的不同。

B) 偷换概念 To translate their study into languages accessible to readers overseas 把 more accessible language 偷换为 languages accessible to readers overseas（让海外读者读懂）——原文从未提及 overseas / readers abroad 等概念，只说"通俗易懂"，不涉及外语翻译。

C) ✓ 正确 to help with translating their study into more accessible language↔

To make their publications correctly understood by the public There could be misunderstanding of the findings presented by the researcher because of technical terms.

↔ correctly understood by the public 选项 To make their publications correctly understood by the public 是 P11 整段问题（误解）与解决（翻译成通俗语言）的目的合成，与预判完全吻合。

D) 与原文相反 To render their findings acceptable by prominent journals 说"让顶级期刊接受研究"——这是 P4 中谈到的另一动机（评 tenure 时投顶级期刊），且 P1 明确批判"留在期刊里就发挥不了作用"；聘请写手的目的恰恰是"走出期刊面向公众"，方向相反。
questions.hint: 回到原文定位题干关键词，比较选项与原文的含义。

items.title: 2023年12月六级第3套 · 仔细阅读 · 第二篇
items.passage:
Spiders make their presence felt in late August and through early autumn. This is the mating season of some of the most common varieties, when male house spiders come out of hidden corners to look for females, and garden spiders reach adult size and spin their most dazzling webs.

Yet while the spider is a familiar fixture of nursery poems or songs and Halloween decorations, its relationship with humans is complicated. Fear of spiders is common and has serious impacts on the lives of sufferers. Its prevalence appears unrelated to any rational assessment of risk. Spiders in the UK are almost all harmless. Farmland species perform valuable ecosystem services, by preying on insects that are our competitors for crops. But they are a constant source of human anxieties—with a cultural association with witches and wickedness dating back to the middle ages.

Does this perhaps explain, in part, the lack of data about how spiders are faring in our age of ecological crisis? British butterflies are the most studied group of insects in the world, due to the long tradition of collecting and observing them. But spider conservationists point out that it was only in the 1980s that the classification of house spiders was properly sorted out. And while information about insect populations is gathered by experiments that measure the numbers hitting windscreens or traps, there have been few attempts to count spiders.

The huge reductions in the numbers of flying insects can only mean a reduction in spiders' food supply. A recent landmark study identified a 75% fall in insect populations between 1989 and 2016, with pesticide use thought to be to blame along with the destruction of wild areas for development. This means the overall picture for spiders is worrying, as it is for most creatures. But conservationists are most concerned about those varieties that are threatened due to habitat loss and fragmentation, which makes it impossible for them to migrate.

Of around 650 spider species regularly recorded in the UK, the majority thrive in marshes and wasteland. Conservation efforts, often led by determined individuals, have helped some species to recover by reintroducing them to new areas. With rewilding now firmly on the environmental policy agenda, the hope is that in future, spiders will be enabled to migrate by themselves, adapting to climate change by moving along wildlife corridors.

It seems unlikely that spiders will ever attract the same level of human enthusiasm as bees, birds or butterflies, in spite of their unique status as nature's spinners. But as they reveal themselves in all their splendour this autumn, it would be a good thing if more animal lovers recognised the ways in which spiders are simply terrific.

questions.prompt: What do we learn about spiders in the UK since the middle ages?

options.text: They have adversely impacted crop growth.
They have been a constant reminder of bad luck.
They have made their presence felt when spinning webs.

questions.shortExplanation: But they are a constant source of human anxieties—with a cultural association with witches and wickedness dating back to the middle ages.
questions.detailedExplanation:
【答案】 A （细节题）

【判型】 What do we learn about spiders in the UK since the middle ages? 用 What do we learn about 引出，问的是关于某对象的客观事实，没有 infer/imply/suggest 等推断信号

【拆句】 题干主句是 What do we learn about spiders in the UK since the middle ages，主干是 What do we learn about X，X 是 spiders in the UK，后面 since the middle ages 是表时间起点的介词短语，整体平铺直叙、无陷阱。

【定位】 But they are a constant source of human anxieties—with a cultural association with witches and wickedness dating back to the middle ages.

但它们一直是人类焦虑的来源——与女巫和邪恶的文化关联可追溯至中世纪。

【选项】 A) ✓ 正确 a cultural association with witches and wickedness ↔ generally misconceived its prevalence appears unrelated to any rational assessment of risk ↔ misconceived 预判落在蜘蛛被文化误解上，A They have been generally misconceived 用 misconceived 概括了原文女巫、邪恶等不实联想，与预判完全对应，是定位句的高度抽象同义替换。

B) 与原文相反 B 选项 They have adversely impacted crop growth 称蜘蛛对农作物生长有不利影响，但原文 Farmland species perform valuable ecosystem services, by preying on insects that are our competitors for crops 明确说农田蜘蛛吃掉与人类争粮的昆虫， 是有利的；B 把有利说成有害，与原文相反。 C) 偷换概念 C 选项 They have been a constant reminder of bad luck 说蜘蛛是坏运气的提醒，但原文说的是与女巫、邪恶（witches and wickedness）的文化关联， witches/wickedness 是邪恶/巫术，不等于坏运气（bad luck）；二者是不同的文化概念，C 偷换了概念。 D) 答非所问 D 选项 They have made their presence felt when spinning webs 取自首段 Spiders make their presence felt in late August and through early autumn，讲的是晚夏初秋的自然现象，与题干 since the middle ages 的时间范围毫无关系；属答非所问。
questions.hint: 回到原文定位题干关键词，比较选项与原文的含义。

questions.prompt: What have spiders been associated with in the UK for centuries?
questions.shortExplanation: But they are a constant source of human anxieties—with a cultural association with witches and wickedness dating back to the middle ages. 但它们一直是人类焦虑的来源——与女巫和邪恶的文化关联可追溯至中世纪。
questions.detailedExplanation:
【答案】 B （细节题）

【判型】 What have spiders been associated with in the UK for centuries? 用 What 引出过去完成时的事实问句，问的是被关联的对象，没有任何推断信号

【拆句】 题干主干是 What have spiders been associated with，spiders 为主语，谓语为现在完成时被动 have been associated with，介词 with 后的宾语正是要回答的内容；in the UK 是地点状语，for centuries 是时间状语，结构清晰。

【定位】 But they are a constant source of human anxieties—with a cultural association with witches and wickedness dating back to the middle ages. 但它们一直是人类焦虑的来源——与女巫和邪恶的文化关联可追溯至中世纪。

【选项】 A) 偷换概念 A Harm 意为有形的伤害，对应原文应是 spiders 对人造成的实质损害；但原文 Spiders in the UK are almost all harmless 明确说英国蜘蛛几乎都无害——蜘蛛被关联的是文化上的邪恶，而不是实际伤害；A 偷换概念。

B) ✓ 正确 wickedness ↔ Evil witches ↔ Evil 由预判与巫术与邪恶相关联，选项 B Evil 把 witches 与 wickedness 两个并列宾语用一个上位词 Evil 同时归纳，是定位句的精准同义替换。 C) 张冠李戴 C Suffering 指痛苦/折磨，原文 Fear of spiders is common and has serious impacts on the lives of sufferers 出现 sufferers 一词——但 sufferers 描述的是怕蜘蛛的人所承受的影响，而题干问蜘蛛被关联的对象，主体错位；C 张冠李戴。

D) 无中生有 D Aggression 指攻击性，原文从未把蜘蛛与攻击性联系起来——焦虑、恐惧、邪恶都不等于攻击；这是文中没有的概念，属无中生有。
questions.hint: 回到原文定位题干关键词，比较选项与原文的含义。

questions.prompt: What partly accounts for the reduction in spiders' food supply?

options.text: The long tradition of collecting insects.
The extinction of a lot of wildlife

questions.shortExplanation: A recent landmark study identified a 75% fall in insect populations between 1989 and 2016, with pesticide use thought to be to blame along with the destruction of wild areas for development.
questions.detailedExplanation:
【答案】 C （细节题）

【判型】 What partly accounts for the reduction in spiders' food supply? 用 What accounts for 直接问原因，是典型的因果型细节题，不是推断

【拆句】 题干主干是 What partly accounts for X，partly 修饰 accounts for，X 为名词短语 the reduction in spiders' food supply，其中 spiders' 是所有格修饰 food supply；句子结构简单，重点是 partly 这一限定词。

【定位】 A recent landmark study identified a 75% fall in insect populations between 1989 and 2016, with pesticide use thought to be to blame along with the destruction of wild areas for development.

近期一项标志性研究发现，1989 到 2016 年间昆虫种群下降了 75%，元凶是杀虫剂使用以及为开发而破坏野生区域。

【选项】 A) 答非所问 A The long tradition of collecting insects 取自 British butterflies are the most studied group of insects in the world, due to the long tradition of collecting and observing them，那里讲的是蝴蝶被研究多的原因，与蜘蛛食物减少没有任何因果关系；A 答非所问。

B) 无中生有 B Fast reproduction of their competitors 称蜘蛛竞争者快速繁殖导致食物减少；但原文 preying on insects that are our competitors for crops 说的是昆虫是人类的庄稼竞争者，主体是人类的庄稼竞争者，并非蜘蛛的竞争者；且原文从未提及 fast reproduction；属无中生有。

C) ✓ 正确 pesticide use ↔ Chemicals used for killing insects thought to be to blame ↔ Chemicals used for killing insects 由预判杀虫剂，C Chemicals used for killing insects 是 pesticide 的标准释义，是定位句最直接的同义替换，无任何外加信息。 D) 过度推断 D The extinction of a lot of wildlife 称大量野生动物灭绝；原文说的是 the destruction of wild areas for development——破坏野生区（栖息地），不是野生动物灭绝；二者范围与程度都不同，D 过度推断。
questions.hint: 回到原文定位题干关键词，比较选项与原文的含义。

questions.prompt: What does the passage say is conservationists' biggest worry?

options.text: A variety of spiders are threatened due to pollution of marshes and wasteland.
Certain species of spiders are endangered due to loss of their natural homes.
An increasing number of spiders are being killed by deadly pesticides.
More and more spider species are found losing their ability to migrate.

questions.shortExplanation: But conservationists are most concerned about those varieties that are threatened due to habitat loss and fragmentation, which makes it impossible for them to migrate. 但保护者最担忧的是那些因栖息地丧失与碎片化而受威胁的物种，这种碎片化使得它们无法迁徙。
questions.detailedExplanation:
【答案】 B （细节题）

【判型】 What does the passage say is conservationists' biggest worry? 用 What does the passage say 直接问文中陈述的事实/观点，是细节题

【拆句】 题干是嵌套疑问句：主干 What does the passage say is X，间接引语 the passage say (that) X is conservationists’ biggest worry 被改写成 What...is...的疑问形式；要回答的是 What 所代的 X，即保护者最担心的事，结构稍复杂但无陷阱。

【定位】 But conservationists are most concerned about those varieties that are threatened due to habitat loss and fragmentation, which makes it impossible for them to migrate. 但保护者最担忧的是那些因栖息地丧失与碎片化而受威胁的物种，这种碎片化使得它们无法迁徙。

【选项】 A) 无中生有 A A variety of spiders are threatened due to pollution of marshes and wasteland 称蜘蛛因沼泽与荒地受污染而受威胁；但原文 the majority thrive in marshes and wasteland 说蜘蛛多在沼泽与荒地繁衍，从未提到污染；A 用了原文出现的 marshes and wasteland 字眼，但污染（pollution）是无中生有。

B) ✓ 正确 those varieties ↔ Certain species of spiders are threatened ↔ are endangered habitat loss and fragmentation ↔ loss of their natural homes 由预判栖息地丧失威胁某些物种，B Certain species of spiders are endangered due to loss of their natural homes 与原文 those varieties、are threatened、habitat loss 三处词一一对应，是定位句的高度同义替换。 C) 答非所问 C An increasing number of spiders are being killed by deadly pesticides 称越来越多蜘蛛被杀虫剂直接杀死；但原文 pesticide use thought to be to blame 说杀虫剂杀的是昆虫（飞虫）、进而影响蜘蛛食物，并非杀虫剂直接杀蜘蛛；C 答非所问，且与题干 biggest worry 不符。

D) 过度推断 D More and more spider species are found losing their ability to migrate 称越来越多物种正失去迁徙能力；原文 habitat loss and fragmentation, which makes it impossible for them to migrate 说的是栖息地丧失与碎片化导致无法迁徙——无法迁徙是栖息地丧失的结果，而题干问的是最担忧的原因/对象；D 把结果当作主担忧，且加入了原文没有的 more and more（递增趋势），属过度推断。
questions.hint: 回到原文定位题干关键词，比较选项与原文的含义。

questions.prompt: What wish does the author express close to the end of the passage?

options.text: More people would recognise spiders' unique status in the ecosystem.
People would show greater enthusiasm for spiders than for butterflies.
There would be sufficient corridors for spiders to move along.
There would be more people appreciating spiders' splendour.

questions.shortExplanation: But as they reveal themselves in all their splendour this autumn, it would be a good thing if more animal lovers recognised the ways in which spiders are simply terrific.
questions.detailedExplanation:
【答案】 D （细节题）

【判型】 What wish does the author express close to the end of the passage? 直接问作者在末尾表达的具体愿望，是局部细节题，不是整篇主旨/态度题

【拆句】 题干主干 What wish does the author express，倒装疑问句，主语 the author、谓语 express、宾语 what wish；close to the end of the passage 是位置状语，限定答题范围在末段附近；句子无生词、无难句。

【定位】 But as they reveal themselves in all their splendour this autumn, it would be a good thing if more animal lovers recognised the ways in which spiders are simply terrific.

但当它们在这个秋天展现出全部精彩时，如果有更多动物爱好者能认识到蜘蛛之妙，那真是一件好事。

【选项】 A) 偷换概念 A More people would recognise spiders' unique status in the ecosystem 称作者希望更多人认识到蜘蛛在生态系统中的独特地位；但原文 in spite of their unique status as nature's spinners 说蜘蛛的独特地位是纺织者，而非生态系统中的地位； 且 unique status 出现在 in spite of 让步状语里，不是作者愿望句的内容；A 偷换了概念。

B) 与原文相反 B People would show greater enthusiasm for spiders than for butterflies 称作者希望人们对蜘蛛比对蝴蝶更热情；但原文 It seems unlikely that spiders will ever attract the same level of human enthusiasm as bees, birds or butterflies 是作者承认蜘蛛不太可能像蜜蜂/鸟/蝴蝶那样受欢迎，这是事实判断而非作者愿望——B 把作者认为不可能的对照句反向当成愿望，与原文相反。

C) 答非所问 C There would be sufficient corridors for spiders to move along 称作者希望有足够的廊道供蜘蛛通行；但 wildlife corridors 出现在 spiders will be enabled to migrate by themselves, adapting to climate change by moving along wildlife corridors， 属于上一段保护政策的内容；题干已限定 close to the end of the passage，C 位置不对、答非所问。

D) ✓ 正确 more animal lovers ↔ more people recognised the ways in which spiders are simply terrific↔appreciating spiders' splendour 由预判更多人能欣赏到蜘蛛的精彩，D There would be more people appreciating spiders' splendour 用 more people 概括 animal lovers，用 appreciating spiders’ splendour 概括 recognised the ways in which spiders are simply terrific——一一对应，是定位句的精准同义替换。
questions.hint: 回到原文定位题干关键词，比较选项与原文的含义。

items.title: 2023年3月六级第1套 · 选词填空
items.passage:
Unthinkable as it may be, humanity, every last person, could someday be wiped from the face of the Earth. We have learned to worry about asteroids( ⼩⾏星 ) and super volcanoes, but the more likely [26] _____ , according to Nick Bostrom, a professor of philosophy at Oxford, is that we humans will destroy ourselves.

Professor Bostrom, who directs Oxford's Future of Humanity Institute, has argued over the course of several papers that human [27] _____ risks are poorly understood and, worse still, [28] _____ underestimated by society. Some of these existential risks are fairly well known, especially the natural ones. But others are [29] _____ or even exotic. Most worrying to Bostrom is the subset of existential risks that [30] _____ from human technology, a subset that he expects to grow in number and potency over the next century.

Despite his concerns about the risks [31] _____ to humans by technological progress, Bostrom is no luddite( 科技进步反对者 ). In fact, he is a longtime [32] _____ of trans-humanism—the effort to improve the human condition, and even human nature itself, through technological means. In the long run he sees technology as a bridge, a bridge we humans must cross with great care, in order to reach new and better modes of being. In his work, Bostrom uses the tools of philosophy and mathematics, in [33] _____ ,

probability theory, to try and determine how we as a [34] _____ might achieve this safe passage. What follows is my conversation with Bostrom about some of the most interesting and worrying existential risks that humanity might [35] _____ in the decades and centuries to come, and about what we can do to make sure we outlast them.

questions.prompt: the more likely __(26)__, according to Nick Bostrom, … is that we humans will destroy ourselves
questions.shortExplanation: scenario = 可能发生的情景，对应"我们自我毁灭"这种假设性结局
questions.detailedExplanation:
【答案】 K) scenario 名词

【词性槽】 the more likely ___：形容词比较级后接单数名词作主语中心词

【依据】 scenario = 可能发生的情景，对应"我们自我毁灭"这种假设性结局

the more likely __(26)__, … is that we humans will destroy ourselves：与小行星、超级火山"可能发生的情景"作比较，"可能性更大的情景"就是人类自毁，是 scenario 的典型用法 （the more likely scenario is that…）。

【竞争词】 F) evaporation evaporation 与上下文"灾难情景"无关

evaporation 指物理"蒸发"，无法与 asteroids、super volcanoes 这些"可能事件"作平行比较。

O) variety the more likely variety 不构成自然搭配

variety 表"种类、多样性"，是分类词，不指向某个"具体可能事件"，与 is that 引导的同位语从句"具体事件"不匹配。
questions.hint: 根据空格前后的词性、搭配与上下文选择词语；每个词最多使用一次。

questions.prompt: human __(27)__ risks are poorly understood
questions.shortExplanation: human extinction risks = 人类灭绝风险，呼应全文 wiped from the face of the Earth 的主旨
questions.detailedExplanation:
【答案】 G) extinction 名词

【词性槽】 human ___ risks：两名词之间夹一空，作 noun adjunct 修饰 risks

【依据】 human extinction risks = 人类灭绝风险，呼应全文 wiped from the face of the Earth 的主旨

首段 humanity, every last person, could someday be wiped from the face of the Earth 已把全文核心议题定为"人类灭绝"；human extinction risks 是该议题在学术语篇里的标准表达，与 human __(27)__ risks are poorly understood 中"被理解得很差"的对象完全吻合；extinction 作 noun adjunct 前置修饰 risks，语法上完全合法（参照 climate change risks 同类构造）。

【竞争词】 E) essentialessential risks 语义模糊、不切主题

essential 意为"必不可少的"，essential risks 不构成有意义的表达，更无法对应下文反复出现的 existential risks（生存性风险）这一主题词。

F) evaporation human evaporation 与主题不符

evaporation 表"蒸发"，与 human 组合无主流学术意义，也不与下文"existential risks"形成对应。

H) obscure obscure 留给 29 题、且不修饰本句主语

下文 But others are __(29)__ or even exotic 才会用到"鲜为人知"这层意思；本句要刻画的是"人类面临的何种类别的风险被低估"，应是题材性限定（灭绝），而非性质性修饰（模糊）。

O) variety human variety risks 不成立

variety 几乎只能用在 a variety of 结构中，无法作 noun adjunct 给 risks 加题材限定。

【易错】 最具迷惑性的错误词是 E) —— essential risks 听着像"关键风险"很诱人。human __(27)__ risks are poorly understood 处若只看本句、不回主旨，很容易误选 essential"本质风险"；防坑：始终回到首段 humanity, every last person, could someday be wiped from the face of the Earth 这句话定题材，与 extinction 一一对应。
questions.hint: 根据空格前后的词性、搭配与上下文选择词语；每个词最多使用一次。

questions.prompt: human __(27)__ risks are poorly understood and, worse still, __(28)__ underestimated by society
questions.shortExplanation: severely underestimated = 被严重低估，与 poorly understood 程度副词平行
questions.detailedExplanation:
【答案】 L) severely 副词

【词性槽】 worse still, ___ underestimated：修饰过去分词 underestimated

【依据】 severely underestimated = 被严重低估，与 poorly understood 程度副词平行

poorly understood and, worse still, __(28)__ underestimated by society：前后并列结构，副词位都修饰被动分词，描述"理解不充分"与"低估"的负面程度；severely 与 poorly 同色调、加重语气，呼应 worse still。

【竞争词】 M) shrewdly shrewdly 是褒义"精明地"，与 underestimated 的负面语境冲突

shrewdly underestimated 等于说"精明地低估了"，自相矛盾，且与 worse still 表示的"更糟"色调相反。

【易错】 最具迷惑性的错误词是 M) —— shrewdly 与 severely 都是副词，词性对、易混。worse still, __(28)__ underestimated by society 处考生若只卡词性、不看色调，可能误选 shrewdly；防坑：紧盯 worse still 这一句间连接词，色调一负到底。
questions.hint: 根据空格前后的词性、搭配与上下文选择词语；每个词最多使用一次。

questions.prompt: But others are __(29)__ or even exotic
questions.shortExplanation: obscure 与 exotic 同色调：鲜为人知 → 甚至怪异
questions.detailedExplanation:
【答案】 H) obscure 形容词

【词性槽】 others are ___ or even exotic：系动词 are 后接形容词作表语

【依据】 obscure 与 exotic 同色调：鲜为人知 → 甚至怪异

But others are __(29)__ or even exotic 与上句 Some of these existential risks are fairly well known 形成"有些众所周知，但另一些则……"的转折；空处需与 "well known" 反义， 与 exotic 同向，先"鲜为人知"再"怪异"层层递进，正是 obscure。

【竞争词】 E) essential essential 与 exotic 不同色、且与 well known 不构成反义

essential 意为"本质的、必要的"，既无法与 exotic 形成程度递进，也无法与上句 well known 构成转折，逻辑链断裂。
questions.hint: 根据空格前后的词性、搭配与上下文选择词语；每个词最多使用一次。

questions.prompt: the subset of existential risks that __(30)__ from human technology
questions.shortExplanation: arise from = 源自、由……产生，对应"来自人类技术的风险"
questions.detailedExplanation:
【答案】 B) arise 动词

【词性槽】 risks that ___ from：that 引导的定语从句中作谓语，后接 from

【依据】 arise from = 源自、由……产生，对应"来自人类技术的风险"

the subset of existential risks that __(30)__ from human technology 表达"源自人类技术的那一类生存风险"，arise from 是英语描述"源自/由……引起"的固定搭配，与主语 risks 复数原形相配。
questions.hint: 根据空格前后的词性、搭配与上下文选择词语；每个词最多使用一次。

questions.prompt: Despite his concerns about the risks __(31)__ to humans by technological progress
questions.shortExplanation: pose a risk to sb by sth = 由某物对某人造成风险
questions.detailedExplanation:
【答案】 J) posed 动词

【词性槽】 risks ___ to humans by …：名词后接非谓语作后置定语

【依据】 pose a risk to sb by sth = 由某物对某人造成风险

the risks __(31)__ to humans by technological progress：pose 与 risk/threat/challenge 是英语里"造成……威胁/风险"的强搭配，且 to humans 与 by technological progress 分别充当 pose 的间接宾语方向与施事，被动式 posed 一招到位。

【竞争词】 C) emphasized emphasize 与 risk 不构成"造成风险"的语义

emphasize 意为"强调"，emphasized to humans by 表达不出"由技术进步带给人类的风险"的因果关系；且 risks emphasized to humans 在逻辑上与"Bostrom 担忧技术造成的风险"主线偏离。
questions.hint: 根据空格前后的词性、搭配与上下文选择词语；每个词最多使用一次。

questions.prompt: he is a longtime __(32)__ of trans-humanism
questions.shortExplanation: an advocate of X = X 的倡导者，与上下文呼应 he is a longtime __(32)__ of trans-humanism—the effort to improve the human condition…through technological means，前句 Bostrom is no luddite 说他不是科技进步反对者，正面身份就是"长期倡导者"，an advocate of trans-humanism 是固定搭配。
questions.detailedExplanation:
【答案】 A) advocate 名词

【词性槽】 a longtime ___ of：a 后接单数可数名词，of 引出对象

【依据】 an advocate of X = X 的倡导者，与上下文呼应 he is a longtime __(32)__ of trans-humanism—the effort to improve the human condition…through technological means，前句 Bostrom is no luddite 说他不是科技进步反对者，正面身份就是"长期倡导者"，an advocate of trans-humanism 是固定搭配。

【竞争词】 D) encounter encounter 作名词义为"遭遇"，不指人

a longtime encounter of trans-humanism = "超人类主义的一段长期遭遇"，既不指人也无法被 of 紧跟一个学说作宾语，与前句"他不是反对者"的逻辑承接不上。

F) evaporation evaporation 是物理过程词、不指人

evaporation of trans-humanism 无意义，且无法承接"he is"的身份判定。

O) variety a longtime variety of … 不指人，逻辑也不通

variety of 通常表"……的多种类型"，无法与 he is 构成身份关系。
questions.hint: 根据空格前后的词性、搭配与上下文选择词语；每个词最多使用一次。

questions.prompt: Bostrom uses the tools of philosophy and mathematics, in __(33)__, probability theory
questions.shortExplanation: in particular = 尤其，引出后面的具体例子 probability theory
questions.detailedExplanation:
【答案】 I) particular 形容词

【词性槽】 in ___ 介词后接名词或形容词，与 in particular 构成固定短语

【依据】 in particular = 尤其，引出后面的具体例子 probability theory

in __(33)__, probability theory 后半段对前半句 the tools of philosophy and mathematics 中的 mathematics 作"尤其是"的细化举例，正是 in particular 的典型用法。

【竞争词】 E) essential in essential 不是英语固定搭配

essential 意为"本质的"，常说 in essence（本质上）而非 in essential；放进 in __(33)__, probability theory 既无搭配支撑、语义上也不能引出举例。

H) obscure in obscure 不成搭配且语义反向

obscure 是"模糊/鲜为人知的"，在此既无固定短语，也与 Bostrom"明确使用概率论"的语境冲突。
questions.hint: 根据空格前后的词性、搭配与上下文选择词语；每个词最多使用一次。

questions.prompt: how we as a __(34)__ might achieve this safe passage
questions.shortExplanation: we as a species = 我们作为一个物种，与全文"人类整体存亡"主旨严丝合缝
questions.detailedExplanation:
【答案】 N) species 名词

【词性槽】 we as a ___：as a 后接单数可数名词，we 的同位

【依据】 we as a species = 我们作为一个物种，与全文"人类整体存亡"主旨严丝合缝

items.title: 2023年3月六级第1套 · 信息匹配
items.passage:
A) The fog still chills the morning air and the cable cars still climb halfway to the stars. Yet on the ground, the Bay area has changed greatly since singer Tony Bennett left his heart here. Silicon Valley and the tech industry have led the region into a period of unprecedented wealth and innovation. But existing political and land limits have caused an alarming housing crisis and astronomical rise in social and economic difference.

B) While the residents of most cities display pride and support for their home industries, drastic market distortions in the San Francisco Bay Area have created boiling resentment in the region towards the tech industry. A vocal minority is even calling on officials to punish those who are benefitting from the economic and housing boom. If this boom and its consequences are not resolved, a drastic increase in social and economic difference may have a profound impact on the region for generations. A history and analysis of this transformation may hold invaluable insights about the opportunities. Perils of tech cities are currently being cultivated across the US, and indeed around the world.

C) According to a recent study, San Francisco ranks first in California for economic difference. The average income of the top 1% of households in the city averages $3.6 million. This is 44 times the average income of those at the bottom, which stands at $81,094. The top 1% of the San Francisco peninsula's share of total income now extends to 30.8% of the region's income. This was a dramatic jump from 1989, where it stood at 15.8%.

D) The region's economy has been fundamentally transformed by the technology industry springing from Silicon Valley. Policies pushed by Mayor Ed Lee provided tax breaks for tech companies to set up shop along the city's long-neglected Mid-Market area. The city is now home to Twitter, Uber, Airbnb, Pinterest, Dropbox and others. In short, the Bay Area has become a global magnet for those with specialized skills, which has in turn helped fuel economic enthusiasm, and this economic growth has reduced unemployment to 3.4%, an admirable feat.

E) In spite of all that, the strength of the recent job growth, combined with policies that have traditionally limited housing development in the city and throughout the peninsula, did not help ease the affordability crisis. In 2015 alone, the Bay Area added 64,000 in jobs. In the same year, only 5,000 new homes were built.

F) With the average house in the city costing over $1.25 million and average flat prices over $1.11 million, the minimum qualifying income to purchase a house has increased to $254,000. Considering that the average household income in the city currently stands at around $80,000, it is not an exaggeration to say that the dream of home ownership is now beyond the grasp of the vast majority of today's people who rent.

G) For generations, the stability and prosperity of the American middle class have been anchored by home ownership. Studies have consistently shown that the value of land has overtaken overall income growth, thus providing a huge advantage to property owners as a vehicle of wealth building. When home prices soar above the reach of most households, the gap between the rich and the poor dramatically increases.

H) If contributing factors leading to housing becoming less than affordable are not resolved over multiple generations, a small elite will control a vast share of the country's total wealth. The result? A society where the threat of class warfare would loom large. A society's level of happiness is tied less to measures of quantitative wealth and more to measures of qualitative wealth. This means that how a person judges their security in comparison to their neighbors' has more of an impact on their happiness than their objective standard of living. At the same time, when a system no longer provides opportunities for the majority to participate in wealth building, it not only robs those who are excluded from opportunities, but also deprives them of their dignity.

I) San Francisco and the Bay Area have long been committed to values which embrace inclusion and rejection of mainstream culture. To see these values coming apart so publicly adds insult to injury for a region once defined by its progressive social fabric. In the face of resentment, it is human to want revenge. But deteriorating policies such as heavily taxing technology companies or real estate developers are not likely to shift the balance.

J) The housing crisis is caused by two primary factors: the growing desirability of the Bay Area as a place to live due to its excellent economy, and our limited housing stock. Although the city is experiencing an unprecedented boom in new housing, more units are sorely needed. Protection policies were originally designed to suppress bad development and boost historic preservation in our urban areas. Now, too many developers are experiencing excessive delays. Meanwhile, there are the land limitations of the Bay Area to consider. The region is surrounded by water and mountains. Local governments need to aid development as well. This means increasing housing density throughout the region and building upwards while streamlining the approval process.

K) Real estate alone will not solve the problem, of course. Transportation, too, needs to be updated and infrastructure extended to link distant regions to Silicon Valley and the city. We need to build an effective high-speed commuting system linking the high-priced and crowded Bay Area with the low-priced and low-density Central Valley. This would dramatically reduce travel times. And based on the operating speeds of hovering trains used in countries such as Japan or Spain, high-speed rail could shorten the time to travel between San Francisco and California's capital, Sacramento, or from Stockton to San Jose, to under 30 minutes. This system would bring once distant regions within reasonable commute to heavy job centers. The city also needs to update existing transportation routes combined with smart home-building policies that dramatically increase housing density in areas surrounding high-speed rail stations. By doing so, we will be able to build affordable housing within acceptable commuting distances for a significant bulk of the workforce.

L) Our threatening housing crisis forces the difficult question of what type of society we would like to be. Will it be one where the elite command the vast bulk of wealth and regional culture is defined by an aggressive business world? We were recently treated to a taste of the latter, when local tech employee Justin Keller wrote an open letter to the city complaining about having to see homeless people on his way to work.

M) It doesn't have to be this way. But solutions need to be implemented now, before angry crowds grow from a nuisance to serious concern. It may take less than you might think. And in fact, the solutions to our housing crisis are already fairly clear. We need to increase the density of housing units. We need to use existing technology to shorten travel times and break the land limits. There is a way to solve complex social and economic problems without abandoning social responsibility. This is the Bay Area's opportunity to prove that it can innovate more than just technology.

items.title: 2023年3月六级第1套 · 仔细阅读 · 第一篇
items.passage:
The ability to make inferences from same and different, once thought to be unique to humans, is viewed as a cornerstone of abstract intelligent thought. A new study, however, has shown that what psychologists call same-different discrimination is present in creatures generally seen as unintelligent: newborn ducklings(⼩鸭 ).

The study, published Thursday in Science, challenges our idea of what it means to have a birdbrain, said Edward Wasserman, an experimental psychologist at the University of Iowa who wrote an independent review of the study.

"In fact, birds are extremely intelligent and our problem pretty much lies in figuring out how to get them to 'talk' to us, or tell us how smart they really are," he said.

Antone Martinho and Alex Kacelnik, co-authors of the new paper, devised a clever experiment to better test bird intelligence.

First, they took 1-day-old ducklings and exposed them to a pair of moving objects. The two objects were either the same or different in shape or color. Then they exposed each duckling to two entirely new pairs of moving objects.

The researchers found that about 70% of the ducklings preferred to move toward the pair of objects that had the same shape or color relationship as the first objects they saw. A duckling that was first shown two green spheres, in other words, was more likely to move toward a pair of blue spheres than a mismatched pair of orange and purple spheres.

Ducklings go through a rapid learning process called imprinting shortly after birth—it's what allows them to identify and follow their mothers.

These findings suggest that ducklings use abstract relationships between sensory inputs like color, shape, sounds and odor to recognize their mothers, said Dr. Kacelnik.

By studying imprinting, the authors of this study have shown for the first time that an animal can learn relationships between concepts without training, said Jeffrey Katz, an experimental psychologist at Auburn University who was not involved in the study.

Previous studies have suggested that other animals, including pigeons, dolphins, honeybees and some primates(灵⻓类动物 ), can discern same from different, but only after extensive training.

Adding ducklings to the list—particularly untrained newborn ducklings—suggests that the ability to compare abstract concepts "is far more necessary to a wider variety of animals' survival than we previously thought," Dr. Martinho said. He believes the ability is so crucial because it helps animals consider context when identifying objects in their environment.

It's clear from this study and others like it that "animals process and appreciate far more of the intricacies in their world than we've ever understood," Dr. Wasserman said. "We are in a revolutionary phase in terms of our ability to understand the minds of other animals."
