【定位】 The ability to make inferences from same and different, once thought to be unique to humans, is viewed as a cornerstone of abstract intelligent thought. 曾被认为是人类独有的、对 "同" 与 "异" 进行推断的能力，被视为抽象智力思维的基石。

【选项】 A) 无中生有选项 Being a major source of animal intelligence 说人类是 "动物智力的主要来源"， 原文从未提出这一观点；文章只对比人与动物的智力，没说人是动物智力的源头。

B) 偷换概念 cornerstone of abstract intelligent thought 修饰的是 "同/异推断能力"，是 "抽象智力的基石"，不是 "创造性世界的基石"；选项 Being the cornerstone of the creative world 把对象偷换成 the creative world。 C) ✓ 正确 make inferences from same and different ↔ same-different discrimination once thought to be unique to humans ↔ Being capable of same-different discrimination 预判 "人类独有的是 same-different 推断能力"，C 选项 Being capable of same-different discrimination 把这一信息完整还原，且来源于原文同一句话，是定位句的标准同义改写。 D) 无中生有原文只提及 abstract intelligent thought，从未提及 concrete 这一概念；选项 Being able to distinguish abstract from concrete 把抽象与具体编造成可区分的对象。
questions.hint: 回到原文定位题干关键词，比较选项与原文的含义。

questions.prompt: What do we learn from the study published in Science?

options.text: Our understanding of the bird world was biased.
Our conception of birds' intelligence was wrong.
Our communication with birds was far from adequate.
Our knowledge about bird psychology needs updating.

questions.shortExplanation: The study, published Thursday in Science, challenges our idea of what it means to have a birdbrain, said Edward Wasserman, an experimental psychologist at the University of Iowa who wrote an independent review of the study.
questions.detailedExplanation:
【答案】 B （细节题）

【判型】 What do we learn from the study published in Science? 限定了来源，问该研究告诉我们什么客观结论，对应原文该研究的总评句。

【拆句】 题干主干是 What do we learn from the study；过去分词短语 published in Science 后置修饰 the study，相当于定语从句 which was published in Science，用来锁定具体哪一项研究。

【定位】 The study, published Thursday in Science, challenges our idea of what it means to have a birdbrain, said Edward Wasserman, an experimental psychologist at the University of Iowa who wrote an independent review of the study.

Wasserman 表示，这项发表于周四《科学》杂志上的研究挑战了我们对 "birdbrain" 一词含义的认知。

【选项】 A) 以偏概全选项 Our understanding of the bird world was biased 把对象从 "鸟的智力" 扩大成 "鸟的世界"——原文只挑战对鸟智力的看法，没说我们对整个鸟类世界的理解有偏见。

B) ✓ 正确 challenges our idea of what it means to have a birdbrain ↔

Our conception of birds' intelligence was wrong birds are extremely intelligent and our problem pretty much lies in figuring out how to get them to 'talk' to us

↔ Our conception of birds' intelligence was wrong 预判 "鸟脑认知被推翻"，Our conception of birds' intelligence was wrong 与之严丝合缝；B 是定位句的标准同义改写。 C) 答非所问 our problem pretty much lies in figuring out how to get them to 'talk' to us 是 Wasserman 的延伸说明，不是该研究本身告诉我们的核心结论；选项 Our communication with birds was far from adequate 误把延伸内容当作主结论。

D) 偷换概念选项 Our knowledge about bird psychology needs updating 用 bird psychology 替换 birds' intelligence，鸟类心理学是更广的学科范畴，且 needs updating 改变了原文 "挑战"（即推翻）的强度。
questions.hint: 回到原文定位题干关键词，比较选项与原文的含义。

questions.prompt: What did the researchers discover about most ducklings from their experiment?

options.text: They could associate shape with color.
They reacted quickly to moving objects.
They preferred colored objects to colorless ones.
They could tell whether the objects were the same.

questions.shortExplanation: The researchers found that about 70% of the ducklings preferred to move toward the pair of objects that had the same shape or color relationship as the first objects they saw. 研究者发现，约 70% 的小鸭更倾向于走向与它们第一次看到的物体保持同种形状或颜色关系的那一对物体。
questions.detailedExplanation:
【答案】 D （细节题）

【判型】 What did the researchers discover about most ducklings from their experiment? 直接问研究者发现了什么，是对实验结果的客观提问。

【拆句】 主干是 What did the researchers discover；about most ducklings 是 discover 的内容限定，from their experiment 是来源状语。整句无陷阱，按 "实验 → 发现 → 关于多数小鸭的结论" 这一链条去原文找即可。

【定位】 The researchers found that about 70% of the ducklings preferred to move toward the pair of objects that had the same shape or color relationship as the first objects they saw. 研究者发现，约 70% 的小鸭更倾向于走向与它们第一次看到的物体保持同种形状或颜色关系的那一对物体。

【选项】 A) 偷换概念原文是 the same shape or color relationship——这里 or 表示 "形状或颜色" 二者之一的关系，不是把形状和颜色 "关联起来"；选项 They could associate shape with color 是错读 or 的产物。 B) 无中生有原文从未谈及小鸭 "反应速度"；选项 They reacted quickly to moving objects 是利用 moving objects 这一原词，凭空加上 quickly 这一速度属性。 C) 无中生有原文只提到不同颜色（green、blue、orange、purple）之间的对照，从未涉及 "colorless 无色" 物体；选项 They preferred colored objects to colorless ones 凭空造出有色与无色的对比。 D) ✓ 正确 the same shape or color relationship as the first objects they saw ↔

They could tell whether the objects were the same make inferences from same and different ↔

They could tell whether the objects were the same 预判 "小鸭能识别同异关系"，They could tell whether the objects were the same 与之精确对应；tell whether X were the same 正是 same-different discrimination 的口语化表述。
questions.hint: 回到原文定位题干关键词，比较选项与原文的含义。

questions.prompt: What was novel about the experiment in the study reported in Science?

options.text: The animals used received no training.
It used a number of colors and shapes.
It was conducted by experimental psychologists.
The ducklings were compared with other animals.

questions.shortExplanation: By studying imprinting, the authors of this study have shown for the first time that an animal can learn relationships between concepts without training, said Jeffrey Katz, an experimental psychologist at Auburn University who was not involved in the study.
questions.detailedExplanation:
【答案】 A （细节题）

【判型】 What was novel about the experiment...? 问该实验本身新颖在哪里，是对实验属性的客观提问，答案在原文有直接对应。

【拆句】 题干主干 What was novel about the experiment；过去分词短语 reported in Science 后置修饰 the study，相当于 which was reported in Science。novel 在此意为 "前所未有的、首次的"，与原文 for the first time 直接呼应。

【定位】 By studying imprinting, the authors of this study have shown for the first time that an animal can learn relationships between concepts without training, said Jeffrey Katz, an experimental psychologist at Auburn University who was not involved in the study.

Auburn 大学的实验心理学家 Jeffrey Katz（未参与本研究）表示，通过研究印随现象，本研究作者首次证明动物可以在 "无需训练" 的情况下学会概念之间的关系。

【选项】 A) ✓ 正确 an animal can learn relationships between concepts without training ↔

The animals used received no training untrained newborn ducklings ↔ The animals used received no training 预判 "未受训练即首次"，The animals used received no training 与之严丝合缝；A 是 without training 与 untrained 的标准动宾化改写。

B) 答非所问原文 two objects ... in shape or color 提到使用了不同颜色和形状，但这只是实验材料的描述，不是 "新颖之处"——只是惯常做法；选项 It used a number of colors and shapes 把背景信息冒充为新颖之处。 C) 答非所问 experimental psychologist 与 experimental psychologist 只是介绍研究人员身份， 从未将 "实验心理学家" 当作本研究的新颖之处；选项 It was conducted by experimental psychologists 把背景信息错认为答案。

D) 与原文相反原文 Previous studies have suggested that other animals ... can discern same from different 是用来反衬本研究新颖性的，而不是说本实验 "把小鸭与其他动物作了比较"；选项 The ducklings were compared with other animals 误把语段功能当成实验设计。

questions.prompt: What do we learn from Dr. Wasserman's comment on the study of animal minds at the end of the passage?

options.text: It is getting more and more intricate.
It is attracting more public attention.

questions.shortExplanation: We are in a revolutionary phase in terms of our ability to understand the minds of other animals. 在理解其他动物心智的能力方面，我们正处于一个 "革命性的阶段"。
questions.detailedExplanation:
【答案】 D （细节题）

【判型】 What do we learn from Dr. Wasserman's comment...? 限定具体人和具体位置，问其评论传达的客观信息，仍是细节题，不是推断题。

【拆句】 主干 What do we learn from Dr. Wasserman's comment；on the study of animal minds 是介词短语限定 comment 的内容范围；at the end of the passage 是位置状语限定 comment 的物理位置。注意 comment on 是固定搭配，意为 "对……的评论"。

【定位】 We are in a revolutionary phase in terms of our ability to understand the minds of other animals. 在理解其他动物心智的能力方面，我们正处于一个 "革命性的阶段"。

【选项】 A) 偷换概念原文 far more of the intricacies in their world 说的是 "动物世界的复杂性"，不是 "研究本身越来越复杂"；选项 It is getting more and more intricate 把 intricacies 这一原词扎根，但用错了对象。

B) 无中生有 Wasserman 谈的是认知层面的革命，不是方法层面的革新；原文未提 research methods are being updated。 C) 无中生有 Wasserman 谈的是学界对动物心智认知的进展，没有提及 "公众关注" 这一话题；选项 It is attracting more public attention 完全偏离。

D) ✓ 正确 revolutionary phase in terms of our ability to understand the minds of other animals↔

Remarkable progress is being made animals process and appreciate far more of the intricacies in their world than we've ever understood

↔ Remarkable progress is being made 预判 "动物心智研究取得突破"，Remarkable progress is being made 把 revolutionary phase 这一比喻翻译为 "显著进展"，是定位句的标准还原。

items.title: 2023年3月六级第1套 · 仔细阅读 · 第二篇
items.passage:
The suggestion that people should aim for dietary diversity by trying to eat a variety of foods has been a basic public health recommendation for decades in the United States and elsewhere. Now, however, experts are warning that aiming for a diverse diet may actually lead to just eating more calories, and, thus, to obesity. One issue is that people may not interpret "variety" the way nutritionists intend. This problem is highlighted by new research conducted by the American Heart Association. Researchers reviewed all the evidence published related to dietary diversity and saw a correlation between dietary diversity and a greater intake of both healthy and unhealthy foods. This had implications for obesity, as researchers found a greater prevalence of obesity amongst people with a greater dietary diversity.

One author of the new study explained that their findings contradict standard dietary advice, as most dietary guidelines around the world include a statement of eating a variety of foods. But this advice does not seem to be supported by science, possibly because there is little agreement about the meaning of "dietary diversity," which is not clearly and consistently defined. Some experts measure dietary diversity by counting the number of food groups eaten, while others look at the distribution of calories across individual foods, and still others measure how different the foods eaten are from each other.

Although the findings of this new study contradict standard dietary advice, they do not come as a surprise to all of the researchers involved. Dr. Rao, one of the study authors, noted that, after 20 years of experience in the field of obesity, he has observed that people who have a regimented lifestyle and diet tend to be thinner and healthier than people with a wide variety of consumption. This anecdotal evidence matches the conclusions of the study, which found no evidence that dietary diversity promotes healthy body weight or optimal eating patterns, and limited evidence that eating a variety of foods is actually associated with consuming more calories, poor eating patterns and weight gain. Further, there is some evidence that a greater variety of food options in a single meal may delay people's feeling of fullness and actually increase how much they eat.

Based on their findings, the researchers endorse a diet consisting of a limited number of healthy foods such as vegetables, fruits, grains, and poultry. They also recommend that people simultaneously endeavor to restrict consumption of sweets, sugar and red meat. The researchers stress, however, that their dietary recommendations do not imply dietary diversity is never positive, and that, in the past, diversity in diets of whole, unprocessed food may have actually been very beneficial.

questions.prompt: What has been a standard piece of dietary advice for decades?

options.text: People should cultivate a healthy eating habit.
People should have a well-balanced diet.
People should diversify what they eat.
People should limit calorie intake to avoid obesity.

questions.shortExplanation: The suggestion that people should aim for dietary diversity by trying to eat a variety of foods has been a basic public health recommendation for decades in the United States and elsewhere. 几十年来，在美国及其他地方，建议人们通过尝试多种食物来追求饮食多样化，一直是一条基本的公共健康建议。
questions.detailedExplanation:
【答案】 C （细节题）

【判型】 题干 What has been a standard piece of dietary advice for decades? 直接发问"几十年来标准建议是什么"，要的是文本陈述的客观事实。

【拆句】 What has been a standard piece of dietary advice for decades? 是 What 引导的特殊疑问句，谓语用现在完成时 has been，强调"从过去几十年延续至今的状态"，与 for decades 时间状语呼应；无陷阱。

【定位】 The suggestion that people should aim for dietary diversity by trying to eat a variety of foods has been a basic public health recommendation for decades in the United States and elsewhere. 几十年来，在美国及其他地方，建议人们通过尝试多种食物来追求饮食多样化，一直是一条基本的公共健康建议。

【选项】 A) 无中生有 cultivate a healthy eating habit 是合理的常识建议，但原文标准建议特指"多样化"而非泛泛的"健康习惯"——属于范围模糊的偷换。

B) 偷换概念 well-balanced diet 在中文里和"多样化"语感相近，但原文用的是 dietary diversity， 强调"种类多"而非"营养均衡"，两者不等值。 C) ✓ 正确 aim for dietary diversity by trying to eat a variety of foods ↔ diversify what they eat 预判要的是"使饮食多样化"，C 项 diversify what they eat 就是这层意思的标准同义改写，锁定 C。 D) 张冠李戴 limit calorie intake to avoid obesity 是文章后文 obesity 话题的延伸，但题干问的是"几十年来的标准建议"，原文标准建议是 diversity 而非"限制热量"。
questions.hint: 回到原文定位题干关键词，比较选项与原文的含义。

questions.prompt: What did the new research by the American Heart Association find?

options.text: People seeking dietary diversity tend to eat more.
Big eaters are more likely to become overweight.
Dietary diversity is positively related to good health.
Unhealthy food makes people gain weight more easily.

questions.shortExplanation: Researchers reviewed all the evidence published related to dietary diversity and saw a correlation between dietary diversity and a greater intake of both healthy and unhealthy foods. This had implications for obesity, as researchers found a greater prevalence of obesity amongst people with a greater dietary diversity. 研究者回顾了所有已发表的与饮食多样化相关的证据，发现饮食多样化与摄入更多健康和不健康食物之间存在相关性。这对肥胖问题有重要含义，因为研究者发现，饮食多样化程度更高的人群中肥胖患病率也更高。
questions.detailedExplanation:
【答案】 A （细节题）

【判型】 题干 What did the new research by the American Heart Association find? 问"研究发现了什么"，找的是研究结论的客观陈述。

【拆句】 What did the new research by the American Heart Association find? 是 What 引导的一般疑问倒装，主干是 the new research found what，by 短语作后置定语；结构平铺直叙，无陷阱。

【定位】 Researchers reviewed all the evidence published related to dietary diversity and saw a correlation between dietary diversity and a greater intake of both healthy and unhealthy foods. This had implications for obesity, as researchers found a greater prevalence of obesity amongst people with a greater dietary diversity. 研究者回顾了所有已发表的与饮食多样化相关的证据，发现饮食多样化与摄入更多健康和不健康食物之间存在相关性。这对肥胖问题有重要含义，因为研究者发现，饮食多样化程度更高的人群中肥胖患病率也更高。

【选项】 A) ✓ 正确 a correlation between dietary diversity and a greater intake of both healthy and unhealthy foods

↔ People seeking dietary diversity tend to eat more 预判是"多样化与吃得更多相关"，A 项 People seeking dietary diversity tend to eat more 即此意，且与原文 correlation 关系无矛盾，锁定 A。

B) 偷换概念 Big eaters are more likely to become overweight 的主语是"吃得多的人"，而原文论述对象是"追求多样化的人"；"吃得多→变胖"是常识，但不是本研究发现的关系。 C) 与原文相反原文说多样化与"更多肥胖患病率"相关，是负面相关；positively related to good health 却说与"健康"正相关——意思完全相反。

D) 无中生有 Unhealthy food makes people gain weight more easily 是常识，但原文研究发现的是"多样化与吃得更多/肥胖率高"相关，并非"不健康食物本身致胖"。

questions.prompt: What could help to explain the contradiction between the new findings and the common public health recommendation?

options.text: Most dietary guidelines around the world contradict one another.
Conventional wisdom about diet is seldom supported by science.
The methods researchers use to measure nutrition vary greatly.
There is little consensus on the definition of dietary diversity.

questions.shortExplanation: But this advice does not seem to be supported by science, possibly because there is little agreement about the meaning of "dietary diversity," which is not clearly and consistently defined. 但这一建议似乎并未得到科学的支持，可能是因为对于"饮食多样化"的含义，学界几乎没有共识——它本身就没有清晰一致的定义。
questions.detailedExplanation:
【答案】 D （细节题）

【判型】 题干 What could help to explain the contradiction 要求找原文给出的解释，答案是文本中明示的原因陈述。

【拆句】 What could help to explain the contradiction between the new findings and the common public health recommendation? 主干是 What could help to explain the contradiction，between A and B 双介短语作 contradiction 的后置定语；结构略长但平铺直叙，无陷阱。

【定位】 But this advice does not seem to be supported by science, possibly because there is little agreement about the meaning of "dietary diversity," which is not clearly and consistently defined. 但这一建议似乎并未得到科学的支持，可能是因为对于"饮食多样化"的含义，学界几乎没有共识——它本身就没有清晰一致的定义。

【选项】 A) 偷换概念 Most dietary guidelines around the world contradict one another 把"指南间彼此矛盾"安给原文，原文实际说的是"新研究与指南矛盾"，而不是"指南之间矛盾"。

B) 过度推断 Conventional wisdom about diet is seldom supported by science 把原文"这条建议似乎未被科学支持"扩大为"所有饮食常识都很少被科学支持"，从个例跳到普遍规律。

C) 偷换概念 The methods researchers use to measure nutrition vary greatly 把"测量饮食多样化的方法不同"偷换为"测量营养的方法不同"——nutrition ≠ dietary diversity，主体偏离。

D) ✓ 正确 there is little agreement about the meaning of "dietary diversity" ↔

There is little consensus on the definition of dietary diversity. 预判"定义没共识"，D 项 little consensus on the definition of dietary diversity 是其标准同义改写，锁定 D。
questions.hint: 回到原文定位题干关键词，比较选项与原文的含义。

questions.prompt: What did Dr. Rao find after 20 years of research on obesity?

options.text: Dietary diversity promotes healthy body weight.
Eating patterns and weight gain go hand in hand.
Diversified food intake may not contribute to health.
There is no clear definition of optimal eating patterns.

questions.shortExplanation: Dr. Rao, one of the study authors, noted that, after 20 years of experience in the field of obesity, he has observed that people who have a regimented lifestyle and diet tend to be thinner and healthier than people with a wide variety of consumption.
questions.detailedExplanation:
【答案】 C （细节题）

【判型】 题干 What did Dr. Rao find after 20 years of research on obesity? 锁定具体人物的具体发现，是典型的人物观点细节题。

【拆句】 What did Dr. Rao find after 20 years of research on obesity? What 引导一般疑问倒装，after 短语作时间状语；结构平铺直叙，无陷阱。

【定位】 Dr. Rao, one of the study authors, noted that, after 20 years of experience in the field of obesity, he has observed that people who have a regimented lifestyle and diet tend to be thinner and healthier than people with a wide variety of consumption.

研究作者之一 Rao 博士指出，凭借 20 年肥胖研究领域的经验，他观察到饮食和生活方式有规律的人，往往比饮食种类繁多的人更瘦、也更健康。

【选项】 A) 与原文相反 Dietary diversity promotes healthy body weight 说"多样化促进健康体重"，与原文 Rao 的观察（多样化的人不如规律饮食的人瘦）方向完全相反。

B) 答非所问 Eating patterns and weight gain go hand in hand 谈"饮食模式与体重增加同步"，与原文 Rao 的观察焦点（多样化 vs 规律化的比较）不对位，且 Rao 句中并未直接给出这一结论。 C) ✓ 正确 people who have a regimented lifestyle and diet tend to be thinner and healthier than people with a wide variety of consumption

↔ Diversified food intake may not contribute to health. 预判是"多样化未必有利于健康/体重"，C 项 Diversified food intake may not contribute to health 用否定形式表达同义，锁定 C。

D) 张冠李戴 no clear definition of optimal eating patterns 把 53 题里"dietary diversity 没有清晰定义"换成"optimal eating patterns 没有清晰定义"，并把这个内容安到 Rao 的发现头上——既偷换概念又移花接木。

questions.prompt: What does the passage say about people who eat a great variety of food?

options.text: They tend to consume more sweets, sugar and red meat.
They don't feel they have had enough until they overeat.
They don't have any problems getting sufficient nutrition.
They are more likely to eat foods beneficial to their health.

questions.shortExplanation: Further, there is some evidence that a greater variety of food options in a single meal may delay people's feeling of fullness and actually increase how much they eat. 此外，还有一些证据表明，一餐中食物种类越多，可能会推迟人们的饱腹感，反而让他们吃得更多。
questions.detailedExplanation:
【答案】 B （细节题）

【判型】 题干 What does the passage say about people who eat a great variety of food? 要求找原文对该群体的直接陈述。

【拆句】 What does the passage say about people who eat a great variety of food? What 引导特殊疑问句，about 介短语后接 people who... 限定性定语从句修饰 people；结构平铺直叙，无陷阱。

【定位】 Further, there is some evidence that a greater variety of food options in a single meal may delay people's feeling of fullness and actually increase how much they eat. 此外，还有一些证据表明，一餐中食物种类越多，可能会推迟人们的饱腹感，反而让他们吃得更多。

【选项】 A) 张冠李戴 tend to consume more sweets, sugar and red meat 出自末段研究者建议的"少吃这些"，并不是"饮食多样的人实际吃得更多"的内容——把第四段研究者的建议张冠到第三段对群体的描述上。

B) ✓ 正确 may delay people's feeling of fullness and actually increase how much they eat↔

They don't feel they have had enough until they overeat. 预判是"饱腹感推迟、吃过头"，B 项 don't feel they have had enough until they overeat 是这一因果链的同义改写，锁定 B。 C) 无中生有 don't have any problems getting sufficient nutrition 谈"获取营养无障碍"，原文从未涉及"营养是否充足"这个话题——属凭空捏造。

D) 与原文相反 more likely to eat foods beneficial to their health 说"更可能吃有益健康食物"，与原文 Rao 的观察（多样化者更胖更不健康）方向相反。
questions.hint: 回到原文定位题干关键词，比较选项与原文的含义。

items.title: 2023年6月六级第1套 · 选词填空
items.passage:
Scientists recently examined studies on dog intelligence and compared them with research into the minds of other intelligent animals. The researchers found that dogs are among the more intelligent carnivores( ⻝⾁动物 ), social hunters and domestic animals, but that their intelligence does not [26] _____ other intelligent animals in any of those categories. Though a significant body of research has examined dog cognition [27] _____ , the authors of this new study found little to warrant the [28] _____ of work that has been devoted to the topic.

Stephen Lea, lead author of the new study, argues that many researchers seem to have designed their studies to [29] _____ how clever dogs are, rather than simply to study dogs' brains. Lea and a colleague examined more than 300 studies of dog cognition, comparing the studies' results with those from research into other animals. The researchers made specific comparisons between the different species in different categories of intelligence. These comparisons [30] _____ that dogs are intelligent, but their intelligence is not as [31] _____ as some researchers might have believed.

In many areas, though, comparisons were not possible. For example, the researchers noted that both dogs and cats are known to be able to recognize and [32] _____ human voices. But the investigators could not find any data to indicate which species can remember a greater number of [33] _____ human voices, so it was impossible to compare the two on that front. However, not all researchers agree [34] _____ with the findings of this study. Zachary Silver, an American researcher, believes the authors of the new study [35] _____ the idea that an excessive amount of research has been devoted to dogs, as the field of dog cognition is young, and there is much to be learned about how dogs think.

questions.prompt: their intelligence does not __(26)__ other intelligent animals in any of those categories
questions.shortExplanation: “并不超过其他聪明动物”照应主旨
questions.detailedExplanation:
【答案】 N) surpass 动词

【词性槽】 does not 后接动词原形

【依据】 “并不超过其他聪明动物”照应主旨

前句说 dogs are among the more intelligent carnivores(食肉动物), social hunters and domestic animals，下半句用 but 转折，意思必然是“但并不在这些类别里 X 其他聪明动物”。surpass 表“超过、胜过”，正合“狗虽聪明但并未超越同类”的论断，与第二段 their intelligence is not as __(31)__ as some researchers might have believed 互相印证。

【竞争词】 D) differentiate“区分”后通常接 between/from

differentiate 表“区分”，差异辨别义，与 intelligence does not differentiate other animals 搭不上；且 D 另有去处（见 32 题“辨别人声”）。

J) pledge “保证”不接动物作宾

pledge 表“承诺、保证”，主语必须是人或机构，intelligence 作主语不能 pledge animals，语义彻底错位。

M) prove “证明其他动物”逻辑断裂

prove 后通常接 that 从句或形容词补足语；intelligence does not prove other animals 不构成完整意思，且 M 另有去处（见 29 题）。

【易错】 最具迷惑性的错误词是 H) —— outperformed 词义近、形态却错。outperformed 意为 “胜过”，词义几乎与 surpass 一致，最容易被误选进 their intelligence does not __(26)__ other intelligent animals。一句话防坑：does not 后必跟动词原形，outperformed 是过去分词/过去式，词形先被淘汰。
questions.hint: 根据空格前后的词性、搭配与上下文选择词语；每个词最多使用一次。

questions.prompt: a significant body of research has examined dog cognition __(27)__
questions.shortExplanation: 与完成时呼应的“此前已研究”
questions.detailedExplanation:
【答案】 K) previously 副词

【词性槽】 完成时谓语后修饰动词的状语位

【依据】 与完成时呼应的“此前已研究”

has examined 现在完成时强调“到目前为止已有研究”，previously 表“先前、以前”，正好对应“此前已有大量研究考察过狗的认知”，与下半句 found little to warrant the __(28)__ of work 形成“前人研究虽多、却未必必要”的转折逻辑。

【竞争词】 B) approximately 近似义不修饰研究行为

approximately 表“大约”，通常修饰数字或量，如 approximately 300，不会用来修饰 examined 这种研究动作。

C) completely “完全考察”语义荒谬且与下文矛盾

completely 表“彻底地”，说“研究已经彻底考察了狗的认知”与下句“认为投入的工作量并不值得” 自相矛盾；且 C 另有去处（见 34 题）。
questions.hint: 根据空格前后的词性、搭配与上下文选择词语；每个词最多使用一次。

questions.prompt: found little to warrant the __(28)__ of work that has been devoted to the topic
questions.shortExplanation: “工作量之多”才能被 warrant 衡量
questions.detailedExplanation:
【答案】 O) volume 名词

【词性槽】 the 与 of 短语之间的名词中心词

【依据】 “工作量之多”才能被 warrant 衡量

warrant 意为“证明…是必要/正当的”，宾语应是某种可被衡量的“量”。volume 表“数量、规模”，the volume of work 即“工作量”，承接前文 Though a significant body of research has examined dog cognition __(27)__ 中的 a significant body of research，呼应“研究量之大是否值得”的主线，是全文论点的关键词。

【竞争词】 F) domain “工作领域”与 warrant 搭不上

domain 表“领域”，the domain of work 听上去是“工作的领域”，但 warrant the domain of work（证明这一工作领域的合理性）逻辑别扭，且与下文“量”的比较主题不符。
questions.hint: 根据空格前后的词性、搭配与上下文选择词语；每个词最多使用一次。

questions.prompt: many researchers seem to have designed their studies to __(29)__ how clever dogs are
questions.shortExplanation: “证明狗有多聪明”而非客观研究
questions.detailedExplanation:
【答案】 M) prove 动词

【词性槽】 不定式 to 后接动词原形

【依据】 “证明狗有多聪明”而非客观研究

本句关键是对比 to __(29)__ how clever dogs are, rather than simply to study dogs' brains——前后是“证明 vs 研究”的对立。prove 后接 how 从句意为“证明狗有多聪明”，恰好讽刺这些研究的预设立场，与后文“狗其实没那么 formidable”的反转呼应。

【竞争词】 D) differentiate “区分”不带 how 从句

differentiate 后跟 between/from + 名词，不接 how clever dogs are 这类问句式从句。

J) pledge “承诺狗有多聪明”不合事理

pledge 是“承诺/誓言”，研究者不会“承诺狗多聪明”，逻辑荒谬。
questions.hint: 根据空格前后的词性、搭配与上下文选择词语；每个词最多使用一次。

questions.prompt: These comparisons __(30)__ that dogs are intelligent, but their intelligence is not as __(31)__ as some researchers might have believed
questions.shortExplanation: “比较结果证实了…”最贴合 affirmed 表“证实、肯定”，后接 that 从句意为“这些比较证实了…”，与上句 Lea and a colleague examined more than 300 studies of dog cognition 形成“做完比较→得出结论”的因果衔接，承接自然。
questions.detailedExplanation:
【答案】 A) affirmed 动词

【词性槽】 主语后缺谓语

【依据】 “比较结果证实了…”最贴合 affirmed 表“证实、肯定”，后接 that 从句意为“这些比较证实了…”，与上句 Lea and a colleague examined more than 300 studies of dog cognition 形成“做完比较→得出结论”的因果衔接，承接自然。

【竞争词】 H) outperformed “胜过”宾语应是对手而非从句

outperformed 表“胜过”，宾语应为竞争对象（人或物），不接 that 从句；comparisons outperformed that... 不成句。

I) overstated “夸大”后接概念名词，不接“狗聪明”这种事实从句

overstated 表“夸大”，宾语多为 risk、importance、case 等抽象名词，主语 these comparisons 也不会“夸大”自身得出的事实；且 I 另有去处（见 35 题）。
questions.hint: 根据空格前后的词性、搭配与上下文选择词语；每个词最多使用一次。

questions.prompt: their intelligence is not as __(31)__ as some researchers might have believed
questions.shortExplanation: “没有大家想的那么了不起”
questions.detailedExplanation:
【答案】 G) formidable 形容词

【词性槽】 系动词 as 后的形容词作表语

【依据】 “没有大家想的那么了不起”

整段在质疑“狗的智力被高估”：dogs are intelligent, but their intelligence is not as __(31)__ as some researchers might have believed。formidable 表“令人敬畏的、了不起的”，与 intelligent 同向但程度更强，正好对应“没研究者以为得那么强”的反差。

【竞争词】 L) prospective “潜在的智力”与同级比较语义错位

prospective 表“未来的、有望的”，多修饰人或角色（prospective student/buyer），不修饰 intelligence；且与 as...as 比较“以前有多相信”逻辑不通。

【易错】 最具迷惑性的错误词是 E) —— distinct 在 33 题用过、勿用过即划失败。distinct 也是形容词、且“独特的智力”乍听通顺，主体考生若没坚持“用过即划”，容易在 31 题二次选 E，导致 33 题反而崩盘。防坑：每填一空立刻在草稿上划掉该字母。
questions.hint: 根据空格前后的词性、搭配与上下文选择词语；每个词最多使用一次。

questions.prompt: both dogs and cats are known to be able to recognize and __(32)__ human voices
questions.shortExplanation: 与 recognize 并列形成“识别+辨别”
questions.detailedExplanation:
【答案】 D) differentiate 动词

【词性槽】 情态动词 + 并列动词原形

【依据】 与 recognize 并列形成“识别+辨别”

recognize 是“认出”，differentiate 是“辨别（区分不同的）”，二者构成“识别并区分人声”的常见认知能力描述，且呼应下句 remember a greater number of __(33)__ human voices 中 distinct 的“不同”主题——能 differentiate 才谈得上记住多少 distinct voices。

【竞争词】 J) pledge “狗保证人声”完全不通

pledge 表“承诺、立誓”，主语是猫狗、宾语是人声，无法构成任何合理含义。
questions.hint: 根据空格前后的词性、搭配与上下文选择词语；每个词最多使用一次。

questions.prompt: remember a greater number of __(33)__ human voices
questions.shortExplanation: “不同的人声”才好谈“记住多少种”
questions.detailedExplanation:
【答案】 E) distinct 形容词

【词性槽】 名词前作定语

【依据】 “不同的人声”才好谈“记住多少种”

本句讨论 which species can remember a greater number of __(33)__ human voices， 要比较谁能记住更多“不同的”人声。distinct 意为“截然不同的、可分辨的”，与 a greater number of 搭配自然，正好突出“记住的人声种类多寡”这一比较点。

【竞争词】 G) formidable “强大的人声”不通

formidable 多形容“令人生畏的对手/任务”，搭配 voices 在语义和搭配上都怪异；且 G 另有去处（见 31 题）。

L) prospective “潜在的人声”逻辑跑偏

prospective 表“未来的、潜在的”，多修饰 buyer、employer、student 这类“未来角色”，与“记住已经听过的人声数量”这个语境不搭。
questions.hint: 根据空格前后的词性、搭配与上下文选择词语；每个词最多使用一次。

questions.prompt: not all researchers agree __(34)__ with the findings of this study
questions.shortExplanation: “完全同意”与下文反对意见呼应
questions.detailedExplanation:
【答案】 C) completely 副词

【词性槽】 助动词 do 与实义动词 agree 之间的状语

【依据】 “完全同意”与下文反对意见呼应

原文紧接出现 Zachary Silver, an American researcher, believes the authors of the new study __(35)__ the idea，表明确有研究者持不同看法。因此“并非所有研究者都 completely（完全）赞同这一结论”最贴切——not...completely 是地道的部分否定表达。

【竞争词】 B) approximately “大约同意”不像人话

approximately 表数量上的近似，不与 agree 搭配；agree approximately with 不是英语习语。
questions.hint: 根据空格前后的词性、搭配与上下文选择词语；每个词最多使用一次。

questions.prompt: Zachary Silver, an American researcher, believes the authors of the new study __(35)__ the idea that an excessive amount of research has been devoted to dogs
questions.shortExplanation: “夸大了‘狗研究过多’的论断”才符合反对者立场 Zachary Silver 持反对意见，认为新研究 the authors of the new study __(35)__ the idea that an excessive amount of research has been devoted to dogs, as the field of dog cognition is young, and there is much to be learned——下半句给出原因（领域年轻、 还有很多要学），正是为了说明新研究“言过其实”。overstated 表“夸大”，与 overstated the idea/case 是固定搭配，精准命中。
questions.detailedExplanation:
【答案】 I) overstated 动词

【词性槽】 主语 + 谓语 + 宾语的过去式动词

【依据】 “夸大了‘狗研究过多’的论断”才符合反对者立场 Zachary Silver 持反对意见，认为新研究 the authors of the new study __(35)__ the idea that an excessive amount of research has been devoted to dogs, as the field of dog cognition is young, and there is much to be learned——下半句给出原因（领域年轻、 还有很多要学），正是为了说明新研究“言过其实”。overstated 表“夸大”，与 overstated the idea/case 是固定搭配，精准命中。

【竞争词】 H) outperformed “胜过观点”搭配荒谬

outperformed 表“在表现上胜过”，宾语应是竞争者；overperform the idea 不构成英语表达， 与反对立场也无关。
questions.hint: 根据空格前后的词性、搭配与上下文选择词语；每个词最多使用一次。

items.title: 2023年6月六级第1套 · 信息匹配
items.passage:
A) Gratitude may be more beneficial than we commonly suppose. One recent study asked participants to write a note of thanks to someone and then estimate how surprised and happy the recipient would feel—an impact that they consistently underestimated. Another study assessed the health benefits of writing thank-you notes. The researchers found that writing as few as three weekly thank-you notes over the course of three weeks improved life satisfaction, increased happy feelings and reduced symptoms of depression.

B) While this research into gratitude is relatively new, the principles involved are anything but. Students of mine in a political philosophy course at Indiana University are reading Daniel Defoe's 300-year-old Robinson Crusoe, often regarded as the first novel published in English. Left alone on an unknown island with no apparent prospect of rescue or escape, Crusoe has much to lament(悲叹). But instead of giving in to despair, he makes a list of things for which he is grateful, including the fact that he is the sole survivor from the shipwreck(海难) and has been able to salvage many useful items from the wreckage.

C) Defoe's masterpiece, which is often ranked as one of the world's greatest novels, provides a portrait of gratitude in action that is as timely and relevant today as it has ever been. It is also one with which contemporary psychology and medicine are just beginning to catch up. Simply put, for most of us, it is far more helpful to focus on the things in life for which we can express gratitude than those that incline us toward resentment and lamentation.

D) When we focus on the things we regret, such as failed relationships, family disputes, and setbacks in career and finance, we tend to become more regretful. Conversely, when we focus on the things we are grateful for, a greater sense of happiness tends to spread through our lives. And while no one would argue for cultivating a false sense of blessedness, there is mounting evidence that counting our blessings is one of the best habits we can develop to promote mental and physical health.

E) Gratitude has long enjoyed a privileged position in many of the world's cultural traditions. For example, some ancient Western philosophers counsel gratitude that is both enduring and complete, and some Eastern thinkers portray it as not merely an attitude but a virtue to be put into practice.

F) Recent scientific studies support these ancient teachings. Individuals who regularly engage in gratitude exercises, such as counting their blessings or expressing gratitude to others, exhibit increased satisfaction with relationships and fewer symptoms of physical illness. And the benefits are not only psychological and physical. They may also be moral—those who practice gratitude also view their lives less materialistically and suffer from less envy.

G) There are multiple explanations for such benefits of gratefulness. One is the fact that expressing gratitude encourages others to continue being generous, thus promoting a virtuous cycle of goodness in relationships. Similarly, grateful people may be more likely to reciprocate(回报) with acts of kindness of their own. Broadly speaking, a community in which people feel grateful to one another is likely to be a more pleasant place to live than one characterized by mutual suspicion and resentment. The beneficial effects of gratitude may extend even further. For example, when many people feel good about what someone else has done for them, they experience a sense of being lifted up, with a corresponding enhancement of their regard for humanity. Some are inspired to attempt to become better people themselves, doing more to help bring out the best in others and bringing more goodness into the world around them.

H) Gratitude also tends to strengthen a sense of connection with others. When people want to do good things that inspire gratitude, the level of dedication in relationships tends to grow and relationships seem to last longer. And when people feel more connected, they are more likely to choose to spend their time with one another and demonstrate their feelings of affection in daily acts.

I) Of course, acts of kindness can also foster discomfort. For example, if people feel they are not worthy of kindness or suspect that some ulterior(别有⽤⼼的 ) motive lies behind it, the benefits of gratitude will not be realized. Likewise, receiving a kindness can give rise to a sense of indebtedness, leaving beneficiaries feeling that they must now pay back whatever good they have received. Gratitude can flourish only if people are secure enough in themselves and sufficiently trusting to allow it to do so. Another obstacle to gratitude is often called a sense of entitlement. Instead of experiencing a benefaction( 善⾏ ) as a good turn, people sometimes regard it as a mere payment of what they are owed, for which no one deserves any moral credit.

J) There are a number of practical steps anyone can take to promote a sense of gratitude. One is simply spending time on a regular basis thinking about someone who has made a difference, or perhaps writing a thank-you note or expressing such gratitude in person. Others are found in ancient religious disciplines, such as reflecting on benefactions received from another person or actually praying for the health and happiness of a benefactor. In addition to benefactions received, it is also possible to focus on opportunities to do good oneself, whether those acted on in the past or hoped for in the future. Some people are most grateful not for what others have done for them but for chances they enjoyed to help others. In regularly reflecting on the things in his life he is grateful for, Defoe's Crusoe believes that he becomes a far better person than he would have been had he remained in the society from which he originally set out on his voyage.

K) Reflecting on generosity and gratitude, the great basketball coach John Wooden once offered two counsels to his players and students. First, he said, "It is impossible to have a perfect day unless you have done something for someone who will never be able to repay you." In saying this, Wooden sought to promote purely generous acts, as opposed to those performed with an expectation of reward. Second, he said, "Give thanks for your blessings every day."

L) Some faith traditions incorporate such practices into the rhythm of daily life. For example, adherents of some religions offer prayers of thanksgiving every morning before rising and every night before lying down to sleep. Others offer thanks throughout the day, such as before meals. Other less frequent special events, such as births, deaths and marriages, may also be heralded by such prayers.

M) When Defoe depicted Robinson Crusoe making thanksgiving a daily part of his island life, he was anticipating findings in social science and medicine that would not appear for hundreds of years. Yet he was also reflecting the wisdom of religious and philosophical traditions that extend back thousands of years. Gratitude is one of the healthiest and most nourishing of all states of mind, and those who adopt it as a habit are enriching not only their own lives but also the lives of those around them.

questions.prompt: It does us far more good to focus on things we can be grateful for than what makes us sad and resentful.
questions.shortExplanation: 对比聚焦点的核心命题
questions.detailedExplanation:
【答案】 C 段（强锚点）

【锚点】 对比聚焦点的核心命题

【定位】 Simply put, for most of us, it is far more helpful to focus on the things in life for which we can express gratitude than those that incline us toward resentment and lamentation.

简单地说，对我们大多数人而言，专注于生活中那些值得感恩之事，远比专注于让人心生怨恨、悲叹之事更有益处。

【改写】 does us far more good ↔ far more helpful 比较级同义替换

focus on things we can be grateful for ↔

focus on the things in life for which we can express gratitude 动词到名词的同义改写

what makes us sad and resentful ↔ those that incline us toward resentment and lamentation 形容词与抽象名词的同义对换

items.title: 2023年6月六级第1套 · 仔细阅读 · 第一篇
items.passage:
Technology is never a neutral tool for achieving human ends. Technological innovations reshape people as they use these innovations to control their environment. Artificial intelligence, for example, is altering humanity.

While the term AI conjures up anxieties about killer robots or catastrophic levels of unemployment, there are other, deeper implications. As AI increasingly shapes the human experience, how does this change what it means to be human? Central to the problem is a person's capacity to make choices, particularly judgments that have moral implications.

Aristotle argued that the capacity for making practical judgments depends on regularly making them—on habit and practice. We see the emergence of machines as substitute judges in a variety of everyday contexts as a potential threat to people learning how to effectively exercise judgment themselves.

In the workplace, managers routinely make decisions about who to hire or fire and which loan to approve, to name a few. These are areas where algorithmic(算法的 ) prescription is replacing human judgment, and so people who might have had the chance to develop practical judgment in these areas no longer will.

Recommendation engines, which are increasingly prevalent intermediaries in people's consumption of culture, may serve to constrain choice and minimize luck. By presenting consumers with algorithmically selected choices of what to watch, read, stream and visit next, companies are replacing human taste with machine taste. In one sense, this is helpful. After all, machines can survey a wider range of choices than any individual is likely to have the time or energy to do on their own.

At the same time, though, this selection is optimizing for what people are likely to prefer based on what they've preferred in the past. We think there is some risk that people's options will be constrained by their past in a new and unanticipated way.

As machine learning algorithms improve and as they train on more extensive data sets, larger parts of everyday life are likely to become utterly predictable. The predictions are going to get better and better, and they will ultimately make common experiences more efficient and pleasant.

Algorithms could soon—if they don't already—have a better idea about which show you'd like to watch next and which job candidate you should hire than you do. One day, humans may even find a way for machines to make these decisions without some of the biases that humans typically display.

But to the extent that unpredictability is part of how people understand themselves and part of what people like about themselves, humanity is in the process of losing something significant. As they become more and more predictable, the creatures inhabiting the increasingly AI-mediated world will become less and less like us.

questions.prompt: What do we learn about the deeper implications of AI?

options.text: It is causing catastrophic levels of unemployment.
It is doing physical harm to human operators.

questions.shortExplanation: While the term AI conjures up anxieties about killer robots or catastrophic levels of unemployment, there are other, deeper implications. As AI increasingly shapes the human experience, how does this change what it means to be human?
questions.detailedExplanation:
【答案】 D （细节题）

【判型】 题干What do we learn about the deeper implications of AI?是直接问对某概念了解到的内容，没有infer/imply等推断信号。

【拆句】 Q46是一个标准的what引导的特殊疑问句，主干是"What do we learn about X"，about 后接the deeper implications of AI整个名词短语，无陷阱。

【定位】 While the term AI conjures up anxieties about killer robots or catastrophic levels of unemployment, there are other, deeper implications. As AI increasingly shapes the human experience, how does this change what it means to be human?

虽然"AI"一词让人联想到杀人机器人或灾难性的失业，但还有其他更深层的影响。随着AI日益塑造人类经验，这将如何改变"作为人"的含义？

【选项】 A) 与原文相反原文恰恰把catastrophic levels of unemployment列为人们对AI的浅层焦虑，作者要说的"更深层影响"是与之对立的——A把作者明示否定的浅层焦虑拿来当深层影响，方向反了。

B) 无中生有全文从未提及AI对操作者造成身体伤害，physical harm属凭空虚构。 C) 以偏概全道德判断（moral implications）只是judgments that have moral implications里举的一个具体例子，是"改变人之为人"的下属支撑，不是"deeper implications"本身。

D) ✓ 正确 Technological innovations reshape people as they use these innovations ↔

It is reshaping humanity. how does this change what it means to be human ↔ It is reshaping humanity. 预判"改变人本身"，四个选项里只有It is reshaping humanity.在说人本身被改写，正面命中。

questions.prompt: What is the consequence of algorithmic prescription replacing human judgment?

options.text: People lose the chance to cultivate the ability to make practical judgments.
People are prevented from participating in making major decisions in the workplace.
Managers no longer have the chance to decide which loan to approve.
Managers do not need to take the trouble to determine who to hire or fire.

questions.shortExplanation: These are areas where algorithmic prescription is replacing human judgment, and so people who might have had the chance to develop practical judgment in these areas no longer will.
questions.detailedExplanation:
【答案】 A （细节题）

【判型】 What is the consequence of …是问某行为带来的具体后果，答案在原文有明确对应句而非需推断。

【拆句】 Q47结构清晰：主干what is the consequence of X，of后接动名词短语algorithmic prescription replacing human judgment，其中replacing为现在分词作定语修饰 prescription，相当于"算法处方替代了人的判断"。

【定位】 These are areas where algorithmic prescription is replacing human judgment, and so people who might have had the chance to develop practical judgment in these areas no longer will.

这些就是算法处方正在取代人类判断的领域，因此本来可能有机会在这些领域培养实践判断力的人，不再有此机会。

【选项】 A) ✓ 正确 people who might have had the chance to develop practical judgment in these areas no longer will

↔ People lose the chance to cultivate the ability to make practical judgments. 预判正是"失去培养判断力的机会"，People lose the chance to cultivate the ability to make practical judgments.逐字对应。

B) 偷换概念原文是"失去培养判断力的练习机会"，B把它偷换成"被阻止参与重大决策"——重大决策的参与权并未被剥夺，被剥夺的是"练手"机会。

C) 张冠李戴原文说被剥夺机会的是普通人（people），不是经理（managers）；经理本是行使判断的一方，正被算法替代。 D) 与原文相反原文是中性陈述"经理们日常会做这些决定"，并未说他们觉得麻烦或希望被替代；D把负面后果"失去机会"扭曲成正面"省事"。

【答案】 A （细节题）

【判型】 What may result from …直接问由某事导致的具体结果，是典型的细节题问法。

【拆句】 Q48主干what may result from X，may弱化了语气表"可能性"，X是动名词短语 increasing application of recommendation engines in our consumption of culture， 其中increasing修饰application，整体意为"推荐引擎在文化消费里日益增多的应用"。

【选项】 A) ✓ 正确 may serve to constrain choice and minimize luck ↔

Consumers will have much limited choice. 预判"限制选择"，Consumers will have much limited choice.恰是其形容词化版本， 正面对应。

B) 与原文相反原文是minimize luck（削减偶然/运气），B却说"享受更好的运气"——意思完全反向。

C) 以偏概全原文中"机器能扫描更广范围"只是让步性铺垫（"In one sense, this is helpful"），紧接 P6"At the same time, though"明确转折，作者的核心结论是限制选择，而不是"决定更容易"。 D) 偷换概念原文是"用机器口味替代人的口味"（machine taste replaces human taste），即人的口味被压制；D却说"人将培养出与机器相似的口味"，主客体反了。

questions.prompt: What is likely to happen to larger parts of our daily life as machine learning algorithms improve?

options.text: They will turn out to be more pleasant.
They will repeat our past experience.
They may become better and better.

questions.shortExplanation: As machine learning algorithms improve and as they train on more extensive data sets, larger parts of everyday life are likely to become utterly predictable.
questions.detailedExplanation:
【答案】 C （细节题）

【判型】 What is likely to happen to … as …是问条件下将发生的具体情况，找原文对应预测句即可。

【拆句】 Q49结构是"What is likely to happen to A as B"，as引导时间/条件状语从句，意为"随着 B，A身上可能发生什么"；考生易把as误读为"因为"，这里其实更接近"随着"。

【定位】 As machine learning algorithms improve and as they train on more extensive data sets, larger parts of everyday life are likely to become utterly predictable.

随着机器学习算法的改进、以及在更大数据集上的训练，日常生活越来越大的部分将变得完全可被预测。

【选项】 A) 答非所问 P7主句的核心结论是utterly predictable；more efficient and pleasant是其后的次级描述。题干问的是larger parts of daily life本身会如何，而非体验如何——A答非所问。

B) 偷换概念 constrained by their past说的是推荐引擎按过去偏好限制选择，与P7"算法越准、生活越可预测"是两段不同论点；B把前一段的素材搬来回答后一段的问题，错位。

C) ✓ 正确 larger parts of everyday life are likely to become utterly predictable ↔

They can be completely anticipated. 预判核心是"完全可预测"，They can be completely anticipated.中 completely+anticipated双重对应，是唯一保留"utterly"程度的选项。 D) 张冠李戴原文是"预测会越来越好"（The predictions are going to get better and better）， 即"算法预测"这个东西本身越来越好；D却把better and better的主语挂在larger parts of daily life上，主语错位。

questions.prompt: Why does the author say the creatures living in the more and more AI-mediated world will become increasingly unlike us?

options.text: They will have lost the most significant human element of being intelligent.
They will no longer possess the human characteristic of being unpredictable.
They will not be able to understand themselves as we can do today.
They will be deprived of what their predecessors were proud of about themselves.

questions.shortExplanation: But to the extent that unpredictability is part of how people understand themselves and part of what people like about themselves, humanity is in the process of losing something significant. As they become more and more predictable, the creatures inhabiting the increasingly AI-mediated world will become less and less like us. 但是，由于不可预测性本身就是人类自我认知与自我喜爱的一部分，人类正在失去某种重要的东西。随着他们变得越来越可预测，居住在愈发AI化的世界里的这些"生物"，将越来越不像我们。
questions.detailedExplanation:
【答案】 B （细节题）

【判型】 题干Why does the author say …问的是作者作出某判断的直接依据，原文末段有显性原因句，不需推断。

【拆句】 Q50是Why疑问句，宾语从句中the creatures …是主语，living in …是分词后置定语，will become是主句谓语；表面长，骨架是"creatures will become unlike us"。

【定位】 But to the extent that unpredictability is part of how people understand themselves and part of what people like about themselves, humanity is in the process of losing something significant. As they become more and more predictable, the creatures inhabiting the increasingly AI-mediated world will become less and less like us. 但是，由于不可预测性本身就是人类自我认知与自我喜爱的一部分，人类正在失去某种重要的东西。随着他们变得越来越可预测，居住在愈发AI化的世界里的这些"生物"，将越来越不像我们。

【选项】 A) 无中生有全文从未把intelligent列为人类最重要特征；作者强调的是unpredictability。A自行虚构了一种"智能"的核心人性。

B) ✓ 正确 unpredictability is part of how people understand themselves and part of what people like about themselves

↔ They will no longer possess the human characteristic of being unpredictable. As they become more and more predictable ↔

They will no longer possess the human characteristic of being unpredictable. 预判核心词是unpredictability，四个选项中只有They will no longer possess the human characteristic of being unpredictable.点出unpredictable，正面命中。 C) 过度推断原文说unpredictability是"how people understand themselves"的一部分，并没有说"未来人将无法理解自己"——C把作为成分的unpredictability当成了理解能力本身。 D) 以偏概全 D只说"被剥夺了前人曾为之自豪的东西"——但"前人曾为之自豪的东西"具体是什么，D 避而不答；正确答案B则点明那就是unpredictability。Why题要的是具体原因，不是含糊代称。

items.title: 2023年6月六级第1套 · 仔细阅读 · 第二篇
items.passage:
Phonics, which involves sounding out words syllable( ⾳节 ) by syllable, is the best way to teach children to read. But in many classrooms, this can be a dirty word. So much so that some teachers have had to sneak phonics teaching materials into the classroom. Most American children are taught to read in a way that study after study has found to be wrong.

The consequences of this are striking. Less than half of all American adults were proficient readers in 2017. American fourth graders rank 15th on the Progress in International Literacy Study, an international exam.

America is stuck in a debate about teaching children to read that has been going on for decades. Some advocate teaching symbol-sound relationships (the sound k can be spelled as c, k, ck, or ch), known as phonics. Others support an immersive approach (using pictures of a cat to learn the word cat), known as "whole language". Most teachers today, almost three out of four according to a survey by the Ed Week Research Centre in 2019, use a mix called "balanced literacy". This combination of methods is ineffective. "You can't sprinkle in a little phonics," says Tenette Smith, executive director of elementary education and reading at Mississippi's education department. "It has to be systematic and explicitly taught."

Mississippi, often behind in social policy, has set an example here. In a state once notorious for its low reading scores, the Mississippi state legislature passed new literacy standards in 2013. Since then Mississippi has seen remarkable gains. Its fourth graders have moved from 49th (out of 50 states) to 29th on the National Assessment of Educational Progress, a nationwide exam. In 2019 it was the only state to improve its scores. For the first time since measurement began, Mississippi's pupils are now average readers, a remarkable achievement in such a poor state.

Mississippi's success is attributed to implementing reading methods supported by a body of research known as the science of reading. In 1997 Congress requested the National Institute of Child Health and Human Development and the Department of Education to convene a National Reading Panel to end the "reading wars" and synthesize the evidence. The panel found that phonics, along with explicit instruction in phonemic(⾳位的 ) awareness, fluency and comprehension, worked best.

Yet over two decades on, "balanced literacy" is still being taught in classrooms. But advances in statistics and brain imaging have disproved the whole-language method. To the teacher who is a proficient reader, literacy seems like a natural process that requires educated guessing, rather than the deliberate process emphasized by phonics. Teachers can imagine that they learned to read through osmosis(潜移默化 ) when they were children. Without proper training, they bring this to classrooms.

questions.prompt: What do we learn about phonics in many American classrooms?
questions.shortExplanation: But in many classrooms, this can be a dirty word. So much so that some teachers have had to sneak phonics teaching materials into the classroom. 但在许多课堂里，它（拼读法）几乎成了一个令人嫌弃的词。以至于一些老师不得不偷偷把拼读法教材带进教室。
questions.detailedExplanation:
【答案】 A （细节题）

【判型】 What do we learn about phonics in many American classrooms? 用 What do we learn about 直接索取关于某物的客观信息，对应原文应有一句明确表态。

【拆句】 结构平铺直叙：What do we learn about phonics in many American classrooms? 是一个简单的特殊疑问句，about phonics 是 learn 的宾语补足部分，in many American classrooms 是地点状语，无陷阱。

【定位】 But in many classrooms, this can be a dirty word. So much so that some teachers have had to sneak phonics teaching materials into the classroom. 但在许多课堂里，它（拼读法）几乎成了一个令人嫌弃的词。以至于一些老师不得不偷偷把拼读法教材带进教室。

【选项】 A) ✓ 正确 this can be a dirty word ↔ It is ill reputed. some teachers have had to sneak phonics teaching materials into the classroom ↔ ill reputed 预判得到 phonics 在课堂里名声不好；四个选项里只有 It is ill reputed. 把 dirty word 的核心语义 "被嫌弃/名声差" 直接压缩出来，与预判同义。

B) 无中生有 It is mostly misapplied. 指 phonics 被错误地使用，但定位句只说它名声差、被偷偷带进教室，并未说它被 "误用"。 C) 过度推断 It is arbitrarily excluded. 指被武断地排除在课堂之外，但 Most teachers today, almost three out of four ... use a mix called "balanced literacy" 表明 phonics 至少被以混合形式部分使用，并未被武断排除；且 Q51 问的是 in many classrooms 的状况，不是普遍排除。 D) 无中生有 It is misrepresented. 指被歪曲/错误地呈现，但定位句谈论的是它在课堂氛围中受冷遇，并不涉及 "歪曲"。
questions.hint: 回到原文定位题干关键词，比较选项与原文的含义。

questions.prompt: What has America been witnessing for decades?

options.text: An obsession with innovating teaching methodologies of reading.
An enduring debate over the approach to teaching children to read.
An increasing concern with many children's inadequacy in literacy.
An ever-forceful advocacy of a combined method for teaching reading.

questions.shortExplanation: America is stuck in a debate about teaching children to read that has been going on for decades.
questions.detailedExplanation:
【答案】 B （细节题）

【判型】 What has America been witnessing for decades? 索取一个客观的、贯穿数十年的事实，应在原文找到对应陈述。

【拆句】 What has America been witnessing for decades? 主干 America has been witnessing what，for decades 是持续性时间状语，与现在完成进行时呼应。

【定位】 America is stuck in a debate about teaching children to read that has been going on for decades.

美国陷入了一场关于如何教孩子阅读的争论，这场争论已经持续了几十年。

【选项】 A) 偷换概念 An obsession with innovating teaching methodologies of reading. 把核心从 "争论" 偷换成 "对创新阅读教学法的痴迷"，原文谈的是两派持续对立而非痴迷创新。

B) ✓ 正确 a debate about teaching children to read ↔

An enduring debate over the approach to teaching children to read. has been going on for decades ↔ enduring B 项把定位句里 "持续数十年" + "关于教孩子阅读的争论" 两个核心元素分别压缩为 enduring + debate over the approach to teaching children to read，与预判精准对应。 C) 偷换概念 An increasing concern with many children's inadequacy in literacy. 把对象换成 "对许多孩子识字不足的担忧"，原文 P2 提到识字率低只是后果数据，并不是 "美国数十年来一直在见证" 的主体。 D) 与原文相反 An ever-forceful advocacy of a combined method for teaching reading. 说 "对组合法越来越有力的倡导"，但原文明确通过 Tenette Smith 说 This combination of methods is ineffective，与选项方向相反。
questions.hint: 回到原文定位题干关键词，比较选项与原文的含义。

questions.prompt: Why does Tenette Smith think a combination of teaching methods is ineffective?

options.text: Elementary schoolchildren will be frustrated when taught with several methods combined.
Phonics has to be systematically applied and clearly taught to achieve the desired effect.
Sprinkling in a little phonics deters the progress of even adequately motivated children.
Balanced literacy fails to sustain children's interest in developing a good reading habit.

questions.shortExplanation: "You can't sprinkle in a little phonics," says Tenette Smith, executive director of elementary education and reading at Mississippi's education department. "It has to be systematic and explicitly taught." "你不能只是零星地撒点拼读法进去"，密西西比州教育部基础教育与阅读执行主任 Tenette Smith 说，"它必须被系统、明确地教授。"
questions.detailedExplanation:
【答案】 B （细节题）

【判型】 Why does Tenette Smith think a combination of teaching methods is ineffective? 用 Why 索取原因，对应原文里这位人物所说的解释。

【拆句】 Why does Tenette Smith think a combination of teaching methods is ineffective? Why 引导，think 后接 that 从句（that 省略），从句主语是 a combination of teaching methods，谓语 is ineffective，结构清晰。

【定位】 "You can't sprinkle in a little phonics," says Tenette Smith, executive director of elementary education and reading at Mississippi's education department. "It has to be systematic and explicitly taught." "你不能只是零星地撒点拼读法进去"，密西西比州教育部基础教育与阅读执行主任 Tenette Smith 说，"它必须被系统、明确地教授。"

【选项】 A) 无中生有 Elementary schoolchildren will be frustrated when taught with several methods combined. 把 ineffective 的原因换成 "孩子受挫"，原文未提及任何 frustration。

B) ✓ 正确 It has to be systematic and explicitly taught. ↔

Phonics has to be systematically applied and clearly taught to achieve the desired effect. You can't sprinkle in a little phonics ↔ Phonics has to be systematically applied 选项 Phonics has to be systematically applied and clearly taught to achieve the desired effect. 把 Tenette Smith 引号里的两条要求 systematic + explicitly taught 完整保留，与预判一致。 C) 过度推断 Sprinkling in a little phonics deters the progress of even adequately motivated children. 把原文的 "不能零星撒拼读法" 错误延伸为 "零星撒拼读法会阻碍连足够有动力的孩子的进步"，文中并未谈到 "motivated children" 或被 "deter" 这一具体后果。 D) 偷换概念 Balanced literacy fails to sustain children's interest in developing a good reading habit. 把无效的原因换成 "无法维持孩子对培养良好阅读习惯的兴趣"，原文 Tenette Smith 完全没谈兴趣/习惯。
questions.hint: 回到原文定位题干关键词，比较选项与原文的含义。

questions.prompt: What does the author say Mississippi's success is attributed to?

options.text: Convening a National Reading Panel to synthesize research evidence.
Placing sufficient emphasis upon both fluency and comprehension.
Adopting scientifically grounded approaches to teaching reading.
Obtaining support from Congress to upgrade teaching methods.

questions.shortExplanation: Mississippi's success is attributed to implementing reading methods supported by a body of research known as the science of reading.
questions.detailedExplanation:
【答案】 C （细节题）

【判型】 What does the author say Mississippi's success is attributed to? 直接索取一个归因事实，是细节题。

【拆句】 What does the author say Mississippi's success is attributed to? 嵌套结构：What 是 attributed to 的宾语前置；the author say 是插入的引述层；核心是 Mississippi's success is attributed to what。

【定位】 Mississippi's success is attributed to implementing reading methods supported by a body of research known as the science of reading.

密西西比州的成功要归因于实施了由一整套被称为 "阅读科学" 的研究所支持的阅读教学法。

【选项】 A) 张冠李戴 Convening a National Reading Panel to synthesize research evidence. 把 1997 年国会召集小组这一历史背景错当成密西西比成功的直接归因，但原文归因句的对象是 implementing reading methods，不是 convening a panel。 B) 以偏概全 Placing sufficient emphasis upon both fluency and comprehension. 取的是 panel 结论 phonics, along with explicit instruction in phonemic awareness, fluency and comprehension 中的两个并列项，但归因对象是整体阅读科学，不是 fluency + comprehension 这两点。 C) ✓ 正确 reading methods supported by a body of research known as the science of reading ↔

Adopting scientifically grounded approaches to teaching reading. implementing reading methods ↔ Adopting ... approaches to teaching reading 选项 C 把 "实施" "由研究支持的" "阅读教学法" 三要素分别压缩为 Adopting、 scientifically grounded、approaches to teaching reading，与预判精确对应。

D) 无中生有 Obtaining support from Congress to upgrade teaching methods. 误把 1997 年国会的角色解读为对密西西比的支持，但原文中国会只是请专家组综述证据，并未对密西西比直接 upgrade 教学法。
questions.hint: 回到原文定位题干关键词，比较选项与原文的含义。

questions.prompt: What have advances in statistics and brain imaging proved ineffective?

options.text: Efforts to end the reading wars.

questions.shortExplanation: But advances in statistics and brain imaging have disproved the whole-language method.
questions.detailedExplanation:
【答案】 D （细节题）

【判型】 What have advances in statistics and brain imaging proved ineffective? 索取一个具体被证伪的对象，是细节题。

【拆句】 What have advances in statistics and brain imaging proved ineffective? 主干 advances have proved what ineffective，What 同时充当 proved 的宾语，ineffective 是宾语补足语；此处 prove 接复合宾语，意为证明某物是无效的。

【定位】 But advances in statistics and brain imaging have disproved the whole-language method.

但统计学和脑成像方面的进展已经证伪了整体语言法。

【选项】 A) 与原文相反 The teaching of symbol-sound relationships. 取自 Some advocate teaching symbol-sound relationships ... known as phonics，但被证伪的对象是 whole-language，而 phonics 在文中被反复认定为 the best way to teach children to read。

B) 与原文相反 Explicit instruction in phonemic awareness. 取自 phonics, along with explicit instruction in phonemic awareness, fluency and comprehension, worked best， 是 panel 推荐有效的做法，并非被证伪的对象。 C) 答非所问 Efforts to end the reading wars. 来自 end the "reading wars"，但原文并未说这种努力被证伪；被证伪的是具体的 whole-language method。

D) ✓ 正确 the whole-language method ↔ The immersive approach. disproved ↔ proved ineffective 本题难度在于：题干用 proved ineffective、原文用 disproved、选项用 The immersive approach. 而非 the whole-language method——只有读出 P3 里 immersive approach = whole language 的等值，才能锁定 D。

items.title: 2023年6月六级第2套 · 选词填空
items.passage:
Imagine sitting down to a big dinner: a massive steak, a large portion of fried potatoes, and cake for dessert. After eating so much, you should be too full to eat another bite. But some people experience a powerful urge to keep eating, even after [26] _____ in a huge meal, a behavior that makes little sense, as most adults are well-versed in the dangers of obesity, which researchers have shown correlates with [27] _____ health issues and is even linked to increased [28] _____ risk. But some people still keep eating long after they should stop, a phenomenon Dr. Susan Thompson calls "insatiable(永不满⾜的) hunger." It is characterized by two main [29] _____ : not being satisfied by eating, and having a desire to stay sedentary(久坐不动的 ).

This is at [30] _____ with how humans are biologically programmed. When there was a great deal of food available, ancient people would gorge on calories; this massive calorie intake was accompanied by an urge to get active. Humans were also programmed for something called "compensation," which is the brain's [31] _____ mechanism for preventing the accumulation of excess weight. With compensation, if you eat one large meal in the morning, you are naturally [32] _____ to eat less for the rest of the day.

But recent studies show that 70% of American adults have lost the ability to naturally compensate for the calories they consume; worse [33] _____ , a significant number of them report [34] _____ hunger halfway through an eating session, but, by the end of the meal, they feel the same or higher levels of hunger than when they sat down. Dr. Thompson argues that the main cause of this phenomenon is the modern diet, which is [35] _____ of food high in sugar, carbohydrates and calories.

questions.prompt: even after __(26)__ in a huge meal
questions.shortExplanation: indulge in=纵情大吃，与“吃完一顿大餐”语义一致句意是“即使在 indulging in a huge meal（沉溺/纵享一顿大餐）之后还想继续吃”， indulge in 是固定搭配，且语义恰是“尽情享用一顿大餐”，与开篇 Imagine sitting down to a big dinner: a massive steak, a large portion of fried potatoes, and cake for dessert. 的“暴饮暴食”场景严丝合缝。
questions.detailedExplanation:
【答案】 H) indulging 动词

【词性槽】 介词 after 后必跟动名词

【依据】 indulge in=纵情大吃，与“吃完一顿大餐”语义一致句意是“即使在 indulging in a huge meal（沉溺/纵享一顿大餐）之后还想继续吃”， indulge in 是固定搭配，且语义恰是“尽情享用一顿大餐”，与开篇 Imagine sitting down to a big dinner: a massive steak, a large portion of fried potatoes, and cake for dessert. 的“暴饮暴食”场景严丝合缝。

【竞争词】 B) comprised 搭配是 be comprised of，不接 in

comprised 的固定搭配是 be comprised of（由……组成），不与 in 连用，且这里没有 be 动词；语义“一顿大餐由……组成”也与“吃完后还想吃”的语境无关。

E) diminishing 义为“递减”，与“暴饮暴食”反向

diminish in 表示“在……方面减少”，可这里要表达的是“纵享了一顿大餐”，diminishing in a huge meal（在一顿大餐中递减？）语义讲不通，方向恰好相反。
questions.hint: 根据空格前后的词性、搭配与上下文选择词语；每个词最多使用一次。

questions.prompt: which researchers have shown correlates with __(27)__ health issues
questions.shortExplanation: “无数的”健康问题，与肥胖危害的客观表述匹配
questions.detailedExplanation:
【答案】 I) innumerable 形容词

【词性槽】 correlates with ___ health issues，名词前作定语

【依据】 “无数的”健康问题，与肥胖危害的客观表述匹配

原文是说肥胖 correlates with __(27)__ health issues——医学常识告诉我们肥胖会引发“多到数不清”的健康问题（心血管、糖尿病、关节、肿瘤……），innumerable 是常见且中性的描述。

【竞争词】 O) unmatchable 感情色彩偏褒，且语义不通

unmatchable 表“无与伦比”，是积极/褒义评价词，用来形容“健康问题”从感情色彩到搭配都明显错位——说“无与伦比的健康问题”更像是把“好”和“坏”拼接起来，逻辑不通。
questions.hint: 根据空格前后的词性、搭配与上下文选择词语；每个词最多使用一次。

questions.prompt: is even linked to increased __(28)__ risk.
questions.shortExplanation: mortality risk=死亡风险，肥胖危害的高频搭配
questions.detailedExplanation:
【答案】 J) mortality 名词

【词性槽】 increased ___ risk，名词前作定语

【依据】 mortality risk=死亡风险，肥胖危害的高频搭配

is even linked to increased __(28)__ risk. 上承“肥胖关联无数健康问题”，再用 even 递进，意指“甚至与死亡风险升高相关”——mortality risk 是医学英语里极常见的固定搭配， 且 even 的递进语气也只有“死亡”这级别的代价能配得上。

【竞争词】 A) attributesattribute risk 搭配不存在

attributes 是“属性”，与 risk 不能复合构成“属性风险”这种意义，且语义也不递进。

D) conservation 话题错位

conservation 是“资源保护”，conservation risk 偏环保领域，与肥胖语境完全不接轨。

L) plights 复数名词无法作单数前置定语，且无此搭配

plights 用复数，且 plights risk 不是固定搭配，无法表达“困境风险”这种意思。
questions.hint: 根据空格前后的词性、搭配与上下文选择词语；每个词最多使用一次。

questions.prompt: It is characterized by two main __(29)__: not being satisfied by eating, and having a desire to stay sedentary(久坐不动的 ).
questions.shortExplanation: attributes=特征，正好对应冒号后并列的两件特征 It is characterized by two main attributes：两个主要特征——一是“吃不饱”，二是“想久坐不动”，正好两条；attributes 在描写“现象/事物的标志性特征”时最常用，与 characterized by 形成 collocation 闭环。
questions.detailedExplanation:
【答案】 A) attributes 名词

items.title: 2023年6月六级第2套 · 信息匹配
items.passage:
A) When psychologist Jessica Pryor lived near an internationally renowned university, she once saw a student walking into a library holding a sleeping bag and a coffee maker. She has heard of graduate students spending 12 to 18 hours at a time in the lab. Their schedules are meant to be literally punishing: If they are scientists-in-training, they won't allow themselves to watch Netflix until their experiments start generating results. "Relationships become estranged( 疏远的 )—people stop inviting them to social gatherings or dinner parties, which leads them to spend even more time in the lab," Pryor told me.

B) Along with other therapists, Pryor, who is now with the Family Institute at Northwestern University, is trying to sound the alarm about a tendency among young adults and college students to strive for perfection in their work—sometimes at any cost. Though it is often portrayed as a positive trait, Pryor and others say extreme perfectionism can lead to depression, anxiety, and even suicide.

C) What's more, perfectionism seems to be on the rise. In a study of thousands of American, Canadian, and British college students published earlier this year, Thomas Curran of the University of Bath and Andrew Hill of York St. John University found that today's college students report higher levels of perfectionism than college students did during the 1990s or early 2000s. They measured three types of perfectionism: self-oriented, or a desire to be perfect; socially prescribed, or a desire to live up to others' expectations; and other-oriented, or holding others to unrealistic standards. From 1989 to 2016, they found, self-oriented perfectionism scores increased by 10 percent, socially prescribed scores rose by 33 percent, and other-oriented perfectionism increased by 16 percent.

D) A person living with an other-oriented perfectionist might feel criticized by the perfectionist spouse for not doing household chores exactly the "right" way. "One of the most common things couples argue about is the proper way of loading the dishwasher," says Amy Bach, a psychologist in Providence, Rhode Island.

E) Curran describes socially prescribed perfectionism as "My self-esteem is contingent on what other people think." His study didn't examine the causal reasons for its rise, but he assumes that the rise of both standardized testing and social media might play a role. These days, LinkedIn alerts us when our rival gets a new job, and Instagram can let us know how well "liked" our lives are compared with a friend's. In an opinion piece earlier this year, Curran and Hill argue that society has also become more dog-eat-dog. "Over the last 50 years, public interest and civic responsibility have been progressively eroded," they write, "replaced by a focus on self-interest and competition in a supposedly free and open marketplace." We strive for perfection, it seems, because we feel we must in order to get ahead. Michael Brustein, a clinical psychologist in Manhattan, says when he first began practicing in 2007, he was surprised by how prevalent perfectionism was among his clients, despite how little his graduate training had focused on the phenomenon. He sees perfectionism in, among others, clients who are entrepreneurs, artists, and tech employees. "You're in New York because you're ambitious, you have this need to strive," he says. "But then your whole identity gets wrapped into a goal."

F) Perfectionism can, of course, be a positive force. Think of professional athletes, who train aggressively for ever-higher levels of competition. In well-adjusted perfectionism, someone who doesn't get the gold is able to forget the setback and move on. In maladaptive(不当的) perfectionism, meanwhile, people make an archive of all their failures. They revisit these archives constantly, thinking, as Pryor puts it, "I need to make myself feel terrible so I don't do this again." Then they double down, "raising the expectation bar even higher, which increases the likelihood of defeat, which makes you self-critical, so you raise the bar higher, work even harder," she says. Next comes failure, shame, and pushing yourself even harder toward even higher and more impossible goals. Meeting them becomes an "all or nothing" premise. Pryor offered this example: "Even if I'm an incredible attorney, if I don't make partner in the same pacing as one of my colleagues, clearly that means I'm a failure."

G) Brustein says his perfectionist clients tend to devalue their accomplishments, so that every time a goal is achieved, the high lasts only a short time, like "a gas tank with a hole in it." If the boss says you did a great job, it's because he doesn't know anything. If the audience likes your work, that's because it's too stupid to know what good art actually is. But, therapists say, there are also different ways perfectionism manifests. Some perfectionists are always pushing themselves forward. But others actually fall behind on work, unable to complete assignments unless they are, well, perfect. Or they might handicap their performance ahead of time. They're the ones partying until 2 a.m. the night before the final, so that when the grade C rolls in, there's a ready excuse.

H) While educators and parents have successfully convinced students of the need to be high performing and diligent, the experts told me, they haven't adequately prepared them for the inevitability of failure. Instead of praises like "You're so smart," parents and educators should say things like "You really stuck with it," Pryor says, to emphasize the value of perseverance over intrinsic talent. Pryor notes that many of her clients are wary she'll "turn them into some degenerate couch potato and teach them to be okay with it." Instead, she tries to help them think through the parts of their perfectionism they'd like to keep, and to lose the parts that are ruining their lives.

I) Bach, who sees many students from Brown University, says some of them don't even go out on weekends, let alone weekdays. She tells them, "Aim high, but get comfortable with good enough." When they don't get some award, she encourages them to remember that "one outcome is not a basis for a broad conclusion about the person's intelligence, qualifications, or potential for the future."

J) The treatment for perfectionism might be as simple as having patients keep logs of things they can be proud of, or having them behave imperfectly in small ways, just to see how it feels. "We might have them hang the towels crooked( 不正的 ) or wear some clothing inside out," says Martin Antony, a professor in the department of psychology at Ryerson University in Toronto.

K) Brustein likes to get his perfectionist clients to create values that are important to them, then try to shift their focus to living according to those values rather than achieving specific goals. It's a play on the "You really stuck with it" message for kids. In other words, it isn't about doing a headstand in yoga class; it's about going to yoga class in the first place, because you like to be the kind of person who takes care of herself. But he warns that some people go into therapy expecting too much—an instant transformation of themselves from a pathological( 病态的 ) perfectionist to a (still high-achieving) non-perfectionist. They try to be perfect, in other words, at no longer being perfect.

items.title: 2023年6月六级第2套 · 仔细阅读 · 第一篇
items.passage:
How on earth did we come to this? We protect our children obsessively from every harm; we scrutinize every carer, teacher or doctor with whom they come into contact. Yet despite all this, one group, which in no way has their best interests at heart, has almost unconstrained access.

We seem to take it for granted that advertisers and marketers are allowed to condition even the youngest children. Before children have even developed a proper sense of their own identity, or learned to handle money, they're encouraged to associate status and self-worth with stuff, and to look to external things such as fame and wealth for validation. We're turning out little consumers rather than young citizens who will value themselves for what they contribute to the society in which they live.

We've reached this point so gradually that many of us have never questioned it. It's crept up on us in the 60 years since advertisers started to target the young and found that they could recruit them to a commercial assault on their parents. We've come to know it as "pester power" or the ability of children to pressure parents to make certain purchases.

Many psychologists, child development experts and educators point to research suggesting that this emerging cradle-to-grave consumerism is contributing to growing rates of low self-esteem, depression and other forms of mental illness.

Not all psychologists agree. There're plenty working hand in glove with a ￡12bn-a-year industry that has turned the manipulation of adult emotions and desires into an art form—often literally. It's also one that's forever developing new ways to persuade our children to desire material possessions, and because of advertisements' viral effect they only need to infect a few to reach the many. Advertising and marketing can serve a useful purpose for children. Marketing may help socialize children as consumers, inform them about products, and help them carve out unique identities as they reach adulthood.

Then, should we ban all advertising aimed at young children? I say yes.

Of course there'll be plenty of objections to an outright ban on advertising to the under-11s. There'll be those who argue that would be a breach of freedom of speech and infringe the rights of corporations to brainwash little children into demanding their products.

Most parents hate what advertising does to their children, but we do have the power to end it and let our children grow up free from many of the pressures of consumerism until they're old enough to make their own decisions. And though advertising is only part of an all-pervasive(⽆ 处不在的) marketing culture we need to make a start somewhere. Let's ban all advertising targeting children of primary school age and younger now.

questions.prompt: Which group of people does the author say has almost unrestricted access to children?

questions.detailedExplanation:
【答案】 A （细节题）

【判型】 Which group of people does the author say has almost unrestricted access to children? 直接询问「哪一群人」，要求在原文里找出对应群体，是典型的事实细节追问。

【拆句】 主干为 Which group of people ... has almost unrestricted access to children，does the author say 是插入语，去掉后剩「哪一群人对孩子有几乎不受限制的接触权」，结构平铺直叙，无陷阱。

【定位】 Yet despite all this, one group, which in no way has their best interests at heart, has almost unconstrained access. 然而尽管如此，有一个群体，他们丝毫不把孩子的最大利益放在心上，却几乎不受限制地接触着孩子。

【选项】 A) ✓ 正确 advertisers and marketers are allowed to condition even the youngest children ↔ Advertisers 预判的「对孩子不友好却不受限制的群体」在 P2 被明示为广告商和营销者，与选项 Advertisers 直接对应。 B) 与原文相反 Carers 属于 every carer, teacher or doctor with whom they come into contact 中被严格审查的一方，是「保护孩子」的角色，与「几乎不受限地接触孩子」的群体相反。 C) 与原文相反 Teachers 同样位于 every carer, teacher or doctor 列表中，是被审查的对象，不是 「几乎不受限地接触孩子」的群体。 D) 与原文相反 Doctors 也是 every carer, teacher or doctor 列表中的被审查对象，原文未把医生列为 「几乎不受限接触孩子」的群体。

【答案】 A （细节题）

【选项】 A) ✓ 正确 this emerging cradle-to-grave consumerism ↔ life-long consumerism growing rates of low self-esteem, depression and other forms of mental illness ↔

【答案】 A （推断题）

它（广告业）也是这样一个行业：不断开发新方法来诱使我们的孩子渴望物质；而由于广告的病毒式效应，他们只需感染少数即可触及多数。

It is actually infectious to many rather than a few they only need to infect a few to reach the many ↔ rather than a few 由 infect a few to reach the many 一步推出「广告其实波及多数而非少数」，正好是 imply 题所要的「一步推断」型答案。

会有人辩称（禁止广告）将构成对言论自由的侵犯，并损害企业「向幼儿洗脑、让他们索要产品」的权利。

items.passage:
Many oppose workplace surveillance, because of the inherent dehumanizing effect it has and the relentless pressure it brings. But it's on the rise around the world as firms look to become more efficient by squeezing more productivity from their workers. More than half of companies with over $750m in annual revenue used "non-traditional" monitoring techniques on staff last year.

Monitoring employee performance gives firms the ability to assess how their staff are performing and interacting, which can be good for both the firm and employees themselves. A growing number of analytics companies offer this service. They gather "data exhaust" left by employees' email and instant messaging apps, and use name badges equipped with radio-frequency identification devices and microphones. These can check how much time you spend talking, your volume and tone of voice, even if you do not dominate conversations. While this may sound intrusive, exponents argue that it can also protect employees against bullying and sexual harassment.

Some of this data analysis can produce unexpected results. For example, it was found that people who sat at 12-person lunch tables tended to interact, share ideas more and outperform those who regularly sat at four-person tables, a fact that would probably have gone undetected without such data analysis.

Over the last few years a Stockholm co-working space called Epicenter has gone much further and holds popular "chipping parties", where people can have microchips implanted in their hands. They can use the implants to access electronically-controlled doors, or monitor how typing speed correlates with heart rate. Implanted chips may seem extreme, but it is a relatively small step from ID cards and biometrics to such devices.

As long as such schemes are voluntary, there will probably be a growing number of convenience-oriented uses so that a substantial number of workers would opt to have a chip inserted. But if implanted chips are used to reduce slack time or rest breaks, that could prove to be detrimental. And if surveillance tools take away autonomy, that's when they prove most unpopular. A lot depends on how such monitoring initiatives are communicated and this could prevent possible revolts being staged.

If bosses don't communicate effectively, employees assume the worst. But if they're open about the information they're collecting and what they're doing with it, research suggests 46% of employees are generally okay with it. Although many such monitoring schemes use anonymised data and participation is voluntary, many staffers remain sceptical and fear an erosion of their civil liberties.

So workplace surveillance could be empowering for staff and useful for companies looking to become more efficient and profitable. But implemented in the wrong way, it could also become an unpopular tool of oppression that proves counterproductive.
