Analyzing data gathered from workers can yield something unexpected.
More workmates sitting at a lunch table tend to facilitate interaction and idea sharing.
It is hard to decide on how many people to sit at a lunch table without data analysis.

questions.shortExplanation: Some of this data analysis can produce unexpected results. For example, it was found that people who sat at 12-person lunch tables tended to interact, share ideas more and outperform those who regularly sat at four-person tables, a fact that would probably have gone undetected without such data analysis.
questions.detailedExplanation:
【答案】 B （例证目的题）

【判型】 What does the author want to show by the example...中by the example明示题干在追问例子的论证目的而非例子的字面内容。

【拆句】 题干主干What...want to show中by the example为方式状语,后接of介词短语different numbers of people interacting at lunch tables修饰example;considering动名词成分较长,但句意线性无歧义。

【定位】 Some of this data analysis can produce unexpected results. For example, it was found that people who sat at 12-person lunch tables tended to interact, share ideas more and outperform those who regularly sat at four-person tables, a fact that would probably have gone undetected without such data analysis.

这种数据分析有时会产生出人意料的结果。例如,研究发现坐12人餐桌的人比坐4人餐桌的人更倾向于互动、分享想法,表现也更好,而这一事实如果没有这种数据分析很可能会被忽略。

【选项】 A) 过度推断原文从未声称数据分析是监控成功实施的key;论点只是说"数据分析能产生意外结果",而非"数据分析是监控成功的关键";key一词无原文支撑。

B) ✓ 正确 Some of this data analysis can produce unexpected results. ↔

Analyzing data gathered from workers can yield something unexpected. B项主谓宾三段(Analyzing data/can yield/something unexpected)与原文(this data analysis/can produce/unexpected results)逐成分对应,是论点句的标准同义重写。 C) 答非所问 C项More workmates sitting at a lunch table tend to facilitate interaction and idea sharing字面复述了例子内容,但题干问的是例子要说明的论点,不是例子本身,答非所问。 D) 偷换概念原文末尾a fact that would probably have gone undetected without such data analysis强调的是"数据分析揭示了这一事实",而非"数据分析帮助决定餐桌人数";D项把焦点偏到"决定餐桌坐几人"上。
questions.hint: 回到原文定位题干关键词，比较选项与原文的含义。

questions.prompt: What does much of the positive effect of monitoring initiatives depend on?

options.text: How frequently employees are to be monitored.
What specific personal information is being excluded.
What steps are taken to minimize their detrimental impact.
How well bosses make known their purpose of monitoring.

questions.shortExplanation: A lot depends on how such monitoring initiatives are communicated and this could prevent possible revolts being staged.
questions.detailedExplanation:
【答案】 D （细节题）

【判型】 What does much of the positive effect of monitoring initiatives depend on?问的是文中明确写出的依赖条件,不需推断。

【拆句】 题干主干What does...depend on?中谓语动词是depend on,主语是较长的名词短语much of the positive effect of monitoring initiatives;of短语层层修饰,但语义线性,认出动词短语 depend on即可。

【定位】 A lot depends on how such monitoring initiatives are communicated and this could prevent possible revolts being staged.

很多事情取决于这些监控举措是如何被传达的,这种沟通可能阻止潜在的抵制行动发生。

【选项】 A) 无中生有原文从未提到监控的frequency(频率),只谈how communicated;A项把"如何沟通"偷换为"多频繁地监控",原文无任何对应。

B) 偷换概念原文many such monitoring schemes use anonymised data谈匿名化处理,但语境是"虽然匿名,员工仍恐惧";B项specific personal information is being excluded把焦点偏到"排除哪些信息",且与题干"positive effect depend on"无对应。 C) 过度推断原文确实提到detrimental一词,但句子是"如果用监控减少休息,可能detrimental";题干问的是"positive effect depend on",答案应回到A lot depends on的主句而非 detrimental前的条件句;C项把"减少不利影响的步骤"作为positive effect的依赖,属过度推断。

D) ✓ 正确 how such monitoring initiatives are communicated ↔

How well bosses make known their purpose of monitoring D项核心动词make known精确对应原文communicated,主语bosses合理补出施动者,purpose of monitoring为补全语境的合理增添,语义聚焦于"沟通"这一关键变量。
questions.hint: 回到原文定位题干关键词，比较选项与原文的含义。

questions.prompt: What concern do monitoring initiatives cause among many staffers?

options.text: They may erode the workplace environment.
They may infringe upon staffers' entitled freedom.
They may become counterproductive in the long run.

questions.shortExplanation: Although many such monitoring schemes use anonymised data and participation is voluntary, many staffers remain sceptical and fear an erosion of their civil liberties.
questions.detailedExplanation:
【答案】 C （细节题）

【判型】 What concern do monitoring initiatives cause among many staffers?问的是员工在原文中明确表达的某项顾虑,不是作者推断。

【拆句】 题干主干What concern do monitoring initiatives cause中concern作cause的宾语前置,among many staffers为范围状语;倒装并未改变句意,主语是monitoring initiatives。

【定位】 Although many such monitoring schemes use anonymised data and participation is voluntary, many staffers remain sceptical and fear an erosion of their civil liberties.

尽管许多此类监控方案使用匿名数据且参与是自愿的,许多员工仍持怀疑态度,担心他们的公民自由被侵蚀。

【选项】 A) 与原文相反原文workplace surveillance could be empowering for staff中的empower指的是"赋权员工",而非"赋权雇主";A项empower employers excessively反转了方向,且 excessively无原文支撑。 B) 偷换概念原文用an erosion of their civil liberties,erosion的对象是公民自由,而非workplace environment;B项保留了erosion的同根词erode,但把宾语偷换为"工作环境",熟词陷阱。 C) ✓ 正确 an erosion of their civil liberties↔infringe upon staffers' entitled freedom 预判的"公民自由被侵蚀"被C项以infringe upon...entitled freedom精确改写,主谓宾结构对应,语义内核完整保留。 D) 张冠李戴 an unpopular tool of oppression that proves counterproductive是作者在末段的两面性总评,主体是作者而非many staffers;D项把作者的总评搬来作员工的顾虑,主体错位。
questions.hint: 回到原文定位题干关键词，比较选项与原文的含义。

items.title: 2023年6月六级第3套 · 选词填空
items.passage:
You might not know yourself as well as you think. According to a new study, people are [26] _____ accurate judges of only some of their behaviors. While most previous studies on how well people know themselves have been done on long-term personality traits, this new study [27] _____ how well people understand how they are acting from one moment to the next. Researchers asked participants to wear audio recorders that automatically [28] _____ every 9.5 minutes between 7 a.m. and 2 a.m. to record 30 seconds of audio. These participants were then emailed surveys four times a day asking them to [29] _____ how outgoing, agreeable, or conscientious they were during a particular hour of the day. The study used data from 248 participants, all of whom answered questions about their behavior for two [30] _____ weeks and wore the audio device for one of those weeks.

Six laboratory assistants rated each participant's audio clips to see how their observations compared with people's [31] _____ of themselves. The six assistants were generally in agreement with one another about how the people they were observing acted. Further, participants' ratings of their own behaviors agreed with observers' for how outgoing and how conscientious they were being. But the agreement between participants and outside observers was much smaller for agreeableness. Some of this [32] _____ could be because the observers used only audio clips, and thus could not read [33] _____ like body

language, but there are [34] _____ other explanations, as people should be able to hear when a participant is being kind versus being rude. The weak agreement between how participants thought they were acting and what observers heard could be because people would rather [35] _____ rude behavior.

questions.prompt: According to a new study, people are __(26)__ accurate judges of only some of their behaviors.
questions.shortExplanation: 与 of only some of their behaviors 的"有限/不完全"语义共振
questions.detailedExplanation:
【答案】 L) relatively 副词

【词性槽】 空在 are 与 accurate judges 之间，修饰形容词 accurate

【依据】 与 of only some of their behaviors 的"有限/不完全"语义共振

句尾 only some of their behaviors 已经把人对自己行为的判断范围限定为"只有部分"，作者要表达的是"对自身行为只能算是相对准确的判断者"，relatively 这种程度副词正好与"only some"形成呼应——不是绝对准确、只是相对准确。

【竞争词】 H) probably 情态偏"可能性"，与后文"only some"的限定语义错位

probably 表"很可能"，强调命题的真假概率；但原句要表达的不是"人可能是准确判断者"，而是"在准确程度上是相对的、有限的"。况且 probably 留给第 34 题更贴——那里 are __ other explanations 需要的正是"很可能还有其他解释"，这个词更值得留给后面。
questions.hint: 根据空格前后的词性、搭配与上下文选择词语；每个词最多使用一次。

questions.prompt: this new study __(27)__ how well people understand how they are acting from one moment to the next.
questions.shortExplanation: 研究"深入探究"问题是惯用搭配句意是"这项新研究深入探究人们对自己片刻行为的理解程度"，与前句 While most previous studies on how well people know themselves have been done on long-term personality traits 的对比正好——以前的研究做长期人格、这项新研究则"深入考察"短时行为。a study probes/explores how... 是学术语境的高频表达。
questions.detailedExplanation:
【答案】 I) probes 动词

【词性槽】 主语 this new study 后缺谓语

【依据】 研究"深入探究"问题是惯用搭配句意是"这项新研究深入探究人们对自己片刻行为的理解程度"，与前句 While most previous studies on how well people know themselves have been done on long-term personality traits 的对比正好——以前的研究做长期人格、这项新研究则"深入考察"短时行为。a study probes/explores how... 是学术语境的高频表达。

【竞争词】 B) articulatesarticulate 偏"清晰表达观点"，主语应是人或文章

articulates 的典型主语是人/作者/政策文件，意为"清晰阐明（一种立场）"；用在"研究"上多见于"该研究阐明了某结论"，但本句宾语是 how-从句问号式的"研究问题"，与"探究/调查"的语义更贴，与 articulate 的"明确表达已有观点"语义错位。

【易错】 最具迷惑性的错误词是 B) —— B articulates 三单形态完全合，靠语义才能区分。 articulates 在 this new study ___ how... 的位置看似也通，但 articulate 指"清晰表达观点"，主语应是已经形成立场的人或文件；而本句宾语是 how-从句的研究问题，本质是"研究在调查/探究某问题"。一句话防坑：研究＋how 问题＝probe/explore，研究＋that 结论 ＝articulate/state。
questions.hint: 根据空格前后的词性、搭配与上下文选择词语；每个词最多使用一次。

questions.prompt: Researchers asked participants to wear audio recorders that automatically __(28)__ every 9.5 minutes between 7 a.m. and 2 a.m. to record 30 seconds of audio.
questions.shortExplanation: 录音机"被启动/启动"是描述设备机制的标准表达录音机"每 9.5 分钟自动启动一次以录 30 秒音频"才符合实验设计。activated 在此为过去式作谓语，与全文研究描述的过去时态一致（如 asked、used、were 都是过去时），且 automatically activated 是描述自动设备的常见搭配 audio recorders that automatically __(28)__ every 9.5 minutes between 7 a.m. and 2 a.m.。
questions.detailedExplanation:
【答案】 A) activated 动词

【词性槽】 that 引导定语从句，空作从句谓语

【依据】 录音机"被启动/启动"是描述设备机制的标准表达录音机"每 9.5 分钟自动启动一次以录 30 秒音频"才符合实验设计。activated 在此为过去式作谓语，与全文研究描述的过去时态一致（如 asked、used、were 都是过去时），且 automatically activated 是描述自动设备的常见搭配 audio recorders that automatically __(28)__ every 9.5 minutes between 7 a.m. and 2 a.m.。

【竞争词】 I) probes 时态为现在时、且语义不指设备启动

probes 是第三人称单数现在时，与复数主语 recorders 不一致；语义上指"探究/调查"，多与人或问题搭配，不与"录音机每 9.5 分钟探究"搭配。

B) articulates 单复数不匹配 + 语义指"清晰表达"

articulates 主语应是人（清晰表达），与"录音机"在主谓搭配上严重失配，单复数也与复数 recorders 不一致。

K) recall 语义指人的"回忆"，与设备主语冲突

recall 的主语通常是人，意为"回忆/想起"；机器"recall every 9.5 minutes"不成立，且 K 在 29 题有更刚需的位置（让参与者"回忆"自己当时的行为）。

O) terminate 语义反向："终止"与"启动录音"完全相反

若代入 terminate every 9.5 minutes，意为"每 9.5 分钟终止一次"，与后半句 to record 30 seconds of audio（启动后录 30 秒）形成逻辑矛盾。
questions.hint: 根据空格前后的词性、搭配与上下文选择词语；每个词最多使用一次。

questions.prompt: These participants were then emailed surveys four times a day asking them to __(29)__ how outgoing, agreeable, or conscientious they were during a particular hour of the day.
questions.shortExplanation: 回忆某时段自己有多外向/友善＝实验任务
questions.detailedExplanation:
【答案】 K) recall 动词

【词性槽】 asking them to＋空，不定式中的动词原形

【依据】 回忆某时段自己有多外向/友善＝实验任务

原句要求参与者评估"自己在某一小时里有多外向、友善或尽责" how outgoing, agreeable, or conscientious they were during a particular hour of the day，这是典型的"回忆性自评"任务，recall 表"回想起"与"a particular hour of the day（白天某一小时）"的过去时间状语精准匹配。

【竞争词】 F) deny 语义反向："否认"自己有多外向不成立

ask them to deny how outgoing they were 意为"让他们否认自己当时有多外向"，逻辑荒谬；且 F 在 35 题处有更贴切的位置（参与者"否认"粗鲁行为）。

O) terminate 搭配错误：终止"自己有多外向"不通

terminate 通常与活动、合同、过程搭配，不能与 how-从句搭配描述自我评估。
questions.hint: 根据空格前后的词性、搭配与上下文选择词语；每个词最多使用一次。

questions.prompt: answered questions about their behavior for two __(30)__ weeks and wore the audio device for one of those weeks.
questions.shortExplanation: two consecutive weeks＝"连续两周"是高频固定搭配原文说参与者要回答两周的行为问卷、其中一周还要戴录音设备，强调的是"连着进行的两周"。consecutive 与 weeks 是英语里"连续 N 周"的标准说法，语义与研究设计完全吻合 answered questions about their behavior for two __(30)__ weeks。
questions.detailedExplanation:
【答案】 D) consecutive 形容词

【词性槽】 数词 two 与名词 weeks 之间的限定位置

【依据】 two consecutive weeks＝"连续两周"是高频固定搭配原文说参与者要回答两周的行为问卷、其中一周还要戴录音设备，强调的是"连着进行的两周"。consecutive 与 weeks 是英语里"连续 N 周"的标准说法，语义与研究设计完全吻合 answered questions about their behavior for two __(30)__ weeks。

【竞争词】 J) random 与"两周"严密的实验时段矛盾

random weeks 意为"随机的（任选的）几周"，但研究是两周连续追踪、并明确其中一周戴录音设备 wore the audio device for one of those weeks，时间是确定段落而非随机选取，与 random 的"任意性"冲突。

M) saturated 搭配不成立、语义不通

saturated 多用于"饱和脂肪/被…浸透/市场饱和"，从未与"weeks"构成日常表达；语义上也无法解释一段"被饱和的两周"，搭配直接证伪。

【易错】 最具迷惑性的错误词是 J) —— J random 词性、搭配都看似通。random 是形容词、可修饰 weeks、读起来也顺，但与原文研究设计"连续两周＋其中一周戴录音"的精密时段冲突。 一句话防坑：先去原文找时间安排的描述（wore the audio device for one of those weeks），看时段是"连续"还是"随机"再下笔。
questions.hint: 根据空格前后的词性、搭配与上下文选择词语；每个词最多使用一次。

questions.prompt: to see how their observations compared with people's __(31)__ of themselves.
questions.shortExplanation: 与前文 observations 形成"他评 vs 自评"对比
questions.detailedExplanation:
【答案】 C) assessment 名词

【词性槽】 形容词性物主代词 people's 后接名词

【依据】 与前文 observations 形成"他评 vs 自评"对比

句子在比较"助理们的 observations"与"参与者对自己的 ___"，这正是研究的核心对照—— 他人观察 vs 自我评估。assessment 意为"评估/判断"，与 observations 在抽象层级上对等，构成"observations of A vs assessment of A"的标准学术对照 how their observations compared with people's __(31)__ of themselves。

【竞争词】 G) discrepancy discrepancy 是"差异"本身、不是"参与者对自己的判断"

discrepancy of themselves 不成立——人不会"对自己有差异"。况且 G 在 32 题处恰好用来描述"自评与他评之间的分歧"，那里才是它的归宿。
questions.hint: 根据空格前后的词性、搭配与上下文选择词语；每个词最多使用一次。

questions.prompt: Some of this __(32)__ could be because the observers used only audio clips
questions.shortExplanation: 回指上文"自评与他评在 agreeableness 上分歧明显"
questions.detailedExplanation:
【答案】 G) discrepancy 名词

【词性槽】 代词 this 后＋空 → 抽象名词作主语

【依据】 回指上文"自评与他评在 agreeableness 上分歧明显"

上句说 But the agreement between participants and outside observers was much smaller for agreeableness. 这正是"分歧/不一致"。this ___ 概括的就是这种 agreeableness 上的不一致，discrepancy 恰是"差异/出入"的标准名词，与 agreement 反义构成上下文呼应。
questions.hint: 根据空格前后的词性、搭配与上下文选择词语；每个词最多使用一次。

questions.prompt: could not read __(33)__ like body language
questions.shortExplanation: cues 与 body language 同属"非语言线索"语义集
questions.detailedExplanation:
【答案】 E) cues 名词

【词性槽】 动词 read 的宾语 + like body language 的同位列举

【依据】 cues 与 body language 同属"非语言线索"语义集

cues 指"线索/信号"，nonverbal cues / visual cues 与 body language 构成同位列举，语义自然贴合："观察者无法读取诸如肢体语言这类的线索" could not read __(33)__ like body language——正好解释为什么仅听音频会让宜人评分出现偏差。

【竞争词】 N) symptoms symptoms 是"病症"，与"肢体语言"不同类

symptoms 多指疾病征候，无法与 body language 构成同位列举；read symptoms 在医学语境可成立，但与本文心理学行为观察主题不符。
questions.hint: 根据空格前后的词性、搭配与上下文选择词语；每个词最多使用一次。

questions.prompt: but there are __(34)__ other explanations
questions.shortExplanation: but 后引出"可能还有别的解释"的推测语气
questions.detailedExplanation:
【答案】 H) probably 副词

【词性槽】 are 与 other explanations 之间的存在句结构

【依据】 but 后引出"可能还有别的解释"的推测语气

前句 could be because the observers used only audio clips, and thus could not read __(33)__ like body language 给出一种解释（可能因为只听音频），但作者用 but 引出另一种猜测：很可能还有别的解释。probably 恰好承担"作者的推测口吻"，与 could be 的不确定基调一致。
questions.hint: 根据空格前后的词性、搭配与上下文选择词语；每个词最多使用一次。

questions.prompt: could be because people would rather __(35)__ rude behavior.
questions.shortExplanation: 人们"宁可否认"自己粗鲁——解释自评偏差
questions.detailedExplanation:
【答案】 F) deny 动词

【词性槽】 would rather＋空 → 动词原形

【依据】 人们"宁可否认"自己粗鲁——解释自评偏差

items.title: 2023年6月六级第3套 · 信息匹配
items.passage:
A) We're experiencing the rebirth of smallness. Farmers markets, tiny homes, and brew pubs all exemplify our love of smallness. So do charter schools, coffee shops, and local bookstores. Small is often (but not always) more affordable, healthier, and sustainable, but its finest characteristic, the one that turns charm into love, is that going small allows us to be more fully who we are.

B) In higher education the trend is mostly in the opposite direction: Universities with 20,000 or 30,000 students are considered "mid-sized". The nation's largest university, Arizona State University, has 80,000 students on campus and aims to enroll another 100,000 students online. At the other end of the spectrum is a handful of colleges that have fewer than a hundred students on campus and no online courses: colleges such as Sterling College, Thomas More College of Liberal Arts, and Deep Springs College. These colleges are so small that they can only be called "tiny."

C) Tiny colleges focus not just on a young person's intellect, but on the young person as a whole. Equally important, tiny colleges ask, "How can education contribute to human flourishing and the well-being of the world?" And they shape a college experience to address that question. They replace concerns about institutional growth with attention to the growth of students as fully developed participants in their communities.

D) I've had the privilege of teaching at three different institutions of higher learning during my career— a small liberal arts college and two mid-sized public universities. I've also been profoundly disappointed in each of these institutions, and in many of my colleagues, especially when it comes to helping students and preparing them for the many responsibilities of adulthood. Administrators focus on the business of running a university, and most faculty focus on their scholarship and teaching their discipline. Little deliberate attention is given to how students mature as individuals and social beings.

E) Having just retired from teaching at a public university, I'm now returning to my hometown of Flagstaff, Arizona, to establish a tiny college—Flagstaff College. I'm convinced there's a need for another type of education, one devoted to helping students come into their own and into this beautiful and troubled world. Young people need an education that will provide them with meaning, hope, courage, and passion, as well as information and skills. Large institutions, I believe, are particularly ill-suited to this type of education.

F) There's no "best of" list when it comes to tiny colleges, at least not yet. But around the country people are creating new colleges that provide an alternative to small liberal arts colleges, large public universities, and online education.

G) With only 26 students, Deep Springs is the smallest college in the country and, quite likely, the most atypical( ⾮ 典型的 ). Located on a working cattle ranch on the California-Nevada border, Deep Springs is a private, residential, two-year college for men, committed to educating students for "a life of service to humanity." Founded by the electricity tycoon( ⼤亨 ) L.L. Nunn in 1917, Deep Springs "curriculum" revolves around academics, labor, and self-governance. In addition to their courses, students are charged with running the 155-acre ranch and overseeing the functioning of the college. Students chair both the admissions and the curriculum committees.

H) "Living in close community with one's teachers and fellow students, and being forced to take on adult responsibilities, makes for one's growth as a person," says William Hunt, who graduated last year. "To exist for very long in a community like that, you have to get over the question of whether you're sufficiently talented or principled and get started worrying about how you can stretch yourself and your peers, how much you can manage to learn with them."

I) Sterling College, in Craftsbury Common, Vermont, is also very small—fewer than 100 students. Unlike Deep Springs, Sterling focuses its curriculum on environmental and social justice issues, but like Deep Springs it places a high value on personal responsibility and manual labor. According to its catalog, a college education at Sterling combines "rigorous academics, roll-up-your-sleeves challenges, and good old hard work."

J) The average tuition at a small liberal-arts college is $30,000 to $40,000 a year, not including the cost of living on campus, as compared to $8,000 to $10,000 a year for tuition alone at a public university. Of the tiny colleges, only Deep Springs doesn't charge tuition or room and board; students pay only for books and the cost of traveling to and from college. If tiny schools are to become a player on the higher education scene, they will need to find a way to be truly affordable.

K) Doing so may not be that difficult so long as they do not pattern themselves too closely on existing norms. We've come to believe that a good college should have many academic programs and excellent facilities, posh(豪华的 ) dorms, an array of athletic programs, and a world-class student activity center. Imagine a good college without a climbing wall! We also have accepted the idea that college presidents, and their many vice-presidents, should be paid like their counterparts in the business world and that higher education requires an elaborate, up-to-date technology infrastructure. All of this drives up the cost of education.

L) The "trick" to making tiny colleges affordable, if that's the right word, is simplicity. At its core, education is a human-to-human interaction. Reflecting on his own college education, President Garfield once commented that an ideal college would consist of nothing more than the legendary teacher Mark Hopkins on one end of a log and a student on the other. The economics of a tiny college, in other words, might be similar to that of a tiny house. Because it is small, a tiny house costs less to build and less to furnish, insure, and maintain. But the economic benefits of a small house don't end there. Tiny homes discourage homeowners from buying stuff that they really don't need, because there's no place to put it.

M) I'm a late convert to the idea of tiny colleges, and I fully understand the need for many diverse types of educational institutions. Academic research and job training are important, but tiny colleges aren't suited for either. The educational needs of a complex society are themselves complex, and no single model can meet all of these needs. But I'm now convinced there's an educational need that's now going almost completely unmet: namely, the need to help young people transition into adulthood. Tiny colleges can do this better than any other type of educational institution.

N) The ultimate justification for a tiny college is the conviction that each of us comes into our full humanity by close interaction with those who know and care for us, and that one of the basic purposes of higher education is social. Although we give lip service to the idea that a college education will make us better people, when all's said and done, we think of higher education primarily in economic terms. We've come to think of higher education as a means to make a living rather than make a life. We've also come to see higher education as a private good rather than a public one. Tiny colleges are not the answer to all of our educational requirements, but they're an answer to one of our most basic educational necessities; the need to produce thoughtful, engaged, and compassionate human beings.

items.title: 2023年6月六级第3套 · 仔细阅读 · 第一篇
items.passage:
If you're someone who has turned to snacking on junk food more in the pandemic( ⼤流⾏病 ), you're not alone. Investigative reporter Michael Moss says processed food is engineered to hook you, not unlike alcohol, cigarettes, or other harmful substances. His 2013 book, Salt Sugar Fat, explored food companies' aggressive marketing of those products and their impact on our health. In his new book, Hooked, Moss updates the food giants' efforts to keep us eating what they serve, and how they're responding to complaints from consumers and health advocates.

Processed food is inexpensive, it's legal, and it's everywhere. Companies' advertising is cueing us to remember those products and we want those products constantly. So the food environment is one of those key things that makes food even more problematic for so many people. Memory, nostalgia(怀旧) in particular, plays a big role in the foods we crave. Soda companies discovered that if they put a soda in the hands of a child when they're at a ball game with their parents, that soda will forever be associated with that joyous moment. Later in life, when that child wants to experience a joyous moment, they're going to think of soda. Many people seek comfort in the snacks they remember from childhood.

Moss examines the way companies capitalize on our memories, cravings and brain chemistry to keep us snacking.

One of the reasons I came to think that some of these food products are even more powerful, more troublesome than drugs can be is memory. What we eat is all about memory. And we begin forming memories for food at a really early age. And we keep those memories for a lifetime. Knowing this, the food industry spends lots of time trying to shape the memories that we have for their products. One of the features of addiction that scientists studying drug addiction discovered back in the 1990s was that the faster a substance hits the brain, the more apt we are as a result to act impulsively. There's nothing faster than food in its ability to hit the brain. For Moss, this puts the notion of "fast food" in an entirely new light as this isn't limited to fast food chains-almost 90% of food products in grocery stores are processed foods. Everything in the industry is about speed, from manufacturing to packaging.

Overall, Moss outlines the industry's dependence on making their products inexpensive, super delicious, and incredibly convenient for consumers. Now that more and more people care about what they put in their bodies and are wanting to eat healthier, these companies are finding it really difficult to meet that new demand because of their own addiction to making these convenience foods.

questions.prompt: In what way does Michael Moss think processed food is comparable to alcohol and cigarettes?

They are all in increasingly great demand.

questions.shortExplanation: Investigative reporter Michael Moss says processed food is engineered to hook you, not unlike alcohol, cigarettes, or other harmful substances.
questions.detailedExplanation:

【判型】 In what way does Michael Moss think processed food is comparable to alcohol and cigarettes? 问的是一个明确的可比关系，答案应能从原文一句话直接读出。

【拆句】 主干 does Michael Moss think processed food is comparable to alcohol and cigarettes，从句 that 省略，理解关键是 comparable to 的语义"与……可比"，不是"被比作"。结构平铺直叙、无陷阱。

B) 无中生有 necessary evils 原文未提及；Moss 全文批评加工食品，没有任何"必要"评价。 C) 偷换概念 engineered to be enjoyed 把原文 engineered to hook you 偷换为"为享受而设计"——hook 是"勾住、使上瘾"的强迫语义，与"被享受"的中性愉悦语义不等。 D) 偷换概念 increasingly great demand 原文未提及"需求日益增大"；Moss 说的是公司在"积极推销"（aggressive marketing），不是消费者需求暴涨。

如今越来越多的人在意吃进体内的东西、想吃得更健康，这些公司发现自己很难满足这一新需求，原因在于它们自身已经"上瘾"于生产这些便利食品。

items.title: 2023年6月六级第3套 · 仔细阅读 · 第二篇
items.passage:
Chimpanzees(⿊猩猩), human beings' closest animal relatives, share up to 98% of our genes. Yet humans and chimpanzees lead very different lives. Fewer than 300,000 wild chimpanzees live in a few forested corners of Africa today, while humans have colonized every corner of the globe. At more than 7 billion, human population dwarfs that of nearly all other mammals—despite our physical weaknesses.

What could account for our species' incredible evolutionary successes?

One obvious answer is our big brains. It could be that our raw intelligence gave us an unprecedented ability to think outside the box, innovating solutions to thorny problems as people migrated across the globe.

But a growing number of cognitive scientists and anthropologists(⼈类学家 ) are rejecting that explanation. They think that, rather than making our living as innovators, we survive and thrive precisely because we don't think for ourselves. Instead, people cope with challenging climates and ecological contexts by carefully copying others.

In a famous study, psychologists Victoria Horner and Andrew Whiten showed two groups of test subjects—children and chimpanzees—a mechanical box with a treat inside. In one condition, the box was opaque, while in the other it was transparent. The experimenters demonstrated how to open the box to retrieve the treat, but they also included the irrelevant step of tapping on the box with a stick.

Oddly, the children carefully copied all the steps to open the box, even when they could see that the stick had no practical effect. That is, they copied irrationally: Instead of doing only what was necessary to get their reward, children slavishly imitated every action they'd witnessed.

Of course, that study only included three—and four-year-olds. But additional research has shown that older children and adults are even more likely to mindlessly copy others' actions, and infants are less likely to over-imitate—that is, to precisely copy even impractical actions.

By contrast, chimpanzees in the study only over-imitated in the opaque condition. In the transparent condition—where they saw that the stick was mechanically useless—they ignored that step entirely. Other research has since supported these findings.

When it comes to copying, chimpanzees are more rational than human children or adults.

Where does the seemingly irrational human preference for over-imitation come from? Anthropologist Joseph Henrich points out that people around the world rely on technologies that are often so complex that no one can learn them rationally. Instead, people must learn them step by step, trusting in the wisdom of more experienced elders and peers.

So the next time you hear someone arguing passionately that everyone should embrace nonconformity and avoid imitating others, you might laugh a little bit. We're not chimpanzees, after all.

questions.prompt: What might explain humans' having the largest population of almost all mammals?

options.text: They are equipped with raw strength for solving the most challenging problems.
They cope with the outside world more effectively than their animal relatives.
They possess the most outstanding ability to think.
They know how to survive everywhere on earth.

questions.shortExplanation: One obvious answer is our big brains. It could be that our raw intelligence gave us an unprecedented ability to think outside the box, innovating solutions to thorny problems as people migrated across the globe.
questions.detailedExplanation:
【答案】 C （细节题）

【判型】 题干 What might explain humans' having the largest population of almost all mammals? 指向文章中给出原因解释的某一句，并非全文主旨，属于细节题。

【拆句】 主干是 What might explain X，其中 X 由动名词短语 humans' having the largest population of almost all mammals 充当 explain 的宾语；不定式般的动名词结构是六级常见考点，注意 humans' 是 having 的逻辑主语，不是 population 的所有格。

【定位】 One obvious answer is our big brains. It could be that our raw intelligence gave us an unprecedented ability to think outside the box, innovating solutions to thorny problems as people migrated across the globe.

一个显而易见的答案是我们的大脑。可能是我们的纯粹智力赋予了我们一种前所未有的跳出思维定式的能力，让人们在迁徙到全球各处时能够创新性地解决棘手难题。

【选项】 A) 偷换概念选项 equipped with raw strength for solving the most challenging problems 用 raw strength 替换原文 raw intelligence，正话反说——文章首段恰恰强调 despite our physical weaknesses，人类身体反而是弱的。 B) 答非所问 They cope with the outside world more effectively than their animal relatives 用 animal relatives 把题点引向 Chimpanzees, human beings' closest animal relatives ——黑猩猩，但 51 题问的是 largest population of almost all mammals 的原因，原因句在 P3 而非 P1。 C) ✓ 正确 our raw intelligence gave us an unprecedented ability to think outside the box ↔

possess the most outstanding ability to think our big brains ↔ possess 预判已锁定卓越的思考能力，C 选项 possess the most outstanding ability to think 在词面与语义上都与定位句一一对应，是定位句的标准同义替换。

D) 答非所问 They know how to survive everywhere on earth 是 humans have colonized every corner of the globe 的同义改写，但这是现象本身，不是题目所问的解释；题干 What might explain 要的是原因。

questions.prompt: What accounts for humans' evolutionary successes according to a growing number of cognitive scientists and anthropologists?

options.text: They are better at innovating solutions.
They are naturally adaptive to ecological contexts.
They meet challenges by imitating others carefully.

questions.shortExplanation: They think that, rather than making our living as innovators, we survive and thrive precisely because we don't think for ourselves. Instead, people cope with challenging climates and ecological contexts by carefully copying others.
questions.detailedExplanation:
【答案】 D （细节题）

【判型】 题干 according to a growing number of cognitive scientists and anthropologists 限定了观点来源，要求回原文找到该群体说了什么，属典型署名细节题。

【拆句】 主干 What accounts for humans' evolutionary successes，后接 according to 短语作状语限定信息来源；account for 在此意为解释/导致，是六级高频熟词僻义。

【定位】 They think that, rather than making our living as innovators, we survive and thrive precisely because we don't think for ourselves. Instead, people cope with challenging climates and ecological contexts by carefully copying others.

他们认为：我们之所以存活下来并蓬勃发展，恰恰不是因为我们以创新者的身份谋生，而恰恰是因为我们不自己思考。相反，人类是通过仔细地模仿他人来应对极具挑战的气候与生态环境的。

【选项】 A) 张冠李戴 They are better at innovating solutions 来自 innovating solutions to thorny problems——但这是 P4 But 转折之前被驳的旧解释，不是 a growing number of 科学家的观点；题干限定了观点出处，必须取转折之后。

B) 与原文相反 They thrive through creative strategies 用 creative——这与 we don't think for ourselves 直接相反，文章明确说人类成功不靠自己思考创新。

C) 无中生有 They are naturally adaptive to ecological contexts 把 ecological contexts 抄过来制造熟悉感，但 naturally adaptive（与生俱来的适应性）这种说法在原文没有任何出处 ——文章强调的是后天模仿。

D) ✓ 正确 by carefully copying others ↔ imitating others carefully cope with challenging climates and ecological contexts ↔ meet challenges 预判已锁定靠仔细模仿来应对挑战，They meet challenges by imitating others carefully 在结构（meet challenges by + 动名词短语）和措辞上与定位句完全同义。

questions.prompt: What does the author think is odd about the findings of the study by Victoria Horner and Andrew Whiten?

options.text: Children irrationally imitated every action of the experimenters.
Chimpanzees could tell the transparent box from the opaque one.
Chimpanzees could retrieve the treat more quickly than children did.
Children omitted the step of tapping on the box with a stick to open it.

questions.shortExplanation: Oddly, the children carefully copied all the steps to open the box, even when they could see that the stick had no practical effect. That is, they copied irrationally: Instead of doing only what was necessary to get their reward, children slavishly imitated every action they'd witnessed.
questions.detailedExplanation:
【答案】 A （细节题）

【判型】 题干问的是作者认为某项研究中 odd 的具体内容，需要回到原文一句话找出对应描述，是细节题而非态度题。

【拆句】 主干 What does the author think is odd about X，think 后跟省略 that 的宾语从句 is odd about the findings，about 短语限定 odd 的范围；考生易把 think is odd 误读成主旨态度题。

【定位】 Oddly, the children carefully copied all the steps to open the box, even when they could see that the stick had no practical effect. That is, they copied irrationally: Instead of doing only what was necessary to get their reward, children slavishly imitated every action they'd witnessed.

奇怪的是，儿童仔细地模仿了开盒子的每一步动作，哪怕他们能看出那根木棒并没有任何实际作用。也就是说，他们的模仿是非理性的：他们没有只做获得奖励所必需的动作，而是奴隶般地模仿了所看到的每一个动作。

【选项】 A) ✓ 正确 children slavishly imitated every action they'd witnessed ↔

Children irrationally imitated every action of the experimenters every action they'd witnessed ↔ every action of the experimenters A 选项 Children irrationally imitated every action of the experimenters 完整对应定位句的两个关键点：irrationally 对应 slavishly/irrationally，every action of the experimenters 对应 every action they'd witnessed。

B) 答非所问 Chimpanzees could tell the transparent box from the opaque one 描述黑猩猩能区分透明与不透明盒子——这是 P8 黑猩猩对比段的隐含信息，但题干问的是作者认为 odd 的发现，奇怪在儿童这边，不在黑猩猩能不能区分上。 C) 无中生有 Chimpanzees could retrieve the treat more quickly than children did 提到黑猩猩比儿童更快取得食物——这种速度比较在文中没有任何描写。

D) 与原文相反 Children omitted the step of tapping on the box with a stick to open it 说儿童跳过了敲打这一步——与 children carefully copied all the steps 完全相反，且 P8 显示是黑猩猩在透明条件下才跳过这一步。

questions.prompt: What is anthropologist Joseph Henrich's explanation for the human preference for copying?

options.text: It originates in the rationality of people around the world.
It stems from the way people learn complex technologies.
It results from people distrusting their own wisdom.
It derives from the desire to acquire knowledge step by step.

questions.shortExplanation: Anthropologist Joseph Henrich points out that people around the world rely on technologies that are often so complex that no one can learn them rationally. Instead, people must learn them step by step, trusting in the wisdom of more experienced elders and peers. 人类学家 Joseph Henrich 指出：世界各地的人都依赖于一些非常复杂的技术，复杂到没有人能够完全理性地学会它们。因此，人们必须一步一步地学习这些技术，并信任那些更有经验的前辈与同伴的智慧。
questions.detailedExplanation:
【答案】 B （细节题）

【判型】 题干 What is anthropologist Joseph Henrich's explanation for the human preference for copying? 明确指向某专家对某行为的解释，属于署名+原因型细节题。

【拆句】 主干 What is anthropologist Joseph Henrich's explanation for the human preference for copying，anthropologist 是 Joseph Henrich 的同位语；preference for copying 名词化结构相当于 prefer to copy。

【定位】 Anthropologist Joseph Henrich points out that people around the world rely on technologies that are often so complex that no one can learn them rationally. Instead, people must learn them step by step, trusting in the wisdom of more experienced elders and peers. 人类学家 Joseph Henrich 指出：世界各地的人都依赖于一些非常复杂的技术，复杂到没有人能够完全理性地学会它们。因此，人们必须一步一步地学习这些技术，并信任那些更有经验的前辈与同伴的智慧。

【选项】 A) 与原文相反 It originates in the rationality of people around the world 说模仿源于人们的理性 ——可文中明确说 no one can learn them rationally，恰恰是没法理性学才需要模仿；选项把因果反过来了。

B) ✓ 正确 people must learn them step by step, trusting in the wisdom of more experienced elders and peers

↔ It stems from the way people learn complex technologies technologies that are often so complex ↔ complex technologies rely on technologies ↔ stems from B It stems from the way people learn complex technologies 把 Henrich 的两步因果（技术复杂 → 必须一步步模仿）压缩成模仿源于学习复杂技术的方式，与预判完全吻合。 C) 过度推断 It results from people distrusting their own wisdom——文章里只有 trusting in the wisdom of more experienced elders and peers，即信任前辈与同伴的智慧，并未说不信任自己的智慧；distrust their own 是过度推断 + 与原文相反的合成。

options.text: It is arguable whether everyone should avoid imitation.

questions.shortExplanation:
【答案】 B （推断题）

【判型】 What point does the author want to emphasize 询问的是作者借这句反语想强调什么， 属典型推断题。

【拆句】 题干主干 What point does the author want to emphasize when he says "We're not chimpanzees"?，when 引导时间状语从句，指明这句话所在的语境；需要把 not chimpanzees 当作对照、推出人类的特征。

【选项】 A
questions.detailedExplanation:
【答案】 B （推断题）

【判型】 What point does the author want to emphasize 询问的是作者借这句反语想强调什么， 属典型推断题。

【拆句】 题干主干 What point does the author want to emphasize when he says "We're not chimpanzees"?，when 引导时间状语从句，指明这句话所在的语境；需要把 not chimpanzees 当作对照、推出人类的特征。

【选项】 A) 偷换概念 It is arguable whether everyone should avoid imitation 把作者的话理解为模仿是否该避免是个值得讨论的问题——但作者并没有在讨论是否该避免，而是直接调侃那些反模仿者；arguable（有争议的）是无中生有的态度。

B) ✓ 正确 We're not chimpanzees, after all↔It is characteristic of human beings to copy others carefully copying others↔to copy others B It is characteristic of human beings to copy others 恰好把反语还原为正面陈述： 模仿是人类的特征；其余三项要么没抓到反语指向、要么停留在字面。

C) 以偏概全 It is desirable to trust in more knowledgeable peers 来自 trusting in the wisdom of more experienced elders and peers——这只是 Henrich 一段的局部解释，不是末段反语 We're not chimpanzees 想强调的点；末段强调的是人类天性模仿，不是信任前辈这件事好不好。 D) 与原文相反 It is naive to laugh at someone embracing nonconformity 说嘲笑追求不从众的人是天真的——可文中作者恰恰说 you might laugh a little bit，即可以笑一笑，作者站的是支持嘲笑那一方；naive（天真的）正话反说。
questions.hint: 回到原文定位题干关键词，比较选项与原文的含义。

items.title: 2024年12月六级第1套 · 选词填空
items.passage:
With the rapid progress in the economy, it is natural that people's ideology is bound for change. Being [26] _____ is no longer a virtue to some people, and they are not alone in holding this view. Each might have different viewpoints on how to lead one's lifestyle: some prefer simplicity, some love luxuries, some spend [27] _____ , some accumulate as much as they can like a country mouse. As I was born poor and in the countryside, the simple rural life seldom loses its [28] _____ to me, but as my station changes, I have an opportunity to [29] _____ with the newly rich, an experience which has revolutionized my view of lifestyle.

It is evil or sinful to spend little and to save much, an idea only recently being revealed to me. Actually the whole world is in a [30] _____ to borrow and to spend, with the USA leading the trend. The USA is still the richest and most powerful country in the world, but the [31] _____ is that they borrow money from us. Though a [32] _____ of economics, at least I know that investing with borrowed money will turn the borrower into the [33] _____ rather than the decent and kind lender. An apparent case is real estate. Those who are [34] _____ and have got loans from the bank become relatively rich by selling their purchased home at a price several folds higher. Even education is not immune from this theory. Many of those poor parents who have the vision to send their children to college have benefited from this

investment, even though they have to [35] _____ a living. It is reasonable to conclude that spending is praiseworthy, supposing it is not beyond your means.

questions.prompt: Being __(26)__ is no longer a virtue to some people
questions.shortExplanation: 全文主题是「省与花」，被评为美德的正是「节俭」
questions.detailedExplanation:
【答案】 O) thrifty 形容词

【词性槽】 Being ___ 是动名词作主语，空位须填形容词作表语

【依据】 全文主题是「省与花」，被评为美德的正是「节俭」

结合 overview 与下一段 It is evil or sinful to spend little and to save much，作者反思的正是把「节俭/少花多存」当美德这件事；此处需要一个表「节俭」的形容词，thrifty 精准对应；它也与第 27 题的 extravagantly 形成全文核心对照。

【竞争词】 G) majestic 「雄伟的」与个人生活态度无关

majestic 多用于山河、宫殿等宏伟事物，描述人时也偏「庄严威严」，与「美德/生活习惯」的语义场不沾边。

H) malicious 感情色彩反了——它是贬义

malicious 意为「心怀恶意的」，是贬义词；而后文紧跟 a virtue（美德），褒贬色彩冲突，直接排除。

N) shrewd 「精明」更偏处世手腕，且第 34 题更需要它

shrewd 指头脑精明、会算计，并不直接对应「省钱」这一道德范畴；而且本卷第 34 题 Those who are __(34)__ and have got loans from the bank 在「精明地借贷投资房产」的语境里几乎只能由 shrewd 填上，先做易空的策略告诉我们 shrewd 要留给第 34 题。

【易错】 最具迷惑性的错误词是 N) —— shrewd 也是形容词，且常被夸为美德。shrewd 既是形容词、又含「精明」这一常被视作褒义的特质，很容易被误填到 Being __(26)__ is no longer a virtue to some people；防坑点：本卷主旨是「省 vs 花」，第 34 题更需要 shrewd， 先看全文再回填，节俭（thrifty）才是和「a virtue」「spend little and save much」前后呼应的那个。
questions.hint: 根据空格前后的词性、搭配与上下文选择词语；每个词最多使用一次。

questions.prompt: some prefer simplicity, some love luxuries, some spend __(27)__, some accumulate as much as they can like a country mouse.
questions.shortExplanation: 与前文 luxuries、后文 accumulate 形成对照前一分句 some love luxuries 已立「奢华爱好」，下一分句 some accumulate as much as they can like a country mouse 立「拼命攒钱」；本空在「花钱方式」的维度上需要一个「挥霍地、毫无节制地」的副词，与「攒钱」形成强对比，extravagantly（奢侈地、挥霍地）正好对应。
questions.detailedExplanation:
【答案】 B) extravagantly 副词

【词性槽】 动词 spend 后缺修饰语，要填副词

【依据】 与前文 luxuries、后文 accumulate 形成对照前一分句 some love luxuries 已立「奢华爱好」，下一分句 some accumulate as much as they can like a country mouse 立「拼命攒钱」；本空在「花钱方式」的维度上需要一个「挥霍地、毫无节制地」的副词，与「攒钱」形成强对比，extravagantly（奢侈地、挥霍地）正好对应。

【竞争词】 C) intrinsically「本质上」与「花钱方式」无关

intrinsically 描述「事物的内在属性」，搭配 spend 既不构成常见用法，也讲不通「本质地花钱」这种意思，与前后并列项的「花钱风格」维度对不上。

F) literally「字面意义上」无法与 spend 直接搭出对照

literally 用于强调「真的、确确实实」，常修饰带夸张色彩的动词短语，但此处需要的是「花钱的程度/方式」对照「攒钱」，literally spend 无法形成对比意义，方向偏离。
questions.hint: 根据空格前后的词性、搭配与上下文选择词语；每个词最多使用一次。

questions.prompt: the simple rural life seldom loses its __(28)__ to me
questions.shortExplanation: lose one's appeal to sb.＝对某人失去吸引力
questions.detailedExplanation:
【答案】 A) appeal 名词

【词性槽】 形容词性物主代词 its 后接名词

【依据】 lose one's appeal to sb.＝对某人失去吸引力

lose one's appeal to sb. 是固定搭配；结合 As I was born poor and in the countryside, the simple rural life seldom loses its __(28)__ to me——「简单的乡村生活对我从未失去吸引力」，语义自洽，搭配地道。

【竞争词】 D) irony 「讽刺」与「失去」搭配方向不对

lose its irony 表「失去讽刺意味」，与「乡村生活对我」之间没有「讽刺」可言，且第 31 题 the irony is that... 是高度匹配 irony 的句型，应留给第 31 题。

E) layman 「外行」是指人，不能作生活的属性

layman 指「门外汉」，是描述人的身份名词，不会被「乡村生活」拥有；且第 32 题 a ___ of economics 是典型 a layman of 用法，应留给那里。

I) meadow 「草地」是具体物，不能被「失去」

meadow 是具体名词（草地、牧场），代入 lose its meadow 完全讲不通——乡村生活不会 「失去它的一块草地」。

K) predator 「掠夺者」与本句感情色彩冲突

predator 多含贬义「掠食者/剥削者」，与「乡村生活对我从未失去 ___」这种偏温情的语境冲突；且第 33 题 turn the borrower into the ___ rather than the decent and kind lender 明显需要它形成对照，应留给第 33 题。

L) rage 「盛怒/风潮」与「乡村生活对我」不搭

rage 作名词表「盛怒」或「时尚风潮」，lose its rage 不构成英文常见搭配，且语义与「乡村生活的吸引力」无关；第 30 题 in a rage to do 的固定结构更需要它。
questions.hint: 根据空格前后的词性、搭配与上下文选择词语；每个词最多使用一次。

questions.prompt: I have an opportunity to __(29)__ with the newly rich
questions.shortExplanation: mingle with sb. 是「与人交往」的固定搭配
questions.detailedExplanation:
【答案】 J) mingle 动词

【词性槽】 have an opportunity to ___ 中 to 后接动词原形

【依据】 mingle with sb. 是「与人交往」的固定搭配

mingle with the newly rich 即「与新富阶层打交道」，正是作者所说的 an experience which has revolutionized my view of lifestyle.——能改变其生活观的，只有「亲身接触」这件事，语义、搭配双双契合。

【竞争词】 M) scrape scrape 不与 with sb. 搭配「交往」

scrape 作动词意为「刮、擦、勉强凑集」，常见搭配是 scrape by/along/a living，并不存在 scrape with sb. 表示与人交往的用法；而且第 35 题 they have to __(35)__ a living 恰好是 scrape a living 的经典搭配，先做易空策略提示要把 M 留给第 35 题。
questions.hint: 根据空格前后的词性、搭配与上下文选择词语；每个词最多使用一次。

questions.prompt: Actually the whole world is in a __(30)__ to borrow and to spend, with the USA leading the trend.
questions.shortExplanation: in a rage to do＝狂热地、风靡地做某事 rage 作名词除「盛怒」外，常指「时尚、风靡一时的事物」；in a rage to borrow and to spend 即「世界都疯狂地借钱、花钱」，与后文 with the USA leading the trend（trend 也是同义复现）完全呼应。
questions.detailedExplanation:
【答案】 L) rage 名词

【词性槽】 be in a ___ to do sth. 中 a 后接名词

【依据】 in a rage to do＝狂热地、风靡地做某事 rage 作名词除「盛怒」外，常指「时尚、风靡一时的事物」；in a rage to borrow and to spend 即「世界都疯狂地借钱、花钱」，与后文 with the USA leading the trend（trend 也是同义复现）完全呼应。

【竞争词】 I) meadow 「草地」与「全世界都在借钱花钱」毫无关联

meadow 是具体名词且语义场完全脱节，代入后 in a meadow to borrow 不成句，立即排除。

【易错】 最具迷惑性的错误词是 I) —— meadow 看似与 borrow/spend 无关却最容易被排除得太晚。in a meadow 听上去像「在一片草地上」，部分考生扫到 the whole world is in a ___ 时可能短暂迷惑；防坑点：be in a ___ to do sth. 是固定结构，后接表「热潮/狂热」的抽象名词，meadow 不在此类，看 to do 这条线就能立排。
questions.hint: 根据空格前后的词性、搭配与上下文选择词语；每个词最多使用一次。

questions.prompt: but the __(31)__ is that they borrow money from us.
questions.shortExplanation: 「最强最富却向别人借钱」恰是反讽
questions.detailedExplanation:
【答案】 D) irony 名词

【词性槽】 定冠词 the 后＋is 前，须是名词作主语

【依据】 「最强最富却向别人借钱」恰是反讽

前一句 The USA is still the richest and most powerful country in the world，紧接 but the irony is that they borrow money from us——「最富最强反而要向我们借钱」正是 「反讽」最典型的用法；the irony is that... 也是英语固定句型。

【竞争词】 E) layman 「外行」无法承担 the ___ is that... 的语义

the layman is that... 不成立，layman 是指人，无法被引出「事实」的句型使用。

I) meadow 「草地」与 borrow money 无关

meadow 是具体名词，与「美国借钱」的话题完全脱节，语义不接。

K) predator 「掠夺者」做主语后接 is that 不通

predator 也是指人/动物的名词，the predator is that they borrow money from us 在意思上不通，且第 33 题 turn the borrower into the ___ 才是它的归宿。

L) rage 「盛怒/风潮」不能承担 the ___ is that... 的「事实/反差」语义

the rage is that... 不构成英文中表达「事实/反讽」的句型；且第 30 题 in a rage to do 的固定结构更需要它。
questions.hint: 根据空格前后的词性、搭配与上下文选择词语；每个词最多使用一次。

questions.prompt: Though a __(32)__ of economics, at least I know that...
questions.shortExplanation: a layman of economics＝经济学外行
questions.detailedExplanation:
【答案】 E) layman 名词

【词性槽】 Though a ___ of economics 是名词性短语作让步状语

【依据】 a layman of economics＝经济学外行

作者紧接说 at least I know that investing with borrowed money will turn the borrower into...——「虽是外行，但至少懂得……」，前后形成「让步＋让步内的肯定」逻辑；layman of 是「某领域的外行」的常见说法。

【竞争词】 I) meadow 「草地」不能修饰人的身份

meadow 不指人，与 Though I am a meadow of economics 完全不通，词义层面就排除。

K) predator 「掠夺者」与作者自谦语气冲突

predator 多用于贬义的「掠食者/掠夺者」，且后文紧跟 at least I know that... 这种「自谦但仍有见识」的口吻，搭配 predator 在语气和语义上都冲突；且第 33 题更需要它。

L) rage 「盛怒/风潮」不能描述人在某学科的身份

rage 作名词不指人，a rage of economics 不构成「某学科的人」这种用法；第 30 题 in a rage to do 才是它的归宿。
questions.hint: 根据空格前后的词性、搭配与上下文选择词语；每个词最多使用一次。

questions.prompt: investing with borrowed money will turn the borrower into the __(33)__ rather than the decent and kind lender.
questions.shortExplanation: predator vs. lender＝掠夺者 vs. 仁慈的放贷人
questions.detailedExplanation:
【答案】 K) predator 名词

【词性槽】 turn A into the ___ rather than the decent and kind lender 中 the 后名词

【依据】 predator vs. lender＝掠夺者 vs. 仁慈的放贷人

the decent and kind lender 是「正派善良的放贷人」，与之对照、且语义反向的恰是 predator（掠夺者/剥削者）；句意：「借钱投资会把借款人变成掠夺者，而非正派的放贷人」，与作者「借钱投资可致富」的论点完全一致。

【竞争词】 I) meadow 「草地」无法与「放贷人」并列对照

meadow 是具体名词，rather than 两端必须同类，meadow 与 lender 不同类，直接排除。

L) rage 「盛怒」也不指人，无法与 lender 同类并列

rage 作名词指「盛怒」或「风潮」，不指人，与 lender 不同类，无法承担 rather than 两端的对照；且第 30 题 in a rage to do 才是它的归宿。
questions.hint: 根据空格前后的词性、搭配与上下文选择词语；每个词最多使用一次。

questions.prompt: Those who are __(34)__ and have got loans from the bank become relatively rich by selling their purchased home at a price several folds higher.
questions.shortExplanation: 「精明」恰好描述会借贷投资房产致富的人 shrewd 意为「精明的、有眼光的」，与下文 have got loans from the bank become relatively rich by selling their purchased home at a price several folds higher. 描述的 「从银行贷款 → 倒卖房产 → 致富」的精明操作完全契合。
questions.detailedExplanation:
【答案】 N) shrewd 形容词

【词性槽】 Those who are ___ and have got loans 中 are 后＋and 并列谓语，空位须为形容词

【依据】 「精明」恰好描述会借贷投资房产致富的人 shrewd 意为「精明的、有眼光的」，与下文 have got loans from the bank become relatively rich by selling their purchased home at a price several folds higher. 描述的 「从银行贷款 → 倒卖房产 → 致富」的精明操作完全契合。

【竞争词】 G) majestic 「雄伟」不能形容人的投资能力

majestic 多用于山川、宫殿等宏伟事物，做表语形容人时偏「庄严威严」，与「会贷款投资房产」的精明操作无关。

H) malicious 贬义「恶意」与「合法投资致富」语境冲突

malicious 是「怀有恶意的」，但本句并未对借贷投资者作道德谴责，只是陈述「精明者→致富」的因果，贬义色彩不合适。
questions.hint: 根据空格前后的词性、搭配与上下文选择词语；每个词最多使用一次。

questions.prompt: they have to __(35)__ a living
questions.shortExplanation: scrape a living＝勉强糊口的固定搭配
questions.detailedExplanation:
【答案】 M) scrape 动词

【词性槽】 they have to ___ a living 中 to 后接动词原形带宾语

【依据】 scrape a living＝勉强糊口的固定搭配

上下文 Many of those poor parents who have the vision to send their children to college have benefited from this investment, even though they have to __(35)__ a living. 说穷父母为送孩子上大学不惜「勉强糊口」，scrape a living 是六级常考的固定搭配，含义完全契合「贫困到只够维持生活」的语境。
questions.hint: 根据空格前后的词性、搭配与上下文选择词语；每个词最多使用一次。

items.title: 2024年12月六级第1套 · 信息匹配
items.passage:
A) On a small fruit farm near the Straits of Malacca, Lim Kok Ann is down to just one tree growing kedondong, a crunchy, sour berry that Malaysians mostly use in pickles(腌菜) and salads. "It's not very well-known," says the 45-year-old, who is instead focusing on longan(⻰ 眼) berries and pineapples, which have bigger markets. "We have to grow what is profitable," he says.

B) But less than an hour away in the Malaysian countryside, inside three giant, silver domes, scientists are trying to change the future of food. They're pushing the boundaries of what humans eat by growing and processing so-called "alternative" crops—such as kedondong. At the headquarters of global research centre Crops For the Future (CFF) this particular under-used fruit has been turned into a sugar-free juice, high in vitamin C and getting top marks in sensory evaluations. "Anything you see here is a forgotten crop," says Sayed Azam-Ali of the abundant plants weaving through the gardens of CFF outside Malaysia's capital Kuala Lumpur.

C) Prof Azam-Ali explains that just four crops—wheat, maize, rice and soybean—provide two-thirds of the world's food supply. "We're dependent on these four," he says. "But actually there're 7,000 crops we've been farming for thousands of years. We ignore all of those." Researchers are trying to unlock the potential of these ignored crops—plants they describe as forgotten, under-used or "alternative" as they are displaced by increasingly uniform diets fuelled by processed ingredients from the major crops.

D) It's a timely quest. The food sector is already responsible for nearly a third of global greenhouse gas emissions. By 2050 it estimates the world must produce 50% more food to feed the projected global population of 10 billion. Meeting this demand without contributing to climate change calls for urgent solutions.

E) Forgotten crops hold key answers. By investing in neglected local plants, countries can reduce their reliance on imported crops and their carbon-heavy supply chains. Bringing back the variety of crops humans once ate also boosts food security at a time warming climates threaten existing crops. On top of that forgotten crops are among the most climate-resilient(具有⽓候韧性的 ) and nutritious, argues Azam-Ali. His summary is plain: "Dietary diversification is critical to the future of humanity."

F) Food security experts agree. "There is no food insecurity in the world, there is food ignorance," says Cecilia Tortajada, a senior research fellow at the Institute of Water Policy at the National University of Singapore. "Whenever we have native crops we tend to disregard them as if they were not valuable but they are," she adds.

G) Azam-Ali knows that scepticism firsthand. He came across alternative crops in the 1980s through the work of women farmers he met in Niger. The then-PhD student remembers marvelling at the crops they grew in their backyards, without the benefits of technology, to feed their families when the big crops failed. He saw a tremendous opportunity to build alternative food systems. But "the resistance was enormous," he recalls.

H) Undeterred, he ploughed on. Project after project helped prove these crops were viable in different environments as alternatives to the staple ones. But the question of whether these crops would be marketable remained. "That's the critical thing," he says. In one of the centre's domes, food technologist Tan Xinlin uses powdered moringa( 辣⽊ ) leaves in place of some wheat flour to bake a cake lower in gluten(⾕㬵 ) and higher in nutrients. Tan's job is to create recipes with these still-unfamiliar ingredients that will appeal to both local and international tastes. In recent years she has used some of the forgotten crops grown at CFF, such as moringa and bambara groundnut, to make everything from instant soup to Indian snacks. "I try to modernise forgotten crops instead of using old recipes." says Tan, who is also a trained chef. It's a strategy to appeal to the world's growing middle classes who are increasingly turning to the fast and processed food industries. It's also a way to help counter perceptions of local crops as "old or poor people's food" or as inferior "women's crops", adds Tan.

I) The roots of these connotations about local foods can run deep. The bambara groundnut, a protein-rich native crop of sub-Saharan Africa that is also grown in parts of southeast Asia, can trace its marginalisation to colonial rule. "African women who grew bambara groundnut were actually punished for growing it," says Azam-Ali. "Colonial powers said you can't grow that because there's no oil. We can't get a market for it." But today the bambara murukku is one of CFF's best reviewed foods and they are aiming to get it into grocery stores, pointing to the success of crops like quinoa to potential investors. Some 30 years ago, quinoa was virtually unheard of outside its native mountains in Bolivia and Peru. Today the nutritious grain is found on the menus of lavish restaurants across the world.

J) Measuring crops by nutrition instead of yield is at the heart of the forgotten foods enterprise. Ever since the "green revolution" of the 1960s, high-yielding crops have dominated modern agriculture. That was in part a crucial response to devastating famines at a time when the world needed to increase its food supply. Today "nutrition is becoming a time bomb", says Azam-Ali, as growing carbon dioxide levels strip crops of their minerals. Instead of bio-fortifying major crops we should be investing in those forgotten crops that are already more nutritious, he asserts.

K) In the bowels of CFF's third dome, lab manager Gomathy Sethuraman opens a window into the centre's "crown jewels", revealing vines of winged beans growing under a bright yellow light. It's one of multiple chambers where scientists are studying the impact of higher temperatures and carbon dioxide levels on the nutritional make-up of alternative crops. This research is "the game changer", says Azam-Ali, ensuring that "future crops" are also the healthiest ones in warmer climates.

L) There is a growing global momentum around forgotten foods, says Danielle Nierenberg, president of Food Tank, a US-based think tank. Other than CFF, which bills itself as the world's first research centre dedicated solely to under-utilised crops, there are other key groups championing agricultural diversity including Crop Trust, Slow Food, Icrisat and Bioversity International. Add to that more middle-income consumers searching for nutritious foods and others eager to try the unprocessed foods their grandparents once ate, she says.

M) But the rising interest in forgotten foods in some quarters is overtaken by the global spread of Western-style diets heavy in sugar, fat and processed foods in others.

N) A key obstacle to promoting fading local crops in Malaysia, for example, is "the obsession with imported products", says Jenifer Kuah, co-founder of a restaurant that champions locally-sourced food in an affluent suburb of Kuala Lumpur. Customers at Sitka, regarded as a pioneer in the country's small farm-to-table dining scene, still seek foreign ingredients as a "status symbol", she says.

O) The argument for forgotten foods feels intuitive. Some analysts say it is in fact inevitable. "Climate change is going to mean almost certainly tastes are going to be forced to change," says Tim Lang, professor of food policy at City, University of London. We "have to get used to eating other crops" as yields of staple crops fall, he says.

items.passage:
Imagine you're an alien sent to Earth to document the behaviour of the mammals inhabiting the planet. You stumble into a movie theatre that's showing the latest Hollywood horror film.

Several dozen humans are gathered together in a dark, undecorated room. They're all staring at a rectangular area on which patterns of light change rapidly.

They are clearly in a state of high arousal. Their heart rate is elevated, they occasionally glance around nervously, and they sometimes jump collectively in their seats, and emit high-pitched warning calls.

Eventually, the lights come up and the rectangular screen goes black. The humans stand up and leave the room, chatting and laughing, and showing signs of pleasure.

Why do these humans voluntarily expose themselves to what appears to be a deeply unpleasant experience? And why do they react so strongly to those patterns of light on a screen?

I am fascinated with the paradox of horror—the strange fact that many people seek out scary entertainment.

I think the answer to the puzzle lies in human nature.

My research suggests that we humans evolved to find pleasure in situations that allow us to experience negative emotions in a safe context. You can see these elements of horror in children's games. Take hide-and-seek for example, which is a simulation of a predator-prey interaction. The kid hides and the adult pretends to be a predator, searching for the child while howling like a dangerous beast.

This simulation gives the child crucial information about how to avoid becoming prey, and children tend to find that kind of activity deeply satisfying, presumably because it gives them a safe experience of a potentially catastrophic scenario.

They find it pleasurable, and pleasure is evolution's way of motivating us toward adaptive behaviour.

Horror is pleasurable to many people because it lets us play with negative emotions and develop coping strategies. We learn what it feels like to be truly afraid, and we learn how to handle negative emotion.

How, then, does horror work? My research suggests that horror works by exploiting an ancient set of biological defence mechanisms—an evolved fear system, which we share with other animals. But humans are uniquely imaginative, and we use our evolved imagination to travel into virtual worlds that are full of danger.

There are good reasons for watching a horror film, even if you're not a loyal horror fan. If you make it through the film in one piece, you'll probably experience a strong sense of mastery, a sense that you were able to make it through an appalling experience. Anyway, watching a horror film makes you better at handling your own fear, and who knows when that will become critically relevant?

questions.prompt: The alien finds the audience in the movie theatre clearly in a state of ______.
questions.shortExplanation: They are clearly in a state of high arousal. Their heart rate is elevated, they occasionally glance around nervously, and they sometimes jump collectively in their seats, and emit high-pitched warning calls.
questions.detailedExplanation:
【答案】 B （细节题）

【判型】 The alien finds the audience in the movie theatre clearly in a state of ______ 问的是外星人眼中观众的客观状态，无 infer/imply/mainly 等抽象信号，是单点事实细节。

【拆句】 Q46 句子主干是 The alien finds the audience ... in a state of ______，find sb. in a state of ... 是「发现某人处于某种状态」的复合宾语结构；clearly 修饰整个判断，强调状态显而易见；in the movie theatre 是 audience 的后置定语，无陷阱。

【定位】 They are clearly in a state of high arousal. Their heart rate is elevated, they occasionally glance around nervously, and they sometimes jump collectively in their seats, and emit high-pitched warning calls.

他们显然处于一种高度唤起的状态。心率加快，偶尔紧张地四下张望，时不时在座位上一齐惊跳，并发出尖叫般的警示声。

【选项】 A) 与原文相反 total mindfulness 指「完全的正念/平静专注」，与 high arousal 描绘的生理躁动完全相反。

B) ✓ 正确 high arousal ↔ extreme excitement Their heart rate is elevated ... jump collectively ... emit high-pitched warning calls ↔

extreme excitement 预判语义「高度兴奋」与 extreme excitement 在程度词 extreme=high、情绪词 excitement=arousal 两个维度上完全对位。

C) 无中生有 spiritual elevation 指「精神升华」，原文只描写心率 elevated 这种生理升高，未提及任何精神层面的升华。 D) 偷换概念 intense curiosity 把状态偷换成「强烈好奇」；但原文是因恐怖剧情引发的恐惧式高唤起，不是认知性好奇。

这种模拟向孩子提供了关于「如何避免成为猎物」的关键信息，孩子往往觉得这种活动极其令人满足，大概是因为它让他们在安全条件下体验了一种潜在的灾难性情境。

【选项】 A) ✓ 正确 how to avoid becoming prey ↔ How to avoid falling prey to an attacker The kid hides and the adult pretends to be a predator ↔ an attacker How to avoid falling prey to an attacker 是预判的近乎逐字改写，avoid 对 avoid、 falling prey 对 becoming prey、attacker 对 predator。

B) 答非所问 How to simulate a predator-prey interaction 学的是「如何模拟捕食情境」，但原文说「这场模拟（this simulation）」是大人创造的，孩子从中学到的是避险知识，而不是模拟技巧本身。

C) 无中生有 How to keep themselves from catastrophic errors 凭空造出「灾难性错误」一说； 原文只有 catastrophic scenario「灾难性情境」，且讨论的是体验该情境而非「避免错误」。 D) 偷换概念 How to turn a dangerous scenario into a safe one 把原文「在安全条件下体验潜在的灾难性情境」偷换成「把危险情境变安全」——原文的 safe 是体验时的环境条件，并非孩子把危险情境改造成了安全情境。
questions.hint: 回到原文定位题干关键词，比较选项与原文的含义。

questions.prompt: Why is horror gratifying to many people?

options.text: It reminds them of an ancient set of biological defence mechanisms.
It triggers their imagination to travel into dangerous virtual worlds.
It allows them to learn what fear feels like and how to tackle it.
It activates their evolved fear system and their unique fantasy.

questions.shortExplanation: Horror is pleasurable to many people because it lets us play with negative emotions and develop coping strategies. We learn what it feels like to be truly afraid, and we learn how to handle negative emotion. 对许多人而言，恐怖之所以令人愉悦，是因为它让我们演练负面情绪并发展出应对策略。我们由此了解真正害怕的感觉，也学会如何处理负面情绪。
questions.detailedExplanation:
【答案】 C （细节题）

【判型】 Why is horror gratifying to many people 问的是可在一句原文中找到的因果细节，作者给出明确的 because 句，非整体主旨。

【拆句】 Q49 主干 Why is horror gratifying to many people 是 be + adj. 的因果疑问句； gratifying 是现在分词作表语，等同 pleasing，要在原文找其同义表达 pleasurable，无结构陷阱。

【定位】 Horror is pleasurable to many people because it lets us play with negative emotions and develop coping strategies. We learn what it feels like to be truly afraid, and we learn how to handle negative emotion. 对许多人而言，恐怖之所以令人愉悦，是因为它让我们演练负面情绪并发展出应对策略。我们由此了解真正害怕的感觉，也学会如何处理负面情绪。

【选项】 A) 偷换概念 It reminds them of an ancient set of biological defence mechanisms 把「让我们演练负面情绪」偷换成「让我们想起远古防御机制」——原文是「利用」(exploiting) 防御机制，而不是「使我们回忆起」。 B) 答非所问 It triggers their imagination to travel into dangerous virtual worlds 描述的是恐怖如何作用（机制），而非「为什么令人满足」（原因）；机制 vs 原因不同问，且 P12 的话题是 how，不是 why。

C) ✓ 正确 We learn what it feels like to be truly afraid ↔ learn what fear feels like develop coping strategies ... learn how to handle negative emotion ↔ how to tackle it learn what fear feels like and how to tackle it 用并列结构同时覆盖预判的两层「体验」和「应对」，是原文最完整的同义改写。 D) 答非所问 It activates their evolved fear system and their unique fantasy 是把 P12 机制段的两个核心要素「evolved fear system」与「imagination」拼起来，依旧回答的是「机制」而非「为什么令人满足」。
questions.hint: 回到原文定位题干关键词，比较选项与原文的含义。

questions.prompt: What will one experience if they watch a horror film through without being hurt?

options.text: A strong sense of clear relevance.
A profound sense of good fortune.
A profound sense of intense relief.
A strong sense of being in control.

questions.shortExplanation: If you make it through the film in one piece, you'll probably experience a strong sense of mastery, a sense that you were able to make it through an appalling experience.
questions.detailedExplanation:
【答案】 D （细节题）

【判型】 What will one experience 询问的是一段可被定位的具体心理体验，原文末段以 you'll probably experience 直接给出，按细节题处理。

【拆句】 Q50 主干 What will one experience 是宾语前置的 wh- 疑问；if they watch a horror film through without being hurt 是条件状语从句，through 是副词「自始至终」， without being hurt 是被动动名词作伴随状语；they 指代 one，无指代陷阱。

【定位】 If you make it through the film in one piece, you'll probably experience a strong sense of mastery, a sense that you were able to make it through an appalling experience.

如果你能毫发无损地撑过这部电影，你大概会体验到一种强烈的掌控感——一种自己能挺过令人毛骨悚然之体验的胜任感。

【选项】 A) 偷换概念 A strong sense of clear relevance 摘取原文末句 critically relevant 中 relevant 的衍生形态，把后置的 critically relevant 偷换为 clear relevance；原文是说「处理恐惧的能力未来可能会变得至关重要」，并非「看完后体验到清晰的相关感」。 B) 无中生有 A profound sense of good fortune 描述「幸运感」，原文从未提及；作者强调的是因撑过而获得的胜任感，而非「庆幸自己运气好」。 C) 无中生有 A profound sense of intense relief 描述「释然感」，原文没有任何「relief/放松」语义；mastery 强调的是控场，而非紧张消退。

D) ✓ 正确 a strong sense of mastery↔ A strong sense of being in control a sense that you were able to make it through an appalling experience↔being in control strong sense of 对原文原词，mastery 与 being in control 是同义场最佳对应，D 字面命中预判。

items.title: 2024年12月六级第1套 · 仔细阅读 · 第二篇
items.passage:
An awakening has been taking place in the physical world against the beauty model that has been dictated to us for years. But in the digital arena, social media determines what is considered beautiful.

The two opposing struggles are taking place in parallel. In the physical world, the struggle goes against the underlying pressure exerted on women to conform to an unrealistic beauty ideal. As part of the struggle, various media outlets have presented women whose bodies don't correspond to the so-called ideal. All those women who had previously been excluded from the covers of magazines, television series and the public agenda, have become "legitimate". At the same time, a group of influencers have begun to upload to social media photos of themselves without makeup, and even photos in which they highlight supposed flaws.

Technology has reshaped our beauty ideal and is doing a great job communicating that message to the masses. One of the bizarre legacies of the past decade is the popularity of the "cyborg look", which illustrates what Americans will look like in 2050.

The cyborg look spread rapidly. Today, however, the Instagram face has become the new beauty ideal.

The internalization of accepted beauty norms is much more effective when there is active involvement in the learning process. The active involvement of users is reflected in the gamified(游戏化的 ) interaction offered by the social media platforms—the ability to like, write a comment, compare, share.

Once the desired beauty ideal has been internalized, users are given tools or features to change their appearance to suit the accepted beauty ideal such as editing the image, choosing the ideal filter, the right background.

A survey conducted in the United States revealed that more than 50% filter the images before posting them. And you will not be surprised to hear that the majority of them are women. One of the significant consequences of obsessive filtering is the emerging tendency to treat oneself as an object to be observed and valued, in the same way another person observes and judges from the side.

The effect of the filters is already far beyond amiable amusement. The filters and the entire game played on the networks affect the mental health of the users. According to a study, apps like Instagram, Snapchat and FaceTune allow users to achieve a level of perfection that was previously only observed in beauty magazines.

Even though humanity has always cherished beauty, in the last decade our obsession with looks has reached an unprecedented peak. The time spent on social media creates an urge to achieve an impossible beauty ideal so powerful that the only thing that can fix it is not cosmetic intervention, but mental health care.

questions.prompt: What do we learn about beauty in the digital arena?

options.text: It dictates the taste of digital media.
It has been in the making for years.
It has ushered in a new awakening.
It is defined by social media.

questions.shortExplanation: But in the digital arena, social media determines what is considered beautiful.
questions.detailedExplanation:
【答案】 D （细节题）

【判型】 题干 What do we learn about beauty in the digital arena 是问"关于 X 我们了解到什么",指向原文对 X 的客观陈述。

【拆句】 Q51 是一个简单的 wh-疑问句,主干 What do we learn (about X),about 短语作 learn 的状语,整句无从句、无否定,无理解陷阱。

【定位】 But in the digital arena, social media determines what is considered beautiful.

但在数字领域,是社交媒体决定了什么才被认为是美的。

【选项】 A) 与原文相反 It dictates the taste of digital media 让"美"反过来去 dictate digital media,原文是 social media 在 determine beauty,主客被掉换。

B) 张冠李戴 It has been in the making for years 谈的是"已经酝酿多年",原文只说 dictated to us for years 的是"physical world 的旧美标准",并非 beauty in the digital arena 本身。

C) 张冠李戴 It has ushered in a new awakening 说"数字领域的美开启了新觉醒",但原文 An awakening has been taking place in the physical world 明确把觉醒放在 physical world,而非 digital arena。

D) ✓ 正确 social media determines what is considered beautiful ↔ It is defined by social media It is defined by social media 几乎就是预判句"美由社交媒体决定"的英文被动版,正中定位句 social media determines what is considered beautiful 的核心信息。
questions.hint: 回到原文定位题干关键词，比较选项与原文的含义。

questions.prompt: What does the passage say about beauty in the physical world?

options.text: Women are under constant pressure to keep up with beauty models.
Women are encouraged to pursue a beauty ideal that has never existed.
A fight is going on to remove pressure on women to conform to an absurd beauty ideal.
Media outlets have begun to present as beauty models trendy women without any makeup.

questions.shortExplanation: In the physical world, the struggle goes against the underlying pressure exerted on women to conform to an unrealistic beauty ideal. 在现实世界里,这场斗争所反对的是施加在女性身上、要求她们顺从一种不切实际的美标准的潜在压力。
questions.detailedExplanation:
【答案】 C （细节题）

【判型】 What does the passage say about beauty in the physical world 直接问"文章对 X 怎么说",取的是原文事实陈述。

【拆句】 Q52 主干 What does the passage say (about X),about 短语后置作 say 的状语,无从句、 无否定,理解无障碍。

【定位】 In the physical world, the struggle goes against the underlying pressure exerted on women to conform to an unrealistic beauty ideal. 在现实世界里,这场斗争所反对的是施加在女性身上、要求她们顺从一种不切实际的美标准的潜在压力。

【选项】 A) 与原文相反 Women are under constant pressure to keep up with beauty models 强调女性"持续被施压",方向恰好与原文的"对抗这种压力"相反,文章重点在抗争,而非顺从。

B) 无中生有 Women are encouraged to pursue a beauty ideal that has never existed 中的 encouraged to pursue 在原文找不到对应——原文谈的是被施压,而非被鼓励;"never existed"也并非原文 unrealistic 的等值表达。 C) ✓ 正确 the struggle goes against the underlying pressure exerted on women to conform to an unrealistic beauty ideal

↔ A fight is going on to remove pressure on women to conform to an absurd beauty ideal A fight is going on to remove pressure on women to conform to an absurd beauty ideal 把"正在进行抗争"+"对象是施加在女性身上的、要她们顺从荒谬美标准的压力"两层全保留,正是预判内容。

D) 偷换概念 Media outlets have begun to present as beauty models trendy women without any makeup 把媒体改变形象人选(那些"不符合所谓理想身材"的女性)与 influencers 不化妆自拍混在一起,且原文是 influencers 上传素颜照,不是 media outlets 把"时尚的不化妆女性"包装成 beauty models。
questions.hint: 回到原文定位题干关键词，比较选项与原文的含义。

questions.prompt: What do we learn from the passage about the Instagram face?

options.text: It is now regarded as the new beauty ideal.
It is what most women will go after in 2050.
It is being much talked about on social media.
It is a perfect illustration of the ultimate beauty.

questions.shortExplanation: Today, however, the Instagram face has become the new beauty ideal.
questions.detailedExplanation:
【答案】 A （细节题）

【判型】 What do we learn from the passage about the Instagram face 仍是问对 X 这一具体对象的客观陈述。

【拆句】 Q53 主干 What do we learn (from the passage) (about X),两个介词短语都作状语,无从句、无陷阱。

【定位】 Today, however, the Instagram face has become the new beauty ideal.

然而,如今 Instagram face 已经成为新的美标准。

【选项】 A) ✓ 正确 the Instagram face has become the new beauty ideal ↔

It is now regarded as the new beauty ideal It is now regarded as the new beauty ideal 几乎是定位句的字面同义改写,锁定即可。

B) 张冠李戴 It is what most women will go after in 2050 把"2050"这个时间安在 Instagram face 头上,而 the popularity of the cyborg look, which illustrates what Americans will look like in 2050 里 2050 描述的是 cyborg look,而非 Instagram face。

C) 无中生有 It is being much talked about on social media 加入了"正在被大量讨论"这层意思,原文只说它"成了新美标准",并未提及讨论度。

D) 过度推断 It is a perfect illustration of the ultimate beauty 用 perfect 与 ultimate 两个最高程度词,原文只说 the new beauty ideal,既无"完美"也无"终极"。
questions.hint: 回到原文定位题干关键词，比较选项与原文的含义。

questions.prompt: What has obsessive filtering resulted in?

options.text: A good many women striving to reach an impossible level of perfection.
An urge to turn the entire game played on the network to one's advantage.
A tendency to regard one's body as an object of observation and judgment.
An increasing number of women filtering their images before uploading them.

questions.shortExplanation: One of the significant consequences of obsessive filtering is the emerging tendency to treat oneself as an object to be observed and valued, in the same way another person observes and judges from the side. 过度滤镜化的一个显著后果是,人们正在出现一种倾向:把自己当作一个被观察、被评价的客体,就好像旁人从一旁观察并评判一样。
questions.detailedExplanation:
【答案】 C （细节题）

【判型】 What has obsessive filtering resulted in 问的是某行为带来的具体后果,在原文中必有对应陈述。

【拆句】 Q54 是简单 wh-疑问句,现在完成时 has resulted in 强调动作的延续后果,主语 obsessive filtering 是名词化结构,理解上把它读作"反复地过度滤镜化"即可。

【定位】 One of the significant consequences of obsessive filtering is the emerging tendency to treat oneself as an object to be observed and valued, in the same way another person observes and judges from the side. 过度滤镜化的一个显著后果是,人们正在出现一种倾向:把自己当作一个被观察、被评价的客体,就好像旁人从一旁观察并评判一样。

【选项】 A) 张冠李戴 A good many women striving to reach an impossible level of perfection 中"impossible level of perfection"是 P8 与 P9 关于滤镜带来的整体后果,不是 P7 这句关于 obsessive filtering 的 consequence。

B) 无中生有 An urge to turn the entire game played on the network to one's advantage 的"为己所用"是原文完全没有的概念,只是借用了 the entire game played on the networks 的字面壳。 C) ✓ 正确 the emerging tendency to treat oneself as an object to be observed and valued ↔

A tendency to regard one's body as an object of observation and judgment A tendency to regard one's body as an object of observation and judgment 把"被观察与被评价的客体"这层意思以名词化方式呈现,与预判完全一致。

D) 答非所问 An increasing number of women filtering their images before uploading them 描述的就是 obsessive filtering 这一行为本身(原因),而非 resulted in 所问的后果。
questions.hint: 回到原文定位题干关键词，比较选项与原文的含义。

questions.prompt: What does the author want to emphasize at the end of the passage regarding Americans' obsession with looks?

options.text: Cosmetic surgery should be made more accessible to the masses.
Psychological intervention should be introduced to alleviate it.
Their time spent on social media should be strictly controlled.
Its root cause should be meticulously examined and analyzed.

questions.shortExplanation:
【答案】 B （态度题）

【判型】 What does the author want to emphasize at the end of the passage 关心的是作者"想强调什么",指向作者的主观倾向与建议。

【拆句】 Q55 主干 What does the author want to emphasize,后接 at the end of the passage(位置状语)和 regarding X(关于 X 的话题状语),两段状语只是补充语境,核心动词是 emphasize
questions.detailedExplanation:
【答案】 B （态度题）

【判型】 What does the author want to emphasize at the end of the passage 关心的是作者"想强调什么",指向作者的主观倾向与建议。

【拆句】 Q55 主干 What does the author want to emphasize,后接 at the end of the passage(位置状语)和 regarding X(关于 X 的话题状语),两段状语只是补充语境,核心动词是 emphasize。

【选项】 A) 与原文相反 Cosmetic surgery should be made more accessible to the masses 主张更易获得整容,但原文 not cosmetic intervention 已经明确排除"美容干预"。

B) ✓ 正确 the only thing that can fix it is not cosmetic intervention, but mental health care ↔

Psychological intervention should be introduced to alleviate it cosmetic intervention ↔ Psychological intervention Psychological intervention should be introduced to alleviate it 把作者真正强调的 mental health care 改成同义表达 psychological intervention,正中作者立场。

C) 过度推断 Their time spent on social media should be strictly controlled 提出严格控制使用时间,而原文 The time spent on social media creates an urge… 只把"花在社媒的时间"作为成因列出,并未呼吁去 strictly control 它。

D) 无中生有 Its root cause should be meticulously examined and analyzed 主张"细致检查与分析其根本原因",但原文只给方案(mental health care),并未呼吁去"分析根因"。
questions.hint: 回到原文定位题干关键词，比较选项与原文的含义。

items.title: 2024年12月六级第2套 · 选词填空
items.passage:
Ever been talking about something important with someone you care about and found the discussion frustrating instead of fruitful? Negative energy can then cast a [26] _____ over your efforts to build a shared understanding.

In fact collaborative problem-solving conversations require skills. Strong listening skills are essential. Sprinkling in positivity via appreciation, [27] _____ smiles, and warm comments helps. So does the essential ability to keep your emotional tone in the calm zone. If the tone of a dialogue heats up and anger erupts, the dialogue [28] _____ from collaborative to adversarial, and progress is likely to come to an immediate [29] _____ .

In addition, effective dialogue generally has another important characteristic: symmetry.

Symmetry in dialogue refers to the balance of how much each partner talks. Are you each getting equal airtime? When one participant does most of the talking, this asymmetry or lack of balance tends to

become annoying to one or both of you. The silent partner [30] _____ tires of only listening, while the talker can feel [31] _____ . Usually, both would prefer more equal give and take.

Different rates of speech and levels of voice volume can [32] _____ symmetry as well. The faster or louder partner can easily begin taking up more airtime. The slower-talking or softer-voiced one can have trouble getting the floor.

Conversations also lose balance when one partner's opinions count more than the other's. One person's input may carry more sway because their style of expression is more [33] _____ . One viewpoint may tend to get lost because it is expressed more [34] _____ .

If either partner fairly consistently [35] _____ or evaporates, modifying the pattern will be helpful. The dialogue will feel more productive, and at the same time, the relationship overall is likely to feel more positive.

questions.prompt: Negative energy can then cast a __(26)__ over your efforts to build a shared understanding.
questions.shortExplanation: cast a shadow over——投下阴影的固定隐喻
questions.detailedExplanation:
【答案】 L) shadow 名词

【词性槽】 「cast a ___ over」固定搭配，宾语位 → 名词

【依据】 cast a shadow over——投下阴影的固定隐喻

shadow 与 cast ... over 构成 cast a shadow over（给某事投下阴霾），形象表达 Negative energy（消极情绪）笼罩 efforts to build a shared understanding（构建共识的努力），地道贴切。

【竞争词】 K) scenario cast a scenario 不成话

scenario 表「设想情景」，英语中没有 cast a scenario over 的用法；且消极情绪「投下一个情景」逻辑也不通。
questions.hint: 根据空格前后的词性、搭配与上下文选择词语；每个词最多使用一次。

questions.prompt: Sprinkling in positivity via appreciation, __(27)__ smiles, and warm comments helps.
questions.shortExplanation: 亲切的微笑，与 warm comments 同色
questions.detailedExplanation:
【答案】 A) affectionate 形容词

【词性槽】 并列名词前的修饰位 → 形容词

【依据】 亲切的微笑，与 warm comments 同色

affectionate 意为「亲切、充满感情的」，修饰 smiles 是高频搭配（affectionate smile/look），与并列项 warm comments 共同构成积极正能量信号，正切「Sprinkling in positivity」主旨。

【竞争词】 E) flattered 对象错位：人才会 flattered，微笑本身不会

flattered 描述「（人）受宠若惊的」，修饰 smiles 语义不通——是「人对微笑感到受宠若惊」，而非「flattered smiles」。

H) overburdened 感情色彩相反

overburdened 意为「负担过重的」，是消极色，与「Sprinkling in positivity」整段正向氛围冲突。

O) vigorous 搭配不当：强烈的微笑不地道

vigorous 意为「强有力的、激烈的」，常修饰 exercise/debate，不修饰 smiles；且与温柔的 warm comments 不同色。此处先留作下文 33 题候选。
questions.hint: 根据空格前后的词性、搭配与上下文选择词语；每个词最多使用一次。

questions.prompt: the dialogue __(28)__ from collaborative to adversarial,
questions.shortExplanation: flip from X to Y——突然翻转
questions.detailedExplanation:
【答案】 F) flips 动词

【词性槽】 主句缺谓语，单数主语 → 动词单三

【依据】 flip from X to Y——突然翻转

flips 表「（状态）突然翻转」，正好对应 from collaborative to adversarial（从协作翻成对抗）；与上文 anger erupts（怒气爆发）的「突变」语气吻合。

【竞争词】 C) elapses elapse 只用于「时间流逝」

elapses 仅与 time/hours/days 搭配表「时间过去」，不接 from...to... 表对话「转变」。
