items.title: 2024年12月六级第2套 · 信息匹配
items.passage:
A) Blue moons, rose moons, supermoons. For some reason all the websites seem to think you really want to know all about these moons. "Catch This Weekend's AMAZING SUPERMOON," one headline will announce. "The Supermoon Isn't Actually A Big Deal And You're All Ruining Astronomy," another will complain.

B) The latest example is the super blood wolf moon eclipse which sounds like the name of an emotional song I would have performed a modern dance routine to in 9th grade, but is, in fact, an astronomical event set to occur on January 20. As we'll explain below, there is nothing truly mysterious or otherwise special about this moon, and it will not look like a bloody wolf head in the sky or anything wild like that. We get these super lunar events by smashing together all the qualifiers we've historically used to keep track of full moons throughout the year, and in the age of the internet we can get a little too enthusiastic.

C) Consider this your go-to resource for all moon-gazing news. Here's what you need to know about the latest lunar event.

D) Look, it's okay if you don't know. There are probably loads of folks who walk around pretending they totally know why that thing in the sky seems to get bigger and smaller at regular intervals but who totally do not.

E) The moon orbits Earth, and it's tidally locked—that means it always shows us the same face, instead of spinning around like our planet does. That's why you can always see the man on the moon (or the moon rabbit, depending on your cultural preferences) even as it spins around us. But while the moon is big and bright in the sky when it's full, that's only because it's reflecting light from the sun. But the moon is always moving, so it's getting hit with sunlight at different angles. It's invisible to us during the new moon, because our satellite is parked right between us and the sun; the so-called dark side of the moon is lit up like Las Vegas, but the side we can see is in shadow. A full moon happens when the earth is right between the sun and the moon, so sunlight hits the part we can see. And all the other phases are just the transition from one of those extremes to the other.

F) The moon isn't always exactly the same distance from Earth, because its orbit isn't perfectly circular. We call the closest point perigee(近地点 ), and the most distant point is apogee(远地点). 2018's closest perigee and most distant apogee both happened in January, and the difference was about 30,000 miles.

G) The reason you care about this ordinary change in distance is that it turns a moon super. When a full moon happens close to perigee, it's going to look a bit bigger. Honestly, the difference is not that profound, but if you're in a position to photograph the supermoon next to something that shows the slight increase in scale, it can look pretty cool. January's super blood wolf moon eclipse is super because the date lines up with the closest the moon will get to us during January, but the moon won't actually be at its closest for the year until February's supermoon, which you can expect plenty of undue excitement over.

H) Blood moons only occur during total lunar eclipses (which can happen a few times a year in any given location). When the moon slips through our shadow, we give it a reddish coloring. The moon can also look orange whenever it's rising or setting, or if it hangs low in the horizon all night—the light bouncing off of it has to travel through a thicker atmosphere there, which scatters more blue light away. But you'll probably only see that deep, sinister red during an eclipse.

I) A lot of headlines about moons are just ridiculous (you do not need to be particularly excited about a blue moon, it just looks like a regular full moon), but you should definitely roll out of bed to look at a blood moon if one is going to be visible in your region, even though they're just lunar eclipses and not evidence of bloody battles between the sky gods.

J) In March of 2018, we had our second "blue moon" of the year, to much acclaim. And while that's not necessarily special in an oh-gosh-get-out-and-look-at-it way, it's certainly special: a blue moon is a nickname for when two full moons fall in the same calendar month, and we hadn't previously had two in one year since 1999. We won't have it happen again until 2037. Astronomer David Chapman explained that this is merely a peculiarity of our calendar; once we stopped doing things based on the moon and started trying to follow the sun and the seasons, we stopped having one reliable full moon per month. The moon cycle is 29.53 days long on average, so in most months we still end up with a single new moon and a single full one. But every once in a while, one month steals a full moon from another. In 2018 (and in 1999, and again in 2037) both January and March stacked full moons on the first and last nights of the month, leaving February in the dark.

K) Getting two blue moons a year is rare, but we have individual blue moons every few years. Also, fun fact: not actually blue. A moon can indeed take on a moody blue color, but this only happens when particles of just the right size disperse through the sky—and it has nothing to do with the moon's status as "blue". Big clouds of ash from volcanic eruptions or fires can do the trick, but it doesn't happen often, and the stars would certainly have to align for two such rare instances to occur at once.

L) You may have heard that the super special second blue moon of 2018 was also a Paschal moon. This is true! That just means it was the first full moon of spring, which is often used to determine the date of Easter Sunday. All of this is just calendar nonsense and we refuse to go into it further.

M) Sometimes you'll see a headline that promises a moon with so many qualifiers it makes your head spin. A super blue blood worm moon, perhaps? Or a super blood wolf moon? Lots of websites will tell you that "wolf moon" is the traditional name of the first full moon of the year in "Native American" cultures, which is kind of a weird thing to claim given that there are 573 registered Tribal Nations in the US alone today, not to mention historically. The idea that hungry, howling wolves were such a universal constant in January that all of North America with its different cultures, geographies, and languages spontaneously came up with the same nickname is illogical.

N) Many cultures have traditional names for the full moon in a given month or season, so there's quite a list to draw from if you're trying to really juice up a story on a slightly-bigger-than-average view of the moon. But these are all based on human calendars and activities and folklore; you will not go outside and see a pink moon in April, though I wish it were so.

items.title: 2024年12月六级第2套 · 仔细阅读 · 第一篇
items.passage:
With population increases and global urbanisation ever accelerating, much attention is focused on the sustainability of our cities and scarce attention is paid to the countryside.

Rural life is associated with closely-knit communities, sense of belonging, and a simple, tranquil life. Yet whilst some or all of these elements exist in the countryside, so do conservatism and a lack of employment opportunities. And it is mostly due to the latter that rural communities are suffering. Attracted by the improved economics of urban areas, country-dwellers across the world are moving out, contributing to the excessive crowdedness of densely populated cities, and leaving the countryside in desolation.

So how can the countryside ensure its survival among these changes; or should it at all? Due to both the distance between residences and facilities and often intermittent public transport, those living in the countryside are heavier automobile users. Rural dwellers also use more energy maintaining their mostly detached buildings. We may be piled up like boxes in the city, but this brings energy efficiency that the countryside cannot match. Rural energy requirements result in higher carbon emissions per person than in the city, so it is actually irresponsible to endorse such a lifestyle choice.

Protecting the countryside is a hot topic. Those who have made their fortunes in the city often buy second homes in the countryside, visiting intermittently for a sample of a supposedly simple life. The side-effect of this is that house prices are pushed up due to increased demand, leaving them unaffordable for local people. A solution has yet to be found for this challenge, for market forces are further forcing residents out of the countryside. For those who believe in rural preservation, this is deplorable.

Whilst an idealised view of the countryside is common, the reality is that rural life has continuously evolved. Industrialisation brought an increase in divisions of labour, changing social links between rural people. The internet has introduced once foreign cultures into the countryside. Improved travel connections and affordability have made the world more accessible, creating a "global village". Considering these changes, surely an evolving countryside is inevitable.

Perhaps the countryside should also prepare itself for massive population increases in the future. With cities across the world growing rapidly, how will the current urban generation respond to the inevitable social changes of mass urbanisation? Will the longing for a simpler life become stronger, fueling a rural renaissance?

As the world continues to urbanise, the voices calling for rural preservation may well grow louder. But change is inevitable. We know that the world is going to see new cities emerging from the dust and current cities growing into megacities, but the future of the countryside is less clear.

questions.prompt: What has become of the rural areas nowadays?
questions.shortExplanation: Attracted by the improved economics of urban areas, country-dwellers across the world are moving out, contributing to the excessive crowdedness of densely populated cities, and leaving the countryside in desolation.
questions.detailedExplanation:
【答案】 A （细节题）

【判型】 What has become of the rural areas nowadays? 问的是「现在乡村怎么样了」，要的是客观状态描述，不含 infer/suggest/imply。

【拆句】 What has become of the rural areas nowadays? 是常规疑问句，become of 是固定搭配，意为「（某事物）变成了什么样、下场如何」，整句直译为「乡村现在变成什么样了」，无陷阱。

【定位】 Attracted by the improved economics of urban areas, country-dwellers across the world are moving out, contributing to the excessive crowdedness of densely populated cities, and leaving the countryside in desolation.

受城市改善的经济条件吸引，世界各地的乡村居民正在外迁，加剧了人口稠密城市的过度拥挤，并使乡村陷入荒凉。

【选项】 A) ✓ 正确 leaving the countryside in desolation ↔ They are becoming somewhat deserted. country-dwellers across the world are moving out ↔ They are becoming somewhat deserted. A 把「正在外流→正变得荒凉」浓缩成 becoming somewhat deserted，与预判完全一致；somewhat 还为「程度词」留了余地，避免被「过于绝对」反驳。

B) 与原文相反原文讲的是 contributing to the excessive crowdedness of densely populated cities ——人去了城市，乡村反而空了；选项 They are being increasingly urbanised. 却说乡村正被「城市化」，方向完全相反。

C) 张冠李戴 Rural life is associated with closely-knit communities 说的是乡村生活「被联想为」 紧密社区，是一种「印象」，并非 nowadays 的现实；选项 They are closely-knit communities. 把印象当现状。

D) 以偏概全 so do conservatism and a lack of employment opportunities 把 conservatism 与 「就业不足」并列为问题，原文紧接着说 And it is mostly due to the latter that rural communities are suffering——主因是后者（就业），并非保守主义；D 把次要因素夸大为现状。
questions.hint: 回到原文定位题干关键词，比较选项与原文的含义。

questions.prompt: What does the author think of the rural lifestyle?

options.text: It is unlikely to survive given the on-going changes.
It is less energy-efficient compared to that in cities.
It is highly dependent upon heavy automobiles.
It is a choice more affluent people will endorse.

questions.shortExplanation: We may be piled up like boxes in the city, but this brings energy efficiency that the countryside cannot match. Rural energy requirements result in higher carbon emissions per person than in the city, so it is actually irresponsible to endorse such a lifestyle choice.
questions.detailedExplanation:
【答案】 B （细节题）

【判型】 What does the author think of the rural lifestyle? 问作者对乡村生活方式的明确观点， 答案是原文直接写出的评价，并未要求做逻辑推断。

【拆句】 What does the author think of the rural lifestyle? 是固定句型，think of=「对……的看法」；直译「作者怎么看乡村生活方式」，无陷阱。

【定位】 We may be piled up like boxes in the city, but this brings energy efficiency that the countryside cannot match. Rural energy requirements result in higher carbon emissions per person than in the city, so it is actually irresponsible to endorse such a lifestyle choice.

我们在城市里也许像盒子一样堆在一起，但这带来了乡村无法企及的能效。乡村的能耗导致人均碳排比城市更高，因此推崇这种生活方式实际上是不负责任的。

【选项】 A) 答非所问 P3 评价乡村生活方式不可取，但并未说它「无法存活」；It is unlikely to survive given the on-going changes. 借用了 how can the countryside ensure its survival 里的 survival，却把「能否生存」的话题误植到「作者对生活方式的判断」上。 B) ✓ 正确 this brings energy efficiency that the countryside cannot match ↔

It is less energy-efficient compared to that in cities. higher carbon emissions per person than in the city ↔

It is less energy-efficient compared to that in cities. 整段评价的核心证据就是「乡村能效低、碳排高」，B 一字不差地复述了这层比较关系，且严格限定在「能效」维度，与预判一致。

C) 偷换概念 those living in the countryside are heavier automobile users 说的是「乡村人是更重度的汽车使用者」（使用频率/比例更高），选项 It is highly dependent upon heavy automobiles. 把 heavier 移植到 automobiles 之前，变成「依赖重型汽车」， 偷换了 heavier 的修饰对象。 D) 与原文相反原文 it is actually irresponsible to endorse such a lifestyle choice 直接评价「推崇这种生活方式是不负责任的」，作者持反对态度；选项 It is a choice more affluent people will endorse. 不仅没指出作者的反对，反而把「有钱人会推崇」当成结论。
questions.hint: 回到原文定位题干关键词，比较选项与原文的含义。

questions.prompt: What does the author think of rich urban residents buying a second home in the countryside?

options.text: It is bound to mar the traditional rural life.
It adversely impacts rural social stability.
It is detrimental to rural preservation.

questions.shortExplanation: A solution has yet to be found for this challenge, for market forces are further forcing residents out of the countryside. For those who believe in rural preservation, this is deplorable.
questions.detailedExplanation:
【答案】 D （细节题）

【判型】 What does the author think of rich urban residents buying a second home in the countryside? 问的是作者对这一具体行为的明确评价，答案出现在原文同一段的总结句。

【拆句】 rich urban residents buying a second home in the countryside 中 buying 是现在分词作 residents 的后置定语，相当于「买第二套乡村房的城市富人」；定语稍长但不绕。

【定位】 A solution has yet to be found for this challenge, for market forces are further forcing residents out of the countryside. For those who believe in rural preservation, this is deplorable.

这一难题尚无解决方案，因为市场力量正在进一步把居民赶出乡村。对那些信奉乡村保护的人而言，这是令人痛心的。

【选项】 A) 无中生有 P4 谈的是房价与本地居民问题，并未提及 traditional rural life 是否被破坏；考生易把第二段提到的「亲密社区/简单生活」的传统印象嫁接到此，但原文未在 P4 谈这一面。

B) 偷换概念原文 house prices are pushed up... leaving them unaffordable for local people 谈的是房价与可负担性，并未谈 rural social stability；选项把经济层面问题升格成「社会稳定」这种更大的范畴。 C) 无中生有 P4 谈的是市场力量与房价，并未提及 rural economies' revitalisation；revitalisation 这一话题在 P6 rural renaissance 处才隐约出现，与 P4 的论点无关。

D) ✓ 正确 For those who believe in rural preservation, this is deplorable ↔

It is detrimental to rural preservation. leaving them unaffordable for local people ↔ It is detrimental to rural preservation. 原文连续给出「房价上涨→本地人买不起→市场力量进一步驱赶居民→对乡村保护者而言可悲」四步推理，落脚点正是「对乡村保护不利」；D 既保留了评价的负面性，又精准落到 preservation 这个对象上。
questions.hint: 回到原文定位题干关键词，比较选项与原文的含义。

questions.prompt: What do we learn about the countryside with industrialisation and technological advances?

options.text: It is destined to change gradually.
It will present an idealised way of life.
It is likely to embrace foreign cultures.

questions.shortExplanation: Whilst an idealised view of the countryside is common, the reality is that rural life has continuously evolved. Industrialisation brought an increase in divisions of labour, changing social links between rural people. The internet has introduced once foreign cultures into the countryside. Improved travel connections and affordability have made the world more accessible, creating a "global village". Considering these changes, surely an evolving countryside is inevitable.
questions.detailedExplanation:
【答案】 A （细节题）

【判型】 What do we learn about the countryside with industrialisation and technological advances? 问从文中得知什么，答案直接来自原文表述，不要求二步推断。

【拆句】 the countryside with industrialisation and technological advances 中 with 引出伴随状语，意为「在工业化与技术进步的影响下」，with 短语作 countryside 的后置修饰，整句直译「在工业化与技术进步下，我们对乡村得知什么」。

【定位】 Whilst an idealised view of the countryside is common, the reality is that rural life has continuously evolved. Industrialisation brought an increase in divisions of labour, changing social links between rural people. The internet has introduced once foreign cultures into the countryside. Improved travel connections and affordability have made the world more accessible, creating a "global village". Considering these changes, surely an evolving countryside is inevitable.

尽管对乡村理想化的印象很常见，现实却是乡村生活一直在持续演变。工业化带来分工增加，改变了乡村人之间的社会联系。互联网把曾经陌生的文化带进了乡村。交通改善与可承受让世界更触手可及，造就了「地球村」。鉴于这些变化，乡村必然在演变之中。

【选项】 A) ✓ 正确 surely an evolving countryside is inevitable ↔ It is destined to change gradually. rural life has continuously evolved ↔ It is destined to change gradually. P5 段尾既明示必然性（inevitable）又通过 continuously evolved 暗示渐进性，A 把这两层语义都包含进 destined to change gradually，与预判完全一致。 B) 与原文相反原文 Whilst an idealised view of the countryside is common, the reality is that rural life has continuously evolved 用 whilst 让步、the reality is 转折，明确把「理想化乡村」当成被否定的印象；选项 It will present an idealised way of life. 反把它说成将要呈现的现实。

C) 以偏概全 The internet has introduced once foreign cultures into the countryside 只是段中三件平行例证之一，与「分工」「全球村」共同支撑「乡村必然演变」这一论点；选项 It is likely to embrace foreign cultures. 把单一例子当成结论。 D) 过度推断 creating a "global village" 强调「世界更可及、变成地球村」，并不等于乡村会「越来越多元化」；选项 It will become increasingly diversified. 在「多文化进入」之上多走一步，推出 diversified 这个原文未说的结论。

questions.prompt: What does the author think of the future of the countryside compared with cities?

options.text: It is going to be harder for the locals.
It is going to resemble that of cities.
It is less likely to stay static.
It is less easy to envisage.

questions.shortExplanation: We know that the world is going to see new cities emerging from the dust and current cities growing into megacities, but the future of the countryside is less clear. 我们知道，世界将看到新城从尘土中崛起、现有城市发展为超大型城市，但乡村的未来则不那么清晰。
questions.detailedExplanation:
【答案】 D （细节题）

【判型】 What does the author think of the future of the countryside compared with cities? 问作者对未来的对比判断，原文末段直接给出明示对比，不需推断。

【拆句】 What does the author think of the future of the countryside compared with cities? 中 compared with cities 是过去分词短语作 future 的后置定语，意为「与城市相比的乡村的未来」；句子结构稍长但语义直白。

【定位】 We know that the world is going to see new cities emerging from the dust and current cities growing into megacities, but the future of the countryside is less clear. 我们知道，世界将看到新城从尘土中崛起、现有城市发展为超大型城市，但乡村的未来则不那么清晰。

【选项】 A) 无中生有 P7 未提及 harder for the locals；本地人变难的话题在 P4 leaving them unaffordable for local people 出现过，但与「未来对比」无关；选项把跨段细节挪过来冒充末段对比的结论。

B) 与原文相反原文 but the future of the countryside is less clear 把乡村未来与城市未来拉开差距；选项 It is going to resemble that of cities. 反说「乡村未来会像城市的未来」，把对比关系反转为类似关系。 C) 答非所问 But change is inevitable 谈的是变化必然，It is less likely to stay static. 复述这一变化必然性；但本题问的是「乡村未来与城市未来相比」这一对比维度，C 答的是「乡村是否会变」的另一维度。 D) ✓ 正确 but the future of the countryside is less clear↔It is less easy to envisage. We know that the world is going to see new cities emerging from the dust and current cities growing into megacities

↔ It is less easy to envisage. 对比型细节题正确项必须同时保留比较关系与比较内容；D 既保留 less，又把 clear 同义置换为 easy to envisage，与预判完全契合。

items.title: 2024年12月六级第2套 · 仔细阅读 · 第二篇
items.passage:
Statements, like "beauty is in the eye of the beholder( 观看者 )", are rarely questioned. They've become so embedded in our consciousness that people think it's absurd to think otherwise. It might be useful, however, to at least push back on this assumption because people evaluate environment, situations, and people aesthetically. We may find that we still believe it is correct, but we may also find that there is a lot more to the situation than you suppose.

A recent study exploring aesthetic taste was published in Cognition. The results from this study show that people agree very much in their aesthetic evaluation of natural objects, but they disagree more about artifacts, or human-made objects.

The study found that shared taste was most common for faces and natural landscapes, but least common among works of architecture and art. The hypothesis is the commonly pleasing features, like proportion or symmetry, are at work.

Preferences for natural scenes might be learned through life experiences. Factors like habitability, safety, and openness might be preferred as people develop. Some of the details of landscapes change, but the basics are more common, e.g., water, open spaces, and signs of care.

Art and architecture, unlike natural spaces, do not have the same level of exposure. So, people do not have the same level of shared taste.

It's possible that the lower amount of agreement in the shared taste of artifacts has to do more with elements of style, rather than "behavioral consequences".

All of the consequences seem reasonable (or at least possible), but I think there might be an interesting philosophical conclusion that they did not draw. It seems that there is an objective ground to our aesthetic preferences or evaluations. I am not saying this would mean beauty is completely objective, just that there could possibly be general objective principles at work, i.e., beauty is not simply in the eye of the beholder.

Nature exhibits some of the universal aesthetic features, such as radiance, in a common way throughout the world. It's not exactly the same everywhere, but it is common. For example, a sunset is similar enough in different places to warrant almost universal appeal.

Possible universal principles of beauty—such as proportion, fittingness, radiance, and others—are general categories, which allow for a wide array of embodiments. When people get involved in making artifacts in architecture or art, they apply these very general concepts in unique ways. But the way they applied the principle may not have universal appeal.

This is why it's important to experience diverse cultures and their artifacts because it opens us up to different ways of approaching or constructing beauty. And it is always good to question our assumptions.

questions.prompt: What does the passage say about the statement "beauty is in the eye of the beholder"?

options.text: It has hardly ever been disputed.
Many people have found it absurd.
People have long been misled by it.

questions.shortExplanation: Statements, like "beauty is in the eye of the beholder(观看者 )", are rarely questioned. 诸如「美在观看者的眼中」这样的说法，几乎从不受到质疑。
questions.detailedExplanation:
【答案】 A （细节题）

【判型】 题干 What does the passage say about the statement 把范围圈死在那句引语上，要求复述作者对它的具体描述，不是推断也不是主旨。

【拆句】 What does the passage say about the statement "beauty is in the eye of the beholder"? 主干是 What does the passage say about X，X = the statement "beauty is in the eye of the beholder"；structure 平铺直叙，无陷阱。

【定位】 Statements, like "beauty is in the eye of the beholder(观看者 )", are rarely questioned. 诸如「美在观看者的眼中」这样的说法，几乎从不受到质疑。

【选项】 A) ✓ 正确 rarely questioned ↔ hardly ever been disputed 预判「几乎无人质疑」与 hardly ever been disputed 在频率与语义上完全等值，锁定 A。 B) 偷换概念 It can be interpreted aesthetically 说「它可被审美地解读」，与原文 rarely questioned 完全无关；作者只说「无人质疑」，没说「可被审美解读」。

C) 与原文相反原文说「人们觉得 absurd to think otherwise」（反着想才荒谬），而 Many people have found it absurd 把「荒谬」直接扣给那句谚语本身，正话反说。

D) 无中生有 People have long been misled by it 说「人们长期被它误导」，原文只说作者「想 push back 一下」，并未给该谚语贴「误导」标签。
questions.hint: 回到原文定位题干关键词，比较选项与原文的含义。

questions.prompt: What does a recent study exploring aesthetic taste show?

options.text: Aesthetic tastes tend to differ from person to person.
Natural beauty is rarely surpassed by artificial beauty.
There is less consensus on objects shaped by human craft.
There is general agreement on what is pleasing to the eye.

questions.shortExplanation: The results from this study show that people agree very much in their aesthetic evaluation of natural objects, but they disagree more about artifacts, or human-made objects.
questions.detailedExplanation:
【答案】 C （细节题）

【判型】 What does a recent study exploring aesthetic taste show 问的是一项具体研究 show 出什么——属于事实复述。

【拆句】 What does a recent study exploring aesthetic taste show? 主干是 What does a study show；exploring aesthetic taste 是 study 的现在分词后置定语，作用是限定哪项研究。 结构清晰，无陷阱。

【定位】 The results from this study show that people agree very much in their aesthetic evaluation of natural objects, but they disagree more about artifacts, or human-made objects.

这项研究的结果显示，人们对自然物的审美评价高度一致，但对人造物（即人工制造的物品）则分歧更多。

【选项】 A) 以偏概全 Aesthetic tastes tend to differ from person to person 把原文「人造物上分歧」扩大成「审美口味本来就因人而异」，丢掉了原文「自然物上一致」这一半。

B) 偷换概念 Natural beauty is rarely surpassed by artificial beauty 把研究讲成「自然美几乎不被人造美超越」，原文谈的是「评价一致性」，不是「美的优劣比较」。

C) ✓ 正确 they disagree more about artifacts, or human-made objects ↔

less consensus on objects shaped by human craft 预判要求选项聚焦「人造物上分歧更多」，less consensus on objects shaped by human craft 完整对应该语义，锁 C。 D) 以偏概全 There is general agreement on what is pleasing to the eye 只说「人们对什么好看普遍一致」，丢掉了原文「对人造物分歧更多」这关键一半，与研究的对比结论不符。
questions.hint: 回到原文定位题干关键词，比较选项与原文的含义。

questions.prompt: Why do people differ in their aesthetic appraisal of artifacts?

options.text: They come out in a great variety of designs.
They lead to varying behavioral consequences.
They take up much less natural space than landscapes.
They come into people's view less often than natural spaces.

questions.shortExplanation:
【答案】 D （细节题）

【判型】 Why do people differ in their aesthetic appraisal of artifacts 问的是一项已写明的具体原因，不是让你推断作者的言外之意。

【拆句】 Why do people differ in their aesthetic appraisal of artifacts? 一般疑问句结构 Why do
questions.detailedExplanation:
【答案】 D （细节题）

【判型】 Why do people differ in their aesthetic appraisal of artifacts 问的是一项已写明的具体原因，不是让你推断作者的言外之意。

【拆句】 Why do people differ in their aesthetic appraisal of artifacts? 一般疑问句结构 Why do
questions.hint: 回到原文定位题干关键词，比较选项与原文的含义。

questions.prompt: What does the example of sunset tell about nature?

options.text: It creates a powerful appeal through its brilliant radiance.
It displays aesthetic traits in a similar way the world over.
It embodies beauty with a wide array of aesthetic features.
It establishes the principles of beauty in a number of ways.

questions.shortExplanation: Nature exhibits some of the universal aesthetic features, such as radiance, in a common way throughout the world. It's not exactly the same everywhere, but it is common. For example, a sunset is similar enough in different places to warrant almost universal appeal.
questions.detailedExplanation:
【答案】 B （例证目的题）

【判型】 What does the example of sunset tell about nature 问的是举这个例子是为了告诉读者关于 nature 的什么——典型的「例证目的」考法。

【拆句】 What does the example of sunset tell about nature? 主干 What does X tell about Y； tell 在此处意为 reveal / indicate（说明、揭示），不要按字面理解为「告诉某人某事」。

【定位】 Nature exhibits some of the universal aesthetic features, such as radiance, in a common way throughout the world. It's not exactly the same everywhere, but it is common. For example, a sunset is similar enough in different places to warrant almost universal appeal.

自然界以共通的方式在世界各地呈现某些普遍的审美特征（比如光辉）。各处并不完全相同，但确实有共通之处。例如，落日在不同地方足够相似，因而几乎能引起普世的吸引力。

【选项】 A) 答非所问 It creates a powerful appeal through its brilliant radiance 谈的是「落日靠光辉本身创造强烈吸引力」，是 sunset 例子的表层描写，不是例子要说明的论点（共通性）。 B) ✓ 正确 Nature exhibits some of the universal aesthetic features, such as radiance, in a common way throughout the world

↔ It displays aesthetic traits in a similar way the world over 预判要求「自然在全球以共通方式呈现审美特征」，It displays aesthetic traits in a similar way the world over 与论点句逐项匹配，锁 B。

C) 张冠李戴 It embodies beauty with a wide array of aesthetic features 借用 a wide array of embodiments 与 Possible universal principles of beauty 的短语，但 P9 谈的是「美的原则允许多样体现」，不是 sunset 例子要说明的内容。 D) 过度推断 It establishes the principles of beauty in a number of ways 把「sunset 例证一种共通呈现方式」夸大成「确立了多个美学原则」，原文从未把 sunset 提到「确立原则」的高度。
questions.hint: 回到原文定位题干关键词，比较选项与原文的含义。

questions.prompt: Why do artifacts not always hold universal appeal?

options.text: The appreciation of their beauty is not subject to objective standards.
The universal principle of beauty prevents a wide array of embodiments.
The way their creators apply the principle of beauty may not be pleasing to everybody.
Their creators interpret the universal principle of beauty each in their preferred way.

questions.shortExplanation: When people get involved in making artifacts in architecture or art, they apply these very general concepts in unique ways. But the way they applied the principle may not have universal appeal.
questions.detailedExplanation:
【答案】 C （细节题）

【判型】 Why do artifacts not always hold universal appeal 仍是对已写明原因的复述问法，作者已经直接写出「为什么」，不是推断。

【拆句】 Why do artifacts not always hold universal appeal? 否定副词 not always 表示「并非总是」（部分否定），不是「从来不」；不要错读成 never。

【定位】 When people get involved in making artifacts in architecture or art, they apply these very general concepts in unique ways. But the way they applied the principle may not have universal appeal.

当人们投身于建筑或艺术中的人造物创作时，他们以独特的方式运用这些非常宽泛的概念。 但他们运用原则的方式未必能引起所有人的共鸣。

【选项】 A) 与原文相反 The appreciation of their beauty is not subject to objective standards 说「人造物之美不受客观标准约束」，但作者在 P7 与 P9 都坚持存在 objective ground / Possible universal principles of beauty，A 与作者立场相反。

B) 与原文相反 The universal principle of beauty prevents a wide array of embodiments 说原则 「阻止」多样体现，原文恰恰说 are general categories, which allow for a wide array of embodiments——「允许」多样体现。 C) ✓ 正确 the way they applied the principle may not have universal appeal ↔

The way their creators apply the principle of beauty may not be pleasing to everybody 「运用方式」+「未必人人喜欢」两个语义落点在 The way their creators apply the principle of beauty may not be pleasing to everybody 都得到对应，锁 C。

D) 以偏概全 Their creators interpret the universal principle of beauty each in their preferred way 只说「创作者各自按偏好诠释原则」，并未传达「未必人人喜欢」这层「为何没有普遍吸引力」的因果；它只复述了 they apply these very general concepts in unique ways 的前半段，丢掉了 But 之后的关键否定。
questions.hint: 回到原文定位题干关键词，比较选项与原文的含义。

items.title: 2024年12月六级第3套 · 选词填空
items.passage:
About 23% of the global population lives in absolute poverty. In developing countries there is a low life expectancy, a high infant [26] _____ rate, high levels of unemployment and illiteracy, nutritional levels below acceptable standards and widespread disease with very little or poor quality medical assistance. Others live [27] _____ wealthy and luxurious lives and so the wealth is distributed in a very [28] _____ manner. These are the central problems to questions of charity though charity also includes many other areas such as assisting the elderly.

We all [29] _____ when very rich people pledge to give away most of their billions, but they are usually left with millions to pass on, still much more than most people would expect to earn in their lifetime. Even comparatively [30] _____ salaries in the west are very high when compared globally. Someone on £ 20,000 could easily afford to give away £ 2,000 per year and still have plenty to live on plus some luxuries.

Most people agree that giving to charity is morally [31] _____ but charitable behaviour tends to be regarded as above and beyond the call of duty. Some argue, however, that charitable behaviour is

morally required. This means that to fail to behave charitably would be wrong. The majority of arguments in this vein refer to giving aid to poorer nations but they may also refer to giving time within one's [32] _____ community. Arguments tend to place different requirements on people in different income brackets and [33] _____ entirely people who are merely making ends meet. Some argue that people should all contribute a certain percentage of their earnings. I will [34] _____ together all those arguments that place a moral requirement on people to give to charity, despite the fact that there is wide disagreement as to the [35] _____ of that moral requirement.

questions.prompt: a high infant __(26)__ rate
questions.shortExplanation: 高频固定搭配——婴儿死亡率
questions.detailedExplanation:
【答案】 J) mortality 名词

【词性槽】 形容词后的名词中心词

【依据】 高频固定搭配——婴儿死亡率

infant mortality rate 是描述发展中国家健康指标的标准术语，意为'婴儿死亡率'。它与前文a low life expectancy（低预期寿命）并列，共同刻画发展中国家的医疗卫生困境，语义完全自洽。

【竞争词】 B) casualty casualty 主指事故伤亡，不与 rate 常配

casualty 多用于战争/事故场景（如交通事故伤亡），与婴儿在出生/成长阶段的死亡话题不匹配；且 infant casualty rate 不是固定术语，正确的固定术语是 infant mortality rate。
questions.hint: 根据空格前后的词性、搭配与上下文选择词语；每个词最多使用一次。

questions.prompt: Others live __(27)__ wealthy and luxurious lives
questions.shortExplanation: 修饰程度——极其富裕奢华
questions.detailedExplanation:
【答案】 H) incredibly 副词

【词性槽】 修饰形容词的空——副词

【依据】 修饰程度——极其富裕奢华

上下文要表达富人'极其富裕奢华'的生活，与下句still much more than most people would expect to earn in their lifetime的'远超普通人想象'相呼应，需要一个程度副词来强化形容词，incredibly（极其、难以置信地）正是程度修饰。

【竞争词】 N) sceptically态度副词不可修饰程度

sceptically 表'怀疑地'，是表说话/看待事物的态度副词，无法修饰 wealthy/luxurious 这种性质形容词；说'怀疑地富有'语义不通。
questions.hint: 根据空格前后的词性、搭配与上下文选择词语；每个词最多使用一次。

questions.prompt: so the wealth is distributed in a very __(28)__ manner
questions.shortExplanation: 贫富悬殊——不平等的分配方式
questions.detailedExplanation:
【答案】 O) unequal 形容词

【词性槽】 限定词 a + 空 + 名词 manner——形容词

【依据】 贫富悬殊——不平等的分配方式

前文About 23% of the global population lives in absolute poverty.与本句Others live __(27)__ wealthy and luxurious lives共同刻画极端贫富对比，得出'财富分配极不平等'的结论；unequal'不平等的'最直接命中此语义。

【竞争词】 F) hierarchical义近但侧重'等级'而非'不均'

hierarchical 强调按层级/等级排列，描述组织结构（如公司、社会阶层）；财富'分配方式'用'等级制的'不如'不平等的'贴切，且本段语境强调'贫富两极'而非'层级'。

G) immediate '立刻的'与分配方式不搭

immediate 表'立刻、直接'，与财富分配的'公平/不公平'话题无关，搭配 manner 也不形成有意义短语。

I) moderate 感情色彩反向

moderate 表'适中、温和'，与上文'富人极奢、穷人绝对贫困'的强烈对比语义相反，方向错误。

K) overt 强调'公开/明显'而非'不公'

overt 只表示是否公开，不评价分配公正与否；语义与贫富悬殊话题不对齐。

【易错】 最具迷惑性的错误词是 F) —— hierarchical 蒙混'分层分配'。看到wealth is distributed in a very __(28)__ manner很容易因为'分配'联想到'层级'而选hierarchical。防坑：看上一句的对比方向——'极穷 vs 极富'要的是'不公平'，是 unequal，不是描述层级结构的 hierarchical。
questions.hint: 根据空格前后的词性、搭配与上下文选择词语；每个词最多使用一次。

questions.prompt: We all __(29)__ when very rich people pledge to give away most of their billions
questions.shortExplanation: 对捐赠之举的正向反应——称赞
questions.detailedExplanation:
【答案】 A) applaud 动词

【词性槽】 主语后缺谓语——动词

【依据】 对捐赠之举的正向反应——称赞

上下文是'当富豪承诺捐出大部分财产时，我们都会 ___'，普通人对慷慨捐赠的自然反应是赞许；下半句but they are usually left with millions to pass on用 but 转折，暗示前半句是正面态度，applaud（称赞、鼓掌）恰好提供这种正面反应。

【竞争词】 C) exclude及物动词缺宾语且语义不符

exclude 意为'排除'，需要宾语（exclude sb./sth.），本空后直接接 when 从句没有宾语；且'我们排除（什么）当富人捐款时'语义完全不通。

E) group 动词义不搭对象

group 作动词表'归类、聚集'，同样需要宾语，且'我们归类当富人捐款时'语义荒谬，与上下文的'反应'语义不契合。

M) probe 调查义与情感反应不符

probe 意为'探查、深入调查'，常用于侦查/科研语境；这里要表达普通人对富豪行为的即时情绪反应，不需要也不可能是'调查'。
questions.hint: 根据空格前后的词性、搭配与上下文选择词语；每个词最多使用一次。

questions.prompt: Even comparatively __(30)__ salaries in the west are very high when compared globally.
questions.shortExplanation: 相对中等的工资仍属全球高位
questions.detailedExplanation:
【答案】 I) moderate 形容词

【词性槽】 comparatively + 空 + 名词 salaries——形容词

【依据】 相对中等的工资仍属全球高位

本句逻辑是'即使西方相对___的工资全球比较仍很高'，用 even 让步：空位的形容词应表'不算高、中等'的程度。moderate 表'适中、中等'恰好与后面 are very high when compared globally 的让步形成对照——西方人觉得普通，全球看仍高。

【竞争词】 F) hierarchical'等级制的'不评价工资高低

hierarchical 形容结构，不形容工资数额，与'相对'这个程度副词也搭不上。

G) immediate '即时/直接的'不评价工资数额

immediate 描述时间或空间近距离，与工资数额的高低无关；'相对即时的工资'语义不通。

K) overt'公开的'非数额评价词

overt 强调'公开/明显'，与工资'高低/多少'话题无关。

【易错】 最具迷惑性的错误词是 F) —— 把 even 让步读反。Even comparatively __(30)__ salaries in the west are very high里 even 是让步：'即使相对___的工资也很高'。读快了容易往'高'方向选词，从而被hierarchical或别的形容词迷惑。防坑：even ... still/very + 强 → 前面是弱（中等/适中），选moderate。
questions.hint: 根据空格前后的词性、搭配与上下文选择词语；每个词最多使用一次。

questions.prompt: Most people agree that giving to charity is morally __(31)__
questions.shortExplanation: 道德褒义——值得称赞
questions.detailedExplanation:
【答案】 L) praiseworthy 形容词

【词性槽】 系动词 is + morally + 空——形容词作表语

【依据】 道德褒义——值得称赞

morally praiseworthy 意为'道德上值得称赞'，正好对应'多数人认为捐款值得称许'。下文 but 转折说charitable behaviour tends to be regarded as above and beyond the call of duty（被视为超出本分），这种'分外的善举'恰是 praiseworthy 而非 required。

【竞争词】 F) hierarchical'等级制的'与道德评价不挂钩

hierarchical 描述结构等级，无法被 morally 修饰，'道德上等级制'语义不通。

G) immediate '立刻的'与道德评价不在同一维度

immediate 表时间/空间近，不是道德褒贬词，'道德上立刻的'语义不成立。

I) moderate '适中的'非道德评价词

moderate 描述程度适中，与'值得称赞'相去甚远，不构成对慈善的道德评价。

K) overt '公开的'非道德属性

overt 强调'公开、明显'，无道德褒贬色彩，'道德上公开'不通。

O) unequal '不平等的'反向语义

unequal 是负面评价词，且通常修饰资源/机会分布；评价捐款本身'道德不平等'语义不通且方向相反。
questions.hint: 根据空格前后的词性、搭配与上下文选择词语；每个词最多使用一次。

questions.prompt: they may also refer to giving time within one's __(32)__ community
questions.shortExplanation: 固定搭配——身边/直系的社区 immediate community 是常见搭配，意为'身边的、直接所在的社区'，与上文giving aid to poorer nations（对外远方的援助）相对，构成'远（poorer nations）vs 近 （immediate community）'的对照。immediate 在这里取'紧邻、直接的'义。
questions.detailedExplanation:
【答案】 G) immediate 形容词

【词性槽】 形容词性物主代词 one's + 空 + 名词 community——形容词作定语

【依据】 固定搭配——身边/直系的社区 immediate community 是常见搭配，意为'身边的、直接所在的社区'，与上文giving aid to poorer nations（对外远方的援助）相对，构成'远（poorer nations）vs 近 （immediate community）'的对照。immediate 在这里取'紧邻、直接的'义。

【竞争词】 F) hierarchical等级制的社区与捐时间无关

hierarchical community 强调社区按等级排列，与'在身边社区内贡献时间'毫无关联，方向跑偏。

K) overt '公开的社区'语义空洞

overt community 不是常见搭配，'公开的社区'也不切合'就近行善'的语境；命题点是远近对照，不是公开与否。
questions.hint: 根据空格前后的词性、搭配与上下文选择词语；每个词最多使用一次。

questions.prompt: Arguments tend to place different requirements on people in different income brackets and __(33)__ entirely people who are merely making ends meet.
questions.shortExplanation: 把'仅能维持生计者'整体排除在外句意是'各种论点对不同收入档提出不同要求，并把仅能维持生计的人完全 ___'。entirely （完全地）+ people who are merely making ends meet（仅能维持生计的人）暗示这一群人被'排除'在道德要求之外——经济上自顾不暇，自然不被要求捐款。exclude entirely 是常见搭配。
questions.detailedExplanation:
【答案】 C) exclude 动词

【词性槽】 并列连词 and 后缺谓语——动词

【依据】 把'仅能维持生计者'整体排除在外句意是'各种论点对不同收入档提出不同要求，并把仅能维持生计的人完全 ___'。entirely （完全地）+ people who are merely making ends meet（仅能维持生计的人）暗示这一群人被'排除'在道德要求之外——经济上自顾不暇，自然不被要求捐款。exclude entirely 是常见搭配。

【竞争词】 E) group '归类'与 entirely 矛盾

group 作动词表'把……归为一类'，但'完全地归类他们'语义不通，且对'仅能维持生计的人'怎么归类与整句逻辑（区别对待不同收入者）不对接。

M) probe '调查'与道德要求语境无关

probe 是'探查、调查'，与本段讨论'谁该被要求捐款'的道德分配话题无关；'完全调查他们'也不构成与前句的逻辑延伸。
questions.hint: 根据空格前后的词性、搭配与上下文选择词语；每个词最多使用一次。

questions.prompt: I will __(34)__ together all those arguments that place a moral requirement on people to give to charity
questions.shortExplanation: 把众多论点'归在一起'——group together group together 是固定搭配，意为'把……归为一组、合在一起'。本句意为'我将把所有把道德要求加在人们头上的论点归为一组'，对应作者要做的概括综合工作。与上文'尽管在程度上分歧很大'呼应：先归类再综合讨论。
questions.detailedExplanation:
【答案】 E) group 动词

【词性槽】 情态动词 will + 空——动词原形

【依据】 把众多论点'归在一起'——group together group together 是固定搭配，意为'把……归为一组、合在一起'。本句意为'我将把所有把道德要求加在人们头上的论点归为一组'，对应作者要做的概括综合工作。与上文'尽管在程度上分歧很大'呼应：先归类再综合讨论。

【竞争词】 M) probe probe 与 together 不形成固定搭配

probe together 不是常见搭配；probe 多用于'深入调查（具体事件）'，与'把多种论点归在一起综合讨论'语义不合。

items.passage:
A) Trade is one of the policy areas where the hostility that exists between populists(⺠粹主义者 ) and classical liberals is most visible. Free-traders point to the undeniable good that tariff-free trade has done for consumers across the world and to the observable alleviation of poverty in corners of the world where previously closed markets have been opened up. Protectionists point to the domestic producers who've paid the price for this globalized economy in the form of lost livelihoods and hollowed-out communities.

B) The ongoing conservative civil war often degenerates into content-free tribal warfare, but trade is a rare exception. There are substantial, thought-out policy proposals on both sides of the argument.

C) Consequently, trade as a topic of discussion provides an opportunity for liberals and populists to have a real meeting of minds. Fruitful debates might actually take place in this area, as opposed to the familiar ritual we've become accustomed to of condemnation met with counter-condemnation.

D) Strange as it might sound, the problem with trade in the modern world isn't a matter of dollars and cents. It's a matter of false consciousness. This observation is bound to set Marxist alarm bells ringing in the minds of some readers, but it was first made by Alexis de Tocqueville in 1840.

E) Tracking the economic development of mankind from primitive to modern societies, Tocqueville observed a paradox unfolding over the centuries as economic realities and human experience of those realities strayed further and further from each other. In primitive societies, he notes, the division of labor was as yet undeveloped for the most part, requiring each person, family, or tribe to be relatively independent when it came to meeting their own basic material needs. Men built their own dwellings, farmed their own land, tended to their own livestock. This is not to deny that basic forms of trade took place, but, for the most part, our primitive ancestors lived fairly self-reliant, if crushingly poor, lives.

F) However, the exclusively local and face-to-face nature of economic and political organization in the ancient and prehistoric worlds constantly impressed upon these primitive peoples the uncontrollable reality of others and their needs. As Tocqueville notes, "as soon as a man begins to deal with common affairs in public, he begins to perceive that he is not so independent of his fellow men as he had first imagined, and that in order to obtain their support he must often lend them his cooperation."

G) At the advent of the modern world, the division of labor spread further and further throughout society. Each person became more and more dependent on others for their basic needs. And yet, robbed of the engagement with our neighbors and with our local communities that our ancestors were forced into by circumstance, we feel ourselves to be more and more independent of one another. As we become more and more dependent on others, we become less and less conscious of our dependence on others. This is the paradox of trade in the modern world.

H) The false consciousness that this paradox generates causes havoc on the debates we have about free trade. There is scarcely a single commodity in any American household that isn't dependent for its manufacture and sale, through one supply chain or another, on scores of different people spread out across the entire globe. But as Tocqueville already foresaw in 1840, we do not feel dependent on these strangers for our way of life. No sense of the dependence of our own material welfare on their work ever strikes our national consciousness. We rarely contemplate the globalized avenues of free trade with gratitude.

I) There are two reasons for this. The first, to put it bluntly, is money. Money allows us to purchase the work of others without giving any thought to them as human beings. Unlike our ancestors in their primitive townships, we rarely have to meet face-to-face the people who've invented, built, shipped, or supplied our goods. No relationship has to be built before an exchange can take place. Simply agree on a price, and you can have any goods you wish without taking a second thought for the human being involved on the other side of the transaction. In this way, money makes us feel more independent than we actually are. Each of us senses the hold that it has over our fellows. We know that if we bid highly enough we can buy ourselves out of the time-consuming labor of building relationships. Money is kind of like magic in that way. It gives us a set of rituals to perform and promises that if we do so we'll be able to wield power over others. The illusion is created that having enough money to buy something is the equivalent of knowing how to make it yourself. Gratitude for the anonymous men and women who make up the supply chain rarely makes its way into our consciousness.

J) Anonymity, in fact, is the second root cause of the free-trade paradox. Modernity has emancipated everyone from the limits of location and community. By and large, when we trade, we trade with strangers; when we vote, we vote for strangers; when we watch, read, or listen to stories, the tellers of the tales are strangers. As opposed to the ancestors Tocqueville compares us to, we do not know the people with whom we have to do, in either the economic or the political sphere. This is simply the shadow side of the miracle of markets, which, for the first time in history, have allowed strangers to look after each other. They've also allowed each of us to live more and more of our lives exclusively as strangers to other people. This is how Tocqueville—rather pessimistically—describes us: Each, standing apart, is like a stranger to the destiny of others; his children and personal friends forming for him the entire human race. As for the remainder of his fellow citizens, he is beside them, but he does not see them. He touches them, but he does not feel them. He exists only in and for himself.

K) The last sentence but one is as apt a summary as one could hope to come by of how each of us functions in the modern economy: "He touches them, but he does not feel them."

L) This is the greatest challenge facing defenders of free trade. It's exceedingly difficult for human beings to feel gratitude toward strangers, and the global marketplace that has made us so rich has also made us strangers to one another. Our brains are hardwired for tribal life, and tribes do not take kindly to strangers. Impressing a sense of dependence upon and gratitude toward foreign strangers is therefore an uphill task.

M) If free-traders are going to win policy arguments in the future, they'll have to find a way of forging bonds of affection between American consumers and foreign producers. Only by de-anonymizing the men and women who supply us with the goods and services we enjoy from overseas and by creating a sense of solidarity and relationship across borders that transcends economic interest can free trade win the day. Otherwise, the inborn biological upper hand that protectionists have in the form of nationalist solidarity is bound to win the day at the ballot box.

items.title: 2024年12月六级第3套 · 仔细阅读 · 第一篇
items.passage:
There are hundreds of personality quizzes online that assert they can ascertain whether the right or left half of your brain is dominant. Left-brained people are supposedly logical and excel at language and math while right-brained people are more imaginative, emotionally intelligent and skilled with spatial reasoning. There's just one problem: That's not how brains work.

Popular science enthusiasts sort of took this idea and ran with it, and it's become woven in popular culture now, and it's not going away.

Despite this enduring belief, there's no such thing as being "right-brained" or "left-brained". Whether you're someone who tends more towards creativity or logic has nothing to do with one hemisphere of your brain being dominant over the other. But the actual science of how the two halves of our brains work together is sometimes stranger than fiction.

The human brain is divided into two hemispheres, the left and right. In all vertebrate(脊椎的) animals, the right hemisphere controls the left side of the body and vice versa. And scientists have long known, thanks to the behaviors of patients who suffered brain injuries, that different areas of the brain do different things.

But many scientists struggled with this idea, because the very suggestion that the left and right halves of the brain operate differently disrupted the idea that nature tends toward perfect symmetry.

Work by neuroscientists(神经科学家) has revealed the importance of different hemispheres of the brain for different activities. However, their research quickly saw some misinterpretations in the general public: Some presumed creative people must be right-brained and logical people left-brained. It is proven that not only is personality unrelated to the different halves of the brain, but people aren't really right-or left-brained to begin with. The idea that we have left-dominant people and right-dominant people, and that this is related to personality, is categorically false. That's never been supported in the neuroscience community. Neuroscientists don't believe that and never have.

What scientists learned is that there are really important differences between the left hemisphere and the right hemisphere. It's just that they have nothing to do with personality or whether cognitive strategy is more logical or free spirited or creative. While researchers have shown the limitations of how the hemispheres of our brains influence our lives, it's not difficult to understand the appeal of such ideas. People are endlessly fascinated by themselves and their friends, and the subtle differences in how people think about the world are really meaningful to them. When you come up with an online quiz that tells us something about ourselves, we're drawn to that. It's irresistible. But you have to take it with an enormous grain of salt.

options.text: Distinguish between the two hemispheres of one's brain.
Determine whether one is left-brained or right-brained.
Tell if one is more of a linguist or of a mathematician.
Ascertain how one's brain performs different tasks.

questions.shortExplanation: There are hundreds of personality quizzes online that assert they can ascertain whether the right or left half of your brain is dominant.
questions.detailedExplanation:
【答案】 B （细节题）

【判型】 What do numerous personality quizzes online claim they are able to do? 是 What 引导的事实性提问，问"quizzes 声称做什么"，可直接回原文找事实陈述。

【拆句】 题干主干 What do…quizzes…claim they are able to do?，What 作 do 的宾语，they are able to do 是 claim 的宾语从句；结构平铺，无陷阱。

【定位】 There are hundreds of personality quizzes online that assert they can ascertain whether the right or left half of your brain is dominant.

网络上有成百上千的性格测试，宣称它们能够查明你的左半脑还是右半脑占主导。

【选项】 A) 偷换概念 Distinguish between the two hemispheres of one's brain 说的是"区分大脑的两个半球"——这是解剖事实而非测试声称的本事，与原文承诺的"判断哪边占主导"不同。

B) ✓ 正确 ascertain whether the right or left half of your brain is dominant ↔

Determine whether one is left-brained or right-brained B 项把定位句改写成"判断一个人是左脑型还是右脑型"，与预判一致，且严格落在 P1 首句的字面承诺范围内。

C) 答非所问 Tell if one is more of a linguist or of a mathematician 取自 excel at language and math 的延伸描述，是"左脑型人"的衍生特征，而非测试本身宣称要做的事。 D) 张冠李戴 Ascertain how one's brain performs different tasks 的内容来自 different areas of the brain do different things，那是科学界的事实，不是"测试"声称要做的；动词 Ascertain 虽与原文同词，但宾语错配。

questions.prompt: What does the author say is sometimes stranger than fiction?

options.text: How one hemisphere of the brain impacts creativity.
How the two halves of our brains work alternately.
How the two hemispheres of our brains cooperate.
How one half of the brain dominates the other.

questions.shortExplanation: But the actual science of how the two halves of our brains work together is sometimes stranger than fiction.
questions.detailedExplanation:
【答案】 C （细节题）

【判型】 What does the author say is sometimes stranger than fiction? 问作者明说的内容，是对原文一句话的事实复现。

【拆句】 题干主干 What does the author say is…?，What 是表语补足语，is sometimes stranger than fiction 修饰 What 指向的具体事物；结构简单。

【定位】 But the actual science of how the two halves of our brains work together is sometimes stranger than fiction.

但关于我们大脑两个半球如何协同运作的真实科学，有时比小说还要离奇。

【选项】 A) 偷换概念 How one hemisphere of the brain impacts creativity 关注"某一个半脑对创造力的影响"，定位句强调的是"两半协同"，主体数量不符；creativity 也是从前文带过来的旁支话题。 B) 偷换概念 How the two halves of our brains work alternately 把 work together 改成 work alternately（轮流工作），意思完全不同——一个是同时合作，一个是交替使用。

C) ✓ 正确 the two halves of our brains work together ↔ the two hemispheres of our brains cooperate C 项把 "halves…work together" 替换成 "hemispheres…cooperate"，是定位句的等值改写。 D) 与原文相反 How one half of the brain dominates the other 正是文章一开头就否定的"左右脑主导说"，与定位句乃至全文立场相反。

questions.prompt: Why did many scientists have difficulty endorsing the idea that different areas of the brain do different things?

options.text: It contradicts the assumption that the two hemispheres of the brain are symmetrical.
It dismisses the view that the universe has been evolving in a consistent manner.
It is in conflict with the suggestion that the left and right halves of the brain work together.
It disrupts the idea that the right hemisphere of the brain controls the left side of the body.

questions.shortExplanation: But many scientists struggled with this idea, because the very suggestion that the left and right halves of the brain operate differently disrupted the idea that nature tends toward perfect symmetry. 但许多科学家难以接受这个观点，因为"大脑左右半球运作方式不同"这一论断本身就动摇了"自然界趋向完美对称"的观念。
questions.detailedExplanation:
【答案】 A （细节题）

【判型】 Why did many scientists have difficulty endorsing the idea…? 问原因，且原因通常在原文同句以 because/since 给出。

【拆句】 题干主干 Why did many scientists have difficulty endorsing the idea…?，that different areas of the brain do different things 是 idea 的同位语从句，解释 idea 内容；理解关键是 endorsing="赞同/接受"，不是"支持"商业意味。

【定位】 But many scientists struggled with this idea, because the very suggestion that the left and right halves of the brain operate differently disrupted the idea that nature tends toward perfect symmetry. 但许多科学家难以接受这个观点，因为"大脑左右半球运作方式不同"这一论断本身就动摇了"自然界趋向完美对称"的观念。

【选项】 A) ✓ 正确 disrupted the idea that nature tends toward perfect symmetry ↔

contradicts the assumption that the two hemispheres of the brain are symmetrical A 项把"动摇自然对称预设"这一动作改写为"与左右脑对称的预设相矛盾"，二者在本语境下指代同一观念，定位句即等于 A 项。

B) 无中生有 It dismisses the view that the universe has been evolving in a consistent manner 把对象从"自然对称"扩展为"宇宙演化方式"，原文未涉及宇宙演化的话题。 C) 张冠李戴 It is in conflict with the suggestion that the left and right halves of the brain work together 把矛盾对象说成"两半脑协同"，但原文中科学家排斥的不是"协同"，而是"对称"预设；况且"协同"是 P3 的肯定观点，本身不会被科学家抗拒。

D) 张冠李戴 It disrupts the idea that the right hemisphere of the brain controls the left side of the body 取自 P4 的解剖事实，是脊椎动物的客观规律，不可能被科学家抗拒；动词 disrupts 虽与原文同词，宾语却换错。

questions.prompt: What belief have neuroscientists long rejected according to the passage?

options.text: There are left-dominant people and right-dominant people with different personalities.
There are noticeable differences between the left and right hemispheres of the brain.
One's personality is hardly related to the different halves of the brain.
Different areas of the brain are responsible for different activities.

questions.shortExplanation: The idea that we have left-dominant people and right-dominant people, and that this is related to personality, is categorically false. That's never been supported in the neuroscience community. Neuroscientists don't believe that and never have.
questions.detailedExplanation:
【答案】 A （细节题）

【判型】 What belief have neuroscientists long rejected according to the passage? 问"哪个观念被拒"，是对原文一处明确表态的复现。

【拆句】 题干主干 What belief have neuroscientists long rejected…?，long 修饰 rejected 表"长久以来一直拒绝"；现在完成时 + long，强调持续否定，是定位句的语气信号。

【定位】 The idea that we have left-dominant people and right-dominant people, and that this is related to personality, is categorically false. That's never been supported in the neuroscience community. Neuroscientists don't believe that and never have.

"存在左脑主导型人和右脑主导型人、并且这与人格有关"这一观念是完全错误的。神经科学界从未支持过这种说法。神经科学家不相信这种说法，也从未相信过。

【选项】 A) ✓ 正确 we have left-dominant people and right-dominant people, and that this is related to personality

↔ There are left-dominant people and right-dominant people with different personalities A 项就是定位句被 categorically false / never been supported 否定的那个具体观念， 与预判一致。 B) 与原文相反 There are noticeable differences between the left and right hemispheres of the brain 是 there are really important differences between the left hemisphere and the right hemisphere 明确肯定的事实，神经科学界并不拒斥它。 C) 与原文相反 One's personality is hardly related to the different halves of the brain 正是作者本人和神经科学界所持的立场（人格与左右脑无关），不是他们"长期拒绝"的观念。 D) 与原文相反 Different areas of the brain are responsible for different activities 是 different areas of the brain do different things 的同义改写，是科学界共识，不可能被"长期拒绝"。

questions.prompt: What are we advised to do with an online quiz that tells us something about ourselves?
questions.shortExplanation: When you come up with an online quiz that tells us something about ourselves, we're drawn to that. It's irresistible. But you have to take it with an enormous grain of salt. 当出现一份告诉我们自身某些情况的网络测试时，我们会被吸引，难以抗拒。但你必须对它持极大的保留态度。
questions.detailedExplanation:
【答案】 D （细节题）

【判型】 What are we advised to do…? 问作者给出的具体建议，原文末段必有对应明示。

【拆句】 题干主干 What are we advised to do with an online quiz…?，that tells us something about ourselves 是 quiz 的定语从句；advise sb. to do 的被动 are advised to do 是常见结构，注意 with 引出对象 "对……怎么办"。

【定位】 When you come up with an online quiz that tells us something about ourselves, we're drawn to that. It's irresistible. But you have to take it with an enormous grain of salt. 当出现一份告诉我们自身某些情况的网络测试时，我们会被吸引，难以抗拒。但你必须对它持极大的保留态度。

【选项】 A) 过度推断 Challenge its authority 暗示要去"挑战其权威性"，但原文只是建议保留态度、不轻信结论，并未要求与之对抗。 B) 无中生有 Scrutinize its originality 让人去审查"原创性"，原文丝毫未涉及测试是否原创的问题。

C) 答非所问 Evaluate its popularity 评的是"测试的流行程度"，与作者给读者的"个人如何对待结论"的建议完全错位。 D) ✓ 正确 take it with an enormous grain of salt ↔ Question its reliability 把习语 take it with an enormous grain of salt 还原为字面意 question its reliability，与预判一致。

items.title: 2024年12月六级第3套 · 仔细阅读 · 第二篇
items.passage:
One hundred thirty-five students, four teachers, one giant classroom: This is what 9th grade looks like at Westwood High School, in Mesa, Arizona's largest school system. There, an innovative teaching model has taken hold, and is spreading to other schools in the district and beyond.

Five years ago, faced with high teacher turnover and declining student enrollment, Westwood's leaders decided to try something different. Working with professors at Arizona State University's teachers college, they piloted a classroom model known as team teaching, which allows teachers to dissolve the walls that separate their classes across physical or grade divides.

The teachers share large groups of students—sometimes 100 or more—and rotate between group instruction, one-on-one interventions, small study groups, or whatever the teachers as a team agree is a priority that day. What looks at times like chaos is in fact a carefully orchestrated plan: Each morning, the Westwood teams meet to hammer out a personalized program for every student the team will focus on that day.

By giving teachers more opportunity to collaborate, Mesa's administrators hoped to fill staffing gaps and boost teacher morale and retention. Initial research suggests the gamble could pay off.

"Teachers are doing fantastic things, but it's very rare a teacher walks into another room to see what's happening," said Andi Fourlis, superintendent of Mesa Public Schools. "Our profession is so slow to advance because we are working in isolation."

Of course, overhauling teaching approaches can't fix all the frustrations teachers have, such as low pay, but early results from Mesa show team teaching may be helping to reverse low morale. In a survey of hundreds of the district's teachers, researchers found those who worked on teams reported greater job satisfaction, more frequent collaborations with colleagues, and more positive interactions with students.

Another benefit of teams, teachers say, is that they can help each other improve their instruction. During one planning session, English teacher Jeff Hall shared a performance appraisal with a science teacher: Her recent lecture on something she called "the central dogma of biology" had bewildered him and their other teammates.

"If the science is too confusing for me, can you imagine the frustration you feel as kids?" Hall said. But the science teacher, he said, wouldn't have known about the confusion on her own.

The model is not for everyone. Some teachers approached about volunteering for a team have said they prefer to work alone. Team teaching can also be a scheduling nightmare, especially at schools like Westwood where only some staff work in teams. There are also thorny questions like how to evaluate four teachers on the performance of 135 students. But for the time being, it seems to be working.

questions.prompt: What do we learn about team teaching from the passage?

options.text: It is generally conducted in classrooms without walls.
It allows students to choose teachers they favor most.
It prioritizes peer work over classroom instruction.
It is closely coordinated despite seeming confusion.

questions.shortExplanation: What looks at times like chaos is in fact a carefully orchestrated plan: Each morning, the Westwood teams meet to hammer out a personalized program for every student the team will focus on that day. 看上去时不时像一团乱麻的场面，实际上是经过精心编排的方案：每天清晨，Westwood 的团队会碰头，为当天他们要重点关注的每个学生敲定一份个性化方案。
questions.detailedExplanation:
【答案】 D （细节题）

【判型】 题干 What do we learn about team teaching from the passage? 不含 infer/imply/main idea，问的是对 team teaching 的客观描述，属概括式细节。

【拆句】 What do we learn about team teaching from the passage? 主干为 What...do we learn，about team teaching 修饰 learn 的对象，from the passage 是来源状语，结构平铺直叙，无陷阱。

【定位】 What looks at times like chaos is in fact a carefully orchestrated plan: Each morning, the Westwood teams meet to hammer out a personalized program for every student the team will focus on that day. 看上去时不时像一团乱麻的场面，实际上是经过精心编排的方案：每天清晨，Westwood 的团队会碰头，为当天他们要重点关注的每个学生敲定一份个性化方案。

【选项】 A) 偷换概念 classrooms without walls 把 dissolve the walls that separate their classes 的比喻当成物理上没有墙的教室，完全曲解原意。

B) 无中生有文中从未提及让学生选择喜爱的教师；The teachers share large groups of students 强调教师轮换而非学生选师。 C) 偷换概念原文 rotate between group instruction, one-on-one interventions, small study groups 把团体讲授与小组活动并列，并未说同伴协作优先于课堂讲授。 D) ✓ 正确 What looks at times like chaos is in fact a carefully orchestrated plan ↔

It is closely coordinated despite seeming confusion 预判要求的看似混乱/实则编排两层语义，It is closely coordinated despite seeming confusion 两层都覆盖，结构对应整齐。

questions.prompt: What does initial research suggest regarding Westwood's innovative teaching model?

options.text: It could help raise teachers' pay.
It could turn out to be a success.
It could cut down overall costs.
It could end up like a gamble.

questions.shortExplanation: By giving teachers more opportunity to collaborate, Mesa's administrators hoped to fill staffing gaps and boost teacher morale and retention. Initial research suggests the gamble could pay off.
questions.detailedExplanation:
【答案】 B （细节题）

【判型】 题干 What does initial research suggest 直接索取研究的结论，属客观事实复述。

【拆句】 What does initial research suggest regarding Westwood’s innovative teaching model? 主干是 What does initial research suggest，regarding... 引导对象状语，等同 about，结构清楚。

【定位】 By giving teachers more opportunity to collaborate, Mesa's administrators hoped to fill staffing gaps and boost teacher morale and retention. Initial research suggests the gamble could pay off.

通过让教师有更多协作机会，Mesa 的管理层希望补齐师资缺口、提升教师士气与留任率。 初步研究显示这场赌博可能会奏效。

【选项】 A) 与原文相反 overhauling teaching approaches can’t fix all the frustrations teachers have, such as low pay 明确指出教学模式改革解决不了低薪问题，故团队教学不能 raise teachers’ pay。

B) ✓ 正确 Initial research suggests the gamble could pay off ↔ It could turn out to be a success 预判要求团队教学可能成功，It could turn out to be a success 与定位句语义、情态强度完全对齐。

C) 无中生有全文未提及团队教学能降低总体成本；P4 谈的是士气、留任率与师资缺口，不是成本。 D) 偷换概念原文 the gamble could pay off 中 gamble 仅是对 the model 的比喻指代，意为这场赌博能赢；end up like a gamble 把赌博当成最终结果，等于说一切像赌博一样不确定，与原文积极语义相反。

questions.prompt: What did superintendent Andi Fourlis say about the teaching profession?

options.text: Morale cannot be boosted until teaching models are overhauled.
Teachers are simply too busy to visit classes of their colleagues.
Progress is slow due to lack of collaboration among teachers.
Teachers often do fantastic things without being noticed.

questions.shortExplanation: "Teachers are doing fantastic things, but it's very rare a teacher walks into another room to see what's happening," said Andi Fourlis, superintendent of Mesa Public Schools. "Our profession is so slow to advance because we are working in isolation."
questions.detailedExplanation:
【答案】 C （细节题）

【判型】 题干 What did superintendent Andi Fourlis say 直接索取人物原话观点，属观点细节。

【拆句】 What did superintendent Andi Fourlis say about the teaching profession? 主干 What did Andi Fourlis say，superintendent 同位语解释身份，about the teaching profession 限定话题，结构无陷阱。

【定位】 "Teachers are doing fantastic things, but it's very rare a teacher walks into another room to see what's happening," said Andi Fourlis, superintendent of Mesa Public Schools. "Our profession is so slow to advance because we are working in isolation."

Mesa 公立学校负责人 Andi Fourlis 说：教师们正在做着了不起的事情，但教师走进另一间教室看看发生什么的情况非常少见。我们这个行业进步如此缓慢，是因为我们在孤立地工作。

【选项】 A) 过度推断原文未提出士气提升必须先 overhaul 教学模式这一条件关系；P5 谈的是进步缓慢的原因，不是 morale 的前提条件。

B) 偷换概念原文是 it’s very rare a teacher walks into another room，即极少发生，并未给出 too busy 这一原因；选项擅自补充忙作为原因。

C) ✓ 正确 Our profession is so slow to advance because we are working in isolation ↔

Progress is slow due to lack of collaboration among teachers C 完整保留进步慢←孤立工作的因果方向，且情态/极性与原文一致。

D) 偷换概念原文 Teachers are doing fantastic things, but it’s very rare a teacher walks into another room 的重点是同行看不见，而非不被注意；选项把同行无法观摩偷换为更宽泛的不被注意。

【拆句】 What does the author want to show by citing English teacher Jeff Hall’s experience? 主干 What does the author want to show，by citing... 现在分词作方式状语， experience 是 citing 的逻辑宾语，结构无陷阱。

questions.prompt: What does the author think is one of the difficult problems in implementing the new teaching model?

What to include in teaching schedules.
How to recruit volunteers for a team.
How to assess each teacher's performance.

questions.detailedExplanation:
【答案】 D （细节题）

【判型】 What does the author think is one of the difficult problems 索取作者列举的困难之一，属细节列举。

【拆句】 What does the author think is one of the difficult problems in implementing the new teaching model? 主干 What is one of the difficult problems；the author think 是插入语；in implementing... 介词短语作后置定语，限定 problems 的范围。

还有一些棘手的问题，比如如何依据 135 名学生的成绩去评估四位教师。

【选项】 A) 答非所问原文 Some teachers approached about volunteering for a team have said they prefer to work alone 只是说有人不愿参加，并未说要拿独立工作者怎么办这一难题； 选项把现象包装成处理难题。

B) 偷换概念原文 Team teaching can also be a scheduling nightmare 把排课描述为难题，并非问在课表里加什么内容；选项把排课难偷换为加什么内容。

C) 无中生有原文未把招募志愿者列为难题；Some teachers…prefer to work alone 是结果性描述，并未涉及怎么招募。 D) ✓ 正确 how to evaluate four teachers on the performance of 135 students ↔

How to assess each teacher’s performance 原文 thorny questions 后 like 引出例子 evaluate four teachers，D 项保留了 evaluate→assess 的核心语义，是列举项之一的标准改写。

items.title: 2024年6月六级第1套 · 选词填空
items.passage:
It's quite remarkable how different genres of music can spark unique feelings, emotions, and memories. Studies have shown that music can reduce stress and anxiety before surgeries and we are all attracted toward our own unique life soundtrack.

If you're looking to [26] _____ stress, you might want to give classical music a try.

The sounds of classical music produce a calming effect letting [27] _____ pleasure-inducing dopamine(多巴胺) in the brain that helps control attention, learning and emotional responses. It can also turn down the body's stress response, resulting in an overall happier mood. It turns out a pleasant mood can lead to [28] _____ in a person's thinking.

Although there are many great [29] _____ of classical music like Bach, Beethoven and Handel, none of these artists' music seems to have the same health effects as Mozart's does. According to researchers, listening to Mozart can increase brain wave activity and improve [30] _____ function. Another study found that the distinctive features of Mozart's music trigger parts of the brain that are responsible for

high-level mental functions. Even maternity [31] _____ use Mozart to help newborn babies adapt to life outside of the mother's belly.

It has been found that listening to classical music [32] _____ reduces a person's blood pressure. Researchers believe that the calming sounds of classical music may help your heart [33] _____ from stress. Classical music can also be a great tool to help people who have trouble sleeping. One study found that students who had trouble sleeping slept better while they were listening to classical music.

Whether classical music is something that you listen to on a regular basis or not, it wouldn't [34] _____ to take time out of your day to listen to music that you find [35] _____ . You will be surprised at how good it makes you feel and the potentially positive change in your health.

questions.prompt: If you're looking to __(26)__ stress, you might want to give classical music a try.
questions.shortExplanation: alleviate stress=缓解压力，是固定搭配
questions.detailedExplanation:
【答案】 A) alleviate 动词

【词性槽】 be looking to + 动词原形 + stress

【依据】 alleviate stress=缓解压力，是固定搭配

If you're looking to __(26)__ stress, you might want to give classical music a try. 与开篇 Studies have shown that music can reduce stress and anxiety before surgeries 中的 reduce stress 同义改写，alleviate stress 在英语里就是「减轻压力」的标准说法。

【竞争词】 L) recover 搭配错位：通常 recover from stress，不直接 recover stress

recover 表「从……恢复」时几乎都用 recover from sth，直接接 stress 不合英语习惯；且本句要表达的是「减轻」而非「恢复」压力。

questions.prompt: The sounds of classical music produce a calming effect letting __(27)__ pleasure-inducing dopamine(多巴胺 ) in the brain

questions.detailedExplanation:
【答案】 I) loose 动词

【词性槽】 letting + 空 + 名词短语（pleasure-inducing dopamine）

【依据】 loose dopamine=释放多巴胺 letting __(27)__ pleasure-inducing dopamine(多巴胺) in the brain，loose 这里作动词意为「释放」，与「大脑释放令人愉悦的多巴胺」语义完美对应，也呼应 produce a calming effect 的因果链。

【易错】 最具迷惑性的错误词是 F) —— 看到 letting 容易误以为后跟 -ing 并列。考生可能把 letting __(27)__ pleasure-inducing dopamine(多巴胺) in the brain 误读成两个 -ing 并列，从而填 inhibiting；但 let + 宾语 + 动词原形才是正解，且 inhibiting 与「释放多巴胺」语义相反，是典型反向干扰。

It turns out a pleasant mood can lead to __(28)__ in a person's thinking. 中 clarity in (one's) thinking 是英语固定表达，意思是「思路清晰」，与「愉悦情绪带来思维清晰」的因果链贴合，也承接前文古典音乐的认知促进作用。

questions.prompt: Although there are many great __(29)__ of classical music like Bach, Beethoven and Handel
questions.shortExplanation: 三位人名=三位作曲家的上义词 like Bach, Beethoven and Handel 是教科书级的古典作曲家清单，composers 与之构成 「上义词—举例」的关系，语义和复数形态都完美对上。

【依据】 三位人名=三位作曲家的上义词 like Bach, Beethoven and Handel 是教科书级的古典作曲家清单，composers 与之构成 「上义词—举例」的关系，语义和复数形态都完美对上。

questions.prompt: listening to Mozart can increase brain wave activity and improve __(30)__ function.
questions.shortExplanation: cognitive function=认知功能，脑科学固定搭配
questions.detailedExplanation:
【答案】 C) cognitive 形容词

【词性槽】 improve + 空 + function（名词）

【依据】 cognitive function=认知功能，脑科学固定搭配

listening to Mozart can increase brain wave activity and improve __(30)__ function. 与前文 brain wave activity、以及后文 high-level mental functions 同主题串联， cognitive function 是脑科学英语中最常见的搭配，意为「认知功能」。

【竞争词】 J) majestic 义为「雄伟壮丽」，与脑功能不搭

majestic 用来修饰山川宫殿等宏伟事物，与 function 搭配语义不通，且本段讨论的是大脑健康，不存在审美维度。

K) mandatory 义为「强制的」，与「improve」宾语逻辑冲突

mandatory function 意思变成「强制功能」，与「听莫扎特改善大脑功能」的因果链完全错位。
questions.hint: 根据空格前后的词性、搭配与上下文选择词语；每个词最多使用一次。

questions.prompt: Even maternity __(31)__ use Mozart to help newborn babies adapt to life outside of the mother's belly.
questions.shortExplanation: maternity wards 固定搭配=产科病房
questions.detailedExplanation:
【答案】 O) wards 名词

【词性槽】 maternity + 空 + use…

【依据】 maternity wards 固定搭配=产科病房

Even maternity __(31)__ use Mozart to help newborn babies 中「产科病房放莫扎特给新生儿听」是常识场景，wards 与 maternity 形成医院科室专名，语义、形态、搭配三对齐。

questions.prompt: It has been found that listening to classical music __(32)__ reduces a person's blood pressure.
questions.shortExplanation: 实验结论描述效果 → 显著地
questions.detailedExplanation:
【答案】 M) significantly 副词

【词性槽】 主谓之间修饰谓语动词的位置

【依据】 实验结论描述效果 → 显著地

It has been found that listening to classical music __(32)__ reduces a person's blood pressure. 是科研结论句，常用 significantly 表达「显著降低血压」——这是研究类英语的高频搭配。

【竞争词】 H) intrinsically 义为「本质上」，与外在效果不搭

intrinsically 强调「内在属性」，但 reduces a person's blood pressure 描述的是可观测的外部效果，逻辑指向不一致；研究语境惯用 significantly 表统计学显著。

questions.prompt: the calming sounds of classical music may help your heart __(33)__ from stress.
questions.shortExplanation: recover from stress=从压力中恢复
questions.detailedExplanation:
【答案】 L) recover 动词

【词性槽】 help your heart ___ from stress

【依据】 recover from stress=从压力中恢复

the calming sounds of classical music may help your heart __(33)__ from stress. 是医学/心理类英语固定表达，与本段「古典音乐降血压、护心」的主题完全契合。

questions.prompt: it wouldn't __(34)__ to take time out of your day to listen to music
questions.shortExplanation: it wouldn't hurt to do = 做……不会有坏处
questions.detailedExplanation:
【答案】 E) hurt 动词

【词性槽】 it wouldn't ___ to do 句型，情态助动词后接动词原形

【依据】 it wouldn't hurt to do = 做……不会有坏处

it wouldn't __(34)__ to take time out of your day to listen to music that you find __(35)__. 是英语固定句式「it wouldn't hurt to do sth」，意为「不妨做某事/做……没坏处」，与作者鼓励读者抽空听音乐的语气完全匹配。

【竞争词】 A) alleviate 及物动词，需要直接宾语，与 to do 不配

alleviate 后必须接被缓解的对象（如 alleviate stress），而本句结构是 it wouldn't ___ to take…，空后没有宾语而是不定式短语，与 alleviate 的及物用法不匹配；且 26 题已用 A。

L) recover 义为「恢复」，与「做某事不会有坏处」语义错位

it wouldn't recover to do 不构成英语习惯表达，recover 通常接 from / sth，且与作者「建议你抽空听听音乐」的语气也对不上；且 33 题已用 L。

questions.prompt: to take time out of your day to listen to music that you find __(35)__.
questions.shortExplanation: music + soothing=令人舒缓的音乐 to take time out of your day to listen to music that you find __(35)__. 与全文 The sounds of classical music produce a calming effect 形成首尾呼应，soothing 与 calming 同义，「舒缓的」音乐正是作者建议大家去听的类型。
questions.detailedExplanation:
【答案】 N) soothing 形容词

【词性槽】 find + 宾语 + 空（宾语补足语）

【依据】 music + soothing=令人舒缓的音乐 to take time out of your day to listen to music that you find __(35)__. 与全文 The sounds of classical music produce a calming effect 形成首尾呼应，soothing 与 calming 同义，「舒缓的」音乐正是作者建议大家去听的类型。

【竞争词】 F) inhibiting 义为「抑制的」，感情色彩与劝勉语气冲突

inhibiting 带消极色彩，意为「让人放不开/受抑制」，与作者鼓励读者享受音乐、放松身心的结尾语气完全相反；命题人故意把它放进来当陷阱。

【易错】 最具迷惑性的错误词是 F) —— find sth + 空，形容词诱惑+词性同位。inhibiting 和 soothing 同为 -ing 形容词，词性都对、都能修饰 music，区别仅在感情色彩；如果不回头核对全文「舒缓/愉悦」的基调，很容易掉坑。
