items.title: 2024年6月六级第1套 · 信息匹配
items.passage:
A) In the city of Athens, Georgia, there exists a rather curious local landmark—a large white oak that is almost universally stated to own itself. Because of this, it is considered one of the most famous trees in the world. So how did this tree come to own itself and the land around it?

B) Sometime in the 19th century a Georgian called Colonel William Jackson reportedly took a liking to the said tree and endeavored to protect it from any danger. As to why he loved it so, the earliest documented account of this story is an anonymously written front page article in the Athens Weekly Banner published on August 12, 1890. It states, "Col. Jackson had watched the tree grow from his childhood, and grew to love it almost as he would a human. Its luxuriant leaves and sturdy limbs had often protected him from the heavy rains, and out of its highest branches he had many a time gotten the eggs of the feathered singers. He watched its growth, and when reaching a ripe old age he saw the tree standing in its magnificent proportions, he was pained to think that after his death it would fall into the hands of those who might destroy it."

C) Towards this end, Jackson transferred by means of a deed ownership of the tree and a little land around it to the tree itself. The deed read, "W. H. Jackson for and in consideration of the great affection which he bears the said tree, and his great desire to see it protected has conveyed unto the said oak tree entire possession of itself and of all land within eight feet of it on all sides."

D) In time, the tree came to be something of a tourist attraction, known as The Tree That Owns Itself. However, in the early 20th century, the tree started showing signs of its slow death, with little that could be done about it. Father time comes for us all eventually, even our often long lived, tall and leafy fellow custodians( 看管者 ) of Earth. Finally, on October 9, 1942, the over 30 meter tall and 200-400 year old tree fell, rumor has it, as a result of a severe windstorm and/or via having previously died and its roots rotted.

E) About four years later, members of the Junior Ladies Garden Club (who'd tended to the tree before its unfortunate death) tracked down a small tree grown from a nut taken from the original tree. And so it was that on October 9, 1946, under the direction of Professor Roy Bowden of the College of Agriculture at the University of Georgia, this little tree was transplanted to the location of its ancestor. A couple of months later, an official ceremony was held featuring none other than the Mayor of Athens, Robert L McWhorter, to commemorate the occasion.

F) This new tree became known as The Son of the Tree That Owns Itself and it was assumed that, as the original tree's heir, it naturally inherited the land it stood on. Of course, there are many dozens of other trees known to exist descending from the original, as people taking a nut from it to grow elsewhere was a certainty. That said, to date, none of the original tree's other children have petitioned the courts for their share of the land, so it seems all good. In any event, The Son of the Tree That Owns Itself still stands today, though often referred to simply as The Tree That Owns Itself.

G) This all brings us around to whether Jackson ever actually gave legal ownership of the tree to itself in the first place and whether such a deed is legally binding.

H) Well, to begin with, it turns out Jackson only spent about three years of his life in Athens, starting at the age of 43 from 1829 to 1832, sort of dismissing the idea that he loved the tree from spending time under it as a child and watching it grow, and then worrying about what would happen to it after he died. Further, an extensive search of land ownership records in Athens does not seem to indicate Jackson ever owned the land the tree sits on.

I) He did live on a lot of land directly next to it for those three years, but whether he owned that land or not isn't clear. Whatever the case, in 1832 a four acre parcel, which included the land the tree was on and the neighboring land Jackson lived on, among others, was sold to University professor Malthus A Ward. In the transaction, Ward was required to pay Jackson a sum of $1,200 (about $31, 000 today), either for the property itself or simply in compensation for improvements Jackson had made on the lot. In the end, whether he ever owned the neighboring lot or was simply allowed to use it while he allegedly worked at the University, he definitely never owned the lot the tree grew on, which is the most important bit for the topic at hand.

J) After Professor Ward purchased the land, Jackson and his family purchased a 655 acre parcel a few miles away and moved there. Ten years later, in 1844, Jackson seemed to have come into financial difficulties and had his little plantation seized by the Clarke County Sheriff's office and auctioned off to settle the mortgage. Thus, had he owned some land in Athens itself, including the land the tree sat on, presumably he would have sold it to raise funds or otherwise had it taken as well.

K) And whatever the case there, Jackson would have known property taxes needed to be paid on the deeded land for the tree to be truly secure in its future. Yet no account or record indicates any trust or the like was set up to facilitate this.

L) On top of all this, there is no hard evidence such a deed ever existed, despite the fact that deed records in Athens go back many decades before Jackson's death in 1876 and that it was supposed to have existed in 1890 in the archives according to the original anonymous news reporter who claims to have seen it.

M) As you might imagine from all of this, few give credit to this side of the story. So how did all of this come about then?

N) It is speculated to have been invented by the imagination of the said anonymous author at the Athens Weekly Banner in the aforementioned 1890 front page article titled "Deeded to Itself", which by the way contained several elements that are much more easily proved to be false. As to why the author would do this, it's speculated perhaps it was a 19th century version of a click-bait thought exercise on whether it would be legal for someone to deed such a non-conscious living thing to itself or not.

O) Whatever the case, the next known instance of the Tree That Owns Itself being mentioned wasn't until 1901 in the Centennial Edition of that same paper, the Athens Weekly Banner. This featured another account very clearly just copying the original article published about a decade before, only slightly reworded. The next account was in 1906, again in the Athens Weekly Banner, again very clearly copying the original account, only slightly reworded, the 19th century equivalent of re-posts when the audience has forgotten about the original.

questions.prompt: Jackson was said to have transferred his ownership of the oak tree to itself in order to protect it from being destroyed.

questions.detailedExplanation:
【答案】 B 段（强锚点）

【定位】 Its luxuriant leaves and sturdy limbs had often protected him from the heavy rains, and out of its highest branches he had many a time gotten the eggs of the feathered singers.

questions.prompt: There is no evidence that Jackson had made arrangements to pay property taxes for the land on which the oak tree sat.

questions.detailedExplanation:
【答案】 K 段（强锚点）

【锚点】 无证据证明他为缴财产税做过安排

items.title: 2024年6月六级第1套 · 仔细阅读 · 第一篇
items.passage:
It is irrefutable that employees know the difference between right and wrong. So why don't more employees intervene when they see someone exhibiting at-risk behavior in the workplace?

There are a number of factors that influence whether people intervene. First, they need to be able to see a risky situation beginning to unfold. Second, the company's culture needs to make them feel safe to speak up. And third, they need to have the communication skills to say something effectively.

This is not strictly a workplace problem; it's a growing problem off the job too. Every day people witness things on the street and choose to stand idly by. This is known as the bystander effect— the more people who witness an event, the less likely anyone in that group is to help the victim. The psychology behind this is called diffusion of responsibility. Basically, the larger the crowd, the more people assume that someone else will take care of it—meaning no one effectively intervenes or acts in a moment of need.

This crowd mentality is strong enough for people to evade their known responsibilities. But it's not only frontline workers who don't make safety interventions in the workplace. There are also instances where supervisors do not intervene either.

When a group of employees sees unsafe behavior not being addressed at a leadership level it creates the precedent that this is how these situations should be addressed, thus defining the safety culture for everyone.

Despite the fact that workers are encouraged to intervene when they observe unsafe operations, this happens less than half of the time. Fear is the ultimate factor in not intervening. There is a fear of penalty, a fear that they'll have to do more work if they intervene. Unsuccessful attempts in the past are another strong contributing factor to why people don't intervene—they tend to prefer to defer that action to someone else for all future situations.

On many worksites, competent workers must be appointed. Part of their job is to intervene when workers perform a task without the proper equipment or if the conditions are unsafe. Competent workers are also required to stop work from continuing when there's a danger.

Supervisors also play a critical role. Even if a competent person isn't required, supervisors need a broad set of skills to not only identify and alleviate workplace hazards but also build a safety climate within their team that supports intervening and open communication among them.

Beyond competent workers and supervisors, it's important to educate everyone within the organization that they are obliged to intervene if they witness a possible unsafe act, whether you're a designated competent person, a supervisor or a frontline worker.

questions.prompt: What is one of the factors contributing to failure of intervention in face of risky behavior in the workplace?
questions.shortExplanation: Second, the company's culture needs to make them feel safe to speak up. 第二，公司的文化需要让他们觉得发声是安全的。
questions.detailedExplanation:
【答案】 B （细节题）

【判型】 What is one of the factors contributing to failure of intervention in face of risky behavior in the workplace? 用 What 直接问一个具体因素，答案落点为原文明确给出的某项 factor，是典型客观细节题。

【拆句】 主干为 What is one of the factors，后接现在分词短语 contributing to failure of intervention 作定语修饰 factors，再用介词短语 in face of risky behavior in the workplace 限定场景。结构平铺直叙，无陷阱。

【定位】 Second, the company's culture needs to make them feel safe to speak up. 第二，公司的文化需要让他们觉得发声是安全的。

【选项】 A) 无中生有 P2 列举的三个因素中并无 Slack supervision style（监管松懈）。supervisors 在 P4 P8 才出现，且讨论的是是否亲自干预，与「监管风格松懈」无关。

B) ✓ 正确 the company's culture needs to make them feel safe to speak up ↔

Unfavorable workplace culture 原文说「需要文化让人敢说」，预判答案是「文化不让人敢说」，B 项 Unfavorable workplace culture 正是这一缺失态的同义改写，因此锁定 B。 C) 与原文相反 they need to be able to see a risky situation beginning to unfold 说的是「员工要能预见风险」，而 Unforeseeable risk 反过来说「风险无法预见」，与原文方向相反； 且不在 P2 的三因素列表中。

D) 偷换概念 they need to have the communication skills to say something effectively 说的是 「需要具备沟通技能」，强调的是个人技能层面；而 Blocked communication 说「沟通被阻塞」，把「技能不足」偷换为「通道被堵」，对象完全不同。
questions.hint: 回到原文定位题干关键词，比较选项与原文的含义。

questions.prompt: What does the author mean by "diffusion of responsibility" (Para. 3)?

options.text: The more people are around, the more they need to worry about their personal safety.
The more people who witness an event, the less likely anyone will venture to
The more people idling around on the street, the more likely they need taking care of.
The more people are around, the less chance someone will step forward to intervene.

questions.shortExplanation: Basically, the larger the crowd, the more people assume that someone else will take care of it —meaning no one effectively intervenes or acts in a moment of need.
questions.detailedExplanation:
【答案】 D （词义句意题）

【判型】 What does the author mean by 是经典的释义提问框架，答案为原文对该术语的同义解释。

【拆句】 主干 What does the author mean by，by 后跟引号词作宾语，括号内 (Para. 3) 为定位提示。结构清晰，无陷阱。

【定位】 Basically, the larger the crowd, the more people assume that someone else will take care of it —meaning no one effectively intervenes or acts in a moment of need.

基本上，人群越大，越多人就假定别人会处理这事——也就是说，在需要出手时反而无人有效干预或行动。

【选项】 A) 偷换概念 they need to worry about their personal safety 把原文「无人干预他人」的话题偷换成「担心自身安全」，自身安全在 P3 里根本未提及。 B) 答非所问 The more people who witness an event, the less likely anyone will venture to 后半句 venture to 后无宾语，句子残缺；即便补全也只是 the more people who witness an event, the less likely anyone in that group is to help the victim 的 bystander effect 释义，而题干问的是 diffusion of responsibility 这一更深层心理机制，对应的是 P3 后半句而非这句。

C) 偷换概念 people idling around on the street 把原文 stand idly by 的「袖手旁观者」读成「街上闲逛的人」，并称他们「需要被照顾」，与 diffusion of responsibility 的心理机制无关。

D) ✓ 正确 the larger the crowd, the more people assume that someone else will take care of it ↔

The more people are around, the less chance someone will step forward to intervene 选项 D 的两段比较级与原文的两段比较级一一对应：人多→人多假定→更少人出手干预，与预判「越多越没人挺身而出」严丝合缝，故锁定 D。
questions.hint: 回到原文定位题干关键词，比较选项与原文的含义。

questions.prompt: What happens when unsafe behavior at the workplace is not addressed by the leaders?

options.text: No one will intervene when they see similar behaviors.
Everyone will see it as the easiest way to deal with crisis.
Workers have to take extra caution executing their duties.
Workers are left to take care of the emergency themselves.

questions.shortExplanation: When a group of employees sees unsafe behavior not being addressed at a leadership level it creates the precedent that this is how these situations should be addressed, thus defining the safety culture for everyone.
questions.detailedExplanation:
【答案】 A （细节题）

【判型】 What happens when unsafe behavior at the workplace is not addressed by the leaders? 问「当条件 X 成立时结果是什么」，答案为原文明文给出的客观后果。

【拆句】 主干 What happens when，when 引导时间/条件状语从句，从句主语 unsafe behavior at the workplace，谓语为被动语态 is not addressed by the leaders。注意被动否定结构，主体是「领导层不去处理」。

【定位】 When a group of employees sees unsafe behavior not being addressed at a leadership level it creates the precedent that this is how these situations should be addressed, thus defining the safety culture for everyone.

当一群员工看到领导层不处理不安全行为时，就会形成「这类情况就该这样处理」的先例， 从而为所有人定义了安全文化。

【选项】 A) ✓ 正确 it creates the precedent that this is how these situations should be addressed ↔

No one will intervene when they see similar behaviors 结合上下文（领导没干预+形成先例），先例的具体内容就是「对类似行为不干预」，选项 A 正是该先例的客观转述，故锁定 A。

B) 过度推断原文只说形成「该这样处理」的先例，并未评价它是 the easiest way；且「危机处理」 角度也是 crisis 强加的描述。 C) 无中生有 Workers have to take extra caution 在原文中找不到根据，原文是说大家集体不干预，并非「工人变得更小心」。 D) 与原文相反 Workers are left to take care of the emergency themselves 说工人会自己去处理紧急情况，而 P5 的逻辑是「没人去处理」，方向完全相反。
questions.hint: 回到原文定位题干关键词，比较选项与原文的含义。

questions.prompt: What is the ultimate reason workers won't act when they see unsafe operations?

options.text: Preference of deferring the action to others.
Fear of being isolated by coworkers.
Fear of having to do more work.

questions.shortExplanation: Fear is the ultimate factor in not intervening. There is a fear of penalty, a fear that they'll have to do more work if they intervene.
questions.detailedExplanation:
【答案】 D （细节题）

【判型】 What is the ultimate reason workers won't act when they see unsafe operations? 直问最终原因，答案为原文一句明文判断，非推断。

【拆句】 主干 What is the ultimate reason，后接省略了 why/that 的定语从句 workers won't act，再嵌套时间状语从句 when they see unsafe operations。注意「won't act」等价于 「don't intervene」。

【定位】 Fear is the ultimate factor in not intervening. There is a fear of penalty, a fear that they'll have to do more work if they intervene.

恐惧是不干预的最终因素。存在对惩罚的恐惧，以及对「一旦干预就得做更多工作」的恐惧。

【选项】 A) 答非所问 Preference of deferring the action to others 对应 they tend to prefer to defer that action to someone else for all future situations，但这是 Unsuccessful attempts in the past（过去失败经验）的副产品，是 another strong contributing factor，不是 ultimate factor。

B) 无中生有 Anticipation of leadership intervention 在 P6 没有依据。文中 P4 P5 提到 leadership 不干预，但谈的是「领导自己不出手」形成先例，而非「员工等领导干预」。 C) 无中生有 Fear of being isolated by coworkers 中「被同事孤立」在 P6 罗列的几种 fear （penalty / do more work / unsuccessful attempts）中并无对应。

D) ✓ 正确 a fear that they'll have to do more work if they intervene ↔ Fear of having to do more work 原文罗列了两类 fear，选项 D 把第二类「怕多干活」原样收纳，与预判完全一致，故锁定 D。
questions.hint: 回到原文定位题干关键词，比较选项与原文的含义。

questions.prompt: What is critical to ensuring workplace safety?

options.text: Workers be trained to operate their equipment properly.
Workers exhibiting at-risk behavior be strictly disciplined.
Supervisors create a safety environment for timely intervention.
Supervisors conduct effective communication with frontline workers.

questions.shortExplanation: Supervisors also play a critical role. Even if a competent person isn't required, supervisors need a broad set of skills to not only identify and alleviate workplace hazards but also build a safety climate within their team that supports intervening and open communication among them.
questions.detailedExplanation:
【答案】 C （细节题）

【判型】 What is critical to ensuring workplace safety? 问「对确保职场安全至关重要的是什么」，答案为原文显式给出的某项做法，非主旨概括。

【拆句】 主干 What is critical to ensuring workplace safety?，critical to 后接动名词短语 ensuring workplace safety 作介词宾语。注意 to 是介词不是不定式，故跟动名词。结构无陷阱。

【定位】 Supervisors also play a critical role. Even if a competent person isn't required, supervisors need a broad set of skills to not only identify and alleviate workplace hazards but also build a safety climate within their team that supports intervening and open communication among them.

主管也起着至关重要的作用。即便不需要专门的胜任人员，主管也需要一整套技能，既要能识别和消除职场隐患，也要在团队中营造支持干预和坦诚沟通的安全氛围。

【选项】 A) 无中生有 Workers be trained to operate their equipment properly 中「培训工人正确操作设备」在原文中无对应；without the proper equipment 谈的是「没有合适设备」，与 「培训操作设备」不是一回事。 B) 过度推断 Workers exhibiting at-risk behavior be strictly disciplined 中「对有风险行为的工人进行严厉惩戒」，P6 只是说工人怕 penalty，不代表全文主张要 strictly discipline，原文并未把「严厉惩戒」作为确保安全的做法。

C) ✓ 正确 build a safety climate within their team that supports intervening↔

Supervisors create a safety environment for timely intervention 主语对位（Supervisors↔Supervisors）、动作对位（build↔create）、对象对位 （safety climate↔safety environment）、目的对位（supports intervening↔for timely intervention），与预判一致，故锁定 C。

D) 以偏概全 Supervisors conduct effective communication with frontline workers 抓住了 open communication，但漏掉原文核心 build a safety climate within their team that supports intervening——主管的关键不仅是沟通，而是建立支持干预的安全氛围；且 communication with frontline workers 把原文 open communication among them （团队内部沟通）偷换为「主管与一线工人之间的沟通」，对象错位。

items.title: 2024年6月六级第1套 · 仔细阅读 · 第二篇
items.passage:
The term "environmentalist" can mean different things. It used to refer to people trying to protect wildlife and natural ecosystems. In the 21st century, the term has evolved to capture the need to combat human-made climate change.

The distinction between these two strands of environmentalism is the cause of a split within the scientific community about nuclear energy.

On one side are purists who believe nuclear power isn't worth the risk and the exclusive solution to the climate crisis is renewable energy. The opposing side agrees that renewables are crucial, but says society needs an amount of power available to meet consumers' basic demands when the sun isn't shining and the wind isn't blowing. Nuclear energy, being far cleaner than oil, gas and coal, is a natural option, especially where hydroelectric capacity is limited.

Leon Clarke, who helped author reports for the UN's Intergovernmental Panel on Climate Change, isn't an uncritical supporter of nuclear energy, but says it's a valuable option to have if we're serious about reaching carbon neutrality.

"Core to all of this is the degree to which you think we can actually meet climate goals with 100% renewables," he said. "If you don't believe we can do it, and you care about the climate, you are forced to think about something like nuclear."

The achievability of universal 100% renewability is similarly contentious. Cities such as Burlington, Vermont, have been "100% renewable" for years. But these cities often have small populations, occasionally still rely on fossil fuel energy and have significant renewable resources at their immediate disposal. Meanwhile, countries that manage to run off renewables typically do so thanks to extraordinary hydroelectric capabilities.

Germany stands as the best case study for a large, industrialized country pushing into green energy. Chancellor Angela Merkel in 2011 announced Energiewende, an energy transition that would phase out nuclear and coal while phasing in renewables. Wind and solar power generation has increased over 400% since 2010, and renewables provided 46% of the country's electricity in 2019.

But progress has halted in recent years. The instability of renewables doesn't just mean energy is often not produced at night, but also that solar and wind can overwhelm the grid during the day, forcing utilities to pay customers to use their electricity. Lagging grid infrastructure struggles to transport this overabundance of green energy from Germany's north to its industrial south, meaning many factories still run on coal and gas. The political limit has also been reached in some places, with citizens meeting the construction of new wind turbines with loud protests.

The result is that Germany's greenhouse gas emissions have fallen by around 11.5% since 2010 —slower than the EU average of 13.5%.

questions.prompt: What accounts for the divide within the scientific community about nuclear energy?

options.text: Attention to combating human-made climate change.
Emphasis on protecting wildlife and natural ecosystems.
Evolution of the term "green energy" over the last century.
Adherence to different interpretations of environmentalism.

questions.shortExplanation: The distinction between these two strands of environmentalism is the cause of a split within the scientific community about nuclear energy.
questions.detailedExplanation:
【答案】 D （细节题）

【判型】 What accounts for the divide within the scientific community about nuclear energy? 问的是"分裂的原因是什么"，是对原文具体因果关系的客观追问。

【拆句】 Q51 主语是疑问词 What，谓语 accounts for（=解释/导致），宾语是 the divide within the scientific community about nuclear energy，about 短语限定 divide 的具体领域。 结构清晰、无陷阱。

【定位】 The distinction between these two strands of environmentalism is the cause of a split within the scientific community about nuclear energy.

这两种环保主义之间的区别，正是科学界在核能问题上发生分裂的原因。

【选项】 A) 以偏概全 Attention to combating human-made climate change 只对应 P1 里 environmentalist 的"第二种含义"，不是"两种含义的差异"。 B) 以偏概全 Emphasis on protecting wildlife and natural ecosystems 只对应 P1 里 environmentalist 的"第一种含义"，同样只覆盖单侧。

C) 偷换概念原文谈的是 The term "environmentalist" 在 21 世纪的演变，Evolution of the term "green energy" over the last century 把术语换成了 green energy、时间换成了 the last century。 D) ✓ 正确 The distinction between these two strands of environmentalism ↔

Adherence to different interpretations of environmentalism 预判要求答案体现"对环保主义的不同理解→科学界分裂"这一因果链，Adherence to different interpretations of environmentalism 是四项中唯一精准覆盖该因果的表述。
questions.hint: 回到原文定位题干关键词，比较选项与原文的含义。

questions.prompt: What is the solution to energy shortage proposed by purists' opponents?

options.text: Relying on renewables firmly and exclusively.
Using fossil fuel and green energy alternately.
Opting for nuclear energy when necessary.

questions.shortExplanation: The opposing side agrees that renewables are crucial, but says society needs an amount of power available to meet consumers' basic demands when the sun isn't shining and the wind isn't blowing. Nuclear energy, being far cleaner than oil, gas and coal, is a natural option, especially where hydroelectric capacity is limited.
questions.detailedExplanation:
【答案】 C （细节题）

【判型】 What is the solution to energy shortage proposed by purists\' opponents? 问对立方提出的具体方案，是原文已有的客观表述。

【拆句】 Q52 主干 What is the solution，to energy shortage 修饰 solution，过去分词短语 proposed by purists\' opponents 后置修饰 solution。注意 purists\' 是所有格， opponents 才是真正的主语方。

【定位】 The opposing side agrees that renewables are crucial, but says society needs an amount of power available to meet consumers' basic demands when the sun isn't shining and the wind isn't blowing. Nuclear energy, being far cleaner than oil, gas and coal, is a natural option, especially where hydroelectric capacity is limited.

对立方认同可再生能源关键，但表示在阳光不足、无风时社会仍需一定量电力以满足消费者的基本需求。核能比油、气、煤都清洁得多，是自然之选，尤其在水电能力有限的地方。

【选项】 A) 与原文相反 Relying on renewables firmly and exclusively 描述的恰恰是 purists 的立场，而非对立方——对立方主张的是核能补缺，绝不"独占"可再生能源。

B) 无中生有 Using fossil fuel and green energy alternately 谈"化石燃料和绿色能源交替使用"， 原文从未提出过"交替使用"这一方案，且对立方明确说核能 far cleaner than oil, gas and coal，即反对烧煤气油。 C) ✓ 正确 Nuclear energy, being far cleaner than oil, gas and coal, is a natural option, especially where hydroelectric capacity is limited

↔ Opting for nuclear energy when necessary 预判结论"必要时启用核能补缺"在四项中只有 Opting for nuclear energy when necessary 精准匹配。

D) 无中生有 Limiting people\'s non-basic consumption 谈"限制非基本消费"，原文只提 consumers\' basic demands——"满足基本需求"和"限制非基本消费"是两回事，后者属凭空引申。
questions.hint: 回到原文定位题干关键词，比较选项与原文的含义。

questions.prompt: What point does the author want to make with cities like Burlington as an example?

options.text: It is controversial whether the goal of the whole world's exclusive dependence on renewables is attainable.
It is contentious whether cities with large populations have renewable resources at their immediate disposal.
It is arguable whether cities that manage to run off renewables have sustainable hydroelectric capabilities.
It is debatable whether traditional fossil fuel energy can be done away with entirely throughout the world.

questions.shortExplanation: The achievability of universal 100% renewability is similarly contentious. Cities such as Burlington, Vermont, have been "100% renewable" for years.
questions.detailedExplanation:
【答案】 A （例证目的题）

【判型】 What point does the author want to make with cities like Burlington as an example? 直接问"举这个例子是为了说明什么"，是典型例证目的题。

【拆句】 Q53 主干 What point does the author want to make，介词短语 with cities like Burlington as an example 作伴随状语，说明作者作出该 point 时所凭借的例子。with… as… 是"以……作为……"的固定结构。

【定位】 The achievability of universal 100% renewability is similarly contentious. Cities such as Burlington, Vermont, have been "100% renewable" for years.

全球 100% 可再生能源是否能实现同样有争议。像佛蒙特州 Burlington 这样的城市多年来一直号称"100% 可再生"。

【选项】 A) ✓ 正确 The achievability of universal 100% renewability is similarly contentious ↔

It is controversial whether the goal of the whole world\'s exclusive dependence on renewables is attainable 预判结论包含三要素"全球范围、独占可再生、可达成性存疑"，A 是四项中唯一同时覆盖三要素的表述。

B) 偷换概念 cities with large populations have renewable resources at their immediate disposal 谈"大人口城市是否有可再生资源"，原文 P6 只说 Burlington 这类"小人口"城市，并未把议题转向"大人口城市能否做到"。 C) 偷换概念原文 countries that manage to run off renewables typically do so thanks to extraordinary hydroelectric capabilities 只说"靠可再生运转的国家"通常水电禀赋强， 并未质疑其"可持续性"；选项 sustainable hydroelectric capabilities 把客观描述偷换为"是否可持续"的争议。

D) 过度推断 traditional fossil fuel energy can be done away with entirely throughout the world 谈"是否能在全球范围彻底废除化石燃料"，原文只论"是否能 100% 可再生"，并未直接讨论"彻底废除化石燃料"，两者虽相关但不等价。
questions.hint: 回到原文定位题干关键词，比较选项与原文的含义。

questions.prompt: What do we learn about Germany regarding renewable energy?

options.text: It has increased its wind and solar power generation four times over the last two decades.
It represents a good example of a major industrialized country promoting green energy.
It relies on renewable energy to generate more than half of its electricity.
It has succeeded in reaching the goal of energy transition set by Merkel.

questions.shortExplanation: Germany stands as the best case study for a large, industrialized country pushing into green energy.
questions.detailedExplanation:
【答案】 B （细节题）

【判型】 What do we learn about Germany regarding renewable energy? 是对原文中关于德国可再生能源相关事实的复核问题。

【拆句】 Q54 主干 What do we learn about Germany，regarding renewable energy 介词短语限定话题范围（regarding=关于）。句式平铺，无陷阱。

【定位】 Germany stands as the best case study for a large, industrialized country pushing into green energy.

德国是大型工业化国家推进绿色能源的最佳案例。

【选项】 A) 偷换概念原文 Wind and solar power generation has increased over 400% since 2010 是"自 2010 年以来"约 10 年，而 over the last two decades 是"过去二十年"——时间维度被夸大一倍。 B) ✓ 正确 Germany stands as the best case study for a large, industrialized country pushing into green energy

↔ It represents a good example of a major industrialized country promoting green energy 预判结论"大型工业国推进绿能的范本"与 B 在主谓宾每个成分上都做到同义替换，是最高质量的同义匹配。 C) 偷换概念原文 renewables provided 46% of the country\'s electricity in 2019 是 46%，more than half 是">50%"——46% 显然不到一半，是数字偷换。

D) 与原文相反原文只说默克尔 2011 年宣布 Energiewende，未说德国"已成功达成"该目标；事实上 But progress has halted in recent years 直接表明进展停滞，说明远未达成。
questions.hint: 回到原文定位题干关键词，比较选项与原文的含义。

questions.prompt: What may be one of the reasons for Germany's progress having halted in recent years?

options.text: Its grid infrastructure's capacity has fallen behind its development of green energy.
Its overabundance of green energy has forced power plants to suspend operation during daytime.
Its industrial south is used to running factories on conventional energy supplies.
Its renewable energy supplies are unstable both at night and during the day.

questions.shortExplanation: Lagging grid infrastructure struggles to transport this overabundance of green energy from Germany's north to its industrial south, meaning many factories still run on coal and gas.
questions.detailedExplanation:
【答案】 A （细节题）

【判型】 What may be one of the reasons for Germany\'s progress having halted in recent years? 问"原因之一"，对应原文列出多条原因中的一条，本质是细节复述。

【拆句】 Q55 主干 What may be one of the reasons，介词短语 for Germany\'s progress having halted 后置修饰 reasons，其中 having halted 是动名词完成式作 progress 的语义谓语，表明"进展已经停滞"这件事。in recent years 是时间状语。

【定位】 Lagging grid infrastructure struggles to transport this overabundance of green energy from Germany's north to its industrial south, meaning many factories still run on coal and gas.

滞后的电网基础设施难以把过剩的绿电从德国北部输送到工业化南部，这意味着许多工厂仍靠煤气运转。

【选项】 A) ✓ 正确 Lagging grid infrastructure struggles to transport this overabundance of green energy↔

Its grid infrastructure\'s capacity has fallen behind its development of green energy 预判结论"电网跟不上绿电规模"在四项中只有 A 精准命中，主语"grid infrastructure"与原文同名重合，谓语"has fallen behind"与 Lagging 同义。

B) 偷换概念原文 solar and wind can overwhelm the grid during the day, forcing utilities to pay customers to use their electricity 是"电网超负荷迫使电力公司付钱让顾客用电"， forced power plants to suspend operation during daytime 把"付钱让顾客用电"偷换为"电厂停运"，主语和动作均失实。 C) 偷换概念原文 many factories still run on coal and gas 是"由于电网无法把北部绿电输到南部"这一被动结果；Its industrial south is used to running factories on conventional energy supplies 把它说成"南部工业区习惯于用传统能源"——把客观限制偷换为主观习惯。 D) 偷换概念原文 The instability of renewables doesn\'t just mean energy is often not produced at night, but also that solar and wind can overwhelm the grid during the day 是"不仅夜里没电、白天还过剩"——表面看选项 D 似乎和原文一致，但 unstable both at night and during the day 把"夜间缺供+白天过剩"这一具体二元情况偷换为笼统的"昼夜都不稳定"，丢失了关键差异。
questions.hint: 回到原文定位题干关键词，比较选项与原文的含义。

items.title: 2024年6月六级第2套 · 选词填空
items.passage:
The Sun Is Also a Star is a truly lovely story of love, romance, fate, and destiny.

Natasha is a Jamaican-born immigrant living [26] _____ in America, not by choice exactly. Her parents brought her over and created the situation she [27] _____ to be out of.

Daniel is an American born of Korean immigrants. He believes in true love, fate, and all that other nonsense that Natasha [28] _____ through scientific reasoning.

Daniel and Natasha meet by [29] _____ on the streets of New York on the day that she is to be [30] _____ . She doesn't tell him that but does allow him to keep her company while he tries to get her to fall in love with him over the course of the day.

Natasha is me. I found her so similar to myself. She's scientifically-minded, practical, somewhat cynical, and always [31] _____ . Her obsession with the universe through a scientific lens is infectious and I [32] _____ Daniel seeing that too.

Daniel is charming and passionate and has a way with words that even [33] _____ Natasha's tough outer shell. By the end of the book I fell in love with both of them.

I used to find romance stories to always be cheap or laughable. I think now I can see the value in escaping into a story of pure optimism. I got [34] _____ in The Sun Is Also a Star and finished it cover to cover in a weekend. I couldn't wait to get to what I hoped would be a happy ending.

It's nice every once in a while to give in to magic. It doesn't have to be a hard fantasy novel with actual spells, it can be the magic found between two people who just have that special something. That [35] _____ that causes them to react and spark when they're near each other.

questions.prompt: Natasha is a Jamaican-born immigrant living __(26)__ in America
questions.shortExplanation: 与下句「想脱离的处境」呼应=非法滞留紧接着的 Her parents brought her over and created the situation she __(27)__ to be out of. 说明父母带她过来、造成了她想摆脱的「处境」——这种典型「移民却想脱身」的处境就是「非法居留」。illegally 修饰 living，正好把这条暗线一句话点透。
questions.detailedExplanation:
【答案】 I) illegally 副词

【词性槽】 living 后缺修饰语，需副词

【依据】 与下句「想脱离的处境」呼应=非法滞留紧接着的 Her parents brought her over and created the situation she __(27)__ to be out of. 说明父母带她过来、造成了她想摆脱的「处境」——这种典型「移民却想脱身」的处境就是「非法居留」。illegally 修饰 living，正好把这条暗线一句话点透。

【竞争词】 K) perpetually 语义不指向她想脱离的困境

perpetually=「永久地」只描述时间长度，无法解释她「想 be out of」的那种处境，与后文的脱身意愿不咬合。
questions.hint: 根据空格前后的词性、搭配与上下文选择词语；每个词最多使用一次。

questions.prompt: the situation she __(27)__ to be out of
questions.shortExplanation: strive to be out of=努力摆脱
questions.detailedExplanation:
【答案】 O) strives 动词

【词性槽】 she 后缺谓语 + to be 不定式

【依据】 strive to be out of=努力摆脱

Natasha 想摆脱「非法居留即将被遣返」的处境，strives to be out of 正好表达「她一直在努力跳出这处境」的奋斗感，与全文中她「practical、cynical、scientifically-minded」 的人物形象一致。
questions.hint: 根据空格前后的词性、搭配与上下文选择词语；每个词最多使用一次。

questions.prompt: all that other nonsense that Natasha __(28)__ through scientific reasoning
questions.shortExplanation: dismiss=不予理会、驳回她对 Daniel 那些「真爱、命运」之类的「nonsense（胡说八道）」用「scientific reasoning（科学推理）」来对待——最贴的就是「dismiss=驳回 / 不予理会」。一个 skeptical 的人对超验信念的标准反应就是 dismiss。
questions.detailedExplanation:
【答案】 H) dismisses 动词

【词性槽】 定语从句中 Natasha 后缺谓语

【依据】 dismiss=不予理会、驳回她对 Daniel 那些「真爱、命运」之类的「nonsense（胡说八道）」用「scientific reasoning（科学推理）」来对待——最贴的就是「dismiss=驳回 / 不予理会」。一个 skeptical 的人对超验信念的标准反应就是 dismiss。

【竞争词】 C) assaults 攻击太过激烈，搭配也不自然

assault 一般指人身/语言上的猛烈攻击，「用科学推理 assault 胡话」搭配生硬、语气也过激， 不像理性书评的写法。

F) cracks crack 通常指「攻破壳/裂开」，留给 33 题

crack 的「击破外壳」义更贴合 33 题 that even __(33)__ Natasha's tough outer shell 那种 「攻破她那层硬壳」的形象化表达，把它放在这里会和那条线抢词。

【易错】 最具迷惑性的错误词是 F) —— cracks 极易被误填到 28。cracks 也是 -s 动词、也能搭 「攻破 nonsense」，但它真正的家在 33 题的 outer shell；若 28 用了 cracks，33 题就只能勉强配 assaults，全篇逻辑塌方。防坑口诀：看到 outer shell/wall 这种 metaphor 宾语，先把 crack 留给它。
questions.hint: 根据空格前后的词性、搭配与上下文选择词语；每个词最多使用一次。

questions.prompt: Daniel and Natasha meet by __(29)__ on the streets of New York
questions.shortExplanation: by coincidence=偶然地，固定搭配
questions.detailedExplanation:
【答案】 E) coincidence 名词

【词性槽】 介词 by 后接名词

【依据】 by coincidence=偶然地，固定搭配

by coincidence 是英语里非常稳定的方式状语短语，意为「偶然、巧合地」；正好对应 The Sun Is Also a Star is a truly lovely story of love, romance, fate, and destiny. 里反复出现的「命运」基调——两个陌生人街头偶遇、命中注定的故事开端。

【竞争词】 D) chemistry 搭配不立 + 语义留给最后一空

by chemistry 不是英语固定搭配；而且 chemistry「人与人之间的默契火花」更适合留给 35 题里 That __(35)__ that causes them to react and spark when they're near each other. 那种 「化学反应」语义。
questions.hint: 根据空格前后的词性、搭配与上下文选择词语；每个词最多使用一次。

questions.prompt: she is to be __(30)__
questions.shortExplanation: 与 26 题非法居留对应=即将被驱逐
questions.detailedExplanation:
【答案】 G) deported 动词

【词性槽】 be to be __(30)__ 是被动不定式

【依据】 与 26 题非法居留对应=即将被驱逐

26 题已经定下 Natasha 是 Natasha is a Jamaican-born immigrant living __(26)__ in America 非法身份；那么「她今天即将 be __(30)__」最合逻辑的就是「被驱逐出境」 （deported），整本书最大的戏剧张力——一日相恋、当晚遣返——也由此而来。

【竞争词】 L) prescribed 语义指向开药/规定，不切人物处境

prescribed=「被规定 / 被开药」，与一个非法移民、纽约街头偶遇的剧情语境完全脱节，属于看着是过去分词却被语义淘汰。
questions.hint: 根据空格前后的词性、搭配与上下文选择词语；每个词最多使用一次。

questions.prompt: She's scientifically-minded, practical, somewhat cynical, and always __(31)__.
questions.shortExplanation: 与 scientifically-minded、cynical 同向 skeptical「怀疑论的」与前面 scientifically-minded（科学头脑）、cynical（愤世）属于同一族——理性、不轻信。下一段 He believes in true love, fate, and all that other nonsense that Natasha __(28)__ through scientific reasoning. 也再次印证她「凡事用科学理性质疑」。
questions.detailedExplanation:
【答案】 N) skeptical 形容词

【词性槽】 she is 的并列表语

【依据】 与 scientifically-minded、cynical 同向 skeptical「怀疑论的」与前面 scientifically-minded（科学头脑）、cynical（愤世）属于同一族——理性、不轻信。下一段 He believes in true love, fate, and all that other nonsense that Natasha __(28)__ through scientific reasoning. 也再次印证她「凡事用科学理性质疑」。

【竞争词】 M) shrewd shrewd 是「精明」，与「不信」无关

shrewd 形容人「精明、商业上敏锐」，更偏褒义的判断力强，跟前文「scientifically-minded、cynical」的「怀疑、不轻信」语义族对不上。
questions.hint: 根据空格前后的词性、搭配与上下文选择词语；每个词最多使用一次。

questions.prompt: and I __(32)__ Daniel seeing that too
questions.shortExplanation: adore + sb. + doing=超爱看到某人做某事
questions.detailedExplanation:
【答案】 A) adore 动词

【词性槽】 主语 I 后缺谓语

【依据】 adore + sb. + doing=超爱看到某人做某事

items.title: 2024年6月六级第2套 · 信息匹配
items.passage:
A) According to recent research, behavioral change involves physical changes in the brain. In the past decade, researchers have shown that when it comes to the duration of making a new behavior a deep-rooted habit there is not a simple answer. Even for the most productive and disciplined among us, undoing something that has become an automatic part of who we are takes more than an overnight effort. Once we've successfully made that change, we then have to make other adjustments to our lives to ensure that we continue to maintain it, which is often a whole other challenge in itself.

B) At its core, success in changing and maintaining a behavior rarely occurs without the introduction of some sort of system. When there isn't the right framework in place, we face a greater likelihood of derailing our hard-earned progress. To ensure success in changing and maintaining a behavior, we should stay away from some detrimental habits.

C) The first one to avoid is relying on willpower. Think about the last time you vowed to resist a temptation. Perhaps you didn't want to check your phone every 15 minutes, or you were determined not to reach for a chocolate bar at 3 p. m. Think about how difficult it must have been not to glance at your phone when it was within reach, or not to walk to the vending machine when your afternoon slump hit.

D) The research on whether we have finite or infinite willpower is inconclusive, but experts do generally agree that you can't change and sustain a habit if you rely on your willpower alone. The old military saying "You never rise to the occasion, you only sink to the level of training" also applies to behavior change. The idea is simple—you repeat something so many times that it becomes automatic.

E) Think about what else you can change about your surrounding that makes it easier for you to perform this change on a daily basis. This is called your "cue." Basically, it's a trigger to perform that particular habit. If you don't want to reach for a sugary treat at 3 p. m. , have a box of herbal tea ready at your desk. When 3 p. m. comes around, that's your cue to pour yourself a cup of hot water and drink that tea, instead of walking to the vending machine.

F) The second one to avoid is focusing on negative goals. Sometimes, it's not your process that lets you down, but the habit that you want to change in the first place. For starters, not eating chocolate to beat your afternoon slump is a harder goal than swapping chocolate for herbal tea when you reach the designated time. Your brain wants to find routines that have succeeded in the past and allow you to repeat those actions again in the future without having to think about them explicitly. However, this habit-learning system isn't so effective when it comes to learning not to do something. That's why rather than giving up something, think about introducing something in its place. Focus on actions you are going to take that will ultimately conflict with the behaviors you want to stop. When your attention is on doing something new, you give your habit system a chance to operate.

G) The third one to avoid is using the same strategies in different circumstances. Because we are creatures of habit, it's natural to assume that when we do manage to adopt and sustain a desirable behavior, that same strategy will work when we want to make another behavior change. But that's not always the case. Sometimes, the system that got you to change one behavior might not work for another.

H) Sometimes we become accustomed to relying on our guts when it comes to decision-making. This serves us well in certain situations, but can hinder us in others especially when we need to consider metrics and data, rather than letting our instinct override everything. For example, if you want to stop checking your email first thing in the morning, you might decide to substitute another activity in its place. But if you want to stop indulging in video games, simply deciding you will go for a run might not be as effective. You might need to introduce another reinforcement, such as meeting a friend and booking an exercise class together.

I) The fourth one to avoid is not forgiving ourselves for slipping up. Of course, even the best-laid plans fail sometimes. You might have stuck to your screen-free nighttime routine for five days, and then a big project landed on your desk and you found yourself in bed with your laptop before you went to sleep. Or you prepared meals on Sunday and stuck to eating healthy dinners at home, but by Friday you found yourself so exhausted and opted to order greasy takeout. Life happens and even if your behavior change is small, every single day can prove pretty inflexible, and at some point your luck may run out, even if just for a day. The perfectionist in you might be screaming to abandon your goals altogether, but try to see it in the bigger picture. Just because you might have temporarily strayed off course doesn't mean you can't start afresh the next day.

J) The final one to avoid is discounting small progress. There's a habit that many perfectionists tend to fall into when they try to establish a behavior change. They focus too much on the big goal and don't take the time to celebrate the small progress they make in the process. Your brain responds to rewards. The basal ganglia, the brain region linked to our performance of habits, is most active at the beginning of a behavior, when the habit is cued, and at the end, when it's rewarded. Say your goal is to run five miles three times a week, and this week you ran one mile on Monday, Wednesday, and Friday. Rather than focusing on how far you've gone toward your goal, think about how you can reward yourself for the progress you've made. It doesn't have to be big or expensive; it can be something as simple as making your favorite fruit juice after your run. Whatever your reward, it has to be more than just the activity itself to get you going.

K) Initiating a new behavior usually seems like the hardest part of the process of change. However, people often fail to adequately prepare for maintaining it. One of the reasons for this is because we mistakenly believe the strategies we used to initiate the change will be equally effective in helping us continue the change. But they won't. Where changing a strongly deep-rooted habit requires changing our belief about that habit that penetrates deeply into our lives, continually manifesting that wisdom requires that we maintain a positive outlook. If our mood is low, the wisdom to behave differently seems to disappear and we go back to eating more and exercising less. The key, then, to maintaining new behaviors is to be happy! Which is why it's so hard to maintain new behaviors.

L) Remember, overcoming the behavioral inertia that prevents us from implementing new changes, like eating a healthy diet or exercising, can benefit us in the long run and can improve our physical and mental health. No one was born with habits. They were all learned, and can all, therefore, be unlearned. The question is: how badly do you really want to change?

items.title: 2024年6月六级第2套 · 仔细阅读 · 第一篇
items.passage:
The "American Dream" promises that in the Land of Opportunity, any individual can climb the economic ladder and prosper through hard work and ambition alone. And yet, young Americans today are struggling to earn more than their parents did at the same age, and upward mobility in the US actually compares unfavourably to that of other industrialised nations.

So why does the idea of the American Dream persist? A new study in the American Journal of Political Science identifies one factor that has been overlooked: the influence of reality TV.

Reality shows have come to dominate US television over the past 20 years, notes Eunji Kim from Vanderbilt University. And the overwhelming majority of these have a "rags-to-riches" storyline: they feature ordinary Americans who work hard to achieve great economic success. And while these programmes are regularly among the most-watched shows, news broadcasts—which paint a more realistic view of the economic hardship faced by millions of Americans—get a much smaller proportion of the viewership.

Rags-to-riches stories are ubiquitous(⽆处不在的 ) on TV—but does watching these programmes actually convince people that economic mobility is easily attainable? To find out, Kim's team had participants watch a 5-minute clip from a reality show with a rags-to-riches storyline. Control participants watched a clip from a reality show that didn't have a rags-to-riches story. After watching the shows, participants rated how much they agreed with four statements relating to the American Dream.

The results showed that those who'd watched a rags-to-riches clip did indeed have a significantly greater belief in the American Dream. Interestingly, when participants were separated by party affiliation, this effect was significant among Republicans but not Democrats, suggesting that the kind of messages implicit in these TV shows may play into people's existing socioeconomic beliefs.

Kim also conducted a survey of 3,000 US residents. They also rated the extent to which they believed success in life is related to various internal factors (such as ambition) and external factors (such as family wealth). Finally, they read a list of TV programmes and indicated which they regularly watched.

Participants who were heavy viewers of rags-to-riches programmes or frequent viewers had a stronger belief in the American Dream than those who never watched such shows.

Kim concludes that "rags-to-riches entertainment media are an important cultural force that promotes and perpetuates beliefs in upward mobility". And here's the problem: if people mistakenly believe that hard work is all that is needed for individuals to make a better life for themselves, they may be less supportive of policies that could actually combat inequality.

"In this era of choice, entertainment media is what captures hearts and minds," Kim writes. "Its political consequences are anything but trivial".

questions.prompt: What do we learn from the passage about young Americans of today?

questions.shortExplanation: And yet, young Americans today are struggling to earn more than their parents did at the same age, and upward mobility in the US actually compares unfavourably to that of other industrialised nations.
questions.detailedExplanation:
【答案】 B （细节题）

【判型】 What do we learn from the passage about young Americans of today 明确问的是关于某个具体群体的事实信息，没有出现 infer / imply / mainly about 等推断或主旨信号。

【拆句】 题干主干是 What do we learn from the passage about young Americans of today？ about 引导的介宾短语限定 learn 的对象。介词 about 把『青年美国人』锁为定位词，结构平铺无陷阱。

【定位】 And yet, young Americans today are struggling to earn more than their parents did at the same age, and upward mobility in the US actually compares unfavourably to that of other industrialised nations.

然而，今天的美国年轻人正在艰难地试图挣得比父辈同龄时更多的收入，而且美国的向上流动性事实上比其他工业化国家逊色。

【选项】 A) 无中生有原文只说他们在收入上难超父辈，从未比较两代人的『抱负』。

B) ✓ 正确 struggling to earn more than their parents did at the same age ↔

find it difficult to achieve upward mobility upward mobility in the US actually compares unfavourably ↔ upward mobility 预判结论是『难以向上流动』，选项 B 几乎是这句话的字面化，二者构成最直接的同义替换。 C) 与原文相反原文说青年正在 struggling to earn more than their parents，意即尚未超过；C 选项却说 overtaken their parents in terms of earnings，恰好相反。

D) 过度推断原文只把美国向上流动与其他工业化国家比较得出『美国更差』，从未提及青年的情绪态度，更未说他们 envy。

questions.prompt: What does Kim's team find about reality TV shows in America?

options.text: They reinterpret the essence of the popular rags-to-riches culture.
They urge people to achieve economic success through hard work.
They help strengthen people's conviction in the American Dream.
They feature ordinary Americans striving for social recognition.

questions.shortExplanation: The results showed that those who'd watched a rags-to-riches clip did indeed have a significantly greater belief in the American Dream.
questions.detailedExplanation:
【答案】 C （细节题）

【判型】 What does Kim’s team find about reality TV shows in America 问的是研究团队的具体发现，是对原文实验结论的事实性提问。

【拆句】 主干 What does Kim’s team find about reality TV shows，about 引出研究对象。结构干净，无从句无陷阱。

【定位】 The results showed that those who'd watched a rags-to-riches clip did indeed have a significantly greater belief in the American Dream.

结果显示，那些看过『白手起家』短片的人确实显著加深了对美国梦的信仰。

【选项】 A) 无中生有原文只说真人秀展示 rags-to-riches storyline 并验证其加深观众信仰，从未提到节目在 『重新诠释』该文化的本质。

B) 偷换概念 they feature ordinary Americans who work hard to achieve great economic success 的主语是节目所呈现的人物在努力，而非节目敦促观众去努力。

C) ✓ 正确 significantly greater belief in the American Dream ↔

help strengthen people’s conviction in the American Dream 预判为『真人秀加深美国梦信仰』，选项 C 把『加深』表达为 help strengthen，把 『美国梦信仰』表达为 conviction in the American Dream，二者一一对应。 D) 偷换概念原文明确写 great economic success，与选项的 social recognition 不是一回事。

questions.prompt: What does the author say about news broadcasts in America?

options.text: They attract far fewer viewers than reality TV.
They are bent on reporting the dark side of life.
They stand in striking contrast with reality TV.
They focus on Americans' economic hardships.

questions.shortExplanation: And while these programmes are regularly among the most-watched shows, news broadcasts —which paint a more realistic view of the economic hardship faced by millions of Americans —get a much smaller proportion of the viewership. 而尽管这些节目（真人秀）经常位列收视率最高的电视节目之列，新闻播报——它们描绘了数以百万计的美国人所面临的经济困境这一更现实的图景——只占据小得多的观众份额。
questions.detailedExplanation:
【答案】 A （细节题）

【判型】 What does the author say about news broadcasts in America 问对某具体对象的陈述， 没有 infer / suggest，是事实型细节题。

【拆句】 主干 What does the author say about news broadcasts in America。结构平铺直叙，无陷阱。

【定位】 And while these programmes are regularly among the most-watched shows, news broadcasts —which paint a more realistic view of the economic hardship faced by millions of Americans —get a much smaller proportion of the viewership. 而尽管这些节目（真人秀）经常位列收视率最高的电视节目之列，新闻播报——它们描绘了数以百万计的美国人所面临的经济困境这一更现实的图景——只占据小得多的观众份额。

【选项】 A) ✓ 正确 get a much smaller proportion of the viewership ↔ attract far fewer viewers than reality TV 预判结论是『观众远少于真人秀』，选项 A 把 smaller proportion 改写为 far fewer viewers，把对照对象明示为 reality TV，与定位句的对比关系完全一致。 B) 过度推断 paint a more realistic view of the economic hardship 只描述了新闻所呈现的内容， 并未对新闻的意图作 be bent on（一心要、决意）这种主观倾向判断。

C) 偷换概念原文用 while 引出对比，但描述对象是『收视份额』，并未对新闻与真人秀做 striking contrast（鲜明反差）的整体定性评价。

D) 以偏概全 paint a more realistic view of the economic hardship 是把经济困境作为更真实图景的一部分来呈现，并未说新闻 focus on（聚焦于）经济困境；况且 Q48 问的是作者对新闻的总评，而 D 只是从句里附带说明的内容。
questions.hint: 回到原文定位题干关键词，比较选项与原文的含义。

questions.prompt: What can we infer from the passage about Republicans in general?

options.text: They believe strongly in the American Dream.
They strive to climb the socio-economic ladder.
They have a very strong affiliation with their party.
They tend to watch more rags-to-riches TV shows.

questions.shortExplanation: Interestingly, when participants were separated by party affiliation, this effect was significant among Republicans but not Democrats, suggesting that the kind of messages implicit in these TV shows may play into people's existing socioeconomic beliefs.
questions.detailedExplanation:
【答案】 A （推断题）

【判型】 What can we infer from the passage about Republicans in general 中明确出现 infer， 是典型推断信号。

【拆句】 主干 What can we infer from the passage about Republicans in general。in general 提示答案不应是局部小结论，而是适用于该群体的整体性推断。

【定位】 Interestingly, when participants were separated by party affiliation, this effect was significant among Republicans but not Democrats, suggesting that the kind of messages implicit in these TV shows may play into people's existing socioeconomic beliefs.

有趣的是，当按党派分组时，这种效应在共和党人中显著、而在民主党人中不显著，这意味着真人秀里隐含的信息可能契合了人们既有的社会经济观念。

【选项】 A) ✓ 正确 this effect was significant among Republicans but not Democrats ↔

believe strongly in the American Dream play into people’s existing socioeconomic beliefs ↔ believe strongly in the American Dream 预判结论是『共和党人本就更信美国梦』，选项 A 是这一推断的标准表达。 B) 无中生有原文只比较了党派对美国梦的信念差异，从未提到任一党派的人在 socio-economic ladder 上的实际行动。 C) 偷换概念 when participants were separated by party affiliation 中 party affiliation 只是『按党派分组』的研究操作变量，并未评价共和党人对自己政党的归属感强弱。

D) 过度推断原文只说看了 rags-to-riches 短片后，对美国梦信仰加深的效应在共和党人中显著；并未说共和党人比民主党人更常或更多地观看此类节目。
questions.hint: 回到原文定位题干关键词，比较选项与原文的含义。

questions.prompt: What is stated about people who believe in upward mobility?

options.text: They are likely to blame the government for their plight.
They regard political consequences as anything but trivial.
They respect individuals striving to climb the social ladder.
They are less likely to approve of policies to fight inequality.

questions.shortExplanation: And here's the problem: if people mistakenly believe that hard work is all that is needed for individuals to make a better life for themselves, they may be less supportive of policies that could actually combat inequality.
questions.detailedExplanation:
【答案】 D （细节题）

【判型】 What is stated about people who believe in upward mobility 用 stated 询问对该人群所作的陈述，是细节题。

【拆句】 主干 What is stated about people…？被动语态，who believe in upward mobility 是 people 的定语从句，提示要找作者直接说明这类人会怎样的句子。

【定位】 And here's the problem: if people mistakenly believe that hard work is all that is needed for individuals to make a better life for themselves, they may be less supportive of policies that could actually combat inequality.

问题就在这里：如果人们错误地以为只要努力工作就足以让个人过上更好的生活，他们就可能更不支持那些其实能对抗不平等的政策。

【选项】 A) 无中生有 P8 只说他们更不支持反不平等政策，从未提到他们指责政府或抱怨自身困境。

B) 张冠李戴 Its political consequences are anything but trivial 中代词 Its 指向 entertainment media；选项 B 把这一评价偷塞到『相信向上流动者』身上，属于张冠李戴。 C) 无中生有原文只说他们因为相信努力万能而更不支持反不平等政策，从未提到他们对其他奋斗者的态度（如尊敬）。

D) ✓ 正确 they may be less supportive of policies that could actually combat inequality↔

less likely to approve of policies to fight inequality 预判结论『更不支持反不平等政策』与选项 D 完全等义，combat 与 fight 是六级阅读高频可互换词。

items.title: 2024年6月六级第2套 · 仔细阅读 · 第二篇
items.passage:
When someone asks us 'what do you do?' we nearly always reply with our occupation. Work, for many of us, is much more than a job. It is the defining aspect of our identity. For many of us it is through our job that we can define ourselves.

"Without my job I don't know who I am," is a sentence that has been uttered on more than a handful of occasions from my office chair. Indeed, it can be one of the most challenging aspects I work on with clients who have lost or been forced into changing their jobs. This loss provokes an identity crisis much greater than the loss of the job itself.

One of the things I have come to understand, however, is that our identity is much more complex than we recognise at first glance. If we take the time to reflect we might recognise that as well as our work we can also identify as a friend, a spouse, a son or daughter, a parent, a member of a sports team or religious community. We may recognise that we feel and act differently in these roles and relationships than we do at work. The passive daughter becomes an assertive leader at work. Furthermore, our identities at work are not static. They change over time. I myself have been a shop assistant, a waitress, a student, a graduate, and a clinical psychologist. At each stage my ability to adapt to and develop my career identity has been crucial to my wellbeing. Whilst we like to eliminate uncertainty in our lives at some level we have to manage uncertainty, especially in today's volatile and ever-shifting job market.

How we see ourselves is central to the issue of our identity. When we tell ourselves "I'm good at starting projects but not so great at seeing them through" it can become part of our belief system. But if you have the unfortunate experience of an enforced job change you will need to examine those beliefs to see how grounded in reality they are. You will be required to ask yourself how helpful these beliefs are and consider personal change. We can change our beliefs, behaviours and emotional experience at any time through experimentation, practice and conscious self-discipline. In an age where career progression may lead us into new sectors it is ever more important to challenge our sense of self and explore whether you can create a new experience of your identity by changing the beliefs you hold about yourself in order to expand your career options. Ultimately it is you who define who you are. You are only your job if you let it be so.

questions.prompt: What do we learn from the passage about one's loss of a job?

options.text: It compels them to visit a clinical psychologist.
It offers them a chance to play different roles.
It renders them puzzled about who they are.
It forces them to redefine their life's goals.

questions.shortExplanation: "Without my job I don't know who I am," is a sentence that has been uttered on more than a handful of occasions from my office chair. Indeed, it can be one of the most challenging aspects I work on with clients who have lost or been forced into changing their jobs. This loss provokes an identity crisis much greater than the loss of the job itself. 「没有了工作，我就不知道自己是谁」——这话在我办公室的椅子上不止一次被来访者说出。事实上，与那些失去或被迫更换工作的来访者一起处理这种感受，是我工作中最具挑战的部分之一。这种失落所引发的身份危机，要远远大于失业本身。
questions.detailedExplanation:
【答案】 C （细节题）

【判型】 What do we learn from the passage about one's loss of a job? 指向一个具体事实—— 失业会带来什么——并未问推断或主旨。

【拆句】 主干 What do we learn from the passage 中 we 是主语、learn 是谓语；about one's loss of a job 是 learn 的范围介词短语，指明问的对象是「失去工作这件事」。句式平铺直叙，无陷阱。

【定位】 "Without my job I don't know who I am," is a sentence that has been uttered on more than a handful of occasions from my office chair. Indeed, it can be one of the most challenging aspects I work on with clients who have lost or been forced into changing their jobs. This loss provokes an identity crisis much greater than the loss of the job itself. 「没有了工作，我就不知道自己是谁」——这话在我办公室的椅子上不止一次被来访者说出。事实上，与那些失去或被迫更换工作的来访者一起处理这种感受，是我工作中最具挑战的部分之一。这种失落所引发的身份危机，要远远大于失业本身。

【选项】 A) 偷换概念原文只是说作者本人是 clinical psychologist 处理来访者的身份危机，并未要求 visit a clinical psychologist；A 把作者视角偷换成失业者的行为。

B) 张冠李戴原文段 2 并未说失业「提供了扮演不同角色的机会」；段 3 才谈多重身份，但与「失业带来什么」是两个话题。

C) ✓ 正确 Without my job I don't know who I am ↔ puzzled about who they are This loss provokes an identity crisis ↔ It renders them puzzled 预判的「不知道自己是谁」与 It renders them puzzled about who they are 在主语、 谓语致使关系、宾语状态上完全对应，确定 C。 D) 过度推断原文谈的是 identity crisis 与重新审视自我信念，并没有说失业必然要 redefine their life's goals，把身份层面的事推到了「人生目标」的宏大命题上。
questions.hint: 回到原文定位题干关键词，比较选项与原文的含义。

questions.prompt: What has the author come to understand about our identity?

options.text: It is crucial to our emotional wellbeing.
It plays a big role in many facets of life.
It reflects our changing status in society.
It is more complicated than it appears.

questions.shortExplanation: One of the things I have come to understand, however, is that our identity is much more complex than we recognise at first glance.
questions.detailedExplanation:
【答案】 D （细节题）

【判型】 What has the author come to understand about our identity? 指向原文一句明确表述，不要求跨段推理。

【拆句】 完成时 What has the author come to understand 用 has come to understand 强调认知过程已完成；about our identity 指明认知对象。结构简单。

【定位】 One of the things I have come to understand, however, is that our identity is much more complex than we recognise at first glance.

然而，我逐渐明白的一件事是：我们的身份远比乍看之下复杂得多。

【选项】 A) 偷换概念原文段 3 后半句说 my ability to adapt to and develop my career identity has been crucial to my wellbeing，主语是「适应身份的能力」，并非身份本身；A 把「能力对幸福重要」偷换成「身份对情绪幸福重要」。

B) 答非所问原文确实列了多种身份角色，但作者「come to understand」的核心是「身份复杂」这一判断，而非「身份在生活方方面面起作用」；B 只描述现象，未答出认知本身。

C) 过度推断原文 They change over time 谈的是「我们在不同时期的身份变化」（学生、毕业生、 咨询师等），并非社会地位的变化；C 偷偷加上了 status in society。 D) ✓ 正确 much more complex than we recognise at first glance ↔ more complicated than it appears 预判要点「复杂」「超出表面认知」两块在 more complicated than it appears 里一一落地，无遗漏，确定 D。
questions.hint: 回到原文定位题干关键词，比较选项与原文的含义。

questions.prompt: What does the passage say about our identities at work?

options.text: They are essential to our self-esteem.
They evolve with the passage of time.
They are key to understanding ourselves.

questions.shortExplanation: Furthermore, our identities at work are not static. They change over time. 此外，我们在工作中的身份并非一成不变。它们会随时间而变化。
questions.detailedExplanation:
【答案】 B （细节题）

【判型】 What does the passage say about our identities at work? 让考生回原文找关于「职场身份」的明示句。

【拆句】 What does the passage say about our identities at work：say 是谓语、about 引出宾语对象；our identities at work 中 at work 修饰 identities，限定「工作中的」身份。无难点。

【定位】 Furthermore, our identities at work are not static. They change over time. 此外，我们在工作中的身份并非一成不变。它们会随时间而变化。

【选项】 A) 无中生有原文谈的是 wellbeing、identity crisis，没有 self-esteem（自尊）的概念，A 属于原文未提的新信息。

B) ✓ 正确 They change over time ↔ They evolve with the passage of time 预判「随时间而变」直接命中 They evolve with the passage of time，主谓宾全对应，定 B。

C) 与原文相反段 3 强调的是身份的「多元」与「变化」，并未说工作身份压倒其他身份；恰相反，作者承认我们还可作为朋友、配偶等存在。

D) 答非所问 「身份是理解自己的关键」与 Q52 的「身份很复杂」更接近，但题问的是 our identities at work 的具体属性；D 没有答出「随时间而变」这一具体属性。
questions.hint: 回到原文定位题干关键词，比较选项与原文的含义。

questions.prompt: What do we have to do in today's ever-changing job market?

options.text: Strive to develop our social identity.
Try to be assertive at all times.

questions.shortExplanation: Whilst we like to eliminate uncertainty in our lives at some level we have to manage uncertainty, especially in today's volatile and ever-shifting job market.
questions.detailedExplanation:
【答案】 D （细节题）

【判型】 What do we have to do in today's ever-changing job market? 指向原文一句给出具体动作的陈述。

【拆句】 What do we have to do in today's ever-changing job market?：do 是询问的动作；in 引导的状语 in today's ever-changing job market 限定背景。句式直白。

【定位】 Whilst we like to eliminate uncertainty in our lives at some level we have to manage uncertainty, especially in today's volatile and ever-shifting job market.

尽管我们倾向于消除生活中的不确定性，但在某种程度上我们必须学会管理不确定性，尤其是在如今这个动荡多变的就业市场中。

【选项】 A) 偷换概念原文谈 career identity / our identities at work，从未出现 social identity；A 凭空替换了限定语。

B) 张冠李戴 「为不同职业路径做准备」更接近段 4 的 career progression / new sectors，但 Q54 问的是动荡市场下「必须做的事」，原文给的明确答案是 manage uncertainty。

C) 以偏概全原文只是举例说有人在职场会变得 assertive，并未要求所有人 at all times 都要果断； C 把范围扩到全部场景，与原文不符。

D) ✓ 正确 we have to manage uncertainty ↔ Learn to manage uncertainty predict 的「学会管理不确定性」与 Learn to manage uncertainty 字面几乎一致，确定 D。
questions.hint: 回到原文定位题干关键词，比较选项与原文的含义。

questions.prompt: What should we do to expand our career options?
questions.shortExplanation: In an age where career progression may lead us into new sectors it is ever more important to challenge our sense of self and explore whether you can create a new experience of your identity by changing the beliefs you hold about yourself in order to expand your career options.
questions.detailedExplanation:
【答案】 A （细节题）

【判型】 What should we do to expand our career options? 求一个明确的应对动作。

【拆句】 What should we do to expand our career options?：should we do 是主干，to expand our career options 是目的状语，说明动作要服务的目标。结构平铺直叙。

【定位】 In an age where career progression may lead us into new sectors it is ever more important to challenge our sense of self and explore whether you can create a new experience of your identity by changing the beliefs you hold about yourself in order to expand your career options.

在一个职业发展可能把我们带入新行业的时代，挑战我们对自我的认知、并探索是否能通过改变你对自己持有的信念来创造一种新的身份体验、以拓宽你的职业选择，变得越来越重要。

【选项】 A) ✓ 正确 changing the beliefs you hold about yourself↔Alter our perceptions of ourselves challenge our sense of self↔Alter our perceptions of ourselves 预判要点「改变自我信念」在 Alter our perceptions of ourselves 中以同义改写完整呈现，确定 A。

B) 无中生有原文谈的是「改变信念以扩展选择」，并非 Compare various job opportunities；B 把心理层面的动作偷换为外部信息搜集行为。

C) 答非所问原文 career progression may lead us into new sectors 只是时代背景描述，作者并未让读者去 Look into newly emerging sectors。 D) 以偏概全原文 through experimentation, practice and conscious self-discipline 只是改变信念的途径之一；题干问的是「为扩展职业选择」最直接该做的事，作者明确给出的是改变信念，而非单独突出自律。
questions.hint: 回到原文定位题干关键词，比较选项与原文的含义。

items.passage:
A rainbow is a multi-colored, arc-shaped phenomenon that can appear in the sky. The colors of a rainbow are produced by the reflection and [26] _____ of light through water droplets(⼩滴) present in the atmosphere. An observer may [27] _____ a rainbow to be located either near or far away, but this phenomenon is not actually located at any specific spot. Instead, the appearance of a rainbow depends entirely upon the position of the observer in [28] _____ to the direction of light. In essence, a rainbow is an [29] _____ illusion.

Rainbows present a [30] _____ made up of seven colors in a specific order. In fact, school children in many English-speaking countries are taught to remember the name "Roy G. Biv" as an aid for remembering the colors of a rainbow and their order. "Roy G. Biv" [31] _____ for: red, orange, yellow, green, blue, indigo, and violet. The outer edge of the rainbow arc is red, while the inner edge is violet.

A rainbow is formed when light (generally sunlight) passes through water droplets [32] _____ in the atmosphere. The light waves change direction as they pass through the water droplets, resulting in two processes: reflection and refraction( 折射 ). When light reflects off a water droplet, it simply [33] _____ back in the opposite direction from where it [34] _____ . When light refracts, it takes a different direction. Some individuals refer to refracted light as "bent light waves." A rainbow is formed because

white light enters the water droplet, where it bends in several different directions. When these bent light waves reach the other side of the water droplet, they reflect back out of the droplet instead of [35] _____ passing through the water. Since the white light is separated inside of the water, the refracted light appears as separate colors to the human eye.

questions.prompt: The colors of a rainbow are produced by the reflection and [26] _____ of light through water droplets(⼩滴) present in the atmosphere.
questions.shortExplanation: reflection and dispersion 是描述彩虹成因的标准搭配
questions.detailedExplanation:
【答案】 C) dispersion 名词

【词性槽】 and 并列连接：reflection and ___，并列成分要求同性

【依据】 reflection and dispersion 是描述彩虹成因的标准搭配

The colors of a rainbow are produced by the reflection and dispersion of light through water droplets 光经过水滴时发生「反射 + 色散」是彩虹七色形成的物理原理； 与下一段 reflection and refraction（折射）共同呼应「光在水滴中的多重作用」。

【易错】 最具迷惑性的错误词是 N) —— spectrum 也是名词，且与彩虹七色话题强相关，极易抢答 26。produced by the reflection and __(26)__ of light through water droplets 26 题若考生没等到 30 题就抢着填，看到「彩虹 + 光」很容易顺手填 N spectrum；但 26 题靠 and 并列须填与 reflection 同类的「光学过程」名词（dispersion 色散），spectrum「光谱」属结果性名词，且 spectrum 真正归属 30 题 a ___ made up of seven colors。防坑： 严格执行「用过即划 + 先做高把握空」，让 30 题先把 spectrum 划走。

questions.prompt: An observer may __(27)__ a rainbow to be located either near or far away
questions.shortExplanation: perceive sb/sth to be ... 「察觉/认为……是……」

【答案】 H) perceive 动词

【词性槽】 情态动词 may 后接动词原形

【依据】 perceive sb/sth to be ... 「察觉/认为……是……」

An observer may perceive a rainbow to be located either near or far away perceive 后可直接接「宾语 + to be + 状态」，意为「察觉/认为彩虹位于近处或远处」，与下句 but this phenomenon is not actually located at any specific spot 形成「主观感知 vs 客观事实」的转折。

【竞争词】 J) ponder ponder 表「沉思」，不接「宾语 + to be」

ponder 通常作不及物或接 sth/on sth/over sth，不构成「ponder sth to be ...」结构；语义上 「观察者沉思彩虹位于近处或远处」也极不自然。

【答案】 M) relation 名词

N) spectrum spectrum 指「光谱/范围」，搭配错误

spectrum 是后文 30 题对应「七色光谱」的名词，与「相对位置」语义不沾边，且无 in spectrum to 短语。

questions.detailedExplanation:
【答案】 F) optical 形容词

【词性槽】 不定冠词 an + 空 + 名词 illusion

【依据】 optical illusion = 「视错觉、光学幻象」固定搭配

In essence, a rainbow is an optical illusion. 上文已经指出彩虹「并非真实位于某一地点，而是取决于观察者的相对位置」，结论自然是「光学幻象」——optical illusion 是英语中表「视错觉」的标准搭配，与全段论证完全吻合。

【竞争词】 D) eccentric eccentric 表「古怪的」，色彩与语境不符

eccentric 多形容人/行为「古怪、反常」，描述彩虹这一自然光学现象时既不准确也不带这种语义色彩；eccentric illusion 并非英语习用搭配。

【依据】 spectrum = 「光谱」，正对应「七色按特定顺序」

Rainbows present a spectrum made up of seven colors in a specific order. 「由七种颜色按特定顺序组成」正是 spectrum（光谱）的定义；下文 Roy G. Biv 口诀也是为了记忆这一光谱顺序。

【竞争词】 C) dispersion dispersion 强调「色散过程」，非结果性的「七色排列」

dispersion 指光被分解的「过程/动作」，而本句 made up of seven colors in a specific order 描述的是一个由七色组成的「结果性序列」——这是 spectrum 的语义，不是 dispersion 的语义；且 dispersion 已被 26 题预订（见后）。

【答案】 O) stands 动词

【词性槽】 主语 "Roy G. Biv" 后缺谓语 + 后接 for

【依据】 固定搭配 stand for = 「代表、缩写指代」

"Roy G. Biv" __(31)__ for: red, orange, yellow, green, blue, indigo, and violet. 紧随其后的就是七色英文首字母对应的全称，文意正是「Roy G. Biv 这一串字母代表红橙黄绿蓝靛紫」，stand for 是固定搭配，意为「代表 / 是……的缩写」，与语境完全契合。

【竞争词】 G) originates originate 后不接 for

originate 表「起源于」，常搭 originate from/in，无 originate for 这一搭配；语义也讲不通 ——「Roy G. Biv 起源于红橙黄……」不成立。

H) perceive 形态不符 + 搭配不通

perceive 非单三，且 perceive for 不是固定搭配；它的宾语应是被感知的对象（如本文 27 题用法），与此处「代表七色」不符。

I) permeates permeate 意为「渗透」

permeate 表液体/气味/影响渗透弥漫，搭配介词通常是 through/into，与「字母代表颜色」毫不相干。

J) ponder 形态不符 + 语义不通

ponder 非单三；其义为「沉思」，主语「Roy G. Biv」是个口诀，不会「沉思」，逻辑不成立。

【答案】 A) bounces 动词

【依据】 bounce back = 「反弹回去」，与 reflect 同义改写 When light reflects off a water droplet, it simply bounces back in the opposite direction from where it __(34)__. 上文 reflects 已给出动作，本句用 simply bounces back 同义改写以「反弹回来」的形象语言再说一遍，与 in the opposite direction 表方向反向严丝合缝。

I) permeates permeate 是「渗透、弥漫」，与 bounce back 行为完全相反

items.title: 2024年6月六级第3套 · 信息匹配
items.passage:
A) Phyllis Hartman knows what it's like to make one's way through the depths of office meeting hell. Managers at one of her former human resources jobs arranged so many meetings that attendees would fall asleep at the table or intentionally arrive late. With hours of her day blocked up with unnecessary meetings, she was often forced to make up her work during overtime. "I was actually working more hours than I probably would have needed to get the work done," says Hartman, who is founder and president of PGHR Consulting in Pittsburgh, Pennsylvania.

B) She isn't alone in her frustration. Between 11 million and 55 million meetings are held each day in the United States, costing most organisations between 7% and 15% of their personnel budgets. Every week, employees spend about six hours in meetings, while the average manager meets for a staggering 23 hours.

C) And though experts agree that traditional meetings are essential for making certain decisions and developing strategy, some employees view them as one of the most unnecessary parts of the workday. The result is not only hundreds of billions of wasted dollars, but an annoyance of what organisational psychologists call "meeting recovery syndrome (MRS)": time spent cooling off and regaining focus after a useless meeting. If you run to the office kitchen to get some relief with colleagues after a frustrating meeting, you're likely experiencing meeting recovery syndrome.

D) Meeting recovery syndrome is a concept that should be familiar to almost anyone who has held a formal job. It isn't ground-breaking to say workers feel fatigued after a meeting, but only in recent decades have scientists deemed the condition worthy of further investigation. With its links to organisational efficiency and employee wellbeing, MRS has attracted the attention of psychologists aware of the need to understand its precise causes and cures.

E) Today, in so far as researchers can hypothesise, MRS is most easily understood as a slow renewal of finite mental and physical resources. When an employee sits through an ineffective meeting their brain power is essentially being drained away. Meetings drain vitality if they last too long, fail to engage employees or turn into one-sided lectures. The conservation of resources theory, originally proposed in 1989 by Dr Stevan Hobfoll, states that psychological stress occurs when a person's resources are threatened or lost. When resources are low, a person will shift into defence to conserve their remaining supply. In the case of office meetings, where some of employees' most valuable resources are their focus, alertness and motivation, this can mean an abrupt halt in productivity as they take time to recover.

F) As humans, when we transition from one task to another on the job—say from sitting in a meeting to doing normal work—it takes an effortful cognitive switch. We must detach ourselves from the previous task and expend significant mental energy to move on. If we are already drained to dangerous levels, then making the mental switch to the next thing is extra tough. It's common to see people cyber-loafing after a frustrating meeting, going and getting coffee, interrupting a colleague and telling them about the meeting, and so on.

G) Each person's ability to recover from horrible meetings is different. Some can bounce back quickly, while others carry their fatigue until the end of the workday. Yet while no formal MRS studies are currently underway, one can loosely speculate on the length of an average employee's lag time. Switching tasks in a non-MRS condition takes about 10 to 15 minutes. With MRS, it may take as long as 45 minutes on average. It's even worse when a worker has several meetings that are separated by 30 minutes. "Not enough time to transition in a non-MRS situation to get anything done, and in an MRS situation, not quite enough time to recover for the next meeting," says researcher Joseph Allen. "Then, add the compounding of back-to-back bad meetings and we may have an epidemic on our hands."

H) In an effort to combat the side effects of MRS, Allen, along with researcher Joseph Mroz and colleagues at the University of Nebraska-Omaha, published a study detailing the best ways to avoid common traps, including a concise checklist of do's and don'ts applicable to any workplace. Drawing from around 200 papers to compile their comprehensive list, Mroz and his team may now hold a remedy to the largely undefined problem of MRS.

I) Mroz says a good place to start is asking ourselves if our meetings are even necessary in the first place. If all that's on the agenda is a quick catch-up, or some non-urgent information sharing, it may better suit the group to send around an email instead. "The second thing I would always recommend is keep the meeting as small as possible," says Mroz. "If they don't actually have some kind of immediate input, then they can follow up later. They don't need to be sitting in this hour-long meeting." Less time in meetings would ultimately lead to more employee engagement in the meetings they do attend, which experts agree is a proven remedy for MRS.

J) Employees also feel taxed when they are invited together to meetings that don't inspire participation, says Cliff Scott, professor of organisational science. It takes precious time for them to vent their emotions, complain and try to regain focus after a pointless meeting—one of the main traps of MRS. Over time as employees find themselves tied up in more and more unnecessary meetings—and thus dealing with increasing lag times from MRS—the waste of workday hours can feel insulting.

K) Despite the relative scarcity of research behind the subject, Hartman has taught herself many of the same tricks suggested in Mroz's study, and has come a long way since her days of being stuck with unnecessary meetings. The people she invites to meetings today include not just the essential employees, but also representatives from every department that might have a stake in the issue at hand. Managers like her, who seek input even from non-experts to shape their decisions, can find greater support and cooperation from their workforce, she says.

L) If an organisation were to apply all 22 suggestions from Mroz and Allen's findings, the most noticeable difference would be a stark decrease in the total number of meetings on the schedule, Mroz says. Less time in meetings would ultimately lead to increased productivity, which is the ultimate objective of convening a meeting. While none of the counter-MRS ideas have been tested empirically yet, Allen says one trick with promise is for employees to identify things that quickly change their mood from negative to positive. As simple as it sounds, finding a personal happy place, going there and then coming straight back to work might be key to facilitating recovery.

M) Leaders should also see themselves as "stewards of everyone else's valuable time", adds Steven Rogelberg, author of The Surprising Science of Meetings. Having the skills to foresee potential traps and treat employees' endurance with care allows leaders to provide effective short-term deterrents to MRS.

N) Most important, however, is for organisations to awaken to the concept of meetings being flexible, says Allen. By reshaping the way they prioritise employees' time, companies can eliminate the very sources of MRS in their tracks.
