items.passage:
Sarcasm and jazz have something surprisingly in common: You know them when you hear them. Sarcasm is mostly understood through tone of voice, which is used to portray the opposite of the literal words. For example, when someone says, "Well, that's exactly what I need right now," their tone can tell you it's not what they need at all.

Most frequently, sarcasm highlights an irritation or is, quite simply, mean.

If you want to be happier and improve your relationships, cut out sarcasm. Why? Because sarcasm is actually hostility disguised as humor.

Despite smiling outwardly, many people who receive sarcastic comments feel put down and often think the sarcastic person is rude, or contemptible. Indeed, it's not surprising that the origin of the word sarcasm derives from the Greek word "sarkazein" which literally means "to tear or strip the flesh off." Hence, it's no wonder that sarcasm is often preceded by the word "cutting" and that it hurts.

What's more, since actions strongly determine thoughts and feelings, when a person consistently acts sarcastically it may only serve to heighten their underlying hostility and insecurity. After all, when you come right down to it, sarcasm can be used as a subtle form of bullying—and most bullies are angry, insecure, or cowardly.

Alternatively, when a person stops voicing negative comments, especially sarcastic ones, they may soon start to feel happier and more self-confident. Also, other people in their life benefit even more because they no longer have to hear the emotionally hurtful language of sarcasm.

Now, I'm not saying all sarcasm is bad. It may just be better used sparingly—like a potent spice in cooking. Too much of the spice, and the dish will be overwhelmed by it. Similarly, an occasional dash of sarcastic wit can spice up a chat and add an element of humor to it. But a big or steady serving of sarcasm will overwhelm the emotional flavor of any conversation and can taste very bitter to its recipient.

So, tone down the sarcasm and work on clever wit instead, which is usually without any hostility and thus more appreciated by those you're communicating with. In essence, sarcasm is easy while true, harmless wit takes talent.

Thus, the main difference between wit and sarcasm is that, as already stated, sarcasm is often hostility disguised as humor. It can be intended to hurt and is often bitter and biting. Witty statements are usually in response to someone's unhelpful remarks or behaviors, and the intent is to untangle and clarify the issue by emphasizing its absurdities. Sarcastic statements are expressed in a cutting manner; witty remarks are delivered with undisguised and harmless humor.

items.passage:
Variability is crucially important for learning new skills. Consider learning how to serve in tennis. Should you always practise serving from the exactly same location on the court, aiming at the same spot? Although practising in more variable conditions will be slower at first, it will likely make you a better tennis player in the end. This is because variability leads to better generalisation of what is learned.

This principle is found in many domains, including speech perception and learning categories. For instance, infants will struggle to learn the category "dog" if they are only exposed to Chihuahuas, instead of many different kinds of dogs.

"There are over ten different names for this basic principle," says Limor Raviv, the senior investigator of a recent study. "Learning from less variable input is often fast, but may fail to generalise to new stimuli."

To identify key patterns and understand the underlying principles of variability effects, Raviv and her colleagues reviewed over 150 studies on variability and generalisation across fields, including computer science, linguistics, categorisation, visual perception and formal education.

The researchers discovered that, across studies, the term variability can refer to at least four different kinds of variability, such as set size and scheduling. "These four kinds of variability have never been directly compared—which means that we currently don't know which is most effective for learning," says Raviv.

The impact of variability depends on whether it is relevant to the task or not. But according to the 'Mr. Miyagi principle', practising seemingly unrelated skills may actually benefit learning of other skills.

But why does variability impact learning and generalisation? One theory is that more variable input can highlight which aspects of a task are relevant and which are not.

Another theory is that greater variability leads to broader generalisations. This is because variability will represent the real world better, including atypical(⾮典型的 ) examples.

A third reason has to do with the way memory works: when training is variable, learners are forced to actively reconstruct their memories.

"Understanding the impact of variability is important for literally every aspect of our daily life. Beyond affecting the way we learn language, motor skills, and categories, it even has an impact on our social lives," explains Raviv. "For example, face recognition is affected by whether people grew up in a small community or in a larger community. Exposure to fewer faces during childhood is associated with diminished face memory."

"We hope this work will spark people's curiosity and generate more work on the topic," concludes Raviv. "Our paper raises a lot of open questions. Can we find similar effects of variability beyond the brain, for instance, in the immune system?"

questions.detailedExplanation:
【答案】 A （细节题）

【判型】 What does the passage say about infants learning the category "dog" if they are exposed to Chihuahuas only? 以 What does the passage say about... 起手，要求复述原文事实，没有 infer/suggest 等推断信号。

【拆句】 Q51 是 What 引导的特殊疑问句，主干 What does the passage say about infants learning the category "dog"，其中 learning the category "dog" 是 v-ing 短语做 infants 的后置定语；末尾 if they are exposed to Chihuahuas only 是条件状语从句，被动语态 are exposed to 意为“只接触到”，是理解前提。

【定位】 For instance, infants will struggle to learn the category "dog" if they are only exposed to Chihuahuas, instead of many different kinds of dogs.

举例来说，如果婴儿只接触吉娃娃，而不是接触多种不同种类的狗，他们将很难学会“狗”这一类别。

【选项】 A) ✓ 正确 struggle to learn the category "dog" ↔ encounter some degree of difficulty 预判“会有学习困难”与 encounter some degree of difficulty 在语义上严格对应，无需推断，直接锁定 A。 B) 无中生有 They will try to categorise other objects first 在 P2 找不到任何对应——原文只说他们 struggle to learn“狗”，未说他们会先去分类别的东西。

C) 偷换概念 They will prefer Chihuahuas to other dog species 把原文“只接触到吉娃娃”曲解为“偏好吉娃娃”——原文谈的是输入受限导致学习困难，与个人偏好无关。

D) 张冠李戴 They will imagine Chihuahuas in various conditions 把第 1 段“在多变条件下练习”的概念硬塞到婴儿身上——原文中婴儿并不会主动 imagine，“in various conditions”是上一段网球训练的语境。
questions.hint: 回到原文定位题干关键词，比较选项与原文的含义。

questions.prompt: What does Raviv say about the four different kinds of variability?

options.text: Which of them is most relevant to the task at hand is to be confirmed.
Why they have an impact on learning is far from being understood.
Why they have never been directly compared remains a mystery.
Which of them is most conducive to learning is yet to be identified.

questions.shortExplanation: "These four kinds of variability have never been directly compared—which means that we currently don't know which is most effective for learning," says Raviv.
questions.detailedExplanation:
【答案】 D （细节题）

【判型】 What does Raviv say about the four different kinds of variability? 用 say about 句式问 Raviv 对四种 variability 的明确表述，是事实复述而非推断。

【拆句】 Q52 主干 What does Raviv say，介词短语 about the four different kinds of variability 限定话题范围；句中 the four different kinds of 含定冠词 the，提示原文已先有这“四种” 的提及。

【定位】 "These four kinds of variability have never been directly compared—which means that we currently don't know which is most effective for learning," says Raviv.

Raviv 说：“这四种 variability 从未被直接比较过——这意味着我们目前还不知道哪种对学习最有效。”

【选项】 A) 偷换概念 Which of them is most relevant to the task at hand is to be confirmed 把原文的 most effective for learning（对学习最有效）偷换为 most relevant to the task at hand（对手头任务最相关）——relevant to the task 是第 6 段的话题，不是第 5 段 Raviv 引语的内容。

B) 答非所问 Why they have an impact on learning is far from being understood 是关于“机制为何”的论断，不是 Raviv 在第 5 段就四种 variability 所说的话；况且第 7–9 段恰恰给出了三种 theory，“远未被理解”与原文也不符。 C) 过度推断 Why they have never been directly compared remains a mystery 把原文 These four kinds of variability have never been directly compared 的事实（“未被比较”） 扭曲成“为何未被比较仍是谜”——原文从未说“为何未被比较”是个谜。 D) ✓ 正确 we currently don't know which is most effective for learning ↔

Which of them is most conducive to learning is yet to be identified most effective for learning ↔ most conducive to learning 无论是“目前不知→尚待确认”的含蓄否定，还是“最有效→最有助益”的形容词替换，都精准落在 D 项措辞上，锁定 D。
questions.hint: 回到原文定位题干关键词，比较选项与原文的含义。

questions.prompt: How does one of the theories explain the importance of variability for learning new skills?

options.text: Learners regard variable training as typical of what happens in the real world.
Learners receiving variable training are compelled to reorganise their memories.
Learners pay attention to the relevant aspects of a task and ignore those irrelevant.
Learners focus on related skills instead of wasting time and effort on unrelated ones.

questions.shortExplanation: A third reason has to do with the way memory works: when training is variable, learners are forced to actively reconstruct their memories.
questions.detailedExplanation:
【答案】 B （细节题）

【判型】 How does one of the theories explain the importance of variability for learning new skills? 问“某个理论怎么解释”，要求复述原文中三个理论之一的具体内容，仍属细节题。

【拆句】 Q53 How 引导特殊疑问，主干 How does one of the theories explain the importance，of 短语 of variability for learning new skills 限定 importance，并不影响理解。注意 one of the theories 用单数动词 explain，提示只问其中一个理论。

【定位】 A third reason has to do with the way memory works: when training is variable, learners are forced to actively reconstruct their memories.

第三个原因与记忆的运作方式有关：当训练具有多变性时，学习者被迫主动地重构他们的记忆。

【选项】 A) 与原文相反 Learners regard variable training as typical of what happens in the real world 把 variability will represent the real world better, including atypical examples 颠倒 ——原文是“多变训练能更好地代表真实世界（包含非典型例子）”，并非“学习者把多变训练视为典型”。

B) ✓ 正确 learners are forced to actively reconstruct their memories ↔

Learners receiving variable training are compelled to reorganise their memories when training is variable ↔ receiving variable training 条件状语从句→v-ing 定语、被动词组→被动词组、动词短语→动词短语三层替换齐全， 正确项 B 与定位句构成一对一映射。

C) 偷换概念 Learners pay attention to the relevant aspects of a task and ignore those irrelevant 把 more variable input can highlight which aspects of a task are relevant and which are not 偷换主语——原文是“多变输入会突显相关/不相关方面”， 并非“学习者主动关注/忽略”。

D) 与原文相反 Learners focus on related skills instead of wasting time and effort on unrelated ones 把 practising seemingly unrelated skills may actually benefit learning of other skills 的意思颠倒——原文是“练习看似无关的技能也能助益”，选项却说“专注相关技能而不浪费在无关技能上”，恰恰相反。
questions.hint: 回到原文定位题干关键词，比较选项与原文的含义。

questions.prompt: What does the passage say about face recognition?

options.text: People growing up in a small community may find it easy to remember familiar faces.
Face recognition has a significant impact on literally every aspect of our social lives.
People growing up in a large community can readily recognise any individual faces.
The size of the community people grow up in impacts their face recognition ability.

questions.shortExplanation: For example, face recognition is affected by whether people grew up in a small community or in a larger community.
questions.detailedExplanation:
【答案】 D （细节题）

【判型】 What does the passage say about face recognition? 仍是 What does the passage say about 句式，问原文如何陈述 face recognition 这一事实。

【拆句】 Q54 结构与第 51 题同款，主干 What does the passage say about face recognition? 无从句无否定，平铺直叙，无陷阱。

【定位】 For example, face recognition is affected by whether people grew up in a small community or in a larger community.

例如，面孔识别会受到人们是在小社区还是大社区长大这一因素的影响。

【选项】 A) 与原文相反 People growing up in a small community may find it easy to remember familiar faces 给“小社区”贴上“易记熟人脸”的标签，但 Exposure to fewer faces during childhood is associated with diminished face memory 恰恰说“接触少→记忆减弱”， 与 A 的方向相反；且原文没区分 familiar faces。

B) 张冠李戴 Face recognition has a significant impact on literally every aspect of our social lives 把“variability 影响每一方面”安到 face recognition 头上——原文 Understanding the impact of variability is important for literally every aspect of our daily life 的主语是 variability，不是 face recognition。 C) 过度推断 People growing up in a large community can readily recognise any individual faces 用 any individual faces 把原文中性的“识别能力受影响”夸大为“能轻松识别任何个人面孔”，是绝对化推断。

D) ✓ 正确 face recognition is affected by whether people grew up in a small community or in a larger community

↔ The size of the community people grow up in impacts their face recognition ability D 既保留了“社区规模→识别能力”的因果，也保留了“人群”层面的中性陈述，没有像 A/C 那样把因果方向具体化、特例化，最贴近原文。
questions.hint: 回到原文定位题干关键词，比较选项与原文的含义。

questions.prompt: What does Raviv hope to do with their research work?

options.text: Highlight which aspects of a task are relevant and which are not to learning a skill.
Use the principle of variability in teaching seemingly unrelated skills in education.
Arouse people's interest in variability and stimulate more research on the topic.
Apply the principle of variability to such fields of study as the immune system.

questions.shortExplanation: "We hope this work will spark people's curiosity and generate more work on the topic," concludes Raviv.
questions.detailedExplanation:
【答案】 C （细节题）

【判型】 What does Raviv hope to do with their research work? 问 Raviv 对其研究的具体期望， 要求复述原文具体表述，不需推断。

【拆句】 Q55 主干 What does Raviv hope to do，with 短语 with their research work 是状语， 说明 do 的对象是 research work。their 在此泛指研究团队，非语法陷阱。

【定位】 "We hope this work will spark people's curiosity and generate more work on the topic," concludes Raviv.

Raviv 总结说：“我们希望这项工作能激发人们的好奇心，并产生更多关于这一主题的研究。”

【选项】 A) 答非所问 Highlight which aspects of a task are relevant and which are not to learning a skill 是 more variable input can highlight which aspects of a task are relevant and which are not 中第 1 个理论的措辞，并非 Raviv 在末段表达的研究愿景。

B) 答非所问 Use the principle of variability in teaching seemingly unrelated skills in education 取自 practising seemingly unrelated skills may actually benefit learning of other skills 的 Mr. Miyagi 原则，也并非 Raviv 末段表达的愿景。

C) ✓ 正确 spark people's curiosity↔ Arouse people's interest in variability generate more work on the topic ↔ stimulate more research on the topic C 把原文两个并列愿望 spark...curiosity 与 generate...work 都同义改写并对齐，没有遗漏其中任何一个，符合“并列动作全保留”原则。 D) 过度推断 Apply the principle of variability to such fields of study as the immune system 把 Can we find similar effects of variability beyond the brain, for instance, in the immune system? 这一开放性问题当成 Raviv 的具体计划——原文是疑问句、是抛出问题，并非“打算应用到免疫系统”。
questions.hint: 回到原文定位题干关键词，比较选项与原文的含义。

items.title: 2025年12月六级第1套 · 选词填空
items.passage:
By now, it is generally accepted that regular exercise comes with an assortment of health benefits for people who maintain the habit over time. But is it [26] _____ too late to start?

New research looked at people who increased their exercise levels after their 40s beyond levels they had when they were younger and those individuals showed declines in their risk of early [27] _____ which were similar to those of people who exercised consistently throughout their lives. This was a [28] _____ of 32% to 35% compared to people who did not exercise. Those who began exercising in middle age also saw reductions in their incidence of [29] _____ diseases, such as heart disease and cancer, which were similar to the steady exercisers.

So why bother exercising consistently throughout your life? The authors of the study [30] _____ that some might interpret the study's findings to mean that they can delay starting an exercise program but this would be a mistake. There are other benefits, both mental and physical, to staying consistently active that we should not [31] _____ . These real health benefits include better [32] _____ functioning and lowered risk of gaining weight. The latter is [33] _____ important given the global obesity epidemic. In addition, experts assert that starting younger is better because, if you make a habit of exercising when you are young, you are more likely to keep up those [34] _____ later in life. It is ideal, then, for people to start exercising when they are children or [35] _____ , and it is good to maintain an active lifestyle at

all times regardless of your age. However, this study does indicate that, if you have not been active, you can still benefit if you start becoming active in your 40s and 50s.

questions.prompt: But is it __(26)__ too late to start?
questions.shortExplanation: ever 与 too…to 在疑问句中构成 "是否真的太……以至于不能……" 的强调 But is it __(26)__ too late to start? 是承接 "运动有诸多益处" 后的设问：是否"真的"太晚了？ever 在疑问句中作副词，与 too late 连用强调"究竟、真的"，自然过渡到第二段用研究数据回应这个疑问。
questions.detailedExplanation:
【答案】 H) ever 副词

【词性槽】 too…to 框架里嵌一个副词修饰 too

【依据】 ever 与 too…to 在疑问句中构成 "是否真的太……以至于不能……" 的强调 But is it __(26)__ too late to start? 是承接 "运动有诸多益处" 后的设问：是否"真的"太晚了？ever 在疑问句中作副词，与 too late 连用强调"究竟、真的"，自然过渡到第二段用研究数据回应这个疑问。

【竞争词】 B) arbitrarily义不符——"任意地太晚"逻辑不通

arbitrarily 指"任意地、武断地"，描述的是行为的随意性，而too late to start问的是时间晚不晚，与"任意"不搭。

K) particularly particularly 留给第 33 题更贴

particularly 意为"尤其"，虽可修饰 too late 但语气勉强；且第 33 题 The latter is __(33)__ important given the global obesity epidemic. 中"尤其重要"是 particularly 的经典搭配，留给那里更合身。
questions.hint: 根据空格前后的词性、搭配与上下文选择词语；每个词最多使用一次。

questions.prompt: those individuals showed declines in their risk of early __(27)__ which were similar to those of people who exercised consistently throughout their lives.
questions.shortExplanation: risk of early mortality = 早死风险，是流行病学固定表述 declines in their risk of early __(27)__ 描述"早死风险的下降"，early mortality（早死） 是公共卫生研究的标准术语；第二段后文又提 reductions in their incidence of __(29)__ diseases 谈疾病发病率，整段就是"死亡风险 + 疾病风险"双线索。
questions.detailedExplanation:
【答案】 J) mortality 名词

【词性槽】 形容词 early 后接名词作 of 短语的宾语

【依据】 risk of early mortality = 早死风险，是流行病学固定表述 declines in their risk of early __(27)__ 描述"早死风险的下降"，early mortality（早死） 是公共卫生研究的标准术语；第二段后文又提 reductions in their incidence of __(29)__ diseases 谈疾病发病率，整段就是"死亡风险 + 疾病风险"双线索。

【竞争词】 A) adolescents early adolescents 与 risk of 不构成有意义搭配

adolescents 是"青少年"，与 risk of 搭配不出"早期青少年的风险"这种话题；且 adolescents 留给第 35 题 when they are children or __(35)__ 与 children 并列才贴。
questions.hint: 根据空格前后的词性、搭配与上下文选择词语；每个词最多使用一次。

questions.prompt: This was a __(28)__ of 32% to 35% compared to people who did not exercise.
questions.shortExplanation: drop of 32% to 35% = "32% 到 35% 的下降" 上文 declines in their risk of early __(27)__ 用到 declines（下降）；本句 This was a __(28)__ of 32% to 35% 的 This 就指代那个 decline，drop 与 decline 同义对接"下降幅度"。
questions.detailedExplanation:
【答案】 G) drop 名词

【词性槽】 This was a __ of 32% to 35%，空是单数名词作表语

【依据】 drop of 32% to 35% = "32% 到 35% 的下降" 上文 declines in their risk of early __(27)__ 用到 declines（下降）；本句 This was a __(28)__ of 32% to 35% 的 This 就指代那个 decline，drop 与 decline 同义对接"下降幅度"。

【竞争词】 I) maneuver maneuver 是"操纵/策略"，不与百分比搭

maneuver of 32% to 35% 在英语里讲不通——maneuver 不表示数量增减，纯属词性对、语义偏的干扰。
questions.hint: 根据空格前后的词性、搭配与上下文选择词语；每个词最多使用一次。

questions.prompt: Those who began exercising in middle age also saw reductions in their incidence of __(29)__ diseases, such as heart disease and cancer
questions.shortExplanation: such as heart disease and cancer 是 chronic diseases 的典型例证原文 reductions in their incidence of __(29)__ diseases, such as heart disease and cancer——心脏病与癌症都是医学上的典型"慢性病"（chronic diseases）。such as 后的例子直接锁死形容词的语义指向。
questions.detailedExplanation:
【答案】 C) chronic 形容词

【词性槽】 名词 diseases 前缺一个定语形容词

【依据】 such as heart disease and cancer 是 chronic diseases 的典型例证原文 reductions in their incidence of __(29)__ diseases, such as heart disease and cancer——心脏病与癌症都是医学上的典型"慢性病"（chronic diseases）。such as 后的例子直接锁死形容词的语义指向。

【竞争词】 D) cognitive cognitive diseases 不与 heart disease/cancer 类配

cognitive 指"认知的"，cognitive diseases 通常指阿尔茨海默等认知障碍；与 such as 后举出的 heart disease and cancer 不属同一范畴。且 cognitive 留给第 32 题 better __(32)__ functioning 与 functioning 搭配是"认知功能"的固定表达。

O) vocal vocal diseases 搭配不成立

vocal 指"直言的/嗓音的"，与心脏病、癌症完全无关，纯属词性对、语义不搭的干扰。
questions.hint: 根据空格前后的词性、搭配与上下文选择词语；每个词最多使用一次。

questions.prompt: The authors of the study __(30)__ that some might interpret the study's findings to mean that they can delay starting an exercise program but this would be a mistake.
questions.shortExplanation: concede 承认"研究结论可能被误读"这一让步语气
questions.detailedExplanation:
【答案】 E) concede 动词

【词性槽】 主语 The authors + __ + that 宾语从句

【依据】 concede 承认"研究结论可能被误读"这一让步语气

上下文 The authors of the study __(30)__ that some might interpret the study's findings to mean that they can delay starting an exercise program but this would be a mistake. 是研究作者主动承认"有人可能会误读"——这是不利于研究主张的让步，再用 but this would be a mistake 反驳。concede（承认不利事实）正是这种"先让步、后反驳"的标志性动词。

【竞争词】 M) refute refute 与 that 后内容方向相反

refute 是"反驳"——若作者反驳了"some might interpret"这件事，后面就不会再出现 but this would be a mistake（反驳的反驳），逻辑跑偏；且 refute 的宾语通常是论点本身，而非"某些人可能这样理解"这一描述性事实。

【易错】 最具迷惑性的错误词是 M) —— refute 与 concede 都能接 that 从句，最易反向。考生若忽略后半句 but this would be a mistake 的反驳信号，就可能错选 refute；防坑做法是先把整句的 but…mistake 看完，确认"先让步后反驳"的链条，再回头锁定 concede。
questions.hint: 根据空格前后的词性、搭配与上下文选择词语；每个词最多使用一次。

questions.prompt: There are other benefits, both mental and physical, to staying consistently active that we should not __(31)__.
questions.shortExplanation: disregard the benefits = 忽视这些好处 There are other benefits, both mental and physical, to staying consistently active that we should not __(31)__.——"还有其他身心益处是我们不应当 ___ 的"，逻辑要的是"忽视"；disregard the benefits 是惯用搭配，且与下文 These real health benefits include better cognitive functioning and lowered risk of gaining weight. 顺承——正因为不应忽视，所以列举出来。
questions.detailedExplanation:
【答案】 F) disregard 动词

【词性槽】 should not + 动词原形

【依据】 disregard the benefits = 忽视这些好处 There are other benefits, both mental and physical, to staying consistently active that we should not __(31)__.——"还有其他身心益处是我们不应当 ___ 的"，逻辑要的是"忽视"；disregard the benefits 是惯用搭配，且与下文 These real health benefits include better cognitive functioning and lowered risk of gaining weight. 顺承——正因为不应忽视，所以列举出来。

【竞争词】 E) concede concede 是"承认"，与"不应"组合后逻辑反

concede the benefits = "承认好处"，should not concede 变成"不应承认"，与作者鼓励大家重视好处的态度相悖；且 concede 在本文已被第 30 题占用是动词中性候选，留给第 30 更贴。

M) refute refute the benefits 搭配勉强、语义反

refute 是"反驳（观点/论断）"，宾语通常是 claim/argument/theory；refute the benefits （反驳益处）既不常见，逻辑上 should not refute 也偏向辩论场景，与本句"忽视"含义不合。

【易错】 最具迷惑性的错误词是 E) —— concede 与 disregard 都是动词原形、且都接抽象宾语， 最易混。other benefits…that we should not __(31)__ 中考生若没注意到下文紧接着列举具体益处（better cognitive functioning and lowered risk of gaining weight），就可能误填 concede（"不应承认"），从而把作者的态度搞反；防坑做法是把空填后整段读一遍 ——作者要肯定益处，对应的动词必为"忽视"类。

questions.prompt: These real health benefits include better __(32)__ functioning and lowered risk of gaining weight.
questions.shortExplanation: cognitive functioning 是"认知功能"的固定搭配

【依据】 cognitive functioning 是"认知功能"的固定搭配

better __(32)__ functioning and lowered risk of gaining weight 列举运动的真实健康好处——"更好的认知功能"与"降低增重风险"并列；cognitive functioning 是医学/心理学常用术语，正合此处。

【竞争词】 O) vocal vocal functioning 不构成健康层面表述

vocal 指"嗓音的、直言的"，与运动带来的整体健康收益毫无逻辑关联，留作干扰。

questions.prompt: The latter is __(33)__ important given the global obesity epidemic.

questions.detailedExplanation:

【竞争词】 B) arbitrarily arbitrarily important 语义矛盾

items.title: 2025年12月六级第1套 · 信息匹配
items.passage:
A) Like most chefs, Flippy is not afraid of hard work. Since last summer, that has meant 11 am until 7 pm shifts at Caliburger in Pasadena, California, as well as short assignments at Chick-N-Tots at Dodger Stadium in Los Angeles. These are long hours of repetitive work, where the boss demands absolute consistency. But you won't hear Flippy complain or say anything, in fact. For Flippy is a robot — a cloud-connected mechanical arm with 3D thermal scanners for eyes — that can flip burgers or fry 80 baskets of food an hour, monitor that food and even clean up afterwards.

B) Flippy was created by Miso Robotics, part of the Cali Group, which is described by its CEO, John Miller, as: "A technology company that happens to sell cheeseburgers." Cali creates new machines that it road-tests in its Caliburger restaurants across the world, into which Flippy will be deployed this year. And Flippy is not alone. Also in California, Bear Robotics has developed a self-guiding robot, Penny, which has so far served 40,000 diners.

C) Ten years ago, robot-chefs and waiters were pure science fiction. Today, they are a reality, and at prices that make them a plausible investment. From May, Penny will be shipped on a subscription basis that offers "an immediate return", says Bear Robotics' chief operating officer, Juan Higueros. Flippy will cost a reported $60,000 to $100,000. Fully automated burger restaurants managed with minimal human oversight — where customers order at screens, pay electronically, and eat food cooked and delivered by robots — are now a possibility.

D) The technology exists; it just needs knitting together cost-effectively and in a way diners buy into. In an industry keen to slash labor costs and increase profits, further automation seems inevitable. After an eight-month test at Kang Nam Tofu House in California, Bear Robotics credited Penny with driving a 28% increase in sales. Meanwhile, in US trials, the self-ordering screens that McDonald's is currently installing at its 1,300 UK restaurants yielded a reported 30% rise in order values.

E) Personalisation is seen as key to the appeal of this technology, alongside its ability to reliably push so-called "upsells" (meal deals, extras, larger drinks) to customers. Soon when you log into a restaurant app, it will be able to use your data and purchasing history to recommend dishes to you — factoring in everything from the weather to, if you are ordering at a screen that can read your face, your mood.

F) "Right now people compromise on choice. We're presented with a one-size-fits-all menu. Ultimately, technology can allow us to make personal choices. You love spicy food and chicken? Here's the dish people like you mostly order," says Tom Weaver, CEO at the hospitality tech company Flyt. He talks enthusiastically about the Helsinki pop-up Take-In, a full-service restaurant where diners ordered dishes in from various delivery services. "For the first time in a few hundred years, digital is allowing us to create new versions of restaurants."

G) If high-street fast food is automation-ready, its impact on high-end restaurants is likely to be subtler and slower. "It'll probably be a very long time before we see a five-star robot-chef," says Noel Sharkey, professor of AI and robotics at the University of Sheffield. "Apart from the AI creativity gap, great cooking involves a subtle understanding of ingredients and delicate cooking that would be enormously challenging for robots. Placing fragile foods on plates would be incredibly slow."

H) Currently, robots have limited functionality. A human needs to load Penny with plates that diners lift off themselves. At the robot-powered US pizza-delivery company Zume, the more difficult jobs, such as topping pizzas, are still done by humans. But Moley, which will launch soon, offers an idea of the sophistication to come. Modelled on the movements of a MasterChef contest winner, Tim Anderson, its robotic arms are fixed over a stove and programmed to prepare dishes from raw ingredients. It is designed for domestic use, but a commercial version is planned that opens up the possibility of restaurant kitchens automating even highly technically challenging tasks.

I) For now, the kitchen technology that QSR Automations supplies to Mitchells & Butlers' pubs or KFC is less glamorous. Rather than having a chef shouting out diners' orders, the QSR system automatically distributes those orders across screens. The kitchen screens then tell chefs when to start cooking each dish, so that your plate of fish, chips and peas comes together at the right time.

J) The restaurant industry is currently suffering a severe shortage of skilled chefs — a deficit of 11,000, according to the skills agency People 1st. "Automation systems designed to make the process more idiot-proof are trying to bridge that gap," says Stefan Chomka, the editor of Restaurant magazine.

K) In terms of simplifying or enhancing the customer experience, online restaurant booking has been the easily-won success of the internet age. Automated at-table ordering and payment is seen as the next landmark. Until then, early adopters, such as the Manchester bar owner Andy Smith, who uses the Ordoo app at his venue 33 Oldham Street, may well experience growing but "lower than expected" acceptance.

L) Embarrassing failures in restaurant tech frequently hit the headlines. The TGI Fridays drone( ⽆⼈机 ) that injured a Brooklyn Daily photographer; US burger chain Shake Shack having to retreat from plans for entirely cashless ordering sites. But, says Chomka, such technology could miss the mark if it only offers "solutions to problems that don't really exist". "Payments being automatic" could be useful, he adds. But, in an expensive restaurant, "how quick do you need dinner to be?"

M) That attachment to the human art of hospitality will be heartening for staff who see automation as a threat to jobs. "Unite is concerned that without safeguards, any benefits will bypass workers in low-paying jobs, such as waiters," says the union's London regional officer, Dave Turnbull. "We're urging Members of Parliament to ensure automation does not just benefit a wealthy few like previous industrial revolutions."

N) The industry principle is that automation will allow it to redeploy staff more effectively. Jobs will change, if not immediately decrease in number. "Self-order screens mean more demand for people front-of-house. Last year, we recruited 1,000 new managers," says McDonald's COO, Jason Clark. Caliburger has a programme to retrain staff as robot engineers or "chef techs".

O) But ultimately the chance to reduce overheads(管理费⽤ ) by employing fewer people or at lower rates will be what attracts big brands to technology. Invariably, over the next 10 years, jobs will go in conventional bricks-built restaurants, not least because automation will boost their rapidly growing rival: delivery. Companies such as Domino and Just Eat have both experimented with robot and drone delivery, which is already legal in Reykjavik, Iceland. "Robot food deliveries are the future," says Noel Sharkey. "Small, 4 mph ground robots are safe and will work 24 hours a day."

P) Combined with machine learning of anticipated order volumes and the minute-by-minute cooking data generated by systems such as QSR, that robot fleet could deliver almost instantly. "Restaurants will prepare food ahead of orders coming in," predicts Just Eat's director of engineering, Daniel Richardson. "I'll be able to say 'Let's have pizza' to my family, my intelligent assistant will hear and 10 minutes later the food will be at my door." No one is putting an exact date on it yet. But in the dining room and on your doorstep, the robots are coming.

items.title: 2025年12月六级第1套 · 仔细阅读 · 第一篇
items.passage:
Many see friendships as a comfort blanket: a shoulder to cry on, a reliable soul to confide in. However, more often than not, in our eagerness to seek individual success, we lose friends along the way and that has become part of the process.

The chaos and never-ending turmoil that accompanies everyday life is an aggressive obstacle in the pursuit of stable friendships. As students, we use this excuse to shrug off losing people who we once thought to be loved ones.

Instead of viewing our lives as a race, where everyone is on their own path to some form of success, we must relearn to value the connections we make along the track. We must reevaluate the harm of radical, individual freedom.

Radical individualism elevates the freedom of the individual over the collective. It argues, for instance, that universal healthcare, an example of collectivism, threatened the dream of many Americans.

Many of us have fallen victim to an individualistic culture. Society tends to celebrate personal achievement and commend it based on the assumption that winning or succeeding is a consequence of working harder than the next person.

As a society, we idolize the concept of "losing friends on the road to success". I remember hearing in high school, "Don't worry about losing friendships, just focus on study and getting into college. That's all that will matter in the long run," a sentiment that is not unique to my experience. It's preached in many success stories, and it's embedded in the way we see growth. Motivational speakers will push their audience to be complacent to the inevitable end of losing friends. Spend too much time with friends? You're losing time better utilized on your achievements. Invest time in your relationships? Invest time in your work instead.

This constant need to succeed has blinded us from seeing through the whirlwind of change that accompanies our everyday lives. We are expected to tangibly succeed, earn awards, get higher positions, earn better grades. In order to succeed, we lose friends, and that has sadly become normalized.

We cannot be complacent with losing friendships because they are our anchors. Yes, pursue success. Challenge yourself. Push limits. But contrary to all the self-proclaimed success experts, doing it alone does not make you more successful or any better than someone who achieved it with the help of others.

Put effort into fostering healthy relationships, and maintaining them through your busy schedule that seems like it leaves no time for anyone else. Although we may be living in a society that treasures the independent pursuit of achievement, having people to support and love you on the way is far more important than any end result.

questions.prompt: What often happens when people are eager to pursue individual success?

options.text: They lack a shoulder to cry on.
They have no soul to confide in.
They ignore their ties with friends.

questions.shortExplanation: However, more often than not, in our eagerness to seek individual success, we lose friends along the way and that has become part of the process.
questions.detailedExplanation:
【答案】 D （细节题）

【判型】 What often happens when people are eager to pursue individual success? 是 What 引导的事实性问句，问 "经常发生什么"，无 infer/imply/suggest 等推断信号。

【拆句】 What often happens when people are eager to pursue individual success? 主句 What often happens 是 wh- 主语疑问句；when 引导时间状语从句，be eager to do 意为 "急于做某事"。句意 "当人们急于追求个人成功时，常常会发生什么？" 结构平铺直叙， 无陷阱。

【定位】 However, more often than not, in our eagerness to seek individual success, we lose friends along the way and that has become part of the process.

然而，多数情况下，在我们急于追求个人成功的过程中，我们沿途失去了朋友，而这已经成为这一过程的一部分。

【选项】 A) 答非所问 They lack a shoulder to cry on. 把 a shoulder to cry on 这一对友谊功能的比喻直接当作 "人们当下缺什么" 的结论，但原文这一句是描述 "许多人对友谊的看法"，不是 "人们追求个人成功时发生的结果"。

B) 答非所问 They have no soul to confide in. 与 A 同套路，把 a reliable soul to confide in 这一对友谊作用的描绘当作题干所问的 "结果"，但原文这是 "友谊在人们眼中的样子"，不是 "追求成功时发生的事"。 C) 偷换概念 They cannot find reliable friends. 说 "找不到可靠朋友"，但原文 we lose friends 强调的是 "主动放弃/丢失现有朋友"，与 "找不到" 是两种不同动作；原文从未说过 "找不到"。 D) ✓ 正确 we lose friends along the way ↔ They ignore their ties with friends. 在四项中，只有 They ignore their ties with friends. 与预判 "失去/疏远朋友" 在主谓宾三层都吻合，故选 D。

questions.prompt: What does the author advise people to do in their pursuit of radical individualism?

options.text: Shrug off the loss of their loved ones.
Avoid the chaos and turmoil involved.
Remove aggressive obstacles in the way.

questions.shortExplanation: We must reevaluate the harm of radical, individual freedom.
questions.detailedExplanation:
【答案】 A （细节题）

【判型】 What does the author advise people to do in their pursuit of radical individualism? 直接问作者建议做什么，是对文中作者表态句的事实性提问，不是推断。

【拆句】 What does the author advise people to do in their pursuit of radical individualism? advise sb. to do sth. = 建议某人做某事；their pursuit of radical individualism 是 "his/her/their + 名词 + of" 的所属结构，等价于 "when they pursue radical individualism"。句意：作者建议人们在追求极端个人主义时做什么？

【定位】 We must reevaluate the harm of radical, individual freedom.

我们必须重新评估极端个人自由的危害。

【选项】 A) ✓ 正确 reevaluate the harm of radical, individual freedom ↔ Reexamine its detrimental effects. 在四项中，只有 Reexamine its detrimental effects. 同时覆盖了 "再审视" 与 "危害" 两个语义成分，故选 A。

B) 与原文相反 Shrug off the loss of their loved ones. 是 we use this excuse to shrug off losing people who we once thought to be loved ones 里被作者批判的 "错误做法"，并非作者建议。 C) 无中生有 Avoid the chaos and turmoil involved. 把 The chaos and never-ending turmoil that accompanies everyday life 这一对生活状态的描述当作作者建议，但原文只是把它列为 "我们丢友谊的借口"，作者既未说要避免也未说要拥抱。

D) 偷换概念 Remove aggressive obstacles in the way. 把 an aggressive obstacle in the pursuit of stable friendships 的名词搭配换皮成 "清除前进路上的强劲障碍"，但作者要清除的不是抽象意义上的 "前进路上的障碍"——他要重新评估的是极端个人主义之害。

questions.prompt: What is American society's assumption of personal achievement?

options.text: It is to be duly celebrated and highly commended.
It is a sure way to fulfill a person's dream.
It revolves around an individualistic culture.
It reflects a person's exceptional endeavor.

questions.shortExplanation: Society tends to celebrate personal achievement and commend it based on the assumption that winning or succeeding is a consequence of working harder than the next person.
questions.detailedExplanation:
【答案】 D （细节题）

【判型】 What is American society's assumption of personal achievement? 是 What is 引导的事实性问句，问 "美国社会对个人成就的预设是什么"，无推断信号词。

【拆句】 What is American society's assumption of personal achievement? American society's assumption of personal achievement 是双层所属结构：assumption of personal achievement 等于 "对个人成就的预设"；前置 American society's 进一步说明这是 "美国社会的"。句意：美国社会对个人成就的预设是什么？

【定位】 Society tends to celebrate personal achievement and commend it based on the assumption that winning or succeeding is a consequence of working harder than the next person.

社会倾向于赞美个人成就，并基于一种预设来推崇它，这种预设是：获胜或成功是比别人更努力工作的结果。

【选项】 A) 答非所问 It is to be duly celebrated and highly commended. 把 Society tends to celebrate personal achievement and commend it 的 "社会的做法" 直接当成 "对个人成就的预设"，但题干问的是 the assumption 这个预设本身的内容，不是社会怎么做。

B) 无中生有 It is a sure way to fulfill a person's dream. 说 "个人成就是实现梦想的可靠途径"，原文从未将个人成就与 "实现梦想" 直接挂钩；原文涉及 dream 只出现在 threatened the dream of many Americans 中，且是普及医保的对立面，与个人成就的预设无关。 C) 偷换概念 It revolves around an individualistic culture. 把 Many of us have fallen victim to an individualistic culture 的上位归类（属于个人主义文化）当作预设本身，但题干问的是 "对个人成就所持的预设"，不是 "个人成就属于哪种文化"。 D) ✓ 正确 winning or succeeding is a consequence of working harder than the next person ↔

It reflects a person's exceptional endeavor. 四项中只有 It reflects a person's exceptional endeavor. 准确捕捉 "成功背后是个人非凡努力" 这一预设，故选 D。

questions.prompt: What is preached in many success stories?

options.text: Attaching importance to academic gains on the road to success.
Investing one's time in work instead of connecting with friends.
Trying to strengthen friendships in one's pursuit of personal success.
Excelling in academic performance to get into a prestigious college.

questions.shortExplanation: Motivational speakers will push their audience to be complacent to the inevitable end of losing friends. Spend too much time with friends? You're losing time better utilized on your achievements. Invest time in your relationships? Invest time in your work instead.
questions.detailedExplanation:
【答案】 B （细节题）

【判型】 What is preached in many success stories? 问的是 "很多励志故事中宣扬了什么"，是对文中具体表述的事实性追问。

【拆句】 What is preached in many success stories? 主语 What 是宾语提前的 wh-；is preached 为被动语态，意为 "被宣扬"。句意：很多励志故事中宣扬的是什么？句式简单、无陷阱。

【定位】 Motivational speakers will push their audience to be complacent to the inevitable end of losing friends. Spend too much time with friends? You're losing time better utilized on your achievements. Invest time in your relationships? Invest time in your work instead.

励志演讲者会推动听众坦然接受 "失去朋友" 这一不可避免的结局。和朋友花太多时间？你正在浪费本可用于个人成就的时间。把时间投入到人际关系上？不如把时间投入到工作上。

【选项】 A) 张冠李戴 Attaching importance to academic gains on the road to success. 来自 Don't worry about losing friendships, just focus on study and getting into college，但这是 "高中时听到的话"（作者的个人经历），紧接其后才提到 "a sentiment that is not unique to my experience. It's preached in many success stories"——题干问的是 "在 many success stories 中被宣扬的"，即作者随后展开的演讲家观点，不是高中老师的话。

B) ✓ 正确 Invest time in your relationships? Invest time in your work instead. ↔

Investing one's time in work instead of connecting with friends. 四项中只有 Investing one's time in work instead of connecting with friends. 同时覆盖 "投入工作" 与 "放弃朋友联系" 两层，故选 B。

C) 与原文相反 Trying to strengthen friendships in one's pursuit of personal success. 是作者自己在 P8 P9 提出的反向建议，不是 success stories 所宣扬的内容；many success stories 宣扬的恰恰是放弃友谊。

D) 以偏概全 Excelling in academic performance to get into a prestigious college. 同样源自 focus on study and getting into college 这句高中老师的话，且把 college 升级为 prestigious college（名校）属于无中生有；不属于 many success stories 所宣扬的内容。

questions.prompt: What can we infer from the passage regarding the pursuit of success?

options.text: No one can succeed without pushing limits.
No one can afford to neglect close friends.
Success experts often lead people to ruin.

questions.shortExplanation: We cannot be complacent with losing friendships because they are our anchors. Yes, pursue success. Challenge yourself. Push limits. But contrary to all the self-proclaimed success experts, doing it alone does not make you more successful or any better than someone who achieved it with the help of others.
questions.detailedExplanation:
【答案】 B （推断题）

【判型】 What can we infer from the passage regarding the pursuit of success? 中 infer 一词直接亮明题型属性。

【拆句】 What can we infer from the passage regarding the pursuit of success? What 作 infer 的宾语；regarding = 关于，介词短语作后置定语限定 infer 的范围。句意：关于追求成功，我们可以从本文推断出什么？句式平铺直叙。

【定位】 We cannot be complacent with losing friendships because they are our anchors. Yes, pursue success. Challenge yourself. Push limits. But contrary to all the self-proclaimed success experts, doing it alone does not make you more successful or any better than someone who achieved it with the help of others.

我们不能对失去友谊袖手旁观，因为朋友是我们的锚。是的，去追求成功，挑战自己，突破极限。但与所有自封的成功专家所言相反，独自一人完成它，并不会让你更成功，也并不比那些借助他人之力成功的人更高一筹。

【选项】 A) 过度推断 No one can succeed without pushing limits. 借 Push limits 一词夸大为 "没有人不突破极限就能成功"，但原文仅说 "是的，去突破极限" 作为肯定后退一步的让步话，并未声明 "不突破极限就不能成功"。

B) ✓ 正确 We cannot be complacent with losing friendships because they are our anchors.↔

No one can afford to neglect close friends. having people to support and love you on the way is far more important than any end result↔

No one can afford to neglect close friends. 在四项中，只有 No one can afford to neglect close friends. 是从 P8 P9 两处强表态合理延伸一步得到的结论，故选 B。 C) 过度推断 Collectivism is superior to individualism. 把 Radical individualism elevates the freedom of the individual over the collective 与 universal healthcare, an example of collectivism 加工成 "集体主义比个人主义优越" 的全称比较，但原文只反对 "极端" 个人主义，并未抬高集体主义本身。

D) 过度推断 Success experts often lead people to ruin. 来自 contrary to all the self-proclaimed success experts，作者只是 "与所谓的成功专家相反"，并未宣称 "成功专家把人引向毁灭"——ruin 一词是文外强化。

items.title: 2025年12月六级第1套 · 仔细阅读 · 第二篇
items.passage:
During his acceptance speech for the Nobel Peace Prize, Martin Luther King Jr. said, "I believe that unarmed truth and unconditional love will have the final word in reality."

More than five decades later, our society is still struggling to separate truth from fantasy, fact from fiction. From disputes over the climate change to debates about how slavery is taught, America is at a crossroads. And the battle for equity is at the heart of these vital conversations.

Study after study shows that inequity has had appalling consequences. A 2020 report by Citi indicated that "Black students could have increased their lifetime incomes $90 – $113 billion" if equity issues related to higher education had been adequately addressed over the past two decades.

This statistic represents a flood of issues we've failed to confront as a nation. It also highlights one truth: We're missing out on valuable opportunities to bridge the differences that divide us. However, by honoring King's legacy, we can get our country back on the path toward true equity.

Students — and adults for that matter — simply cannot understand the conflicts we have today without understanding what caused them in the first place. That means we have a responsibility to help them make connections between US history and current events. It also means giving them the tools they need to address inequity and bias in their own lives. Adherence to these principles, along with a commitment to truthful dialogue, can help every student better appreciate how far we've come and more clearly see the roads we have yet to travel.

With more truthful analysis of the need for more qualified, diverse educators, we can improve our recruiting, training, and retention strategies for schools across the country.

Unfortunately, our deeply rooted divisions are delaying these advancements. A recent survey found that 77 percent of Americans believe the nation is "more divided than ever before". But reports of increased polarization shouldn't persuade us to look away from one another. Instead, they should compel us to address our shared issues head-on.

We are not, as some would suggest, living in a "post-racial society". We simply cannot afford to keep our heads buried in the sand when it comes to racial inequity. Unless we get honest about intolerance, bias, and how these social diseases impact the ways we treat one another, injustice will continue to haunt us. But our children and our grandchildren deserve better.

On this Martin Luther King Day and beyond, let's commit to working together to disrupt the status quo. Let's continue to build a better, more inclusive nation; and in the words of Martin Luther King Jr., "A society at peace with itself, a society that can live with its conscience."

questions.prompt: What does the author think about today's America?

options.text: It is struggling to transform fiction into reality.
It has been the focus of many vital conversations.
It still has a long way to go before equity can be truly realized.
It has got to a point where people disagree on nearly every issue.

questions.shortExplanation: However, by honoring King's legacy, we can get our country back on the path toward true equity.
questions.detailedExplanation:
【答案】 C （细节题）

【判型】 题干 What does the author think about today's America? 问的是作者对一个明确对象的具体看法，不是问全文主旨、不含 infer/imply。

【拆句】 句子结构是 What does the author think about today's America?，主语 the author、谓语 think、介词宾语 today's America；无从句、无否定，结构平铺直叙，无陷阱。

【定位】 However, by honoring King's legacy, we can get our country back on the path toward true equity.

然而，只要传承（马丁·路德·）金的精神遗产，我们就能让国家重新回到通向真正公平的道路上。

【选项】 A) 与原文相反 struggling to transform fiction into reality 的字面义是「努力把虚构变成现实」，与 struggling to separate truth from fantasy（努力分清真相与幻象）方向相反——原文是要分开两者，不是把虚构变成现实。

B) 张冠李戴 It has been the focus of many vital conversations 把美国当成「对话的焦点」；但 the battle for equity is at the heart of these vital conversations 里说的是「公平之战是这些对话的核心」，焦点是 equity，不是美国。 C) ✓ 正确 get our country back on the path toward true equity ↔

still has a long way to go before equity can be truly realized our society is still struggling to separate truth from fantasy↔ still has a long way to go 预判「离真正公平还远」与 still has a long way to go before equity can be truly realized 一一对应，且呼应 still struggling——锁定 C。

D) 以偏概全 disagree on nearly every issue 把分歧泛化到「几乎每一个议题」；原文只举了 climate change 与 how slavery is taught 等具体议题，且作者关心的核心是 equity， 没有「几乎每个议题都有分歧」的论断。

questions.prompt: What do we learn from the passage about black students in the past 20 years?

options.text: They have been unfairly treated regarding higher education.
They have been battling hard to address equity issues.
They have boosted their lifetime incomes by billions of dollars.
They have come to see the consequences of racial discrimination.

questions.shortExplanation: A 2020 report by Citi indicated that "Black students could have increased their lifetime incomes $90 – $113 billion" if equity issues related to higher education had been adequately addressed over the past two decades.
questions.detailedExplanation:
【答案】 A （细节题）

【判型】 题干 What do we learn from the passage about black students in the past 20 years? 问从文中「得知」什么，明确锁定群体加时间，是要求回原文复述事实。

【拆句】 What do we learn from the passage about black students in the past 20 years? 是 What...about... 结构，about 后跟的 black students in the past 20 years 是定位对象；结构清晰，无陷阱。

【定位】 A 2020 report by Citi indicated that "Black students could have increased their lifetime incomes $90 – $113 billion" if equity issues related to higher education had been adequately addressed over the past two decades.

花旗集团 2020 年的一份报告指出：如果过去二十年里高等教育中的公平问题得到了妥善处理，黑人学生本可以多挣 900 亿到 1130 亿美元的终身收入。

【选项】 A) ✓ 正确 if equity issues related to higher education had been adequately addressed over the past two decades

↔ unfairly treated regarding higher education Black students could have increased their lifetime incomes $90 – $113 billion ↔

They have been unfairly treated 预判「过去二十年高等教育对黑人学生不公」与 unfairly treated regarding higher education 一一对应——锁定 A。

B) 无中生有 battling hard to address equity issues 把「被动遭遇不公」换成「主动奋力解决公平问题」；原文只说公平问题如果被妥善处理黑人学生本可多挣钱，并未说他们自己在奋斗解决。

C) 与原文相反 They have boosted their lifetime incomes by billions of dollars 用现在完成时陈述 「已经多挣了」；原文是 could have increased 虚拟语气，含义是「本可以但实际没有」——选项把虚拟当作了现实。

D) 偷换概念 come to see the consequences of racial discrimination 把话题偷换成「看清种族歧视的后果」；原文谈的是高等教育公平问题与黑人学生的收入损失，并未提及他们「认识到歧视后果」这一心理变化。

questions.prompt: How can Americans bridge the differences that divide them?

options.text: By dealing with the thorny issues confronting them.
By seizing every chance to enhance racial harmony.
By continuing to pursue Martin Luther King Jr.'s cause.
By striving to identify exceedingly valuable opportunities.

questions.shortExplanation: However, by honoring King's legacy, we can get our country back on the path toward true equity.
questions.detailedExplanation:
【答案】 C （细节题）

【判型】 题干 How can Americans bridge the differences that divide them? 问的是「如何做到 X」，要求从原文找具体路径，是细节题。

【拆句】 How can Americans bridge the differences that divide them? 中 that divide them 是定语从句修饰 differences，等于 the differences which divide Americans；结构稍长， 但无否定无比较，逻辑直白。

【定位】 However, by honoring King's legacy, we can get our country back on the path toward true equity.

然而，只要传承（马丁·路德·）金的精神遗产，我们就能让国家重新回到通向真正公平的道路上。

【选项】 A) 答非所问 dealing with the thorny issues confronting them 描述的是「直面棘手问题」。原文 address our shared issues head-on 这一表述是作者对 polarization 的回应，并非他给出的「弥合分歧」路径；定位句 P4 给出的路径只有 honoring King's legacy。 B) 无中生有 seizing every chance to enhance racial harmony 把答案拉到「抓住一切机会促进种族和谐」。原文只谈 equity、bridge differences、honor King's legacy，没有 racial harmony 的提法，也没有 every chance 这种全称量化。

C) ✓ 正确 by honoring King's legacy ↔ continuing to pursue Martin Luther King Jr.'s cause in the words of Martin Luther King Jr., "A society at peace with itself, a society that can live with its conscience."

↔ Martin Luther King Jr.'s cause 预判「继承金的精神遗产」与 By continuing to pursue Martin Luther King Jr.'s cause 一一对应——锁定 C。

D) 偷换概念 striving to identify exceedingly valuable opportunities 截取了 missing out on valuable opportunities 中的 valuable opportunities，但原文的语义是「我们正在错失机会」，并非「努力识别极有价值的机会」；选项把「错过」扭成「努力寻找」。

questions.prompt: How do most Americans view America as a nation according to a recent survey?

options.text: It is compelled to address its historical social issues.
It is delaying advancements toward racial equality.
It has kept itself from polarization.

questions.shortExplanation: A recent survey found that 77 percent of Americans believe the nation is "more divided than ever before".
questions.detailedExplanation:
【答案】 D （细节题）

【判型】 题干 How do most Americans view America as a nation according to a recent survey? 明确说 according to a recent survey，要求复述调查数据，是细节题。

【拆句】 How do most Americans view America as a nation according to a recent survey? 主干是 How do most Americans view America，as a nation 是补足语相当于把 America 视作一个国家整体，according to a recent survey 是状语限定信息来源；无陷阱。

【定位】 A recent survey found that 77 percent of Americans believe the nation is "more divided than ever before".

一项近期调查发现，77% 的美国人认为这个国家「前所未有地分裂」。

【选项】 A) 张冠李戴 compelled to address its historical social issues 借用了 they should compel us to address our shared issues head-on 的措辞，但那句话是作者对 polarization 报告的回应，不是 most Americans 在调查中表达的看法；本题问的是 most Americans 的看法。 B) 张冠李戴 delaying advancements toward racial equality 借用 our deeply rooted divisions are delaying these advancements，但原文里拖延进步的主语是 our deeply rooted divisions（根深蒂固的分裂），且这是作者的判断而非调查结论；本题问的是调查里美国人怎么看美国。 C) 与原文相反 has kept itself from polarization 意为「避免了两极分化」。原文 reports of increased polarization 明确说「两极分化在加剧」，且 77% 的美国人认为国家更分裂 ——选项与调查结论方向相反。

D) ✓ 正确 more divided than ever before ↔ increasingly split 77 percent of Americans believe ↔ It has become increasingly split 预判「国家越来越分裂」与 has become increasingly split 一一对应——锁定 D。
questions.hint: 回到原文定位题干关键词，比较选项与原文的含义。

questions.prompt: What does the author suggest Americans do?

options.text: Ensure the well-being of their children and grandchildren.
Make joint efforts to tackle the nation's equity issues.
Restore social order for a harmonious nation.

questions.shortExplanation: On this Martin Luther King Day and beyond, let's commit to working together to disrupt the status quo.
questions.detailedExplanation:
【答案】 B （细节题）

【判型】 题干 What does the author suggest Americans do? 问作者建议美国人做什么——是一个落到具体动作的细节题，不是问全文中心。

【拆句】 What does the author suggest Americans do? 是宾语从句结构，suggest 后省略 that，Americans 是从句主语、do 是从句谓语原形；结构清晰，无陷阱。

【定位】 On this Martin Luther King Day and beyond, let's commit to working together to disrupt the status quo.

在马丁·路德·金日及今后，让我们一起承诺携手努力，打破现状。

【选项】 A) 答非所问 Ensure the well-being of their children and grandchildren 借用 our children and our grandchildren deserve better，但那句是说「下一代值得更好」——是作者的忧虑动机，不是他给读者的具体建议；选项把动机当成了行动。 B) ✓ 正确 let's commit to working together to disrupt the status quo↔

Make joint efforts to tackle the nation's equity issues the path toward true equity↔the nation's equity issues 预判「联手打破现状」与 Make joint efforts to tackle the nation's equity issues 一一对应——锁定 B。 C) 偷换概念 Restrain their intolerance and discrimination 把答案换成「克制偏狭与歧视」。原文 Unless we get honest about intolerance, bias 要求的是「对偏狭与偏见保持诚实」 ——是承认与谈论，而不是 restrain（克制压抑）。 D) 偷换概念 Restore social order for a harmonious nation 借用末段 build a better, more inclusive nation 的「建设国家」色彩，但 restore social order（恢复社会秩序）原文从未提及；原文是「建设更包容」，不是「恢复秩序」。
questions.hint: 回到原文定位题干关键词，比较选项与原文的含义。

items.title: 2025年12月六级第2套 · 选词填空
items.passage:
We humans love to believe we are special, but science and technology have repeatedly proved this conviction wrong. People [26] _____ thought that humans were the only animals to use tools, to form teams or to propagate culture, but science has shown that other animals do each of these things.

Meanwhile, technology has quashed( 使⽆效 ), one by one, claims that [27] _____ tasks require a human brain. The first adding machine was invented in 1623. This past year, a computer-generated work won an art contest. I believe the moment when computers meet and [28] _____ human intelligence is on the horizon.

How will human intelligence and creativity be valued when machines become smarter and more creative than the brightest people? There will likely be a spectrum. In some [29] _____ , people still value humans doing things, even if a computer can do it better. It's been a quarter of a century since a computer beat world champion Garry Kasparov, but human chess hasn't gone away.

In other fields, human skill will seem costly and [30] _____ . Take illustration for example: most readers don't care whether the graphic [31] _____ a magazine article was drawn by a person or a

computer — they just want it to be relevant, new and perhaps [32] _____ .

And, of course, this question isn't black or white. Many fields will be a [33] _____ , where some humans find a lucky place, but most of the work is done by computers, like in manufacturing today, where much of the work is accomplished by robots, but some humans must be there to [34] _____ the machines.

If history is any guide, it's almost certain that advances in AI will cause more jobs to [35] _____ , that creative workers with human-only skills will become richer but fewer in number, and that those who own creative technology will become the new ultra-rich.

questions.prompt: People __(26)__ thought that humans were the only animals to use tools
questions.shortExplanation: 与 but 后的 has shown 构成今昔对比
questions.detailedExplanation:
【答案】 I) once 副词

【词性槽】 主语与谓语之间的状语位

【依据】 与 but 后的 has shown 构成今昔对比

People __(26)__ thought that humans were the only animals to use tools, to form teams or to propagate culture, but science has shown that other animals do each of these things. 前半句过去时 thought、后半句现在完成时 has shown，典型 "过去曾以为 / 如今已证明" 结构，填 once（曾经）正好咬合这条时间逻辑。

【竞争词】 N) tentatively 语义指向不对，是 "试探性地" 而非 "曾经"

tentatively 意为 "暂时地、试探性地"，强调态度不坚定。但原文说人们 "长久以为人类是唯一会用工具的动物"，这是一种**坚信**而非试探，与下句被 but 反转的语气不匹配。
questions.hint: 根据空格前后的词性、搭配与上下文选择词语；每个词最多使用一次。

questions.prompt: technology has quashed(使⽆效), one by one, claims that __(27)__ tasks require a human brain
questions.shortExplanation: 与 "require a human brain" 同义呼应
questions.detailedExplanation:
【答案】 B) cognitive 形容词

【词性槽】 名词 tasks 前的前置定语

【依据】 与 "require a human brain" 同义呼应

claims that __(27)__ tasks require a human brain——能 require a human brain（需要人脑）的任务，正是 cognitive tasks（认知性的任务、需要思维加工的任务）。下一句又用 adding machine、computer-generated art、computer matches human intelligence 反复指向 "智力/认知"，B 与上下文构成最稳同义网。

【竞争词】 H) intuitive"直觉的" 与 "人脑认知" 范围不符

intuitive 指 "凭直觉的"，强调非理性、不依靠分析。而本段下文举例（加法机、AI 绘画、计算机匹敌人类智能）恰恰是**理性认知**任务被机器接管，与 intuitive 的语义指向相反。

D) entertaining"有趣的" 偏娱乐，与 "需要人脑" 不沾边

entertaining 指 "令人愉快的、有娱乐性的"，与 require a human brain（需要人脑）这一论点完全脱节，纯属词性诱饵。

K) redundant "多余的任务" 与原意南辕北辙

redundant 是 "多余的、被裁掉的"——"多余的任务需要人脑" 在逻辑上根本说不通；况且 K 后文 30 题正等着它。

【易错】 最具迷惑性的错误词是 H) —— 看到 AI 话题就联想 "直觉"。intuitive 词性对、又与 AI 话题表面沾边（"机器没有直觉"），最易让考生误填。防坑：claims that __(27)__ tasks require a human brain 里同句锚词是 a human brain，"需要人脑的任务" = cognitive （认知性的），而非 intuitive（直觉的）。"找同句同义锚" 是六级选词填空的必修招式。
questions.hint: 根据空格前后的词性、搭配与上下文选择词语；每个词最多使用一次。

questions.prompt: the moment when computers meet and __(28)__ human intelligence is on the horizon.
questions.shortExplanation: "匹敌并超越" 是 AI 论述的固定搭配
questions.detailedExplanation:
【答案】 M) surpass 动词

【词性槽】 and 并列谓语：computers meet and __ human intelligence

【依据】 "匹敌并超越" 是 AI 论述的固定搭配

I believe the moment when computers meet and __(28)__ human intelligence is on the horizon.——meet（达到/匹敌）+ surpass（超越）是 AI 话题里最常见的递进搭配， 且呼应第三段 when machines become smarter and more creative than the brightest people（变得比最聪明的人更聪明、更有创造力），证实方向就是 "超越"。
questions.hint: 根据空格前后的词性、搭配与上下文选择词语；每个词最多使用一次。

questions.prompt: In some __(29)__, people still value humans doing things, even if a computer can do it better.
questions.shortExplanation: "在某些领域里" 与下文 In other fields 形成对照
questions.detailedExplanation:
【答案】 C) domains 名词

【词性槽】 介词 In some 后的名词复数

【依据】 "在某些领域里" 与下文 In other fields 形成对照

下一段开头 In other fields, human skill will seem costly and __(30)__. 用 In other fields 与本段 In some __(29)__ 形成 "在某些领域 / 在另一些领域" 的并列对照；domains（领域）与 fields 同义，正好咬合这条段间对照逻辑。

【竞争词】 L) stances "立场" 与下文 fields 不对应

stances 指 "立场、姿态"，是抽象观点。但下段 in other fields 明确把对比维度定在 "领域" 而非 "立场"——填 stances 会让段间对照失锚。

G) impetus 形态不对：单数且不可数

impetus 通常作不可数单数（推动力），与 some + 复数名词的结构不合；语义上 "在某些推动力里人们仍重视人类" 也不通。

【易错】 最具迷惑性的错误词是 L) —— 复数名词形态一致的假同义。stances 与 domains 同为复数名词、同能套进 In some __ 结构，最易混。防坑：盯紧下段段首 In other fields——"领域 vs 立场" 是两条线，fields 同义对应 domains。"段间对照锁名词" 一招直接破。
questions.hint: 根据空格前后的词性、搭配与上下文选择词语；每个词最多使用一次。

questions.prompt: In other fields, human skill will seem costly and __(30)__.
questions.shortExplanation: "昂贵 + 多余" 共同描述被淘汰的人类技能本段例 most readers don't care whether the graphic __(31)__ a magazine article was drawn by a person or a computer——读者并不在意是人画的还是机器画的，意味着人类技能既贵又**没必要**，redundant（多余的、被裁掉的）正好把这层负面评价点透。
questions.detailedExplanation:
【答案】 K) redundant 形容词

【词性槽】 并列连词 and 后接形容词，与 costly 并列

【依据】 "昂贵 + 多余" 共同描述被淘汰的人类技能本段例 most readers don't care whether the graphic __(31)__ a magazine article was drawn by a person or a computer——读者并不在意是人画的还是机器画的，意味着人类技能既贵又**没必要**，redundant（多余的、被裁掉的）正好把这层负面评价点透。

【竞争词】 D) entertaining 褒义色彩与 costly 不同向

entertaining（有趣的）偏褒，而 costly 偏负面——并列时色彩不一致，逻辑上 "昂贵且有趣" 也无法描述被市场淘汰的人类劳动。

H) intuitive"直觉的" 与 "被淘汰" 主线不沾

intuitive 指 "直觉的"，并不直接传递价值高低、是否被取代的信息，与本段 "人类技能将变得不值" 的论点错位。
questions.hint: 根据空格前后的词性、搭配与上下文选择词语；每个词最多使用一次。

questions.prompt: most readers don't care whether the graphic __(31)__ a magazine article was drawn by a person or a computer
questions.shortExplanation: "配文插图" 是固定搭配 the graphic __(31)__ a magazine article was drawn by a person or a computer—— graphic accompanying a magazine article 即 "配在杂志文章旁的插图"，accompany 与 graphic/article 是新闻出版中的常规搭配。
questions.detailedExplanation:
【答案】 A) accompanying 形容词

【词性槽】 the graphic __ a magazine article：现在分词作后置定语

【依据】 "配文插图" 是固定搭配 the graphic __(31)__ a magazine article was drawn by a person or a computer—— graphic accompanying a magazine article 即 "配在杂志文章旁的插图"，accompany 与 graphic/article 是新闻出版中的常规搭配。

【竞争词】 E) evoking "唤起一篇文章" 搭配不成立

evoking 是 "唤起、引发"，搭配对象多是 emotion/memory 等抽象名词；evoke a magazine article（唤起一篇杂志文章）语义不通，逻辑上也不是 "插图与文章" 的关系。
questions.hint: 根据空格前后的词性、搭配与上下文选择词语；每个词最多使用一次。

questions.prompt: they just want it to be relevant, new and perhaps __(32)__.
questions.shortExplanation: 读者期待 "贴题、新颖、有趣" 三件套 they just want it to be relevant, new and perhaps __(32)__.——读者作为大众，对杂志插图的诉求是 relevant（与文章相关）、new（新鲜）、entertaining（有趣）这三件套， 构成同色彩并列；perhaps 又留了余地，正合 "有趣" 这种偏锦上添花的属性。
questions.detailedExplanation:
【答案】 D) entertaining 形容词

【词性槽】 and 并列形容词链：relevant, new and __

【依据】 读者期待 "贴题、新颖、有趣" 三件套 they just want it to be relevant, new and perhaps __(32)__.——读者作为大众，对杂志插图的诉求是 relevant（与文章相关）、new（新鲜）、entertaining（有趣）这三件套， 构成同色彩并列；perhaps 又留了余地，正合 "有趣" 这种偏锦上添花的属性。

【竞争词】 H) intuitive "直觉的" 与并列项不同色彩

intuitive 偏认知/操作领域（如 intuitive interface 易上手的界面），与读者读杂志插图时的诉求错位；与 relevant、new 也无法构成同色彩并列。
questions.hint: 根据空格前后的词性、搭配与上下文选择词语；每个词最多使用一次。

questions.prompt: Many fields will be a __(33)__, where some humans find a lucky place, but most of the work is done by computers
questions.shortExplanation: where 从句直接定义 "人机混合"
questions.detailedExplanation:
【答案】 F) hybrid 名词

【词性槽】 a + __ 单数可数名词位

【依据】 where 从句直接定义 "人机混合"

Many fields will be a __(33)__, where some humans find a lucky place, but most of the work is done by computers, like in manufacturing today, where much of the work is accomplished by robots, but some humans must be there to __(34)__ the machines.——where 从句里 "some humans … but most of the work is done by computers" 把空名词定义成 "人机混合体"，hybrid 是唯一精准对应词。

【竞争词】 G) impetus "推动力" 与 "人机混合" 错位

impetus 是 "推动力、动力"，无法被 where 从句中 "既有人又有计算机" 的描述合理修饰；"许多领域将成为一种推动力" 在语义上也不通。
questions.hint: 根据空格前后的词性、搭配与上下文选择词语；每个词最多使用一次。

questions.prompt: some humans must be there to __(34)__ the machines.
questions.shortExplanation: "机器为主、人来监管" 正是本段图景
questions.detailedExplanation:
【答案】 J) oversee 动词

【词性槽】 must be there to + 动词原形

【依据】 "机器为主、人来监管" 正是本段图景

much of the work is accomplished by robots, but some humans must be there to __(34)__ the machines. 转折 but 之后明确：活儿主要由机器人干，但仍要有人 "在场"——"在场对机器" 干什么？最贴合的就是 "监督、监管" oversee，与制造业现实经验也一致。

【竞争词】 M) surpass "超越机器" 与本段 "人辅助机器" 逻辑反向

surpass（超越）会把句意变成 "人必须在场以超越机器"，与 but 引出的 "机器为主、人为辅" 的图景反向；况且 surpass 已是 28 题的答案。

O) vanish 不及物动词不能带 machines

vanish 是不及物动词（消失），其后不能直接接 the machines 作宾语；语义上 "人必须在那里以消失机器" 也不通。
questions.hint: 根据空格前后的词性、搭配与上下文选择词语；每个词最多使用一次。

questions.prompt: advances in AI will cause more jobs to __(35)__
questions.shortExplanation: AI 会让更多工作消失，对应全段悲观预测 advances in AI will cause more jobs to __(35)__, that creative workers with human-only skills will become richer but fewer in number——后半 "人类技能工作者会变少" 直接揭示前半 "更多工作 __" 的方向是 "消失"，vanish 正中靶心。
questions.detailedExplanation:
【答案】 O) vanish 动词

【词性槽】 cause more jobs to + 动词原形

【依据】 AI 会让更多工作消失，对应全段悲观预测 advances in AI will cause more jobs to __(35)__, that creative workers with human-only skills will become richer but fewer in number——后半 "人类技能工作者会变少" 直接揭示前半 "更多工作 __" 的方向是 "消失"，vanish 正中靶心。
questions.hint: 根据空格前后的词性、搭配与上下文选择词语；每个词最多使用一次。

items.title: 2025年12月六级第2套 · 信息匹配
items.passage:
A) Projects, relationships, and jobs don't always work out as planned — and it's not always clear when to give up. We've all repeatedly heard the saying that "quitters never win", but sometimes the best decision is to cut our losses.

B) Think about that relationship you held on to even after it had run its course or the job you stayed in despite your boss making you miserable. Many of us try to hold onto the last ray of hope, thinking we can make it work, whatever "it" is. And while perseverance is generally an excellent quality, it may also incline you to over-invest in something that is no longer a good idea.

C) As an executive coach, I work with numerous passionate and hard-working leaders who don't want to "quit". But the smartest leaders learn to discern the difference between quitting too soon and holding onto something that they shouldn't.

D) We are all susceptible to the sunk-cost delusion, an unconscious bias that leads us to persist in an endeavor we have already invested time, effort, or money into — even when abandoning it would be more beneficial. We realize that we can't get back the resources we've given, so we persevere — investing in a project that should be halted, staying in a relationship that should be over, or finishing a book we no longer enjoy and should put down, because we're already halfway through it. If quitting is "not your thing", you may be especially susceptible to this bias.

E) The sunk-cost delusion causes us to overly worry about what we'll lose if we move on and not think enough about the costs of not moving on. To offset this bias, deliberately refocus your thinking on the gains so you can more objectively weigh the alternatives. Ask yourself: What might I gain by cutting my losses now? Will you be happier or have time for another (better) opportunity? Then ask yourself: What will it cost me to soldier on? For example, is it possible that you'll be throwing more good money after what you've already lost? Or that you won't have the energy to capitalize on other promising possibilities?

F) The illusion of control can also interfere with our best judgment, leading us to overestimate our ability to control events and attain a positive outcome. This bias gives us a sense of agency and can promote mental health. However, the bias can also result in escalating commitment to a losing course of action. Especially when combined with an "I'm not a quitter" mentality, feeling like we have more control over an event or person than we do puts us at risk of doubling down when we should pull out.

G) To counteract this bias, consider your situation and make a simple two-column list of what's in your control and what's not. Think rigorously. While you may be able to influence other people and various circumstances, you can't force them to change or go your way.

H) Getting clear on what you can control and what you can't is essential to making a quality decision about whether to call it quits or persevere. With a written list in hand, you can ensure you focus on what you can control and better assess whether your continued efforts are worth the expense. Expending effort and emotion on things you can't control can be both draining and disempowering.

I) Research indicates that people link their self-identity and social status to their commitments. And because we identify with our commitments, withdrawing from one can feel like a threat to our identity or status.

J) Take my client Ryan, a leader at a technology company. Ryan had invested two years and a lot of effort in a design project that wasn't delivering the needed outcomes, but the thought of abandoning it after all she had put in was hard to bear. As Ryan and I explored whether she should cancel the initiative she'd been leading or continue to persevere, she stated, "The thing is, I'm not a quitter." This singular, fixed sense of self was clouding her judgment and limiting her choices for action.

K) Our self-concept and identity are mental concepts that influence our behavior. If you strongly identify as not being a quitter, you can end up staying stuck in a course of action due to your narrow and rigid self-concept. To overcome this kind of internal obstacle, recall your other positive traits and personality characteristics. Ask yourself: What additional strengths do I have (or aspire to have) that would be helpful to employ here? For example, when I asked Ryan what other positive qualities from her personality she needed to leverage for decision making, she replied, "Discernment and bravery."

L) Now, examine your situation through the lens of each of these facets of yourself. What does the discerning part of you say? The brave part? Considering your decision through these different characteristics will enable you to see that you have more choices. It's also helpful to seek external sources of information, rather than relying solely on your thinking and instincts. But it's important to think through whose opinions you solicit.

M) Ideally, seek out people who are less invested in your decision than you are. If you're considering whether to shut down your entrepreneurial venture, for instance, reach out to other founders as opposed to just your business partner. Similarly, if you're looking for love advice, ask someone removed from the ups and downs of your relationship instead of relying only on your best friend. In all cases, I recommend describing your situation and following up with a question like: "How would you manage this situation?"

N) Alternately, you could also seek out hard data that illuminates your real chance of success in whatever endeavor you are contemplating. Sticking with the example of the entrepreneurial venture, numbers are your best friend. Use them to remove yourself from the love you have for this idea and consider your burn rate relative to growth plan, industry growth rates, and other factors that predict start-up success. External sources of information can help you see angles and possibilities you might not have considered.

O) When something that seemed so promising at the start doesn't turn out the way we imagined, we can become overly self-critical. Nobody likes to feel that they've made a poor decision, especially if making intelligent decisions is a quality you hold in high esteem. The most effective strategy here is to give yourself a break. Practicing self-compassion increases your resilience(韧性), emotional intelligence, compassion toward others, and can boost your performance as well as help you develop a growth mindset.

P) Instead of deliberating and criticizing yourself, focus instead on what you can learn from this situation. For example, Ryan recognized she had developed various new skills and leadership capabilities from leading the design project. And despite ultimately deciding to drop it, she was still happy she had tried and grateful for what the experience taught her.

Q) Undeniably, perseverance can help us succeed. But for your well-being, it's important to learn how to distinguish quitting too soon and clinging to a losing course of action. While letting go can be difficult, it will free up your time, energy, and mental space to imagine new possibilities and pursue new opportunities.

items.title: 2025年12月六级第2套 · 仔细阅读 · 第一篇
items.passage:
As interdependent beings we cannot thrive independent of others. We like to work with people who are like-minded, with whom we share a common interest, or who also believe in a cause we are serious about. This is evident in how we have organized ourselves into various collective groups such as nations, regions, communities, organizations, and families.

Does the group you belong to have a strong collective consciousness or shared beliefs? Is there interdependence among its members? Do you consider this group a significant part of your existence? If your answers are affirmative, then you are experiencing a micro version of solidarity.

What is solidarity? Its simplest definition in the dictionary is: "… a unifying opinion, feeling, purpose or interest among a group of people."

In this increasingly diverse society we live in, solidarity takes on a complex and multifaceted character as it forms bonds of interdependence among unique individuals living in a fast-changing environment and working within a complex division of labor.

One facet of solidarity fits well with the principles of communitarianism(社群主义). In this setting, individuals give up their own interests to serve the common good. However, its strict adherence to social cohesiveness and exclusiveness restricts expression and practice of individual differences and preferences. Consequently, individuality and autonomy are sacrificed to maintain the unity of the group.

Solidarity is also viewed as a reaction to the extreme emphasis on individualism and freedom of choice. It goes against the liberal idea of unrestricted individuals who see society as a hindrance to their freedom to make choices and to act according to what is good for them regardless of how these will affect others.

But despite its many facets, social theorists have viewed solidarity as a key factor in bringing about order and progress in society. They believe that for human society to survive as it becomes more diverse, more new bonds need to be formed based on the differences. In the light of this, they regard a genuine solidarity as more than just shallow relationships based on common interests. Solidarity is not just a product of strategic calculations of how much it will benefit the self. It is not an exclusive class founded on the you-and-me-against-the-world principle. Rather, it is inclusive and is not forced. Acting out of solidarity means supporting and standing up for each other — in recognition that one's fate is in the fate of the other. It is a bond characterized by cooperative practices and strengthened by the concern for the well-being of others or the common good. It fights for the protection of human dignity and listens to and acts on the cries of the most vulnerable.

questions.prompt: What does the author say about human beings?

options.text: They cannot prosper without cooperating with each other.
They share a common interest and believe in a just cause.
They think and behave alike in different social groups.
They cannot gain independence without fighting for it.

questions.shortExplanation: As interdependent beings we cannot thrive independent of others.
questions.detailedExplanation:
【答案】 A （细节题）

【判型】 What does the author say about human beings? 问的是作者就 human beings 这一具体对象说了什么，落点在某一具体陈述上而非整篇主旨。

【拆句】 What does the author say about human beings? 是常规疑问句结构，主干 "the author say"，关于 human beings，无从句、无否定、无比较，结构平铺直叙，无陷阱。

【定位】 As interdependent beings we cannot thrive independent of others.

作为相互依赖的存在，我们无法脱离他人独自繁荣兴盛。

【选项】 A) ✓ 正确 thrive ↔ prosper cannot thrive independent of others ↔ cannot prosper without cooperating with each other They cannot prosper without cooperating with each other. 把 cannot thrive independent of others 改写为"必须合作才能兴旺"，正是预判内容的同义转述。

B) 偷换概念 They share a common interest and believe in a just cause. 取自 we share a common interest, or who also believe in a cause we are serious about，但原文这是"喜欢和谁一起工作"的举例，不是对 human beings 的总体陈述；且 cause 被偷换为 just cause（正义事业）。 C) 过度推断 They think and behave alike in different social groups. 声称"在不同群体中想法行为都一样"，原文只说人喜欢和"like-minded"的人共事，并未说人在所有群体中思想行为都相同。

D) 与原文相反 They cannot gain independence without fighting for it. 谈"独立要靠斗争争取"，但原文 we cannot thrive independent of others 强调的是"无法独立"而非"为独立而战"，话题相反。
questions.hint: 回到原文定位题干关键词，比较选项与原文的含义。

questions.prompt: What do we learn about solidarity in an increasingly diverse society?

options.text: It gives rise to a complicated division of labor.
It involves many aspects with great complexity.
It brings individuals together as environment changes.
It embraces the characteristics of different individuals.

questions.shortExplanation: In this increasingly diverse society we live in, solidarity takes on a complex and multifaceted character as it forms bonds of interdependence among unique individuals living in a fast-changing environment and working within a complex division of labor.
questions.detailedExplanation:
【答案】 B （细节题）

【判型】 What do we learn about solidarity in an increasingly diverse society? 提问限定在"多元化社会下的 solidarity"这一局部，并非整篇主旨。

【拆句】 What do we learn about solidarity in an increasingly diverse society? 主干 "we learn about solidarity"，介词短语 "in an increasingly diverse society" 限定语境，无难句结构。

【定位】 In this increasingly diverse society we live in, solidarity takes on a complex and multifaceted character as it forms bonds of interdependence among unique individuals living in a fast-changing environment and working within a complex division of labor.

在我们所处的这个日益多元化的社会里，solidarity 呈现出复杂而多面的特征，因为它在快速变化的环境中、在复杂的分工内部，于各不相同的个体之间形成了相互依赖的纽带。

【选项】 A) 强加因果 It gives rise to a complicated division of labor. 说 solidarity 导致了复杂分工，但原文 working within a complex division of labor 是说 solidarity 发生"在"复杂分工"之内"，分工是背景而非结果。 B) ✓ 正确 takes on a complex and multifaceted character ↔

involves many aspects with great complexity takes on ↔ involves involves many aspects with great complexity 同时覆盖原文的 complex 和 multifaceted 两个核心修饰语，且未做任何额外延伸。 C) 以偏概全 It brings individuals together as environment changes. 把"形成相互依赖纽带"窄化为"把个体聚拢"，且偷换了主线——题干问的是"我们关于 solidarity 在多元社会中学到什么"，正确答案应概括其"特征"，C 选了一处细节当主答。 D) 偷换概念 It embraces the characteristics of different individuals. 说 solidarity"接纳"个体差异，但原文只说它在 unique individuals 之间形成纽带，并未说它"接纳"或"包含"个体特征。
questions.hint: 回到原文定位题干关键词，比较选项与原文的含义。

questions.prompt: What would we witness in the setting of communitarianism?

options.text: Ruling of social norms and ridding of individuality.
Emphasis on the adherence to individual differences.
Sacrifice of personal interests for the common good.
Elimination of individualism and personal choices.

questions.shortExplanation: In this setting, individuals give up their own interests to serve the common good.
questions.detailedExplanation:
【答案】 C （细节题）

【判型】 What would we witness in the setting of communitarianism? 问的是该情境下会观察到什么，指向文中具体描述句。

【拆句】 What would we witness in the setting of communitarianism? 主干 "we would witness"，"in the setting of communitarianism" 限定情境，would 表示一般陈述语气， 无难点。

【定位】 In this setting, individuals give up their own interests to serve the common good.

在这种情境下，个人放弃自身利益以服务于共同利益。

【选项】 A) 以偏概全 Ruling of social norms and ridding of individuality. 把"个体在某情境下放弃个人利益"夸大为"社会规范统治、个性被彻底清除"，原文虽提到 individuality 被牺牲，但用的是 sacrificed（让位）而非 ridding（彻底清除）。

B) 与原文相反 Emphasis on the adherence to individual differences. 说社群主义强调坚持个体差异，但原文 strict adherence to social cohesiveness and exclusiveness restricts expression and practice of individual differences 明说它限制了个体差异的表达，完全相反。

C) ✓ 正确 individuals give up their own interests ↔ Sacrifice of personal interests to serve the common good ↔ for the common good Sacrifice of personal interests for the common good. 是对 individuals give up their own interests to serve the common good 的完整、保守的名词化改写，与预判完全吻合。

D) 过度推断 Elimination of individualism and personal choices. 用 Elimination（彻底消除）描述社群主义的效果，但原文只说 individuality and autonomy are sacrificed（让位/牺牲），并未达到"彻底消除"的程度。
