questions.prompt: What does solidarity entail according to the passage?

options.text: An inevitable end to liberal pursuits.

questions.shortExplanation: Solidarity is also viewed as a reaction to the extreme emphasis on individualism and freedom of choice.
questions.detailedExplanation:
【答案】 B （细节题）

【判型】 What does solidarity entail according to the passage? 询问 solidarity 本质内涵，对应文中明确陈述句。

【拆句】 What does solidarity entail according to the passage? 标准疑问句，谓语动词 entail 是关键考词，"according to the passage" 为状语，结构简单。

【定位】 Solidarity is also viewed as a reaction to the extreme emphasis on individualism and freedom of choice.

solidarity 也被视为对极端强调个人主义与选择自由的一种反应（反对）。

【选项】 A) 张冠李戴 A limit to personal differences. 来自 restricts expression and practice of individual differences，那是讲社群主义的代价，不是讲 solidarity 整体的内涵；题干问的是 solidarity entail 什么。 B) ✓ 正确 a reaction to the extreme emphasis on individualism ↔ An opposition to individualism the extreme emphasis on individualism and freedom of choice ↔ individualism An opposition to individualism 是 a reaction to the extreme emphasis on individualism 最直接的同义改写，与预判一致。

C) 张冠李戴 A hindrance to social advancement. 把 solidarity 说成"社会进步的障碍"，但原文 see society as a hindrance to their freedom to make choices 是说"自由派认为社会是其自由的障碍"，hindrance 的主语应为 society 而非 solidarity；并且 P7 明说 solidarity 是 order and progress 的关键。

D) 过度推断 An inevitable end to liberal pursuits. 说 solidarity 会"不可避免地终结"自由派追求， 但原文只说它是对极端个人主义的 reaction（反对/回应），并未说会"终结"或必然成功，且 inevitable 加重了语气。

questions.prompt: What do social theorists think of solidarity?

options.text: It is especially relevant to the most vulnerable.

It is indispensable to avoiding shallow relationships.

questions.shortExplanation: But despite its many facets, social theorists have viewed solidarity as a key factor in bringing about order and progress in society.
questions.detailedExplanation:
【答案】 C （细节题）

【判型】 What do social theorists think of solidarity? 问的是 social theorists 这一具体群体的看法，定位明确，不是整篇作者主旨。

【拆句】 What do social theorists think of solidarity? 主语 "social theorists"，think of 是固定搭配"看待/认为"，结构平铺直叙。

【定位】 But despite its many facets, social theorists have viewed solidarity as a key factor in bringing about order and progress in society.

但是，尽管 solidarity 有诸多面向，社会理论家们仍把它视为推动社会秩序与进步的关键因素。

【选项】 A) 以偏概全 It is especially relevant to the most vulnerable. 取自 listens to and acts on the cries of the most vulnerable，原文这是对 solidarity 内涵的一种延伸描述， 且"especially relevant"是干扰项的额外断言；题干问的是社会理论家对 solidarity 的整体看法，而非"它最关乎谁"。 B) 过度推断 It is most effective in protecting human dignity. 用 most effective（最有效）做绝对化判断，但原文 It fights for the protection of human dignity 仅说它"为人类尊严而战"，并未与其他事物比较"最有效"。

C) ✓ 正确 a key factor in bringing about order and progress in society ↔

essential to progress and order in society bringing about order and progress in society ↔ progress and order in society essential to progress and order in society 是 a key factor in bringing about order and progress in society 的标准同义改写，与预判完全对应。 D) 偷换概念 It is indispensable to avoiding shallow relationships. 说 solidarity 对"避免肤浅关系"必不可少，但原文 they regard a genuine solidarity as more than just shallow relationships based on common interests 是说"真正的 solidarity 不仅仅是肤浅关系"，是在界定 solidarity 本身，而非说它用于"避免肤浅关系"。

items.title: 2025年12月六级第2套 · 仔细阅读 · 第二篇
items.passage:
People who repeatedly give unwanted advice can be well-meaning and genuinely want to help. Others might do this out of a sense of self-worth around the ability to influence others. One study found that people with a high tendency to seek power were more likely to give advice than those with an opposite tendency.

Under the guise( 外表 ) of unselfishness, people may be driven to give you unwanted advice because it makes them feel powerful or in control. They may not be fully aware of this drive, however.

These people may also display a problematic degree of emotional vulnerability, becoming upset very quickly, and taking a long time to calm down. It is possible that their emotions were only validated in childhood when they were at their loudest, encouraging them to adopt responses to discomfort that are excessive in most situations.

When someone is giving advice in order to make themselves feel more powerful, there is underlying anxiety to their behavior that recipients of the advice tend to notice. It can be tempting in this situation to react harshly to the advice giver and to accuse them of being manipulative, but this approach might produce an undesired result.

If the act of giving advice is contributing actively to someone's feelings of self-worth, an outright(直率的 ) rejection may be perceived as a threat, activating their fight-or-flight response, possibly causing them to double down on their validation-seeking behavior, or leading to a larger conflict.

The key is to validate without over-identifying. You can let them know that you have heard them and appreciate where they are coming from without taking on the potentially damaging narrative that you could not have gotten by without their help. You had better say something like, "Thanks for the idea. I have my own plan for handling this, but I really appreciate your perspective and will take it into consideration. Can I let you know when I need help in the future?"

If you have trouble setting boundaries tactfully, prioritize working on your own ability to self-regulate. As uncomfortable as it may be to continuously receive, if you can respond with compassion, the situation will likely defuse much faster.

Though it is usually not the intended outcome of giving unsolicited advice, many who receive it often feel stressed, offended, or simply annoyed by unwanted suggestions. Setting a boundary in this regard, if you feel you need one, is perfectly reasonable and something that can bring you increased emotional safety.

It is best to set boundaries in a way that takes into account the individual's underlying reasons for doing what they are doing to avoid unnecessary conflict and more stress.

questions.prompt: What is the finding of one study about people who keep giving unsolicited advice?

options.text: They turn out to be well-meaning.
They are capable of influencing others.
They are inclined to crave for power.

questions.shortExplanation: One study found that people with a high tendency to seek power were more likely to give advice than those with an opposite tendency.
questions.detailedExplanation:
【答案】 D （细节题）

【判型】 题干 What is the finding of one study 指向某个具体研究的事实性结论，不含 infer/imply/mainly。

【拆句】 题干主干是 What is the finding of one study，about 引导的介词短语修饰 finding，限定研究对象是 people who keep giving unsolicited advice（who 引导定语从句修饰 people）。结构平铺直叙，无陷阱。

【定位】 One study found that people with a high tendency to seek power were more likely to give advice than those with an opposite tendency.

一项研究发现，求权欲望强的人比求权欲望相反（低）的人更倾向于给出建议。

【选项】 A) 答非所问 They turn out to be well-meaning 取自首句 can be well-meaning，但那只是 give advice 的一种可能动机的铺垫，并非“研究的发现”。 B) 答非所问 They are genuinely kind-hearted 改写自 genuinely want to help，同样位于铺垫句，不是研究结论。

C) 偷换概念 They are capable of influencing others 把 self-worth around the ability to influence others 中“自我价值感来自影响他人的能力”误读为“具备影响他人能力”，且这同样不在 study 结论里。 D) ✓ 正确 a high tendency to seek power ↔ inclined to crave for power 四项中只有 inclined to crave for power 与预判“求权欲强者更爱给建议”形成 1:1 同义对应。
questions.hint: 回到原文定位题干关键词，比较选项与原文的含义。

questions.prompt: What is the problem with people who are driven to give you unsolicited advice?

options.text: They may be quick to upset others.
They want their voice to be the loudest.

questions.shortExplanation: These people may also display a problematic degree of emotional vulnerability, becoming upset very quickly, and taking a long time to calm down.
questions.detailedExplanation:
【答案】 B （细节题）

【判型】 题干 What is the problem with 指向一个可在原文中找到具体描述的缺陷。

【拆句】 主干 What is the problem，介词短语 with people who are driven to give you unsolicited advice 修饰 problem；who 引导被动语态定语从句。注意 driven 是被动，表示“被某种力量驱使”，而不是主动选择。

【定位】 These people may also display a problematic degree of emotional vulnerability, becoming upset very quickly, and taking a long time to calm down.

这些人还可能表现出某种程度上有问题的情绪脆弱性——很快就情绪激动，且久久不能平复。

【选项】 A) 张冠李戴 They may be quick to upset others 把原文中“自己易激动”扭曲为“使他人易激动”—— 动作发出者由 these people 变成对他人施加影响。 B) ✓ 正确 a problematic degree of emotional vulnerability ↔ emotionally vulnerable 预判的“情绪脆弱”在四项中只与 emotionally vulnerable 对应；A/C/D 都来自定位句的修饰部分。 C) 偷换概念 They want their voice to be the loudest 改自 their emotions were only validated in childhood when they were at their loudest，那是对成因的猜测且发生在童年，并非“现在的问题”本身。

D) 答非所问 They respond to discomfort excessively 取自 adopt responses to discomfort that are excessive in most situations，那是脆弱情绪导致的“反应方式”，是表现/后果，而题干问的是“问题本身”。
questions.hint: 回到原文定位题干关键词，比较选项与原文的含义。

questions.prompt: What is the advice receiver tempted to do when noticing the advice giver's underlying anxiety?

options.text: Reveal the undesired result of their approach.
Refuse their advice in an undisguised manner.
Bring their real motives to the surface.
Accuse them of trying to control others.

questions.shortExplanation: It can be tempting in this situation to react harshly to the advice giver and to accuse them of being manipulative, but this approach might produce an undesired result.
questions.detailedExplanation:
【答案】 D （细节题）

【判型】 题干 What is the advice receiver tempted to do 指向一个原文中可直接对应的具体行为。

【拆句】 主干 What is the advice receiver tempted to do，when 引导时间状语从句 when noticing the advice giver’s underlying anxiety（noticing 为分词短语）。注意 tempted to do 不等于“已经做”，而是“被诱使想去做”。

【定位】 It can be tempting in this situation to react harshly to the advice giver and to accuse them of being manipulative, but this approach might produce an undesired result.

在这种情况下，人很容易被诱使去强硬回怼劝告者并指责他们在操控自己，但这种做法可能导致不希望出现的结果。

【选项】 A) 无中生有 Reveal the undesired result of their approach 把原文 this approach might produce an undesired result 中“己方做法的结果”硬塞为“揭露对方做法的结果”，且 reveal 这一动作原文从未出现。 B) 张冠李戴 Refuse their advice in an undisguised manner 取自 an outright rejection 的 outright（直率的），属于 Q54 区间内容；与 Q53 问的“被诱使做什么”无关。 C) 无中生有 Bring their real motives to the surface 谈“把真实动机暴露出来”，原文虽提到 They may not be fully aware of this drive，但从未说被诱使去把动机带到台面上。

D) ✓ 正确 accuse them of being manipulative ↔ Accuse them of trying to control others 在 to react harshly 与 to accuse them of being manipulative 两个候选动作里，只有 Accuse them of trying to control others 与后者形成精确同义改写。
questions.hint: 回到原文定位题干关键词，比较选项与原文的含义。

questions.prompt: How is the advice giver likely to react to the rejection of their advice?

options.text: They may regard it as a threat.
They get ready for a larger conflict.
They begin to doubt their self-worth.

questions.shortExplanation: If the act of giving advice is contributing actively to someone's feelings of self-worth, an outright rejection may be perceived as a threat, activating their fight-or-flight response, possibly causing them to double down on their validation-seeking behavior, or leading to a larger conflict.
questions.detailedExplanation:
【答案】 A （细节题）

【判型】 题干 How is the advice giver likely to react 问的是一个原文中有具体描述的反应方式。

【拆句】 主干 How is the advice giver likely to react，to 引导的介词短语 to the rejection of their advice 表反应对象。likely to 是预测性短语，对应原文的 may/possibly 等情态表达。

【定位】 If the act of giving advice is contributing actively to someone's feelings of self-worth, an outright rejection may be perceived as a threat, activating their fight-or-flight response, possibly causing them to double down on their validation-seeking behavior, or leading to a larger conflict.

如果给建议这一行为正主动地构建着对方的自我价值感，那么一次直率的拒绝可能被对方视为威胁，激活其“战或逃”反应，可能导致他们加倍寻求认可，或引发更大的冲突。

【选项】 A) ✓ 正确 may be perceived as a threat ↔ They may regard it as a threat 预判“视为威胁”在四项中只与 They may regard it as a threat 形成 1:1 同义对应； B/C/D 均取自定位句末尾的分词链或脱离原文。

B) 与原文相反 They may modify their behavior 暗示劝告者会调整行为；原文却是 double down on their validation-seeking behavior——加倍重复原行为，方向相反。 C) 过度推断 They get ready for a larger conflict 描述劝告者“准备好”打更大架；原文是 possibly...leading to a larger conflict，只是分词链中可能的下游结果，并非劝告者主动准备。

D) 与原文相反 They begin to doubt their self-worth 说劝告者开始怀疑自己；原文方向相反——他们的 self-worth 被威胁后，会更努力地寻求认可（double down on validation-seeking），而不是怀疑。
questions.hint: 回到原文定位题干关键词，比较选项与原文的含义。

questions.prompt: What should the advice receiver do to avoid unnecessary conflict?

options.text: Concede the advice is perfectly reasonable.
Give their reasons for not taking the advice.
Understand why the advice giver offers the advice.
Explain their chosen way of handling the situation.

questions.shortExplanation: It is best to set boundaries in a way that takes into account the individual's underlying reasons for doing what they are doing to avoid unnecessary conflict and more stress.
questions.detailedExplanation:
【答案】 C （细节题）

【判型】 题干 What should the advice receiver do 指向作者给出的明确建议，文章末段往往有归纳。

【拆句】 主干 What should the advice receiver do，to 引导目的状语 to avoid unnecessary conflict。should 是关键情态动词，意味着答案对应文中明确的建议性陈述，而非可能性陈述。

【定位】 It is best to set boundaries in a way that takes into account the individual's underlying reasons for doing what they are doing to avoid unnecessary conflict and more stress.

最好以一种顾及当事人行为背后深层动机的方式来设界限，以避免不必要的冲突和更多压力。

【选项】 A) 张冠李戴 Concede the advice is perfectly reasonable 让步承认建议合理，是放弃自己立场；原文是劝考者“自己设界限是 perfectly reasonable”，主语完全不同。

B) 偷换概念 Give their reasons for not taking the advice 让 receiver 说出自己的拒绝理由；原文范本话术 I have my own plan for handling this 谈的是“我自有方案”，并未要求陈述拒绝理由，更不是 P9 给出的总策略。 C) ✓ 正确 takes into account the individual's underlying reasons for doing what they are doing ↔

Understand why the advice giver offers the advice 预判“顾及对方深层动机”在四项中只与 Understand why the advice giver offers the advice 形成 1:1 同义对应。

D) 以偏概全 Explain their chosen way of handling the situation 描述 receiver 解释自己的处理方式，对应 I have my own plan for handling this 的示范话术之一，但题干问的是“避免冲突的做法”——文末 P9 的总结才是答案。
questions.hint: 回到原文定位题干关键词，比较选项与原文的含义。

items.title: 2025年12月六级第3套 · 选词填空
items.passage:
It's best to think of an accent as a distinct, systematic and rule-governed way of speaking. Accent is not a [26] _____ for dialect, but it's related. Dialect is an umbrella term for the way a community pronounces words, creates words, and orders words; accent refers to that first part only.

Many [27] _____ presume that there is a single standard way of speaking in each country, with one single standard accent, and that this perceived standard is [28] _____ the best form of speech, but linguists(语⾔学家) often point out that the concept of a standard accent is better understood as an ideal rather than a [29] _____ . In other words, no one speaks "standard English"; rather, it is an imagined way of using language that exists only in grammar and style books.

One reason linguists agree there is no one true standard is that, through the years, there have been [30] _____ supposed standards, depending on time and place. The standard for English in British newsreels( 新闻⽚ ) from the 1950s, for example, differs greatly from the standard found on American national news broadcasts today. In fact, there has never been a single standard that's been fully agreed

upon — and broadcast outlets across the [31] _____ have never consistently held to those standards anyway.

Even so, this idea of a standard accent is [32] _____ and many workplace and educational environments perpetuate the idea that accents that [33] _____ from the current standard are less appropriate, or even inappropriate. Scholars have found that southern US accent features are more accepted in [34] _____ such as government, law and service-oriented workplaces, but less accepted in the technology sector. The acceptability of nonstandard accents may [35] _____ with differences in class and culture, with newer or higher prestige industries expecting more standard speech in the workplace.

questions.prompt: Accent is not a __(26)__ for dialect, but it's related.
questions.shortExplanation: a synonym for 固定搭配
questions.detailedExplanation:
【答案】 N) synonym 名词

【词性槽】 不定冠词 a 后 + for 介词框架

【依据】 a synonym for 固定搭配

原文 Accent is not a __(26)__ for dialect, but it's related. Dialect is an umbrella term...; accent refers to that first part only. 说"accent 不是 dialect 的 ___，但相关"，紧接着解释 dialect 是包含 accent 的更大范畴——也就是两者不是同义词。a synonym for X 即"X 的同义词"，是英语中固定搭配，语义与逻辑双合。

【竞争词】 L) specimen 样品义不合语境

specimen 指"标本、样品"，说"accent 不是 dialect 的样品"逻辑不通，且无 a specimen for 这一搭配。

J) reality现实义与对比关系不符

reality 指"现实"，原文是在做术语对比（accent 与 dialect），并非讨论虚实，且 a reality for 在此搭配生硬。

M) spectrum 范围义无法对应同义对比

spectrum 指"范围、谱系"，与下文"二者相关但不重合"的同义/上下位对比不匹配。

D) domains 复数形式不匹配冠词 a

domains 为复数，与不定冠词 a 不兼容；语义"领域"也不构成 accent 与 dialect 的术语对照。

G) laymen 复数且指人，不合语境

laymen 为复数指"外行人"，与 a 不搭，且整句是在定义术语，非指代人群。

I) properties 复数且抽象属性义偏移

properties 复数与 a 不兼容；"属性"也无法解释 accent 与 dialect 的术语关系。
questions.hint: 根据空格前后的词性、搭配与上下文选择词语；每个词最多使用一次。

questions.prompt: Many __(27)__ presume that there is a single standard way of speaking in each country
questions.shortExplanation: 外行人对应"想当然以为"的认知主体
questions.detailedExplanation:
【答案】 G) laymen 名词

【词性槽】 形容词 Many 后 + 之后为谓语动词 presume

【依据】 外行人对应"想当然以为"的认知主体

Many laymen presume… 即"许多外行人想当然以为……"，恰好与下半句 but linguists(语言学家) often point out that the concept of a standard accent is better understood as an ideal rather than a __(29)__ 中的 linguists 构成"外行 vs 专家"对照，逻辑严丝合缝。

【竞争词】 D) domains 领域无法做"以为"的主体

domains 指"领域"，是抽象范畴，不能作 presume 的逻辑主语；且与下句 linguists 的对照对象不符。

I) properties 属性无法做"以为"的主体

properties 指"属性、财产"，同样是抽象概念，无法 presume；与对照结构不匹配。
questions.hint: 根据空格前后的词性、搭配与上下文选择词语；每个词最多使用一次。

questions.prompt: this perceived standard is __(28)__ the best form of speech
questions.shortExplanation: 本质上即最佳，对应"理想型"叙述
questions.detailedExplanation:
【答案】 F) inherently 副词

【词性槽】 be 动词与表语形容词之间的修饰位

【依据】 本质上即最佳，对应"理想型"叙述

原文 Many __(27)__ presume that there is a single standard way of speaking in each country, with one single standard accent, and that this perceived standard is __(28)__ the best form of speech 描述"外行人以为感知到的标准在本质上就是最佳说话方式"， inherently 表"本质上、生来就是"，正好对应这种被想当然的本体论断言。

【竞争词】 K) reciprocally相互义与单向断言不符

reciprocally 表"相互地"，需双向主体；句中只是单方面"被认为是最佳"，无相互关系可言。

【易错】 最具迷惑性的错误词是 K) —— 副词类目仅二选一，词义辨义易翻车。F) inherently 与 K) reciprocally 同为副词，考生若只看到"副词"就随手填，可能误选 reciprocally；防坑：be + ___ + the best form of speech 这种单向断言句不存在"相互"关系，必须看断言方向再选副词。
questions.hint: 根据空格前后的词性、搭配与上下文选择词语；每个词最多使用一次。

questions.prompt: the concept of a standard accent is better understood as an ideal rather than a __(29)__
questions.shortExplanation: an ideal rather than a reality
questions.detailedExplanation:
【答案】 J) reality 名词

【词性槽】 rather than 后并列名词位

【依据】 an ideal rather than a reality

标准口音"更适合被理解为一种理想，而不是现实"，ideal 与 reality 是英语中最经典的反义对子；紧接的下一句 no one speaks "standard English"; rather, it is an imagined way of using language that exists only in grammar and style books. 用"想象的、只存在于语法书中"再次坐实"非现实"，对照成立。

【竞争词】 L) specimen 样品义与理想无反义对应

specimen 指"样本、标本"，与 ideal 不构成对照，且语义上说"标准口音是样本"不通。

M) spectrum 范围义与理想不对仗

spectrum 指"频谱、范围"，与 ideal 既无反义、也不切下句"想象的语言用法"语境。

I) properties 复数与 a 不兼容

properties 复数，违背 a + 单数名词的语法约束；语义"属性"也不构成与 ideal 的对照。
questions.hint: 根据空格前后的词性、搭配与上下文选择词语；每个词最多使用一次。

questions.prompt: through the years, there have been __(30)__ supposed standards
questions.shortExplanation: 多个标准支撑"无统一"论点
questions.detailedExplanation:
【答案】 H) multiple 形容词

【词性槽】 there have been + 空 + 复数名词

【依据】 多个标准支撑"无统一"论点

本段中心是"语言学家认为没有唯一真标准"，紧跟的例子 The standard for English in British newsreels(新闻片) from the 1950s, for example, differs greatly from the standard found on American national news broadcasts today. 用"50 年代英国 vs 当下美国"佐证存在多个标准，multiple supposed standards 切中要害。

【竞争词】 O) unanimous 一致同意与无统一标准矛盾

unanimous 表"一致同意的"，若说"存在一致同意的标准"，与下文 there has never been a single standard that's been fully agreed upon 直接打架。
questions.hint: 根据空格前后的词性、搭配与上下文选择词语；每个词最多使用一次。

questions.prompt: broadcast outlets across the __(31)__ have never consistently held to those standards
questions.shortExplanation: across the spectrum 全谱系
questions.detailedExplanation:
【答案】 M) spectrum 名词

【词性槽】 the + 空 + 介词短语

【依据】 across the spectrum 全谱系

items.passage:
A) Timed traffic lights are set according to schedules that are supposed to coordinate with peak traffic hours. Cities need to monitor and update signal light time schedules at least every two years to keep these systems effective. In Los Angeles, California, an ambitious project to go a step further and synchronize( 使同步 ) every red light in Los Angeles cost over 400 million dollars. Ask a resident of the city and they are likely to agree that saving time on the road is well worth it. If implemented nationwide, synchronization could shave 10% off traffic congestion( 堵塞 ) and 20% off air pollution. Congestion costs time, money, and lives. Big data can help improve how millions of people safely share the road. However, none of this would be possible without the traffic light!

B) The first traffic light was invented in London in the 1860's, but it was hardly recognizable — or effective. It had been adapted from the railroad signal system by a railway manager, John Peak Knight, in 1868. The railroads used red gas lights at night to signal stops and green gas lights during the daytime. Knight installed a similar gas light, semaphore(臂板信号) system near London's Westminster Bridge in December of 1868.

C) The life of the first traffic light signal was short-lived. A gas leak caused one of the signal lights to explode on its police officer operator within a month of being installed.

D) Automating traffic signals stalled after the London incident. Forty years passed before cars crowding city streets urged the development of traffic lights in the United States. London would not see another traffic light until 1929.

E) The United States is a car culture like no other country. Unlike most European cities that started urban planning when horses were high-tech, many cities in the United States were designed around urban sprawl, suburban tracts, and motor cars.

F) As traffic and cities grew, so did the race to solve growing traffic problems. The first traffic signals were semaphores. Semaphores are towers with moving arms signaling for traffic to stop or go. They could be manual or automatic. There was no consistent design. Various models were invented and put into place in cities as the need arose.

G) In 1912, Lester Wire was a police officer exhausted by traffic at Main Street and 200 South. He developed a manually switched stop light. The four-sided box, raised on a ten-foot pole, looked like a birdhouse and was operated manually by an officer. The officer would flip a switch to change between the dipped red and green lights.

H) Like the 1910 semaphore, the first electric signal used words. However, the words were no longer written on arms that raised and fell. The words "stop" or "move" were on lights. The posts lit up on each of four corner-posts around an intersection(⼗字路⼝ ). It was not automated, though. A booth with an operator was required to flip the switches.

I) The system allowed police officers to move from the middle of the street to a corner. From that vantage( 有利地位 ), an officer could oversee the crowd. If an emergency vehicle came, the officer could flip a switch and clear the intersection by triggering all red lights. The emergency vehicle could now pass effortlessly. Finally, in San Francisco the first red and green electric light system that could be operated automatically (or manually) was introduced in 1917.

J) In 1920, the first three-color light system was introduced in Detroit — also known as Motor City, USA. The evolution of traffic light signals could not have a more appropriate context than Motor City. Ford Motor Company was founded in Detroit in 1903 (and other motor companies followed). Ford made cars affordable for more common people, rather than the wealthy, by creating larger scale factory production.

K) Stop and go were insufficient for the new volumes of cars zooming through intersections. Streets were full of new numbers of cars in addition to delivery wagons, bustling crowds, bicycles, horse-drawn carriages, and street cars. The introduction of the cautionary yellow light helped increase driver safety, decreasing accidents that come from running red lights.

L) Stop lights were incredibly important in chaotic city streets. Crosswalks weren't even introduced until 1951. The first pedestrian fatality in the United States was in 1899.

M) The development of the modern traffic light may have started in London, but it grew up in the United States. In Cleveland, an African-American inventor named Garrett Morgan came up with an affordable, patented traffic signal. The yellow light made intersections safer than the old stop and go system. The new design was inexpensive enough that it allowed the installation of a lot more lights.

N) Morgan sold the patent to General Electric — and the spread of the traffic light was green lighted. Green means go. It is that simple, but it's still best to check both ways for oncoming traffic that may not be paying attention or is running the light. Yellow means slow down and prepare to stop. It does not mean full-throttle( 全速 ) ahead. While you may get away with gunning it into the intersection, running a yellow can lead to tickets and dangerous accidents. Red lights are a clear and consistent warning to stop. Even where right turns are allowed on red lights, you must come to a complete stop before turning right. You must also yield to any through traffic, which has the right of way. In most states and cities, you can take a right on red unless otherwise indicated. New York City does not allow a right on red.

O) Red arrows mean you cannot turn right on a red in most states. The green arrow, in these cases, is the only time you can make the turn. However, you can take a right on a red arrow after a full stop in the states of Illinois, Kansas, Louisiana, Maryland, Michigan, New Hampshire, North Dakota, Oregon, South Carolina, Utah, Washington State and Wyoming.

P) Flashing Red is the same as a stop sign, generally used at four-way intersections where there is minimal traffic. When arriving at a flashing red light, make a full and complete stop. Flashing Red Arrows similarly mean to stop and then proceed to take the turn. Flashing Yellow lights mean yield or signal caution, like outside of a fire station. There are no all-direction flashing yellow lights, since it is prohibited in the United States. If you have a flashing yellow light, you are to yield to oncoming traffic.

Q) Flashing Yellow Arrows are part of a four-signal traffic light. These are used in some states after a protected green turn signal, or arrow, but before a steady yellow arrow. When a flashing yellow arrow is shown, you can take the turn after yielding to pedestrians and traffic. Steady Yellow Arrows maintain the normal yellow light caution in three-light signals, meaning to stop or prepare to stop. In a four-signal system that has a flashing yellow arrow, the steady yellow arrow is a signal that the yield period is ending. The red arrow is about to start. Vehicles should stop if safely possible. Traffic tickets are possible for running a steady yellow arrow.

R) Traffic light meaning is fairly consistent across the board with various deviations. Green means it's safe to proceed (though you should still exercise caution). Yellow means caution and yield. Red means danger and stop. Always drive defensively and obey traffic signals.

items.title: 2025年12月六级第3套 · 仔细阅读 · 第一篇
items.passage:
Mindfulness has been shown to have a number of meaningful health benefits — it can help reduce anxiety and promote healing in those suffering from chronic illness.

The practice is based on an insight first described in ancient Buddhist texts that human beings have the capacity to observe experience without being caught up in it. This means simply that it is possible to observe ourselves having a craving, or a happy thought, or even a scary emotion, without reacting in the moment in a way that amplifies the feeling or sends the mind spiraling off into thinking about old memories or anticipating events.

This practice of mindfulness can help calm the mind and the body as we learn not to react to experience with likes and dislikes or judgments of good and bad. It does not make us cold or indifferent but more fully present.

One of the challenges of practicing mindfulness in our contemporary world is that there has been a profound transformation in human attention. The artist Jenny Odell argues that in our "attention economy" human attention has been transformed into a commodity that big corporations buy and sell. This economy rests on a technological revolution of mobile phones and social media that makes it possible for corporations to target our attention with their content at every moment.

The devices most people use are a perpetual diversion from the present moment. The result is that it can feel as though our ability to focus, and be fully present, has been stolen. But mindfulness can help us resist the attention economy and relish the things that make life special, like being together with those we love.

Most mindfulness research focuses on the individual benefits of the practice, but some scholars assert that we can not only practice mindfulness for ourselves but also practice it for others. It can help us build stronger, healthier relationships.

The sad truth is that living in the attention economy, most of us have become bad listeners. However, just as it is possible to watch ourselves having an experience without reacting, it's possible to watch another person have an experience without getting tied up in reactivity and judgment.

The gift of mindfulness is a practice of listening with compassion to others describe their experiences. To give this gift means putting away your phone, turning off social media, and setting aside other common distractions. It means practicing being fully present in another person's presence and listening to them with complete attention without judgment, while resisting the urge to make the interaction about you.

If we judge the value of gifts based on their price, this gift may seem worthless, but in a distracted world, it is a precious one.

questions.prompt: What do we learn from the passage about practicing mindfulness?

options.text: It triggers our mind to reflect on past experiences or anticipate future events.
It focuses our attention on the present moment without making judgments.
It concentrates our mind on our personal feelings, happy or scary.
It helps our mind to stay calm when facing judgments from others.

questions.shortExplanation: This means simply that it is possible to observe ourselves having a craving, or a happy thought, or even a scary emotion, without reacting in the moment in a way that amplifies the feeling or sends the mind spiraling off into thinking about old memories or anticipating events. 这意味着，我们可以观察自己产生渴望、愉快念头甚至恐惧情绪，而无需在当下作出反应、 不放大该情绪，也不让心思滑向旧时记忆或对未来事件的预期。
questions.detailedExplanation:
【答案】 B （细节题）

【判型】 What do we learn from the passage about practicing mindfulness 问的是文章关于 mindfulness 的客观陈述，没有 infer/imply/mainly 这类信号，是一道关于 mindfulness 本质特征的细节题。

【拆句】 What do we learn from the passage about practicing mindfulness? 主干是 What do we learn from the passage，about practicing mindfulness 是介词短语后置补充询问对象，结构直白无陷阱。

【定位】 This means simply that it is possible to observe ourselves having a craving, or a happy thought, or even a scary emotion, without reacting in the moment in a way that amplifies the feeling or sends the mind spiraling off into thinking about old memories or anticipating events. 这意味着，我们可以观察自己产生渴望、愉快念头甚至恐惧情绪，而无需在当下作出反应、 不放大该情绪，也不让心思滑向旧时记忆或对未来事件的预期。

【选项】 A) 与原文相反原文 without … sends the mind spiraling off into thinking about old memories or anticipating events 明确把「回想旧事 / 预期未来」放在否定结构里，是正念要避免的，A 把它说成正念的作用，恰好与原文相反。 B) ✓ 正确 observe ourselves having a craving, or a happy thought, or even a scary emotion, without reacting in the moment

↔ focuses our attention on the present moment we learn not to react to experience with likes and dislikes or judgments of good and bad ↔

without making judgments 预判落在「观察当下、不卷入、不评判」三点上，focuses our attention on the present moment without making judgments 把前两点合在一句里全覆盖，是定位句的紧贴改写。 C) 偷换概念原文 observe ourselves having a craving, or a happy thought, or even a scary emotion, without reacting in the moment 强调观察情绪而不卷入，C 项却说「把注意力集中在个人情绪上」，把「观察」偷换成「集中」，两者一冷静一沉浸，语义错位。

D) 张冠李戴原文谈的是「自己不对体验作好坏评判」（judgments of good and bad），并未涉及 「他人评判我们」，D 项把评判主体从「自我」换成「他人」，无原文依据。

questions.prompt: What do we see in today's "attention economy" according to Jenny Odell?

options.text: Focus on technological advances continuously updates products and services.
People's attention is turned into something that can be bought and sold.
Businesses profit from selling mobile phones and revolutionizing social media.
People tend to purchase products and services without careful thinking.

questions.shortExplanation: The artist Jenny Odell argues that in our "attention economy" human attention has been transformed into a commodity that big corporations buy and sell.
questions.detailedExplanation:
【答案】 B （细节题）

【判型】 What do we see in today's attention economy according to Jenny Odell 用 according to 把答案归到 Jenny Odell 名下，是事实归属型细节题。

【拆句】 What do we see in today's "attention economy" according to Jenny Odell? 主干 What do we see in today's attention economy，according to Jenny Odell 是把观点归属到具体人物的状语，关键在于答案必须落到 Odell 的话上，而不是文章自己说的。

【定位】 The artist Jenny Odell argues that in our "attention economy" human attention has been transformed into a commodity that big corporations buy and sell.

艺术家 Jenny Odell 论述道：在我们的「注意力经济」中，人的注意力已经被转化成大公司买卖的商品。

【选项】 A) 偷换概念原文 This economy rests on a technological revolution of mobile phones and social media that makes it possible for corporations to target our attention with their content at every moment 说技术革命让公司能持续抢占注意力，没说技术让产品/服务持续更新，A 项偷换了技术革命的作用。

B) ✓ 正确 human attention has been transformed into a commodity that big corporations buy and sell ↔

People's attention is turned into something that can be bought and sold 选项 B 几乎是 Odell 原话的一对一改写，主语、动词、对象、属性四要素全对齐，是 according to 型细节题里最干净的同义替换。 C) 偷换概念原文 buy and sell 的宾语是 human attention（人的注意力），C 项把宾语偷换成 mobile phones and social media，是把抽象对象偷换成具体技术，正好踩中考生「具象更易接受」的认知偏误。

D) 无中生有原文谈的是公司买卖「人的注意力」，并未谈消费者本身是否冲动消费；D 项关于「人们购买商品不细想」属凭空生造。
questions.hint: 回到原文定位题干关键词，比较选项与原文的含义。

questions.prompt: What happens with the prevalent use of mobile phones or social media?

options.text: They keep distracting users from the here and now.
They render users incapable of resisting temptation.
They rob users of their ability to observe experience.
They tempt users to endorse the attention economy.

questions.shortExplanation: The devices most people use are a perpetual diversion from the present moment.
questions.detailedExplanation:
【答案】 A （细节题）

【判型】 What happens with the prevalent use of mobile phones or social media 直接问 What happens，是问客观结果，属于细节题。

【拆句】 What happens with the prevalent use of mobile phones or social media? 主干 What happens，with the prevalent use of… 是介词短语作伴随状语，相当于 when… are widely used，结构平实。

【定位】 The devices most people use are a perpetual diversion from the present moment.

大多数人使用的这些设备是一种让人持续偏离当下的干扰。

【选项】 A) ✓ 正确 The devices most people use are a perpetual diversion from the present moment ↔

They keep distracting users from the here and now A 项两个核心语义点（keep distracting、from the here and now）与原文 perpetual diversion、from the present moment 一一对应，是定位句的紧贴改写。 B) 过度推断原文 But mindfulness can help us resist the attention economy 谈的是正念能帮我们抵抗，B 项却说设备让用户「彻底失去抵御诱惑的能力」，把「分心」夸大为「丧失抵抗力」，无原文依据。 C) 张冠李戴原文 our ability to focus, and be fully present, has been stolen 谈被偷走的是「专注、全在当下」的能力，而 capacity to observe experience 才是 observe experience 的能力，C 项把两者混在一起，张冠李戴。

D) 无中生有原文只说设备让人分心、注意力被卖，没说设备诱使用户主动「支持/认同」注意力经济，D 项凭空多出一个「用户主动认同」的环节。

questions.prompt: What benefit can practicing mindfulness bring to us according to some scholars?

options.text: It prevents us from making arbitrary judgments about others.
It shifts our attention from material things to spiritual pursuits.
It is conducive to our forging better interpersonal relationships.
It is helpful in regaining our ability to enjoy what we have in life.

questions.shortExplanation: Most mindfulness research focuses on the individual benefits of the practice, but some scholars assert that we can not only practice mindfulness for ourselves but also practice it for others. It can help us build stronger, healthier relationships.
questions.detailedExplanation:
【答案】 C （细节题）

【判型】 What benefit can practicing mindfulness bring to us according to some scholars 用 according to some scholars 归属信息源，是出处型细节题。

【拆句】 What benefit can practicing mindfulness bring to us according to some scholars? 主干 What benefit can practicing mindfulness bring to us，according to some scholars 是把观点归到学者群体的状语，注意不要把作者自己其它段落的好处当成学者说的。

【定位】 Most mindfulness research focuses on the individual benefits of the practice, but some scholars assert that we can not only practice mindfulness for ourselves but also practice it for others. It can help us build stronger, healthier relationships.

多数正念研究关注其个人层面的益处，但一些学者论断：正念不仅可为己练，也可为他人而练；它能帮我们建立更稳固、更健康的人际关系。

【选项】 A) 张冠李戴 「不作评判」是 P3 谈 mindfulness 个体效用时的内容，而 Q49 问的是 some scholars 的观点；把 P3 的句子嫁接到学者名下属于张冠李戴，且 prevent us from making arbitrary judgments about others 也夸大了原文「自己不评判体验」的限定。

B) 无中生有原文没有把好处归结为「从物质转向精神追求」，B 项凭空生造一组对立维度。 C) ✓ 正确 help us build stronger, healthier relationships ↔

conducive to our forging better interpersonal relationships C 项把学者观点收束句 help us build stronger, healthier relationships 完整改写成 conducive to our forging better interpersonal relationships，主体、动作、对象逐项对齐。

D) 张冠李戴 「重拾享受生活的能力」对应 relish the things that make life special, like being together with those we love，是作者自己的论述而非 some scholars 的观点；嫁接到学者名下属于张冠李戴。

questions.prompt: What does the author suggest we do in another person's presence?

options.text: Share each other's experience frankly and compassionately.
Pay full attention to establishing close relationships with them.
Be attentive listeners while refraining from making judgments.
Remind them of the distraction from mobile phones and social media.

questions.shortExplanation: It means practicing being fully present in another person's presence and listening to them with complete attention without judgment, while resisting the urge to make the interaction about you.
questions.detailedExplanation:
【答案】 C （细节题）

【判型】 What does the author suggest we do in another person's presence 问的是作者对一个具体场景给出的具体做法，是建议型细节题。

【拆句】 What does the author suggest we do in another person's presence? 主干 What does the author suggest we do，in another person's presence 是地点状语；suggest 后接省略 that 的从句 we do…，注意 suggest 在此为「建议」义、不是「暗示」义。

【定位】 It means practicing being fully present in another person's presence and listening to them with complete attention without judgment, while resisting the urge to make the interaction about you.

这意味着练习在另一个人面前全然临在，全神贯注地倾听他们，不作评判，同时克制把对话焦点拉回到自己身上的冲动。

【选项】 A) 与原文相反原文 resisting the urge to make the interaction about you 明确要求克制把谈话拉回到「自己」，强调单向倾听对方；A 项却说 share each other's experience 双向分享， 与原文要求方向相反。 B) 偷换概念原文要求把全部注意力放在对方的体验上，目的是「以正念之心送出倾听这一礼物」 （practicing being fully present in another person's presence）；B 项却把目的偷换成 establishing close relationships with them——这是 Q49 的话题，且原文未把它定为这一场景的目的。 C) ✓ 正确 listening to them with complete attention without judgment↔

Be attentive listeners while refraining from making judgments C 项把作者建议的两项核心动作（with complete attention、without judgment）都直接对应到选项的两个分句，是同义改写最紧贴的一项。

D) 无中生有原文要求自己 putting away your phone, turning off social media, and setting aside other common distractions，即「自己」放下手机，并未要求去提醒对方；D 项把动作主体从「自己」偷换到「提醒他人」，无原文依据。

items.title: 2025年12月六级第3套 · 仔细阅读 · 第二篇
items.passage:
The other day I had to log into a service I hadn't used before. Since I was a new user, the website decided that it needed to check I wasn't a robot and so set me a Captcha test to determine whether the user is a person or a machine.

I was presented with an image of a roadside scene over which was laid a grid. My "challenge" was to click on each cell in the grid that contained a traffic sign. I did so, a bit irritated. Then I was presented with another image and another grid — also with a request to identify road signs. Like a lamb, I complied, after which the website accepted my input.

And then I realised what I had been doing was adding to a dataset for training the machine-learning software that guides self-driving cars. So, to gain access to an automated service that will benefit financially from my input, I first have to do some unpaid labor to help improve the performance of autonomous vehicles.

Neat, eh? But note also the delicious additional irony that the Captcha is described as an "automated Turing test". The Turing test was conceived, you may recall, as a way of enabling humans to determine whether a machine could respond in such a way that one couldn't tell whether it was a human or a robot. So we have wandered into a world in which machines make us do tricks to prove that we are humans!

The strangest aspect of this unparalleled shift is how under-discussed it has been. The metaphor of the boiling frog comes to mind. Have we become so subtly conditioned by digital technology that we don't see what's been happening to us? Have we been conditioned to accept a world governed by "smart" tech, trading convenience to the point where we become a bit like machines ourselves?

In a recent startling and thoughtful book, two scholars — Brett Frischmann, a law professor, and Evan Selinger, a philosopher — argue that the answer to that question is "yes".

And they're right. There's nothing technophobic(技术恐惧的) about that. We shape our tools and then our tools shape us. Technology is supposed to provide tools that serve human ends. But, as the machine-learning Captcha demonstrates, a significant proportion of digital tech now sees (and uses) humans as means to ends that are not ours. In the process, they reduce us to the status of cheery rats running on treadmills(踏⻋ ) designed by people who do not have our interests at heart. So back to the frog metaphor. Are we smart enough to jump out before it's too late? You don't even have to Google it to know the answer.

But, as the machine-learning Captcha demonstrates, a significant proportion of digital tech now sees (and uses) humans as means to ends that are not ours. 他们说得没错。这并不是什么技术恐惧。我们塑造工具，反过来工具也塑造我们。技术本应提供服务于人类目的的工具。但是，正如机器学习版 Captcha 所展示的那样，相当一部分数字技术如今把人类当作（并加以利用为）实现非人类目的之手段。

【选项】 A) ✓ 正确 a significant proportion of digital tech ↔ A large part of digital tech now sees (and uses) humans as means to ends that are not ours ↔

now making use of humans to meet its own ends 预判要的是"技术把人当工具达成自身目的"，A large part of digital tech is now making use of humans to meet its own ends. 同时覆盖"相当大一部分"+"利用人"+"达成自身目的"三个要点，与原文逐一吻合。 B) 无中生有 Humans are now fast locked in a race against digital tech to control the world 说"人在与数字技术赛跑争夺世界控制"，但原文从未把人与技术描绘成赛跑或争控关系。

C) 与原文相反 Digital tech can serve human needs in ways previously thought impossible 在赞美技术服务人类的能力，但作者 But 之后说的恰是相反——技术正反过来利用人。 D) 过度推断 Digital tech is now doing thinking while humans are doing repetitive work 把人机的工作分工说成"技术思考、人重复劳动"，原文虽然提到作者做了 some unpaid labor，但并未把它对立到"技术负责思考"的层面。
questions.hint: 回到原文定位题干关键词，比较选项与原文的含义。

questions.prompt: What does the author imply by asking "Are we smart enough to jump out before it's too late?" at the end of the passage?

options.text: It is not sensible to expect digital tech to take humans' interest to heart.
It is hard to say whether technology or humans will get the upper hand.
We may have to search the web to get the answer to the question.
We may not awake in time to the danger digital tech poses to us.

questions.shortExplanation: So back to the frog metaphor. Are we smart enough to jump out before it's too late? You don't even have to Google it to know the answer.
questions.detailedExplanation:
【答案】 D （推断题）

【判型】 What does the author imply by asking ... 中的 imply 明确要求由作者的反问句推导言外之意，不能停在字面。

【拆句】 What does the author imply by asking "Are we smart enough to jump out before it's too late?" at the end of the passage? 主干是 What does the author imply，by asking ... 是方式状语，引号内是反问句（rhetorical question），表达否定意味，是理解全题的关键。

【定位】 So back to the frog metaphor. Are we smart enough to jump out before it's too late? You don't even have to Google it to know the answer.

那么回到青蛙的比喻。我们够聪明，能在为时已晚之前跳出来吗？这个问题，你甚至都不用上网搜就能知道答案。

【选项】 A) 答非所问 It is not sensible to expect digital tech to take humans' interest to heart 在评判"指望技术为人着想是否明智"，对象是技术；但题干反问的主语是 we——问的是人是否够聪明，主体偏移。 B) 偷换概念 It is hard to say whether technology or humans will get the upper hand 把作者立场说成"难说人机谁占上风"，但原文反问 + 反讽尾句强烈暗示作者倾向悲观，并非中立。

C) 与原文相反 We may have to search the web to get the answer to the question 字面理解了 You don't even have to Google it——把"不用搜也知道"反向解成"必须搜才知道"。 D) ✓ 正确 Are we smart enough to jump out before it's too late?↔

We may not awake in time to the danger digital tech poses to us Have we become so subtly conditioned by digital technology that we don't see what's been happening to us?

↔ the danger digital tech poses to us 预判要的是"恐怕来不及醒悟"，We may not awake in time to the danger digital tech poses to us. 把"反问 → 否定断言"与"温水煮青蛙 → 数字技术的危险"两层一起兜住，是唯一贴着原文走一步的推断。
questions.hint: 回到原文定位题干关键词，比较选项与原文的含义。

items.title: 2025年6月六级第1套 · 选词填空
items.passage:
In her second year, Charlene Duong learned of the use of poisonous, synthetic pesticides on her college campus. Shocked but not surprised, she knew she had to do something. Along with a couple of classmates, Charlene did a quick web search and discovered a small but growing movement led by the organization, Herbicide-Free Campus (HFC), to rid college campuses of artificial herbicides( 灭草剂 ). They were [26] _____ .

Like many, Charlene experiences climate anxiety—a [27] _____ fear of a climate catastrophe—and was, at the time, looking for an [28] _____ . When she discovered the HFC movement, she said she felt she "had found a specific area to focus on that still fit into the larger picture of fighting for a healthier, safer, cleaner [29] _____ for all."

Toxic herbicide use in university land care is not unique. Most institutions of higher education rely on synthetic pesticides and fertilizers to achieve [30] _____ goals. Having a "beautiful" campus means green and perfectly maintained lawns along with flower beds and paved sidewalks. But these [31] _____

managed campuses can come at a cost: increased cancer risk, [32] _____ waterways, poisoned wildlife and lifeless soil.

Pesticide use on college campuses also contributes to our global climate crisis. The use of chemicals to get rid of insects or unwanted plant life can increase indirect [33] _____ as they can include petroleum-based ingredients. Pesticide use also decreases the life in soil, [34] _____ the ability of soils to absorb carbon or retain water and thus reducing campuses' ability to recover quickly from climate-related extreme weather events like droughts and floods.

Instead of using toxic chemicals, students working with HFC help out with [35] _____ the campus grounds.

"This work reminds me to be in the present moment as I play my role in reducing herbicide use and keeping my campus safe and healthy," says Charlene.

questions.prompt: They were __(26)__
questions.shortExplanation: 发现新天地→产生兴趣
questions.detailedExplanation:
【答案】 J) intrigued 形容词

【词性槽】 be 动词后作表语

【依据】 发现新天地→产生兴趣

上文 discovered a small but growing movement 表明她们发现了一个新兴运动；They were __(26)__ 紧承其后，自然描述她们对这场运动**产生浓厚兴趣**的状态。be intrigued 是描述人被某事吸引的经典搭配。

【竞争词】 A) aesthetic'她们是美学的'语义不通

aesthetic 修饰物的审美属性，不用于描述人的情绪反应，'They were aesthetic'语义荒谬。

C) contaminated '她们被污染了'语义不合

contaminated 修饰水/土等物质或抽象意义的'被污染的（思想）'，描述这群积极投身环保的学生，方向完全相反。

K) juvenile幼稚的与积极行动矛盾

juvenile 含贬义，会把这群有担当的大学生贬为'幼稚'，与全段她们果决行动的基调冲突。
questions.hint: 根据空格前后的词性、搭配与上下文选择词语；每个词最多使用一次。

questions.prompt: climate anxiety—a __(27)__ fear of a climate catastrophe
questions.shortExplanation: 气候焦虑是长期慢性的
questions.detailedExplanation:
【答案】 B) chronic 形容词

【词性槽】 不定冠词与名词之间作定语

【依据】 气候焦虑是长期慢性的

破折号后是对 climate anxiety 的同位解释。气候焦虑本质上是一种**长期、持续**的恐惧，chronic fear（慢性恐惧）是心理学常用搭配，正好刻画这种持续不消退的状态，与 'climate anxiety' 的本义对应。

【竞争词】 A) aesthetic审美的不能修饰 fear

aesthetic 指审美/美学的，与恐惧情绪无逻辑关系，搭配不成立。

C) contaminated 被污染的不修饰情绪

contaminated 用于水、土壤等被污染的物质，不能修饰 fear 这种抽象情绪。

J) intrigued感兴趣的修饰人不修饰 fear

intrigued 表'被深深吸引的'，主语通常是人，且与恐惧情绪在情感色彩上相反。

K) juvenile幼稚的与气候焦虑色彩冲突

juvenile 表'少年的/幼稚的'，带贬义，会把气候焦虑矮化为'孩子气的恐惧'，与下文积极行动的语调相悖。
questions.hint: 根据空格前后的词性、搭配与上下文选择词语；每个词最多使用一次。

questions.prompt: was, at the time, looking for an __(28)__
questions.shortExplanation: 气候焦虑需要情绪出口
questions.detailedExplanation:
【答案】 L) outlet 名词

【词性槽】 不定冠词 an 后缺单数名词

【依据】 气候焦虑需要情绪出口

上文 Charlene experiences climate anxiety—a __(27)__ fear of a climate catastrophe 说她有气候焦虑，下文 she felt she "had found a specific area to focus on" 表明她找到了可投入精力的具体领域——这正是焦虑情绪的**释放出口**（outlet）。look for an outlet 是描述情绪宣泄的固定搭配。

【竞争词】 I) infringement 侵权不是被'寻找'的对象

look for an infringement（寻找一项侵权行为）在语义上荒谬，且与 climate anxiety 的语境完全脱节。

N) vibrations 辅音开头不能跟 an

vibrations 以辅音 /v/ 开头，先被 an 拒之门外；且词义与气候焦虑无关。
questions.hint: 根据空格前后的词性、搭配与上下文选择词语；每个词最多使用一次。

questions.prompt: a healthier, safer, cleaner __(29)__ for all
questions.shortExplanation: 三形容词指向'环境'
questions.detailedExplanation:
【答案】 F) environment 名词

【词性槽】 形容词串后缺名词中心词

【依据】 三形容词指向'环境'

healthier、safer、cleaner 是描述**生存环境**的高频搭配三件套，a healthier, safer, cleaner __(29)__ for all 整句承接上文 fighting for，正是为所有人争取一个更健康、安全、洁净的**环境**，与全文反对除草剂、保护校园生态的主旨完全吻合。

【竞争词】 E) emissions 排放物不能被'更健康'修饰

emissions 指废气排放物，搭配 healthier/safer/cleaner 在语义上矛盾——人们要的是减少排放，而不是'更健康的排放'。

I) infringement 侵权与三形容词南辕北辙

infringement 指对权利的侵犯，是负面行为，无法用 healthier/safer/cleaner 来修饰，且与本文话题无关。

L) outlet 释放渠道与'更健康'不搭

outlet 指情绪/精力的发泄出口，是个体层面的概念，不能用 healthier/safer/cleaner for all 这种宏观三连修饰。

N) vibrations 振动与文章话题无关

vibrations 指物理振动，与气候、校园生态无关，纯粹凑数的干扰项。
questions.hint: 根据空格前后的词性、搭配与上下文选择词语；每个词最多使用一次。

questions.prompt: rely on synthetic pesticides and fertilizers to achieve __(30)__ goals
questions.shortExplanation: 美观目标对应下文绿色草坪
questions.detailedExplanation:
【答案】 A) aesthetic 形容词

【词性槽】 名词 goals 前作定语

【依据】 美观目标对应下文绿色草坪

下文 Having a "beautiful" campus means green and perfectly maintained lawns along with flower beds and paved sidewalks 立刻解释了所谓 'goals' 就是把校园弄得 **美观漂亮**——这正是 aesthetic（审美/美观）目标。命题人用引号 "beautiful" 直接回扣 aesthetic。

【竞争词】 C) contaminated 被污染的目标语义颠倒

contaminated goals（被污染的目标）语义不通；高校追求的不可能是'被污染'目标，方向反了。

K) juvenile幼稚目标与高校追求不符

juvenile goals 含贬义，高校公开追求'幼稚目标'语义荒诞，与下文美观校园语境无关。
questions.hint: 根据空格前后的词性、搭配与上下文选择词语；每个词最多使用一次。

questions.prompt: But these __(31)__ managed campuses can come at a cost
questions.shortExplanation: 传统方式=合成农药管理
questions.detailedExplanation:
【答案】 D) conventionally 副词

【词性槽】 形容词 managed 前作状语

【依据】 传统方式=合成农药管理

上文 Most institutions of higher education rely on synthetic pesticides and fertilizers 说大多数高校沿用合成农药——这正是**传统/常规**管理方式；these __(31)__ managed campuses 中的 these 回指前句，因此填 conventionally（按传统方式）正好呼应。

【竞争词】 H) incidentally顺便地与代价主句无关

incidentally 意为'顺便提一句、偶然地'，常作插入语，无法刻画'校园被怎样管理'的方式；与下文 'come at a cost' 的因果论证脱节。

【易错】 最具迷惑性的错误词是 H) —— 副词只剩两个，色彩不挑就翻车。31 题词性确定后只剩 conventionally 和 incidentally 两选一。考生若只看词性、不回头读上文 Most institutions of higher education rely on synthetic pesticides and fertilizers 的'常规手段'铺垫，就可能误选 incidentally。防坑：副词空二选一时，必回上文找语义铺垫。
questions.hint: 根据空格前后的词性、搭配与上下文选择词语；每个词最多使用一次。

questions.prompt: increased cancer risk, __(32)__ waterways, poisoned wildlife and lifeless soil
questions.shortExplanation: 并列同义堆叠负面后果
questions.detailedExplanation:
【答案】 C) contaminated 形容词

【词性槽】 名词 waterways 前作定语

【依据】 并列同义堆叠负面后果

increased cancer risk, __(32)__ waterways, poisoned wildlife and lifeless soil 是命题人列出的四宗罪：增加癌症风险、__水道、毒害野生动物、贫瘠土壤。waterways 与化学品代价最自然的搭配就是 contaminated（被污染的），与 poisoned/lifeless 一同构成负面后果链。

【竞争词】 K) juvenile 幼稚的水道语义不通

juvenile waterways（幼稚的水道）搭配不成立，且不属于负面后果范畴。

【易错】 最具迷惑性的错误词是 K) —— 形容词色彩一错全错。32 题在并列负面后果 poisoned wildlife、lifeless soil 之间，考生若只挑形容词词性不察色彩，可能把 juvenile 硬塞进去。 防坑：并列项前的修饰词必须与左右邻居在感情色彩上一致。
questions.hint: 根据空格前后的词性、搭配与上下文选择词语；每个词最多使用一次。

questions.prompt: can increase indirect __(33)__ as they can include petroleum-based ingredients
questions.shortExplanation: 石油成分对应温室气体排放
questions.detailedExplanation:
【答案】 E) emissions 名词

【词性槽】 形容词后作宾语缺名词复数

【依据】 石油成分对应温室气体排放

as they can include petroleum-based ingredients 明示这些化学品含石油基成分，正是温室气体排放（emissions）的来源；上文 Pesticide use on college campuses also contributes to our global climate crisis 也铺垫了气候话题，indirect emissions 即'间接排放'是气候议题的标准术语。

【竞争词】 I) infringement 侵权与石油成分无逻辑链

infringement 指权利侵犯，无法解释为何'含石油成分'会导致它增加，与气候危机话题完全无关。

L) outlet 发泄渠道与排放概念错位

outlet 虽有'出口'义，但常指情感/能量的发泄渠道或电源插座，不用于描述温室气体的间接产生，与 petroleum-based ingredients 接不上。

N) vibrations 振动与石油成分无关

vibrations 指物理振动，与气候危机、石油成分无任何因果链。
questions.hint: 根据空格前后的词性、搭配与上下文选择词语；每个词最多使用一次。

questions.prompt: Pesticide use also decreases the life in soil, __(34)__ the ability of soils to absorb carbon or retain water and thus reducing campuses' ability
questions.shortExplanation: 削弱土壤功能=妨碍其能力 decreases the life in soil, __(34)__ the ability of soils to absorb carbon or retain water，主句说减少土壤生命，分词层进一步说**妨碍**土壤吸收碳/保水的能力； hampering（妨碍）与 reducing（减少）在 and 前后形成同义递进，语义、形态都对齐。
questions.detailedExplanation:
【答案】 G) hampering 动词

【词性槽】 并列分词作伴随状语

【依据】 削弱土壤功能=妨碍其能力 decreases the life in soil, __(34)__ the ability of soils to absorb carbon or retain water，主句说减少土壤生命，分词层进一步说**妨碍**土壤吸收碳/保水的能力； hampering（妨碍）与 reducing（减少）在 and 前后形成同义递进，语义、形态都对齐。

【竞争词】 M) rotating 旋转土壤能力语义不通

rotating the ability of soils（旋转土壤能力）搭配不成立；rotating 通常用于轮作（rotating crops）等，与本句负面后果链脱节。
questions.hint: 根据空格前后的词性、搭配与上下文选择词语；每个词最多使用一次。

questions.prompt: students working with HFC help out with __(35)__ the campus grounds
questions.shortExplanation: 替代农药=人工除草上文 Instead of using toxic chemicals 明示是有毒化学品的**替代方案**——既然不喷除草剂，那学生帮忙做的就是**人工除草**（weeding）。weed the campus grounds（给校园场地除草）也是该词的典型搭配。
questions.detailedExplanation:
【答案】 O) weeding 动词

【词性槽】 with 后接动名词作宾语

【依据】 替代农药=人工除草上文 Instead of using toxic chemicals 明示是有毒化学品的**替代方案**——既然不喷除草剂，那学生帮忙做的就是**人工除草**（weeding）。weed the campus grounds（给校园场地除草）也是该词的典型搭配。

【竞争词】 G) hampering 妨碍校园场地语义颠倒

hampering the campus grounds（妨碍校园场地）语义荒谬，且学生'帮忙'不可能是'妨碍'，与 help out 的色彩反向。

M) rotating 轮作场地与替代农药无关

rotating the campus grounds（旋转/轮换校园场地）语义牵强，与上文'不用化学药品'的对照逻辑接不上。
questions.hint: 根据空格前后的词性、搭配与上下文选择词语；每个词最多使用一次。

items.title: 2025年6月六级第1套 · 信息匹配
items.passage:
A) Librarians know the value of their community services, and their patrons appreciate their importance as well. But in an increasingly digital world, we see the role of libraries as community and cultural centers at times undervalued. When shrinking municipal budgets combine with the nonstop technological revolution, public library services that focus on building communities face-to-face, inspiring and educating patrons about art, literature, and music, and helping patrons engage in civil discourse can seem old-fashioned. But it is precisely those shrinking budgets and the assault of technologically mediated life that make public libraries' cultural and community offerings more important than ever.

B) Many people point out the value public libraries bring to their communities. More than just books and banks of computers, libraries are still places where individuals gather to explore, interact, and imagine. Some of the specific ways in which libraries add value to our communities and serve as cultural centers for our patrons are community builders, centers for the arts, and champions of youth. Libraries serve in these capacities and are more than just about information.

C) As community builders libraries are engaged in incredible work. From tiny public libraries to huge city institutions with multiple branches, libraries across the United States are building community and supporting local culture in exciting ways. These are inspiring and hopefully will encourage librarians interested in community services and cultural outreach to make connections with each other, share ideas, and build partnerships. Supporters of libraries as community builders claim that unless you are out there changing neighborhoods, you are not completing the work you are to do. Strengthening neighborhoods and championing the cultural lives of communities are big responsibilities.

D) Place-based economic development stresses the importance of offering attractive, functional, and community-based places, such as libraries, in town squares and depressed neighborhoods. Like a major department store in a mall, libraries attract large numbers of people, creating economic opportunities for numerous businesses and organizations in the surrounding area. Large cities, medium-sized ones, and even small towns have successfully transformed their libraries into the hubs(枢纽 ) of vibrant neighborhoods.

E) As key municipal agencies, and focal points for community education, libraries are major players in creating livable, environmentally friendly cities and towns. The Urban Libraries Council released a report detailing the unique ways in which libraries can further sustainability at the local level. Beyond ensuring that library construction projects consider environmental impact, libraries can take a lead in supporting local foods and craftsmen, like the Peabody Institute Library's partnering with local businesses to pioneer a farmers' market in their courtyard, or the Richmond Public Library's seed lending library which "nurtures locally-adapted plant varieties, and fosters community resilience(韧性), self-reliance and a culture of sharing."

F) Archives preserve historic artifacts, oral histories, digital history projects, and scholarly writings relevant to the community, including minority groups. Communities lucky enough to have archivists have a great advantage when it comes to organizing historical records and artifacts. An organized archive is a place where people can research their ancestry and immigration history, do environmental research, and more. An archivist is an advocate for preservation who, among other things, coordinates the restoration of maps and paintings, the digitization of vital records, and the creation of oral history projects. With projects like the Massachussets Memories Road Show and the Veterans History Project, evidence of the importance of archives is everywhere.

G) In the words of Robert Putnam, "People may go to the library looking mainly for information, but they find each other there." New moms connect at baby story-times; elderly people, often facing difficult life transitions, attend events and find that they make new friends; teenagers meet up in libraries' teen spaces after school; and readers discuss current events in the periodicals room. In libraries, community-building connections are happening all the time.

H) As Keith Richards said, "The public library is the great equalizer." Despite the rising costs of concert and theater tickets, public library events (including concerts, author visits, and gallery displays) are often offered free of charge, enabling people of any income level to attend. In addition, library book groups allow people to explore and discuss the literary arts, and the Great Stories Club introduces at-risk youth to literature. The best part: it's all free and open to the public.

I) In a time when education is increasingly expensive, public libraries provide information and educational opportunities free for all people, regardless of their socio-economic status. Offered by libraries across the country, American Library Association's Let's Talk about It programs are wonderful examples of scholar-facilitated learning opportunities in libraries. In addition, many libraries present classes and discussion programs, and some even provide online continuing education courses such as the Universal Class database.

J) Librarians know that patrons aren't just information consumers, they're information producers. Patrons use the library to gain knowledge in order to create their own new and independent works. Increasing numbers of libraries provide spaces and services that meet the needs of people who want to learn how to edit Wikipedia, set up blogs or podcasts, create their own magazines, and so much more. Many libraries offer art or writing workshops and groups, and some provide music practice rooms for patrons. Programs like ImaginOn in Charlotte, North Carolina, provide exciting models that take community partnership, creativity, and creation to a new level.

K) The decline of civil discourse stems in part from the fact that it is so easy for people to watch news about, buy products from, and engage—in both the virtual and real worlds—only with those of similar backgrounds and ideologies. Public libraries, through such programs as The Human Library and Socrates Café, can help build small communities of difference that encourage people to interact with and learn from each other through dialogue. By both actively promoting civil discourse through these programs, and modeling and upholding the principles of free inquiry and expression for all, libraries help individuals rediscover the importance of and increased need for civil discourse in American life.

L) Free tutoring, homework help programs, and summer reading programs for kids and teens help bridge the economic divide that impacts students' academic performance. The cost of hiring a private tutor is well beyond what many library patrons can afford, so libraries offer homework help and tutoring online, by phone, in person, and even through social media and homework apps. Annual summer reading programs also have a positive impact on student performance and, according to a 2010 study conducted by Dominican University's Graduate School of Library and Information Science, students' reading skills get a boost from these popular nationwide events.

M) Through library collections, programs, and physical spaces, children learn to share, to be engaged in their communities, to participate in the arts, and to explore their immediate world and the world at large. There are surely endless examples of innovative library services for children, including the Middle Country Public Library's Nature Explorium, which engages children in learning about the natural world.

N) These examples are just a few of the many amazing things that public libraries around the United States (and the world) are doing to build and maintain strong community connections. We encourage you to try some of these ideas in your own libraries, and we hope that these ideas will help you be better able to convince your community leaders of the important role that public libraries play in communities large and small.
