items.title: 2025年6月六级第1套 · 仔细阅读 · 第一篇
items.passage:
Nationally, one in six children miss 15 or more days of school in a year. Education officials have deplored all this missed instruction.

These chronically absent students suffer academically because of all the classroom instruction they miss out on. In 2015, the U.S. secretary of education responded to this crisis, urging communities to support every student to attend every day and be successful in school. His open letter stated that missing 10% of school days in a year for any reason—excused or unexcused—is a primary cause of low academic achievement.

Worrying about whether children attend school makes sense. After all, if students don't show up, teachers can't teach them.

But what if America's attendance crisis is about much more than students missing class? What if, instead, it is a reflection of family and community crises these students face—such as being ejected from the family apartment, fearing for their safety in their neighborhood or suffering an illness?

As social scientists we investigated how excused and unexcused absences relate to children's academic achievement.

We find that absences excused by a parent do little to harm children's learning. In fact, children with no unexcused absences—but 15 to 18 excused absences—have test scores equal to their peers who have no absences.

Meanwhile, the average child with even just one unexcused absence does much worse academically than peers with none.

We believe unexcused absence is a strong signal of the many challenges children and families face, including economic and medical hardships. Unexcused absences can be a powerful signal of how those out-of-school challenges affect children's academic progress.

Our evidence suggests unexcused absences are problematic, but for a different reason than people often think. Absence from school, and especially unexcused absence, matters mainly as a signal of many crises children and their families may be facing. It matters less as a cause of lower student achievement due to missed instruction.

How we choose to think of school absences matters for educational policy. School attendance policies typically hold schools and families accountable for the days children miss, regardless of whether they were excused or unexcused absences.

These policies assume that missing school for any reason harms children academically because they are missing classroom instruction. They also assume that schools will be able to effectively intervene by reducing student absences. We find neither to be the case.

As a result, these attendance policies end up disproportionately punishing families dealing with out-of-school crises in their lives and pressuring schools who serve them to get students to school more often.

We instead suggest using unexcused absence from school as a signal to channel resources to the children and families who need them most.

questions.prompt: What does the U.S. secretary of education say in his open letter?

options.text: It is of vital importance to respond promptly to the school absence crisis.
The academic performance of chronically absent students is deplorable.
Low academic achievement is mainly attributed to school absences.
The effect of school absences on American education is worrisome.

questions.shortExplanation: His open letter stated that missing 10% of school days in a year for any reason—excused or unexcused—is a primary cause of low academic achievement. 他的公开信指出，一年缺课 10%——无论是否有故——是低学业成就的一个主要原因。
questions.detailedExplanation:
【答案】 C （细节题）

【判型】 What does the U.S. secretary of education say in his open letter? 问的是某人具体说的内容，答案就在原文某句话里，不需推断。

【拆句】 结构是 What does the U.S. secretary of education say in his open letter?——典型 what 引导的特殊疑问句，主语 the U.S. secretary of education，谓语 say，介词短语 in his open letter 限定 say 的发生场景；无从句、无否定、无陷阱。

【定位】 His open letter stated that missing 10% of school days in a year for any reason—excused or unexcused—is a primary cause of low academic achievement. 他的公开信指出，一年缺课 10%——无论是否有故——是低学业成就的一个主要原因。

【选项】 A) 过度推断公开信里没有任何关于 "必须迅速回应" 的话——urging communities to support every student 是劝学校社区支持学生出勤，不是对 respond promptly 的呼吁；A 项把作者（urging）的动作改写成信件内容，且加了原文没有的 "vital importance / promptly" 程度词。

B) 偷换概念 deplored 在原文里描述的是 Education officials 对 "all this missed instruction" 的态度，B 项把它偷换成了 "chronically absent students 的 academic performance is deplorable"——主语从 "缺课现象" 偷换成 "学生的学业表现"，evaluatee 错位。 C) ✓ 正确 missing 10% of school days in a year for any reason ↔ school absences is a primary cause of low academic achievement ↔

Low academic achievement is mainly attributed to C 项把 missing 10% of school days … is a primary cause of low academic achievement 的主动因果倒装为 "低学业主要归因于缺课" 的被动因果，与预判 "缺课是学业差的主因" 完全吻合。 D) 张冠李戴公开信原文用 primary cause 的客观因果定性，并未对 "school absences 对美国教育的影响" 作 worrisome 这种情感色彩评价——D 项把 Worrying 段的句首词搬到这里， 但那是作者对 "担心缺勤" 的转述，并非教育部长公开信的内容。
questions.hint: 回到原文定位题干关键词，比较选项与原文的含义。

questions.prompt: What do the authors find about school absences?

options.text: Excused school absences have little impact on children's learning.
There is little difference between unexcused and excused absences.
Excused absences lead to comparatively better school performance.
Unexcused absences are a big challenge to both schools and families.

questions.shortExplanation: We find that absences excused by a parent do little to harm children's learning.
questions.detailedExplanation:
【答案】 A （细节题）

【判型】 What do the authors find about school absences? 问的是作者的客观发现，原文必有对应陈述句，不属于推断。

【拆句】 结构是 What do the authors find about school absences?——What 作 find 的宾语， 主语 the authors，介词短语 about school absences 限定 find 的话题范围；句法简单， 没有陷阱。

【定位】 We find that absences excused by a parent do little to harm children's learning.

我们发现，由家长请假的 excused absences 对孩子的学习几乎没有伤害。

【选项】 A) ✓ 正确 absences excused by a parent ↔ Excused school absences do little to harm children's learning ↔ have little impact on children's learning A 项是 P6 第一句的字面同义改写——主语 excused absences、谓语 do little to harm 全部一一对应，无任何添加或扭曲，与预判完全吻合。

B) 与原文相反原文 the average child with even just one unexcused absence does much worse academically than peers with none 明确指出 unexcused 与 excused 差异很大——B 项 little difference 与原文 much worse 直接相反。

C) 过度推断原文只说 excused absences do little to harm、有 excused 缺勤的孩子 have test scores equal to their peers who have no absences——是 "equal to"（相当），不是 comparatively better（相对更好）。"持平" 被悄悄抬升为 "更好"。 D) 答非所问 Unexcused absences are a big challenge to both schools and families 谈的是 unexcused 对学校和家庭构成挑战——题干 Q47 问的是 "authors 关于 school absences 的发现"，作者的核心发现是 excused 不损学（P6），而非 unexcused 对学校家庭有多挑战。话题偏离。
questions.hint: 回到原文定位题干关键词，比较选项与原文的含义。

questions.prompt: What do the authors believe concerning unexcused school absences?

options.text: They are likely to cause a decrease in students' academic achievements due to missed instruction.
They point directly to many of the out-of-school challenges confronting children and their families.
They are matters the American government typically ignores when formulating educational policies.
They give a clear signal to children and their families of the crises they are likely to face in the future.

questions.shortExplanation: We believe unexcused absence is a strong signal of the many challenges children and families face, including economic and medical hardships.
questions.detailedExplanation:
【答案】 B （细节题）

【判型】 What do the authors believe concerning unexcused school absences? 问的是作者已经明说的观点，原文有原句，属于细节题。

【拆句】 结构是 What do the authors believe concerning unexcused school absences?—— concerning 等于 about，是介词，引出讨论对象；与 Q47 唯一的差异在限定词 unexcused，读题时务必圈出。

【定位】 We believe unexcused absence is a strong signal of the many challenges children and families face, including economic and medical hardships.

我们认为，无故缺勤是孩子和家庭所面临诸多挑战的强烈信号，包括经济与医疗方面的困难。

【选项】 A) 与原文相反 They are likely to cause a decrease in students' academic achievements due to missed instruction 是作者明确反对的观点——It matters less as a cause of lower student achievement due to missed instruction 中 "matters less as a cause" 直接否定了 "缺课通过 missed instruction 导致学业下降" 这一因果。A 项把作者反对的观点扣给作者本人。

B) ✓ 正确 is a strong signal of ↔ point directly to the many challenges children and families face ↔

many of the out-of-school challenges confronting children and their families B 项把 is a strong signal of 改写为 point directly to——"信号" 与 "指向" 是六级常见的隐喻互换，与预判 "无故缺勤指向校外挑战" 完全吻合。 C) 无中生有原文未说政府 typically ignores unexcused absences——恰恰相反，P10 说政策 hold schools and families accountable for the days children miss，是 "管太严" 而非 "忽视"。C 项凭空捏造 "政府忽视" 这一事实。

D) 偷换概念原文 is a strong signal of the many challenges children and families face 用一般现在时 face，指 "当下面对" 的挑战；D 项改成 the crises they are likely to face in the future 把时间挪到未来——把 "反映当下危机" 偷换成 "预测未来危机"。
questions.hint: 回到原文定位题干关键词，比较选项与原文的含义。

questions.prompt: What is the assumption underlying education policies in the U.S.?

options.text: Children's academic performance depends on reducing the number of absences.
Schools can boost children's academic performance by effective intervention.
Schools as well as families should be held responsible for out-of-school crises.
Children's academic performance is closely related to the quality of instruction.

questions.shortExplanation: They also assume that schools will be able to effectively intervene by reducing student absences. 这些政策还预设，学校能通过减少学生缺勤来有效进行干预。
questions.detailedExplanation:
【答案】 B （细节题）

【判型】 What is the assumption underlying education policies in the U.S.? 问的是原文已经写明的预设，不是要读者推断政策背后的隐含逻辑。

【拆句】 结构是 What is the assumption underlying education policies in the U.S.?——主语是 the assumption，underlying 是现在分词作后置定语（= that underlies），限定 assumption 是 "作为政策基础的" 那种预设；不要把 underlying 误读为时间状语。

【定位】 They also assume that schools will be able to effectively intervene by reducing student absences. 这些政策还预设，学校能通过减少学生缺勤来有效进行干预。

【选项】 A) 偷换概念原文 missing school for any reason harms children academically 是 "缺课损学业"——A 项 Children's academic performance depends on reducing the number of absences 把它倒过来说 "学业取决于减少缺勤"，表面相近但因果主语错位：原文主语是 "缺课"，A 项主语变成 "学业"，且 depends on 把单向因果偷换为 "取决于" 这一更强的依存关系。

B) ✓ 正确 schools will be able to effectively intervene ↔

Schools can boost children's academic performance by effective intervention by reducing student absences + These policies assume that missing school for any reason harms children academically

↔ boost children's academic performance B 项把第二个 assume（学校能有效干预）与前一句的因果（缺课损学业）合起来—— 干预 → 减少缺勤 → 提升学业，是政策预设的完整逻辑，与预判吻合。

C) 张冠李戴原文 hold schools and families accountable for the days children miss 说政策让学校和家庭对 "缺课天数" 负责，而不是对 out-of-school crises 负责——"out-of-school crises" 是 out-of-school challenges 里的概念，C 项把它扣到了 "政策让学校家庭负责的对象" 头上，移花接木。

D) 无中生有原文从头到尾在讨论 attendance / absences / missed instruction（错过的教学）， 从未讨论 the quality of instruction（教学质量）——D 项凭空引入 "教学质量" 概念， 与原文核心论域无关。
questions.hint: 回到原文定位题干关键词，比较选项与原文的含义。

questions.prompt: What do the authors suggest doing regarding school absences?

options.text: Directing resources to helping needy children.
Pressuring schools to reduce unexcused ones.

questions.shortExplanation: We instead suggest using unexcused absence from school as a signal to channel resources to the children and families who need them most. 我们反而建议：把无故缺勤作为信号，把资源调配给最需要这些资源的孩子和家庭。
questions.detailedExplanation:
【答案】 C （细节题）

【判型】 What do the authors suggest doing regarding school absences? 问的是作者明说的建议，原文有原句，不需推断。

【拆句】 结构是 What do the authors suggest doing regarding school absences?——suggest doing 是 suggest 接动名词的固定搭配，What 在动名词 doing 后充当宾语；regarding = about，限定话题。结构平铺直叙，无陷阱。

【定位】 We instead suggest using unexcused absence from school as a signal to channel resources to the children and families who need them most. 我们反而建议：把无故缺勤作为信号，把资源调配给最需要这些资源的孩子和家庭。

【选项】 A) 答非所问原文 P13 的建议是 "把 unexcused absence 当信号 → 把资源调配给需要者"，不是 Identifying their underlying causes（找缺勤的根本原因）——作者已经在前文给出原因（家庭/社区危机），末段不再建议 "找原因"，而是 "用信号导资源"。

B) 过度推断原文 P10–P12 批评了现行政策，但 We instead suggest 的建议内容是 "用 unexcused absence 当信号导资源"，而不是 Reframing school attendance policies （重构考勤政策）——作者直接给出替代做法，没把 "重构政策" 作为建议本身提出。 C) ✓ 正确 channel resources to↔ Directing resources to the children and families who need them most↔needy children C 项把 channel resources to 直接对应 Directing resources to，把 who need them most 压缩为 needy——两步同义改写都是六级高频考法，与预判完全吻合。

D) 与原文相反原文 P12 明确指出现行政策 pressuring schools who serve them to get students to school more often 是负面后果，作者是 "批评施压"——D 项 Pressuring schools to reduce unexcused ones 反而把 "施压学校" 作为作者的建议，与原文立场完全相反。
questions.hint: 回到原文定位题干关键词，比较选项与原文的含义。

items.title: 2025年6月六级第1套 · 仔细阅读 · 第二篇
items.passage:
After earning a bachelor's degree, I was determined to do what I love. I headed straight to graduate school to investigate the social problems that fascinated me.

For almost a decade, I told everyone I encountered that they should do the same. "Follow your passion," I counseled. "You can figure out the employment stuff later."

It wasn't until I began to research this widely accepted career advice that I understood how problematic it really was.

As a sociologist, I interviewed college students and professional workers to learn what it really meant to pursue their dreams, which I will refer to here as the passion principle. I was stunned by what I found out about this principle in the research for my new book.

Surveys show the American public has long held the passion principle in high regard as a career decision-making priority. And its popularity is even stronger among those facing job instability.

Advocates of the passion principle found it compelling because they believed that following one's passion can provide workers with both the motivation necessary to work hard and a place to find fulfillment.

Yet, what I found is that following one's passion does not necessarily lead to fulfillment, but is one of the most powerful cultural forces perpetuating overwork. I also found that promoting the pursuit of one's passion helps perpetuate social inequalities due to the fact that not everyone has the same economic resources to allow them to pursue their passion with ease.

While the passion principle is broadly popular, not everyone has the necessary resources to turn their passion into a stable, good-paying job. Passion-seekers from wealthy families are better able to wait until a job they are passionate about comes along without worrying about student loans in the meantime. They are also better situated to take unpaid internships to get their foot in the door while their parents pay their rent. And they often have access to parents' social networks to help them find jobs. Surveys revealed that working-class and first-generation college graduates, regardless of their career field, are more likely than their wealthier peers to end up in low-paying unskilled jobs when they pursue their passion.

Colleges, workplaces and career counselors who promote the "follow your passion" path for everyone, without leveling the playing field, help perpetuate socioeconomic inequalities among career aspirants.

It's not just well-off passion-seekers who benefit from the passion principle. Employers of passionate workers do, too. Potential employers showed greater interest in passionate applicants in part because they believed the applicants would work hard at their jobs without expecting an increase in pay. They even sacrifice a good salary, job stability and leisure time to work in a job they love.

questions.prompt: What did the author advise people do for almost a decade?

options.text: Figure out what is the most fascinating job.
Do whatever they are zealous for.

questions.shortExplanation: For almost a decade, I told everyone I encountered that they should do the same. "Follow your passion," I counseled. "You can figure out the employment stuff later." 在将近十年的时间里，我告诉我遇到的每一个人：他们应该和我做一样的事。我劝告说： 「追随你的激情」「就业那些事儿你以后再琢磨」。
questions.detailedExplanation:
【答案】 D （细节题）

【判型】 What did the author advise people do for almost a decade 用 What did 直接问事实， 没有 infer/suggest/imply/mainly about 等推断或主旨信号。

【拆句】 What did the author advise people do for almost a decade 是 What 引导的特殊疑问句，主干 the author advise people do，advise sb. do 处省略 to（口语化结构），for almost a decade 是时间状语修饰整个动作，无陷阱。

【定位】 For almost a decade, I told everyone I encountered that they should do the same. "Follow your passion," I counseled. "You can figure out the employment stuff later." 在将近十年的时间里，我告诉我遇到的每一个人：他们应该和我做一样的事。我劝告说： 「追随你的激情」「就业那些事儿你以后再琢磨」。

【选项】 A) 偷换概念 Figure out what is the most fascinating job 把 fascinated 这个形容作者自己研究方向的词嫁接到 job 上，原文 P2 是作者劝别人 follow passion，不是劝别人去找最有趣的工作。 B) 张冠李戴 Follow widely accepted career counsel 把作者自己当年发出的建议描述为去跟随别人的建议，但原文 I counseled 表明作者本人就是 counsel 的发出者。

C) 偷换概念 Pursue their careers with passion 是『用激情去追求事业』，原文是『追随你的激情』，二者并不等价：前者是把激情当工作态度，后者是把激情当工作方向。

D) ✓ 正确 Follow your passion ↔ Do whatever they are zealous for 预判答案是『追随激情/做自己热爱的事』，Do whatever they are zealous for 用 zealous for 同义替换 passion，正中预判。
questions.hint: 回到原文定位题干关键词，比较选项与原文的含义。

questions.prompt: How did the author feel about the passion principle through his research?

options.text: He was astonished by its consequences.
He was further convinced of its soundness.
He was actually right to follow it through.
He was struck by its broad popularity.

questions.shortExplanation: I was stunned by what I found out about this principle in the research for my new book.
questions.detailedExplanation:
【答案】 A （细节题）

【判型】 How did the author feel about the passion principle through his research 直接问研究后的具体感受，是有明确指向的事实题。

【拆句】 How did the author feel about the passion principle through his research 是 How 引导的特殊疑问句，主干 the author feel about the passion principle，through his research 作方式状语，限定感受产生的途径，无陷阱。

【定位】 I was stunned by what I found out about this principle in the research for my new book.

在为新书做的研究中，我被自己关于这一原则的发现震惊了。

【选项】 A) ✓ 正确 I was stunned by what I found out ↔ He was astonished by its consequences 预判是『被研究发现震惊』，astonished by its consequences 把震惊源具体落到 consequences 上，与原文 P7 起列举的负面后果一致。

B) 与原文相反 He was further convinced of its soundness 说作者更加确信激情原则的正确性，但原文 how problematic it really was 与 stunned 均显示作者发现了它的问题，立场是反向的。

C) 与原文相反 He was actually right to follow it through 说作者证实自己当初跟随激情是对的，但原文 does not necessarily lead to fulfillment 表明作者得出的是『追随激情未必带来满足』的反思结论，并非自我肯定。

D) 答非所问 He was struck by its broad popularity 把震惊对象错挂到『大众接受度』上，但题干问的是 through his research，原文 P5 谈大众接受度但用的是中性动词 hold ... in high regard，作者并未对此 struck。
questions.hint: 回到原文定位题干关键词，比较选项与原文的含义。

questions.prompt: What is important to turning one's passion into a stable, good-paying job?

options.text: Willingness to take unpaid internships and low-paying jobs.
Full academic preparedness and sound career counseling.
Hard work and sacrifice of leisure time.

questions.shortExplanation: Passion-seekers from wealthy families are better able to wait until a job they are passionate about comes along without worrying about student loans in the meantime. They are also better situated to take unpaid internships to get their foot in the door while their parents pay their rent. And they often have access to parents' social networks to help them find jobs.
questions.detailedExplanation:
【答案】 D （细节题）

【判型】 What is important to turning one's passion into a stable, good-paying job 问的是某事的关键条件，是事实层面的细节题。

【拆句】 What is important to turning one's passion into a stable, good-paying job 中 turning ... job 是动名词短语作介词 to 的宾语，a stable, good-paying job 中两个形容词并列修饰 job，无陷阱。

【定位】 Passion-seekers from wealthy families are better able to wait until a job they are passionate about comes along without worrying about student loans in the meantime. They are also better situated to take unpaid internships to get their foot in the door while their parents pay their rent. And they often have access to parents' social networks to help them find jobs.

出身富裕家庭的激情追随者更有能力等到自己真正热爱的工作出现，同时不必担心助学贷款；他们也更有条件接受无薪实习以打开职业大门，因为有父母替他们付房租；而且，他们往往可以借助父母的社会人脉帮自己找工作。

【选项】 A) 偷换概念 Willingness to take unpaid internships and low-paying jobs 把『愿意做无薪实习和低薪工作』当成转化成功的关键，但原文里无薪实习是富裕者的专利（while their parents pay their rent），而低薪非技能岗位则是工薪阶层 end up in low-paying unskilled jobs 的不利结局，二者都不是『成功条件』。

B) 无中生有 Full academic preparedness and sound career counseling 提到的『学业准备充分』 在 P8 中根本没有任何线索；P9 虽出现 career counselors 但是被批评的对象、不是关键条件。 C) 张冠李戴 Hard work and sacrifice of leisure time 在原文中是 P10 雇主对激情员工的期待与员工实际付出的代价，与题 53 问的『把激情变成稳定高薪』的关键条件无关。

D) ✓ 正确 wait until a job they are passionate about comes along without worrying about student loans ↔

Financial backing access to parents' social networks to help them find jobs ↔ social connections 预判要点是经济和人脉两个维度，Financial backing and social connections 一项即覆盖两条，是与原文论据结构最完整匹配的概括。
questions.hint: 回到原文定位题干关键词，比较选项与原文的含义。

questions.prompt: What happens when everyone is encouraged to follow their passion?

options.text: Many more career aspirants end up unemployed.
People are less concerned with socioeconomic inequality.
Socioeconomic inequality is likely to persist.
Career counselors are going to lose credibility.

questions.shortExplanation: Colleges, workplaces and career counselors who promote the "follow your passion" path for everyone, without leveling the playing field, help perpetuate socioeconomic inequalities among career aspirants.
questions.detailedExplanation:
【答案】 C （细节题）

【判型】 What happens when everyone is encouraged to follow their passion 问的是一个已发生在原文里的具体结果，不需推断。

【拆句】 What happens when everyone is encouraged to follow their passion 是 What 引导的疑问句加 when 时间从句，主干 What happens，everyone is encouraged to follow their passion 是被动语态从句，无陷阱。

【定位】 Colleges, workplaces and career counselors who promote the "follow your passion" path for everyone, without leveling the playing field, help perpetuate socioeconomic inequalities among career aspirants.

那些向所有人推行『跟随激情』路径却不去拉平起跑线的高校、用人单位与职业顾问，正在加剧职业追求者之间的社会经济不平等。

【选项】 A) 无中生有 Many more career aspirants end up unemployed 中的『失业』在原文中没有出现， P8 只说工薪阶层会落入 low-paying unskilled jobs（低薪非技能岗），那是有工作而非失业。 B) 与原文相反 People are less concerned with socioeconomic inequality 说人们对不平等的关注度下降，原文 P9 说的是不平等本身被延续，并不涉及关注度的变化，且 less 反向于作者的批评立场。

C) ✓ 正确 help perpetuate socioeconomic inequalities ↔ Socioeconomic inequality is likely to persist 预判结果是『不平等被延续』，C 用 persist 同义、用 is likely to 对应 help 的中等程度，结构性等值，是 54 的最佳概括。

D) 过度推断 Career counselors are going to lose credibility 推断职业顾问会失去公信力，原文 P9 只是批评他们推行『跟随激情』而不拉平起跑线，并未说他们会丧失公信力。
questions.hint: 回到原文定位题干关键词，比较选项与原文的含义。

questions.prompt: What does the author say about employers of passionate workers?

options.text: They provide these workers with job stability and a good salary.
They exploit these workers' passion to benefit themselves.
They level the playing field for these workers to reach their goals.
They encourage these workers to realize their aspirations.

questions.shortExplanation: Employers of passionate workers do, too. Potential employers showed greater interest in passionate applicants in part because they believed the applicants would work hard at their jobs without expecting an increase in pay.
questions.detailedExplanation:
【答案】 B （细节题）

【判型】 What does the author say about employers of passionate workers 问的是作者就特定对象明示了什么观点，属于事实定位类。

【拆句】 What does the author say about employers of passionate workers 主干 What does the author say about employers，of passionate workers 是 of 短语限定 employers 的范围（雇佣激情工作者的雇主），无陷阱。

【定位】 Employers of passionate workers do, too. Potential employers showed greater interest in passionate applicants in part because they believed the applicants would work hard at their jobs without expecting an increase in pay.

雇用激情员工的雇主也同样受益。潜在雇主对激情型应聘者更感兴趣，部分原因是他们相信这些应聘者会卖力工作而不会指望涨薪。

【选项】 A) 与原文相反 They provide these workers with job stability and a good salary 说雇主给激情员工稳定和高薪，但 They even sacrifice a good salary, job stability 明示员工是在牺牲稳定和高薪、不是获得它。 B) ✓ 正确 Employers of passionate workers do, too↔

They exploit these workers' passion to benefit themselves work hard at their jobs without expecting an increase in pay↔exploit these workers' passion 预判定性为『雇主占便宜』，exploit 准确对应『利用他人 passion 为自己获利』，是对 P10 整段事实最贴近的概括。 C) 张冠李戴 They level the playing field for these workers to reach their goals 把『拉平起跑线』归给雇主，但原文 without leveling the playing field 表明这事根本没人做，更不是雇主在做。 D) 偷换概念 They encourage these workers to realize their aspirations 用『鼓励员工实现抱负』 的正面表述粉饰雇主行为，但 P10 揭示的恰是雇主借此让员工 work hard ... without expecting an increase in pay，本质是利用而非成就员工。
questions.hint: 回到原文定位题干关键词，比较选项与原文的含义。

items.title: 2025年6月六级第2套 · 选词填空
items.passage:
No beast on Earth is tougher than the tiny tardigrade(缓步类动物). It can [26] _____ being frozen at -272° Celsius, being exposed to the vacuum of outer space and even being [27] _____ with 500 times the dose of X-rays that would kill a human. In other words, the creature can endure conditions that don't even exist on Earth. And researchers are looking to the microscopic animals to learn how to prepare humans and crops to handle the [28] _____ of space travel.

The tardigrade's indestructibility stems from its [29] _____ to its environment—which may seem surprising, since it lives in [30] _____ comfortable places, like the cool, wet patches of moss(⻘苔) that dot a garden wall.

But it turns out that a tardigrade's damp, mossy home can dry out many times each year. Drying is pretty [31] _____ for most living things. It does damage to cells in some of the same ways that freezing, vacuum and radiation do. Tardigrades, however, have [32] _____ special strategies for dealing with these kinds of damage.

As a tardigrade dries out, its cells produce several strange proteins that are unlike anything found in other animals. In water, the proteins are shapeless. But as water disappears, the proteins self-assemble into long fibers that fill the cell's [33] _____ . The fibers support the cell's membranes(细胞膜) and proteins, preventing them from breaking or [34] _____ .

Emulating tardigrades could one day help humans colonize outer space. Food crops could be engineered to produce tardigrade proteins, allowing these organisms to grow more efficiently on spacecraft where levels of radiation are elevated compared with on Earth.

So if humans ever succeed in reaching the stars, they may accomplish this [35] _____ , in part, by standing on the shoulders of the tiny eight-legged endurance specialists in your backyard.

questions.prompt: It can __(26)__ being frozen at -272° Celsius, being exposed to the vacuum of outer space and even being __(27)__ with 500 times the dose of X-rays that would kill a human
questions.shortExplanation: 与开篇"地球最坚韧"主旨吻合，survive doing 是地道搭配全文开篇 No beast on Earth is tougher than the tiny tardigrade 在强调它能 "挺过" 各种极端条件；survive 后接动名词意为"挺过、幸存于"，正好对应 being frozen / being exposed / being blasted 这一连串极端待遇。
questions.detailedExplanation:
【答案】 K) survive 动词

【词性槽】 情态动词 can 后需动词原形

【依据】 与开篇"地球最坚韧"主旨吻合，survive doing 是地道搭配全文开篇 No beast on Earth is tougher than the tiny tardigrade 在强调它能 "挺过" 各种极端条件；survive 后接动名词意为"挺过、幸存于"，正好对应 being frozen / being exposed / being blasted 这一连串极端待遇。

【竞争词】 L) tempt "引诱"语义牛头不对马嘴

tempt 是"诱惑/吸引"，宾语通常是人，且后接不定式 to do；说"它诱惑被冷冻在 -272 度"既不搭配也与文意完全相反。
questions.hint: 根据空格前后的词性、搭配与上下文选择词语；每个词最多使用一次。

questions.prompt: being __(27)__ with 500 times the dose of X-rays that would kill a human
questions.shortExplanation: be blasted with 是"被…强力照射/轰击"的固定搭配
questions.detailedExplanation:
【答案】 B) blasted 动词

【词性槽】 being ___ with 结构需被动语态过去分词

【依据】 be blasted with 是"被…强力照射/轰击"的固定搭配

空后接 500 times the dose of X-rays（500 倍剂量的 X 射线），动作是"被高剂量 X 射线轰击"；blast with 表"用…猛烈轰击/照射"，与 X-rays 搭配标准，且与前面 being frozen、being exposed 三件"极端遭遇"形成排比。

【竞争词】 D) evolved evolve 是不及物动词，没有被动义

evolve 意为"进化"，本身不能说"被进化"；evolve with X-rays 也无固定搭配，更与本句"承受极端伤害"的语义方向相反。

questions.prompt: learn how to prepare humans and crops to handle the __(28)__ of space travel
questions.shortExplanation: the rigors of space travel 是新闻文本中描述"太空旅行严酷条件"的高频搭配
questions.detailedExplanation:
【答案】 I) rigors 名词

【词性槽】 定冠词 the 后接介词 of，需名词作 of 短语中心词

【依据】 the rigors of space travel 是新闻文本中描述"太空旅行严酷条件"的高频搭配

上文刚说缓步类动物能 endure conditions that don't even exist on Earth，研究者要让人类与作物准备应对 the __(28)__ of space travel，需要 handle 的应是"严酷条件"；the rigors of X（X 的严酷条件）正是六级阅读常见的固定搭配，与 handle 的宾语"困难/考验"语义匹配。

【竞争词】 H) recurrence "复发"与"太空旅行"搭配不成立

recurrence 用于事件再次发生，the recurrence of space travel 意思变成"太空旅行的复发"， 与"应对严酷条件"的因果链完全错位。

questions.prompt: The tardigrade's indestructibility stems from its __(29)__ to its environment
questions.shortExplanation: adaptation to environment 是地道搭配，且与下文进化呼应本句说"不可摧毁性源自它对环境的某物"，下文 Tardigrades, however, have __(32)__ special strategies for dealing with these kinds of damage 直接给出"特殊策略"，正是"适应"的具体表现；adaptations to its environment 意为"对环境的（多项）适应"，完全贴合。
questions.detailedExplanation:
【答案】 A) adaptations 名词

【词性槽】 形容词性物主代词 its 后需名词

【依据】 adaptation to environment 是地道搭配，且与下文进化呼应本句说"不可摧毁性源自它对环境的某物"，下文 Tardigrades, however, have __(32)__ special strategies for dealing with these kinds of damage 直接给出"特殊策略"，正是"适应"的具体表现；adaptations to its environment 意为"对环境的（多项）适应"，完全贴合。

【竞争词】 H) recurrence "复发"与"环境适应"语义无关

recurrence to its environment 不是固定搭配，且"对环境的复发"在语义上不成立。

I) rigors rigors 表外部严酷，不是它"自己的"特质

rigors to its environment 不通；况且 its rigors 意为"它自己的严酷"，与"不可摧毁性来源"的因果链方向不对，应是"环境的严酷"而非"它的严酷"。

questions.prompt: it lives in __(30)__ comfortable places, like the cool, wet patches of moss
questions.shortExplanation: 与下文的极端耐受形成转折反差
questions.detailedExplanation:
【答案】 J) seemingly 副词

【词性槽】 形容词 comfortable 前需副词修饰

【依据】 与下文的极端耐受形成转折反差

上一段刚说缓步类动物的不可摧毁源自对环境的适应，作者紧接着用 which may seem surprising 提示读者：它住的地方其实 cool, wet patches of moss，看着挺舒服。所以这里要的就是"看似、表面上"——seemingly comfortable 与后文实际会反复干涸的真相形成反差。

【竞争词】 N) unanimously 语义牛头不对马嘴

unanimously 意为"一致地"，描述群体投票或意见，与单数主语 it 的居住环境舒适程度无关， 代入 lives in unanimously comfortable places 完全讲不通。

questions.prompt: Drying is pretty __(31)__ for most living things
questions.shortExplanation: 与下句"破坏细胞、堪比冷冻真空辐射"等量齐观
questions.detailedExplanation:
【答案】 C) catastrophic 形容词

【词性槽】 be 动词 is 后接表语，需形容词

【依据】 与下句"破坏细胞、堪比冷冻真空辐射"等量齐观

紧接着的下一句 It does damage to cells in some of the same ways that freezing, vacuum and radiation do 把"干燥"的伤害与冷冻、真空、辐射并列；这种伤害程度只能用"灾难性的"来形容，catastrophic 程度恰好对得上。

questions.prompt: Tardigrades, however, have __(32)__ special strategies for dealing with these kinds of damage
questions.shortExplanation: evolve 在此作及物动词，意为"演化出"
questions.detailedExplanation:
【答案】 D) evolved 动词

【词性槽】 have ___ special strategies 需过去分词构成现在完成时

【依据】 evolve 在此作及物动词，意为"演化出"

前句指出干燥具有破坏性，本句用 however 转折，强调缓步类动物却"已经演化出"特殊策略；evolve special strategies 表示"（通过进化）形成了特殊策略"，与全段"它的适应性来源"主旨一致，并与 29 题 adaptations 形成主旨内回环。

【易错】 最具迷惑性的错误词是 B) —— blasted 也可作过去分词，词性陷阱。have + 过去分词 + 名词宾语的现在完成时框架里，blasted 与 evolved 都是过去分词，词性符合；但 blast strategies 搭配不成立，且本句靠 however 引出的"它却演化出策略"才是文意。识破法： 动词不仅看词性，还要看与宾语 special strategies 是否能搭配。
questions.hint: 根据空格前后的词性、搭配与上下文选择词语；每个词最多使用一次。

questions.prompt: the proteins self-assemble into long fibers that fill the cell's __(33)__
questions.shortExplanation: fill ... interior 是描述细胞内部空间的典型搭配
questions.detailedExplanation:
【答案】 F) interior 名词

【词性槽】 形容词性所有格 the cell's 后需名词

【依据】 fill ... interior 是描述细胞内部空间的典型搭配

上下文谈到蛋白质组装成长纤维并 fill the cell's __(33)__，下文还说这些纤维 support the cell's membranes(细胞膜) and proteins——能被纤维"填满"且能支撑膜与蛋白的，只能是细胞的"内部空间"，interior 名词义"内部"完全契合。

【竞争词】 A) adaptations义为"适应性变化"，不可被纤维填满

adaptations 指生物层面的适应性特征，是抽象概念，不存在"被长纤维填满"的物理空间含义， 与 fill 在语义上不兼容。

E) feat"壮举"是抽象成就，不能被填满

feat 用于人或行为的伟大成就（如下文 they may accomplish this __(35)__ 才是它的归宿）， 与细胞物理结构毫无关系。

H) recurrence "复发"指事件重复，不指空间

recurrence 是"再次发生"的动作性名词，不是一个可以被纤维 fill 的位置或空间。

I) rigors"严酷条件"指环境而非细胞内部

rigors 表抽象的"艰难考验"，复数语义偏外部环境，且后文马上要用它来描述太空旅行的严酷 （见 26 题语境），与本句"细胞内部"语义错位。
questions.hint: 根据空格前后的词性、搭配与上下文选择词语；每个词最多使用一次。

questions.prompt: The fibers support the cell's membranes(细胞膜) and proteins, preventing them from breaking or __(34)__
questions.shortExplanation: unfold 是生化语境下"蛋白质解折叠/结构散开"的标准说法
questions.detailedExplanation:
【答案】 O) unfolding 动词

【词性槽】 介词 from 后并列的动名词

【依据】 unfold 是生化语境下"蛋白质解折叠/结构散开"的标准说法

本句说纤维 support the cell's membranes(细胞膜) and proteins，防止它们 breaking 或本空所表的另一种损坏；蛋白质受损的两种典型方式就是"断裂"（breaking）与"解折叠/散开"（unfolding），二者并列正好构成对细胞膜/蛋白损伤的全面描述。

【竞争词】 G) probing "探测"是主动动作，与被防止的损坏无关

probe 意为"探查、调查"，主语应是"探查者"；细胞膜或蛋白被防止"探查"在语义上完全说不通，与 breaking 也不成对。

【易错】 最具迷惑性的错误词是 G) —— probing 与 unfolding 同为 -ing 形态，易混。在 preventing them from breaking or __(34)__ 处，两词词性一致；但 probing"探测"是主动动作，与被并列项 breaking"断裂"不在同一语义场。防坑法：or 并列项必须同语义方向，立刻砍掉异类。
questions.hint: 根据空格前后的词性、搭配与上下文选择词语；每个词最多使用一次。

questions.prompt: they may accomplish this __(35)__, in part, by standing on the shoulders of the tiny eight-legged endurance specialists
questions.shortExplanation: accomplish a feat 是"完成壮举"的固定搭配前文 if humans ever succeed in reaching the stars 把人类抵达星辰定调为巨大成就， this feat 正好回指这一壮举，并与 accomplish 构成最地道的"完成壮举"搭配。
questions.detailedExplanation:
【答案】 E) feat 名词

【词性槽】 指示代词 this 后需单数名词

【依据】 accomplish a feat 是"完成壮举"的固定搭配前文 if humans ever succeed in reaching the stars 把人类抵达星辰定调为巨大成就， this feat 正好回指这一壮举，并与 accomplish 构成最地道的"完成壮举"搭配。

【竞争词】 H) recurrence "复发"与"完成壮举"语义相反

recurrence 暗示"再次发生"，常用于疾病或负面事件复发，accomplish this recurrence 既不搭配也与本段"人类首次抵达星辰"的壮举语境完全冲突。

items.title: 2025年6月六级第2套 · 信息匹配
items.passage:
A) As the scale and impacts of climate change become increasingly alarming, meat is a popular target for action. Advocates for the protection of the natural environment from destruction or pollution urge the public to eat less meat. Some activists have even called for taxing meat to reduce consumption of it.

B) A key claim underlying these arguments holds that globally, meat production generates more greenhouse gases than the entire transportation sector. However, this claim is demonstrably wrong, as I will show. And its persistence has led to false assumptions about the linkage between meat and climate change.

C) My recent research focuses on ways in which animal agriculture affects air quality and climate change. In my view, there are many reasons for either choosing animal protein or opting for a vegetarian selection. However, abandoning meat and meat products is not the environmental panacea( 万灵药 ) many would have us believe. And if taken to an extreme, it also could have harmful nutritional consequences.

D) A healthy portion of meat's negative reputation centers on the assertion that livestock is the largest source of greenhouse gases worldwide. For example, an analysis published in 2009 by the World Watch Institute based in Washington, D.C. asserted that 51 percent of global greenhouse gas emissions come from rearing and processing livestock. According to the U.S. Environmental Protection Agency, the largest sources of U.S. greenhouse gas emissions in 2016 were electricity production (28 percent of total emissions), transportation (28 percent) and industry (22 percent). All of agriculture accounted for a total of 9 percent, but all of animal agriculture contributes less than half of this amount, representing 3.9 percent of the total greenhouse emission in the U.S. That is very different from claiming that livestock represents as much as or more than transportation.

E) Why is there such a misconception? In 2006 the United Nations Food and Agriculture Organization (FAO) published a study titled "Livestock's Long Shadow," which received widespread international attention. It stated that livestock produced a staggering 18 percent of the world's greenhouse gas emissions. The agency drew a startling conclusion that livestock was doing more to harm the climate than all modes of transportation combined. This latter claim was wrong, and has since been corrected by Henning Stenfeld, the report's senior author.

F) The problem was that analysts from the FAO used a comprehensive life-cycle assessment to study the climate impact of livestock, but a different method when they analyzed transportation. For livestock, they considered every factor associated with producing meat. This included emissions from fertilizer production, converting land from forests to pastures, growing feed, and direct emissions from animals (manure as well as expelling of gas from the stomach) from birth to death.

G) However, when they looked at transportation's carbon footprint, they ignored impacts on the climate from manufacturing vehicle materials and parts, assembling vehicles and maintaining roads, bridges and airports. Instead, they only considered the exhaust smoke emitted by finished cars, trucks, trains and planes. As a result, the FAO's comparison of greenhouse gas emissions from livestock to those from transportation was greatly distorted.

H) I pointed out this flaw during a speech to fellow scientists in San Francisco on March 22, 2010, which led to a flood of media coverage. To its credit, the FAO immediately owned up to its error. Unfortunately, the agency's initial claim that livestock was responsible for the lion's share of world greenhouse gas emissions had already received wide coverage. To this day, we struggle to "unring" the bell. In its most recent assessment report, the FAO estimated that livestock produces 14.5 percent of global greenhouse gas emissions from human activities. There is no comparable full life-cycle assessment for transportation. However, as Stenfeld has pointed out, direct emissions from transportation versus livestock can be compared and amount to 14 versus 5 percent, respectively.

I) Many people continue to think that avoiding meat as infrequently as once a week will make a significant difference to the climate. But according to one recent study, even if Americans eliminated all animal protein from their diets, they would reduce U.S. greenhouse gas emissions by only 2.6 percent. According to our research at the University of California, Davis, if the practice of Meatless Monday were to be adopted by all Americans, we'd see a reduction of only 0.5 percent.

J) Moreover, technological, genetic and management changes that have taken place in U.S. agriculture over the past 70 years have made livestock production more efficient and less greenhouse gas-intensive. According to the FAO's statistical database, total direct greenhouse gas emissions from U.S. livestock have declined by 11.3 percent since 1961, while production of livestock meat has more than doubled.

K) Demand for meat is rising in developing and emerging economies, especially in the Middle East, North Africa and Southeast Asia. For example, raising livestock such as goats in Kenya is an important source of food and income for many small-scale farmers and herders. But meat consumption per person in these regions still lags that of developed countries. In 2015, average annual meat consumption per person in developed countries was 92 kilograms, compared to 24 kilograms in the Middle East and North Africa and 18 kilograms in Southeast Asia. Still, given projected population growth in the developing world, there will certainly be an opportunity for countries such as the United States to bring their sustainable livestock rearing practices to the table.

L) Removing animals from U.S. agriculture would lower national greenhouse gas emissions to a small degree, but it would also make it harder to meet people's nutritional requirements. Many critics of animal agriculture are quick to point out that if farmers raised only plants, they could produce more pounds of food and more calories per person. But humans also need many essential micro-and macro-nutrients for good health. It's hard to make a compelling argument that the United States has a calorie deficit, given its high national rates of adult and child obesity. Moreover, not all plant parts are edible or desirable. Raising livestock is a way to add nutritional and economic value to plant agriculture.

M) As one example, the energy in plants that livestock consume is most often contained in cellulose(纤维素 ), which is indigestible for humans and many other mammals. But cows, sheep and other ruminant( 反刍的 ) animals can break cellulose down and release the solar energy contained in this vast resource. According to the FAO, as much as 70 percent of all agricultural land globally is range land that can only be utilized as grazing land for ruminant livestock.

N) The world population is currently projected to reach 9.8 billion by 2050. Feeding this many people will raise immense challenges. Meat is more calorie-dense per serving than vegetarian options, and ruminant animals largely thrive on feed that is not suitable for humans. Raising livestock also offers much-needed income for small-scale farmers in developing nations. Worldwide, livestock provides a livelihood for 1 billion people.

O) Climate change demands urgent attention, and the livestock industry has a large overall environmental footprint that affects air, water and land. These, combined with a rapidly rising world population, give us plenty of compelling reasons to continue to work for greater efficiencies in animal agriculture. I believe the place to start is with science-based facts.

items.title: 2025年6月六级第2套 · 仔细阅读 · 第一篇
items.passage:
Why are we so worried about our careers? Partly it's to do with money, but there's a psychological aspect to our fears as well.

We worry because we suspect—not wrongly—that the world is full of a frightening sort of person ready to judge us ruthlessly and swiftly: a person we can call a snob.

A snob is anyone who takes a relatively small part of us and uses it to come to a rigid conclusion about how much of their attention we deserve. In the past, that might be your ancestry and royal connections. Nowadays, the snob cares about one thing only: what you do for a living.

This explains why the first question we will be asked in any new social context is 'What do you do?' and according to how we answer, snobs will either welcome us with broad smiles, or leave us in the cold.

And that is why we are fired up by such a desperate urge to achieve and impress.

Sometimes our behaviour is mistaken for greed and vanity, but it is more than this. A lot of our interest in fancy cars, jobs and houses has nothing to do with materialism. It has to do with a hunger for the respect and esteem that is only available in our societies through the acquisition of material goods. It isn't the goods themselves we seek, it is the love we stand to gain through our possession of them. The next time we see someone driving a Ferrari, we shouldn't condemn them for their greed, we should pity them for the intensity of their need for love from the world.

At the root of snobbery is a lack of imagination and confidence about how to decide who in the world is valuable. The snobs are brutally misguided and slavish in their beliefs about how the superior individuals can be identified. For snobs, it is the already acclaimed and already successful who are the only ones worthy of respect. There is no room in their timid regimented minds to imagine that someone might be clever, kind or good—and yet somehow have been overlooked entirely by society, their qualities lying hidden beneath an unfamiliar veil, and having as yet discovered no obvious outlet.

The true answer to snobbery is not to say that there is no such thing as a better or worse person, but to insist that better or worse exist in constantly unexpected places and carry none of the outward signs of distinction. And because we are such poor judges of the worth of others, our ultimate duty remains to be kind, good, curious and imaginative about pretty much everyone who ever crosses our path.

questions.prompt: What gives rise to our worry about careers apart from money?

options.text: Fear of being judged in a snobbish manner.
The prospect of facing fault-finding managers.

questions.detailedExplanation:
【答案】 A （细节题）

【判型】 What gives rise to our worry about careers apart from money? 问的是一个具体原因， 且用排除句式锁定方向，属典型细节题而非推断题

【拆句】 主干 What gives rise to our worry，gives rise to 是固定搭配，等于 cause；apart from money 是介词短语作状语，意为「除金钱之外」，提示原文里还另有一因。结构简单，无陷阱。

【定位】 Partly it's to do with money, but there's a psychological aspect to our fears as well. 部分原因与金钱有关，但我们的恐惧还有一个心理层面。

【选项】 A) ✓ 正确 a psychological aspect to our fears ↔ Fear of being judged in a snobbish manner ready to judge us ruthlessly and swiftly: a person we can call a snob ↔ in a snobbish manner 预判要的是「金钱之外的心理因 = 怕被评判」，A 项 Fear of being judged in a snobbish manner 把「心理因—怕—被评判—被势利者」四要素全部覆盖 B) 无中生有原文谈的是 a person we can call a snob，并未把恐惧对象限定为 fault-finding managers——经理只是势利者的一种可能，但原文没说

C) 偷换概念原文是「我们怕被人评判」（we are judged），主体是 we；选项 The ruthless way employees are often treated 主语变成 employees，且 treated 把视角换成了「被对待」，与原文 judge us ruthlessly 的「评判」含义不一致 D) 答非所问 Fright at the difficulty in hunting for a job 谈的是「找工作难」，本质仍属经济或金钱因；而题干用 apart from money 明确把金钱因排除在外

【选项】 A) 与原文相反 we shouldn't condemn them for their greed 明确反对「把对物质的兴趣等同于贪婪并加以谴责」；选项 It is the cause for condemnation of their greed 把「对物质兴趣」说成「谴责其贪婪的原因」，与作者立场相反 B) 无中生有 the comforts they provide 指物质带来的「舒适」，但 P6 谈的是「通过物质获得尊重」，不是「物质提供舒适」——comfort 维度是选项凭空添加的 C) 张冠李戴原文 we should pity them for the intensity of their need for love 说「我们应怜悯豪车车主对爱的渴求」——施动者是「我们」，对象是「豪车车主」；选项 It arouses pity rather than respect from the wealthy 却说「（兴趣）引起富人的怜悯而非尊重」，施动者变成了 the wealthy、且把 respect 与 pity 错误对立

D) ✓ 正确 a hunger for the respect and esteem ↔ their craving for social recognition only available in our societies through the acquisition of material goods ↔ arises from 预判的核心三要素：第一是「渴求」（hunger 对应 craving）、第二是对象是「社会层面的尊重」（respect and esteem 对应 social recognition）、第三是驱动了对物质的兴趣（arises from）。D 项三要素全中

items.title: 2025年6月六级第2套 · 仔细阅读 · 第二篇
items.passage:
Women have historically been paid less. But in the US in the 1980s, they began to catch up— fast. During that decade, the gender pay gap closed by about one percentage point a year. Had that trend continued, the gender wage gap would have been closed by 2017.

But the trend didn't continue, and the gap remains yawning.

According to a new study from academics at Harvard, the stagnation can be put down, perhaps counterintuitively, to the introduction of state and federal family leave policies.

The academics argue that during the 1990s, as governments began to introduce leave policies, it was mainly women who took advantage of them. Though the leave policies might have helped those women to stay in the workplace—instead of dropping out to have families—those who returned saw their wages had increased at lower rates than the men.

After family leave was introduced in the US, in fact, the rate of gender wage convergence fell to just 0.03 percentage points per year, and has remained there ever since.

Those monitoring the process towards salary equity at work have long watched as progress slowed in many countries around the world. In fact, that progress began to reverse during the pandemic(⼤流⾏病 ).

The gender pay gap is one of the most outstanding examples of that lack of parity( 平等 ), and still exists just about everywhere. The motherhood penalty has become a shorthand for describing why: In many places, especially rich countries, women earn the same as men until they reach their childbearing years. Women who have children begin to see their salaries slip behind their male counterparts.

Part of this is because women take on more of the unpaid labor at home, which can eat into time available for work and energy for career advancement. But it's also because mothers are passed over for raises and promotion, and because time out of the workplace sets women back, even if that time is taken voluntarily, and supported by company or government policy.

What would have happened if leave policies hadn't been introduced? The study doesn't go into that question, other than to say that if the 1980s trend continued, we would have been at parity by now.

It's possible, however, that the journey towards wage parity would have stalled either way. If women's gains in the 1980s were made through the erasure of things like bias, once those less uncontrollable problems had been addressed, there would still have been an issue with women—who are the ones to bear children and take care of them in the early weeks because of biological factors like the ability to breastfeed, forcing them to take breaks, whether or not those breaks were mandated.

【拆句】 题干主干是 What do we learn about the gender pay gap，in the US during the 1980s 是修饰 "the gender pay gap" 的时间地点状语，句子结构简单、无陷阱。

【选项】 A) 与原文相反 It was being slowly closed 把原文的 fast 偷换成 slowly，方向完全相反。

B) ✓ 正确 they began to catch up—fast ↔ shrinking rapidly closed by about one percentage point a year ↔ rapidly 预判强调"差距在 1980 年代快速缩小"，It was shrinking rapidly 与之完全等值，且未引入任何额外含义，直接锁定 B。

C) 张冠李戴 It started to yawn 借用 the gap remains yawning 制造关联，但 yawning 在原文描述的是 P2 之后趋势停滞后差距依旧巨大的状态，不是 1980 年代发生的事，属于张冠李戴。

D) 答非所问 It remained substantial 描述的是 Women have historically been paid less 这种历史背景下的总体状态，并不针对题干所问的 1980 年代特征。

questions.shortExplanation: After family leave was introduced in the US, in fact, the rate of gender wage convergence fell to just 0.03 percentage points per year, and has remained there ever since.
questions.detailedExplanation:
【答案】 B （细节题）

【判型】 What happened with the introduction of... 问的是政策推行这一具体事件之后的客观结果，是典型的事实型提问。

【拆句】 with the introduction of state and federal family leave policies 是介词短语作状语，提示时间背景；句子无从句、无否定，结构平铺直叙。

【定位】 After family leave was introduced in the US, in fact, the rate of gender wage convergence fell to just 0.03 percentage points per year, and has remained there ever since.

事实上，美国引入家庭休假政策之后，性别工资收敛率降至每年仅 0.03 个百分点，并自此一直停留在这个水平。

【选项】 A) 张冠李戴 The process towards salary equity at work began to reverse 借用 that progress began to reverse during the pandemic，但原文的"反转"发生在大流行期间，不是家庭休假政策引入之后。

B) ✓ 正确 the rate of gender wage convergence fell to just 0.03 percentage points per year ↔

The rate of gender wage convergence started to fall noticeably 选项几乎逐词保留了 the rate of gender wage convergence...fell 的主干，只把后面的具体数字抽象化，是最高度等值的同义替换，直接锁定 B。 C) 无中生有 The trend of women returning to work after childbirth started 借用 helped those women to stay in the workplace—instead of dropping out to have families，但原文只说政策让一些女性留下来，没有说"产后返岗成为新趋势"，且这不是题干"introduction后发生了什么"的核心结果。 D) 无中生有 The narrowing of the gender pay gap attracted more attention 把"差距缩小"和"引起更多关注"拼接在一起，但原文从未提及关注度变化，是凭空捏造。
questions.hint: 回到原文定位题干关键词，比较选项与原文的含义。

questions.prompt: What partly accounts for the slip in women's salaries?

options.text: The insufficient motivation women generally have for career advancement.
The opportunities numerous women give up for pay raise and promotion.
The huge amounts of time and energy women spend taking care of the family.
The lack of policy support from government and business corporations.

questions.shortExplanation: Part of this is because women take on more of the unpaid labor at home, which can eat into time available for work and energy for career advancement.
questions.detailedExplanation:
【答案】 C （细节题）

【判型】 What partly accounts for the slip in women's salaries 问的是导致薪水下滑的部分原因，答案应在原文有明确文本对应，不需推断。

【拆句】 题干主干 What partly accounts for the slip，in women's salaries 修饰 slip；副词 partly 提示原文只承担"部分"原因，不要求穷尽所有因素。

【定位】 Part of this is because women take on more of the unpaid labor at home, which can eat into time available for work and energy for career advancement.

部分原因在于女性在家承担了更多无偿劳动，这会侵蚀她们可用于工作的时间，以及用于职业发展的精力。

【选项】 A) 无中生有 The insufficient motivation women generally have for career advancement 把原因归结为女性自身"职业发展动力不足"，原文从未做出此种心理动机层面的归因。 B) 与原文相反 The opportunities numerous women give up for pay raise and promotion 暗示女性"主动放弃"涨薪机会，但原文 mothers are passed over for raises and promotion 是被动语态——她们是"被跳过"，不是"主动放弃"。

C) ✓ 正确 women take on more of the unpaid labor at home ↔ taking care of the family eat into time available for work and energy for career advancement ↔

The huge amounts of time and energy C 同时包含"时间和精力"与"照顾家庭"两个核心要素，对应定位句的两段含义，是定位句的高度同义改写，直接锁定 C。 D) 与原文相反 The lack of policy support from government and business corporations 把原因归为"缺乏政策支持"，但原文恰恰相反：政策（family leave）已经引入并提供支持，问题反而出在政策支持的副作用上。
questions.hint: 回到原文定位题干关键词，比较选项与原文的含义。

questions.prompt: What does the new study say about wage parity?

options.text: It would have stalled if those controllable problems had not been addressed.
It would have halted if company and government had not worked together.
It would have been achieved with the complete erasure of gender biases.
It would have been attained with the continuation of the 1980s trend.

questions.shortExplanation: The study doesn't go into that question, other than to say that if the 1980s trend continued, we would have been at parity by now.
questions.detailedExplanation:
【答案】 D （细节题）

【判型】 What does the new study say about wage parity 要求复述研究的明确表述，而非读者推论，属于细节复述。

【拆句】 题干是简单疑问句，about wage parity 是介词短语作 say 的状语；结构简单。

【定位】 The study doesn't go into that question, other than to say that if the 1980s trend continued, we would have been at parity by now.

这项研究没有深入探讨那个问题，只是说如果 1980 年代的趋势延续下去，我们现在本应已经实现了薪酬平等。

【选项】 A) 与原文相反 It would have stalled if those controllable problems had not been addressed 借用 once those less uncontrollable problems had been addressed 制造对应，但原文是"问题已被解决之后还会有别的问题"，选项却说"如果没解决就会停滞"，方向颠倒。 B) 无中生有 It would have halted if company and government had not worked together 把"公司和政府合作"作为条件，但原文从未提及二者协同与否，只是说休假可由 company or government policy 支持。

C) 过度推断 It would have been achieved with the complete erasure of gender biases 借用 through the erasure of things like bias，但原文用了 things like bias 这种举例口吻，且只是 if 假设下的推测，并未说"完全消除偏见就能实现"。

D) ✓ 正确 if the 1980s trend continued ↔ with the continuation of the 1980s trend we would have been at parity by now ↔ It would have been attained D 把虚拟条件 if the 1980s trend continued 和结果 would have been at parity 一一对应，无缺漏无外加，是定位句最严格的同义改写。
questions.hint: 回到原文定位题干关键词，比较选项与原文的含义。

questions.prompt: What prevents women from achieving parity with men in the final analysis?

options.text: Ignoring biases against women in the workplace.
Giving birth to children and taking care of them.
Failing to mandate breaks for childbirth and care.
Lacking resources to address biological problems.

questions.shortExplanation: If women's gains in the 1980s were made through the erasure of things like bias, once those less uncontrollable problems had been addressed, there would still have been an issue with women—who are the ones to bear children and take care of them in the early weeks because of biological factors like the ability to breastfeed, forcing them to take breaks, whether or not those breaks were mandated.
questions.detailedExplanation:
【答案】 B （细节题）

【判型】 What prevents women from achieving parity with men in the final analysis 询问作者最终归因，答案对应原文末段一句明确归因句，不需多步推理。

【拆句】 prevents women from achieving parity with men 是 prevent sb from doing sth 结构；in the final analysis 是状语，意为"归根结底"，需要识别这个固定搭配才能锁定原文末段。

【定位】 If women's gains in the 1980s were made through the erasure of things like bias, once those less uncontrollable problems had been addressed, there would still have been an issue with women—who are the ones to bear children and take care of them in the early weeks because of biological factors like the ability to breastfeed, forcing them to take breaks, whether or not those breaks were mandated.

如果 1980 年代女性的进步是通过消除偏见之类的东西取得的，那么一旦这些相对可控的问题被处理掉之后，女性身上仍然会存在一个问题——她们是承担生育以及在最初几周照料孩子的人，因为像哺乳能力这样的生理因素，迫使她们休假，无论这种休假是否被强制规定。

【选项】 A) 与原文相反 Ignoring biases against women in the workplace 把原因归为"忽视偏见"，但原文 through the erasure of things like bias 恰是说偏见已被消除，且作者强调即便消除之后仍有问题——并非"忽视"导致。 B) ✓ 正确 who are the ones to bear children and take care of them in the early weeks↔

Giving birth to children and taking care of them B 把末段长句中的两个核心动作（生育 + 照护）抽出并列，正好对应预判中的"生育和照顾孩子"两层根因，是最纯粹的同义改写，直接锁定 B。

C) 与原文相反 Failing to mandate breaks for childbirth and care 把"不强制规定休假"作为最终原因，但原文 whether or not those breaks were mandated 明确指出强制与否都没用，最终原因不是强制不强制。 D) 无中生有 Lacking resources to address biological problems 借用 biological factors like the ability to breastfeed，但原文从未说"缺乏资源去解决生物学问题"，且作者立场是生物学因素本身就难以绕开，不是资源问题。
questions.hint: 回到原文定位题干关键词，比较选项与原文的含义。

items.title: 2025年6月六级第3套 · 选词填空
items.passage:
The slow progress of women in elective office is frustrating for some political observers and experts —including myself. Achieving gender equality in Congress is an important goal. This is because the number of women involved in legislative decisions has significant [26] _____ for all the policies that governments [27] _____ . Female legislators are more likely than men to introduce, speak about and work to pass policies that disproportionately affect women and girls, such as paid family leave, pay [28] _____ and gender-based violence.

Having more women in Congress also fosters a greater sense of connection between female voters and government. In addition, it [29] _____ women's sense that government cares about their concerns and inspires young women to become more politically engaged.

While women are underrepresented in governments around the globe, it is a particularly [30] _____ problem in the United States. Currently, the U.S. ranks 73rd in the world when it comes to female representation in government.

But the reason women are so [31] _____ underrepresented in U.S. government is not because they face resistance from voters or struggle to raise money. On the contrary, decades of research shows that female candidates raise as much money and win as often as male politicians with similar [32] _____ .

Rather, the slow progress of women in politics is a tale of two political parties.

In the next Congress, there will be 107 female Democratic lawmakers and 42 female Republican lawmakers in the Senate and House combined.

In order for women to gain half of the seats in Congress, more women need to run, [33] _____ on Republican tickets. This will require the Republican Party as a whole to [34] _____ recruiting women— and not just for one election cycle, but in a [35] _____ way.

questions.prompt: the number of women involved in legislative decisions has significant __(26)__ for all the policies that governments __(27)__
questions.shortExplanation: have consequences for 是高频固定搭配，意为'对…产生影响' 本句解释'女性议员数量对所有政策都有重要影响'，与 Female legislators are more likely than men to introduce, speak about and work to pass policies 一脉相承， consequences for policies 完全贴合。
questions.detailedExplanation:
【答案】 B) consequences 名词

【词性槽】 形容词 significant + ___ + for 介词短语

【依据】 have consequences for 是高频固定搭配，意为'对…产生影响' 本句解释'女性议员数量对所有政策都有重要影响'，与 Female legislators are more likely than men to introduce, speak about and work to pass policies 一脉相承， consequences for policies 完全贴合。

【竞争词】 C) credentials '资历'与 for policies 搭配不成立

credentials 指个人证书、资格，对应的是 candidate 本身，不能说'议员数量对政策有 credentials'。

F) equity 义为'公平'，与 have ... for 搭不成立

have significant equity for policies 既不成搭配，也不通逻辑。

J) impetus '推动力'常用 give/provide impetus to，不用 have impetus for

impetus 与 for 共现表'对…的推动'虽可，但句意偏'对政策有影响'而非'推动'，consequences 更贴。

【易错】 最具迷惑性的错误词是 J) —— impetus 看似也能与 for 搭，'对…的推动'',词性也对。考生易被 has significant impetus for policies 的字面看似通顺骗到；防坑点是 have consequences for 才是英语里'对…有影响'的固定搭配，且本段紧接的例证 Female legislators are more likely than men to introduce, speak about and work to pass policies 说的是'影响政策内容'而非'推动政策出现'。
questions.hint: 根据空格前后的词性、搭配与上下文选择词语；每个词最多使用一次。

questions.prompt: all the policies that governments __(27)__
questions.shortExplanation: enact policies 是固定搭配'颁布/制定政策'
questions.detailedExplanation:
【答案】 E) enact 动词

【词性槽】 定语从句 that governments + ___，缺谓语动词

【依据】 enact policies 是固定搭配'颁布/制定政策'

上文谈'女性议员推动政策通过' work to pass policies that disproportionately affect women and girls，governments enact policies 与之同义，且 enact 与 policies/laws 是公认搭配。

【竞争词】 L) prioritize '优先处理'语义偏'排序'，且要被 34 题占用

prioritize policies 也能说，但语义在'优先排序'而非'制定'；而且 34 题需要 prioritize 与 recruiting 搭配，词只能用一次。
questions.hint: 根据空格前后的词性、搭配与上下文选择词语；每个词最多使用一次。

questions.prompt: such as paid family leave, pay __(28)__ and gender-based violence.
questions.shortExplanation: pay equity = 同工同酬，影响女性的典型议题
questions.detailedExplanation:
【答案】 F) equity 名词

【词性槽】 并列名词项 paid family leave, pay ___ and gender-based violence

【依据】 pay equity = 同工同酬，影响女性的典型议题

本段例证 policies that disproportionately affect women and girls 列举与女性相关的政策议题，pay equity（同工同酬）与 paid family leave、gender-based violence 同属'女性权益'范畴，是英语世界讨论性别平等的高频术语。

【竞争词】 J) impetus pay impetus 不成搭配，且与女性议题无关

impetus 是'推动力'，不与 pay 构成复合名词，也无法作为'议题'与 paid family leave 并列。
questions.hint: 根据空格前后的词性、搭配与上下文选择词语；每个词最多使用一次。

questions.prompt: it __(29)__ women's sense that government cares about their concerns
questions.shortExplanation: bolster one's sense 是'增强某人的…感'的常见搭配
questions.detailedExplanation:
【答案】 A) bolsters 动词

【词性槽】 主语 it + ___ + 宾语 women's sense

【依据】 bolster one's sense 是'增强某人的…感'的常见搭配

上文 Having more women in Congress also fosters a greater sense of connection 已用 foster；本句用并列动词继续推进同向语义，bolsters women's sense that government cares 自然衔接。

【竞争词】 M) sufficessuffices 是不及物动词，不能带宾语

suffice 表'足够'，常说 it suffices to do/that...，后面跟从句或不定式；不能直接接 women's sense 作宾语，语法不通。
questions.hint: 根据空格前后的词性、搭配与上下文选择词语；每个词最多使用一次。

questions.prompt: it is a particularly __(30)__ problem in the United States
questions.shortExplanation: 与 problem 构成常见搭配'棘手的问题'
questions.detailedExplanation:
【答案】 I) formidable 形容词

【词性槽】 不定冠词 a + 副词 particularly + ___ + 名词 problem

【依据】 与 problem 构成常见搭配'棘手的问题'

上下文交代美国排名第 73 the U.S. ranks 73rd in the world，说明这一问题在美国'尤其棘手'；formidable problem 是英语高频搭配，与 particularly 程度副词自然衔接。

【竞争词】 K) lavish 词义指向'奢华、铺张'，与 problem 不搭

lavish 多形容花费、款待，无法描述社会问题的严重程度。

O) tenured 义为'终身聘任的'，专用于职位

tenured 常见搭配是 tenured professor/position，修饰 problem 完全不通。
questions.hint: 根据空格前后的词性、搭配与上下文选择词语；每个词最多使用一次。

questions.prompt: But the reason women are so __(31)__ underrepresented in U.S. government
questions.shortExplanation: 强调'代表性偏低'的程度，呼应美国排第 73
questions.detailedExplanation:
【答案】 D) dramatically 副词

【词性槽】 be 动词 are + ___ + 过去分词 underrepresented

【依据】 强调'代表性偏低'的程度，呼应美国排第 73

上文已用 particularly formidable 渲染问题严重，本句继续追问'为何如此严重地代表不足'；dramatically underrepresented 是英文报道里固定的'程度极大'表达。

【竞争词】 G) especially 意为'尤其'，常引出比较或例子

especially 通常需要一个比较对象或后接具体范畴（especially on Republican tickets 那种）， 单独修饰 underrepresented 表程度则不自然，且 G 已被 33 题强需占用。

H) evasively 义为'回避地、含糊地'，与 underrepresented 逻辑不通

evasively 多修饰 answer/respond 等言语动词，描述'代表性不足'毫无语义关联。
questions.hint: 根据空格前后的词性、搭配与上下文选择词语；每个词最多使用一次。

questions.prompt: female candidates raise as much money and win as often as male politicians with similar __(32)__.
questions.shortExplanation: candidates with similar credentials = '资历相当的候选人'
questions.detailedExplanation:
【答案】 C) credentials 名词

【词性槽】 介词 with + 形容词 similar + ___

【依据】 candidates with similar credentials = '资历相当的候选人'

本段反驳一种误解 not because they face resistance from voters or struggle to raise money，再以研究为据 female candidates raise as much money and win as often as male politicians with similar __(32)__. 进行同等条件下的对比，credentials（资历）正是这种'公平比较'的基准。

【竞争词】 J) impetus '推动力'不可用 similar 衡量，且与候选人能力比较无关

similar impetus 在政客比较语境下毫无意义，无法构成对照基准。
questions.hint: 根据空格前后的词性、搭配与上下文选择词语；每个词最多使用一次。

questions.prompt: more women need to run, __(33)__ on Republican tickets.
questions.shortExplanation: 聚焦到共和党票上，呼应'两党之别'主旨
questions.detailedExplanation:
【答案】 G) especially 副词

【词性槽】 逗号后 + ___ + 介词短语 on Republican tickets

【依据】 聚焦到共和党票上，呼应'两党之别'主旨

上文 there will be 107 female Democratic lawmakers and 42 female Republican lawmakers 表明共和党女议员人数远少；本句强调 more women need to run, especially on Republican tickets，正是把'更多女性参选'的火力点向共和党聚焦。

【竞争词】 H) evasively 义不搭

evasively 描述'回避地、含糊地'参选毫无意义，逻辑指向反。
questions.hint: 根据空格前后的词性、搭配与上下文选择词语；每个词最多使用一次。

questions.prompt: This will require the Republican Party as a whole to __(34)__ recruiting women
questions.shortExplanation: prioritize doing 是'优先去做某事'的固定搭配
questions.detailedExplanation:
【答案】 L) prioritize 动词

【词性槽】 情态动词 to + ___ + 动名词 recruiting

【依据】 prioritize doing 是'优先去做某事'的固定搭配

上文已点出共和党女议员稀少 42 female Republican lawmakers，本句号召共和党把'招募女性'放到优先级首位，prioritize recruiting women 既合搭配也合语义。
questions.hint: 根据空格前后的词性、搭配与上下文选择词语；每个词最多使用一次。

questions.prompt: not just for one election cycle, but in a __(35)__ way.
questions.shortExplanation: 与 not just for one election cycle 形成时间维度的对照——'持续的'
questions.detailedExplanation:
【答案】 N) sustained 形容词

【词性槽】 介词 in + 限定词 a + ___ + 名词 way

【依据】 与 not just for one election cycle 形成时间维度的对照——'持续的'

本句要点 not just for one election cycle, but in a __(35)__ way：not just one cycle 暗含'不止一次性'，与之对照的正是'持续地、长期地'，in a sustained way 是英文里强调长期坚持的固定写法。

【竞争词】 K) lavish 义为'奢华的'，与时间维度无关

in a lavish way 形容方式'铺张奢侈'，与'不止一次选举周期'的对照无任何逻辑联系。

【易错】 最具迷惑性的错误词是 K) —— lavish 与 way 搭配看似通顺。in a lavish way 字面读起来似乎成立，考生不细看上下文易误选；防坑点是利用 not just A, but B 的对照结构——A 是 one election cycle（短期），B 必为'长期持续'，sustained 才合方向。
questions.hint: 根据空格前后的词性、搭配与上下文选择词语；每个词最多使用一次。

items.title: 2025年6月六级第3套 · 信息匹配
items.passage:
A) I can be a reluctant socialiser. I'm sometimes secretly pleased when social plans are called off. I get restless a few hours into a hangout. I even once went on a free 10-day silent meditation(冥想) retreat—not for the meditation, but for the silence.

B) So I can relate to author Anneli Rufus, who wrote in *Party of One: The Loners' Manifesto*: "When parents on TV shows punished their kids by ordering them to go to their rooms, I was confused. I loved my room. Being there behind a locked door was a treat. To me a punishment was being ordered to play games with my cousin Louis."

C) Unsocial tendencies like these are often far from ideal. Abundant research shows the harms of social isolation, considered a serious public health problem in countries that have rapidly ageing populations (though talk of a 'loneliness epidemic' may be exaggerated). In the UK, the Royal College of General Practitioners says that loneliness has the same risk level for premature death as diabetes. Strong social connections are important for cognitive functioning, motor function and a smoothly running immune system.

D) This is especially clear from cases of extreme social isolation. Examples of people kept in captivity, children kept isolated in abusive orphanages, and prisoners kept in solitary confinement all show how prolonged solitude can lead to hallucinations(幻觉 ) and other forms of mental instability.

E) But these are severe and involuntary cases of aloneness. For those of us who just prefer plenty of alone time, emerging research suggests some good news: there are upsides to being alone—for both our work lives and our emotional well-being.

F) Solitude is a time for reflection, for thinking about things more deeply. In a world increasingly focused on speed and competitiveness, solitude is precious and something to be treasured. And there are benefits in learning to love your solitude.

G) One key benefit of solitude is improved creativity. Gregory Feist, who focuses on the psychology of creativity at California's San Jose State University, has defined creativity as thinking or activity with two key elements: originality and usefulness. He has found that personality traits commonly associated with creativity are openness (receptiveness to new thoughts and experiences), self-confidence, and autonomy—which may include "a lack of concern for social norms" and "a preference for being alone". In fact, Feist's research on both artists and scientists shows that one of the most prominent features of creative folks is their lesser interest in socialising.

H) One reason for this is that such people are likely to spend sustained time alone working on their craft. Plus, Feist says, many artists "are trying to make sense of their internal world and a lot of internal personal experiences that they're trying to give expression and meaning to through their art." Solitude allows for the reflection and observation necessary for that creative process.

I) A recent justification of these ideas came from University at Buffalo psychologist Julie Bowker, who researches social withdrawal. Social withdrawal is usually categorised into three types: shyness caused by fear or anxiety; avoidance, from a dislike of socialising; and unsociability, from a preference for solitude. A paper by Bowker and her colleagues was the first to show that a type of social withdrawal could have a positive effect—they found that creativity was linked specifically to unsociability. They also found that unsociability had no correlation with aggression (shyness and avoidance did). This was significant because while previous research had suggested that unsociability might be harmless, Bowker and colleagues' paper showed that it could actually be beneficial. Unsociable people are likely to be "having just enough interaction," Bowker says. "They have a preference for being alone, but they also don't mind being with others."

J) Still, it turns out that solitude is important for more than creativity. It's commonly believed that leaders need to be sociable. But this depends, among other things, on the personalities of their employees. One 2011 study showed that in branches of a pizza chain where employees were more passive, outgoing bosses were associated with higher profits. But in branches where employees were more active, introverted( 内向的 ) leaders were more effective. One reason for this is that introverted people are less likely to feel threatened by strong personalities and suggestions. They're also more likely to listen.

K) Since ancient times, meanwhile, people have been aware of a link between isolation and mental focus. After all, cultures with traditions of religious hermits( 隐⼠ ) believe that solitude is important for enlightenment. Recent research has given us a better understanding of why. One benefit of unsociability is the brain's state of active mental rest, which goes hand-in-hand with the stillness of being alone. When another person is present, your brain can't help but pay some attention. This can be a positive distraction. But it's still a distraction.

L) Daydreaming in the absence of such distractions activates the brain's default-mode network. Among other functions, this network helps to consolidate memory and understand others' emotions. Giving free rein to a wandering mind not only helps with focus in the long term but strengthens your sense of both yourself and others. Paradoxically, therefore, periods of solitude actually help when it comes time to socialise once more. And the occasional absence of focus ultimately helps concentration in the long run.

M) A more recent advocate of thoughtful and productive solitude is Susan Cain, author of *Quiet: The Power of Introverts in a World That Can't Stop Talking* and founder of Quiet Revolution, a company that promotes quiet and introvert-friendly workplaces. "These days, we tend to believe that creativity emerges from a decidedly unreserved socialising process, but in fact it requires sustained attention and deep focus," she says. "Also, humans are such absorbent social beings that when we surround ourselves with others, we automatically take in their opinions and aesthetics. To truly chart our own path or vision, we have to be willing to isolate ourselves, at least for some period of time."

N) Still, the line between useful solitude and dangerous isolation can be blurry. "Almost anything can be adaptive and maladaptive, depending on how extreme they get," Feist says. A disorder has to do with dysfunction. If someone stops caring about people and cuts off all contact, this could point to an irrational neglect of social relations. But creative unsociability is a far cry from this. In fact, Feist says, "there's a real danger with people who are never alone." It's hard to examine one's own thoughts, feelings and motives, to be self-aware, and fully relaxed unless you have occasional solitude. In addition, introverts tend to have fewer but stronger friendships—which has been linked to greater happiness.

O) As with many things, quality reigns over quantity. Nurturing a few solid relationships without feeling the need to constantly populate your life with endless chatting ultimately may be better for you.

P) Thus, if your personality tends toward unsociability, you shouldn't feel the need to change. Of course, that comes with qualifications. But as long as you have regular social contact, you are choosing solitude rather than being forced into it, you have at least a few good friends and your solitude is good for your well-being or productivity, there's no point agonising over how to fit a square personality into a round hole.

items.passage:
Simulators are most often utilized within industries such as nuclear power, aviation and surgery where failure results in disastrous consequences. To maximize the value from a simulation learning experience, participants should immediately and directly apply their learning to a specific intervention within their organization.

Most organizations aspire to deploy significant change programs, only to find them nearly impossible to implement. That is largely because successful change requires more than a vision, it requires a workforce that not only doesn't resist change, but embraces it.

To achieve success, an organization must build a transformation program that will allow change to be rapidly pulled across its departments and throughout its layers. Regardless of the level of senior management commitment, unless key thought leaders at all levels embrace the change, the initiative will wither and die. To create this kind of widespread passion, learning leaders must expose the workforce to what could be, which will enable them to rethink their mental models, enable them to break free from their deep-rooted paradigms and embrace the opportunity to learn.

Allowing participants to enter a simulated environment provides them with the opportunity to experience alternative realities which can prompt them to rethink their current beliefs.

Behavioral change is not easy for most adults. Lectures, training programs and workshops can explain the intellectual elements of transformation, but they are seldom effective at getting to the behavioral aspects that lie at the heart of a significant change initiative. Further, under normal working conditions, managers rarely see the full effect of their employee development efforts. As such, an intervention like a simulation can provide the stimulus for change.

An effective simulation can be better than experience as a learning tool because it accelerates time, compresses space, and unlike reality, is specifically designed to maximize participant learning. Simulations provide an immersive learning experience where skills, processes and knowledge all can be highlighted in a way reality cannot. The ability to explore, experiment and repeatedly apply new knowledge in unlimited, risk-free models is what makes simulation one of the most productive forms of learning.

Well-designed simulations can enable individuals and groups to develop a deep level of understanding about how their decisions and intuitive responses to business stimuli affect their fellow participants and the organization as a whole. To reap the benefits, however, simulations must feel like reality. At the end of the successful simulation, participants must declare "this is us." If they don't, they will view the experience as a game, which can be difficult to apply on the job, or worse, irrelevant to everyday work tasks. To maximize benefits from simulation, participants should immediately apply the learning from the experience to forge a smooth link between learning and doing.

questions.prompt: What do we learn about successful changes in organizations?

options.text: They can be immediately implemented with great ease.
They are usually led by organization leaders of vision.
They call for enthusiastic support from the workforce.
They often result from simulation learning experiences.

questions.shortExplanation: That is largely because successful change requires more than a vision, it requires a workforce that not only doesn't resist change, but embraces it.
questions.detailedExplanation:
【答案】 C （细节题）

【判型】 题干 What do we learn about successful changes in organizations? 是对客观信息的直接询问，没有 infer/imply 等推断信号，也没有 main idea/title 等主旨信号，属于典型细节题。

【拆句】 What do we learn about successful changes in organizations? 是 What 引导的特殊疑问句，主干 we learn，about 介词短语限定 learn 的内容，successful changes 是真正的题眼，in organizations 是发生场域。结构平铺直叙，无陷阱。

【定位】 That is largely because successful change requires more than a vision, it requires a workforce that not only doesn't resist change, but embraces it.

这在很大程度上是因为成功的变革不只需要愿景，它还需要一支不但不抵触变革、还会拥抱变革的员工队伍。

【选项】 A) 与原文相反 They can be immediately implemented with great ease. 称变革「轻易立刻落地」， 但 Most organizations aspire to deploy significant change programs, only to find them nearly impossible to implement 明说大多数变革极难落地，两者完全相反。 B) 偷换概念 They are usually led by organization leaders of vision. 把成功变革的关键归到「有远见的领导」上，但定位句 successful change requires more than a vision 恰恰说仅有 vision 不够，关键在 workforce；把强调点偷换了。

C) ✓ 正确 it requires a workforce that not only doesn't resist change, but embraces it ↔

They call for enthusiastic support from the workforce. a workforce ↔ the workforce They call for enthusiastic support from the workforce. 的「require + 全员热情支持」与定位句 requires a workforce that ... embraces it 精准对位，且对位完整、无外加成分。

D) 强加因果 They often result from simulation learning experiences. 说成功变革「源于」模拟学习，但全文逻辑是 simulation 服务于 change，并非 change 的来源；定位句也未涉及 simulation。
questions.hint: 回到原文定位题干关键词，比较选项与原文的含义。
