questions.detailedExplanation:
【答案】 A （细节题）

【判型】 题干 What should learning leaders do to arouse learners' passion for change? 在问主体的具体动作，答案对应原文里一句明确的「该做什么」，属细节题。

【拆句】 What should learning leaders do to arouse learners' passion for change? 主干 What should learning leaders do，to arouse learners' passion for change 是目的状语，for change 进一步修饰 passion。结构清晰，无陷阱。

【定位】 To create this kind of widespread passion, learning leaders must expose the workforce to what could be, which will enable them to rethink their mental models, enable them to break free from their deep-rooted paradigms and embrace the opportunity to learn.

为了激发这种广泛的热情，learning leaders 必须把员工带去看「事情本可以是什么样」， 这将使他们重新审视心智模型、挣脱根深蒂固的旧范式，并拥抱学习机会。

【选项】 A) ✓ 正确 expose the workforce to what could be ↔

Allow them to see what could possibly be achieved. the workforce ↔ them 预判落在主句动作 expose…to what could be 上，A 用 allow them to see what could possibly be achieved 与之一一对应。

B) 答非所问 Help them break free from their old paradigms. 取自定位句后面的 which 从句中的并列动作 enable them to break free from their deep-rooted paradigms，那是 expose 之后的结果，而非 learning leaders 直接「应做」的动作。 C) 答非所问 Encourage them to rethink their thought models. 取自 which 从句中的 rethink their mental models，依然属于 expose 之后的结果，不是题干所问的直接动作。

D) 答非所问 Stimulate them to embrace fresh opportunities. 改写自 embrace the opportunity to learn，仍是 which 结果从句尾部的并列结果之一，不是题干问的 learning leaders 的直接动作。
questions.hint: 回到原文定位题干关键词，比较选项与原文的含义。

questions.prompt: What does the passage say about lectures, training programs and workshops?

options.text: They are generally incapable of changing workers' behaviors on the job.
They are interventions different from simulations in creating stimuli for change.
They aim at transforming the behaviors of the workers in an organization.
They help managers achieve the full effect of employee development efforts.

questions.shortExplanation: Lectures, training programs and workshops can explain the intellectual elements of transformation, but they are seldom effective at getting to the behavioral aspects that lie at the heart of a significant change initiative.
questions.detailedExplanation:
【答案】 A （细节题）

【判型】 What does the passage say about lectures, training programs and workshops? 是 say about + 主体的标准细节题问法，无推断信号。

【拆句】 What does the passage say about lectures, training programs and workshops? 主干 What does the passage say，about 引出讨论对象，对象是三项并列名词。无从句、无否定，无陷阱。

【定位】 Lectures, training programs and workshops can explain the intellectual elements of transformation, but they are seldom effective at getting to the behavioral aspects that lie at the heart of a significant change initiative.

讲座、培训项目和工作坊能讲清变革的认知层面，但它们在触及行为层面（而行为层面恰是重大变革的核心）这件事上几乎无效。

【选项】 A) ✓ 正确 they are seldom effective at getting to the behavioral aspects ↔

They are generally incapable of changing workers' behaviors on the job. the behavioral aspects that lie at the heart of a significant change initiative ↔

workers' behaviors on the job 预判「改不了行为」直接对应 generally incapable of changing workers' behaviors，两端的否定强度通过 seldom↔generally not 桥接成立。 B) 无中生有 They are interventions different from simulations in creating stimuli for change. 把三者说成「在制造变革刺激上不同于 simulation 的干预」，原文只把它们与 simulation 在「能不能触及行为」上作对照，未把它们也定性为 intervention，更未谈它们「创造刺激」。 C) 与原文相反 They aim at transforming the behaviors of the workers in an organization. 称它们 「以改变行为为目标」，与原文「在行为层面 seldom effective」的判定方向相反—— 原文恰是说它们做不到这件事。 D) 张冠李戴 They help managers achieve the full effect of employee development efforts. 让三者「帮助管理者获得员工发展投入的全部成效」，但原文 managers rarely see the full effect of their employee development efforts 是说在常规工作里 managers 几乎看不到全部成效，且这一判断是关于「常规工作条件」整体，不是三者帮助下的状况。
questions.hint: 回到原文定位题干关键词，比较选项与原文的含义。

questions.prompt: What makes simulation one of the most fruitful forms of learning?

options.text: Its capability of saving time by accelerating the immersive learning experience.
Its potential for learners to examine their skills, knowledge and learning process.
Its capability of providing all participants with a practical learning experience.
Its potential for learners to explore, experiment and practice without any risk.

questions.shortExplanation: The ability to explore, experiment and repeatedly apply new knowledge in unlimited, risk-free models is what makes simulation one of the most productive forms of learning. 在数量无限、零风险的模型里探索、实验并反复运用新知的能力，正是让 simulation 成为最高效学习方式之一的原因。
questions.detailedExplanation:
【答案】 D （细节题）

【判型】 What makes simulation one of the most fruitful forms of learning? 用「What makes X Y?」结构直问 simulation 之所以 fruitful 的原因，原文给出明确归因。

【拆句】 What makes simulation one of the most fruitful forms of learning? make 引导 sb./sth. + 宾补结构，simulation 是宾语，one of the most fruitful forms of learning 是宾补；fruitful 与原文 productive 同义。无陷阱。

【定位】 The ability to explore, experiment and repeatedly apply new knowledge in unlimited, risk-free models is what makes simulation one of the most productive forms of learning. 在数量无限、零风险的模型里探索、实验并反复运用新知的能力，正是让 simulation 成为最高效学习方式之一的原因。

【选项】 A) 偷换概念 Its capability of saving time by accelerating the immersive learning experience. 把 accelerates time 拎出来当主因，但原文里它只是 simulation 优点的描述之一，不是 is what makes 强调结构所归的原因。 B) 偷换概念 Its potential for learners to examine their skills, knowledge and learning process. 取自 skills, processes and knowledge all can be highlighted，但原文是 processes （业务流程/作业过程），选项改成了 learning process（学习过程），主体偷换；且原文是 simulation 来 highlight，不是 learners 来 examine。 C) 以偏概全 Its capability of providing all participants with a practical learning experience. 用 practical learning experience 模糊概括 simulation，未含 risk-free、reflect、 experiment 等核心元素；原文 is what makes 主语处也并未用 practical 来归因。 D) ✓ 正确 The ability to explore, experiment and repeatedly apply new knowledge ↔

Its potential for learners to explore, experiment and practice without any risk. in unlimited, risk-free models ↔ without any risk The ability ↔ Its potential D 保留了原文的三动词并列与 risk-free 条件，是唯一同时满足两项核心的选项。
questions.hint: 回到原文定位题干关键词，比较选项与原文的含义。

questions.prompt: What should participants do in a simulation to reap the greatest benefits possible?

options.text: Take the experience as a mere game.
Apply promptly what they learn to their jobs.
Develop a deep level of understanding.
Strive to connect closely with their leaders.

questions.shortExplanation: To maximize benefits from simulation, participants should immediately apply the learning from the experience to forge a smooth link between learning and doing. 为最大化从模拟中获得的收益，参与者应立刻把从体验中所学应用到工作中，以打通「学」 与「做」之间的桥梁。
questions.detailedExplanation:
【答案】 B （细节题）

【判型】 What should participants do in a simulation to reap the greatest benefits possible? 是问明确做法的标准细节题。

【拆句】 What should participants do in a simulation to reap the greatest benefits possible? 主干 What should participants do，in a simulation 是地点状语，to reap the greatest benefits possible 是目的不定式，possible 后置修饰 benefits。无陷阱。

【定位】 To maximize benefits from simulation, participants should immediately apply the learning from the experience to forge a smooth link between learning and doing. 为最大化从模拟中获得的收益，参与者应立刻把从体验中所学应用到工作中，以打通「学」 与「做」之间的桥梁。

【选项】 A) 与原文相反 Take the experience as a mere game. 让参与者「把体验当作单纯的游戏」，但 If they don't, they will view the experience as a game, which can be difficult to apply on the job 明确把「视为游戏」当作负面后果。 B) ✓ 正确 participants should immediately apply the learning from the experience↔

Apply promptly what they learn to their jobs. to forge a smooth link between learning and doing ↔ to their jobs B 在副词（promptly ↔ immediately）、核心动作（apply what they learn ↔ apply the learning）与落点（to their jobs ↔ between learning and doing）三处与定位句完全对位。

C) 答非所问 Develop a deep level of understanding. 取自 enable individuals and groups to develop a deep level of understanding，那是 simulation 的功效（果），不是参与者「应当做什么以最大化收益」（因）。

D) 无中生有 Strive to connect closely with their leaders. 让参与者「努力与领导紧密联系」，但全文从未要求 participants 去与 leaders 建立紧密联系，原文 forge a link 的对象是 learning 与 doing，不是 participants 与 leaders。
questions.hint: 回到原文定位题干关键词，比较选项与原文的含义。

items.title: 2025年6月六级第3套 · 仔细阅读 · 第二篇
items.passage:
GDP growth is not a good indicator of how well a country is performing, and should not be the primary goal of governments. Unlimited growth is not sustainable, and economic thinking is moving toward the idea that we should aim for sustainability in our economic models. But while a sustainable economy is vital to our future, it is a means to an end, not an end in itself.

The idea that governments should focus on happiness has its critics. There are concerns about how happiness can be measured. Is happiness not a fleeting and subjective psychological state? Don't different people experience different levels of happiness? Even on the broadest interpretation of 'happiness' as prosperity or 'life satisfaction', people want different things.

Of course, governments cannot impose life satisfaction on citizens. But our happiness relies on collaborative efforts as a society. A government's obligation lies in creating conditions that promote prosperity. And there is good reason to suppose that such conditions exist, are globally applicable, and are discoverable through research.

In a recently published article, philosopher Julian Baggini suggests we should focus on 'real wealth' for citizens, which does not depend on GDP growth. Access is key: people do not need to own, but rather access things that enable them to live well. Technological advances and changes in social behavior enable us to make more efficient use of the assets that we already have. And focusing on access to the resources people need to live better lives could help reduce inequality.

As far as it goes, this has much in common with proposals tabled by 'happiness' advocates. But it sets the bar far too low for what governments can and should be doing for their citizens.

For example, it's not clear how a 'real wealth' economy would remedy the epidemic of mental ill-health that plagues our society. In Western countries, at least—poor mental health is more detrimental to wellbeing than poverty. Over and above a vastly improved provision of therapeutic mental healthcare, there are preventative measures for improving mental health that governments could and should adopt. The WHO recommends establishing institutions that facilitate community participation—educational programs and interventions that provide skills for promoting mental wellbeing. It says a lot, however, that the WHO feels the need to appeal to the economic benefits of improving mental health to persuade governments that the cost of taking proposed measures is justified. As long as the economy is their priority, governments need go no further than ensuring citizens' continued productivity.

To demand that governments set the 'happiness' of citizens as their highest priority is to demand that they view citizens as ends in themselves.

questions.prompt: What does the passage say is the more recent thinking of economic growth?

options.text: It is vital to the future of humanity.
It should be governments' chief concern.
It is an indicator of government performance.

questions.shortExplanation: Unlimited growth is not sustainable, and economic thinking is moving toward the idea that we should aim for sustainability in our economic models.
questions.detailedExplanation:
【答案】 A （细节题）

【判型】 What does the passage say is the more recent thinking of economic growth\? 问「文章说……是什么」，要的是原文给出的具体表述，不是要考生推断。

【拆句】 主干是 What does the passage say is the more recent thinking of economic growth\?，what 是 say 的宾语，is 引导的从句作 say 的真正宾语；不要把 is 误读成主句谓语。结构清晰、无陷阱。

【定位】 Unlimited growth is not sustainable, and economic thinking is moving toward the idea that we should aim for sustainability in our economic models.

无限增长不可持续，经济思潮正转向「我们应当在经济模型中以可持续为目标」这一理念。

【选项】 A) ✓ 正确 we should aim for sustainability in our economic models ↔ It should be made sustainable 预判「应追求可持续」与 It should be made sustainable 字面同向，无需推断，直接锁定。

B) 偷换概念原文说「可持续经济」对未来重要 a sustainable economy is vital to our future，主语是「sustainable economy」，而非 It（指 economic growth）本身。 C) 与原文相反原文明确 GDP growth … should not be the primary goal of governments，作者主张增长不应是政府首要关切，It should be governments' chief concern 正好相反。 D) 与原文相反原文首句即否定 GDP growth is not a good indicator of how well a country is performing，It is an indicator of government performance 正是这个被否定的旧观点。
questions.hint: 回到原文定位题干关键词，比较选项与原文的含义。

questions.prompt: Why are some people opposed to the idea that governments should focus on happiness?

options.text: Governments cannot impose happiness on citizens.
People's happiness is built upon their own endeavor.
Happiness means different things to different people.
Happiness depends on sustainable economic growth.

questions.shortExplanation: Even on the broadest interpretation of 'happiness' as prosperity or 'life satisfaction', people want different things.
questions.detailedExplanation:
【答案】 C （细节题）

【判型】 Why are some people opposed to the idea that governments should focus on happiness\? 问「反对的原因」，原文必有一段集中陈述反对理由。

【拆句】 主干 Why are some people opposed to the idea，后接 that 引导的同位语从句解释 idea 的内容；opposed to 是固定搭配「反对」，不要看成被动语态。

【定位】 Even on the broadest interpretation of 'happiness' as prosperity or 'life satisfaction', people want different things.

即使把「幸福」理解到最宽泛的程度——视为「繁荣」或「生活满意度」——人们想要的东西也各不相同。

【选项】 A) 张冠李戴 Governments cannot impose happiness on citizens 是作者本人的让步 （governments cannot impose life satisfaction on citizens），而非反对者的反对原因，时空错位。

B) 无中生有原文 P2 从未提到「幸福建立在个人努力上」；endeavor 在全文不存在，是凭空添加的因果。

C) ✓ 正确 people want different things ↔ Happiness means different things to different people Don't different people experience different levels of happiness\? ↔

Happiness means different things to different people 「幸福因人而异」与 Happiness means different things to different people 同义， 三个反问句的共同指向皆收束于此。 D) 强加因果 P1 把 sustainable 与 happiness 视为两条不同线索，原文从未说 Happiness depends on sustainable economic growth；该选项把两个概念强行嫁接。
questions.hint: 回到原文定位题干关键词，比较选项与原文的含义。

questions.prompt: What does philosopher Julian Baggini suggest governments do in a recently published article?

options.text: Try to reduce inequality between the rich and the poor.
Provide people with access to resources for a better life.
Change people's behaviors to put social wealth to better use.
Make use of advanced technologies to improve people's lives.

questions.shortExplanation: Access is key: people do not need to own, but rather access things that enable them to live well.
questions.detailedExplanation:
【答案】 B （细节题）

【判型】 What does philosopher Julian Baggini suggest governments do 是经典「某人的具体主张」型细节题。

【拆句】 主干 What does philosopher Julian Baggini suggest governments do，suggest 后接省略 that 的宾语从句 governments do (what)，what 是 do 的宾语前置——理解为 「Baggini 建议政府做什么」。

【定位】 Access is key: people do not need to own, but rather access things that enable them to live well.

「使用权」是关键：人们不必拥有，而是要能用上那些让他们生活得更好的东西。

【选项】 A) 以偏概全 could help reduce inequality 只是 Baggini 主张的「附带效益」（could help），不是其建议政府该做的核心；选项 A 把附带效益当成主张主体。 B) ✓ 正确 access things that enable them to live well ↔

Provide people with access to resources for a better life 预判「让公民能用上让生活更好的资源」与 Provide people with access to resources for a better life 字面同向。

C) 偷换概念原文说 changes in social behavior enable us to make more efficient use of the assets，是「社会行为已发生的变化」让现有资产用得更高效；选项把它改成「政府去改变人们行为以更好利用社会财富」，主动者与目的都被偷换。 D) 以偏概全 Technological advances 在原文同样只是 access 模型成立的「条件」，不是 Baggini 给政府的建议；选项 D 抓了边缘条件而漏掉主张句。
questions.hint: 回到原文定位题干关键词，比较选项与原文的含义。

questions.prompt: Why does the WHO feel the need to appeal to the economic benefits of improving mental health to justify its recommendations?

options.text: Mental health programs cannot be executed without GDP growth.
Psychological interventions are conducive to people's wellbeing.
Poor mental health is detrimental to a nation's economic system.
Governments still take economic development as their priority.

questions.shortExplanation: It says a lot, however, that the WHO feels the need to appeal to the economic benefits of improving mental health to persuade governments that the cost of taking proposed measures is justified. As long as the economy is their priority, governments need go no further than ensuring citizens' continued productivity. 然而，WHO 不得不诉诸「改善心理健康带来的经济收益」来说服政府这一举措的成本合理，这一点本身就说明了问题：只要政府仍把经济置于首位，他们就只关心公民能否继续创造产值。
questions.detailedExplanation:
【答案】 D （推断题）

【判型】 Why does the WHO feel the need to appeal to the economic benefits 问「WHO 为何觉得有必要诉诸经济利益」，答案不在 WHO 这句的字面，而要从作者紧接的评论中推断政府的倾向。

【拆句】 主干 Why does the WHO feel the need to appeal to the economic benefits of improving mental health to justify its recommendations\?，feel the need to do = 觉得有必要做，to justify 是目的状语——「为了让其建议显得合理」。

【定位】 It says a lot, however, that the WHO feels the need to appeal to the economic benefits of improving mental health to persuade governments that the cost of taking proposed measures is justified. As long as the economy is their priority, governments need go no further than ensuring citizens' continued productivity. 然而，WHO 不得不诉诸「改善心理健康带来的经济收益」来说服政府这一举措的成本合理，这一点本身就说明了问题：只要政府仍把经济置于首位，他们就只关心公民能否继续创造产值。

【选项】 A) 无中生有原文从未说「无 GDP 增长就执行不了心理健康项目」，仅说「政府要看到经济收益才肯掏钱」；选项 A 把动机改成了执行前提，凭空捏造。

B) 答非所问 Psychological interventions are conducive to people's wellbeing 是事实陈述，原文 improving mental health 也支持这一点，但题干问的是「WHO 为何要诉诸经济收益」，与「干预有益健康」无关。 C) 偷换概念原文强调「政府以经济为先」是导致 WHO 必须用经济话术的「原因」；选项 C 反过来说「心理健康差对经济不利」是 WHO 用经济话术的原因——把工具变成了动机来源。

D) ✓ 正确 As long as the economy is their priority ↔

Governments still take economic development as their priority It says a lot, however, that the WHO feels the need to appeal to the economic benefits ↔

Governments still take economic development as their priority 「政府只听经济话术」的根本原因即「政府仍以经济为先」，与 Governments still take economic development as their priority 同义。
questions.hint: 回到原文定位题干关键词，比较选项与原文的含义。

questions.prompt: What message does the author try to convey at the end of the passage?

options.text: Governments should consider citizens' views in decision-making.
Governments should set sustained productivity as their top priority.

questions.shortExplanation:
【答案】 B （主旨题）

【判型】 What message does the author try to convey at the end of the passage\? 问作者结尾要传达的核心信息，是局部主旨题。

【拆句】 主干 What message does the author try to convey at the end of the passage\?，try to convey = 试图传达；message 是宾语前置至 what。

【选项】 A) 与原文相反全文
questions.detailedExplanation:
【答案】 B （主旨题）

【判型】 What message does the author try to convey at the end of the passage\? 问作者结尾要传达的核心信息，是局部主旨题。

【拆句】 主干 What message does the author try to convey at the end of the passage\?，try to convey = 试图传达；message 是宾语前置至 what。

【选项】 A) 与原文相反全文反对把繁荣/产值当目标（should not be the primary goal / ensuring citizens' continued productivity 被作者批评），Governments' goal should be prosperity-driven 正好是作者反对的立场。 B) ✓ 正确 view citizens as ends in themselves↔ Governments' goal should be people-oriented set the 'happiness' of citizens as their highest priority↔

Governments' goal should be people-oriented 末段「把公民视为目的」是全文落点，与 Governments' goal should be people-oriented 同义。 C) 无中生有原文从未谈及「决策时听取公民意见」（views in decision-making）；这是把「以人为本」误解为「问政于民」，添加了原文不存在的程序性内容。

D) 与原文相反作者在 governments need go no further than ensuring citizens' continued productivity 中明显嘲讽了「以产值为先」的政府逻辑；sustained productivity as their top priority 正是作者批评的对象。
questions.hint: 回到原文定位题干关键词，比较选项与原文的含义。
